glosses: to exist, to be (for inanimate objects)
explanations: Expresses the existence of inanimate objects, abstract concepts, events, or locations. The counterpart for animate beings (people, animals) is いる.
Expresses possession, often with the structure [person]は[thing]がある. {お金|おかね}がある (to have money), {時間|じかん}がある (to have time).
Indicates where something is located. {駅|えき}はどこにありますか (Where is the station?).

glosses: X mark; cross mark; wrong answer mark
explanations: A cross-shaped symbol (×) used to indicate something is wrong, incorrect, or not permitted. Opposite of ○ (maru, circle mark for correct).
Colloquially used to indicate that someone has been divorced. バツイチ means divorced once.
Describes something of less than average size. The opposite of {大|おお}きい (big). Used for physical dimensions of objects, spaces, and living things.
When describing voices or sounds, {小|ちい}さい means quiet or soft. {小|ちい}さい{声|こえ} means a quiet/soft voice.
A formal conjunction used to introduce a contrasting statement.
A casual conjunction used to introduce a contrasting statement or add reservation.
A sweet course served at the end of a meal.
The area surrounding or near a particular place.
Marks the grammatical subject of a sentence—who or what performs the action or is being described. Unlike は, が typically introduces new information or emphasizes the identity of the subject.

With certain verbs and adjectives expressing ability, desire, or emotion (できる, {分|わ}かる, {好|す}き, {欲|ほ}しい, etc.), が marks what would be the object in English. {日本語|にほんご}が{分|わ}かる (I understand Japanese), {猫|ねこ}が{好|す}き (I like cats).
Connects two clauses with a contrastive or concessive meaning. Similar to 'but' or 'although' in English.

An educational institution. Can refer to any level: elementary school ({小学校|しょうがっこう}), middle school ({中学校|ちゅうがっこう}), high school ({高校|こうこう}/{高等学校|こうとうがっこう}), or the general concept of school as a place of learning.
A casual apology.
Used when entering someone's home or getting someone's attention.
Politely declining or expressing that one wants to avoid something.

Marks the topic of a sentence—what the sentence is about. The topic is often (but not always) the grammatical subject. は sets up what the speaker wants to comment on, and the rest of the sentence provides information about that topic.

Indicates contrast with something else, either stated or implied. When は is used on an element that would normally take a different particle (like を or に), it often adds a contrastive nuance: 'as for X (as opposed to something else)...'
A bound publication with pages, including novels, textbooks, manga, and other printed materials. The most common word for 'book' in Japanese.
A general positive evaluation. Can describe quality, condition, character, or suitability. One of the most frequently used adjectives in Japanese.
Used to give permission or indicate that something is acceptable. いいですよ (That's fine / Go ahead).
Used to politely decline an offer. When someone offers you something, いいです can mean 'No, thank you' or 'I'm fine (without it).'

glosses: to go, to move (toward a destination)
explanations: Expresses movement away from the speaker's current location toward a destination. The opposite of {来|く}る (to come). Used when the speaker is not at the destination.
When attached to the te-form of another verb (〜ていく), indicates an action continuing into the future or moving away from the speaker's perspective.
The mature ovary of a flowering plant, typically containing seeds. A formal or technical term for fruit.
Figuratively, the results or rewards of one's efforts or work.
The monetary value of goods or services, often in formal or business contexts.
General term for sweets, candies, and confections.
A count or total of things.
A prefix indicating smallness or lesser degree.
Expresses movement toward the speaker's current location or reference point. The opposite of {行|い}く (to go). Used when the speaker is at or identifies with the destination.
When attached to the te-form of another verb (〜てくる), indicates an action that has been continuing up to the present, or movement toward the speaker.

glosses: to see, to look, to watch
explanations: The general verb for visual perception. Can mean passive seeing (something enters your field of vision) or active looking (directing your attention to something).
Used for watching TV, movies, sports, or any extended visual activity. テレビを{見|み}る (to watch TV), {映画|えいが}を{見|み}る (to watch a movie).
When attached to the te-form of another verb (〜てみる), expresses trying or attempting an action to see what happens.
Milk, especially processed or prepared milk for coffee, tea, or baby formula.

glosses: I hear that; they say that
explanations: Refers to any thing without restriction; whatever one wants.
Used to introduce hearsay or reported information.
Marks the destination or target of movement. Used with verbs like {行|い}く (go), {来|く}る (come), {帰|かえ}る (return). {学校|がっこう}に{行|い}く (go to school).
Marks where something exists or is located. Used with いる/ある (to be/exist). {猫|ねこ}が{部屋|へや}にいる (The cat is in the room).
Marks specific points in time (dates, days, clock times). {三時|さんじ}に{会|あ}いましょう (Let's meet at 3 o'clock), {月曜日|げつようび}に (on Monday).
Marks the recipient of an action—the person to/for whom something is done. {友達|ともだち}に{本|ほん}をあげた (I gave a book to my friend).
Marks the purpose of going somewhere, when followed by {行|い}く/{来|く}る. Often with the masu-stem of verbs. {映画|えいが}を{見|み}に{行|い}く (go to see a movie).
Marks the agent in passive and causative constructions. {先生|せんせい}に{褒|ほ}められた (was praised by the teacher).
The standard verb for drinking liquids. Used for water, tea, coffee, alcohol, and any other beverages. Can also be used for taking medicine ({薬|くすり}を{飲|の}む).
Used for swallowing pills or capsules. Also used figuratively for accepting something difficult (e.g., {条件|じょうけん}を{飲|の}む - to swallow/accept conditions).
Describes physical size. Used for objects, spaces, animals, and anything that can be measured by size. The opposite is {小|ちい}さい (chiisai, small).
When describing voices or sounds, {大|おお}きい means loud. {大|おお}きい{声|こえ} (ookii koe) means a loud voice.
A polite or neutral way to refer to an adult male.
Used to introduce a result, action, or response based on the preceding situation.
Despite what was just mentioned; used to introduce a contrasting statement.

glosses: to cost, to be priced at
explanations: The most general verb for doing or performing actions. Often combined with nouns to create compound verbs: 勉強する (to study), 仕事する (to work), 料理する (to cook).
Used with adjective stems or nouns to mean 'make something (into)' or 'render something.' きれいにする (to make clean), 静かにする (to make quiet/be quiet).
Used for accessories like ties, watches, necklaces. ネクタイをする (to wear a tie).
Used to state prices. この本は千円する (This book costs 1000 yen).
A liquid dish, typically made by cooking vegetables, meat, or fish in stock or water.

The most common verb for eating. Used for consuming food by putting it in the mouth and swallowing. This is the neutral form without politeness implications, unlike {召|め}し{上|あ}がる (meshiagaru) which is honorific or いただく (itadaku) which is humble.
Marks the direct object of a transitive verb—the thing that receives the action. {本|ほん}を{読|よ}む (read a book), ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べる (eat rice/a meal).
Marks the space through which movement occurs with verbs of motion. {道|みち}を{歩|ある}く (walk along the road), {空|そら}を{飛|と}ぶ (fly through the sky), {橋|はし}を{渡|わた}る (cross the bridge).

Marks the starting point or place from which one leaves with verbs like {出|で}る (leave), {卒業|そつぎょう}する (graduate from). {家|いえ}を{出|で}る (leave the house), {大学|だいがく}を{卒業|そつぎょう}する (graduate from university).
To look at and comprehend written text. Used for books, newspapers, signs, emails, and any written material.
To speak written words out loud, as in reading poetry or reading to someone.
To anticipate or predict something, as in 'reading' a situation or someone's intentions. {空気|くうき}を{読|よ}む means to read the atmosphere/room.
A prefix indicating an indefinite but notable number.
A prefix used in questions about quantity.

glosses: to know, to be aware of
explanations: To have knowledge or information about something. Usually used in the form {知|し}っている to express current knowledge.
To acquire new knowledge or information. {知|し}った expresses the moment of learning something new.

glosses: to be found out, to become clear
explanations: To grasp the meaning of something. Used for understanding language, concepts, feelings, or situations.
To be able to identify or distinguish something. {違|ちが}いが{分|わ}かる (to know the difference).
For something to be discovered or determined. {結果|けっか}が{分|わ}かる (the results become known).
Low in price, not costing much money. The opposite of {高|たか}い (expensive).
To produce speech, to communicate verbally. Used for speaking a language, talking to someone, or giving a speech.
To convey information or a story to someone. {話|はなし}を{話|はな}す sounds redundant, so often {話|はなし}をする is used instead.
The general concept of time, or a period/amount of time. {時間|じかん}がない (no time), {時間|じかん}がかかる (takes time).
Used as a counter for hours. {三時間|さんじかん} (three hours).

glosses: to look forward to, to await
explanations: To stay in place or delay action until something happens or someone arrives.
To anticipate something with expectation. {楽|たの}しみに{待|ま}つ (to look forward to).

glosses: to sleep, to go to bed
to go to bed, to lie down
explanations: To be in a state of sleep. The basic verb for sleeping.
To get into bed or to lie down, whether or not one actually sleeps.
To employ something for a purpose. The general verb for using tools, devices, languages, or resources.
To expend resources. お{金|かね}を{使|つか}う (to spend money), {時間|じかん}を{使|つか}う (to spend time).
To fail to remember something, or to leave something behind unintentionally.
Not difficult to do or understand. Written as {易|やさ}しい. The opposite of {難|むずか}しい.
Having a mild or caring disposition. Written as {優|やさ}しい.
A human individual. The basic word for referring to people in general.
Used to refer to others in general. {人|ひと}に{言|い}う (to tell someone), {人|ひと}の{話|はなし} (what others say).
The nature or personality of a person. いい{人|ひと} (a good/kind person).
To form letters, characters, or symbols on a surface. Used for writing by hand, typing, or composing text. Covers both the physical act of writing and the creative act of composing.
Can also mean to draw or paint pictures, though {描|えが}く/{描|か}く is more specific for artistic drawing.

glosses: to hold, to have, to carry
explanations: To have something in one's hands or to carry something. Physical possession or holding.
To own or possess something. {車|くるま}を{持|も}っている (to have a car).
For something to remain in good condition or to endure. この{電池|でんち}は{長|なが}く{持|も}つ (this battery lasts long).
To acquire knowledge or skills from a teacher or through study. Emphasizes learning from someone.
Employment or tasks one does professionally. Also refers to specific tasks or duties.
A specific piece of work that needs to be done.

glosses: to make, to create, to produce
explanations: To bring something into existence through effort or skill. Used for cooking, crafting, building, or creating anything.
To arrange or set up something. {計画|けいかく}を{作|つく}る (to make a plan), リストを{作|つく}る (to make a list).
To come together with someone, either by arrangement or by chance. Used when meeting people face-to-face.

glosses: to hear, to listen, to ask
explanations: To perceive sound, whether intentionally or not. The sound reaches your ears.
To actively pay attention to sounds, especially music or speech. {音楽|おんがく}を{聞|き}く (to listen to music).
To ask a question or inquire about something. {道|みち}を{聞|き}く (to ask for directions).

glosses: as many as, as much as
explanations: Indicates that something applies to an additional item or person. Replaces は, が, or を. {私|わたし}も{行|い}きます (I'll go too).
Emphasizes an extreme or unexpected case. {子供|こども}でも{分|わ}かる (even a child can understand).
Used in pairs to mean 'both' (AもBも) or with negatives for 'neither.' {犬|いぬ}も{猫|ねこ}も{好|す}き (I like both dogs and cats).
Emphasizes a large quantity. {三時間|さんじかん}も{待|ま}った (waited for as long as 3 hours).
A calendar year or a period of one year. {今年|ことし} (this year), {来年|らいねん} (next year).
A person's age. {年|とし}を{取|と}る (to age), {年上|としうえ} (older).
The dark part of the day, from sunset until dawn.
Having existed for a long time or no longer new. Used for objects, buildings, traditions, etc. The opposite of {新|あたら}しい.
No longer current or fashionable. {古|ふる}い{考|かんが}え (an outdated idea).
To acquire something by paying money. The basic verb for purchasing goods or services.
Marks the ending point in time. {五時|ごじ}まで{働|はたら}く (work until 5 o'clock), {明日|あした}まで (until tomorrow).
Marks the ending point in space. {駅|えき}まで{歩|ある}く (walk to the station).
Emphasizes an extreme or unexpected extent. {彼|かれ}まで{来|き}た (even he came), {子供|こども}まで{知|し}っている (even children know).
Indicates the degree to which something extends. {泣|な}くまで{笑|わら}った (laughed until [I] cried).
Having great length in physical measurement. The opposite of {短|みじか}い.
Lasting for a considerable amount of time.
To have an opinion or belief about something. Often used with と{思|おも}う to express one's thoughts.
To have an emotional response or impression. そう{思|おも}う (I feel that way).
To anticipate or assume something. {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}ると{思|おも}う (I think it will rain).

glosses: to search for, to look for
explanations: To try to find something or someone. Also written as {捜|さが}す for searching for people.
To move from outside to inside a place. The opposite of {出|で}る (deru).
For something to be inside or included in something else.

glosses: to exist, to be (for living things)
explanations: Expresses the existence of people, animals, and other animate beings. The counterpart for inanimate objects is ある.
Indicates that a person or animal is present in a location. 部屋に猫がいる (There's a cat in the room).
Used to express having family members or pets. 子供がいる (to have children).
The current day. Used as a time expression without a particle in most cases.
A retail establishment where goods are sold. Can refer to any type of shop.
A question word asking about things, actions, or matters. One of the most fundamental question words.
An aquatic animal, or fish as food.
Having great vertical extent. Used for buildings, mountains, or anything with height. {高|たか}い{山|やま} (a tall mountain).
Costing a lot of money. The opposite of {安|やす}い (cheap).
Of great degree or intensity. {品質|ひんしつ}が{高|たか}い (high quality), {熱|ねつ}が{高|たか}い (high fever).
The day after today. Used as a time expression, typically without a particle.
Marks the location where an action takes place. {学校|がっこう}で{勉強|べんきょう}する (study at school). Compare with に, which marks location of existence.
Indicates the means, tool, or method used to do something. バスで{行|い}く (go by bus), {日本語|にほんご}で{話|はな}す (speak in Japanese).
Indicates what something is made from. {木|き}で{作|つく}る (make from wood).
Indicates the cause or reason. {病気|びょうき}で{休|やす}む (absent due to illness).
Sets a boundary or scope. {三人|さんにん}で (among three people), {一時間|いちじかん}で (within an hour).
Marks the age or circumstance at which something happens. {二十歳|はたち}で{大学|だいがく}を{卒業|そつぎょう}した (graduated from university at 20).
To engage in employment or productive activity. The most common verb for working at a job.
Marks the starting point in space or time. {東京|とうきょう}から{来|き}ました (came from Tokyo), {九時|くじ}から (from 9 o'clock).
Connects clauses to give a reason. Placed after the reason clause. {暑|あつ}いから{窓|まど}を{開|あ}けた (opened the window because it's hot).
After the te-form, indicates doing something after another action. {食|た}べてから{行|い}きます (I'll go after eating).
Indicates the source material (especially when transformed). {米|こめ}から{酒|さけ}を{作|つく}る (make sake from rice).
A route or path for traveling from one place to another.
A course of action or the proper way of doing something.
Recently made, acquired, or having come into existence. Not old or used. The opposite of {古|ふる}い.
Innovative or contemporary. {新|あたら}しい{考|かんが}え (a new/novel idea).
An enclosed space within a building, separated by walls and a door.

glosses: to return home, to go back
explanations: To go back to one's home, country, or original location. The destination is typically a place one belongs to or comes from.
The sweet, fleshy product of a tree or plant that contains seeds.
Having little length. The opposite of {長|なが}い (long).
Lasting only a brief amount of time.

glosses: to ride, to get on, to board
explanations: To get onto a vehicle or mount something. Used for trains, buses, cars, bicycles, horses, etc.
Connects nouns in a complete list. りんごとみかん (apples and oranges). Unlike や, と implies a complete enumeration.
Indicates doing something together with someone. {友達|ともだち}と{行|い}く (go with a friend).
Marks quoted speech or thoughts. 「はい」と{言|い}う (say 'yes'), いいと{思|おも}う (think it's good).
Expresses a natural or inevitable consequence. {春|はる}になると{暖|あたた}かくなる (when spring comes, it gets warm).
Shows how something appears or is named. {同|おな}じと{思|おも}う (think it's the same).

glosses: to go out, to leave, to appear
to go out, to leave, to exit
explanations: To move from inside to outside a place. The opposite of {入|はい}る (hairu).
For something to become visible or available, such as results or products.
To be present at meetings, events, or competitions.
Moving or happening at high speed. Written as {速|はや}い. Opposite of {遅|おそ}い (slow).
Happening before the expected or usual time. Written as {早|はや}い. Opposite of {遅|おそ}い (late).

The most common verb for verbal expression. Used when someone speaks words or expresses something verbally. Unlike {話|はな}す (hanasu) which emphasizes conversation or storytelling, {言|い}う focuses on the act of uttering specific words or statements.
A motor vehicle for transportation. The most common word for car in everyday Japanese.
A circular object that rotates. This is the original meaning of the kanji.
Requiring great effort, skill, or intelligence. The opposite of {易|やさ}しい (easy).
To remove clothing or footwear from one's body.
To move quickly on foot. Faster than walking ({歩|ある}く).
To accept something given by someone. The receiver is typically the speaker or someone close to the speaker.

glosses: to wake up, to get up
explanations: Used when someone wakes from sleep and gets out of bed. Can also mean to happen or occur (for events).
Used for events, incidents, or phenomena that take place. Common in news and formal contexts.
A railway vehicle powered by electricity, used for public transportation. The most common word for train in everyday Japanese.
The reproductive structure of flowering plants, often colorful and fragrant.
A tall plant with a trunk, branches, and leaves. A fundamental nature word.
The material obtained from trees, used for building and crafts.
The organ of sight.

glosses: to teach, to tell, to inform
explanations: Used when imparting knowledge or skills to someone. The person being taught is marked with に.
Used when sharing information like phone numbers, addresses, or directions with someone.
To engage in learning activities, typically involving books, courses, or formal education. A suru-verb compound.

glosses: to turn off, to switch off
explanations: To deactivate electrical devices like lights, TV, or air conditioning.
To remove writing, data, or marks.
Located at a great distance. Used for physical distance or metaphorical distance (like distant memories).
Located at a short distance. Used for physical proximity or closeness in relationships or time.
To cause something to begin. A transitive verb - you start something. The intransitive pair is {始|はじ}まる (hajimaru).
To receive something temporarily with the intention of returning it.
To pay to use something temporarily, like an apartment or car.
Describing something that moves or progresses at a low speed. The opposite of {速|はや}い (hayai, fast).
Describing something that happens after the expected or scheduled time. Also used for late hours of the day/night.
A question word asking about the identity of a person.
To give money in exchange for goods or services.
A question word asking about time. Used to inquire when something happens, happened, or will happen.
To move on foot at a normal pace. Distinguished from {走|はし}る (hashiru, to run) which is faster movement.
A question word asking about location or place.
Around 12 o'clock in the day.
The hours when the sun is up, as opposed to night.
To put on clothing worn on the upper body or full body (shirts, jackets, dresses). Different verbs are used for lower body, head, and accessories.
The later part of the day, typically from after work/school until bedtime.
A question word asking about manner, method, or condition.
The time from noon until evening, or the PM hours when telling time.
To move through water using one's limbs. Used for recreational swimming, exercise, or competitive swimming.

glosses: to give (to someone of equal/lower status)
explanations: Used when giving something to someone else. The giver is typically the speaker or someone close to the speaker. Not used when giving to superiors.
To move something to a higher position. Written as {上|あ}げる in this sense.
A question word asking to identify one item from a group of three or more. Used when choices are not directly attached to nouns.
The time from midnight until noon, or the AM hours when telling time.
Humble term used when referring to one's own mother when speaking to others outside the family.

glosses: to hang out, to spend time together
explanations: To engage in recreational activities for enjoyment. Used for children's play, games, and leisure activities.
Casual way to describe spending leisure time with friends. Very common among young people.
A question word used before a noun to ask which specific item. Always followed by a noun.
A group of people related by blood, marriage, or adoption living together.
A baked food made from flour and water. Borrowed from Portuguese 'pão'.
A young human being, or one's own offspring regardless of age.

glosses: to stop, to come to a halt
explanations: For movement to cease. An intransitive verb - the subject stops by itself.
To stay overnight at a place. Written as {泊|と}まる in this sense.
A large body of salt water. In Japanese, {海|うみ} is used for both 'sea' and 'ocean' in everyday contexts.

glosses: to be able to, to be possible
to be completed, to be made
explanations: Expresses ability or possibility. Often used with nouns or the potential meaning of verbs.
For something to come into existence or be finished.
The front part of the head, containing the eyes, nose, and mouth.
An adult female human. Also used as a prefix to indicate female gender of various things.
The opening in the face used for eating and speaking.
An adult male human. Also used as a prefix to indicate male gender of various things.

glosses: to turn on, to switch on
explanations: To activate electrical devices like lights, TV, or air conditioning.
To fasten or attach something to something else.
To cause something closed to become open. A transitive verb - you open something. The intransitive pair is {開|あ}く (aku).
To take hold of something with your hand.
To capture an image. Written as {撮|と}る for photos.
To acquire something like a reservation, license, or vacation time.
Humble term used when referring to one's own father when speaking to others outside the family.
For something to come to an end. An intransitive verb - the subject ends by itself.
To exit a vehicle. Used for trains, buses, cars, etc.
To move from a higher position to a lower one.
The part of the body at the end of the arm, used for grasping.
The entire upper limb from shoulder to hand.
Humble term used when referring to one's own older brother when speaking to others outside the family.
Humble term used when referring to one's own older sister when speaking to others outside the family.
A male sibling who is younger than oneself. Used for both one's own younger brother and others' younger brothers.
A female sibling who is younger than oneself. Used for both one's own younger sister and others' younger sisters.
The upper part of the body containing the brain, eyes, ears, nose, and mouth.
Mental capacity or intelligence.
The lower part of the leg below the ankle.
The entire lower limb from hip to foot.
Japanese green tea.
Tea in general, including other varieties.
A medical facility for treating patients.
A financial institution for deposits, loans, and money transfers.
A government facility for mail services.
A building containing books and other materials for reading and borrowing.
A public outdoor area for recreation.
The state of the atmosphere at a particular time and place.
Water falling from clouds.
Frozen precipitation falling as white flakes.
Having the color of blood or a ripe tomato.
Having the color of a clear sky.
Traditionally used for green things like traffic lights and unripe fruit.
Having the color of snow or milk.
Having the darkest color, the opposite of white.
Attracting attention or curiosity.
Causing laughter or amusement.
Having a lot to do; occupied with tasks.
Time when one has nothing to do.
Having nothing to do; idle.
To a great degree; used to intensify adjectives and verbs.
To a great degree (adverb use).
A situation that is hard to deal with (na-adjective use).
A small amount or degree.
A brief period of time.
Used to soften requests or refusals.
A small amount or degree.
A large amount or number.
Used with negative verbs to mean 'not at all'.
In casual speech, used with positive adjectives to mean 'totally'.
At all times; on every occasion.
In the typical or habitual way.
On some occasions; now and then.
Many times; regularly.
In a good manner; thoroughly.
Before the expected time; by now.
No longer; not from this point forward.
An additional amount.
Continuing to the present time.
Something has not happened up to now.
Used with negatives to express a low degree.
To stand or arrange in a line.

glosses: to rest, to take a day off
to be absent, to take time off
explanations: To relax or take a break.
To not attend school or work.
A business organization.
An institution of higher education.
A person who teaches.
A respectful title for doctors, lawyers, and experts.
A person who attends school or university.
Currency; financial resources.
A building for dwelling; one's residence.
An urban area; a populated place.
The language spoken in Japan.
Used when something rises or goes upward, such as temperature, prices, or physical movement upward.
Used when entering someone's home (stepping up from the genkan entrance area).
Describes a place or thing that is well-lit or bright.
Describes a cheerful, positive personality.
Describes a sweet taste in food or drinks.
Figuratively means being too easy on someone, having naive expectations, or being overly optimistic.
Describes pleasantly warm weather or temperature. Written 暖かい for weather/climate.
Describes a warm, kind personality or warm feelings. Can also be written 温かい for this meaning.
Used to describe hot weather or ambient temperature. For hot objects or drinks, use 熱い (atsui) with a different kanji.
Used to count machines, vehicles, and large equipment such as cars, computers, bicycles, TVs, and appliances.
The first day of the weekend. The kanji 土 means 'earth/soil' and relates to Saturn (the 'earth planet' in East Asian tradition).
The counter for two people, using an irregular reading.
Often used to mean 'the two of us/them together.'
The coldest season of the year, typically from December to February in Japan.
The first day of the work week in Japan. The kanji 月 means 'moon' and relates to the Latin 'Luna' for Monday.
The fifth month of the year. Features Golden Week, Japan's longest holiday period.
The eighth month of the year. The hottest month, featuring Obon (mid-August), a time to honor ancestors.
The season between winter and summer, typically from March to May in Japan, known for cherry blossoms.
The direction or side opposite to right.
A powered flying vehicle with fixed wings.
The counter for one person, using an irregular reading.
Also means 'alone' or 'by oneself.'
The first month of the year. In Japan, January is significant for New Year celebrations (お{正月|しょうがつ}, oshōgatsu).
A domesticated carnivorous mammal, commonly kept as a pet or working animal.
A two-wheeled vehicle propelled by pedaling. Very common transportation in Japan.
The tenth month of the year. Autumn is in full swing with pleasant weather and autumn foliage.
The eleventh month of the year. Late autumn with peak foliage in many areas and the Shichi-Go-San festival for children.
The twelfth and final month of the year. The year-end season with Christmas celebrations and preparation for New Year.
Describes food that is spicy or hot (chili-hot, not temperature-hot).
Can also mean salty, though しょっぱい (shoppai) is more common for 'salty' in eastern Japan.
A device used to protect from rain or sun. In Japanese, the same word covers both rain umbrellas and parasols.
The second day of the work week. The kanji 火 means 'fire' and relates to Mars (the 'fire planet' in East Asian tradition).
The natural movement of air.
The last day of the typical work week. The kanji 金 means 'gold/metal' and relates to Venus (the 'metal planet' in East Asian tradition).
The direction opposite to south, toward the Arctic in the Northern Hemisphere.
A general-purpose counter used for small, compact objects like fruits, eggs, boxes, and other small items.
The ninth month of the year. The new school term resumes after summer vacation. Features the autumn equinox.
Describes a place or thing that lacks light, is dimly lit, or dark in color.
Describes a gloomy mood or depressed personality.
A facility where aircraft take off and land, with terminals for passengers.
Used when giving or following directions to turn at a corner or intersection. Takes the particle を or で to mark the location of the turn.
Describes something that bends or is curved, such as a road or an object.
Used to count flat, thin objects such as paper, plates, shirts, tickets, photos, CDs, and sliced items.
Eyeglasses worn to correct vision or for protection.
The direction opposite to north, where the sun is at midday in the Northern Hemisphere.
The fourth day of the work week. The kanji 木 means 'tree/wood' and relates to Jupiter (the 'wood planet' in East Asian tradition).
The interior part of something.
The central position between two points.
Used when someone cries or sheds tears, whether from sadness, pain, joy, or other strong emotions.
The second day of the weekend and traditionally a day of rest. The kanji 日 means 'sun,' similar to how 'Sunday' derives from 'Sun day' in English.
The second month of the year and the shortest month. Features Setsubun (節分) and Valentine's Day.
A counter used to count people. Note: 1 person and 2 people use different readings (ひとり, ふたり), but 3 and above use 〜人 (〜にん).
The direction where the sun sets.
The sixth month of the year. Known as the rainy season (梅雨, tsuyu) in most of Japan.
A small flat case for carrying money, cards, and other small items.
Used to describe cold weather or ambient temperature. For cold objects or food, use 冷たい (tsumetai) instead.
The third month of the year. In Japan, this is graduation season and the end of the fiscal/school year.
Used to count bound publications such as books, magazines, notebooks, and other bound volumes.
The seventh month of the year. The rainy season ends and summer begins in earnest. Features Tanabata (July 7th).
The fourth month of the year. In Japan, April marks the beginning of the school year and fiscal year.

The basic verb for dying, used of people and animals. Plants wither rather than die: 枯れる is the normal verb for them. When speaking about people, 亡くなる is usually preferred as the gentler, more respectful word.
The position lower than something else or the lower surface of something.
Can indicate someone younger or lower in status.
The exterior or outdoor area; the opposite of inside.
The middle day of the work week. The kanji 水 means 'water' and relates to Mercury (the 'water planet' in East Asian tradition).

glosses: to live, to reside, to dwell
explanations: Used to express where someone lives or resides. Takes the particle に to mark the location of residence.
Describes pleasantly cool weather or temperature, especially refreshing coolness in summer or after hot weather.
A written message sent to someone, typically by mail.
A door, especially a traditional Japanese sliding door. Often used in compounds.
A device for telling time, including wall clocks, watches, and other timepieces.

glosses: to stop, to halt, to turn off
explanations: Used when stopping or halting something. This is a transitive verb—you stop something.
Used when parking a vehicle.
A warm-blooded vertebrate with feathers and wings. Also used as a general term for poultry.
In food contexts, often refers to chicken meat.
Used when someone or something arrives at a destination. This is the standard verb for expressing arrival at a place. Takes the particle に to mark the destination.
Describes cold objects, drinks, or things you can touch. Different from 寒い (samui), which describes cold weather.
Figuratively describes a person who is cold, unfriendly, or indifferent.
The position higher than something else or the upper surface of something.
Can indicate someone older or higher in status.
The position at the back of someone or something; the opposite of the front.
Used for singing songs, whether casually, in karaoke, or professionally.
Used when someone laughs, from a light chuckle to hearty laughter.
Can also mean to smile, though 微笑む (hohoemu) is more specifically 'to smile.'
A sweet confection, typically hard candy made from sugar. Different from {雨|あめ} (rain), which has the same pronunciation.
Used to count long, thin objects such as pencils, bottles, umbrellas, bananas, roads, and train lines.
For something to move from a closed to open position on its own. The intransitive pair of {開|あ}ける.
Describes something with considerable thickness or depth. The opposite of {薄|うす}い (thin). Used for books, walls, slices, etc. Different from {暑|あつ}い (hot weather) and {熱|あつ}い (hot to touch).
A covering for the head, worn for protection from sun or cold, or as a fashion accessory.
Describes something that doesn't work, is broken, or is of poor quality. Also used when efforts fail.
Used to express prohibition or that something shouldn't be done. Very direct way to say 'no' or 'you can't do that.'
Garments worn on the body. A general term for articles of clothing.
Describes a state of good health and vitality. Commonly used in greetings to ask how someone is doing.
Describes someone who is full of energy and vigor.
The number five. A central number in Japanese culture, found in many traditional concepts. Straightforward to use with most counters.
The number eight. Considered a lucky number in Japanese culture because the kanji {八|はち} widens at the bottom, symbolizing growing prosperity. Consistent in most counter combinations.
To wear items on the lower body and feet—shoes, pants, skirts, socks. Different from {着|き}る which is for upper body clothing.

glosses: to clear up, to become sunny
explanations: Describes weather becoming clear or sunny, with clouds disappearing. Used for sky and weather conditions.
Describes something that has a large extent or area. The opposite of {狭|せま}い (narrow). Used for rooms, roads, areas, etc.

The number one. This is the most basic counting number in Japanese. When counting objects, いち is often combined with counters like {一|いっ}つ (hitotsu), {一|いっ}{個|こ} (ikko), or {一|いち}{人|にん} (ichinin), though the pronunciation may change depending on the counter.
A piece of furniture for sitting, typically with a back and four legs. Can refer to any type of chair.
The number ten. A base number in Japanese counting, used to form larger numbers (11 = じゅういち, 20 = にじゅう, etc.). Very consistent in pronunciation across most combinations.
Describes the amount of time required to do something. Used with time expressions.
Describes the amount of money required for something. Used with money/cost expressions.
Material made from wood pulp, used for writing, printing, and wrapping. A basic everyday item.
Describes something that is not difficult to do or understand. The opposite of {難|むずか}しい (difficult).
Can also describe something that is simple and not elaborate.
Describes something undergoing change by itself (intransitive). The transitive counterpart is {変|か}える (to change something).
Describes something or someone that is aesthetically pleasing. Often used for scenery, flowers, people (especially women), and objects.
Describes something free of dirt or mess. Used for rooms, clothes, hands, etc.
The current month; the month we are in now. Used to talk about events or plans within the present month.
The current week; the week we are in now. Used to talk about events or plans within the present week.
The current year; the year we are in now. Used to talk about events, plans, or states within the present year.
To give something to the speaker or someone close to the speaker. Shows the giver's viewpoint and often implies gratitude from the receiver.
Footwear worn to protect and comfort the feet. A general term for shoes of all types.
Cloth coverings for the feet, usually worn inside shoes. Literally means 'under shoes.'
The year before this one; the previous year. Used to refer to events or states in the year that just passed.
The number nine. Like four, nine has two readings: きゅう and く. きゅう is more common because く sounds like {苦|く} (suffering), making it somewhat inauspicious.
Each and every day; daily. Used to express something that happens or is done on a daily basis. Can function as both a noun and an adverb.
Each and every week; weekly. Used to express something that happens on a weekly basis. Functions as both a noun and an adverb.
Each and every year; annually. Used to express something that happens on a yearly basis. Functions as both a noun and an adverb.
Each and every month; monthly. Used to express something that happens on a monthly basis. Functions as both a noun and an adverb.
Describes food or drink that tastes bad. The opposite of おいしい (delicious). Use with caution as it can be rude if directed at someone's cooking.
Can also describe a situation that is problematic, inconvenient, or in bad shape. This sense is common in casual conversation.
The number seven. Like four, seven has two readings: なな and しち. なな is more commonly used in everyday counting because しち can be confused with いち (one) or し (four) when spoken.

glosses: to be repaired, to be fixed
explanations: Describes something being restored to working condition (intransitive). The transitive pair is {直|なお}す (to fix/repair).
Describes recovering from illness or injury. Written as {治|なお}る for this meaning.
The number two. A fundamental counting number used throughout Japanese. Like other numbers, に combines with various counters and may change pronunciation in some combinations.
To commit something to memory, to memorize. The opposite of {忘|わす}れる (to forget).
To acquire a skill or knowledge, often through practice or experience.
Describes food or drink that tastes good. One of the most common and useful adjectives for expressing positive opinions about food. Used in everyday conversation.
Colloquially used to describe a situation that is favorable or beneficial.
To dispatch or transmit something to someone else. Used for letters, packages, emails, etc.
To accompany someone who is leaving, or to escort them partway.
Vibrations that travel through air or other media and can be heard. Includes all kinds of sounds, from music to everyday noises.
The month after this one; the coming month. Used to refer to future events or plans in the month that follows the current one.
The year after this one; the coming year. Used to refer to future events or plans in the year that follows the current one.
The week after this one; the coming week. Used to refer to future events or plans in the week that follows the current one.
The number six. A straightforward number in Japanese with consistent pronunciation in most contexts.
The number three. An important number in Japanese culture, appearing in many expressions and traditions. Combines with counters in straightforward ways.
Describes something with limited space or area. The opposite of {広|ひろ}い (wide, spacious). Used for rooms, roads, areas, etc.
The month before this one; the previous month. Used to refer to events or states in the month that just passed.
The week before this one; the previous week. Used to refer to events or states in the week that just passed.
An image captured by a camera. One of the most common words for talking about pictures.
Describes a place, environment, or person that makes little or no noise. The opposite of うるさい (noisy).
Can also describe a tranquil atmosphere or a person with a calm demeanor.

glosses: to sit down, to take a seat
explanations: To lower oneself into a seated position. Can be on a chair, on the floor, or any surface.

glosses: to be built, to be located
explanations: To rise to an upright position on one's feet. The opposite of {座|すわ}る (to sit).
Can describe buildings or structures being in a location.
Describes movement through the air, as done by birds, planes, insects, etc.
Describes leaping into the air or jumping over something.
To capture an image or video using a camera. Different kanji from {取|と}る (to take/grab).
To fasten, attach, or apply something to something else. The transitive pair of {付|つ}く (to stick to).
To switch on electrical devices. Written as {点|つ}ける for this meaning. Opposite of {消|け}す (to turn off).
A piece of furniture with a flat surface for writing, reading, or working. Common in offices, schools, and homes.
Describes something that makes too much noise or is unpleasantly loud. Can refer to sounds, people, or environments.
Can describe something or someone that is pestering, nagging, or being a nuisance. Often used to tell someone to be quiet or stop bothering you.
Describes something that is not difficult. Written as {易|やさ}しい. Similar to {簡単|かんたん}.
Describes a person who is kind-hearted, gentle, or tender. Written as {優|やさ}しい.
To call out to someone to get their attention, or to summon someone.
To ask someone to come to an event or gathering.
To refer to someone or something by a particular name.
The number four. This reading (よん) is more commonly used in modern Japanese than し because し sounds like {死|し} (death). よん is generally preferred when counting and in most compound numbers.
Involving or causing risk of harm or injury.
Uncertain or unstable, potentially leading to a bad outcome.
The act of learning or acquiring knowledge through reading, practice, or instruction. One of the most common words in Japanese education.
In business contexts, {勉強|べんきょう}する can mean to give a discount or lower the price.
A condition that impairs normal physical or mental functions. Can range from minor to serious.
Indicates that something is satisfactory or that there is no problem.
Indicates that someone or something is safe and not in danger.
A hinged or sliding barrier at an entrance. Often used for Western-style doors.
The official currency of Japan. Symbol: ¥.
A round shape. The kanji literally means 'round/circle'.
A watercraft used for transportation on water. Includes small boats and large ships.
Steamed white rice, the staple food of Japan. Served with most Japanese meals.
More broadly refers to a meal or food in general. Often used to mean breakfast, lunch, or dinner.
Milk from a cow. The standard term for milk as a beverage or cooking ingredient.
The hard structures in the mouth used for biting and chewing. Used for dental care, physical descriptions, and tooth-related expressions.
The number one hundred.
A scheduled period of teaching or learning at a school or educational institution. Refers to the teaching session itself, not the subject or room.
A set of steps leading from one floor or level to another.
Feeling or expressing sorrow or unhappiness.
The physical body of a person or animal. Used when talking about health, physical conditions, or body-related topics.
Often used idiomatically to refer to one's health or physical well-being, as in {体|からだ}に{気|き}をつける (take care of your health).
Not heavy, easy to lift or carry. The opposite of {重|おも}い (heavy).
Can describe something that is not serious or intense, like a light meal or minor injury.
Physical harm or damage to the body from an accident or attack.
Not clean, covered with dirt or stains. Can describe physical dirtiness.
Can describe behavior that is morally dirty or dishonest.
The beverage made from roasted coffee beans. Very popular in Japan both hot and iced.
The correct response to a question or problem. Used in academic contexts for test answers and solutions.
A response to a question or inquiry in general conversation.
The part of the body connecting the head to the shoulders. Used for physical descriptions and neck-related expressions.
Colloquially, {首|くび}になる means to be fired from a job. This usage comes from the old practice of beheading.
A substance used to treat illness or maintain health.
A room in a school or educational institution where classes are taught. The physical space where learning takes place.
Can also refer to a learning class or course, as in {料理|りょうり}{教室|きょうしつ} (cooking class) or {英語|えいご}{教室|きょうしつ} (English class).
The number ten thousand. A key unit in Japanese counting, as large numbers are grouped by 万 (ten thousands) rather than thousands.

glosses: first, first of all, to begin with
for now, for the time being
explanations: Used to indicate the first action in a sequence or to introduce the first point.
Can indicate doing something as a first step before proceeding.
A question to be answered or a problem to be solved, typically in an academic context such as on exams or homework.
A matter that needs to be addressed or solved, a difficulty or concern.

glosses: more, further, to a greater degree
explanations: Used to express a greater quantity, degree, or extent than the current state.
A male child in relation to their parents. This is the neutral/humble form used when referring to one's own son.
One's parent's sister. Can also refer to the wife of one's parent's brother (aunt by marriage).
Used to address or refer to a middle-aged woman who is not related to you. Similar to 'ma'am' in English, though can sound less formal.
A tub filled with hot water for bathing. In Japan, the bath is for soaking after washing outside the tub.
The act of taking a bath, an important daily ritual in Japanese culture.
One's parent's brother. Can also refer to the husband of one's parent's sister (uncle by marriage).
Used to address or refer to a middle-aged man who is not related to you. Similar to 'mister' or 'sir' in English.
Having great weight, difficult to lift or carry. The opposite of {軽|かる}い (light).
Can describe something serious or severe, like a serious illness or heavy responsibility.
The front part of the body between the chest and hips. Most commonly used when talking about hunger or stomach-related feelings.
Refers to both parents together. This is a neutral term that can be used when talking about one's own parents or someone else's parents.
To move something to a lower position or to decrease something like price or temperature.
To hang or carry something, often from the shoulder or hand.
To bring one's hand or body into contact with something. The object touched is marked with に.
The number one thousand.
The rear surface of the human body from the shoulders to the waist. Used for physical descriptions and back-related expressions.
Work assigned by a teacher to be done outside of class. A fundamental part of Japanese education.
Can also refer to something left undone that needs to be addressed, like 'homework' from a meeting or project.
The humble or formal term for one's own grandmother. Used when speaking about your grandmother to others in polite contexts.
Without delay or very shortly after.
With little effort or difficulty.
Very close in distance.
Indicates likelihood or probability. Suggests the speaker thinks something is likely but isn't certain.
Describes something that gives pleasure or enjoyment.
A room containing a toilet. The most common word for toilet/restroom in modern Japanese.
The one that comes immediately after the current one in a sequence.
Having great physical power or force.
Able to withstand difficult conditions or stress.
Physical activity done for health or fitness. Includes both casual exercise and organized sports.
Can also refer to a social or political movement or campaign for a cause.
Feeling or showing pleasure or contentment. Often used when something good happens to you.
Having lived or existed for a short time. Used for people and sometimes animals.
Can also describe someone who acts or looks young, or is inexperienced.
Lacking physical strength or power.
Being vulnerable to or not skilled at something.
The sensation perceived by the tongue when eating or drinking something. Can refer to sweet, salty, sour, bitter, or umami flavors.
Used for cleaning something with water, typically hands, dishes, clothes, or a car. The object being washed takes the particle を.
The day that comes after tomorrow. Part of the sequence: きょう (today) → あした (tomorrow) → あさって (day after tomorrow).
A particular position or area. Can refer to physical locations or more abstract positions.
Used to indicate an approximate amount, time, or degree. Not exact but close enough.
For the most part, in general terms.
Describes a slow, progressive change over time. Things changing step by step rather than suddenly.
To leave one's home or current location to go somewhere. Implies going out for a purpose like shopping, work, or leisure.
Used to ask for the reason or cause of something. Slightly more casual than なぜ.
Used to ask about the method or way to do something.
To pick one option from multiple possibilities. Used for selecting items, making decisions, or choosing people for positions.
For something to commence or start happening. An intransitive verb describing the beginning of an event, action, or state.
Essential or required for a purpose. Can function as a na-adjective or noun.
A visual property of objects resulting from the light they reflect. Used to describe the hue of things like clothes, objects, or nature.
A large, solid piece of stone, bigger than a stone ({石|いし}) but part of the natural landscape. Often found in mountains, by the sea, or in rivers.
The activity of going to stores to buy things. Often used with the verb する to form 'to go shopping'.
To use the mind to process information, reflect on something, or come up with ideas. More deliberate than {思|おも}う which is more about feeling or believing.

Describes something or someone that is endearingly attractive, charming, or lovable. One of the most commonly used adjectives in Japanese, especially when describing children, animals, or aesthetically pleasing items.
The day before today. One of the most basic time expressions in Japanese.

glosses: to be troubled, to be in difficulty
to be troubled, to have difficulty
explanations: To be in a difficult situation, to face a problem, or to not know what to do. Expresses distress or being at a loss.
Describes something that causes fear or is frightening. Can also describe the feeling of being scared.
Someone who visits a home or is invited somewhere. A person being hosted.
Someone who buys goods or services from a business.
In a direct line without curves or turns. Can describe physical direction or going somewhere without detours.
Describing a person's character as straightforward and honest.
To restore something broken to working condition.
To fix errors or mistakes in writing, behavior, etc.
The amount of money required to buy something. The monetary value assigned to goods or services.
Feeling the need or desire to sleep. The state of being tired and wanting to sleep.
Something that seems wrong, unusual, or not quite right. Often implies suspicion that something is amiss.
Something that makes you laugh or smile. Used when something is humorous or comical.

glosses: to get angry, to be angry
explanations: To experience or display anger. Can be directed at someone (に) or about something (を/に).
To express anger at someone, often a child or subordinate, in order to correct their behavior.
The day that was two days ago. Part of the sequence: おととい (day before yesterday) → きのう (yesterday) → きょう (today).
The money returned to you when you pay more than the price of something. The お is an honorific prefix that is typically included.
The machine used to process payments in stores, or the checkout area where payments are made. Short for 'register'.
Refers to the recent past, from a few days to several weeks ago, up to the present. Can function as a noun or adverb.
The first one in a sequence, or the starting point of something. Can function as a noun or adverbial expression.
A flat, typically round container used for serving or eating food. Can refer to the dish itself or the food served on it.
A sweet crystalline substance obtained from sugarcane or sugar beets, used as a sweetener in food and drinks.
A piece of land surrounded by water. Japan itself is an island nation (島国) composed of many islands.
A white crystalline substance (sodium chloride) used for seasoning and preserving food. An essential cooking ingredient.
Something asked to get information or clarification. Used with the verb する to mean 'to ask a question'.
Free from error, conforming to fact or truth. Also means morally right or proper.

glosses: to help, to rescue, to save
explanations: To give assistance to someone in need or danger. Can mean to help with a task or to rescue from a dangerous situation.
A person who works in a store, helping customers and handling sales. Can refer to any retail employee.
To give assistance with a task or activity. Less urgent than {助|たす}ける, used for everyday help with chores or work.
To come into existence through birth. Used for people, animals, and figuratively for ideas or creations coming into being.
To exchange goods or services for money. The item being sold takes the particle を, and the buyer (if mentioned) takes に.
Of low quality, not good, or unsatisfactory.
Used colloquially to apologize or express regret.
To discontinue an action or activity.
To give up a job, membership, or habit permanently.
Not quickly. Taking one's time to do something.
In a relaxed manner without hurrying.
Without interruption, for a long period of time. Indicates something happening or continuing throughout.
Used for emphasis in comparisons to indicate a significant degree of difference.
A polite demonstrative for a direction or location far from both speaker and listener.
A polite way to refer to a third party.
The space or gap between two things or people.
A period of time during which something happens.
The relationship or connection between parties.
A demonstrative adjective used before nouns to indicate something far from both speaker and listener.
Used as a filler word when hesitating or getting someone's attention.
A demonstrative pronoun referring to something far from both the speaker and listener.
An expression of gratitude. Casual form of ありがとうございます.
A demonstrative pronoun for a place far from both speaker and listener.
Indicates that something happens after another event.
At a future time, not now.
A counter for seconds of time.
Describes the color brown. The word literally contains {茶|ちゃ} (tea), referring to the brown color of tea.
An area close to a reference point. As a noun, refers to the surrounding area.
Approximately or almost a certain amount.
A conjunction indicating cause and effect. Casual form of ですから.
A casual conjunction used to contrast or introduce an exception. Used at the beginning of sentences.
When attached to nouns, means 'even' (e.g., {子供|こども}でも - even a child).
The polite form of だから, used to indicate cause and effect in formal speech.
Used to ask about a choice between two options. The polite form of どっち.
A polite way to ask where someone is from or where they are going.
A polite way to ask who someone is, often used in business contexts.
A counter for minutes of time. The reading changes between ふん and ぷん depending on the preceding number.
A set phrase said after finishing a meal to express gratitude. Literally related to {馳走|ちそう} meaning 'feast' or 'to run around (preparing food).'
The number fifty. Formed by combining {五|ご} (five) and {十|じゅう} (ten), literally meaning 'five tens.'
A direct apology, often used when you have done something wrong or caused someone trouble.

glosses: nice to meet you, how do you do
explanations: A greeting used when meeting someone for the first time. Literally means 'for the first time.'
A duration of thirty minutes.
The joint in the middle of the arm where it bends.
A counter for small to medium-sized animals such as fish, insects, cats, dogs, etc. Not used for birds or rabbits.
The joint in the middle of the leg.
The upper part of the legs when sitting, where someone might sit or place things.
A duration of sixty minutes. The basic unit for counting hours of duration.
A period of 24 hours or one full day.
Throughout an entire day from morning to night.
Used to ask about the price or cost of something.
In the pattern いくら〜ても, means 'no matter how much.'
Used to ask about quantity, especially for items counted with the general counter つ.
Used to ask about someone's age, particularly for children or in casual contexts.
Refers to the current time or moment.
Can indicate something that just happened or is about to happen.
A set phrase said before eating to express gratitude for the food. Literally means 'I humbly receive.'
The number fifteen. Formed by combining {十|じゅう} (ten) and {五|ご} (five).
The number eighteen. Formed by combining {十|じゅう} (ten) and {八|はち} (eight).
The number eleven. Formed by combining {十|じゅう} (ten) and {一|いち} (one).
The number nineteen. Formed by combining {十|じゅう} (ten) and {九|きゅう} (nine). Can also be read as じゅうく.
The number seventeen. Formed by combining {十|じゅう} (ten) and {七|なな} (seven). Can also be read as じゅうしち.
The number twelve. Formed by combining {十|じゅう} (ten) and {二|に} (two).
The number sixteen. Formed by combining {十|じゅう} (ten) and {六|ろく} (six).

A polite expression used when making a request or asking someone to do something.

glosses: and so, because of that, therefore
explanations: A conjunction indicating that something happens as a result of what was previously mentioned.
Used to prompt someone to continue their story or explanation.

Used to add items to a list or add information.

The time period in the late afternoon when the sun begins to set, roughly from 4-7 PM.

An alcoholic beverage made from fermented grains. From Dutch/German 'bier.'
The room in a house where food is prepared and cooked.
A traditional Japanese seasoning made from fermented soybeans. Used in soups, sauces, and marinades.
A deep cooking vessel with handles, used for boiling, stewing, etc.
A type of Japanese dish where ingredients are cooked together in a pot at the table.
A round citrus fruit with orange skin. From English 'orange.'
The color orange, between red and yellow.
A general term for alcoholic beverages. The お is an honorific prefix.
Specifically refers to nihonshu, the traditional Japanese rice-based alcoholic drink.
An appliance for keeping food cold and fresh.

A student, typically at middle school or high school level.

Used when asking someone to do something or take care of something.

An expression telling someone to be careful or take care. Often used when someone is leaving. Comes from {気|き}をつける (to pay attention, to be careful).

glosses: to take out, to bring out
explanations: To remove something from inside a container or place and bring it outside or into view.
To formally present documents, homework, or applications to someone in authority.
To mail or send correspondence.

Used as a response to indicate understanding or acknowledgment.

For something to remain unused or inactive.

Exclamation expressing sudden realization, recognition, or remembering something.

explanations: Refers to something distant from both speaker and listener, or something previously mentioned. Part of the ko-so-a-do demonstrative system.

A student attending high school (grades 10-12 in Japan, typically ages 15-18).
A city as an administrative division in Japan, larger than a town ({町|まち}) but smaller than a prefecture ({県|けん}).
Used as a suffix attached to city names.
A written symbol representing a sound or meaning, including hiragana, katakana, kanji, and letters from other writing systems.

explanations: Refers to something near the listener or something just mentioned in conversation. Part of the ko-so-a-do demonstrative system.

Many different places throughout an area.

Term of address used by wives when speaking to their husbands.

Currency used for transactions. The everyday word for money.

A greeting used during the day, from late morning to early evening.

In Japanese, traffic lights that show 'go' are called 青 even though they appear green.

Of considerable size; prenominal adjective form.

Used to emphasize an apology or greeting.
