explanations: A brown seaweed widely used in Japanese cuisine, especially in miso soup and salads.
An aesthetic concept valuing beauty found in imperfection, simplicity, and the transient nature of things. One half of the well-known pair {侘|わ}び{寂|さ}び (wabi-sabi).
A gift given by the hosts to guests at a wedding reception or other formal celebration as a token of thanks for attending.
Prearranged plans or procedures for carrying out something. Implies that steps have been thought out and coordinated in advance.
The quality of being convenient or practical. Often used in the phrase {便宜上|べんぎじょう} (for convenience's sake).
Giving someone special treatment or making an exception for their benefit.

glosses: loss of strength, going limp, relaxing muscles
explanations: The state of losing physical tension or strength, either intentionally (as in relaxation) or involuntarily (from shock, exhaustion, or disappointment).
A relaxed, understated quality, especially in comedy or creative works.
The main communal room in a traditional Japanese house where the family gathers to eat, relax, and watch TV. Typically features tatami flooring and a low table.
Used figuratively to refer to average families or the viewing public, especially in TV broadcasting contexts.
The act of stating one's own name, title, or identity, especially formally or dramatically.
Volunteering or declaring oneself as a candidate, participant, or claimant.

glosses: pilgrimage (anime/media), visiting real-life locations from fictional works
explanations: A journey to visit a series of temples, shrines, or other sacred places, often following an established route.
In modern usage, visiting real-world locations that appeared in anime, manga, films, or other media. Also called {聖地|せいち}{巡礼|じゅんれい}.

glosses: visiting a grave, paying respects at a grave
explanations: The practice of visiting the grave of a deceased family member or friend to clean the grave, offer flowers and incense, and pray.

glosses: glutinous rice, sticky rice, mochi rice
explanations: A variety of short-grain rice that becomes very sticky when cooked. Used to make mochi and other traditional Japanese dishes.
Attached to the masu-stem of a verb to mean 'way of doing.' Functions as a suffix in this usage.
A polite way to refer to a person. More respectful than 人.
To carry something and come with it to the speaker's location. A compound of 持つ (to hold) + くる (to come).

glosses: to arrange flowers, to do ikebana
explanations: To arrange cut flowers or branches in a vase or container, especially in the traditional Japanese art of flower arrangement (生け花).
Leaves growing on or fallen from a tree. Often evokes a literary or seasonal image.

glosses: sitting comfort, how something feels to sit on
sitting comfort, how comfortable something is to sit on
explanations: The feel or comfort level of something when sitting on it. Formed from 座る (to sit) + 心地 (feeling, comfort).

glosses: to rise, to go up, to ascend
explanations: For smoke, steam, mist, or similar things to rise upward. Often used for visual phenomena that drift or billow upward.
The act of entering a restricted or prohibited area. Most commonly seen in prohibition signs and warnings.
Describes a mind, thinking, or logic that is sharp, clear, and well-organized. Often used to praise someone's intellectual clarity.
A place for cooking, especially a shared or communal cooking facility at a campsite, dormitory, or similar setting. Less commonly used for home kitchens, where 台所 or キッチン are preferred.
One of several causes or contributing factors. Implies that the cause mentioned is not the only one, but one among multiple factors.
Employment status where someone works less than full-time or on a temporary basis, without being a permanent staff member. Often used for lecturers, public employees, and similar positions.
A person appointed by law or by a court to manage the affairs of someone who cannot manage them on their own, such as a minor or a person with diminished capacity.

glosses: unopened, sealed, still in original packaging
explanations: Describes a product or container that has not been opened from its original sealed state.

glosses: resting one's chin in one's hand
resting one's chin in one's hand, chin-in-hand
explanations: The posture of propping one's chin or cheek on one's hand, typically with the elbow on a table. Can suggest boredom, deep thought, or idle relaxation.

glosses: to wear out, to go flat, to lose firmness
explanations: For something cushioned or springy to lose its resilience or shape through use and age — pillows becoming flat, springs going soft, cushions losing their bounce.
An imposing, authoritative presence that commands respect. A quality of noble bearing or solemn grandeur.
The quality of being convenient or easily accessible. Often used when evaluating locations, services, or systems.
Entrusting a matter completely to someone else's judgment or discretion, without conditions or reservations.
The outward behavior or demeanor that reveals or conceals one's true feelings or intentions.
A subtle sign or indication of something, especially an attitude or feeling that shows through one's behavior.
A feeling of being fed up with or thoroughly tired of something, leading to a desire to avoid it.

A meeting where people come together to see each other's faces and get acquainted, especially for the first time. Often used for formal or semi-formal occasions like project kickoffs, family introductions, or pre-wedding meetings.

glosses: border, point of entry (for control measures)
explanations: The point where water meets land — the edge of a lake, river, or sea.
Figuratively, the point at which something is stopped before it enters or spreads further. Used especially for border control, infection prevention, and crisis management.

glosses: putting in a good word, recommendation
putting in a good word, recommendation, intercession
explanations: Speaking favorably on someone's behalf to a person of influence, in order to help them gain a favorable outcome.
One's sense of who they are — the qualities, beliefs, and values that define a person or group and distinguish them from others.
The third-born son in a family.
The third-born daughter in a family.
A woman trained in the art of ninjutsu. In popular culture, depicted as a female spy or warrior who uses stealth and cunning.
Feeling drowsy and wanting to sleep. A variant of {眠|ねむ}い with the same meaning.
A spouse's parent — either the father-in-law or mother-in-law.
A parent who is not biologically related but has a parental role through remarriage.
The physical or wireless connection used to access the internet. Refers to both the infrastructure (fiber, cable, etc.) and the connection itself.
Outdoor leisure activities such as camping, hiking, and fishing. Also used as a modifier to describe products or lifestyles oriented toward outdoor recreation.
The ease or means of reaching a particular location, especially by public transportation. Commonly used when describing how convenient it is to get to a station, building, or area.
Connecting to or using a computer system, website, or digital resource.
The pitch or stress pattern in spoken language. In Japanese linguistics, this refers specifically to pitch accent.
A feature that adds contrast, emphasis, or visual interest to something, such as in fashion, interior design, or cooking.
A workspace used by an artist, painter, sculptor, or designer for creating their work. From French "atelier."
A suggestion or recommendation offered to someone about what they should do. Used as a suru-verb when giving advice.
A spoken or broadcast announcement, especially over a public address system such as at train stations, airports, or events.
Actively presenting or emphasizing one's strengths, a product's merits, or a cause to gain attention or support. Often used in job-hunting, marketing, and self-introduction contexts.
A method or strategy for dealing with a problem, task, or goal.
The act of reaching out to or making advances toward a person, often in romantic or business contexts.

A colloquial term for a foolish or stupid person. Strongly associated with the Kansai region, where it is used casually among friends with less bite than バカ. However, in the Kanto region, アホ can sound harsher than バカ.
A creamy green fruit commonly eaten in salads, sushi, and various dishes. Very popular in Japanese cuisine, especially in sushi rolls and as a topping.
A coined Japanese-English term (from "around thirty") referring to people approximately 25 to 34 years old, typically used for women discussing life stages, career, and marriage.
A coined Japanese-English term (from "around forty") referring to people approximately 35 to 44 years old. Used in discussions about lifestyle, career advancement, and aging.
A sound or signal designed to wake someone up or to warn of something. Commonly refers to alarm clocks or phone alarms.
A large indoor venue used for concerts, sporting events, and other performances. Also refers specifically to the floor-level seating area closest to the stage at a concert.
The Latin/Roman alphabet (A-Z). In Japanese contexts, this specifically means the 26 letters of the English alphabet, as distinct from hiragana, katakana, and kanji.
A large, edible sea snail prized in Japanese cuisine for its firm, chewy texture. Considered a luxury ingredient.
A collection of historical documents, records, or digital files preserved for reference. Also used as a suru-verb meaning to archive or store something for future access.
A creative professional, especially a musician, singer, or performing artist. In Japanese, this term is used more broadly than in English and is the default way to refer to musicians and singers.

Visual or creative art in a broad sense. Used as a trendy, modern alternative to the traditional Japanese word {芸術|げいじゅつ}, especially in contexts related to contemporary art, design, and creative culture.
The edible seed of the almond tree, commonly eaten as a snack, used in cooking and baking, or processed into almond milk.
Individual eggs of salmon, typically marinated in soy sauce or salt. A popular sushi topping and rice bowl ingredient in Japanese cuisine.

glosses: top recommendation, number-one pick, best choice
explanations: Something or someone that one recommends above all others. Literally "number one push." Used in casual conversation, marketing, and fan culture.
A picture or drawing, especially one created for a publication, website, or social media. In Japanese, this covers a broad range from professional illustrations to casual sketches and digital art.
A small, oily fish commonly found in Japanese coastal waters. An affordable and nutritious staple of Japanese cuisine, eaten fresh, dried, or processed.
Describes food or products that can be prepared quickly with minimal effort, typically by just adding hot water. Also used figuratively to mean something done without proper effort or depth.

glosses: inbound tourism, foreign tourists visiting Japan
explanations: Tourism from abroad into Japan, or the foreign tourists themselves. A buzzword in Japanese business and media, especially since the tourism boom of the 2010s.
A powerful effect or impression on someone. Used to describe things that are memorable, striking, or attention-grabbing.
The small, flat, overlapping plates that cover the skin of fish and reptiles.
A concentrated substance obtained by extracting the essential components from a plant, food, or other material. Common in cooking, health products, and cosmetics.
A short piece of writing on a personal topic, expressing the author's thoughts, experiences, or observations. In Japanese, this refers to the literary essay genre rather than academic papers.
A protective garment worn over the front of one's clothes when cooking, cleaning, or doing other messy tasks.
A defined space or region, used for geographical zones, designated sections, or coverage ranges.

glosses: to escalate, to intensify, to worsen
explanations: A situation, conflict, or problem gradually becomes more serious or intense.
Factual or scientific basis for a claim or decision. Widely used in business and medical contexts as a loanword from English.
A short, memorable account or story from someone's experience.
One part of a serialized TV show, podcast, or other media.
Someone who does something as a hobby or without professional training, as opposed to a professional.
A general term for oil, used for cooking oils, automotive oils, skincare oils, and other liquid fats or lubricants.
The male sex of an animal. Also used for plugs or connectors in technical contexts.
The state of something being switched off or not active.
A period of rest from work, or the time outside a sport's regular season.
A reduction in price, commonly expressed as a percentage.
The act of producing or expressing information, ideas, or results. Widely used in business and education to mean actively creating or communicating rather than passively receiving.
The act of taking in or receiving information, knowledge, or data. In education and self-improvement contexts, refers to passive learning activities like reading and listening.
The dark material used to surface roads, or a road surface made of this material.
A warning or notification signal, often from a device, system, or authority. Used for emergency alerts, system notifications, and general warnings.
The act of signing up or registering for a competition, event, or job. Also refers to the registration itself.
A sentence-ending particle used when trying to recall something or confirm a vague memory. Conveys the feeling of 'I think it was... but I'm not sure.'
A casual sentence-ending particle expressing possibility or uncertainty. Short form of かもしれない.
An exclamation used to motivate oneself or signal determination before taking action. Expresses resolve or readiness.

glosses: not quite, somewhat lacking, not up to par
explanations: Expresses mild dissatisfaction or the sense that something falls slightly short of expectations. A softer, more indirect way of saying something isn't good enough.
A casual contraction of ちょっと, meaning a small amount or degree.
Used in conversation to express strong agreement or to confirm what someone has said. Often signals that the speaker has just remembered or recognized something.

glosses: what should I do, what am I going to do
explanations: An expression of anxiety or indecision when faced with a problem or unexpected situation. Can be a genuine question or a rhetorical expression of distress.
A casual conversation opener used to get someone's attention before bringing up a topic, especially when the speaker wants to broach something carefully or is hesitating.
The transmission of digital data, especially mobile internet data on smartphones and other devices. Commonly encountered when discussing phone plans and data usage.
Following someone back on social media after they have followed you. An abbreviation of フォローバック.
A specific action or step taken to achieve something. Often used in business contexts.
Physical action sequences in movies, games, or performances.
A person who helps or supports someone in their work. Used for both professional assistants and supportive roles.
An institution for specialized training or education, or an organization dedicated to a particular field of study or art.
A person or company that acts on behalf of another, such as a talent agent, real estate agent, or travel agent.
A spy or operative, as seen in movies and fiction.
A person who creates illustrations for books, magazines, advertisements, games, or other media.
An emphatic exclamation expressing excitement, triumph, or strong determination. More energetic than よし.

glosses: it seems, it looks like, apparently
explanations: Attaches to nouns, verbs (plain form), and adjectives to express resemblance or likeness. More casual than よう.
Expresses conjecture or inference based on what the speaker observes or perceives. Similar to ようだ but more colloquial.
A rough, disreputable person who causes trouble or lives by intimidation. Often used to describe street toughs or petty criminals.
A framework that divides things into two opposing categories. Used in academic, philosophical, and general discussion to describe black-and-white thinking or contrasting pairs.

glosses: to read the room, to pick up on the atmosphere
explanations: To sense the mood or unspoken feelings of those around you and act appropriately. A key social skill in Japanese culture.
Describes something or someone that lacks style or looks bad. The opposite of かっこいい.
Describes a situation or behavior that causes embarrassment or loss of face.

glosses: to click to buy, to order online
explanations: To make an online purchase by clicking the buy button. Coined from the onomatopoeia ポチ (the sound of pressing a button) plus the verb-forming suffix る.

glosses: anything is fine, I don't mind
anything is fine, I don't mind, whatever
explanations: Used to indicate that the speaker has no preference and is happy with any option. Very common in everyday conversation when asked to choose.

glosses: so then, with that said, and so
with that said, on that note
explanations: Used to summarize what was previously said and transition to a conclusion, next topic, or action. Common in both casual and semi-formal speech.
Used to wrap up a discussion or signal the end of a conversation or meeting.
A sentence-ending expression seeking agreement or confirmation from the listener. Casual and friendly in tone.
Used as a response to express agreement with what someone just said.

glosses: right?, see?, I told you so
explanations: A casual, truncated form of でしょう used to seek confirmation or agreement. Common among all speakers but especially associated with feminine speech.
Used when the speaker's prediction or opinion turns out to be correct, with a tone of vindication.

glosses: earthen or concrete floor at a Japanese entrance
explanations: The hard-floored lower area at the entrance of a Japanese house (genkan) where shoes are removed. Originally made by pounding a mixture of earth, lime, and bittern, now typically concrete or tile.

glosses: but you know, but like, however (casual)
explanations: A casual conversation opener used to introduce a contrasting point or objection. The particle さ adds a soft, conversational tone.

glosses: well yeah, I guess so, sort of
explanations: A casual response expressing mild or noncommittal agreement. Conveys that the speaker somewhat agrees but doesn't want to fully commit or elaborate.

glosses: so that means, in other words
so that means, in other words, then
explanations: A casual expression used to draw a logical conclusion from what was just said. Contracted from ということは.

glosses: what's that?, what do you mean?
what do you mean?, that's weird
explanations: A casual expression of curiosity when encountering something unfamiliar or unexpected.
An expression of disbelief, confusion, or mild annoyance in response to something strange or unreasonable.

glosses: it's okay, don't worry about it
explanations: Used to grant permission or express approval of someone's request or suggestion.
Used to reassure someone that something is not a problem, or to decline an offer politely.
The Kansai dialect equivalent of {本当|ほんとう}に. Used as an intensifier or to express genuine surprise or emphasis.
The Kansai dialect form of {面白|おもしろ}い, primarily meaning funny or entertaining. Strongly associated with Osaka comedy culture.
Can also mean interesting in a broader sense, just like {面白|おもしろ}い.

Government bonds issued to cover budget deficits, as opposed to construction bonds ({建設国債|けんせつこくさい}) which fund public works. Formally called {特例国債|とくれいこくさい} (special bonds) because their issuance requires special legislation each year.

glosses: entrance step, threshold step in a genkan
explanations: The raised wooden or stone edge at the boundary between the lower entrance area (tataki) and the elevated floor in a Japanese genkan. This is where people sit to put on or remove shoes.

headword: エンターテインメント
explanations: Entertainment in a broad sense, encompassing movies, music, theater, comedy, games, and other forms of amusement. Also used to describe the entertainment industry.

glosses: to act up, to be naughty, to be wild
to be naughty, to act up, to misbehave
to be wild, to raise hell, to get into trouble
explanations: Describes childish misbehavior or playful troublemaking, typically by children.
When used about teenagers or young adults, describes rebellious or delinquent behavior, often looking back on it nostalgically.

glosses: casual speech, informal language between equals
explanations: Informal, plain-form speech used between people of equal status (same age, close friends, etc.). Contrasted with {敬語|けいご} (polite/formal language).
Describes something that feels slow, dull, or not worth the effort. Can describe activities, situations, or physical feelings of lethargy.

glosses: being a killjoy, no fun, unresponsive
being a killjoy, no fun, poor at going along with the mood
explanations: Describes someone who doesn't join in the fun, doesn't respond to the group energy, or brings down the mood. The opposite of ノリがいい.
An exclamation of alarm or panic when something goes wrong or when realizing a problem. Truncated form of やばい.
An exclamation of surprise or excitement when encountering something impressive or unexpectedly good. Reflects the newer positive usage of やばい.
Describes someone or something that is not good-looking. Can be quite rude when said about a person.
Describes something done without skill or finesse. From the original meaning of {不細工|ぶさいく} (lacking fine craftsmanship).
A casual and rough way to refer to a person. Can be neutral among close friends or derogatory depending on tone and context.
A casual way to refer to an object or thing, used instead of もの or の.
An expletive expressing frustration, anger, or disappointment.
Used as a prefix before nouns or adjectives to add strong negative emphasis, similar to English 'damn' or 'freaking.'

glosses: to joke around, to act silly, to clown around
explanations: To behave in a playful, unserious manner, especially when the situation calls for seriousness. Often used critically to describe someone not taking things seriously enough.
Describes something old and in poor condition, falling apart from age or heavy use. Used for objects, buildings, and vehicles.
An edible bivalve mollusk, widely eaten raw or cooked in Japanese cuisine. Japan is one of the world's largest oyster producers.
A Japanese sponge cake originally introduced by Portuguese missionaries in the 16th century. Made with sugar, flour, eggs, and starch syrup, it has a moist, dense texture.
A round, white root vegetable commonly used in Japanese cooking. Milder and sweeter than Western turnips.
Extremely angry. Used to describe someone who is visibly enraged.
Describes intense, beating heat from the sun.
The sound of metal being struck repeatedly.

glosses: dried gourd shavings, dried calabash strips
explanations: Thin strips of dried gourd (calabash) used as an ingredient in Japanese cuisine, especially in sushi rolls and simmered dishes.
Describes uncontrollable shaking or trembling, typically of the knees or legs from fear, exhaustion, or cold.
Useless or worthless objects; miscellaneous items of little value. Often used for old, broken, or unwanted things cluttering a space.

glosses: imitation crab, crab stick, surimi stick
explanations: A processed seafood product made from surimi (fish paste) shaped and colored to resemble crab meat. A common and affordable ingredient in Japanese cooking.

glosses: wood ear mushroom, cloud ear fungus
explanations: A dark, ear-shaped edible fungus with a crunchy, gelatinous texture. Commonly used in stir-fries and ramen.
Having a rough, uneven edge with sharp points, like the teeth of a saw.
The most important or essential part of something. The critical element that determines success or failure.
The liver organ, or more broadly the internal organs. Also used figuratively to refer to courage or nerve.
A short, catchy phrase used in advertising or promotional materials to attract attention. A Japanese-English coinage (wasei-eigo) not used in English.
A small, flat, sweet baked treat. In Japanese usage, クッキー generally refers to richer, handmade-style cookies, while ビスケット refers to simpler, mass-produced ones.
A soft padded object used for sitting on or leaning against. In Japanese, distinct from まくら (sleeping pillow) and {座布団|ざぶとん} (floor cushion).
Something that absorbs shock or serves as a buffer between things.
Products sold as merchandise, especially branded or character-themed items, fan goods, or promotional products.
A person who is slow to act or make decisions. Can also describe such behavior itself.
An alcoholic beverage made by mixing spirits with other ingredients such as juice, soda, or liqueur.
Having many bright colors. Used to describe objects, designs, clothing, and scenes that are visually vibrant.
A question or set of questions used to test knowledge, often in an entertaining format. In Japanese, クイズ often refers to trivia-style questions rather than formal tests.
A curved band worn over the head to hold hair back. In English this is called a headband or Alice band.
A printed or digital publication listing products, services, or items with descriptions, often used for ordering or reference.
A dish made by beating eggs and cooking them in a pan, often folded around a filling. In Japan, both Western-style omelettes and the Japanese オムライス (omurice) variant are popular.
The small oval fruit of the olive tree, eaten as food or pressed for oil. Also refers to the tree itself.
A planned series of activities or a special promotion aimed at achieving a particular goal, especially in marketing and retail.
A joke or comedic routine, especially a physical or visual gag. Often used for comedy routines and humorous scenes in manga and anime.
The act of wagering money or something of value on an uncertain outcome. Also used figuratively for risky undertakings.
An organized group of people who share a common interest, especially extracurricular activity clubs at schools.
An entertainment venue for dancing and nightlife.

glosses: playing field, sports ground, athletic field
explanations: An open outdoor area used for sports and athletic activities, typically at schools or public facilities. In Japanese, グラウンド specifically refers to an unpaved or dirt playing field.
An organism or cell produced asexually from a single ancestor, being genetically identical to it. Also used figuratively for an exact copy or replica.
A room or area used for cooking and preparing food. Often used for modern or Western-style kitchens, as opposed to the more traditional 台所.
A long table or surface at which customers are served in a shop, restaurant, bar, or office.
An attack or move made in response to an opponent's action, used in sports and martial arts.
A state of utter confusion or disorder. In casual Japanese, used very broadly to describe anything absurd, messy, or unpredictable.
The act of cutting hair, or a hairstyle achieved by cutting.
Removing or reducing something, such as scenes from a film, costs, or unnecessary parts.
A division or grouping used to organize items, topics, or people by shared characteristics.
Color in general, especially when referring to product variations, printing, or design choices.
The process of dyeing hair, or hair color treatment at a salon.
One's professional history, work experience, or career path.
A telecommunications company that provides mobile phone service.
The grounds and buildings of a university or college.
The religion based on the teachings of Jesus Christ, encompassing Catholicism, Protestantism, and Orthodox Christianity.
A present given to someone, especially a commercially packaged or formal gift. Often used in retail and marketing contexts.

glosses: to clear, to pass, to meet (a requirement)
explanations: To successfully overcome, complete, or satisfy a condition, goal, or standard.
Being see-through, transparent, or clean in appearance.
Payment by credit, especially using a credit card.
A listing of contributors in a film, TV show, game, or other production.

glosses: grand prix, top prize, first place
explanations: The highest award or first prize in a competition, contest, or race.
An additional item, service, or feature that can be chosen beyond the standard offering. Often used for optional extras when purchasing products or services.
Something that is not a copy or imitation; a unique or first-of-its-kind creation.
The first or source version of something, as opposed to a translation, adaptation, or reproduction.
The person who owns a business, property, or organization, especially a shop, restaurant, or sports team.
The opening of a new business, shop, or facility.
Being accessible, public, or frank. Used to describe personalities, environments, or policies.
An important or central word or phrase that captures the essence of a topic, or a term used for searching.
A space or building for displaying and selling works of art.
A group of people watching an event, game, or activity, especially in golf or street performances.
A set of recommendations or standards issued by an authority or organization, providing direction on how something should be done.
An onomatopoeic word describing the rhythmic, uneven rattling sound made by vehicles moving over rough surfaces or train tracks.

glosses: ATM card, bank card, cash card
explanations: A card issued by a bank that allows the holder to withdraw cash and check balances at ATMs. Distinct from a credit card.
A chewy candy made from sugar, butter, and cream, or the flavor of caramelized sugar.
A traditional Korean dish of fermented vegetables, typically napa cabbage seasoned with chili pepper, garlic, and other spices. Widely eaten in Japan.

glosses: to keep, to maintain, to hold onto
explanations: To maintain something in its current state or to reserve something for future use.
A service at bars and restaurants in Japan where a customer's unfinished bottle is stored and kept for their next visit.
A trial performance or interview in which a performer demonstrates their ability in order to be selected for a role, group, or show.
The opening segment of a show, event, ceremony, or broadcast. Also refers to the opening theme song of an anime or TV series.
An informational session or set of instructions given to introduce people to a new course, program, workplace, or system.
The chemical element carbon, or materials made from carbon, especially carbon fiber used in manufacturing lightweight, high-strength products.
Culture in a broad sense, or cultural and educational activities pursued as hobbies. Often used in compound words.
A person who appreciates and seeks out high-quality or delicious food.
High-quality or specialty food and dining. Often used as a modifier to describe food-related things.
An ambiguous area that is not clearly defined as right or wrong, legal or illegal, acceptable or unacceptable.
Relating to the whole world; having an international scope or perspective.
Taking care of someone, especially in medical, nursing, or emotional support contexts.
Looking after something to keep it in good condition, such as skin, hair, or equipment.
A person invited to appear on a show, attend an event, or visit a place as a special attendee.

glosses: to get, to obtain, to score
to get, to obtain, to acquire
explanations: To successfully obtain or acquire something desirable. Colloquial and energetic in tone.
A gate or barrier at airports, train stations, stadiums, or other facilities that controls entry and exit.
A metal disc used as money, or a token used in machines and games.
Cosmetic and beauty products, including skincare and makeup items. A shortened form of コスメティック.
A humorous genre of entertainment, including movies, TV shows, plays, and performances.
A cooperative project between two or more parties, such as brands, artists, or companies. Shortened from コラボレーション.
A regular short article or essay in a newspaper, magazine, or website, typically written by a specific author and expressing personal views or expertise.
A deep-fried breaded roll typically filled with mashed potato, ground meat, or cream. A staple of Japanese home cooking and street food.
A hard building material made from cement, sand, gravel, and water. Used for buildings, roads, and other structures.
The central idea or theme behind a product, project, business, or creative work.
Short for コンタクトレンズ. Corrective lenses worn directly on the eye.
Communication or connection with someone, especially initial or deliberate contact.
The ability or act of managing, directing, or restraining something.
Small in size but well-designed and functional, without wasted space.
A feeling of inferiority or deep insecurity about a particular aspect of oneself, such as appearance, ability, or background.
A designated path or route for activities such as running, driving, or golf.
A structured program, plan, or set of dishes served in sequence at a restaurant.
A corner or curve, especially on a road or track.
A designated area or section within a store, or a segment of a TV/radio show.
A carbonated soft drink, typically referring to Coca-Cola or Pepsi-type beverages.
The sound or sensation of something hard being ground, scraped, or chewed with a rough texture.
Doing something in a forceful, uncompromising, or extremely dedicated way. Colloquial and emphatic.
A comic book or manga publication. In Japanese, often refers specifically to the published book format of manga (as opposed to magazine serialization).
A key for a lock, a keyboard key, or a key element/factor.
To modify or adjust something to suit individual preferences or needs.
A person who creates original content, art, or media. Includes designers, video creators, illustrators, and other creative professionals.
The group of actors or performers in a movie, TV show, play, or other production.
The act of catching something, such as a ball, or capturing information or attention.
Short for キャッチコピー or キャッチフレーズ. A catchy phrase used in advertising.
The practice of approaching people on the street to recruit customers for bars, restaurants, or other businesses.
The most exciting, intense, or important point in a story, event, or situation.

glosses: to urge, to press, to prompt
to stimulate, to encourage, to facilitate
explanations: To encourage or push someone to take action, often by reminding them or applying gentle pressure.
To bring about or speed up a process or change, used for abstract subjects like growth or development.

glosses: to block, to obstruct, to shield
explanations: To physically block or cut off something such as light, wind, or a path.
To break into someone's speech or action, preventing them from continuing.

glosses: to entrust, to leave to, to delegate
explanations: To place a matter, decision, or responsibility in someone else's hands, trusting them to handle it.

glosses: to recruit, to solicit, to call for
to grow stronger, to intensify, to mount
explanations: To publicly seek participants, applicants, donations, or ideas from a group of people.
For feelings, conditions, or situations to gradually become more intense or severe.

glosses: to lead, to command, to head
explanations: To be at the head of a group and guide or direct them, often in an organized or official capacity.

glosses: to envy, to be jealous of
to envy, to be jealous of, to resent
explanations: To feel bitter resentment or jealousy toward someone because of their success, talent, or good fortune.

glosses: to perish, to be destroyed, to fall to ruin
explanations: For a civilization, nation, species, or entity to come to an end, be destroyed, or cease to exist entirely.

glosses: to deceive, to lie, to misrepresent
to falsify, to forge, to fabricate
explanations: To present false information or hide the truth, especially about oneself or one's identity.
To alter or create false documents, records, or evidence.

glosses: to compensate, to make up for, to pay for
to atone for, to make amends
explanations: To provide restitution or compensation for damage, loss, or harm caused.
To take action to make up for a wrong or sin one has committed.

glosses: to underestimate, to look down on
to underestimate, to look down on, to scorn
explanations: To regard someone or something as less capable or important than they actually are, often leading to carelessness or mistakes.

glosses: to soothe, to calm down, to pacify
explanations: To comfort or placate someone who is upset, angry, or crying, using gentle words or actions.

glosses: to flick, to flip, to snap
to repel, to splash off, to shed
to calculate, to work out on an abacus
explanations: To strike something with a quick, sharp motion of the finger or a similar small object.
For a surface to cause water, dirt, or other substances to bounce off or not penetrate.
To do calculations, originally referring to using an abacus, now used more broadly for quick mental or rough calculations.
A secret plan by a group to do something harmful or illegal, especially against an authority or rival.
The quality of being open-minded and accepting of differences, mistakes, or opposing views without being judgmental.
Deep sympathy and concern for those who are suffering, often with a desire to help. Originally a Buddhist concept combining loving-kindness and empathy for pain.
Strong anger or displeasure aroused by something perceived as unjust, wrong, or offensive.

glosses: social obligation, moral duty, sense of duty
explanations: A sense of obligation or duty arising from social relationships, customs, or debts of gratitude. A core concept in Japanese interpersonal relationships.
When used as a prefix before family terms, indicates a relationship by marriage rather than blood.
The act of devoting oneself entirely to a cause, person, or duty, often at the expense of one's own interests.
An indirect indication or hint about something, rather than a direct statement. Often used in formal, academic, or analytical contexts.
The act of referring to or touching upon a topic in speech or writing.
The process of something being created, formed, or produced, often used in scientific, technical, or computational contexts.
A written or spoken statement declaring how one's property and affairs should be handled after death, or final words left for the living.
Whether a business, project, or investment yields enough revenue to cover costs and produce a profit.
The practice of a company receiving work from a larger company and carrying it out on their behalf, or the work itself.

glosses: settlement of accounts, final calculation, squaring up
explanations: The act of calculating the exact amount owed and settling the balance, whether for expenses, fares, or shared costs.
Impressively large in scale, scope, or ambition, evoking a sense of awe or grandeur.
Extremely difficult, demanding, or unforgiving, whether describing conditions, treatment, or circumstances.
A hint or clue planted early in a story, plan, or course of events that becomes significant later. Also used figuratively for preparations laid in advance.

glosses: chain, chain reaction, series of linked events
explanations: A sequence of events or phenomena where each one causes or triggers the next, forming a connected chain.
A set of related events, actions, or things that are connected as a group or sequence. Almost always used as a pre-noun modifier with の.
The small, round, red fruit of the cherry tree, eaten fresh or used in desserts. In Japan, cherries from Yamagata Prefecture are particularly famous.
The sale of goods in large quantities to retailers or other businesses, rather than directly to consumers.
Describes a place or scene that lacks warmth, interest, or decoration, giving a cold and uninviting impression.
Describes a person who diligently fulfills obligations and promises, never cutting corners or neglecting responsibilities.
Describes a person who is difficult to satisfy, often picky about details or easily displeased.

glosses: reluctant to part, sorry to leave
explanations: Feeling regret or sadness at parting from someone or something, wishing the moment could continue.
Not paying attention to or caring about something, particularly appearance, manners, or details that others typically notice.
Describes a person or animal that naturally warms up to people and is easy to get along with. Implies an endearing, open quality.
The tendency to become angry or frustrated quickly. As an adjective, describes a person who is easily irritated.
The ability or willingness to adjust rules, procedures, or expectations to fit the situation.
The act of lending money or arranging financial accommodation.
A small, broken-off piece of something larger, whether physical or abstract (such as information or memory).
Short verbal responses such as うん, ええ, そうですね given by a listener during conversation to show they are paying attention. A fundamental part of Japanese communication.
A person's physical movements, gestures, or habitual actions, often observed as characteristic or expressive.
The act of reading books, magazines, or manga at a bookstore or convenience store without purchasing them.
Something a person is especially good at or known for, often a signature skill, dish, song, or trick.

glosses: after all, in the end, ultimately
explanations: Used to express a resigned or realistic conclusion, often implying that something cannot exceed its fundamental nature or limitations.

glosses: opportune time, right moment to act
explanations: The right time to do something, especially to make a change or stop what one has been doing. Often used when deciding to quit, retire, or move on.
A state where growth, increase, or improvement has reached its limit and cannot go higher. Used for numbers, performance, prices, and similar metrics.
A concealed hole in the ground designed to trap animals or people who step on it.
A hidden risk, unexpected problem, or deceptive situation that catches someone off guard.
A mark, sign, or evidence left behind showing that something existed or happened in the past.
An excessively high opinion of oneself, especially regarding one's appearance, abilities, or worth.
A medical condition caused by losing more fluid than the body takes in, leading to insufficient water for normal functions.
The process of removing water from laundry using a washing machine's spin cycle.
The gradual wearing away of rock, soil, or land by natural forces such as water, wind, or ice.
The gradual intrusion into or wearing away of someone's territory, rights, market share, or similar abstract domains.
The act of stirring up emotions or provoking someone into action, often through inflammatory words or behavior.
The indirect negative impact of an event or situation, affecting others who were not directly involved.

glosses: dining and dashing, eating without paying
explanations: The act of eating at a restaurant and leaving without paying the bill.
An edible mushroom native to East Asia, widely used in Japanese cuisine. It has a distinctive savory flavor and is a key source of umami.
A thick, hearty dish of meat and vegetables cooked slowly in liquid. In Japan, this typically refers to either cream stew (white) or beef stew (brown).
A deep, narrow valley with steep sides, typically formed by river erosion. Often a scenic natural feature.
An informal group or club, especially at a university, organized around a shared interest or activity. Less formal and less competitive than a {部活|ぶかつ} (official club).
A round shape or ring.
A scheduled period of work, especially in jobs with rotating schedules such as part-time work, retail, or healthcare.
A move from one state, position, or approach to another.
A heated room or facility used for bathing by sitting in dry heat or steam. Saunas have become extremely popular in Japan in recent years.
An unexpected event, gift, or action planned to delight or astonish someone. Used almost exclusively in positive contexts in Japanese.
A product taken orally that contains vitamins, minerals, or other nutritional ingredients intended to supplement the diet.
A meeting or conference of heads of state or other high-level leaders to discuss important political, economic, or social issues.
A small portion or example of something used for testing, examination, or demonstration.
A written outline or script for a film, TV show, play, or game.
A description of how a situation might develop; a projected sequence of events.
Describes conditions, standards, judgments, or situations that are demanding, unforgiving, or difficult.
A set of related things, events, or works that follow in succession or share a theme.
Describes something that is not complex or elaborate; clean and straightforward in design or approach.
A particular period of the year associated with specific weather, activities, or events.
One cycle or series of episodes in a TV show, or a playing period in a sport.
A thin, flat piece of material used for covering, wrapping, or protecting surfaces.
A place to sit, especially in a vehicle, theater, or stadium.
Professional guidance and support provided by a trained counselor or therapist to help individuals deal with personal, psychological, or practical problems.
The subjects, topics, and structured content that make up a course or educational program.
An object, image, or mark that represents something else, such as an idea, organization, or place.
A room or bed designed for one person.
A music release featuring one or two main songs, as opposed to an album.
Not married; living alone or without a partner.
A live entertainment performance, exhibition, or display put on for an audience.
Something that is short in length, especially referring to hair or clothing styles.
An electrical short circuit, or the act of short-circuiting.
A business establishment where hair, beauty, or wellness services are provided.
A gathering or social space where people with shared interests meet and interact, including online community spaces.
The act or process of surviving in difficult, dangerous, or competitive conditions.
A person who actively supports a sports team, cause, or person.
A band or wrap worn to support and protect a joint or muscle during physical activity.
An aromatic herb in the mint family, widely used in Japanese cuisine. The leaves have a distinctive flavor that is fresh, slightly minty, and herbaceous.
The sound or sensation of cutting, chopping, or biting into something with a coarse, satisfying crunch.
Describes something existing or being produced in large, plentiful quantities.
The social and cultural aspects of being male, female, or another identity, as distinct from biological sex. Often used in discussions of equality, roles, and identity.
A gesture, action, light, or sound that conveys information or serves as a cue for action.
A place where films are shown to an audience, or the art and industry of filmmaking.
An imitation or model of a real-world process or system, used for training, testing, analysis, or entertainment.
The quality or character of sound, especially in the context of music, technology, or audio production.
Footwear, especially athletic, specialized, or fashionable shoes. Often used in compound forms to specify the type of shoe.
A mineral essential for bone health, teeth, and bodily functions. Commonly discussed in the context of diet and nutrition.
A cultural group or movement within a larger culture that has distinct interests, styles, and values. In Japan, often refers to manga, anime, games, and other otaku-related interests.

glosses: to be thirsty, to be parched; to thirst for
to be thirsty, to be parched
explanations: To feel thirst. Used with 喉 (throat) in the pattern 喉が渇く. Written with 渇 to distinguish from 乾く (to dry physically).
To strongly desire or crave something, used figuratively.
The Chinese language, including its various dialects such as Mandarin and Cantonese. In most contexts refers to Modern Standard Chinese (Mandarin).
An additional serving of food or drink. Often used at restaurants or at home when asking for more rice, soup, or a drink.
An informal, affectionate term for one's grandmother.
An informal way to refer to an elderly woman in general.
The physical size or scale of something. Formed from the adjective 大きい by replacing い with さ.
The evening or night of the previous day. A slightly more formal synonym of 昨夜 and ゆうべ.
Tea made from unfermented tea leaves. The most commonly consumed type of tea in Japan, including varieties like sencha, matcha, and gyokuro.

glosses: sea bathing, swimming in the sea
explanations: The activity of swimming or bathing in the ocean, typically for recreation. A common summer activity in Japan.

glosses: middle school student, junior high school student
explanations: A student attending 中学校, which covers grades 7-9 (ages 12-15) in the Japanese education system.
A figure made of packed snow. Traditional Japanese snowmen are made of two stacked snowballs (not three as in Western style).
The hand on the left side of the body.
The left side when giving directions or describing locations.

glosses: to be divided, to branch off, to split into
to be divided, to split into, to branch off
to be classified into, to fall into categories
explanations: For something to separate into two or more parts. Used for roads branching, groups splitting, opinions diverging, etc.
To be divided into distinct categories or types.
A verb that does not take a direct object. In Japanese grammar, intransitive verbs describe actions or states that happen on their own without an agent acting on something.
A count of three people, using the Sino-Japanese number with the counter for people.
A period of seven days.
The time at nine hours past midnight or noon.
The time at twelve hours past midnight or noon. Noon or midnight.
The time at six hours past midnight or noon.
The time at three hours past midnight or noon.
A period of three years, or the third year in a sequence.
A count of one hundred people.
Used after the plain form of a verb to express a decision made by the speaker. Implies a conscious, deliberate choice.

glosses: to try to; to make sure to
to try to; to make sure to; to make an effort to
explanations: Used after the plain form of a verb to express a conscious effort or habit the speaker maintains. Implies ongoing effort rather than a one-time decision.

glosses: because; the thing is; you see
it is natural that; that's just how things are
explanations: Sentence-ending particle used to give a reason or excuse, often with a slightly childish or emotional tone. Common in casual speech.
Used to express that something is natural, expected, or a general truth. Often in the form ものだ.

glosses: I wonder; I'm not sure if
explanations: Sentence-ending particle expressing uncertainty, wondering, or thinking aloud. Used when the speaker is uncertain about something or musing to themselves.

glosses: to visit someone's home or office (polite/humble)
explanations: A humble expression used when visiting someone's home or entering their space. Literally means 'to cause a disturbance' but functions as a polite way of saying 'to visit' or 'to come in.'

glosses: to follow; to keep up with
to follow; to go along with
to keep up with; to keep pace with
explanations: To physically follow someone or go along with them.
To maintain the same pace or level as someone or something, whether physically, intellectually, or in a conversation.

glosses: to transfer money (to a bank account)
explanations: To deposit or transfer money into a bank account. A common financial term used for salary payments, bill payments, and bank transfers.

glosses: the first day of the month
explanations: The first day of any month. An irregular reading of the kanji 一日.
A period of one year.
The first year of school or the first grade. Often used as 一年生.
Cooperative effort by a group working together effectively toward a common goal.
Making something stationary or immovable by attaching or fastening it. Also used figuratively for establishing something as unchanging.
Restricting or confining something to a certain scope, number, or condition. Often used to describe limited-edition products or exclusive access.
Having no days off or holidays. Used to describe businesses or services that operate without closing days.

glosses: unguarded moment, opening, chance to exploit
explanations: A physical space or opening between things.
A moment of carelessness or vulnerability that can be taken advantage of. Common in martial arts, sports, and everyday contexts.
A meeting or class for discussion and instruction on a specific topic. Often used for business training, academic sessions, or professional development events.
Working independently without being permanently employed by a particular company or organization.
Not bound by rules, charges, or restrictions. Used in compound words and set phrases.
A sealed package or container for food or other products. Also the act of packing or packaging something.
A skincare product applied to the face for treatment. Short for フェイスパック.
A repeated sequence or circular process. Used in computing, music, and general contexts for things that repeat in a cycle.
Feeling nervous or uncomfortable around others, especially in unfamiliar social situations. A loanword used as a na-adjective.
A story or work that is invented or imaginary, not based on real events. Includes novels, films, and other creative works.

glosses: with a clattering or rattling sound
explanations: Mimetic word describing a light, repeated tapping or rattling sound, such as typing on a keyboard, teeth chattering, or small objects shaking.
A metric unit of volume equal to 1,000 milliliters. Used for measuring liquids such as water, milk, gasoline, etc.

glosses: to diet; to go on a diet
explanations: To restrict food intake or exercise in order to lose weight. In Japanese, ダイエット focuses primarily on weight loss rather than general dietary habits.
The southernmost prefecture of Japan, consisting of a chain of subtropical islands between Kyushu and Taiwan. Known for its warm climate, beaches, and distinctive culture.
The northernmost of Japan's four main islands and one of its 47 prefectures. Known for its cold winters, natural scenery, dairy farming, and seafood.
A suffix attached to nouns indicating that something is designed for, targeted at, or suitable for a particular audience, purpose, or destination.
A suffix attached to the stem of verbs (masu-stem) to indicate that an action has just been completed and the result is still fresh. Emphasizes the immediate, fresh state.
An attempt to take on something difficult or new. In Japanese, the emphasis is on the positive act of trying, rather than the confrontational sense of the English word "challenge."
A slip, card, or digital pass that grants admission to an event, transportation, or service.
Physical, emotional, or financial harm or injury. Used broadly in everyday conversation, gaming, and business contexts.
The first public appearance or performance in a particular field, especially in entertainment. Also used casually for any first experience.
A category or type, especially of artistic works such as music, literature, film, or games.
The narrative or sequence of events in a movie, novel, game, or other creative work.
A monetary gift given to service staff in addition to the bill. Not customary in Japan but familiar as a foreign practice.
A small piece or component, especially an electronic microchip or a poker/casino chip.

glosses: with a piercing glare, with a sharp look
explanations: Describes the action of looking at someone with a sharp, intimidating, or disapproving gaze. A single, deliberate stare rather than repeated glancing.
Describes the warm, emotional sensation of being deeply moved or touched by something. Often accompanied by tears welling up.
Describes a physical sensation of tingling, numbness, or a dull aching, as from cold, a hit, or a wound.
The sound of light, rhythmic knocking or tapping, as on a door or with a knife while chopping.
A state where gains and losses balance out, resulting in neither profit nor loss.
The most common variety of cherry blossom tree in Japan (Prunus × yedoensis). Produces pale pink to white flowers and accounts for roughly 80% of cherry trees in Japan.
Proceeding without difficulty, delay, or obstruction. Describes processes, operations, or interactions that go well.
A sweet, soft dessert made from gelatin, often fruit-flavored. In Japanese, ゼリー refers primarily to the dessert form rather than jam or preserves.
Performing, playing, or doing something alone, without a partner or group. Used in music, travel, activities, and gaming contexts.
A processed meat product made from ground meat stuffed into a casing. In Japan, ソーセージ typically refers to small, smooth-textured sausages similar to frankfurters or wieners.
A carbohydrate substance found in plants such as potatoes, rice, and corn, used in cooking as a thickener and in industrial applications.
Chicken as a food or ingredient. In Japanese, チキン refers specifically to chicken as prepared food or a menu item, not to the live animal (which is {鶏|にわとり}).
To store or record data, especially saving progress in a video game or saving a file on a computer.
A defensive play that prevents the opposing team from scoring, particularly in baseball (a relief pitcher's save) and soccer (a goalkeeper's save).
A large construction company that manages and oversees major building projects. Abbreviated from "general contractor" (ゼネラル・コントラクター).
Carbonated water or a carbonated soft drink. In Japanese, ソーダ usually refers to plain carbonated water or a simple carbonated flavored drink, rather than to soft drinks in general.
A designated area or section, whether physical (a restricted zone, a parking zone) or abstract (a price range, a mental state of peak focus).
A label or marker attached to an item for identification or information. Includes physical tags (clothing labels, price tags) and digital tags (hashtags, HTML tags, metadata tags).
A tall, narrow building or structure. Used for observation towers, communication towers, and tall residential buildings (tower mansions).
The intended recipient, audience, or objective of an action, plan, or product. Used in business, marketing, and general contexts.
A major station or building where passengers begin or end a journey, such as an airport terminal, bus terminal, or major railway station.
A precious gemstone made of crystallized carbon, prized for its hardness and brilliance. Also used figuratively and in compound expressions.
Something that imitates or substitutes for the real thing. Used for placeholders, decoys, fake items, or test objects.
The board game of chess, played between two players on a checkered board with 16 pieces each.
A retail store or restaurant that is part of a chain with multiple locations operating under the same brand. Includes convenience stores, fast food restaurants, and retail chains.
A visual representation of data or information, such as a graph, flow chart, or organizational chart.
A ranked list, especially of popular music, showing sales or streaming numbers.
A post on X (formerly Twitter) or, by extension, a short post on other social media platforms. Also used as a verb with する.
A tool or instrument used to accomplish a task. In modern Japanese, primarily used for software tools, apps, and business tools rather than physical hand tools (which are {道具|どうぐ}).
A subject of discussion, conversation, or media attention. Often used for trending subjects or noteworthy items in news and online media.
The workers or team members involved in an operation, event, production, or establishment. Unlike English where "staff" is collective, スタッフ can refer to individual members as well as the group.
A raised platform or area where performances, presentations, or events take place.
A distinct phase or level in a process, development, or progression. Used in medical, business, and gaming contexts.
The rate at which something moves or happens. Used for physical speed (of vehicles, movement) and figurative speed (of work, progress).
An available area or room, either physical (a place to put things, parking space) or typographic (a blank space between characters).
The activity of selling products or services, or a person who sells (short for セールスマン/セールスパーソン). Often implies active, direct selling such as door-to-door sales or sales calls.
The act of jumping or leaping into the air. Used in everyday language, sports, and figuratively for sudden increases.
A humorous remark, story, or prank intended to make people laugh. In Japanese, ジョーク tends to imply a more Western-style verbal joke, as opposed to Japanese-style humor.
The act of starting or beginning something. Used for races, projects, new ventures, and processes.
An aromatic or pungent substance used to flavor food. Also used figuratively to mean something that adds interest or excitement.
Chemical substances used in experiments, manufacturing, cleaning, or other industrial and scientific processes.
Medicinal products or drugs, especially in formal or technical contexts.
The exit or entrance on the north side of a building, typically a train station. Japanese stations commonly label exits by compass direction.

glosses: each company, every company, all the companies
explanations: Refers to each of the companies in a group or industry. Commonly used in news and business contexts.
The amount of money paid regularly to an insurance company for coverage. Applies to health insurance, car insurance, life insurance, and other types.

glosses: participation fee, entry fee, registration fee
explanations: A fee charged for participating in an event, class, competition, or gathering.

glosses: commercial use, business use, business purposes
explanations: Use for business or commercial purposes, as opposed to personal or non-profit use. Often appears in terms of service, licensing, and legal contexts.
A chart or list showing planned activities, appointments, or events, usually organized by date and time.

glosses: to become vacant; to become free; to become empty
to become vacant, to become free, to become available
to become empty, to be emptied
explanations: For a space, seat, time slot, or person to become available or unoccupied.
For a container, stomach, or space to become empty.
The act of doing something good for someone in return for kindness or help they previously provided.
A benefit, reward, or compensation received in exchange for doing something for someone else.
A literal swamp or marsh filled with deep mud.
A situation that is difficult to escape from and keeps getting worse, like being stuck in mud.

glosses: to mend, to repair; to keep up appearances
to mend, to repair, to patch up
to keep up appearances, to put on a front
explanations: To fix something that is damaged or torn, especially clothing or fabric.
To disguise or cover up one's true state in order to appear presentable or acceptable to others.
An outcome that defies expectations, especially in competitions or sports where the expected winner loses.
The administration of a vaccine to prevent disease, or the act of receiving such a vaccine.

glosses: medical chart, patient record, clinical record
explanations: A document or digital file containing a patient's medical history, diagnoses, treatments, and other health information maintained by a healthcare provider.
The process of a doctor or nurse asking a patient about their symptoms, medical history, and current condition, typically at the beginning of a consultation.
The branch of medicine dealing with eye diseases and disorders, or a clinic or department specializing in eye care.
The branch of medicine dealing with teeth and oral health, or a clinic or department specializing in dental care.
The branch of medicine dealing with skin conditions and disorders, or a clinic or department specializing in skin care.

glosses: blood draw, blood sampling, taking blood
explanations: The medical procedure of drawing blood from a patient, typically from a vein in the arm, for testing or donation purposes.
A bordered area of soil in a garden or park specifically prepared for growing flowers.
A person's sense of their own worth and dignity. Can refer to healthy self-respect or to excessive pride that makes someone difficult to deal with.
The process of something becoming worse in condition, quality, or state.
The inability to sleep or the condition of being unable to get adequate sleep.
Sleeping deeply and soundly without waking, resulting in a well-rested state.
A person or entity against whom a legal action is brought in court. In criminal cases, the person accused of a crime; in civil cases, the party being sued.

glosses: social pleasantry, polite fiction, lip service
explanations: A polite remark or promise made for the sake of social harmony rather than out of genuine intent. Compliments, invitations, or expressions of interest that are not meant literally.
The process of something increasing in size, volume, or scale. Used for physical expansion (of gases, materials) and figurative growth (of budgets, organizations, problems).

glosses: business partner, client company, trading partner
explanations: A company or individual with whom one conducts business transactions. Can refer to clients, suppliers, or any party in a business relationship.
The process by which water vapor in the air turns into liquid water droplets on cold surfaces, such as windows, walls, or cold drinks.
The party who brings a lawsuit or legal action against another in a court of law.
The government body or process responsible for investigating crimes and bringing criminal charges in court.
A criminal sentence requiring confinement in prison, typically involving mandatory labor.
A formal statement given by a witness, typically in a legal proceeding, to establish facts about an event.
A type of medication used to treat bacterial infections by killing or inhibiting the growth of bacteria.
A patient's first visit to a particular doctor or hospital, or the first consultation for a new condition.
The sugar and starch components in food that serve as the body's primary energy source. In nutritional contexts, refers specifically to digestible carbohydrates excluding dietary fiber.
The fat content in food or the body; a class of nutrients that includes fats and oils used for energy storage and cell function.
The process by which the body converts food into energy and replaces old cells with new ones. Also used figuratively for the renewal or turnover of people or ideas in an organization.
A telecommunications or internet line; the physical or virtual connection used for data transmission or phone calls.
The central part of the body excluding the head and limbs; in fitness, the deep muscles of the torso that support posture and movement.
The act of doing something over and over again; repeating a process or action multiple times.

A collective term for the major ceremonial events in life: coming-of-age ceremonies, weddings, funerals, and ancestral rites. By extension, refers to formal social occasions and their associated customs and etiquette.
An advanced academic degree earned after completing a postgraduate program, typically lasting two years after a bachelor's degree.
A practice examination that simulates the format and difficulty of an actual test, used to assess readiness and identify weak areas. Short for {模擬試験|もぎしけん}.
Official approval or authorization given by a person in authority, typically a manager or executive, to proceed with a plan, expenditure, or action.

glosses: start of construction, commencement of work
explanations: The beginning of construction work on a building, road, or other structure.
Leading and directing a group of people in a coordinated effort, such as military operations, emergency response, or organizational activities.
Directing an orchestra, band, or choir by guiding the tempo, dynamics, and expression of a musical performance.
A written or printed representation of music using musical notation; the physical sheets or document containing the notes to be performed.
The process of removing water from a place, or the water that is discharged or drained away.
A state of physical and mental exhaustion caused by prolonged stress or overwork, leaving a person feeling drained and unable to function effectively.
A chemical element (N) that makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere. An odorless, colorless gas essential for plant growth and used in various industrial processes.
The process of a problem or situation becoming increasingly serious, severe, or difficult to resolve.
The process of something lasting longer than expected or originally planned, typically with negative implications.
Visiting and inspecting a property (apartment, house, office) in person before deciding to rent or buy it.
A viewing or preview of an exhibition, event, or product before it opens to the general public.
An individual panel in a manga or a single frame in a film or animation.
A unit of scheduled time, typically referring to a university lecture period or a scheduled slot in a timetable.
A flat-leafed herb with a mild garlic flavor, widely used in East Asian cooking. The leaves are typically cut and used in stir-fries, dumplings, and soups.
A covert agent or mercenary in feudal Japan, trained in espionage, sabotage, disguise, and martial arts. In modern usage, also refers to the popular cultural image of these figures.
An undesirable situation or outcome that someone ends up in, typically as a result of their own actions or circumstances beyond their control. Almost always used in the pattern 〜する{羽目|はめ}になる.

glosses: to reveal, to expose; to dismantle
to reveal, to expose, to spill (a secret)
explanations: To disclose information that was supposed to be kept secret, often carelessly or deliberately.
To break something down into its component parts; to disassemble a machine or structure.
A tangy Japanese condiment made from citrus juice (typically yuzu, sudachi, or kabosu), rice vinegar, soy sauce, and often dashi. Used as a dipping sauce or dressing.
The most important or decisive point in an event, project, or situation. The moment where things could go either way.
A barrier that runners jump over in track and field events.
A figurative barrier or difficulty that must be overcome. Very common in everyday and business contexts.
A cylindrical container with a handle, used for carrying water, cleaning, or other purposes.
A colloquial term for a person who has been divorced once. Can be used as a noun or as a modifier with の.
A sphere of liquid enclosing air or gas.
A period of rapid economic growth driven by inflated asset prices that eventually collapses. In Japan, often refers specifically to the late 1980s bubble economy.
A person with extensive experience and skill in a particular field. Used as both a noun and a modifier with の.
A tall glass dessert made with layers of ice cream, whipped cream, fruit, sauce, and other toppings. A popular dessert in Japanese cafes and restaurants.
A smooth, jiggly custard dessert topped with caramel sauce. One of the most popular everyday desserts in Japan.
Food coated in flour, egg, and breadcrumbs (panko), then deep-fried. A major category of Japanese Western-style cooking (yoshoku).
A ball hit high into the air in baseball.
Wooden or wood-style flooring, as opposed to tatami or carpet. A common flooring choice in modern Japanese apartments and houses.
A liquid sauce or mixture used to season salads. Many Japanese-style varieties exist alongside Western types.
A ring-shaped fried pastry, often topped with sugar, glaze, or chocolate. A popular snack in Japan.
Having a mild level of spiciness or heat. Used to describe food that has a pleasant kick without being overwhelmingly hot.
A thick, creamy condiment made from egg yolks, oil, and vinegar. Extremely popular in Japanese cooking.

glosses: menma, seasoned bamboo shoots for ramen
explanations: Fermented and seasoned bamboo shoot strips, commonly used as a ramen topping. Also eaten as a side dish or snack with beer.
A green vegetable with a thick stalk and clustered florets. A common ingredient in Japanese home cooking and bento boxes.
A green bell pepper. In Japanese, ピーマン typically refers to the smaller, thinner-walled green peppers common in Asian cooking rather than the larger Western bell peppers.
A fermented milk product with a creamy, tangy taste. Available in many varieties in Japan including plain, flavored, and drinkable types.
A large ocean fish of the family Scombridae, highly prized in Japanese cuisine for sushi and sashimi. Various species and cuts exist at different price points.
A flat-bodied fish that lies on the ocean floor with both eyes on one side. Prized in Japanese cuisine for its delicate white flesh, especially as sashimi and sushi.
An aromatic herb (Artemisia indica) that grows wild throughout Japan. Used in cooking, traditional medicine, and cultural practices.
Practical knowledge and skill acquired through experience, especially regarding how to accomplish specific tasks or achieve results.
A subtle difference in meaning, feeling, or tone. Often used when discussing the fine distinctions between similar words, expressions, or situations.
Social rules and customs governing polite behavior. In Japanese culture, there are detailed manners for many everyday situations.
A general term for plastic film, sheets, or bags. In everyday Japanese, used broadly for various types of plastic materials, not just true vinyl.
A casual chain restaurant offering a wide variety of affordable dishes in a family-friendly atmosphere. Major chains include Gusto, Denny's, Saizeriya, and Royal Host.
One's psychological or emotional state. In modern Japanese, used as both a noun referring to one's mental condition and as a modifier meaning 'mental' or 'psychological.'
A difficult or dangerous situation where things could go wrong. Often used in sports, games, and everyday life to describe being in trouble.
A piece of information that helps someone solve a problem, answer a question, or come up with an idea. Also used for inspiration or a starting point for creative work.
Indicates that something is relatively better when comparing unfavorable options. Implies that none of the choices are ideal, but one is more tolerable than the others.
A common vegetable used extensively in Japanese cooking. Japanese eggplants are typically smaller and more slender than Western varieties.
Not wet; lacking moisture. Used for hair, weather, beverages, and other physical contexts.
Describes a person or attitude that is cool, rational, and unsentimental. Implies someone who does not let emotions influence decisions or relationships.
A power tool or hand tool used for boring holes in hard materials.
A workbook containing repetitive exercises for students to practice skills, especially in math or kanji. Widely used in Japanese elementary education.
A marker or trigger in a program or game that indicates a certain condition has been met.
In internet and otaku culture, an event or statement that foreshadows a particular outcome. Often used for cliché story developments, especially death scenes or romantic developments.

A person with deep, specialized knowledge and passion for a particular subject or hobby. In Japanese, this word carries a more positive connotation than the English 'maniac' and is closer to 'enthusiast' or 'buff.'
A person who speaks a language as their first language. Most commonly used in the context of language learning.
Describes something that is authentic or characteristic of native speakers, often used to describe pronunciation or language ability.
A large retail store selling DIY supplies, tools, gardening equipment, household goods, and building materials. A wasei-eigo term (Japanese-coined English) — not used in this sense in English.

Describes facilities, buildings, or designs that are accessible to people with disabilities, the elderly, or anyone with mobility challenges. Includes ramps, elevators, wide doorways, and other accessibility features.
A wheeled device for transporting infants and young children. A wasei-eigo term — in English, the equivalent is 'stroller' (US) or 'pushchair/pram' (UK).
A professional who specializes in making pastries, cakes, and confections. Borrowed from French pâtissier.
A style of dining where food is displayed and guests serve themselves. Often used for hotel breakfasts, party catering, and restaurant dining.
How well something or someone performs. Used for machines, products, athletes, and employees.
An action done primarily for show or to attract attention, especially by politicians or public figures. Often implies that the action is more about appearance than substance.
A company that manufactures products. In Japanese, メーカー is used much more broadly than 'maker' in English, often serving as the standard word for 'manufacturer' or 'brand.'
A recurring design, pattern, or thematic element in art, fashion, music, or storytelling. Also used to describe the inspiration or source material for a creative work.
The prevailing emotional tone or atmosphere of a place, situation, or group. In Japanese, ムード often emphasizes a romantic, sophisticated, or emotional atmosphere.
A product, song, movie, or other work that achieves widespread popularity and commercial success.
A successful contact in baseball, or a match in a database or search engine query.
Commercial activity, professional work, or the business world in general. Used very broadly in Japanese as a modifier for work-related contexts.
The act of applying cosmetics to the face, or the cosmetics themselves once applied. Short for メイクアップ.
The most important or prominent element among several. Used as a modifier before nouns.
The channels and organizations that distribute news, entertainment, and information to the public, including television, newspapers, radio, and the internet.
A list of food and drink items available at a restaurant, café, or similar establishment.
A set of options, items, or activities planned for a particular purpose. Used for exercise routines, training programs, and digital interfaces.
The prevailing style of clothing and accessories, or an individual's personal style of dress.
A boat or ship that regularly transports passengers, vehicles, and cargo across a body of water.
A large room or building used for concerts, lectures, ceremonies, and other public events.
The main public area of a hotel, restaurant, or building. In restaurants, the dining area as opposed to the kitchen.
The potato vegetable. Used less commonly than じゃがいも for the raw vegetable, but common in food product names and restaurant menus.
Short for フライドポテト (fried potatoes). Very common in fast food and casual dining contexts.
A sudden overwhelming feeling of fear or anxiety that prevents clear thinking. Also used for widespread public alarm or confusion.
When a computer, smartphone, or application stops responding and becomes uncontrollable. The most common usage in Japanese.
To stop moving suddenly, often from shock, fear, or being ordered to stop.
The speed at which something happens or someone does something. Often used for work speed, running speed, or the rate of drinking/eating.
The point at which something reaches its maximum level, whether in quantity, intensity, or activity. Used for business seasons, physical conditions, traffic, and other measurable phenomena.
