To portray a character in a performance, film, or play. Used in theatrical and cinematic contexts.
The way something or someone is treated, managed, or dealt with. Applies to both physical handling of objects and the manner in which people or matters are dealt with.
Formal agreement or acceptance of a request, proposal, or condition. Used in business, legal, and official contexts.
Refined technical skill or artistry, especially in creative or artistic endeavors. Emphasizes the sophistication and polish of the technique rather than raw ability.
The rise and fall of pitch in speech or music. Refers to the natural variation in tone that makes speech or performance expressive and engaging.
An attitude of not caring about the outcome, doing things carelessly without effort or responsibility. Implies giving up on trying properly.
A crane made by folding paper using the traditional Japanese art of origami. One of the most iconic origami shapes, strongly associated with wishes for peace and recovery from illness.
Far superior to others in the same group. Describes something that stands out conspicuously above the rest.

glosses: to hold tightly; to take on alone
to hold tightly, to clutch, to hug closely
to take on alone, to shoulder by oneself, to bottle up
explanations: To wrap one's arms around something and hold it close to the body.
To take on problems, worries, or responsibilities without sharing them with others. Often implies keeping things to oneself when one should ask for help.

glosses: to crush, to squash, to flatten
explanations: To press down on something with force, flattening or destroying it.
To forcefully hold back emotions or feelings, pushing them down rather than expressing them.

glosses: bearer, person responsible for, driving force
bearer, supporter, person responsible for, driving force
explanations: A person or group that takes on the responsibility of carrying forward or sustaining something — a role, a tradition, an industry, or a future. Often used in discussions about who will continue or lead something important.

glosses: to bear, to shoulder, to take on
to bear, to shoulder, to take on (a role or responsibility)
explanations: To physically carry something on one's shoulders or back. The original, literal meaning.
To accept and carry out an important role, responsibility, or duty. The more common figurative usage.
A firm, definitive refusal to accept something — a request, a demand, a person, or an idea. Stronger and more absolute than a simple refusal.

glosses: loading, mounting, equipping; equipped with, onboard
explanations: The act of installing or loading equipment, features, or cargo onto a vehicle, device, or system. Commonly used in technology and transportation contexts to describe built-in features.

glosses: Dear Sir/Madam, To Whom It May Concern
explanations: A formal salutation used at the beginning of a Japanese letter. It is always paired with the closing salutation 敬具 (けいぐ, "Yours sincerely") at the end of the letter.

glosses: to raise, to hold up; to advocate
to raise, to hold up, to hoist
to advocate, to put forward, to espouse
to publish, to post, to list
explanations: To lift something up high so it can be seen — a flag, a sign, a banner, or a light.
To publicly declare a goal, ideal, policy, or slogan. Used when a person or organization prominently promotes a principle or objective.
To display or publish information in a visible place — a notice, an article, or a list.

glosses: furigana, reading aid, phonetic gloss written above or beside kanji
explanations: Small kana characters placed above (in horizontal text) or beside (in vertical text) kanji to indicate their pronunciation. Used in children's books, language learning materials, and to clarify rare or unusual readings.

glosses: to wield, to exercise, to display
to wield, to swing, to brandish
to exercise, to exert (power, ability, violence)
explanations: To swing or brandish a weapon, tool, or implement with force.
To actively use or display power, ability, or force. Often used when describing someone demonstrating their skills or exerting authority.
To crush or grind something into smaller pieces or powder using a mill, grinder, or similar tool. Most commonly used for coffee beans, pepper, and meat.

glosses: to grasp, to capture, to perceive
to catch, to capture, to seize
to grasp, to perceive, to understand
explanations: To physically catch or seize a person, animal, or moving object.
To mentally grasp or comprehend something — a concept, a situation, or a phenomenon. To perceive or interpret something in a particular way.

glosses: to set, to place, to install; to fix
to set, to place, to install, to position
to fix, to settle, to focus (one's eyes, resolve)
explanations: To place something firmly in a fixed position. Used for installing equipment, placing furniture, or positioning something with care.
To fix or steady something abstract — one's gaze, one's resolve, or one's stomach. Often appears in set expressions.

glosses: to be granted, to be blessed with
to be granted, to be given, to receive (from a superior or from heaven)
explanations: To receive something valuable from a person of higher status, or from a divine or fate-like source. Implies gratitude and humility.
To be blessed with a child. A respectful and joyful way to express the birth or conception of a child.

glosses: to recommend, to endorse, to push for
to recommend, to endorse, to nominate
to support enthusiastically, to be a fan of (modern slang)
explanations: To put someone or something forward as a candidate, recommendation, or choice. Used when supporting or endorsing a person for a position, or recommending something as the best option.
In modern Japanese, especially among younger speakers, to passionately support a celebrity, character, or idol. Related to the noun 推し (おし, one's favorite).
The hands and feet collectively, or all four limbs of a person or animal.
A person who acts as an extension of someone else's will, carrying out their orders faithfully. Often used for subordinates or loyal followers.
A specialized method or skill used in art, craft, or other creative fields. Emphasizes the technical or methodological aspect of how something is done.
Practical ability or proficiency acquired through training and experience, especially in a trade, craft, or technical field.
Describes treatment, care, or hospitality that is notably generous, thorough, and considerate. Often used for services, support, or reception.

glosses: to fold up, to fold flat, to collapse
explanations: To fold something into a compact shape by bending it over on itself, or to collapse a structure into a smaller form for storage or transport.

glosses: to slip out; to stand out
to slip out, to sneak out, to escape
to stand out, to surpass, to excel
explanations: To leave a place quietly or without being noticed, or to escape from a situation or confinement.
To be noticeably superior to others in ability, appearance, or quality. To rise above the group.

glosses: to cling to; to embrace tightly
to cling to, to embrace tightly, to throw one's arms around
explanations: To grab hold of someone or something tightly with both arms. Implies a sudden or emotional embrace, often out of joy, fear, or affection.

glosses: to suppress; to restrain; to control
to suppress, to restrain, to hold back
to curb, to keep down, to limit
explanations: To keep feelings, impulses, or reactions from being expressed or from getting out of control.
To prevent something from increasing or spreading, such as costs, inflation, or symptoms.
A formal expression of disapproval or opposition against a decision, action, or situation perceived as unjust or wrong.
The act of breaking through or overcoming an obstacle, barrier, convention, or stalemate. Often used for breaking records or destroying old systems or norms.

glosses: from time to time, occasionally, at times
explanations: At irregular intervals, now and then. Slightly more literary than ときどき.

glosses: to confine; to shut in; to cram in
to confine, to shut in, to lock away
to cram in, to stuff in, to force into
explanations: To force someone or something into a confined space and keep them there. Can be used for physical confinement or figurative suppression.
To push or force something into a tight or limited space.
The process of pulling out or separating a specific substance or component from a mixture or source. Common in scientific and technical contexts.
The process of selecting specific items from a larger set, such as data extraction or random sampling.
The act of making something larger in size, scope, or capacity. Used for physical spaces, systems, territories, and abstract concepts like power or influence.
The act or state of maintaining something over a period of time without interruption. Often used for efforts, conditions, or systems that need to be kept going.

glosses: one's pet theory, personal opinion, cherished view
explanations: A strongly held personal opinion or viewpoint that someone consistently maintains and expresses. Often implies the person has held this view for a long time and brings it up regularly.

glosses: to point at; to indicate with one's finger
to point at, to indicate with one's finger
explanations: To extend one's finger toward a person, object, or direction to indicate it. Can also be used figuratively to mean singling someone out for criticism.
A quantitative or qualitative measure used to evaluate, compare, or track the state or progress of something. Common in economics, business, and policy contexts.

glosses: to muster; to summon; to wring out
to muster, to summon, to squeeze out
explanations: To gather every last bit of one's courage, strength, or voice through great effort. Implies pushing oneself to the limit to produce something.

glosses: illustration, picture inserted in a text
explanations: An illustration or picture inserted within the pages of a book, magazine, or other printed text to complement or decorate the writing.

glosses: predation, preying on, catching and eating prey
explanations: The act of an animal catching and eating another animal for food. A biological/ecological term.
The act of unfairly taking advantage of others for profit or benefit, especially in labor or economic relationships. A strongly negative term implying systematic unfairness.
The act of forming an opinion or conclusion based on incomplete information or indirect evidence. Less certain than a conclusion based on proof.
The act of pulling back troops, forces, or operations from a position or area. Also used for business withdrawal from a market.
The act of attributing human characteristics, emotions, or behaviors to non-human things such as animals, objects, or abstract concepts. Common in literature, art, and pop culture.

glosses: strategy guide, walkthrough, tips for clearing
explanations: The act of attacking and capturing a fortress, city, or position. A military term.
A guide or set of strategies for completing a game, challenge, or difficult task. Extremely common in gaming culture.
The act of voluntarily giving up a right, claim, responsibility, or possession. Often used in legal and formal contexts.

glosses: leaving as is, leaving unattended, neglect
explanations: The act of leaving something or someone alone without taking action, either intentionally or through negligence. Often carries a negative nuance of irresponsible inaction.
The act of deliberately provoking someone into anger, aggression, or action. Can refer to political provocation, personal taunting, or suggestive behavior.
The act of putting or placing something into something else. Used for physical insertion, as well as inserting text, images, or scenes into a document, film, or other work.
A fanatical religious or ideological group, often with a charismatic leader and secretive or manipulative practices. In Japanese, used primarily in the negative sense of a dangerous or harmful group.
A work of art, film, or other cultural product with a small but passionate fan base. Used as a modifier in compounds like カルト{映画|えいが} (cult film).
The act of judging or making a decision, especially in sports or competitions. Also refers to the person who judges (a judge or referee).
A light, bouncy way of moving by hopping on alternate feet. Often associated with children or a happy, carefree mood.
To pass over or omit something, such as a step in a process, a track on an album, or a turn in a game.
Discarded metal, machinery, or other material that can be recycled or is no longer usable. Used for junk or waste destined for disposal or recycling.
A newspaper or magazine clipping, or the practice of collecting such clippings. Short for スクラップブック (scrapbook).
A permanent design made by inserting ink into the skin. In Japanese, タトゥー specifically refers to Western-style tattoos, as distinct from traditional Japanese {入|い}れ{墨|ずみ} (irezumi).

A person who directs or manages a project, program, or creative production. Commonly used in television, advertising, and business contexts. In TV production, the ディレクター handles on-site direction, as distinct from the プロデューサー who oversees the overall project.
A device or scheme for catching or deceiving someone. Used both for physical traps and figurative traps or tricks.
In soccer, the technique of stopping and controlling the ball with the foot, chest, or other body part.
A mythical winged, fire-breathing creature from Western mythology. In Japanese, ドラゴン refers specifically to the Western-style dragon, as distinct from {竜|りゅう} or {龍|りゅう} (the East Asian dragon).

An exaggerated or uncontrollable emotional outburst, typically involving screaming, crying, or irrational behavior. In everyday Japanese, used to describe someone who is emotionally volatile or prone to fits of anger.
The punctuation mark (.) used at the end of a sentence in Western writing. In Japanese, the equivalent is the {句点|くてん} (。).
The end or conclusion of something. Used figuratively to mean putting a definitive end to a matter or chapter in one's life.
A state of calm, tranquility, or absence of conflict. Most commonly encountered in the compound ピースサイン (peace sign) and the gesture of holding up two fingers.
An individual part or unit of something, such as a puzzle piece or a piece in a game.
The act of playing a sport, game, or musical instrument, or a specific action or maneuver in sports. Used broadly for any kind of active participation in games or performance.
A person who oversees and manages the production of a film, television program, music recording, or other creative work. Responsible for budgeting, scheduling, and overall project management.
A large, frightening, or dangerous creature, real or imaginary. Widely used in games, anime, and fantasy contexts.
A person who is extremely demanding, unreasonable, or exceptional in some way. Used in compounds like モンスターペアレント (helicopter/monster parent).
A dried grape, used as a snack and in baking, cereals, and other food.
The lowest or most unfavorable ranking. Used in Japanese primarily in rankings and lists to indicate the worst result, the bottom position, or a record low.

The act of projecting one's emotions onto someone or something, such as a fictional character, or becoming emotionally invested in a story or situation. Originally a psychological term (Einfühlung), now widely used in everyday contexts.

A system during the Edo period (1603–1868) that required feudal lords (daimyō) to alternate their residence between their home domains and Edo (present-day Tokyo). This compelled lords to spend roughly every other year in Edo, keeping their families there as de facto hostages, which served to maintain the shogunate's control.

The residence of the Emperor or other members of the imperial family. Most commonly refers to the Kyoto Imperial Palace ({京都御所|きょうとごしょ}), the former main residence of the Emperor before the capital moved to Tokyo.
Business or errands, especially those conducted on behalf of the government, the imperial household, or a person of high status. The {御|ご} prefix adds formality and respect.
The apprehension of a criminal. Historically, the cry 「{御用|ごよう}だ！」 was used by Edo-period constables when making an arrest, and it remains well known from period dramas.

The traditional Japanese art of espionage, sabotage, and unconventional warfare practiced by ninja. Encompasses stealth, disguise, martial arts, survival skills, and various other techniques. In modern usage, also refers to the fictionalized version of these skills depicted in manga and anime.

The practice of chanting the name of Amida Buddha, specifically the phrase 「{南無阿弥陀仏|なむあみだぶつ}」 (Namu Amida Butsu). Central to Pure Land Buddhism ({浄土宗|じょうどしゅう} and {浄土真宗|じょうどしんしゅう}), where it is believed to lead to rebirth in the Pure Land.

A small, concealable weapon designed to be thrown, historically associated with ninja. Comes in various shapes including star-shaped ({多角形|たかくけい}) and straight needle-like forms ({棒手裏剣|ぼうしゅりけん}). Widely known internationally through ninja-themed media.
The period before a war. In Japanese without further specification, this almost always refers to the period before World War II, particularly the era before Japan's defeat in 1945.

The period after a war. In Japanese without further specification, this almost always refers to the period after World War II, from Japan's surrender in 1945 onward. Used broadly for the social, political, and economic changes that followed.
The act of casting light, an image, or a shadow onto a surface. Used for projecting images onto screens as well as for the mathematical/geometric concept of projection.
The manifestation or reflection of inner feelings, thoughts, or circumstances in something external. Often used in psychology for the unconscious transfer of one's own feelings onto others.

The fundamental reason or basis for something. A somewhat literary word used in the pattern 「...の{所以|ゆえん}」 to express why something is so. Often used to explain the essential nature or defining characteristic of something.
The attitude of questioning or doubting the truth, validity, or reliability of something. A formal term used in intellectual, philosophical, and critical contexts.

A class of supernatural being from Indian mythology, adopted into Buddhism. In Japanese, {夜叉|やしゃ} typically refers to a fierce, terrifying demonic being, though in the original Indian tradition yaksha could be either benevolent or malevolent.
Used figuratively to describe someone who is terrifyingly fierce, ruthless, or relentless.

The direction considered auspicious for a given year, determined by the Chinese zodiac. Traditionally, facing this direction while performing certain activities was believed to bring good fortune. In modern Japan, most commonly associated with the Setsubun custom of eating ehōmaki (lucky direction sushi roll).
Complete or near-complete absence of light. Used both literally for physical darkness and figuratively for a state of ignorance, despair, or uncertainty.
Describes something that is considered ideal, hoped for, or preferred. Often used in formal contexts to express what is recommended or wished for, rather than what is strictly required.
A set point in time by which something must be completed or submitted.
The date after which something is no longer valid or usable, such as a product's shelf life or a document's validity.
A stick or rod used as a support while walking. Includes mobility aids for the elderly or injured, hiking poles, and ceremonial or decorative staffs.
A very short period of time. Emphasizes the transience or brevity of an experience, often with a poignant or wistful nuance.
One's genuine inner thoughts or feelings, as opposed to what is expressed outwardly. Implies a gap between what someone says or shows and what they actually feel.

glosses: to push up, to shove upward
to boost, to drive up, to elevate
explanations: To physically push something upward using force.
To raise or increase something, such as numbers, rankings, or status. Commonly used in economics and business contexts.
Something that serves as the basis or grounds for a judgment, action, or claim.
A person, thing, or idea that provides emotional or psychological support and stability.

glosses: home, birthplace, authentic place of origin
explanations: The place where something originates or where the most authentic version is found. Used especially for food, crafts, and cultural practices.
The act of selecting or calling on a specific person by name for a role, task, or action.
Items used for writing, drawing, and desk work, such as pens, pencils, erasers, notebooks, rulers, and scissors.
A surface that is tilted at an angle rather than being flat or vertical. Used for natural terrain such as mountainsides and hills, as well as man-made inclines.

A person who has just graduated or is about to graduate from a school or university. In Japan, this term is closely tied to the annual mass-hiring system where companies recruit students before graduation.
Being beaten in a battle, competition, election, or conflict. A formal word for losing that carries a sense of gravity and finality.
A person's innate character or nature that is normally hidden beneath a social mask. Often implies that the true nature is negative or surprising when revealed.
A person who has been taught or mentored by a particular teacher or master. Implies a personal, lasting relationship between teacher and student.

glosses: pointer, needle (of a compass or gauge)
explanations: A principle or set of directions that guides decision-making or action. Commonly used in official, business, and policy contexts.
The physical needle or pointer of a measuring instrument such as a compass or dial.
Something understood or agreed upon without being explicitly stated. Refers to silent understanding, unspoken rules, or implied consent.

glosses: main topic, main subject, real issue
explanations: The central or primary topic of a conversation, meeting, or presentation. Often used when transitioning from preliminary remarks or small talk to the actual matter at hand.
Materials used for teaching and learning, including textbooks, workbooks, handouts, digital content, and other instructional resources.
The state of being recently married, or a recently married person or couple. Typically refers to the first year or so of marriage.
The design and arrangement of dance movements and sequences for a performance. Also refers to the movements themselves once arranged.
The act of catching and taking hold of an animal, person, or object, typically by force or with a trap. Most commonly used for animals.

glosses: customer service, serving customers, attending to guests
explanations: The act of serving, attending to, or interacting with customers or guests in a business setting such as a shop, restaurant, or hotel.
The authority or power to govern a country or region. Also used to refer to a specific administration or government in power.
The act of saving or being saved from danger, suffering, or despair. Can be concrete (physical rescue) or abstract (spiritual salvation, emotional relief).
Written works, records, or documents used as sources of information, especially in academic research and historical study.

glosses: shelf life, keeping quality, how well something keeps
explanations: How long food or other perishable items remain fresh or usable. Describes the ability of a product to stay in good condition over time.

glosses: main occupation, primary business, day job
explanations: One's principal line of work or core business activity, as distinguished from side jobs, hobbies, or secondary ventures.
A critical evaluation or commentary on a book, typically published in a newspaper, magazine, or academic journal.
The act of possessing or holding items in a collection, typically used for museums, libraries, or private collectors who maintain works of art, books, or historical artifacts.
Operating something by hand rather than automatically. Used for machines, devices, and systems that require direct human control, as opposed to automatic or automated operation.
Made by hand rather than by machine or factory. Emphasizes the craftsmanship or personal effort involved in making something.
A significant advance or breakthrough in technology that brings about major changes in industry, society, or daily life. Often used in business, economic, and policy contexts.
The act of dropping or releasing something from a height, such as dropping bombs from aircraft or dropping supplies by parachute.
Committing capital, resources, or effort into a project, business, or initiative. A figurative extension of the idea of 'throwing something in.'
The act of giving medicine, drugs, or other therapeutic substances to a patient. A medical and pharmaceutical term that covers oral, intravenous, and other methods of delivery.
The physical act of throwing or putting something into a container, machine, or space.
Committing personnel, funds, time, or other resources to a task, project, or situation. Common in business, military, and policy contexts.
A protein produced by the immune system to identify and neutralize foreign substances such as bacteria and viruses. A key term in medicine, biology, and health-related discussions.

Formal negotiations between parties with differing interests, aimed at reaching a compromise or agreement. More formal than everyday negotiation and often involves institutional or organizational parties.
Addressing the root cause of a problem rather than surface symptoms. Used to describe reforms, changes, or solutions that go to the very foundation of an issue.
An official order or instruction issued by a person or organization in authority. Used in military, governmental, and organizational contexts where directives flow from higher to lower levels.
The formal act of granting or awarding something of honor or value, such as a degree, prize, medal, or certificate. Used in ceremonial and institutional contexts.
The act of collecting or extracting samples, specimens, or natural materials for analysis, research, or use. Common in scientific, medical, and environmental contexts.
The deep, sustained pursuit of truth, knowledge, or meaning. Implies intellectual or philosophical seeking, rather than a simple search for physical objects.

glosses: business entertainment, wining and dining clients
explanations: The practice of entertaining business clients or partners, typically through dinners, golf outings, or other hospitality. A central concept in Japanese corporate culture for building and maintaining business relationships.
The more general act of receiving and serving guests or visitors, including offering tea, food, or other forms of hospitality.
Physical touching or coming into contact between objects, surfaces, or people.
Making contact or establishing communication with a person, organization, or group. Often implies an initial or deliberate approach.
The act of presenting or showing something to someone, such as displaying identification, presenting evidence, or putting forward a proposal or conditions.
The Celsius temperature scale, in which water freezes at 0 degrees and boils at 100 degrees. Japan uses the Celsius scale for all temperature measurements in daily life, weather, and science.
A formal recommendation or endorsement of a product, practice, or course of action. Carries an official or authoritative tone, implying that a qualified party has evaluated and approved something.
Actively promoting or driving forward a plan, policy, project, or initiative. Common in business, government, and organizational contexts.
The physical force that drives a vehicle, vessel, or rocket forward. A technical term used in engineering and aerospace.
The act of providing, offering, or supplying something — such as information, services, goods, or resources — to someone. Widely used in business, broadcasting, and everyday contexts.
The act of officially withdrawing or taking back a statement, proposal, decision, or claim that was previously made. Used in formal, legal, and political contexts.
The act of formally abolishing, repealing, or doing away with a law, regulation, system, or restriction. Implies complete elimination rather than mere revision.
A fundamental change in one's attitudes, behavior, or moral character, especially turning away from wrongdoing or bad habits. Implies genuine inner transformation rather than a superficial change.
A value expressed as a number, used in measurements, calculations, data analysis, and statistics. Refers to the quantitative representation of something rather than qualitative description.
An actively hostile or antagonistic stance toward another person, group, or entity. Implies a deliberate and ongoing adversarial relationship, not a momentary disagreement.

A small, affordable paperback book in the standard Japanese bunko format (approximately A6 size, 105 × 148 mm). A distinctive feature of the Japanese publishing industry, bunko editions are typically reprints of hardcover books released at a lower price point.
A confident, definitive statement made without hesitation or qualification. Implies the speaker is certain of what they are saying and is willing to commit fully to the claim.
Losing a war. In Japanese, this word most commonly refers to Japan's defeat in World War II, but it can also describe any military defeat or, more broadly, losing in a competition or match.
The act of saving or freeing someone from a dangerous, difficult, or life-threatening situation such as a disaster, accident, captivity, or emergency.
The act of searching for something by investigating thoroughly, or exploring an unknown area or topic.

glosses: to come in contact with; to adjoin; to receive, to treat
to come in contact with, to touch, to adjoin
to receive, to treat, to deal with
explanations: To be physically adjacent to or in contact with something. Also used for encountering information, culture, or experiences.
To interact with or treat a person in a particular manner.
To discharge a firearm or weapon at a target. Also used for launching projectiles such as arrows or missiles.
The act of withdrawing troops, personnel, or operations from a location. Used in military, business, and general contexts.
The act of removing or packing up equipment, materials, or structures from a site.

glosses: to reform, to revise; to examine
to reform, to revise, to correct
to examine, to inspect, to check
explanations: To change something for the better, to amend or correct faults, habits, or systems.
To look at something carefully to verify or confirm it. Often used for formal inspections such as checking tickets or identification.
The act of repairing or renovating buildings, infrastructure, or facilities to restore or improve them.

glosses: offense and defense, attack and defense
explanations: The back-and-forth between attacking and defending. Used in military contexts, sports, debates, and competitive situations.
The act of releasing or emitting something such as gas, energy, heat, or stored goods into the environment or market.
The act of saving someone's life, or equipment and procedures designed for that purpose.
The act of saving or providing relief to people in distress, suffering, or difficult circumstances. Used in social, religious, legal, and humanitarian contexts.
A school where people learn to drive and prepare for their driver's license. By extension, any training facility for learning specific practical skills.

glosses: keeping at arm's length; intentional walk (baseball)
explanations: Showing respect on the surface but keeping one's distance. Avoiding a person or thing that is difficult, unpleasant, or troublesome.
In baseball, intentionally walking a batter by pitching four balls outside the strike zone to avoid letting a strong hitter swing.
The characteristic style or manner in which a text is written, including word choice, sentence structure, tone, and rhythm.
Tangible or intangible items of cultural significance, including buildings, artworks, crafts, performing arts, and customs that are deemed worthy of preservation.
The act of approving of and giving backing to a person, opinion, policy, or movement. Also used for physical support or structural bearing.
Something that prevents normal functioning or progress. Often used in the pattern ～に{支障|ししょう}がある/をきたす (to cause problems for).
The act of uncovering and publicly revealing wrongdoing, crimes, or violations, often leading to legal action. Commonly used for law enforcement actions against illegal activities.

glosses: to shake, to rock, to undermine
to undermine, to destabilize, to threaten
explanations: To cause something to shake or sway physically.
To shake the foundations of something figuratively — to threaten the stability of a system, belief, position, or relationship.
A state of readiness or organizational arrangement for dealing with a situation. Refers to the setup or stance taken in preparation for action.
Something that has been decided or set in advance by rules, regulations, or agreement. Used as a modifier before nouns to indicate that something follows an established standard.
The tips of one's fingers, or one's hands in terms of manual skill and dexterity.
A person used as a tool by someone more powerful. Carries a negative connotation of being manipulated.
A person who serves under and follows the orders of someone more powerful. Often implies a boss-subordinate relationship in criminal or villainous contexts.
A person or side that has lost in a competition, battle, or contest. The opposite of {勝者|しょうしゃ} (winner).
A person whose profession is teaching, typically at a school or educational institution. A formal and official term for the teaching profession.
The act of broadcasting a program or film on television or projecting it on a screen.

glosses: historical anecdote, old story, classical tale
explanations: A story or anecdote from ancient times, particularly from Chinese classics, that has been passed down and often serves as the origin of a proverb or set phrase.

glosses: point of contact, connection; contact point
point of contact, connection, common ground
explanations: A point where two things meet or connect, often used figuratively for a shared interest, relationship, or link between people, groups, or ideas.
A physical point where two things touch, especially an electrical contact point in a circuit or device.
The act of attacking or going on the offensive. Used in sports, games, military strategy, and figurative contexts for taking an aggressive approach.
A written or printed document, especially one with official, legal, or formal significance.

glosses: many, a great number of, numerous
explanations: A large number of something. Used to express that there are very many instances, items, or examples of something.

glosses: travel destination, place one is visiting
explanations: The place where one is staying or visiting while traveling. Emphasizes the destination as experienced during the trip, not as a planned target before departure.
A person traveling on a vehicle such as a train, airplane, or ship. A formal term used in transportation and official contexts.

glosses: to depart on a journey, to set out
to pass away, to depart this world
explanations: To leave on a trip or journey. Carries a sense of embarking on something significant, not just a short outing.
A euphemism for dying, likening death to setting out on a final journey.
The act of deciding on a date for an event, or the scheduled date itself. Used for formal or important occasions such as weddings, ceremonies, and meetings.
The count or total of days for a given period, process, or duration.
An alcoholic beverage brewed from rice, water, and koji mold. The term specifically distinguishes traditional Japanese alcohol from foreign alcoholic drinks.
Food prepared in the Japanese culinary tradition. A broad term encompassing everything from sushi and tempura to everyday home cooking.
Describes people of Japanese ancestry living abroad, or companies and organizations with Japanese origins or connections.
A person's surname before marriage or a legal name change. In Japan, married couples must share one surname by law, so one partner's pre-marriage name becomes their former surname.
The traditional lunisolar calendar used in Japan before the adoption of the Gregorian calendar in 1873. Still referenced for traditional festivals and seasonal events.

glosses: promptly, right after; as soon as
explanations: Doing something quickly or immediately, without wasting time.
Used as a suffix after nouns indicating a time or event to mean 'right after' or 'as soon as.' Read as そうそう in this usage.

glosses: to rise, to ascend (sun, smoke, etc.)
explanations: Used for things that rise naturally — the sun, moon, smoke, steam, etc. Describes upward motion of natural phenomena rather than physical climbing by a person.

glosses: to reveal, to disclose; to spend (the night)
to reveal, to disclose, to confess
to spend (the night), to stay up all night
explanations: To make something hidden or secret known. Often used for revealing one's identity, a secret, or the truth.
To pass the night doing something. Often used in the pattern 〜{明|あ}かす to mean spending the entire night engaged in an activity.

glosses: coming to light, public knowledge, exposure
explanations: The state of something hidden becoming publicly known. Almost always used in the fixed phrase {明|あか}るみに{出|で}る (to come to light).

glosses: to reflect, to project, to show on screen
to project, to show on screen
explanations: To cause an image to appear on a reflective surface such as a mirror or water.
To display images or video on a screen, projector, monitor, or similar device.

glosses: to be reflected, to appear (on screen)
to be reflected, to be mirrored
to appear (on screen/in photo), to come out
explanations: For an image to appear on a reflective surface such as a mirror, water, or glass.
For an image to appear on a screen, in a photograph, or through a camera. Also used to describe how something looks or comes across visually.
The present time, especially when contrasted with the past. A formal expression used to introduce current trends, situations, or changes in society.
The time period shortly after midday, roughly from 12:00 to 2:00 PM. Indicates the time has just passed noon.
Matters and events happening in the world at the present time, especially in politics, economics, and society. Used as a compound modifier before other nouns.
A film, TV show, or theater production set in a historical period, typically pre-Meiji Japan. Often features samurai, feudal lords, and life during the Edo period.
The price of goods, stocks, or property at the current moment, as determined by market conditions. Changes over time based on supply and demand.

glosses: point in time, as of (a certain time)
explanations: A specific moment or point on a timeline. Used to indicate when something was true or when a decision was made, often emphasizing that the situation may have changed since then.

glosses: time slot, time zone, time period
explanations: A range or block of time within a day, such as morning hours, rush hour, or a specific broadcast slot.
A geographical region that observes a uniform standard time, such as Japan Standard Time or Eastern Time.
Weather with a cloudless or mostly cloudless sky. A somewhat formal term used in weather reports, written descriptions, and set phrases.
The quality or degree of hot weather. Derived from the adjective {暑|あつ}い (hot weather). Refers specifically to atmospheric heat, not the temperature of objects.
Communicating something without stating it directly. The message is conveyed through hints, implications, or indirect means rather than explicit words.

glosses: abusive language, verbal abuse, offensive remark
explanations: Harsh, rude, or hurtful words directed at someone. Stronger than mere rudeness — implies language that is aggressive, demeaning, or clearly out of line.

The overall visual appearance of an area, especially as shaped by natural features, architecture, and urban planning. Often used in contexts involving preservation and regulation of the visual environment.
A formal closing phrase used at the end of a letter or written correspondence. The standard pair to the opening {拝啓|はいけい} (Dear Sir/Madam).
The official teachings or beliefs of a religion, philosophy, or ideology. The fundamental principles that adherents are expected to accept and follow.

glosses: death in battle, killed in action
explanations: Dying in war or combat. Used for soldiers and combatants who lose their lives during military conflict.
A period during which a war is being fought. Often used as a modifier ({戦時|せんじ}の/{戦時|せんじ}{中|ちゅう}の) to describe conditions, laws, or situations during war.
A woman on her wedding day or who has recently married. Used in formal and ceremonial contexts, especially in wedding speeches and announcements.
A man on his wedding day or who has recently married. Used in formal and ceremonial contexts, especially in wedding speeches and announcements.

glosses: new song, new piece of music
explanations: A recently composed or released song or musical piece. Commonly used in the music industry and everyday conversation about new releases.
Something that has just arrived or been added. Commonly used for new merchandise, email messages, news, or website content.

glosses: to apply, to give (charity), to carry out
to apply, to perform, to carry out
to give (charity), to bestow, to provide (aid)
explanations: To apply a treatment, decoration, or process to something. Used for putting something into effect on a target.
To give to those in need, often implying charity or benevolence. Has a somewhat formal or literary tone.

glosses: departure, setting out on a journey
explanations: The act of departing on a journey or trip. Often carries a poetic or emotional nuance, suggesting a significant life transition or new beginning.

glosses: journey, one's travels, road of travel
explanations: The course or path of a journey. A literary term that evokes the experience and process of traveling, rather than just the destination.
The breaking off or complete cessation of a relationship, connection, or lineage. Implies a definitive, often permanent end.
A writer of exceptional talent and lasting influence. Used to describe authors whose works have become part of the literary canon.
The art of writing; literature as a creative and artistic pursuit. Encompasses novels, poetry, drama, essays, and other written forms of artistic expression.
Language used in formal writing as opposed to spoken language. In Japanese linguistics, refers specifically to the classical written style based on pre-modern grammar.
At some point in the future, whether soon or after some time. Implies that the outcome is inevitable.

glosses: day and night, around the clock
explanations: Daytime and nighttime together, often implying continuous activity without rest. Used to emphasize that something goes on without stopping.

glosses: going to bed early, early bedtime
explanations: The practice of going to sleep early in the evening. Often paired with {早起|はやお}き (early rising) as a healthy habit.

glosses: formal clothes, festive attire, best clothes
explanations: Special clothing worn for celebrations, ceremonies, and other important occasions. Traditionally refers to kimono or other Japanese-style formal garments, but can also refer to any dressy outfit.
Acting secretly to influence events, especially in politics or power struggles. Carries a negative connotation of covert, often self-serving manipulation.
Complete darkness or absence of light. A literary term for deep, total darkness.
A metaphorical sense referring to a period or state of evil, corruption, ignorance, or despair.
Lacking originality or distinction; ordinary and unremarkable. Used to describe ideas, expressions, or things that are unimaginative or hackneyed.
The total amount of money earned in a single month, typically referring to salary or wages before or after tax.
A system of payment or contract calculated on a monthly basis. Most commonly seen on parking lot signs indicating monthly rental spaces.
The traditional Japanese custom of admiring the autumn moon, especially the full moon in mid-September ({十五夜|じゅうごや}). Involves displaying pampas grass and eating rice dumplings.
A style of serving food with a raw egg on top, where the yolk resembles the full moon. Common with soba, udon, and hamburgers.
Having a bad or damaging effect on health, the environment, or society. Used for substances, organisms, content, and other things that cause harm.
The state of having been judged responsible for a crime in a court of law. A legal term used for criminal verdicts.
Having a positive or helpful effect. Used for information, experiences, activities, or substances that provide some advantage or benefit.
People who share a common purpose or interest and voluntarily come together for a cause or activity. Implies willing participation rather than obligation.

glosses: prominent, leading, one of the best
prominent, leading, one of the best, top-ranking
explanations: Being counted among the very best or most notable in a given category. Implies that something or someone ranks highly among peers.
Having great power, authority, or influence. Used for people, organizations, or entities with significant sway.
Having a high likelihood of being correct or winning. Used for candidates, theories, leads, or possibilities that are considered the most probable.
An open-air market held in the early morning, typically selling fresh produce, seafood, and local goods. A traditional feature of many Japanese towns and cities.
The most bad or undesirable; the lowest possible quality or outcome. Used to describe situations, conditions, or scenarios that are as bad as they can be.
Used as a strong negative evaluation in casual speech, expressing that something is really bad or unpleasant. Often used as an exclamation.
The best or most appropriate for a particular purpose, situation, or person. Indicates that something fits the requirements perfectly.
The most advanced or newest stage of development in a field. Often used for technology, research, fashion, and other areas where progress is measured.
The thing that should be dealt with before all others; the most important matter requiring attention.
Coming at the end of a process or series of events; the last or conclusive stage. Often used adverbially with に to mean 'ultimately' or 'in the end'.
Something not yet known or experienced. Refers to areas, fields, or things that have not been explored or understood.
Lacking full development in skill, knowledge, or ability. Used for people who have not yet reached a sufficient level of proficiency.
Not yet ripe or mature. Used for fruit or crops that have not reached the stage for harvesting or eating.
A person who has not yet reached the age of legal adulthood. In Japan, the age of majority was lowered from 20 to 18 in April 2022.
Wood that has been processed for use as a building material or in manufacturing. Refers to cut and prepared wood rather than living trees.

glosses: nut, berry, fruit of a tree
explanations: The fruit, nut, or berry produced by a tree or woody plant. A general term that covers acorns, chestnuts, walnuts, berries, and similar natural tree products.

glosses: presence or absence, whether something exists
explanations: Whether something is present or not; the question of existence or non-existence. Used in formal and written contexts to ask about or indicate whether something applies.
Having value or purpose; worth spending time or effort on. Used to describe experiences, time, discussions, and activities that produce something positive.
A person who has the right to vote in elections. In Japan, all citizens aged 18 and older have the right to vote.

glosses: expert, learned person, person of knowledge
explanations: A person with specialized knowledge or expertise in a particular field. Often used in formal and governmental contexts to refer to advisors or committee members.
A document or communication in written form. Emphasizes that something is put down in writing rather than communicated orally. Used in formal, legal, and business contexts.
The style or design of written characters, whether in calligraphy, printing, or digital fonts. Covers both traditional calligraphic styles and modern digital typefaces.

An organized criminal group. The official and legal term used by Japanese police and media for what is colloquially known as yakuza. These groups are the subject of extensive anti-organized-crime legislation in Japan.
Applicable to or affecting all people, places, or situations without exception. Describes values, truths, or phenomena that are not limited to a particular culture, era, or group.
Having a bright, clear, and cheerful appearance or expression. Often used to describe a person's face or expression that shows happiness, relief, or pride, especially on a momentous occasion.

glosses: new bud, new sprout, young shoot
explanations: A newly emerging bud or shoot on a plant. Associated with spring and the start of new growth.
The act of creating or establishing something new, such as an institution, facility, department, or system. Also used as a modifier to describe something newly created.
To write something down clearly and explicitly so there is no ambiguity. Used in formal, legal, and business contexts for information that must be recorded precisely.

glosses: explicit indication, clearly showing, making clear
explanations: To indicate or show something clearly and unambiguously, whether in writing, speech, or action. Broader than writing alone — can apply to any form of clear communication or display.

glosses: final stage, terminal phase, end period
explanations: The last stage or closing period of something, whether a historical era, a process, or a disease. Often implies decline or approaching end.
The primary or central part of a device, system, or object, as distinguished from its accessories, peripherals, or attachments.
The true nature or essential form of something. Used in philosophical, religious, or narrative contexts to refer to something's real identity.

glosses: real name, true name, birth name
explanations: A person's actual legal name, as opposed to a stage name, pen name, nickname, or pseudonym.
The property of certain substances to emit radiation through the decay of atomic nuclei. Also used loosely in everyday language to refer to radiation or radioactive contamination in general.
To revise or change established standards, prices, rules, or rates. Typically used for official changes to numerical values or established norms rather than text.
Refers to expressions, phrases, or usages that have become established through long custom and repeated use, even if they may not follow strict grammatical or semantic rules.

Something or someone that provides support, whether physical (holding something up) or emotional/figurative (being a source of strength or encouragement). Often used for people who serve as a source of emotional strength.

glosses: stand, platform; counter for machines and vehicles
counter for machines, vehicles, and large equipment
explanations: A raised surface or structure that supports something. Used for tables, stands, platforms, and bases.
Used to count machines, vehicles, appliances, and similar large mechanical or electronic items. One of the most common counters in daily life.

glosses: number, issue (of a magazine or publication)
designation number, name (of a ship, train, typhoon, etc.)
explanations: A sequential number assigned to a publication, edition, or installment. Commonly used for magazines, journals, and periodical issues.
A number or name used to identify a specific ship, train service, typhoon, space mission, or other named entity.
A state of peaceful coexistence, agreement, or balance among people or things. A central concept in Japanese culture.
Used as a prefix to indicate something is Japanese in style or origin, as opposed to Western ({洋|よう}). Common in compound words describing food, clothing, architecture, and other cultural elements.
Happening quickly and without warning. Describes events, changes, or actions that occur with little or no notice.
Describes a slope, hill, or curve that rises or falls at a sharp angle.
Requiring immediate attention or action. Used for matters that cannot wait.
A celestial body that generates its own light through nuclear fusion, as opposed to planets which reflect light. The sun is the nearest star to Earth.

glosses: revision, amendment (of a text, document, or publication)
explanations: The act of correcting, updating, or improving the content of a written work such as a book, textbook, dictionary, or manual. Focuses on textual content rather than legal or institutional rules.

glosses: New Year, the beginning of the new year
explanations: A formal and slightly literary term for the New Year period. Used in greetings, advertisements, and announcements around the start of the year.

glosses: to get new; to replace with new
getting something new, having something newly made
explanations: The act of acquiring a new item, especially clothing, furniture, or equipment, often to replace something old or worn out. Implies purchasing or having something custom-made.
The orientation or direction as indicated by a compass or relative to a fixed reference point. Used in navigation, geography, and traditional practices like feng shui.

glosses: Lunar New Year, Chinese New Year
explanations: The New Year as observed in the traditional lunisolar calendar, falling in late January or February. Widely celebrated in China, Korea, Vietnam, and other Asian countries. In Japan, it is observed in some regions such as Okinawa and by Chinese communities.

glosses: codification, putting into explicit written form
explanations: The act of formally writing down rules, agreements, policies, or understandings that may have previously existed only as unwritten conventions. Often used in legal, business, and organizational contexts.
The act of stating something clearly and unambiguously, leaving no room for doubt or misinterpretation. Often used when someone takes a definitive stance or makes an official position clear.

glosses: to project; to reflect; to portray
to project, to display (on a screen or surface)
to reflect, to reveal, to portray
explanations: To show an image, video, or visual content on a screen, wall, or other surface using a projector, camera, or similar device.
To make something visible or apparent; to depict or represent a situation, emotion, or reality. Used figuratively for media, art, or observation.

glosses: to write in, to fill in
to write in, to fill in, to enter (information)
explanations: To write text, numbers, or data into a designated space such as a form, blank, margin, or document.

glosses: to begin writing; to list out, to extract
to begin writing, to start writing
to write out, to list, to extract (in writing)
explanations: To start the act of writing. Used when someone begins composing a letter, essay, or other written work.
To write down items from a larger body of information; to list or enumerate things by writing them out.

glosses: way of writing, how to write
way of writing, how to write, writing style
explanations: The method, manner, or technique of writing something. Covers both the physical act of forming characters and the stylistic approach to composing text.
A person responsible for keeping records, taking minutes, or handling correspondence in an organization, committee, or political body.

glosses: minimum, bare minimum, at the very least
explanations: The lowest acceptable amount, degree, or standard. Used both as a noun and as an adverb (with の or に) to indicate the absolute minimum requirement.
The most forward position in a conflict, or figuratively, the leading edge of a field, industry, or area of activity. Used both in military and metaphorical contexts.
The period when something is at its most active, productive, or prosperous. Used for seasons, industries, careers, civilizations, and other things that have a high point.

glosses: to bundle, to tie together; to lead, to unite
to bundle, to tie together, to gather into a bunch
to lead, to unite, to bring together (people or groups)
explanations: To collect loose items and bind them together into a single bundle or bunch. Used for physical objects like hair, flowers, documents, or sticks.
To organize and lead a group of people, or to bring diverse individuals or factions together under unified direction.
The act of a non-Japanese person traveling to Japan for a visit, work, performance, or other purpose. Used from the perspective of someone already in Japan.
A person who comes to visit a home, office, or establishment. Slightly more formal than お客さん and often used in business or written contexts.
A person who lives in a village. Used in stories, historical contexts, news, and descriptions of rural life.
The craft or activity of shaping, carving, and building things from wood. Also refers to items produced through woodworking.

glosses: main text, body, main content (of a document, email, or book)
explanations: The primary content of a written work, as distinguished from headings, footnotes, appendices, subject lines, or other supplementary parts.

glosses: end, tail end, last part, conclusion
explanations: The very end or final portion of a document, list, sequence, or other ordered item. Often used in written or formal contexts.
The state of something not yet being completed. Used for works of art, buildings, projects, and other things that are still in progress or were left unfinished.

glosses: visiting a store, coming to a shop
explanations: The act of a customer going to or arriving at a store or restaurant. Commonly used from the shop's perspective to refer to customers who come in.

glosses: to be absorbed in; to spend one's days doing
to be absorbed in, to spend one's days doing, to be occupied with day and night
explanations: To devote oneself to a single activity from morning to night, day after day. Implies that the person does almost nothing else. Often used with に to mark the activity.
The specific words or phrasing used in a document, contract, or official text. Refers to how something is expressed in writing rather than the content itself.
A decorative pattern or design, especially one used in traditional arts, textiles, ceramics, or architecture. Often refers to established, named patterns with cultural significance.
The greatest possible degree or amount. Used as a noun to refer to the upper limit, or adverbially (often with に or の) to mean 'to the fullest extent possible.'
The smallest possible degree or amount. Used as a noun to refer to the lower limit, or adverbially (often with に or の) to mean 'to the minimum extent.'
The superlative of strong — the most powerful among a group. Used to describe people, teams, weapons, strategies, or anything that surpasses all others in strength or effectiveness.

glosses: shortest, minimum (in distance, time, or length)
explanations: The superlative of short — the least in distance, duration, or length among a group. Commonly used for routes, time periods, and records.
The superlative of fast — the greatest speed among a group. Used for vehicles, athletes, records, and also figuratively for the earliest availability of information or results.
The superlative of long — the greatest in length, distance, or duration among a group. Used for physical length, time periods, and records.

glosses: monthly period, span of a month, month-long (campaign or event)
explanations: A period spanning one month. Often used as a suffix attached to a campaign or awareness theme to indicate a designated month — similar to English constructions like 'Fire Prevention Month' or 'Breast Cancer Awareness Month.'

A serious emergency or crisis, especially one involving military conflict, national security threats, or large-scale disasters. In political and legal contexts, it specifically refers to armed conflicts or situations requiring military response.
Having a physical shape or form that can be perceived by the senses. Used in contrast to intangible or abstract things, especially in legal, cultural, and business contexts.
Having practical value or serving a useful purpose. A somewhat formal alternative to words like {便利|べんり} or {役に立つ|やくにたつ}, often used in written or academic contexts.

glosses: imperial court, the emperor and his government
explanations: The court of the emperor, including the emperor himself and the officials who governed under his authority. Primarily used in historical contexts to refer to the seat of imperial governance in Japan, particularly before the Meiji Restoration.
The fifth planet from the Sun and the largest in the solar system. Named after the element wood in the Chinese five-element system.
Made from wood as a material. Used as a の-adjective to describe objects crafted from wood, as opposed to other materials like metal, plastic, or stone.

glosses: before something happens, in advance, preventive
explanations: The state before something (usually something undesirable) has occurred. Almost always used in the phrase 未然に防ぐ (to prevent before it happens). In grammar, refers to the irrealis or imperfective form of a verb.

An act that was attempted but not completed or not successful, especially a crime. In legal usage, it refers to a criminal attempt where the intended result was not achieved. Used as a noun or as a の-adjective modifier.

glosses: for a long time, forever, enduringly
for a long time to come, forever, lastingly
explanations: Expresses the wish or expectation that something will continue far into the future. Commonly used in well-wishes and formal expressions, especially at weddings and in greetings.

glosses: main family, head family, parent house
explanations: The main or senior branch of a family, as opposed to branch families. In traditional Japanese kinship, the eldest son's line forms the main house, while younger sons establish branch houses.
The original or authentic source of something, as opposed to imitators or derivatives. Used colloquially to claim authenticity — e.g., 'the original ramen shop' or 'the birthplace of a certain dish.'

glosses: base, headquarters, home base, home ground
explanations: The main location from which an organization, team, or person operates. Used for military bases, company headquarters, sports team home stadiums, and any central base of operations.

glosses: getting into full swing, becoming serious
getting into full swing, becoming full-scale, becoming serious
explanations: The process of something shifting from a preliminary or partial state to a full, serious, or large-scale one. Used for activities, trends, seasons, and projects that ramp up to their main phase.

glosses: main hall of a Shinto shrine
explanations: The innermost and most sacred building of a Shinto shrine, which houses the enshrined deity (御神体). Visitors typically worship at the worship hall (拝殿) in front, as the main hall is usually not open to the public.

glosses: village chief, village head, village mayor
explanations: The elected head of a village (村) in Japan's local government system. Villages are the smallest unit of municipal government, found mainly in rural areas.

glosses: Japan and the United States, Japan-US, Japanese-American (bilateral)
explanations: An abbreviation combining 日 (Japan) and 米 (America/US), used as a prefix or noun to refer to the bilateral relationship, agreements, or interactions between Japan and the United States.
The latter part of spring, roughly corresponding to April and early May in Japan's calendar. A literary and seasonal term often used in writing, weather descriptions, and the traditional calendar.

glosses: banquet, formal dinner party, state dinner
explanations: A formal evening dinner event, typically hosted by governments, organizations, or dignitaries to honor guests or celebrate occasions. Often associated with diplomatic and state functions.
An ocean current whose water temperature is warmer than the surrounding sea. Warm currents affect climate, weather patterns, and marine ecosystems along the coastlines they flow past.

glosses: musical piece (on a program), selection, track, program item
explanations: A piece of music as listed on a concert program, playlist, or album. Refers to the individual items in a musical performance or collection, rather than to a song in general.
A document that lists items, amounts, or details in a breakdown format. Used for pay slips, medical bills, utility bills, credit card statements, and patent specifications.

glosses: time limit, set period, class period
explanations: A fixed or designated period of time. In school contexts, it refers to a class period (first period, second period, etc.).
Used as a prefix to indicate that something is set to operate within a time limit or is triggered by a timer, as in a time bomb or time-limited legislation.
Indicates that something turned out just as one expected or feared. Often used when confirming a prediction.
Used in questions to express doubt or wonder about whether something is truly the case. Adds a rhetorical or contemplative tone.
A physical frame or border that encloses something, such as a window frame, picture frame, or border around text.
An abstract limit or designated space, such as a time slot, budget allocation, or available position. Widely used in business and media.
Physically soft and bendable, or mentally adaptable and open-minded. Used for both physical flexibility of materials and bodies, and figurative flexibility of thinking and approaches.
A fragrant East Asian citrus fruit, smaller than a grapefruit, with a tart flavor. Widely used in Japanese cooking for its aromatic rind and juice, especially in winter dishes, sauces, and baths.
A structure made of posts and rails or boards used to enclose an area, prevent entry, or mark a boundary. Includes fences around gardens, barriers at construction sites, and railings along paths.

glosses: to prosper, to flourish, to thrive
explanations: To be in a state of success, growth, or vitality. Used for cities, civilizations, businesses, and cultures that are thriving or were once at their peak.

glosses: core, crux, heart of a matter
explanations: The most important or central point of an issue, problem, or argument. Used when referring to the essential part that everything else revolves around.
Describes something that is firmly entrenched and difficult to change or eliminate. Used for beliefs, customs, support, popularity, and prejudices that endure over time.
The most basic and essential element from which everything else arises. Used to describe the underlying cause, principle, or foundation of something.
The act of growing plants, crops, or produce. Covers everything from large-scale agricultural production to home gardening. Used with する to form a verb meaning 'to cultivate' or 'to grow.'
A matter or case requiring attention or resolution. Used in formal, business, and legal contexts for items under discussion, pending decisions, or ongoing projects.
A traditional Japanese preserved food made by salting and drying ume (Japanese apricot) fruits, often with red shiso leaves for color. Known for their extremely sour and salty taste.
Physical fighting at close quarters, grappling with an opponent. Also used figuratively for struggling with a difficult problem or challenge.
Describes a striking degree of difference or improvement compared to before or to others. Emphasizes that the gap is significant and clearly noticeable.

glosses: to take root, to become established
to become established, to take hold
explanations: For a plant to establish its roots in soil and begin growing. Describes the process of a transplanted or newly planted seedling becoming established.
For a custom, idea, culture, or practice to become firmly established in a community or society. A figurative extension of the plant metaphor.
The base or bottom part of something where it connects to the ground or its foundation. Commonly used for the base of trees, teeth, hair, and other things that grow from a fixed point.
The deepest underlying layer or foundation of something abstract, such as a belief system, culture, or way of thinking. Emphasizes what lies at the very bottom, supporting everything above it.
The main gate or entrance to a school campus. A prominent feature of Japanese schools, often the site of morning greetings by teachers and the backdrop for graduation photos.
An organized structure or system that provides the basic shape or rules for something. Used for institutional frameworks, policy structures, agreements, and organizational systems.

A professional chef, particularly one trained in Japanese cuisine (washoku). Refers to a skilled cook who works at a counter or in a kitchen of a Japanese restaurant. The term carries connotations of craftsmanship and traditional skill.
A highly prized wild mushroom that grows in association with pine trees. Known for its distinctive spicy-aromatic scent, it is considered a luxury food in Japan and is closely associated with autumn.
The act of someone coming to visit a place or person. A formal word used when describing visitors arriving, especially in business, official, or polite contexts.

The act of assigning a rank, grade, or rating to something based on quality, creditworthiness, or other criteria. Widely used in finance for credit ratings, and in food and services for quality grading.
Raising the rank, status, or level of something. Used for promotions in organizational hierarchy, upgrading of facilities or services, and elevation of diplomatic or institutional status.

glosses: row of cherry trees, cherry tree-lined road
explanations: A road or path lined with cherry blossom trees on one or both sides. A common and beloved sight in Japan, especially during spring when the trees are in full bloom.
The line on weather maps showing the progression of cherry blossom blooming across Japan, moving generally from south to north between late March and mid-May. A widely reported seasonal phenomenon.

glosses: to be rooted in, to be based on, to originate from
explanations: To have deep roots in something, to be firmly grounded in a particular source, culture, or origin. Almost always used figuratively for ideas, customs, feelings, or problems that stem from a deep underlying source.
Weapons that derive their destructive force from nuclear reactions, either fission or fusion. Includes atomic bombs and hydrogen bombs.

The central and most important part of something. Used in biology for the cell nucleus, in physics for the atomic nucleus, and figuratively for the core member or central element of a group or organization.
Used as a prefix in compound words related to nuclear energy, nuclear weapons, or nuclear science.
A deciduous tree of the genus Salix, characterized by its long, slender, drooping branches. Common along rivers and waterways in Japan, and a traditional symbol in Japanese art and literature.
A particular sector of business or trade, or the people and companies involved in it. Often used to refer to the collective community of professionals in a given field.
A person or company engaged in a particular trade or business. Often refers to outside contractors, suppliers, or service providers rather than individual employees.
An officially administered examination that certifies a person's knowledge or skill level in a particular subject. Common in Japan for language proficiency, academic subjects, and traditional arts.
The process of officially examining and certifying that something meets established standards, such as textbook screening or product testing.
The act of finding or identifying something through examination, testing, or analysis. Used especially for detecting substances, signals, errors, or anomalies through scientific or technical means.
A round, crisp fruit with grainy flesh, widely grown and eaten in Japan. When used without qualification, refers to the Japanese pear (nashi pear), which is round and crisp unlike the Western pear.
A sharp, pointed projection on a plant, such as a rose thorn or cactus spine.
A small, sharp fragment of wood or similar material that becomes embedded in the skin.
A sharp, hurtful quality in someone's words or manner. Used figuratively to describe speech or behavior that is cutting or hostile.
A round, open-topped container traditionally made of wood, used for carrying water, bathing, or storage. In modern use, also refers to plastic basins and tubs.

A traditional Japanese sweet made of pink-tinted rice cake filled with sweet red bean paste and wrapped in a salted cherry leaf. A seasonal confection associated with spring, especially the cherry blossom season and Girls' Day (March 3).

glosses: cherry blossom blizzard, shower of cherry petals
explanations: The spectacle of cherry blossom petals falling thickly through the air, resembling a snowstorm. A poetic image of late spring when the blossoms scatter.
A soft pink color reminiscent of peach blossoms. One of the traditional Japanese color names.
Used figuratively to describe matters related to love, romance, or sexual affairs. Similar to English 'rosy' in the romantic sense.

glosses: to master; to reach the extreme
to master, to carry to perfection
to reach the extreme of, to be extremely
explanations: To pursue something to the highest possible level; to achieve complete mastery of a skill, art, or discipline.
To reach the utmost degree of a state or condition. Often used in the form を{極|きわ}める to express reaching the peak of something.
The highest or most intense degree of something. Used to express that something has reached its absolute limit or pinnacle.
The highest or most intense degree of a state or condition. Used to emphasize that something is at an extreme level, often with negative connotations such as extreme fatigue, tension, or stress.
Vegetables whose edible part grows underground, such as carrots, daikon radish, burdock root, and potatoes. A common category in Japanese cooking and nutrition.

glosses: number of flat objects (sheets, tickets, etc.)
explanations: The count or quantity of flat, thin objects such as sheets of paper, tickets, photographs, plates, or cards. Derived from the counter {枚|まい} (for flat things) plus {数|すう} (number).

glosses: to worry, to be anxious about
explanations: To feel concerned or anxious about something. A somewhat literary or formal word for worrying. Often appears in the proverb {案|あん}ずるより{産|う}むが{易|やす}し.
To think about or come up with a plan or idea. A literary usage meaning to ponder or devise.
The head carpenter who leads a construction project, supervising and coordinating the work of other carpenters. A title of skill and authority in the traditional building trades.
By extension, a leader or head of a group. Used historically for clan leaders and heads of organizations.

glosses: standing close together, rising in clusters
explanations: Many tall things standing densely together like trees in a forest. Used for buildings, towers, smokestacks, and other tall structures clustered in an area.
The relative position, level, or class of a person, organization, or thing within a hierarchy. Indicates social standing, prestige, or grade.
A rule, standard, or established convention that serves as a benchmark.
In linguistics, the grammatical relationship of a noun or pronoun to other words in a sentence (e.g., nominative, accusative).

glosses: for commercial use, for business use
explanations: Intended or designed for use in a business, commercial, or professional setting rather than for personal or household use. Often refers to products sold in large quantities or with commercial-grade quality.

glosses: type of industry, line of business
explanations: The category or type of business or industry that a company or person is engaged in. Used when classifying businesses by their field of activity.
One of the two endpoints of an axis, especially the North or South Pole of the Earth, or the positive/negative pole of a magnet or battery.
The farthest or highest point of something; the ultimate degree. Used in compounds and set phrases to indicate an extreme.
The act of fighting off and forcing back an attacker, invader, or unwanted presence. Used for military repulsion, pest control, and figuratively for overcoming challenges.
The act of disturbing order, stability, or composure. Used for disrupting enemy formations, market stability, public order, or someone's mental state.
The act of counting or listing items individually. Almost always appears in the set phrase {枚挙|まいきょ}にいとまがない (too numerous to list).

glosses: number of long objects; number of runs (trains, buses)
number of runs, frequency of service
explanations: The count or quantity of objects counted with the counter {本|ほん}, such as bottles, pens, trees, or legs.
The number of train runs, bus services, or similar scheduled departures. Commonly used when discussing transportation frequency.

glosses: traditional, conventional, from the old days
explanations: Something that has existed or been done since the old days; a way, method, or custom that has been followed for a long time. Often implies something that may be outdated or in contrast with newer approaches.

A form of traditional Japanese puppet theater in which large, elaborately crafted puppets are manipulated by visible puppeteers, accompanied by a narrator (tayu) and shamisen music. Designated as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage.

glosses: end of a period, beginning of a new era
explanations: The time when night ends and day begins; the break of day.
The point at which a period or season ends and transitions into the next phase. Used for the end of the rainy season, the new year, and similar transitions.
A word that imitates or represents a natural sound, such as animal cries, environmental noises, or the sounds of actions. Japanese is especially rich in these.
Artificially created sounds used in film, television, radio, or theater to represent real-world sounds such as footsteps, rain, or doors closing.
Any device used to produce musical sounds. Covers traditional Japanese instruments, Western instruments, and electronic instruments alike.
The text or words that accompany a piece of music. Used for all genres of music, from pop songs to traditional folk songs and hymns.
Describes something that goes far beyond the normal or expected range, either in degree, opinion, or behavior. Can refer to actions, ideas, weather, or any quality taken to an excess.
The highest level of secrecy. Used for information, documents, plans, or projects that must not be disclosed under any circumstances. Stronger than 秘密 (secret).

A broad plan or vision for something to be created or achieved. Used for large-scale ideas such as urban development plans, novel plots, business strategies, or architectural designs. Implies creative or strategic thinking at a high level.

The act of building or constructing something, especially abstract things like systems, relationships, theories, or networks. While it can refer to physical construction, it is most commonly used for building up non-physical things in a systematic way.
The natural action or purpose that something is designed to perform. Used for the functions of organs, machines, systems, or organizations.
