The part of a person's life that is not related to their work or public activities. Often contrasted with one's professional or public life. Composed of 私 (private) + 生活 (life).
The room or place where a judge presides over legal proceedings. Also used figuratively for the judicial process itself. Composed of 法 (law) + 廷 (court).
A state of not having enough of something essential. Often used for nutrients, resources, or supplies. Can be used as a suru verb meaning 'to be deficient in.' Composed of 欠 (lack) + 乏 (scarce).

glosses: in small increments; bit by bit
in small increments; bit by bit; in small steps
explanations: Describes something done in frequent small amounts or movements rather than in large ones. Often used with に as an adverb. Composed of 小 (small) + 刻み (chopping, increments).

The act of deliberately seeking out faults, mistakes, or weaknesses in someone or something. Carries a negative connotation — the person doing it is seen as petty or unfair. Composed of 粗 (coarse, flaw) + 探し (searching).

glosses: eating while walking; eating on the go
explanations: The act of eating food while walking around, especially street food at festivals or tourist areas.
Visiting multiple restaurants, food stalls, or shops in an area to sample different dishes. A popular leisure activity in Japan.
The indigestible parts of plant foods that aid digestion and promote health. A commonly discussed topic in Japanese health and nutrition contexts. Composed of 食物 (food) + 繊維 (fiber).

A structured game or play activity, especially those played by children or in educational settings. More formal than 遊び and often implies organized or rule-based activities. Composed of 遊 (play) + 戯 (frolic).
A homogeneous liquid mixture in which one substance (the solute) is dissolved in another (the solvent). A standard chemistry and science term. Composed of 溶 (dissolve) + 液 (liquid).
A group of things sharing common characteristics. Used as a standalone noun or as a suffix attached to other nouns to indicate a category or class.

glosses: to have a point; to make sense
to have a point; to make sense; to be reasonable
explanations: Acknowledges that someone's opinion or argument has some merit or logic to it, even if one does not fully agree. Literally means 'there is one reason/logic.' Composed of 一 (one) + 理 (reason) + ある (to exist).

A privately owned agricultural estate in pre-modern Japan, particularly from the Nara through Muromachi periods. Manors were granted tax-exempt status and were controlled by aristocrats, temples, or shrines. Composed of 荘 (estate) + 園 (land).
Living in a place permanently with no intention of moving away. Often used in immigration contexts regarding legal residency status. Composed of 永 (eternal) + 住 (reside).
Exceptionally cheap, much lower than the normal or expected price. Commonly used in advertising and consumer contexts. Composed of 格 (standard) + 安 (cheap) — implying unusually cheap.

A person who has accomplished great things and is remembered for their achievements. Often used in educational contexts when discussing notable historical figures. Composed of 偉 (great, admirable) + 人 (person).

Admitting defeat or yielding to an opponent or difficult situation. Used both in serious military/competitive contexts and in everyday situations where one gives up trying. Composed of 降 (descend, surrender) + 参 (go, come — humble).
An embarrassing mistake or failure, especially in a public or professional context. Implies loss of face or reputation. Composed of 失 (lose) + 態 (appearance, state).

glosses: digression; side note; by the way
explanations: A remark or story that departs from the main topic. Often used as a discourse marker to introduce an aside. Composed of 余 (surplus, extra) + 談 (talk).

glosses: local cuisine; regional dish; local specialty food
explanations: Traditional dishes associated with a particular region, using local ingredients and cooking methods passed down through generations. Composed of 郷土 (homeland, local area) + 料理 (cooking, dish).

glosses: old age; post-retirement years; later years of life
explanations: The period of life after retirement, typically from one's 60s onward. A frequent topic in discussions about finances, health, and life planning. Composed of 老 (old) + 後 (after).

glosses: youngest child; baby of the family
explanations: The youngest child in a family. Often associated with being spoiled or doted on by parents and older siblings. Composed of 末 (end, last) + っ子 (child — suffix).

glosses: to creep up; to steal near
to creep up; to steal near; to sneak up on
explanations: To approach quietly and stealthily, so as not to be noticed. Used both literally (a person sneaking up) and figuratively (danger, old age, or fear approaching gradually).

glosses: to be fascinated by; to gaze admiringly
to be fascinated by; to gaze admiringly; to be captivated
explanations: To stare at someone or something in admiration, unable to look away due to beauty or impressiveness. Composed of 見 (look) + 惚れる (to be charmed).
In the board game go (囲碁), the opening phase where stones are placed across the board to establish a strategic framework for the rest of the game.
By extension from the go term, an action taken in advance to prepare for future goals or events. Implies careful, forward-thinking planning.

glosses: light on one's feet; agile; nimble
explanations: Physically light and able to move quickly and easily. Describes someone who moves with agility.
Having few possessions or responsibilities, making it easy to act freely or travel. Can describe a person with minimal luggage or minimal commitments.
The amount of a substance per unit of volume or area. A standard scientific term. Composed of 密 (dense) + 度 (degree).
The degree of substance or content packed into something, such as time, a schedule, or a piece of work. Implies fullness or richness of content.

glosses: detached house; standalone house; single-family home
explanations: A house that stands on its own, not connected to other buildings — as opposed to an apartment or row house. Also can refer to a solitary house standing alone in an isolated location. Composed of 一 (one) + 軒 (house counter) + 家 (house).
Expresses the speaker's guess or speculation that something might be the case. Conveys a sense of uncertainty with a slight feeling of surprise or unexpectedness.

glosses: how should I put it; what can I say
explanations: A filler expression used when the speaker is searching for the right words or hesitating about how to express something.

glosses: I'm sorry, but...; excuse me, but...
explanations: A polite preamble used before making a request, asking a question, or saying something that might inconvenience the listener. Expresses humility and consideration.
The process of verifying that a person is who they claim to be, typically through documents such as a driver's license, passport, or My Number card.
The act of accomplishing a set goal or target. Commonly used in business, education, and sports contexts.

glosses: beginning of the month; start of the month
explanations: The first few days of a calendar month. Used when referring to events, deadlines, or schedules at the start of a month.

glosses: going up and down; ascent and descent
explanations: The physical act of going uphill and downhill, or ascending and descending. Used for slopes, stairs, and roads.
Figurative use referring to fluctuations, variations, or instability in conditions, prices, or emotions.

glosses: lending and borrowing; debit and credit
explanations: The combined concept of lending and borrowing, especially in financial and accounting contexts. Also used for debit and credit in bookkeeping.

glosses: ascending and descending; going up and down
explanations: The action of moving up and down, typically referring to riding elevators, climbing stairs, or the mechanical raising and lowering of equipment.
A single written or spoken sentence. Used when referring to the structure or content of written text.
A hole or split in fabric, paper, or similar material caused by tearing.

glosses: stock on hand; current inventory; display item
explanations: The physical item in question, as opposed to a description, photo, or catalog listing. Often used when asking to see or inspect the real thing.
The last remaining item in stock, often a display model or floor sample sold at a discount.
A grammatical term referring to the progressive or continuous form of a verb, such as English "-ing" or Japanese ている.
Used figuratively to describe something that is currently ongoing or still in progress, often in the pattern {現在|げんざい}{進行形|しんこうけい}で.
Casual or dialectal contraction of {知|し}らない (shiranai), meaning "I don't know." Common in western Japanese dialects and casual male speech.
Used to dismiss responsibility or express indifference, often with an abrupt or blunt tone.

glosses: flattery; currying favor; trying to please
explanations: The act of trying to win someone's favor or put them in a good mood, often through insincere or excessive pleasantries. Can also refer to the person who does this.
Three occurrences of something. Used as a counter for the number of times an action occurs.
A measurement of three degrees, used for temperature or angles.
A collective term for various incidental expenses or costs that arise in addition to the main expenditure. Common in business, construction, and real estate contexts.
Cooked white rice. A formal or written term used in menus, nutrition labels, and official documents, as opposed to the everyday word ごはん.

glosses: to look around restlessly; to glance about
to look around restlessly; to glance about nervously
explanations: To look around repeatedly in different directions, often suggesting nervousness, unfamiliarity with surroundings, or searching for something.

glosses: House of Councillors; upper house of the Japanese Diet
explanations: The upper house of the National Diet of Japan. Members serve six-year terms, with half elected every three years. It has 248 seats.
Swimming over a long distance, especially in open water such as the sea or a lake. A traditional summer activity at some Japanese schools.

glosses: artistic style; performance style; style of act
explanations: The characteristic style or manner of a performer, comedian, actor, or artist. Refers to their distinctive approach and the impression their performances give.

glosses: beginning of the month; start of the month
explanations: The first few days of a calendar month. A somewhat formal term used mainly in business contexts, contrasting with {月末|げつまつ} (end of the month).

glosses: previous graduate; person who has already graduated
explanations: A person who has already graduated from school but has not yet secured employment. In the Japanese job market, this term specifically refers to graduates who missed the standard new-graduate hiring cycle.
Unwanted substances mixed into a material, making it impure. Used in scientific, industrial, and everyday contexts.
The process of passing a liquid or gas through a filter to remove solid particles or impurities. Used in scientific, industrial, and daily life contexts.
The act of killing every member of a group without exception. Used in historical, literary, and dramatic contexts.

glosses: to be able to sleep; sleeping
to be able to sleep; can sleep
explanations: The potential form of {眠|ねむ}る, indicating the ability to fall asleep or sleep well.
Used as an attributive adjective ({連体形|れんたいけい}) meaning "sleeping" or "dormant," as in {眠|ねむ}れる{森|もり} (sleeping forest).
Each and every evening. A somewhat formal time expression used in writing and news.

glosses: mixed tenancy; mixed-use occupancy; cohabitation of diverse tenants
explanations: A situation where different types of businesses, shops, or residents share the same building or area. Most commonly seen in the term {雑居|ざっきょ}ビル (mixed-use building).

glosses: aromatic vegetables; herbs and aromatics used in cooking
explanations: A collective term for vegetables and herbs used primarily for their fragrance and flavor in cooking, such as ginger, garlic, green onions, shiso, and celery.

glosses: to go too far; to exceed the limit
to go too far; to exceed the proper limit
explanations: Describes behavior, actions, or situations that have passed an acceptable boundary. Often used critically to indicate that someone has overstepped.
A container with a pump mechanism that releases liquid as a fine mist. Used for watering plants, ironing, cleaning, and other household purposes.

glosses: bragging about one's partner; love-boasting story
bragging about one's partner; gushing about one's relationship
explanations: A story or remark where someone proudly talks about how wonderful their romantic partner is or how happy their relationship is. Often perceived as annoying or tiresome by listeners.

glosses: possessiveness; desire to monopolize; jealous desire to have someone or something all to oneself
explanations: A strong desire to have exclusive possession of a person, thing, or resource. Most commonly used about romantic possessiveness, but can also apply to material things or attention.
A person who aspires to or applies for a particular position, school, course, or opportunity.
The collective term for all employees at an educational institution, including both teachers and administrative or support staff.
A seat in a legislative body such as the Diet, a prefectural assembly, or a city council. Refers both to the physical seat and to the position or mandate it represents.

glosses: street parking; parking on the road
explanations: An abbreviation of {路上駐車|ろじょうちゅうしゃ} (parking on a public road). Often implies illegal or inconsiderate parking, though it can also refer to legitimate curbside parking.

glosses: competitive spirit; rivalry; desire to compete
explanations: The feeling of wanting to compete with or outdo someone else. Can be positive (healthy competition) or negative (petty rivalry), depending on context.
Detergent specifically formulated for washing clothes, available in liquid, powder, or pod form.

glosses: retrial; judicial review; re-examination of a case
explanations: A legal proceeding in which a previously decided case is tried again, typically because new evidence has emerged or procedural errors are alleged.

glosses: otaku; geek; obsessive fan or enthusiast
explanations: A person with deep, passionate knowledge of a particular subject, especially anime, manga, video games, or other aspects of pop culture. Originally derogatory, the term has become more neutral or even positive in recent years, particularly among younger generations.
A skin condition characterized by raised, itchy welts that appear suddenly. Caused by allergic reactions, stress, or other triggers.
Reacting more strongly than normal to stimuli, whether physical (allergens, chemicals) or emotional (criticism, noise). Used in both medical and general contexts.
An unspecified multiple, typically implying three to ten times as much. Used to express a large but vague multiplier.

glosses: strong aversion; visceral rejection; instinctive resistance
explanations: The immune system's response when rejecting transplanted organs or tissue.
A figurative extension of the medical meaning, describing an intense, almost physical feeling of rejection toward an idea, person, or situation.
A single-wheeled pedal vehicle ridden for recreation or performance. A common activity in Japanese elementary schools.
A single-wheeled cart pushed by hand, used for carrying loads at construction sites, gardens, and farms.

glosses: sumo rankings; ranking chart of sumo wrestlers
explanations: The official ranking list of professional sumo wrestlers, published before each tournament. The rankings determine a wrestler's position, opponent assignments, and privileges.
By extension, any ranking or league table that orders people or things by performance or popularity.

glosses: lazy person; someone who finds everything bothersome
lazy person; someone who finds everything bothersome; person who can't be bothered
explanations: A person who habitually avoids effort and finds tasks troublesome. Derived from the adjective {面倒|めんどう}くさい with the suffix -がり indicating a personality trait.
Something that was not anticipated or predicted. A literary/formal expression using the classical negative form せぬ (= しない).

glosses: to slip into; to crawl under; to sneak into
to crawl under; to slip into (a space)
explanations: To physically get under or inside something, such as a blanket, a bed, or a narrow space.
To enter a place secretly or without authorization.

glosses: lacking common sense; outrageous; beyond what is considered normal
explanations: Describes behavior, actions, or ideas that deviate from what society considers reasonable or normal. Almost always used critically.
Describes something that happens many times or at short intervals. More formal than よく and emphasizes the high frequency or repetition.

glosses: winning over; placating; appeasement; coaxing into compliance
explanations: The act of bringing someone around to your side or neutralizing opposition through persuasion, flattery, or concessions rather than force. Often implies a calculated or strategic approach.

glosses: leisure time; spare time; free time
explanations: Time free from work or obligations, available for rest and recreation. A somewhat formal word compared to {暇|ひま} or {自由時間|じゆうじかん}.
A formal letter written to endorse someone's character, abilities, or qualifications, typically for university admission, employment, or awards.

glosses: political world; political circles; the world of politics
explanations: The collective sphere of political activity, including politicians, parties, and the institutions of government. Used in news and commentary to refer to the political establishment.

glosses: accompanying; incidental; being attached to; concomitant
explanations: Something that comes along with or is attached to a main thing. Used in formal or written contexts to describe secondary elements, conditions, or consequences that follow from something primary.

glosses: to enter (someone's house); to walk right in
to enter someone's house; to go inside; to walk right in
explanations: To step up into someone's home and make oneself comfortable. Often implies entering without much hesitation or formality, sometimes with a nuance of presumptuousness.
A sumo wrestler who has reached the top two divisions (makuuchi or juryo). Only sekitori receive a salary and various privileges such as wearing silk mawashi.

glosses: to tighten; to become firm; to brace oneself
to tighten; to become firm; to be toned
to become tense; to brace oneself
explanations: Used for physical things becoming firm or taut, such as muscles, skin, or a body becoming well-toned.
Used figuratively for a mental state of heightened focus or seriousness, such as when facing an important situation.

glosses: to wear clothes in a relaxed or disheveled way
to wear clothes in a relaxed, casual, or disheveled way
explanations: To intentionally or unintentionally let one's clothing become loose, untucked, or otherwise less than properly arranged. Can suggest either stylish casualness or sloppiness depending on context.
The tendency to put on airs or make things look fancier than they are. Most commonly used in the negative form (飾り気のない) to praise someone or something as unpretentious.

glosses: to excuse oneself; to be rude; to take one's leave
to excuse oneself; to take one's leave
to be rude; to commit a discourtesy
explanations: A polite way of saying one is leaving or entering a space. Commonly used when departing from a gathering or entering someone's office or room.
To do something impolite or to behave rudely toward someone.

glosses: nationally popular; beloved by the whole nation
explanations: Describes something that enjoys overwhelming popularity or recognition across the entire country, transcending age, region, and social class.
The head of the Japanese government, officially known as the Prime Minister of Japan. Formally selected by the Diet and appointed by the Emperor.
The shared opinion or will of an entire group, organization, or populace. Emphasizes that everyone in the group agrees.

glosses: body warmth; skin temperature; human skin warmth
explanations: The natural warmth of a person's body or skin. Often used to describe warming something to approximately body temperature, or to evoke the comfort of human warmth.

glosses: personal belongings; private property; personal effects
explanations: Items that belong to an individual personally, as opposed to shared or organizational property. Often used in workplace and institutional settings.
A government official appointed to reside in a foreign city to protect the interests and assist citizens of the appointing country. Operates from a consulate.
The body of law that defines criminal offenses and their punishments. In Japan, refers specifically to the Penal Code (刑法典) enacted in 1907.
A position with little real work or responsibility, often implying the person has been sidelined or demoted without being formally dismissed. Carries a negative connotation of being shelved.
A formal document presenting a plan, idea, or suggestion for consideration. Used in business, government, and academic settings.
Objects used for decoration or adornment, including jewelry, accessories, and decorative household items.

A type of sushi where a strip of nori seaweed is wrapped around a ball of rice to form a cup, which is then topped with soft ingredients like sea urchin or salmon roe. Named for its resemblance to a battleship.

glosses: sashimi; artfully arranged sliced raw fish
explanations: A polite or refined term for sashimi, emphasizing the careful preparation and artistic presentation. Commonly used in the Kansai region and in formal dining settings.
The technique of briefly searing the surface of food (especially sushi and sashimi) with an open flame, or food prepared this way. The searing adds a smoky flavor while keeping the inside raw.

glosses: to let something slip; to say something by mistake
to let something slip; to blurt out; to make a slip of the tongue
explanations: To accidentally say something that should have been kept secret or that one did not intend to reveal. Literally 'to let one's mouth slide.'
The construction or installation of a bridge across a river, valley, or other gap.
Figuratively, the act of creating a link or connection between different groups, cultures, or ideas.

glosses: low altitude; low in the sky
explanations: A position relatively close to the ground. Used for aircraft, flying objects, and figuratively for performing at a minimal level.
A formal decision made through discussion and voting in an assembly, parliament, board meeting, or other deliberative body.
A plan or action taken in response to an opponent's move, a threat, or a problem. Implies a reactive or defensive strategy.
The office of the school principal (校長). In Japanese schools, a dedicated room where the principal works and receives visitors.
A wooden stick used with a mortar (すり鉢) to grind sesame seeds, miso, and other ingredients. A traditional Japanese kitchen utensil, typically made from the wood of the Japanese pepper tree (山椒).

glosses: powerful nation; strong country; great power
explanations: A nation with significant military, economic, or political strength on the world stage.

glosses: shareholdings; stocks one owns; equity holdings
explanations: Shares of stock that a person or entity currently holds or owns.
The process of making an abstract idea, concept, or vision into something concrete and tangible. Often used for bringing plans, ideals, or creative visions to life.
Describes behavior, actions, or a person that is rough, aggressive, or lacking in manners. Implies a combination of physical roughness and social crudeness.
Describes a feeling or realization that strikes one deeply and painfully, as though piercing the heart. Often used for emotions like regret, desire, or awareness.

glosses: to butt in; to interrupt; to interject
explanations: To insert a comment or opinion into someone else's conversation or discussion, often uninvited. Literally 'to insert one's mouth.'
A person who appreciates and has refined taste in fine food and drink.
Describes something that is hard to comprehend due to complexity, abstraction, or specialized content. Used for texts, theories, concepts, and similar intellectual material.
An area of land designated for burying the dead, typically containing gravestones and memorials.
A shop that sells fresh meat.
A person who sells meat at a shop.
Describes rice or food that has just been cooked and is still hot and at its best. Most commonly used for rice.

glosses: prepared side dishes; ready-made dishes; deli food
explanations: Pre-cooked dishes sold at supermarkets, department store basements, or specialty shops, meant to be taken home and eaten. Includes items like fried chicken, salads, simmered vegetables, and other everyday dishes.
The act of moving from one residence to another. A formal term commonly used in official documents and administrative contexts.
A baseless or trivial complaint made to find fault with something or someone. Often implies the complaint is unjustified or made with ulterior motives.

glosses: end of an act; finale; conclusion
end of an act; final scene; curtain fall
explanations: The closing scene or final moments of an act in a play or theatrical performance.
The concluding phase or final moments of an event, situation, or era. Used figuratively.
The state of muscles, tension, or discipline becoming loose or relaxed. Used both in medical/physical contexts and figuratively for discipline or vigilance.
A person who is part of an organization, group, or body. A formal term emphasizing the person's role as a component of a larger whole.

glosses: sharp decrease; dramatic drop; drastic reduction
explanations: A sudden and significant decrease in number, quantity, or amount.
The correct order in which the strokes of a kanji or kana character should be written.
Treating something or someone as more important or giving them first consideration over others.
Something or someone that comes after or follows behind another. Often used for vehicles, people in a sequence, or products/works that follow an initial one.

glosses: hard to be around; feeling awkward around someone
explanations: Describes a place or atmosphere that has an unpleasant amount of smoke.
Describes the uncomfortable feeling of being around a strict, intimidating, or overly righteous person whom one finds difficult to relax around.
A state where two or more things do not match, agree, or correspond. Used for data, opinions, facts, and other comparable items.
The quality of following a consistent rule, pattern, or order. Used in scientific, mathematical, and general contexts to describe predictable patterns.
The total amount obtained by adding everything together.
Help or support given to someone to accomplish something. A formal term often used in written or polite contexts.
A formal warning or reprimand issued to someone for misconduct or a violation, typically by an authority or organization. Often used in legal, administrative, and workplace disciplinary contexts.

glosses: swallowing whole; gulping down without chewing
explanations: The act of swallowing food or an object whole without chewing it.
Accepting someone's words, claims, or demands without questioning or thinking critically about them.

glosses: peaceful and uneventful; safe and sound
peaceful and uneventful; safe and sound; tranquil
explanations: A state in which nothing troublesome or dangerous occurs; everything proceeds calmly and without incident.
The supposed distinctive personality traits, customs, and behavioral tendencies attributed to the residents of a particular prefecture. A popular topic in Japanese media and conversation.
Something that will never perish, be destroyed, or fade away. Used for achievements, spirit, legacy, and similar abstract concepts.

glosses: the natural world; the world of nature
explanations: The physical world of plants, animals, and natural phenomena, as opposed to the human or artificial world.
Describes something that is extremely small in size, scale, or amount.
Something that is intended to last indefinitely or for a very long time, without change or end.
The salted roe (eggs) of Alaska pollock or cod, widely eaten in Japan as a rice topping, onigiri filling, or pasta ingredient. Typically pale pink in color.
Using something beyond its intended or appropriate scope, often referring to power, authority, drugs, or rights. Carries a strongly negative connotation.
Describes an action or state that continues without interruption. Somewhat more literary or formal than いつも.

glosses: the whole story; full account from beginning to end
the whole story; full account; every detail from start to finish
explanations: Refers to the complete sequence of events or facts, from the very beginning to the very end, without omitting anything.

glosses: hitting the mark; coming true; proving correct
hitting the mark; hitting the target
coming true; proving correct; being on the mark
explanations: An arrow, bullet, or thrown object successfully striking its intended target.
A prediction, guess, or forecast turning out to be accurate.

glosses: to loosen; to slacken; to relax
to loosen; to slacken; to make less tight
to relax; to ease; to let up on
explanations: To reduce the tightness or tension of something physical, such as a belt, screw, or grip.
To reduce the intensity or strictness of rules, vigilance, speed, or effort.

glosses: to tighten; to brace; to firm up
to tighten; to pull tight; to firm up
to brace oneself; to tighten discipline; to buckle down
explanations: To make something physically tighter or more toned, such as muscles or a body.
To adopt a more serious, focused attitude. Often used about mental or organizational discipline.

glosses: lining up; standing in a row; forming a line
lining up; standing in a row; forming an orderly line
explanations: Arranging people or things in a neat, orderly row or formation. Commonly used in school, military, and public contexts.

glosses: dressing warmly; wearing thick layers of clothing
explanations: Wearing multiple or thick layers of clothing to stay warm, typically in cold weather. The opposite is {薄着|うすぎ} (dressing lightly).
The act of taking medicine orally as directed. A formal term commonly used in medical and pharmaceutical contexts.

glosses: departure; setting out; new start in life
departure; setting out on a journey
new start in life; new beginning; fresh start
explanations: Leaving one's home or familiar place to embark on a journey. Somewhat literary.
Beginning a new chapter in life, such as starting a career, getting married, or entering a new phase. Often used at graduation ceremonies and celebrations.
A powerful wind that can cause disruption or damage. Commonly used in weather reports and news.

glosses: vacant lot; empty plot of land
vacant lot; empty plot of land; unused land
explanations: A piece of land that has no buildings or structures on it and is not being used for any particular purpose.
Plants cultivated for food or commercial purposes. A general term covering rice, vegetables, fruits, grains, and other farm products.
The act of placing a deceased person's body or remains in the ground or a grave. A formal term used in both modern and historical contexts.

glosses: to resemble closely; to be very similar
to resemble closely; to be very similar; to bear a close resemblance
explanations: To share many characteristics or features with something else, to the point where the two are hard to distinguish. Often used for abstract qualities, patterns, or tendencies rather than physical appearance.
A person or entity that owns shares in a company. An important term in business and finance.
Water that is safe for human consumption. Used in official, public health, and emergency contexts.

glosses: landing; touching down; alighting on the ground
explanations: The moment of making contact with the ground after being in the air, whether from a jump, flight, or fall. Used for people, aircraft, and spacecraft.

glosses: extract; excerpt; selection; passage taken from a larger work
explanations: A portion selected from a longer text, document, speech, or other source. Also the act of selecting such a portion.
Having or showing a broad-minded, forgiving attitude toward others' faults or mistakes. Often used to describe a person's character or an official's handling of a situation.
The state of something occurring or being included more than once, or the act of duplicating. Common in administrative, data, and organizational contexts.
The criminal act of taking someone else's property without permission. A formal, legal term commonly used in news reports and legal contexts.

glosses: pet owner; owner of an animal; keeper
explanations: The person who owns and is responsible for taking care of a pet or other domesticated animal.
Occurring once every two weeks. Used for schedules, publications, and recurring events.
Acting or done quickly and without unnecessary delay. A formal term commonly used in official announcements, regulations, and business communications.
A person who has completed their studies and graduated from a school, university, or other educational institution.
An official permit authorizing a person to operate a motor vehicle. In Japan, driver's licenses are issued by each prefecture's public safety commission.

glosses: proselytizing; missionary work; spreading a belief
proselytizing; missionary work; spreading a religion
explanations: The act of spreading religious teachings and trying to convert people to a particular faith.
Informally used to describe passionately recommending a hobby, product, or interest to others, trying to win them over. Common in internet and otaku culture.
Sustaining a physical injury, especially in accidents, disasters, conflicts, or sports. A formal term used in news reports and official communications.

glosses: breach; collapse; bursting (of a dam or levee)
explanations: The breaking or collapse of a dam, levee, embankment, or similar structure, typically caused by the pressure of water. A term frequently used in disaster reporting.

glosses: immediately; right away; on the spot
explanations: Describes doing something without any delay or hesitation, responding or acting the moment a situation arises.

glosses: as scheduled; as planned; on schedule
explanations: Indicates that something proceeds exactly according to the original plan or schedule, without changes or delays.

glosses: from beginning to end; throughout; consistently
explanations: Describes a state or action that continues unchanged from start to finish. Often emphasizes that a particular attitude, mood, or behavior was maintained the entire time.
The act of going somewhere together with another person, or the person who accompanies someone. Often used in formal or official contexts.

glosses: fulfillment; execution; performance (of a duty or contract)
explanations: Carrying out or completing what has been promised, agreed upon, or required by duty. Most commonly used for contracts, obligations, and official commitments.
Not of the highest quality or rank. Used to describe people, things, or organizations that fall short of top-tier standards.
Describes something or someone that is morally upright, socially acceptable, and following the right path. Often used to describe a way of living or earning a livelihood.

glosses: sleeping like a log; dead sleep
sleeping very deeply; dead sleep; sleeping like a log
explanations: Colloquial term for falling into an extremely deep sleep, often to the point of being difficult to wake. The character for "explosion" conveys the intensity.

glosses: royal family; royal house; royal household
explanations: The family of a king or queen; a reigning dynasty. Used primarily for foreign monarchies rather than the Japanese imperial family.
A person who rules a country as king, queen, emperor, or similar hereditary head of state.
Equipment or clothing used to protect oneself from rain, such as umbrellas, raincoats, and rain boots.

glosses: minced meat cutlet; ground meat croquette
explanations: A deep-fried breaded patty made from seasoned ground meat (usually beef, pork, or a mix), onions, and other ingredients. A popular item in Japanese home cooking and at butcher shops.
A camera installed to monitor and record activity in a particular area for security or crime prevention purposes.

glosses: health management; taking care of one's health
health management; taking care of one's physical condition
explanations: The practice of monitoring and maintaining one's physical health through proper diet, sleep, exercise, and lifestyle habits. A concept frequently emphasized in Japanese workplaces and schools.

glosses: visiting a grave; paying respects at a grave
explanations: The act of visiting a family grave to clean it, offer flowers, incense, and food, and pray for the deceased. An important cultural practice in Japan.
A Japanese national holiday on the third Monday of September, dedicated to honoring elderly people and celebrating their longevity.
Brothers related by marriage (a spouse's brother or a sibling's husband) or by a parent's remarriage, rather than by blood.
Men who have formed a bond of brotherhood through an oath or ceremony, though not biologically related. A concept common in historical and fictional contexts.

glosses: itemization on a receipt; description field
explanations: A clause or condition added to a document, rule, or statement that qualifies or limits the main content. Common in legal, contractual, and official documents.
The line on a receipt or invoice that specifies the purpose of payment, such as "for books" or "for meeting expenses."
Items offered to deities, spirits of the deceased, or at Buddhist altars. Typically includes food, drink, flowers, and other items placed at shrines, temples, graves, or household altars.
The practice of protecting the natural environment from pollution, destruction, and degradation through policies, regulations, and individual actions.
The clearing, degradation, or destruction of forests, typically caused by logging, agriculture, or urban development. A major global environmental concern.

glosses: new member of the workforce; fresh graduate entering society
new member of the workforce; person who just started working
explanations: A person who has recently graduated from school and entered the workforce for the first time. In Japan, this typically refers to the cohort of graduates who start their jobs in April.
A school that only admits male students. In Japan, single-sex schools exist mainly at the private middle school and high school levels.
Having vivid, bright, and striking colors. Used to describe things that are visually impressive due to their rich coloring.

glosses: to look down; to cast one's eyes down; to avert one's gaze
to look down; to cast one's eyes downward
explanations: To lower one's gaze, typically out of shyness, sadness, shame, or deference. A common expression in literary and everyday descriptions of body language.
Knitting done by hand rather than by machine. Also used as a modifier to describe items that are hand-knitted.

glosses: suppuration; festering; becoming infected with pus
explanations: The formation of pus in a wound or infected area. A medical term used in both clinical and everyday contexts when a wound becomes infected.

glosses: lack of virtue; immorality; personal failing
explanations: A formal term for moral failings or shortcomings in character. Most commonly encountered in the set phrase of apology: "owing to my lack of virtue."

glosses: to get to the heart of the matter; to hit the nail on the head
explanations: To identify or address the most important, central point of an issue. Used when someone makes a remark or asks a question that goes straight to the core of a problem.
A unique number assigned to each student upon enrollment at a school or university, used for administrative purposes such as exams, records, and identification.
Refers to ashes remaining after something has been burned, or figuratively to the state of total destruction or ruin. A literary word often used in formal or dramatic contexts.

glosses: as expected; as hoped; according to expectations
explanations: Describes a result or outcome that matches what was anticipated or hoped for.

glosses: to whine; to complain of weakness
to whine; to grumble; to show weakness
explanations: To express complaints or negativity about one's situation, showing a lack of resolve or determination. Often used critically or self-reflectively.

glosses: to show off; to put on airs
to show off; to put on airs; to keep up appearances
explanations: To act in a way that makes oneself appear better, richer, or more capable than one actually is. Often implies vanity or insecurity.
A place for sitting, especially a simple seat like a bench or stool.
A job or position that someone takes only temporarily, treating it as a stepping stone to something better.
An act of carelessness, negligence, or improper handling that causes problems. Often used when someone's irresponsible behavior leads to trouble.
A formal or official term for rainy weather. Commonly seen in announcements and signage about weather-dependent events.

glosses: good fight; valiant effort; fighting bravely
explanations: A strong effort or brave performance, especially against difficult odds. Often used in sports and competitive contexts to praise someone who tried hard regardless of the outcome.

glosses: carbonated water; sparkling water; soda water
explanations: Water that has been infused with carbon dioxide gas, creating bubbles. Widely available in Japan as a drink on its own or as a mixer.
Describes something that has an air of mystery or is hard to understand. Derived from the verb 謎めく (to seem mysterious) in its past/attributive form.
Describes a wide range of different types or kinds. A four-character compound emphasizing both quantity and variety.

glosses: love at first sight; falling in love at first glance
explanations: The experience of immediately falling in love with someone (or occasionally something) upon seeing them for the first time.

glosses: to swarm; to crowd; to flock; to throng
explanations: To gather in a large group around something, often in an eager or chaotic way. Used for people, animals, and insects.
A portable device used to put out small fires. Required in buildings throughout Japan by fire safety regulations.

glosses: nightlife; going out at night for fun; late-night entertainment
explanations: Going out to enjoy oneself at night, such as visiting bars, clubs, or entertainment districts. Often implies staying out until late.

glosses: narrow escape from death; having one's life saved
explanations: A close call with death or serious danger. Implies that the person barely survived and was lucky to be alive.
Juice extracted from fruit. Commonly seen on beverage labels and in food-related contexts.
A pale, light shade of blue, like the color of clear shallow water. One of the traditional Japanese color names.
The formal ceremony held for a deceased person. In Japan, funerals typically follow Buddhist traditions, though Shinto and Christian services also occur.

glosses: match; competition; playing against; facing off
explanations: A competitive encounter between two opponents or teams. Used in sports, games, and any head-to-head competition.
The period at the end of the calendar year, especially December. Often used in commercial and seasonal contexts.
A piece of paper stuck or posted on a wall, door, or other surface to convey a message. Common in everyday Japanese life for announcements, warnings, and notices.
A point of weakness or vulnerability, either in a person's character, position, or abilities. Often used in contexts involving leverage or exploitation.
A flowering plant with layered petals, deeply significant in Japanese culture. It is the symbol of the Imperial family and appears on the Japanese passport.

glosses: burglary of an empty house; sneak thief; prowler
explanations: Breaking into and stealing from a house or building while the occupants are away. Also refers to the person who commits this crime.

glosses: valuables; precious items; personal effects of value
explanations: Items of monetary or personal value such as wallets, jewelry, passports, and electronics. Commonly referenced in travel, security, and storage contexts.

glosses: piggy bank; coin bank; money box
explanations: A container, often shaped like an animal, used for saving coins. A familiar household item, especially for children learning to save money.

glosses: casual clothes; everyday clothes; informal wear
explanations: Clothing worn for daily life and relaxation, as opposed to formal or work attire.
A section of tree trunk that has been cut but not yet processed into lumber. Retains its round, natural shape.
A structure built along a waterfront where ships can load and unload cargo or passengers. Often evokes an atmospheric, slightly nostalgic image of port towns.
The act of telling things apart or distinguishing between similar items, concepts, or categories. Often used in technical, analytical, or perceptual contexts.
Working out a numerical result through mathematical operations. Used in formal, business, and technical contexts for computing figures such as costs, statistics, or measurements.
Following orders or yielding to authority, rules, or someone else's will. Implies subordination and acceptance of another's control.
Describes explanations, arguments, or answers that are easy to understand, logically sound, and free of ambiguity. Used to praise the clarity and directness of communication or reasoning.
The act of creating an organization, institution, or company for the first time. Emphasizes the initial creation from nothing, typically of formal bodies like schools, companies, or associations.

glosses: postponement; rescheduling to a later date
explanations: Pushing an event to the next available date, typically the following day. Most commonly used for outdoor events postponed due to weather. Unlike general postponement, {順延|じゅんえん} implies moving to the next sequential date rather than an indefinite delay.
A state of having no motivation, energy, or willpower. Describes a person who lacks drive or enthusiasm, or a condition where someone cannot muster the will to act.

glosses: passing grade; passing mark; acceptable standard
explanations: The minimum score needed to pass, or by extension, a level of performance that is just good enough. Often used figuratively to evaluate whether something meets a minimum acceptable standard.

A visual design or decorative pattern, especially one created for applied arts such as textiles, stamps, ceramics, or graphic design. Can also refer to the preliminary sketch or blueprint for such a design.

A traditional Japanese poetic form consisting of five lines with a 5-7-5-7-7 mora pattern. One of the oldest forms of Japanese poetry, dating back over a thousand years. Still actively composed today, with newspaper columns and poetry contests keeping the tradition alive.

glosses: to investigate thoroughly; to get to the bottom of
to master; to pursue to the utmost
explanations: To pursue the truth or essence of something through deep study or inquiry. Emphasizes the intellectual process of thorough examination.
To reach the highest level of skill or understanding in a field or discipline through dedicated practice and study.

A euphemistic term for taking one's own life. Preferred in journalism, government documents, and support organizations as a less blunt alternative to {自殺|じさつ}. Increasingly used in media style guides in Japan.

A traditional Japanese side dish where vegetables (and sometimes other ingredients) are mixed with a creamy dressing made from mashed tofu, sesame, miso, sugar, and soy sauce. A common item in home cooking and traditional set meals.
A book or work written by two or more authors together. Also refers to the act of co-authoring. Common in academic and publishing contexts.

glosses: to make a blunder; to cause trouble
to make a blunder; to cause trouble; to pull off (something bad)
explanations: To do something that causes a problem or mess, typically a serious mistake, scandal, or embarrassing incident. Almost always used for negative outcomes. The subject may or may not have intended the result.

glosses: hard struggle; bitter fight; uphill battle
explanations: A difficult and painful struggle against adversity, whether physical, emotional, or situational. Emphasizes the suffering and effort involved in fighting through hardship.
A formal written expression of gratitude, typically sent after receiving a gift, attending an event, or being helped. An important part of Japanese social etiquette.

A hereditary emblem used to identify a Japanese family, clan, or household. Originating in the Heian period, family crests feature stylized designs based on plants, animals, geometric shapes, or other motifs. They appear on formal clothing, tombstones, and traditional items.
An object made by skilled manual work, often combining artistic beauty with practical function. Includes pottery, lacquerware, textiles, metalwork, and other traditional or modern crafts.
A performer who entertains through comedy, often in a circus or theatrical setting. Also used figuratively for someone who acts the fool to amuse others or to describe someone being made a fool of.
A very old woman. The word is neutral to literary in tone and often appears in narratives, folklore, and descriptive writing. Not typically used as a direct form of address.

glosses: armor and helmet; suit of armor
explanations: A complete set of Japanese warrior armor, including both the body armor ({甲|かぶと}) and helmet ({冑|かぶと}). Refers to the traditional armor worn by samurai and displayed as cultural artifacts in museums and during festivals.

glosses: enjoying the evening cool; cooling off in the evening
explanations: The practice of going outside or sitting on a veranda in the evening to enjoy the cool air after a hot summer day. A quintessentially Japanese summer custom.

glosses: to die by the roadside; to die a miserable death
to die by the roadside; to die a miserable death in the gutter
explanations: To die alone and uncared-for outdoors, with no one to help. Often used figuratively to warn of or express fear about an impoverished, lonely end.

A walled or designated district in Edo-period Japan where prostitution was officially licensed and regulated by the government. The most famous was Yoshiwara in Edo (Tokyo). These districts were abolished in the modern era.

glosses: oiran; high-ranking courtesan of the Edo period
explanations: The highest-ranking courtesans in Edo-period pleasure quarters. Oiran were distinguished by their elaborate hairstyles, extravagant kimono, and high wooden geta. They were accomplished in arts such as calligraphy, tea ceremony, and music.

glosses: color woodblock print; nishiki-e; polychrome print
explanations: A type of multicolored woodblock print developed in mid-18th century Edo Japan. Called 'brocade pictures' because of their vivid colors, which resembled woven brocade fabric. The technique involved using multiple blocks, each for a different color.

glosses: subject of a painting; title of a painting
subject of a painting; motif; pictorial theme
explanations: The subject matter or theme depicted in a painting or drawing. Can also refer to the title given to a finished artwork.

A literary and historical term for suicide, strongly associated with samurai and historical narratives. Often refers to ritual suicide or suicide to preserve honor, though it can also be used for non-ritual suicide in literary contexts.
A railway locomotive powered by a steam engine. While no longer in regular commercial service in Japan, several are preserved and operated as tourist attractions.
The V-shaped fabric or leather strap on traditional Japanese footwear such as geta (wooden clogs) and zori (flat sandals) that passes between the big toe and second toe to hold the foot in place.

glosses: traditional Japanese umbrella; Japanese paper umbrella
explanations: A traditional umbrella made with a bamboo frame and Japanese paper (washi), coated with oil for waterproofing. Distinguished from Western-style umbrellas (洋傘).
A musical instrument that produces sound by blowing air through a reed or across an opening, such as a flute, clarinet, or oboe. Short for 木管楽器.
A musical instrument made of brass that produces sound by buzzing the lips into a cup-shaped mouthpiece, such as a trumpet, trombone, or horn. Short for 金管楽器.
Cooked rice seasoned with vinegar, sugar, and salt, used as the base for sushi. This is sushi chef jargon that has become widely known.
A dense forest found in areas of heavy rainfall, characterized by tall trees and rich biodiversity.
Describes something or someone that meets ordinary standards of quality, behavior, or reasonableness. Often used to contrast with something deficient or abnormal.
Facing something directly or squarely without avoidance.
The eggs of fish, used as a general term covering all varieties including salmon roe, cod roe, herring roe, and others.

glosses: small amount of money; small sum
explanations: A relatively small quantity of money. Often used in financial, legal, and business contexts.
The external shape or physical form of an object. A somewhat formal or technical term compared to the everyday word 形 (かたち).
A clown or comic entertainer, especially one with a white-painted face. Also used figuratively to mean someone who is made a fool of or plays a ridiculous role.
A person's family name, as opposed to their given name. In Japanese naming order, the surname comes first.
The closing period of the year, typically referring to December and especially the last few weeks. Carries a sense of busyness and urgency as the year draws to a close.
A rope or line attached to a person working at heights or in dangerous conditions to prevent fatal falls.
Something essential that one depends on for survival or success.

glosses: emergence; coming to light; coming to the fore
explanations: The act of coming up to the surface from underwater or underground.
An issue, problem, or candidate becoming apparent or prominent.
Devoting oneself exclusively to one type of work or business, without a side job or other occupation.
Describes extremely cruel or inhumane acts or behavior, involving deliberate infliction of suffering.
The place where a person was born or grew up. A very common topic in self-introductions in Japanese.
A condition in which the available water supply is insufficient to meet demand, often caused by lack of rainfall.
Returning to one's job or position after a period of leave, suspension, or absence.
A figure of speech that directly compares two things using words like 'like' or 'as' (in Japanese, ような, みたいな, のごとく). Contrasts with 隠喩 (metaphor).
A figure of speech that describes one thing as being another, without using explicit comparison words. Contrasts with 直喩 (simile).
Objects coated with lacquer (urushi), such as bowls, trays, and boxes. A traditional Japanese craft with a glossy, durable finish.
An instrument for measuring air temperature. Literally 'cold-warm meter.' Used specifically for room or outdoor thermometers, not for medical thermometers.
The practice of keeping honeybee colonies for the production of honey and other products such as beeswax.
Describes a situation where there is virtually no chance of a positive outcome, or a feeling of complete despair.

glosses: to cut open; to slash; to rip apart
to cut open; to slash; to rip apart; to tear
explanations: To cut or tear something violently with a sharp instrument or forcefully. Can also be used figuratively for things that cut through silence, darkness, etc.
A ruler who holds absolute power over a country, typically one who has seized control by force or maintains power through authoritarian means.

glosses: stone construction; built of stone; stonework
explanations: A building, structure, or object made primarily of stone. Also used as a modifier to describe something built from stone.

glosses: simple and honest; naive; unsophisticated; artless
explanations: Describes a person or character that is naturally honest and unaffected, without the worldliness or cynicism of city life. Generally a positive or neutral descriptor, implying a wholesome simplicity.
The place where something is located, especially the official registered address of a building, organization, or institution. Commonly used in official documents, forms, and business contexts.

glosses: to panic; to lose one's head
to panic; to be flustered; to lose one's head
explanations: To become extremely agitated and confused, losing the ability to act calmly. Stronger than simply being surprised — implies visible confusion and disorganized behavior.
The non-physical essence of a person believed to survive after death. Used in religious, spiritual, and philosophical contexts to refer to the soul or spirit of the deceased.
An educational system where male and female students study together in the same institution. Short for {男女|だんじょ}{共学|きょうがく}.

glosses: to be overwhelmed; to be overpowered
to be overwhelmed; to be overpowered; to be awed
explanations: To feel completely dominated or overcome by something far greater in power, scale, or intensity. Can describe being impressed to the point of speechlessness, or being defeated by a stronger force.
Trees planted along streets and roads for shade, beautification, and environmental purposes. A common feature of Japanese urban landscapes.

glosses: place of origin; area of production
explanations: The region or country where a product, plant, or animal originally comes from. Commonly seen on food labels and product packaging in Japan.
The company or entity that produces or manufactures a product. Commonly found on product packaging and labels.
A hole dug in the ground for burying a coffin or remains.
Used figuratively in the expression {墓穴|ぼけつ}を{掘|ほ}る (to dig one's own grave), meaning to cause one's own downfall through careless actions or words.
Occurring at irregular intervals, repeatedly stopping and starting. Used to describe phenomena like rain, noise, or ongoing situations that come and go.

glosses: one after another; in succession; successively
explanations: Events or actions occurring in rapid sequence, one following closely after another. Often implies an unexpected or noteworthy series of occurrences.

Skilled at speaking fluently and persuasively. Can be used positively (eloquent) or negatively (glib, smooth-talking). Often carries a slightly negative nuance, implying that someone talks their way out of things.
A book that someone loves and reads repeatedly. Often used when talking about books that have had a deep personal impact.

glosses: to plan; to plot; to attempt
to plan; to scheme; to plot; to attempt
explanations: To devise or organize a plan, especially something ambitious or secretive. Often implies large-scale plans or schemes, and can carry a negative connotation when used for plots or conspiracies.

glosses: to be revealed; to be detected; to come to light
explanations: For something hidden, secret, or wrongful to become known. Almost always used for negative discoveries such as crimes, lies, or misconduct being exposed.

glosses: way of talking; tone of voice
way of talking; tone of voice; manner of speaking
explanations: The manner or tone in which someone speaks, often revealing their attitude, feelings, or intentions. Used to describe how something was said rather than what was said.
The ratio between the size of a representation (map, model, drawing) and the actual size of what it represents. Expressed as a fraction like 1/50000.
An unfilled area on paper, a form, or a document.
A figurative emptiness or gap, such as a period of time with no activity or a void left by someone's absence.

glosses: annual event; yearly function; regular annual observance
explanations: An event or ceremony held at the same time every year, such as festivals, holidays, and seasonal observances. Can also refer figuratively to something that happens routinely every year.
A licensed professional who cuts, styles, colors, and treats hair. In Japan, beauticians work at {美容室|びようしつ} (beauty salons) and require a national license.
An intense, unwavering attachment to a goal, desire, or grudge. Can be used positively (admirable persistence) or negatively (unhealthy obsession or deep-seated resentment).
A bridge made of iron or steel, especially one designed to carry railway tracks. Also used for any metal bridge.

glosses: to hit the mark; to come true; to be right on target
to hit the mark; to strike the target
to come true; to prove correct; to be right on target
explanations: For a projectile, arrow, or shot to hit its intended target.
For a prediction, forecast, or guess to turn out to be accurate.

glosses: mild flavor; light seasoning; lightly seasoned
explanations: Food that is seasoned lightly, with less salt, soy sauce, or other seasonings than usual. Often associated with Kyoto-style cuisine and considered healthier.
Shoes made of leather, typically formal or business-style footwear. A standard part of business attire in Japan.
The process of smoothing or shining a surface by rubbing it with an abrasive material. Used for metals, glass, gems, and other materials.
Used figuratively to describe the process of improving and perfecting one's skills or abilities through practice and effort.
A three-dimensional shape with circular cross-sections and straight parallel sides. Used for objects, containers, and geometric descriptions.
A sign posted upright on a board or stake, typically placed outdoors to convey warnings, information, or rules. Historically used by authorities to post official notices.
A performer's very first appearance on stage, or more broadly, someone's first time doing something in a public or prominent setting.
A broad, general explanation or summary of a topic, covering the main points without going into great detail. Often used as a book title or section heading.
Describes interactions, services, or transactions conducted without meeting in person. Became widespread during the COVID-19 pandemic and remains common in business and service contexts.
Indicates that a package, order, or shipment has already been sent. Commonly seen in online shopping notifications, tracking pages, and business correspondence.
Describes something that applies broadly or comprehensively rather than to specific parts. Often used when summarizing or giving an overall assessment.

glosses: to be stubborn; to dig in one's heels
to be stubborn; to dig in one's heels; to insist obstinately
explanations: To stubbornly hold to one's position or pride, refusing to yield or compromise even when it would be reasonable to do so. Often implies the person knows they should back down but won't.

glosses: to sit down; to take a seat
to sit down; to take a seat; to settle down
explanations: To lower oneself into a sitting position. More literary or deliberate than {座|すわ}る, often implying carefully or comfortably settling into a seat.

glosses: unmanageable; beyond one's control; too much to handle
explanations: Describes a person, situation, or problem that is too difficult or unruly to deal with. Literally means 'cannot be borne by one's hands.'

glosses: to take along; to bring (people) with one
to take along; to bring (people) with one; to lead
explanations: To bring along one or more people, typically as companions or followers. Implies leading or having others accompany you, often with a sense of being in charge of the group.

glosses: to scramble for; to fight over; to compete for
explanations: To struggle with others to take possession of something. Formed from {奪|うば}う (to seize) + {合|あ}う (reciprocal suffix), indicating mutual competition or a contest over something.

glosses: to trample; to violate; to treat with contempt
to trample underfoot; to stamp on
to violate; to trample on (rights, feelings); to treat with contempt
explanations: To crush something by stepping on it forcefully and grinding it.
Figuratively, to disregard or cruelly violate someone's rights, dignity, or feelings.

glosses: one's eyes light up; to look at something with sparkling eyes
explanations: Describes the way someone's eyes shine with excitement, curiosity, or eagerness. Used to vividly convey enthusiasm or delight.

glosses: to be frozen with shock; to be flabbergasted
to be frozen with shock; to be flabbergasted; to be so surprised one cannot stand
explanations: To be so startled, frightened, or astonished that one's legs give out and one cannot stand up properly. Literally, one's lower back ({腰|こし}) gives way.

glosses: permanent residency; right of permanent residence
explanations: The legal right to reside permanently in a country. In Japan, this refers to a specific visa status that allows foreign nationals to live and work in Japan indefinitely.
A medication used to relieve pain. Covers both over-the-counter and prescription pain relievers.
A married couple who are both elderly. Often used warmly to describe a couple who have been together for a long time.

glosses: being well-versed; expert knowledge; thorough familiarity
being well-versed in; having expert knowledge of; thorough familiarity
explanations: Having deep, detailed knowledge of a particular subject or field. Used with する to indicate mastering or being thoroughly familiar with something.

glosses: deterrent; deterrent force; power of deterrence
explanations: The power or capability to discourage or prevent an action, especially military aggression or criminal behavior, by making the consequences unacceptable.
An intuitive sense beyond the five physical senses — the ability to perceive or know something without conscious reasoning. Similar to English 'sixth sense.'
A book or written work widely recognized as excellent or important. Refers specifically to written works, not art or music.

glosses: sold out; full house (with thanks to the audience)
sold out; full house; standing room only (with thanks)
explanations: An announcement that a venue is completely full, expressing gratitude to attendees. Originally from sumo and kabuki, where a banner with this phrase is displayed when all seats are filled.

glosses: as before; as usual; as has been the case
as before; as usual; in the same way as before
explanations: Indicates that something continues in the same manner as it has been done previously. Used to state that no change has been or will be made.

glosses: new fiscal year; new academic year
explanations: The beginning of a new fiscal or academic year. In Japan, both the fiscal year and academic year start in April, making this a significant transition point for businesses, schools, and government.
A person's given name (as opposed to their family name). Called 'the name below' because in Japanese vertical writing, the given name appears below the family name.

glosses: beware of fire; fire safety; fire prevention
explanations: A warning phrase about fire safety. Most commonly heard as a call during traditional neighborhood fire-watch patrols, where volunteers walk through residential areas at night, clapping wooden blocks and calling out this phrase.
A person who develops something — software, products, technologies, land, or other projects. In modern usage, often refers to software developers.

glosses: proficiency; mastery; becoming skilled through practice
explanations: The state of having become highly skilled at something through sustained practice and experience. Emphasizes the process of maturing into competence.
An official document certifying that a person has completed a course of study, passed an examination, or been granted a license or qualification.
A prayer or ritual performed to invoke rain during a drought. Historically practiced at shrines and temples across Japan, and still performed as a cultural tradition in some communities.

glosses: to save (a life); to survive; to cling to life
to save (a life); to hold on to life; to barely survive
explanations: To narrowly avoid death; to have one's life saved, typically after an accident or illness. Almost always used in the set phrase {命|いのち}を{取|と}り{留|と}める.

glosses: life-threatening; to be a matter of life and death
explanations: Describes a situation, condition, or action that could result in death. Used to emphasize the extreme seriousness of a danger.

glosses: to nod (in agreement); to say yes; to give one's consent
to nod (in agreement); to say yes; to consent
explanations: To nod one's head vertically, indicating agreement or approval. Often used in the negative to describe someone refusing to agree.
The darkening or reddening of skin from exposure to sunlight. Used both for desirable tanning and painful sunburn.
Discoloration or deterioration of materials such as books, fabric, or furniture caused by prolonged exposure to sunlight.

glosses: detour; dawdling; loitering on the way
explanations: Stopping or lingering along the way instead of going directly to one's destination. Often used with する or {食|く}う. Originally referred to a horse stopping to eat grass on the roadside.

glosses: local train; train stopping at every station
explanations: A train service that stops at every station along its route, as opposed to express or rapid services. Often abbreviated to {各停|かくてい}.

glosses: buying books and leaving them unread
buying books and leaving them unread; piling up unread books
explanations: The habit of acquiring books but letting them pile up without reading them. A playful compound blending {積|つ}む (to pile up) with {読|どく} (reading).
Describing someone who thinks carefully before acting, showing deep consideration and good judgment.
The year two years ago from the present. More formal than the colloquial おととし.
Describing actions or people that are disrespectful toward the gods, religion, or things considered sacred. Also used more loosely to mean "outrageous" or "shameful."

glosses: relying on divine help; prayer as a last resort
relying on divine help; praying to God as a last resort
explanations: Turning to the gods or to prayer when all other options have been exhausted. Implies a desperate or helpless situation.
A person's normal, baseline body temperature when healthy, typically around 36-37°C.

glosses: mastermind; wire-puller; power behind the scenes
explanations: A person who secretly controls or influences events from behind the scenes, especially in politics or crime. Originally referred to the black curtain used in kabuki theater to hide stagehands.

glosses: book collection; library holdings; one's books
explanations: Books owned by a person or institution. Refers to the collection as a whole rather than individual volumes.

glosses: undeniable; cannot be denied; there is no denying that
explanations: The negative potential form of {否|いな}む (to deny), used as a set expression meaning something cannot be denied or is undeniable. Almost always appears in this fixed negative form.
Swimming as a competitive sport, including races in various strokes and distances. Distinct from recreational swimming or water polo.

glosses: packed; full of content; loaded with things
explanations: Having a large amount or variety of things, especially content, events, or food. Conveys a positive sense of abundance.

glosses: breakthrough measure; solution to a deadlock
breakthrough measure; solution to break a deadlock
explanations: A plan or measure to break through a difficult situation or impasse. Implies the situation is stuck and requires decisive action.
Dedicated effort to improve one's knowledge or skills through persistent study and practice. A formal word conveying deep commitment to learning.
A person who does not appreciate or acknowledge kindness received. Also used as an adjective to describe such behavior.

glosses: sole of a shoe; bottom of a shoe
explanations: The bottom part of a shoe that contacts the ground.

glosses: full (parking lot); no parking spaces available
explanations: Indicates that a parking lot has no available spaces. Commonly seen on signs at parking facilities.
A formal term for the hair growing on one's head. Used in official, medical, and regulatory contexts.

glosses: the Japanese syllabary; the fifty sounds
the Japanese syllabary; the fifty sounds; gojūon order
explanations: The systematic arrangement of Japanese kana characters in a grid of rows and columns. Also refers to the traditional ordering system used in dictionaries and indexes.

glosses: wasted talent or possession; having something valuable but not using it
explanations: A proverb describing the situation where someone possesses something valuable — a skill, tool, or resource — but fails to put it to use, making the possession pointless.

glosses: all is lost; it's all over; nothing more can be done
explanations: An expression meaning that the situation is hopeless and there are no remaining options. Used when defeat or failure is inevitable.

glosses: to nitpick; to split hairs; to find fault with trivial details
explanations: To obsessively point out minor, insignificant flaws or details. Used critically of someone who focuses on trivialities instead of the big picture.

glosses: deportment; bearing; manners; the way one carries oneself
explanations: One's overall physical bearing and behavior, including posture, gestures, and general conduct. Covers both standing and sitting movements.
The melodic or rhythmic quality of music, speech, or poetry.
A technical term in music theory referring to the system of dividing the octave into intervals (e.g., equal temperament, just intonation).

glosses: strange tale; variant account; unusual story
strange tale; unusual story; curious report
explanations: A story about something strange or extraordinary, especially supernatural or mysterious events.
A different version or differing account of a known story or historical event.
An area designated for washing, especially the space in a Japanese bathroom where you wash your body before entering the bathtub, or a sink/washing area in a kitchen or workplace.
Any material that has been published, including books, magazines, newspapers, and other printed or digital works.

glosses: many; numerous; a great number; a multitude
explanations: A literary word meaning a large number or great quantity. More formal and poetic than たくさん.
The act of forcibly taking away someone's rights, qualifications, titles, or privileges. Used in legal, political, and formal contexts.
An official order requiring someone to appear before a court or other authority. Used in legal and judicial contexts.
The act of calling forth a being or entity, as in fantasy, games, or mythology.

glosses: to become refined; to become sophisticated
to become refined; to become sophisticated; to become stylish
explanations: To shed an unsophisticated quality and become polished in appearance, manner, or taste. Often used to describe someone whose style or bearing has noticeably improved.

glosses: neglect of health; unhealthy lifestyle; intemperance
explanations: A lifestyle that disregards health, including poor diet, lack of sleep, excessive drinking, or other habits harmful to the body.

glosses: stomach and intestines; digestive organs; gastrointestinal tract
explanations: Refers collectively to the stomach and intestines, or more broadly to the digestive system. Commonly used when discussing digestive health.

glosses: train window; car window (and the view from it)
train window; car window; vehicle window
explanations: The window of a train, bus, or car. Often used to refer not just to the window itself but to the view seen through it while traveling.
The remaining base of a tree after it has been cut down.
A short run taken before jumping, throwing, or performing an athletic movement that requires momentum.

glosses: reversal; relapse; going back to an earlier state
explanations: Returning to a previous or worse state after progress had been made. Used for situations, conditions, and processes that move backward.
The dried or fresh leaves of the tea plant used to brew tea. Refers to the leaves themselves rather than the prepared beverage.
Protecting or defending a position, area, or territory, whether in a military or general sense.
In sports, especially baseball, the act of playing defense or fielding.
The act of throwing a ball, especially a pitcher's throw in baseball. Also used for the number of pitches thrown.
A stadium or ground where baseball games are played.
A feeling or state of being empty inside, lacking substance or meaning. Often describes emotional emptiness or the hollow quality of something without real content.

glosses: wasted effort; futile labor; vain attempt
wasted effort; futile labor; fruitless work
explanations: Effort that produces no result; work done in vain. Emphasizes the pointlessness of the endeavor.
A room made completely dark, used for developing photographs or for scientific experiments that require the absence of light.
A long, thin rod used for knitting yarn into fabric. Typically sold in pairs or sets and available in various thicknesses.
The act of interacting and maintaining relationships with other people. Can refer to one's general ability or willingness to socialize.
Sleeves that extend to the wrist, or a garment with such sleeves. Often used as a modifier for shirts, sweaters, and other clothing.
Sleeves that end above the elbow, or a garment with such sleeves. Standard summer clothing vocabulary.
A deep blue color produced from the indigo plant. One of the traditional Japanese colors with deep cultural significance.

glosses: chief priest of a Buddhist temple
chief priest; head priest of a Buddhist temple
explanations: The priest who resides at and manages a Buddhist temple. The term implies that the priest lives at the temple and is responsible for its religious activities and upkeep.

glosses: beginning of the week; start of the new week
beginning of the week; start of the new week (typically Monday)
explanations: The start of the work week, usually Monday. Commonly used in business and news contexts to refer to the first business day after the weekend.

glosses: erasure; deletion; striking out; removal from a record
explanations: The act of erasing, crossing out, or officially removing something from a record or register. Used in formal and administrative contexts.

glosses: betrayal; breach of trust; treachery; perfidy
explanations: The act of betraying someone's trust or breaking faith. Used in formal, legal, and literary contexts to describe serious violations of trust.
Something that cannot be avoided or prevented. A formal word used in analytical, academic, and news contexts.

glosses: fighting back; returning fire; accepting a challenge
accepting a challenge; rising to the occasion
explanations: Responding to an attack or aggression by fighting back. Used in military and figurative contexts.
Taking on a challenge or competition that has been presented, whether in sports, business, or debate.

glosses: tea utensils; tea implements; tea ware
explanations: Tools and vessels used for preparing and serving tea, especially in the context of the Japanese tea ceremony. Includes items such as tea bowls, tea caddies, and whisks.
