the act of compressing or concentrating the essence of something
the process of a substance dissolving into a liquid solvent
the process of a solid becoming liquid through heat
the operation or running of industrial facilities, factories, or machinery
the transfer of ownership or management of public enterprises to the private sector
the transfer of private enterprises or assets to government ownership
the feeling of disappointment when something turns out to be less exciting, difficult, or significant than expected
having to do something twice because it wasn't done properly the first time, resulting in unnecessary extra work
wind blowing from the sea, often carrying the scent of salt
interrogative asking about the number of times or frequency of an action
interrogative asking about the number of people
interrogative asking about someone's age
the time of day when light first appears in the sky before sunrise
the moment when the sun appears above the horizon; also the time at which this occurs
the thin curved shape of the moon visible shortly after new moon or before the next new moon
the phase of the moon when it appears as a complete circle, fully illuminated by the sun
the phase of the moon when it is not visible from Earth because it is positioned between Earth and the sun
a brief rain shower that passes quickly, often leaving sunny skies behind
a deep, penetrating cold that seems to chill from the core, often associated with damp cold weather
to become familiar with a sound, voice, or expression through repeated exposure

glosses: to wander into; to stray into
explanations: to accidentally enter an unfamiliar place while lost or confused

glosses: to pull out; to extract; to headhunt
explanations: to remove something by pulling it out, such as a plant, cork, or tooth
to recruit talented individuals away from another company or organization
to toss or hurl something into a container, space, or situation
the amount paid for borrowing money or earned on savings and investments
a method of paying for something by dividing the total amount into multiple smaller payments over time
paying the full amount at once rather than in installments
an incorrect understanding or perception based on erroneous assumption or interpretation
the tendency to forget things, often due to age, distraction, or poor memory
temporarily forgetting something you normally know well, often at an inconvenient moment
going somewhere and returning on the same day without staying overnight
sleeping away from one's usual residence, such as at a friend's place, hotel, or elsewhere
the mental capacity to direct attention and maintain focus on a task or subject
the creative mental ability to form images, ideas, or concepts not present to the senses
the mental ability to retain and recall information and experiences
the mental capacity to make sensible decisions and form sound opinions
a room or area in a house containing a sink for washing face and hands, often adjacent to the bathroom
a room where one removes clothing before bathing, typically found adjacent to the bathroom in Japanese homes and at public baths
a traditional Japanese comfort food consisting of meat (usually beef or pork), potatoes, and onions simmered in a sweet soy-based broth
a Japanese rice bowl dish consisting of chicken and egg simmered in a sweet soy-based sauce, served over rice

glosses: to be preoccupied with, to be absorbed in
explanations: To be so focused on one thing that other responsibilities or tasks are neglected. Almost always used with に to mark what one is preoccupied with, and carries a negative nuance of neglecting something else.
A small freshwater bivalve commonly used in Japanese cooking, especially in miso soup. Prized for its rich flavor and believed to be good for the liver.

glosses: chimaki, rice dumpling wrapped in bamboo leaf
explanations: A traditional Japanese confection of glutinous rice or rice flour wrapped in bamboo or reed leaves and steamed. Eaten especially during the Boys' Day festival on May 5th.
A hearty noodle dish originating from Nagasaki, featuring thick noodles in a rich pork-bone and chicken broth topped with stir-fried vegetables, seafood, and pork.
Mixing different types of things together haphazardly, especially different kinds of alcoholic drinks.
A traditional Japanese male hairstyle where the hair is gathered and tied into a knot on top of the head. Historically worn by samurai and now by sumo wrestlers.

glosses: fine points of language, wording details
explanations: A collective term for Japanese grammatical particles (て, に, を, は, etc.).
By extension, the subtle details and nuances of how something is worded or phrased.
A Japanese tax system that allows individuals to make donations to local governments of their choice in exchange for tax deductions and regional specialty gifts in return.
The time of year when a business is at its busiest and earns the most revenue.
A modern Japanese martial art that emphasizes redirecting an attacker's energy through throws and joint locks rather than striking. Founded by Ueshiba Morihei in the early 20th century.

glosses: iaido, art of drawing the sword
explanations: A Japanese martial art focused on the smooth, controlled drawing of the sword from its scabbard, striking an opponent, and resheathing the blade. Practiced primarily through solo forms (kata).
Pellets of ice that fall from cumulonimbus clouds during storms. Larger than sleet, and can cause damage to crops and property.

glosses: karate, the way of the empty hand
explanations: A Japanese martial art originating from Okinawa that emphasizes striking techniques using punches, kicks, knee strikes, and open-hand techniques. The formal name for what is commonly called 空手.
A difference or divergence from a standard, average, or expected value. Used in statistical, scientific, and educational contexts.
A substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without being consumed in the process.
Figuratively, a person or event that triggers or accelerates change.
A sensory perception that appears real but is created by the mind, occurring without any actual external stimulus. Can be visual, auditory, or involve other senses.

glosses: to hold up; to shine in; to pour
to hold up, to put up
to shine in, to come through
to pour, to offer a drink
explanations: To hold something up or over oneself, most commonly an umbrella.
For light or color to come through or appear. Used when sunlight streams in or when a flush of color appears on someone's face.
To pour a drink for someone, especially sake. Part of the traditional custom of pouring for others at meals.
A casual expression of agreement or acknowledgment, used to affirm what the other person has said. Softer and more conversational than はい or ええ.

glosses: I wonder, is that so?, I'm not sure about that
explanations: A casual expression of mild doubt or uncertainty in response to something someone has said. Can express genuine wondering or polite disagreement.

glosses: maybe so, could be, you might be right
explanations: A casual expression of tentative agreement or concession. The speaker acknowledges the possibility without fully committing to agreement. Short form of そうかもしれない.

A casual expression used to seek or express agreement. Can be a tag question confirming what someone said, or a self-directed statement of realization or conviction. Predominantly used by male speakers.

glosses: right?, see?, I told you so
explanations: A casual, assertive expression used to confirm something the speaker believes is true, or to press the listener for agreement. Stronger and more assertive than だよな. Predominantly male speech.
A casual expression of puzzlement or curiosity about the reason for something. Can be directed at others as a question or used as a rhetorical musing to oneself.

glosses: are you serious?, no way, for real?
explanations: An exclamation expressing strong surprise, disbelief, or shock. Predominantly used by male speakers. Can be directed at someone or used as a reaction to a situation.

glosses: I messed up, I screwed up
I messed up, I screwed up, I blew it
explanations: A casual exclamation acknowledging that one has made a significant mistake or blunder. Past tense of やらかす, almost always used in this past form to react to something that has already gone wrong.

glosses: it's no good, it won't work
explanations: Expresses that something is hopeless, broken, or not functioning. Used when a plan, attempt, or object fails.
Expresses personal inability or exhaustion. The speaker is at their limit, physically or mentally.

glosses: it's impossible, I can't do it
it's impossible, I can't do it, no way
explanations: A casual exclamation expressing that something is beyond one's ability or that a situation is hopeless. Often used as a gut reaction to refuse or give up.

glosses: I'm tired, I'm exhausted, I'm worn out
explanations: A common casual expression stating that one is tired. The past tense form of {疲|つか}れる, used as a standalone exclamation rather than as a verb in a sentence.
The standard casual way to say one is hungry. Literally 'my stomach has become empty,' using the past tense of お{腹|なか}が{空|す}く to express the resulting state.
The standard casual way to say one is thirsty. Literally 'my throat has dried,' using the past tense of のどが{渇|かわ}く to express the resulting state.
A casual exclamation of surprise, curiosity, or confusion upon encountering something unexpected. Can be a genuine question or a rhetorical expression of bewilderment.

glosses: wait a moment, hold on, just a second
explanations: A casual request for someone to wait briefly. One of the most common everyday phrases, used to ask for a short pause in conversation or action.

glosses: that's a problem, this is tricky, oh dear
explanations: A casual expression of being troubled or at a loss. Used when facing an inconvenient or difficult situation that requires thought. Often murmured to oneself.
A casual back-channel response indicating that the listener is following along and encourages the speaker to continue. Repeating うん emphasizes active listening.

glosses: unable to read the room, socially clueless
unable to read the room, socially oblivious
explanations: Describes a person who fails to pick up on the unspoken atmosphere or social cues in a situation. Often abbreviated to KY (ケーワイ).

glosses: so for that reason, that's why
so for that reason, and so, that's why
explanations: A discourse connector used to summarize a preceding explanation and transition to a conclusion or result. Links cause to effect in casual conversation.

glosses: so basically, and so, that's why
explanations: A very casual discourse connector used to wrap up an explanation and state the result. A contracted form of というわけで, commonly used in spoken Japanese to transition smoothly.
An emphatic form of すごい, with the double consonant (っ) adding intensity. Used as both an adjective ('that's amazing') and an adverb ('really, super').

glosses: anywhere is fine, I don't mind where
explanations: A casual expression indicating that the speaker has no preference about location. Often used when asked to choose a place for eating, meeting, etc.
A casual expression indicating that the speaker has no preference about timing. Used when asked to choose a time for meeting, scheduling, etc.

glosses: oops, I did it (by accident), I messed up
explanations: A casual exclamation expressing that one has accidentally done something wrong or made a minor mistake. Lighter and more playful than やらかした. Contraction of やってしまった.

glosses: budget SIM card, discount mobile plan
explanations: A low-cost mobile phone SIM card or plan offered by MVNOs (mobile virtual network operators) as an alternative to the major carriers. A significant part of everyday life in Japan for cost-conscious consumers.
An interjection expressing mild annoyance, frustration, or disappointment. Similar to clicking one's tongue. Less harsh than くそ or ちくしょう.

glosses: for now, for the time being, first of all
explanations: A casual abbreviation of とりあえずまあ (well, for starters). Used to suggest doing something as an immediate first step without overthinking.
An ultra-casual abbreviation of {了解|りょうかい} (understood/roger). Used primarily in texting and messaging to quickly acknowledge a message.
A very casual abbreviation of ありがとうございます. Used as a quick, breezy expression of thanks, especially among young people and in informal settings.
The young, edible shoot of a bamboo plant. A prized spring ingredient in Japanese cuisine.
A cooking technique where food is grilled or broiled with a glaze of soy sauce, mirin, and sugar, producing a glossy finish. Also refers to dishes prepared this way.
Pork bones, or the rich, milky-white broth made by boiling pork bones for many hours. Most commonly associated with ramen.
Seasoned pork that is braised or roasted, commonly served as a ramen topping or in rice bowls. Adapted from Chinese char siu.
Chinese-style fried rice, a staple dish at Chinese restaurants in Japan and a popular home-cooked meal.
Machine-dispensed ice cream served in a cone or cup, softer and lighter than regular ice cream. A wasei-eigo term ("soft cream" in Japanese English).
A condiment sauce, especially the brown Worcester-style sauce (ウスターソース) commonly used in Japanese cuisine. Also used as a general term for Western-style sauces.
The origin or source of information, data, or content. Used in journalism, IT, and everyday conversation.
An additional ingredient placed on top of a dish, such as ramen, pizza, or ice cream.

A famous person, or more commonly in Japanese, someone who is wealthy, fashionable, and lives a luxurious lifestyle. The meaning has shifted from the English "celebrity" to emphasize wealth and glamour over fame.
A young, low-ranking delinquent or petty criminal. Often implies someone who acts tough or intimidating but is not a serious organized crime figure.
A school uniform modeled on naval sailor suits, traditionally worn by female middle and high school students in Japan. Features a characteristic sailor collar.
The practice of restricting food intake or exercising to lose weight. In Japanese, ダイエット almost exclusively refers to weight-loss efforts, not a general eating pattern.
A deeply distressing experience that causes lasting psychological harm. In casual usage, also used loosely for any bad experience that leaves a lasting negative impression.
The quality of being considerate and tactful about others' feelings. In Japanese, almost always used in negative contexts — to describe a lack of sensitivity.
The deliberate distortion or simplification of shapes in art, especially making characters or objects look cute, exaggerated, or cartoonish. Common in manga, anime, and character design.
A joint promotional partnership between companies, brands, or media properties. Common in entertainment, where a song or product is paired with a TV drama, anime, or film.
The choice or judgment of when to do something, or the moment at which something happens.
The main subject or central idea of a work, discussion, event, or activity.
Describes an environment or group that is uncomfortably loud or chaotic with sound.
Describes a situation or period that is socially or politically unsettled and full of commotion.
Describes a situation, period, or atmosphere where there is a rush of activity and little time to spare, creating a feeling of restlessness.
Describes an event, occasion, or outcome that is fortunate and calls for celebration.
Used ironically to describe someone who is blissfully unaware or foolishly optimistic.
The final period of the calendar year, typically referring to December and the days leading up to New Year's.

glosses: beginning of the year, New Year
explanations: The first days of the new calendar year, typically referring to early January.
Information or opinions about products, services, or businesses spread informally between people, either in person or through online review platforms.
The act of looking through or reading documents, web pages, or other materials, typically in a formal or official context.
The act of sending electronic messages, data, or signals. Used for email, text messages, and other digital communications.

glosses: just in case; by any chance
just in case, by any chance
explanations: Used to express a very unlikely but possible scenario. Literally "one in ten thousand." Often paired with conditional forms (〜たら、〜ば) or the expression の{場合|ばあい}は to describe precautionary measures or worst-case scenarios.
A comprehensive listing or summary of items, data, or information presented for easy reference. Commonly used in business documents, websites, and administrative contexts.
Describing something that comes from or favors only one side, without balance or reciprocity. Used for communication, decisions, relationships, or actions that lack mutual participation.

glosses: part of, link in a chain
explanations: One component or phase within a larger connected series of actions, plans, or processes. Emphasizes that the item in question is not isolated but belongs to a broader whole.

glosses: a break; a cup of tea
explanations: A short rest or pause, especially one involving tea or a smoke. The word originally referred to one serving of medicine or tea, and has come to broadly mean taking a short breather.
One serving or dose, used as a counter for powdered medicine, tea, or tobacco.
Used almost exclusively with negative predicates to mean "cannot simply say" or "cannot generalize." Indicates that a blanket statement would be inaccurate because there are exceptions or nuances.
Describes how something appears on the surface, often implying that the reality underneath may differ. Used to set up a contrast between appearance and actual nature.
Maintaining the same attitude, policy, or approach from beginning to end without wavering. Emphasizes steadfastness and lack of contradiction.

glosses: to strive, to endeavor, to make an effort
explanations: To exert oneself toward a goal or to try one's best to do something. Typically used with ～ように努める or ～に努める patterns.
Going back to the place where one grew up, typically after living or working elsewhere for a period of time. Often carries a sense of nostalgia or emotional homecoming.

glosses: attendance; visiting a venue or event
explanations: Coming to an event, exhibition, or venue as a visitor or attendee. Commonly used in formal or commercial contexts.

glosses: end of a consecutive holiday; first day back after a long weekend
explanations: The period immediately following a series of consecutive days off, typically referring to the first working day after a long weekend or holiday period like Golden Week or Obon.
Evaluating something or someone more highly than is warranted. Used for abilities, values, risks, or any measurable quality that has been judged too favorably.
The row closest to the stage, screen, or front of a venue. Used for seating at concerts, theaters, classrooms, and similar settings.

glosses: outside rounds; visiting clients; outside sales
explanations: Going outside the office to visit clients, make deliveries, or conduct business at external locations. A common part of many sales and service jobs in Japan.
The outer circle of a loop line (such as the Yamanote Line in Tokyo) or the outer circumference of something.
Attempting something again after a previous failure or setback. Emphasizes determination and willingness to try once more.

The designated day on which garbage, recyclables, or other waste is collected by the municipal service. An essential part of daily life in Japan, where garbage sorting and collection schedules are strictly followed.
The tendency or philosophy of looking at the bright side of things and expecting favorable outcomes. Can refer to a personal attitude or a philosophical position.
Vegetables preserved by burying them in a fermented rice bran (nuka) bed. A traditional Japanese pickling method that produces distinctively tangy, umami-rich pickles.

The large green leaf of the perilla plant (Perilla frutescens), widely used as a garnish and flavoring in Japanese cuisine. In culinary contexts, the green variety is typically called ooba, while the botanical term is aojiso.

A partnership where a couple lives together as if married but has not submitted a marriage registration ({婚姻届|こんいんとどけ}). In Japan, this means the couple functions as spouses in daily life but is not legally recognized as married under the family register system.

glosses: having a promising future; full of promise
explanations: Describes a person, career, or endeavor that shows great potential for future success. A four-character compound (yojijukugo) used as praise or high expectation.
A new version of a book, document, software, or other work that has been updated or corrected from the original.
Formally borrowing something from someone, such as equipment, a room, or a concept. Used in administrative, legal, and academic contexts.

glosses: leaving one's seat; withdrawing from a meeting
leaving one's seat; withdrawing from a meeting or gathering
explanations: Formally leaving one's seat or place during a meeting, class, ceremony, or other gathering. Often implies excusing oneself partway through.
A slight, often unsettling smile that suggests mockery, insincerity, or hidden intent. Almost always carries a negative connotation, unlike a genuine smile.
A close-range physical fight where people grab and wrestle each other. Can describe anything from a playful tussle between children to a serious altercation between adults.
An organized group of singers who perform together, typically in parts (soprano, alto, tenor, bass). Found in schools, communities, churches, and professional settings.
A protected area of natural beauty or ecological significance designated and managed by the national government. Japan has 34 national parks as of 2024.

Hiring someone who has prior work experience, as opposed to recruiting fresh graduates ({新卒採用|しんそつさいよう}). A significant concept in Japanese employment culture, where the traditional model emphasizes hiring new graduates.

glosses: inexperienced; having no experience; no prior experience
explanations: Having no prior experience in a particular field, job, or activity. Very commonly seen in job listings to indicate that applicants without experience are welcome.

glosses: reckless driving; tearing along at high speed
explanations: Driving or riding a vehicle at dangerously high speed, often recklessly. Associated with illegal street racing and biker gangs.
Used figuratively to describe someone or something going at full speed with unstoppable energy, such as a winning streak in sports or a hit product's sales.

Tools, devices, or equipment used for specific purposes, especially in gymnastics, medicine, or scientific work. Distinguished from {機械|きかい} (machine) by emphasis on precision instruments and manual tools rather than powered machinery.
A formal request for advice or opinions from an expert body or advisory committee, especially in government or institutional contexts. The body consulted then provides a formal response ({答申|とうしん}).
Firmly and repeatedly refusing an offer, appointment, or request. Stronger than a simple refusal, implying that the person declines despite pressure or repeated offers.

glosses: taking care of one's health; temperance
taking care of one's health; leading a healthy lifestyle; temperance
explanations: Consciously maintaining healthy habits by moderating diet, exercise, sleep, and other lifestyle factors. Implies self-discipline and restraint in daily living.
Taking revenge for a wrong done to oneself or one's family. Historically referred to sanctioned revenge killings in feudal Japan. Now used more broadly for any act of getting even.

glosses: pupil; disciple; student of a master
explanations: A person who studies under a particular master or teacher, especially in traditional arts, martial arts, crafts, or academic disciplines. Implies a personal teacher-student relationship.
A valuable object passed down through generations within a family. Can be a physical item such as a sword, scroll, or piece of art, or used figuratively for something cherished.

glosses: departing first; leaving ahead of others
explanations: In sports, being selected to play from the beginning of a game, as opposed to being a substitute. Most commonly used in baseball for the starting pitcher.
Leaving or departing before others in a group, such as taking an earlier train or flight.

A high-status Shinto shrine, typically one with imperial connections or dedicated to the imperial family or a major deity. Higher in rank than a regular shrine ({神社|じんじゃ}). When used alone without a place name, it usually refers to Ise Jingu, the most sacred Shinto shrine.

glosses: to inquire, to make an inquiry
to inquire, to make an inquiry, to contact for information
explanations: To contact a person, company, or organization to ask about something. Used for formal or semi-formal information requests, customer service inquiries, and official communications.

glosses: to engrave on one's mind, to keep firmly in mind
explanations: To remember something deeply and never forget it. Stronger than simply remembering — implies carving important lessons, facts, or warnings into one's consciousness. Often used in formal or written contexts.
A system of government or leadership in which one person or group holds absolute power without checks or democratic processes. Used in political, historical, and sometimes figurative contexts.
A wild duck, as distinct from domesticated ducks. Common in Japanese cuisine (especially in soba dishes) and frequently seen in parks and rivers.
Slang for a person who is easy to take advantage of or deceive. From the idea of a duck being easy prey for hunters.

glosses: to be done boiling, to be boiled through
to be done boiling, to be boiled through, to finish cooking (by boiling)
explanations: Used when food has finished boiling and is ready. An intransitive verb indicating the completion of the boiling process.

glosses: party leader, head of a political party
explanations: The leader or chairperson of a political party. Used in news and political discourse.
A state of being pure, clean, or uncontaminated. Used both for physical cleanliness (air, water) and spiritual or moral purity. Common in Buddhist contexts and product labeling.

glosses: long journey, long way, long distance
explanations: A long road or journey. Often used adverbially (遠路はるばる) to express appreciation that someone has come from far away.
A large-scale festival or ceremonial event, often of religious, cultural, or commemorative significance. More formal than 祭り, emphasizing the ceremonial or official nature of the event.

glosses: love affair, romantic relationship, being lovers
explanations: A romantic relationship between two people. Describes the state of being romantically involved. Has a somewhat literary or traditional flavor.

glosses: heart and soul, one's whole energy
heart and soul, one's whole energy, utmost effort
explanations: One's full spiritual and physical energy poured into something. Used to describe wholehearted dedication and effort, especially in creative or demanding work.

glosses: liquid India ink, bottled sumi ink
explanations: Pre-made liquid ink used for calligraphy (書道) and ink painting (水墨画). A convenient alternative to grinding an ink stick on an inkstone.

glosses: ticket issuance, issuing tickets or vouchers
explanations: The act of issuing, printing, or dispensing tickets, vouchers, or certificates. Commonly seen at stations, airports, and event venues.
The concept of absolute nothingness or nonexistence. An important concept in Buddhist philosophy and Zen, representing the absence of all things.
As a prefix, negates or indicates the absence of what follows. Extremely productive — attaches to many nouns to form compound words.

glosses: to build, to construct, to brew
to build, to construct, to manufacture
to brew, to produce (alcohol, miso, etc.)
explanations: To create something large-scale such as buildings, ships, or infrastructure. Used for construction and large-scale manufacturing, as opposed to 作る which covers general making and creation.
To produce fermented or brewed products such as sake, wine, beer, soy sauce, or miso. This is the standard kanji used for brewing and fermentation.
Measures taken to prevent or repel insects. Used for products and methods that keep bugs away from clothing, food, or living spaces.
The quality of producing results immediately or very quickly. Used for medicines, treatments, methods, and strategies that work right away.
A plate of intermediate size, typically around 15-21 cm in diameter. Part of the standard Japanese tableware size system that distinguishes small, medium, and large plates.

glosses: to subside, to be suppressed, to calm down
explanations: For disturbances, pain, emotions, or unrest to settle down and return to a calm state. Implies that something turbulent or agitated has been brought under control or has naturally subsided.
Something that exists in a computer-generated or digital form rather than physically. Widely used in technology and computing contexts.
Something assumed or imagined for the purpose of planning, training, or analysis. Used for hypothetical scenarios and assumed opponents or situations.
Traveling from place to place without a fixed destination or home. Can be romantic (the wandering artist) or negative (homelessness), depending on context.

glosses: dumbfounded, stunned, in a daze, stupefied
explanations: A state of being so shocked, surprised, or overwhelmed that one cannot think or react. Often describes standing or sitting motionless in disbelief.

Feeling upset or offended because something turned out differently from what one expected, especially when one feels wrongly judged or unfairly treated. Expresses a sense of indignation mixed with surprise.
A formal expression of gratitude or thankfulness. Used in official or ceremonial contexts to convey deep appreciation.
A formal expression of apology or regret. Less common than the gratitude meaning.

Having an otherworldly, captivating beauty that is both attractive and slightly mysterious or dangerous. Often describes women, performances, or artistic works that possess a mesmerizing, sensual quality.

glosses: garden tree, yard tree, ornamental tree
explanations: A tree planted in a garden or yard, typically for decorative purposes. Includes both ornamental and fruit-bearing trees grown in residential gardens.

glosses: hand clapping, clapping to a beat
hand clapping, clapping to a rhythm or beat
explanations: Rhythmic clapping of hands, typically done in unison by an audience or group to accompany music, cheering, or traditional celebrations.

glosses: one reading, a single perusal, reading through once
explanations: Reading something once, or giving something a single read-through. Often used as a recommendation — suggesting that something is worth reading.
Briefly boiling ingredients before the main cooking step to remove bitterness, excess starch, or impurities, or to soften tough vegetables. A fundamental technique in Japanese cooking.

glosses: resting in peace, passing on (of spirits), dying peacefully
explanations: In Buddhist terminology, the attainment of enlightenment and release from the cycle of rebirth. The original religious meaning.
In everyday usage, for a spirit or ghost to find peace and move on, or euphemistically for someone to die. Also used humorously for things that are broken beyond repair.

glosses: first ten days of the month, early part of the month
explanations: The period from the 1st to the 10th of a month. Part of the traditional Japanese system of dividing each month into three roughly equal periods.

glosses: backrest, back of a chair or seat
explanations: The part of a chair, sofa, or seat that supports the sitter's back. A common everyday word for furniture and seating.

glosses: residual heat, carryover heat, remaining warmth
explanations: Heat that remains in an oven, pan, or other cooking vessel after the heat source has been turned off. A key concept in cooking, where residual heat continues to cook food. Also used for industrial heat recovery.

glosses: actual conditions, real situation, true state of affairs
explanations: The reality behind appearances or official accounts. Emphasizes the gap between how things seem and how they actually are, often implying that the truth is different from what is publicly known.

glosses: deferred payment, payment after delivery, pay later
explanations: A payment arrangement where the buyer pays after receiving goods or services. Common in online shopping and business transactions.

glosses: lady; noblewoman; woman of high social standing
explanations: A woman of noble birth or refined social status. Used in both historical and literary contexts, and sometimes to describe a woman who carries herself with elegance and grace.
A literary word for time, especially the swift passage of time. Most commonly encountered in the proverb 光陰矢の如し (time flies like an arrow).
A sharply angled slope or hillside. Used in contexts such as skiing, mountaineering, geography, and construction.
The medical procedure of removing surgical stitches or sutures after a wound has healed sufficiently. Also used as a suru verb.
A business or person that buys goods in bulk from manufacturers and sells them to retailers. An intermediary in the supply chain between producers and retail shops.
A country that does not take sides in a conflict or war, or one that has a long-standing policy of neutrality in international affairs. Switzerland is the most well-known example.
Taking multiple photographs in rapid succession by holding down the shutter button. A standard feature on digital cameras and smartphones used to capture fast-moving subjects.

glosses: collection point; collection site; gathering place
explanations: A designated location where things are gathered or collected, most commonly used for garbage and recycling collection points in residential areas.

The second-in-command within an organization or department. Ranks directly below the head (長) and acts as a substitute or assistant. Common in government agencies, corporations, and other organizations.

glosses: guide map; information map; directory map
explanations: A map displayed at a location to help visitors find their way around. Commonly found at stations, parks, shopping centers, tourist spots, and large buildings.
The form of a language as it is currently spoken and written, as opposed to classical or archaic forms. In Japanese studies, refers to modern Japanese as distinct from classical Japanese (古語).

glosses: within the frame; within the limits
within the frame; inside the box
within the limits; within the scope
explanations: Physically inside a border, box, or frame. Used for forms, goal areas in sports, and similar bounded areas.
Figuratively within established limits, such as a budget, quota, or set of rules.
The force of attraction or repulsion produced by magnets or magnetic fields. Also used figuratively to describe a powerful attraction.
The passing down of stories, knowledge, customs, or history by word of mouth rather than through written records. Also used as a suru verb meaning to hand down orally.

glosses: different theory; dissenting view; alternative interpretation
explanations: A theory or opinion that differs from the mainstream or commonly accepted view. Often used in academic, historical, and scholarly discussions.
An insect that is considered useful to humans, typically because it pollinates crops, eats pests, or produces useful substances like silk or honey. The opposite of 害虫 (harmful insect).
A wide field of view, most commonly used in photography and optics. Refers to lenses or camera settings that capture a broader scene than a standard lens.
The technique of photographing a subject from very close range, capturing fine details. Also used as a suru verb.
Not specifically identified or determined. Refers to people, things, or quantities that are not pinpointed or limited to particular individuals or items.
In optics, an image formed where light rays appear to diverge from but do not actually pass through. The image seen in a flat mirror is a virtual image.
A false or idealized image of a person or thing that does not reflect reality. Often used to describe a public persona or reputation that differs from who someone truly is.
A student who is currently enrolled at a school. Used to distinguish current students from graduates (卒業生) or prospective students.

glosses: to be combined; to interlock; to fit together
explanations: For multiple elements to come together and form a unified whole. The intransitive counterpart of 組み合わせる (to combine, to put together).

glosses: appealing to connoisseurs; appreciated by experts; for those in the know
explanations: Describes something that is appreciated or favored by professionals, experts, or connoisseurs rather than by the general public. Often implies subtle quality that requires expertise to appreciate.
The impulsive energy and lack of restraint characteristic of young people. Almost always appears in the fixed expression 若気の至り (a youthful indiscretion).
The overall power or strength of a nation, encompassing its economic, military, political, and cultural capabilities.
The highest rank in the Japanese and European systems of peerage. In the former Japanese peerage system (華族), 公爵 was the top of the five ranks. In European contexts, it corresponds to duke.
Relating to or conforming to principles of right and wrong conduct. Describes behavior, judgments, or standards that align with accepted moral principles.
One's first grandchild. A word that carries a strong emotional connotation of joy and celebration.

glosses: special report; breaking news; news flash
explanations: An urgent or special news bulletin that interrupts regular programming or stands out as particularly important. Also used for special promotional announcements, such as movie trailers.
Describing or explaining something in detail. Also used as a suru verb meaning to describe in detail or to elaborate.

glosses: sense of despair; feeling of hopelessness
explanations: The subjective feeling or emotional experience of despair. Adds the nuance of a felt sensation to the concept of despair (絶望), emphasizing the emotional weight.
A company other than one's own. Used in business contexts to refer to rival companies, partner companies, or simply any other company.
A matter of little importance or significance. A somewhat literary or formal word for something trivial.
Describes something that is of little importance or consequence. A somewhat formal word used to characterize matters, details, or issues as not worth serious attention.
The complete dying out or destruction of living things such as organisms, species, or cells. Also used figuratively for the disappearance of cultures, traditions, or ideas. Used as a suru verb.
The chemical element mercury (Hg), a silvery liquid metal. Historically used in thermometers, barometers, and various industrial applications. Now restricted due to toxicity.

glosses: to leave one's seat; to withdraw from a meeting
explanations: To get up and leave one's seat, especially in a formal setting such as a meeting, hearing, or classroom. Implies a deliberate departure, often before proceedings have ended.

glosses: to project; to cast; to reflect
explanations: To project an image, light, or shadow onto a surface such as a screen or wall.
To reflect or express inner feelings, thoughts, or circumstances in something external. Used figuratively for how personal experiences or emotions are expressed in art, behavior, or situations.

glosses: to borrow; to use on loan
explanations: To borrow something formally, especially objects, equipment, or facilities. More formal than 借りる and often used in written or official contexts. Also used for borrowing words or concepts from other languages or fields.

glosses: to lend; to loan; to provide on loan
explanations: To lend something formally, especially equipment, facilities, or funds. More formal than 貸す and commonly used in institutional, business, and legal contexts.
A well-known or famous person. Used broadly for anyone with public recognition, from entertainers and athletes to politicians and historical figures.

glosses: certain; no doubt; unmistakable; for sure
explanations: An expression used to assert certainty about something. Literally means 'there is no mistake.' Used to confirm facts or express strong conviction.
Small objects or accessories, especially fashion accessories like bags, scarves, and jewelry, or small household items and decorations.
A person of little importance or influence. Used disparagingly to describe someone who lacks ambition, presence, or capability.

glosses: spirit of adventure; adventurousness; sense of adventure
explanations: The desire or willingness to take on challenges, try new things, or explore the unknown. Often used positively to describe curiosity and boldness.

glosses: in other words; to put it another way
in other words; to put it another way; that is to say
explanations: A connective expression used to rephrase or clarify what was just said. Derived from the conditional form of 言い換える (to rephrase).

glosses: to rage; to wreak havoc; to be rampant
explanations: Used to describe the fierce, uncontrollable force of natural disasters, diseases, storms, or other destructive phenomena. Expresses the idea that something is causing widespread damage or disruption.

glosses: to disinfect; to sterilize; to sanitize
explanations: To kill or remove harmful bacteria, viruses, or other microorganisms from a surface, object, or wound using chemicals, heat, or other methods.

glosses: to cry out; to wail; to scream and cry
explanations: To cry loudly while screaming or shouting, expressing extreme grief, pain, or distress. A compound verb combining 泣く (to cry) and 叫ぶ (to shout).

glosses: to feel right; to click; to fit well
to feel right; to click; to fit well; to sit well
explanations: Describes the feeling when something fits perfectly, feels natural, or makes sense. Used for both physical fit (clothes, tools) and abstract fit (words, relationships, ideas).

glosses: locking up; securing doors and windows
explanations: The act of locking doors and closing windows to secure a building before leaving or going to bed. An important daily routine in Japanese life.
A short, memorable phrase used to promote an idea, campaign, or organization. Common in safety campaigns, school activities, advertising, and public awareness efforts in Japan.
A person who prefers to act alone rather than as part of a group. Can be used admiringly for someone independent and self-reliant, or descriptively for someone who avoids social groups.
The generation that follows the current one, or the next version or iteration of a technology, product, or system. Widely used as a modifier before nouns.
A colloquial, non-technical term for harmful microorganisms such as bacteria, viruses, and other pathogens. Used in everyday conversation, especially when talking about hygiene and illness.

A lottery or prize draw typically held at shopping streets, department stores, or festivals, where participants draw lots (often by pulling strings, spinning a wheel, or drawing a ball from a box) to win prizes.

glosses: riskiness; danger; degree of risk; potential hazard
explanations: The quality or degree of being dangerous or risky. Used to discuss the likelihood or potential for harm, often in discussions about safety, health, or decision-making.
The act or state of splitting into branches or divisions. Used literally for trees, roads, and rivers, and figuratively for organizations, topics, and processes that divide into sub-parts.
Having no restrictions, limits, or caps. Used for quantities, time, access, and rules. Common in business, technology, and everyday contexts.

glosses: on the surface; outwardly; ostensibly; superficially
explanations: Describes how something appears externally, with the implication that the reality underneath may be different. Used to contrast appearances with truth.
A device used for mathematical calculations. In modern everyday usage, typically refers to a handheld electronic calculator.
In academic and technical contexts, especially in computer science, 計算機 can refer to a computer. This usage is more common in formal or academic writing.
A pattern consisting of evenly spaced dots, typically of uniform size. The Japanese name literally means 'water droplet pattern,' evoking the image of round water drops.

glosses: to leave alone; to let be; to not disturb
explanations: To refrain from interfering with or disturbing someone or something. Often used when someone is upset, resting, or in a situation where intervention would be unwelcome.
A man who has legally adopted a child and become their father, or who raises a child in place of their biological father. A formal, legal term.
A woman who is one's spouse's older sister, or one's older stepsister through a parent's remarriage. A formal term used in legal and written contexts.

glosses: meritocracy; merit-based system; principle of rewarding ability
explanations: A system or philosophy that evaluates and rewards people based on their actual ability and performance rather than seniority, connections, or background.

glosses: point of compromise; middle ground; common ground
explanations: A point or solution where opposing parties can agree by each making concessions. Used in negotiations, discussions, and conflict resolution.
An airplane designed to carry passengers on commercial flights, as opposed to cargo planes or military aircraft.
The rhythmic beating of arteries as blood is pumped through them by the heart. Measured as beats per minute and used as a basic health indicator.

glosses: present stage; current phase; as things stand
present stage; current phase; as things stand now
explanations: The current point in time or in a process. Used to qualify statements as being true or applicable only at the present moment, implying that things may change.

glosses: drowsy driving; dozing at the wheel
drowsy driving; dozing at the wheel; falling asleep while driving
explanations: The dangerous act of falling asleep or nearly falling asleep while operating a vehicle. A major cause of traffic accidents.
Describes the person or thing one loves most. Often used for close family members or romantic partners, conveying deep emotional attachment.
The number of people involved in or assigned to something. Used in organizational and administrative contexts to refer to staffing levels or group sizes.
Not detailed or precise; giving only a general outline or approximation. Used for plans, estimates, descriptions, and explanations that omit fine details.
The act of translating from a foreign language into Japanese, or the resulting translated text.
A translation that prioritizes conveying the meaning and nuance of the original rather than following the exact wording. Contrasted with literal translation.

glosses: to join a club; to become a member of a club
explanations: To formally join a school club or extracurricular activity group. Primarily used in the context of Japanese schools, where club activities ({部活動|ぶかつどう}) are a central part of student life.

glosses: to be related; to be connected
to be related; to be connected; to be associated
explanations: To have a connection or relationship with something. Used to describe the link between topics, events, people, or concepts.

glosses: to maintain; to put in order; to develop
to maintain; to service; to overhaul
to put in order; to develop; to improve (infrastructure)
explanations: To inspect and repair machinery, vehicles, or equipment to keep them in good working condition.
To establish, organize, or improve systems, facilities, or environments so they function properly.

glosses: to explain; to give commentary; to provide analysis
explanations: To explain something in detail, often providing background information or expert analysis. Commonly used for media commentary, educational explanations, and expert analysis.

glosses: to prove; to verify; to certify
to prove; to demonstrate; to verify
explanations: To show that something is true or valid through evidence, logic, or documentation.
A person who supports a political figure, party, cause, or idea. Often used in political and social contexts.
The Christian cross or crucifix as a religious symbol. Also refers to the physical object.
Used figuratively to mean a heavy burden or responsibility that one must endure.

glosses: Buddhist sutra; Buddhist scripture; chanting of sutras
explanations: Sacred Buddhist texts that are chanted during religious ceremonies, funerals, and memorial services. The お prefix adds a respectful or familiar tone.
The regional dialect spoken in the Kansai area, including Osaka, Kyoto, and Kobe. One of the most widely recognized and influential dialects in Japan.

glosses: to replant; to transplant; to repot
explanations: To move a plant from one location or container to another. Common in gardening contexts.

glosses: to fish up; to hike up (prices)
to fish up; to reel in; to catch and pull up
to raise; to hike up (prices, wages)
explanations: To pull a fish out of the water. Can also refer to lifting something up with a hook or line.
To artificially or forcefully raise prices, wages, or other values, often with a negative connotation of manipulation.

glosses: to command; to lead; to unify
to command; to lead; to direct (a group)
explanations: To exercise leadership and bring a group together under unified direction. Used for military command, team leadership, and organizational management.
A series of events where each one causes or triggers the next. Used both in scientific contexts (nuclear/chemical chain reactions) and figuratively for cascading consequences.
The degree to which something responds to stimuli or signals. Used for technical equipment (cameras, sensors), personal awareness, and figurative sensitivity to trends or issues.
A person who cares for and manages animals at a zoo, aquarium, or similar facility. Responsible for feeding, health monitoring, and habitat maintenance.
Not yet completed. Used for works of art, literature, projects, or tasks that remain unfinished.

glosses: boaster; braggart; teller of tall tales
explanations: A person who habitually exaggerates or tells grand lies. The tone is often playful or critical rather than accusatory.

The basic infrastructure services essential for daily life, including water, electricity, gas, and telecommunications. In Japanese usage, this loanword specifically refers to these utility systems, especially in disaster contexts.

glosses: in small steps; bit by bit; tremblingly
in small steps; in small increments; bit by bit
explanations: Doing something in small, frequent amounts or movements rather than all at once.
Shaking or trembling with small, rapid movements, often from cold, fear, or nervousness.

glosses: blankly; absent-mindedly; with a vacant expression
explanations: Having a dazed or blank expression, typically because one is stunned, confused, or spacing out. Often describes someone staring with their mouth open.

glosses: rather than; or more precisely; more like
explanations: Used to correct or refine a previous statement, offering a more accurate or appropriate description. Indicates that the second description is closer to the truth than the first.
To a very small degree, almost imperceptibly. Describes something that is just barely detectable by the senses or barely present.

glosses: even at this late stage; belatedly
even at this late stage; belatedly; I know it's late but
explanations: Acknowledges that one is realizing, appreciating, or doing something later than expected. Often used when expressing a realization that should have come sooner.

glosses: to grow fond of; to become attached to
to grow fond of; to become attached to; to develop affection for
explanations: To gradually develop feelings of attachment or fondness toward something or someone through familiarity and use over time.

glosses: to be flexible; to be adaptable
to be flexible; to be adaptable; to be accommodating
explanations: To be able to adjust or adapt to changing circumstances. Describes a person, system, or approach that can handle things flexibly rather than rigidly.

glosses: to drain off moisture; to pat dry
to drain off moisture; to pat dry; to wring out water
explanations: To remove excess water or moisture from food, laundry, or other items. A common cooking and household term.
Moving, acting, or responding slowly. Often carries a slightly negative or impatient connotation, implying annoyance at the slowness.

glosses: defamation; libel; slander; damage to one's reputation
explanations: The act of harming someone's reputation through false statements, whether spoken or written. Also used as a legal term for defamation of character.

glosses: state of saturation; saturation point; being at capacity
explanations: A state where no more can be absorbed, added, or accommodated. Used both in scientific contexts (chemistry, physics) and figuratively for markets, schedules, and capacities that are at their limit.

glosses: traffic volume; amount of traffic; traffic flow
explanations: The quantity of vehicles or pedestrians passing through a given point or area. Used in transportation planning, road management, and everyday descriptions of how busy a road is.

glosses: end of a performance; curtain fall
explanations: The conclusion of a play, concert, or other live performance. Used in theater and event contexts to indicate when a show has finished.

glosses: living in luxury; indulgence; extravagant living
explanations: A lifestyle of excessive luxury and self-indulgence. Often carries a negative nuance suggesting wastefulness or lack of restraint.
A small, hard area of thickened skin on the foot, typically caused by friction or pressure. Named because its appearance resembles a fish's eye.

glosses: lead car; front car of a train
explanations: The first car at the front of a train. Often referenced in station announcements to help passengers find the correct boarding position.
The generation of electricity by burning fossil fuels such as coal, natural gas, or oil. A major source of electricity in Japan.

glosses: underground parking lot; underground parking garage
explanations: A parking facility located below ground level. Common in urban areas of Japan where surface space is limited.
The body or structural frame of an aircraft or spacecraft. Also used to refer to the aircraft itself as a unit.
A traditional Buddhist pagoda with five tiers, commonly found at temples throughout Japan. The five stories symbolize the five elements of Buddhist cosmology: earth, water, fire, wind, and sky.
Books or volumes in a series that have already been published, as opposed to forthcoming ones. Commonly used in bookstores and publisher listings for manga and light novel series.
A port where a ship stops during a voyage, either to take on supplies, let passengers disembark, or conduct trade.
The process of absorbing or soaking up water. Used for materials, products, and natural processes.

glosses: when one's stomach is empty; on an empty stomach
explanations: The time or state of having an empty stomach. Frequently used in medical and pharmaceutical instructions.
A tall, pointed tower on a building, especially a church or mosque. Also used for any tall, tapering architectural structure.
An educational system where students study primarily at home through mail, online resources, or periodic in-person sessions rather than attending school daily.
A postage stamp issued to mark a special event, anniversary, or notable person. Collected by philatelists and sometimes sold at a premium.
An astronomical event in which the Earth passes between the Sun and the Moon, completely blocking sunlight from reaching the Moon. The Moon often appears reddish during this phenomenon.

glosses: the Major Leagues; Major League Baseball
explanations: The top professional baseball league in the United States. Used in Japanese to refer to MLB, especially in the context of Japanese players competing there.
A dog that is kept inside the house rather than outdoors. In modern Japan, most pet dogs are kept indoors.
The surgeon who performs or leads a surgical operation. Distinguished from assistant surgeons or other members of the surgical team.
Thick mucus produced in the respiratory tract, especially when one has a cold, bronchitis, or other respiratory illness. Coughed up from the throat.
Material used in nuclear reactors to produce energy through nuclear fission. Typically uranium or plutonium.
The act of recording what is displayed on a computer or smartphone screen as a video. Used in tutorials, presentations, and sharing gameplay.
The region around a magnetic material or a moving electric charge within which the force of magnetism acts. A fundamental concept in physics.
Waves of electric and magnetic energy that travel through space. Includes visible light, radio waves, X-rays, microwaves, and more.

glosses: answer column; answer space; answer box
explanations: The designated space on a test, exam, or worksheet where students write their answers. A common term in Japanese education.
A ticket that guarantees a specific assigned seat, typically on a train such as the Shinkansen. Purchased in addition to or included with a basic fare ticket.

glosses: nuclear power generation; nuclear energy production
explanations: The generation of electricity using nuclear reactors. A major energy source in Japan, though controversial since the 2011 Fukushima disaster.
Concrete strengthened with steel bars or mesh embedded within it. The standard construction material for buildings and infrastructure in Japan.
The consumption of goods and resources on a large scale, characteristic of modern industrial societies. Often discussed critically in the context of environmental issues.

glosses: cancellation of a contract; breach of contract
cancellation of a contract; contract termination; breach of contract
explanations: The act of canceling, voiding, or breaking a contract. Can refer to either a lawful termination or an unlawful breach.
A substance that triggers an immune response in the body, causing the production of antibodies. Commonly encountered in the context of medical testing and vaccines.
Saving a file by replacing the existing version with the updated one. The standard "Save" command in most software applications, as opposed to "Save As."
Waste materials that contain or are contaminated by radioactive substances. Generated by nuclear power plants, medical facilities, and research institutions.
A metal or other durable plate attached to machinery, equipment, or buildings that displays identifying information such as the manufacturer, model number, serial number, or specifications.
Japan's primary law governing working conditions, established in 1947. It sets standards for working hours, wages, rest periods, holidays, and other labor-related matters.
A gymnastics apparatus consisting of a single bar supported by two posts, used for swinging and acrobatic exercises. Also refers to the horizontal bar commonly found in school playgrounds in Japan.
A bar or rod made of iron, used as a tool or weapon.
A tall wooden or concrete pole used to support overhead power lines and telephone cables. A common feature of Japanese streets and neighborhoods.
A large mass of ice that has broken off from a glacier and floats in the sea. Also used figuratively in the expression 'tip of the iceberg.'
In a brief and concise manner, without unnecessary detail. Used when asking someone to keep their explanation short, or when summarizing something quickly.
A spectacular or disastrous failure. Stronger than plain {失敗|しっぱい}, emphasizing the severity or embarrassment of the mistake.

glosses: ready asset; someone who can contribute immediately
ready asset; immediate asset; someone who can contribute right away
explanations: A person or resource that can be effective immediately without requiring additional training or preparation. Commonly used in hiring contexts and sports.
What is presented publicly or officially, as opposed to the real or hidden situation. Implies a gap between appearance and reality.
The act of traveling to a foreign country, especially crossing the sea. A formal term used in official and administrative contexts.
Relating to the very foundation or root of something. Describes changes, solutions, or problems that go to the core rather than addressing surface issues.
A light snack or treat eaten between meals, traditionally in the afternoon. Originally referred to eating at the eighth hour (yatsu) of the traditional Japanese clock, around 2-3 PM.
Describes relationships, situations, or resolutions that are smooth, without conflict or friction. Implies completeness and balance, from the kanji {円|えん} (round, complete).
Interpreting someone's words or intentions in a twisted or incorrect way, often to suit one's own purposes. Implies deliberate or biased distortion rather than innocent misunderstanding.
The geographical and political region spanning from Egypt and Turkey to Iran, including the Arabian Peninsula. Commonly used in news and international affairs.
The quality of being usable in many different situations or for many purposes. Commonly used when evaluating tools, skills, technology, or methods.
A gathering designed for people to socialize and deepen personal connections, typically held after a formal event such as a conference, seminar, or ceremony. Usually involves food and drinks.
Reading only selected parts of a text rather than the whole thing, picking out what seems interesting or relevant. Literally 'picking-up reading.'
A specific aspect in which two or more things differ. Commonly used in academic, business, and analytical contexts when comparing items systematically.
A minimum or maximum age requirement for participation, entry, purchase, or other activities. Common in contexts like alcohol purchase, movie ratings, job applications, and event entry.
The act of temporarily suspending or postponing something, typically a service, plan, or decision. Very commonly heard in train announcements when service is suspended.

glosses: to pester; to badger; to beg
to pester; to badger; to beg persistently
explanations: To repeatedly ask or beg someone for something in a persistent, often childish way. Typically describes children asking parents for things, but can also be used for adults.

glosses: talented; versatile; gifted in many areas
explanations: Having many talents or abilities across different fields. Describes someone who excels in multiple areas rather than just one.

glosses: intended for children; aimed at children; child-friendly
explanations: Describes products, content, events, or services that are designed or suitable for children. Uses the suffix {向|む}け meaning 'aimed at' or 'intended for.'

glosses: for beginners; beginner-friendly; aimed at beginners
explanations: Describes content, products, courses, or activities that are designed for people who are new to a subject or skill.

The Japanese number unit equal to one hundred million (10^8). Part of the Japanese numeral system where large numbers are grouped by ten-thousands: {万|まん} (10,000), {億|おく} (100,000,000), {兆|ちょう} (1,000,000,000,000).
The Japanese number unit equal to one trillion (10^12). The next step above {億|おく} in the Japanese numeral system. Commonly seen in national budgets and large-scale economic figures.

glosses: fan fiction; derivative work; fan-created content
explanations: Creative works made by fans based on existing stories, characters, or settings from manga, anime, games, and other media. A major part of Japanese doujin (self-published) culture.

The act of sweetly or cutely asking someone to buy or give you something. Often describes children asking parents, or can describe coy requests between adults. Has a softer, more endearing nuance than simply asking.

glosses: to cause trouble; to make waves; to stir things up
explanations: To disturb a peaceful situation by creating conflict or controversy. Literally 'to raise waves and wind.' Often used in the negative to advise against creating unnecessary conflict.

glosses: exchange program; student exchange; study abroad exchange
explanations: An educational program where students from one institution study at a partner institution abroad, typically with reciprocal arrangements between the two schools.
A chair with supports for the arms. A compound of {肘掛|ひじか}け (armrest) and {椅子|いす} (chair).

glosses: stinting; holding back; being stingy with
explanations: Reluctantly giving or using something, or withholding what one has. Can refer to being stingy with money, information, effort, or resources.
The practice of people helping each other. A formal term used for organized systems of mutual support, such as community aid groups, insurance cooperatives, and social welfare frameworks.
Facilities owned and operated by the government or local authorities for public use, such as libraries, community centers, parks, and public halls.

glosses: background knowledge; prior knowledge; preliminary knowledge
explanations: Knowledge that one has or needs before engaging with a particular topic, task, or situation. Often mentioned when discussing what is needed to understand something.
A moderate cooking temperature between low heat ({弱火|よわび}) and high heat ({強火|つよび}). One of the standard heat settings referred to in Japanese cooking instructions.

The act of adjusting or fine-tuning something to achieve the right level, amount, or condition. Used for physical settings like temperature or brightness, as well as abstract adjustments like scheduling.
The sandy or pebbly area along the edge of the sea. A slightly literary or poetic word for beach compared to the more common 海辺.
A covering worn over the face to hide one's identity. Used for masks worn by robbers, wrestlers, or in other contexts where concealment is the purpose.
Acting or appearing under a concealed identity. Used figuratively for anonymous or undercover activities.

glosses: pressing palms together (in prayer or greeting)
explanations: The act of placing both palms together in front of the chest or face, as in Buddhist prayer, expressing gratitude before a meal, or making a request. A deeply embedded cultural gesture in Japan.
The human faculty of logical thinking and rational judgment, as opposed to emotion or instinct. Often used in contexts where someone maintains or loses their composure.
Freedom from guilt or wrongdoing, especially in legal or accusatory contexts. Used when someone is cleared of suspicion or asserts they have done nothing wrong.
Moral cleanliness and integrity of character. Describes a person who is honest and free from corruption.

glosses: cherry blossom viewing; flower viewing party
explanations: The traditional Japanese custom of enjoying the beauty of cherry blossoms in spring, typically involving a picnic or party under the trees. The お prefix adds politeness.
The country where one was born or to which one has a strong national or cultural attachment. Carries an emotional or sentimental nuance compared to more neutral alternatives.

glosses: long-cherished wish; heart's desire; long-held dream
explanations: A wish or goal that someone has held for a long time. Used when that wish is finally fulfilled or when describing something someone has always wanted.
Overwhelming, destructive power, especially of natural disasters, epidemics, or other forces beyond human control. Almost always used with を振るう (to rage, to wreak havoc).

glosses: to guess; to conjecture; to surmise
to guess; to conjecture; to surmise; to infer
explanations: To form an opinion or conclusion based on incomplete evidence or reasoning. More formal and analytical than simply guessing.

glosses: to concede; to make a concession; to compromise
explanations: To yield or give ground on a point during a negotiation, argument, or discussion. Implies voluntarily stepping back from one's position to reach an agreement.

glosses: work history; employment record; career history
explanations: A record of one's past jobs and positions. Commonly used in the context of resumes and job applications.

glosses: the next day; the following day
explanations: The day after a referenced event or point in time. A formal or written alternative to the more conversational 次の日.
A priest in the Roman Catholic or Eastern Orthodox Church. Used as both a general term and a form of address (like 'Father' in English).
A person who accompanies one through life, typically a spouse or romantic partner. A somewhat formal or literary word that carries warmth and implies a deep, lasting bond.

glosses: to be utterly exhausted; to be completely worn out
explanations: To be exhausted to the absolute limit, both physically and mentally. The 果てる suffix intensifies 疲れる to mean total, complete exhaustion.

A medical or psychological condition in which a person cannot stop using a substance or engaging in a behavior despite harmful consequences. Used for both substance addictions and behavioral addictions.

glosses: refutation; winning an argument; demolishing someone's argument
explanations: Defeating an opponent's argument through logic and reasoning. In modern internet culture, often used more casually to mean proving someone wrong or shutting them down in a debate.

glosses: rubber boots; rain boots; Wellington boots
explanations: Waterproof boots, typically made of rubber, worn in rainy weather, when working in muddy or wet conditions, or for outdoor activities. Also refers to tall boots in general.
The act of breaking someone's trust or going against a promise, alliance, or loyalty. The noun form of the verb 裏切る.
A small, precise adjustment to improve something that is already mostly correct. Used for both physical settings and abstract processes like plans or strategies.
The sacred text of Christianity, comprising the Old and New Testaments. In Japanese, this word specifically refers to the Christian Bible.
The repeated alternation between being lit and unlit. Used for lights, signals, indicators, and displays that turn on and off in succession.
A feeling of uncertainty or distrust, particularly about someone's motives, honesty, or the truth of a situation. More formal and weighty than ordinary doubt.
Looking at something or someone fixedly and intently without looking away. A formal, literary word for an intense, sustained gaze.

glosses: public eye; notice of others; other people's attention
explanations: The gaze or attention of other people around you. Used when someone is conscious of being watched or judged by others.

glosses: to be conscious of; to be aware of
to be self-conscious about; to be attracted to
explanations: To deliberately pay attention to or be mindful of something. Used when someone becomes aware of or focuses on something they might otherwise overlook.
To become nervously aware of someone, typically due to romantic interest. Used when someone starts feeling awkward or attracted to another person.

glosses: right in half; in two equal pieces
right in half; in two equal pieces; clean in two
explanations: Split or divided into exactly two equal parts. Used literally for physical objects being cut or broken, and figuratively for opinions or groups being evenly divided.
The inner strength or determination to endure difficulties, resist temptation, or push through challenges. Refers to psychological resilience rather than physical power.
The document or ticket that allows a passenger to board an airplane. Issued at check-in or generated digitally.
Information that one has heard from others rather than witnessed firsthand. Often used in formal or legal contexts to distinguish direct knowledge from reported information.
An object that someone has found lying on the ground or left behind. Used for items found by chance.
Something unexpectedly good that one comes across by luck. Used figuratively for bargains, surprisingly talented people, or fortunate discoveries.

glosses: secret talk; private consultation; confidential discussion
explanations: A conversation held in secret, away from others who are not supposed to hear. Often implies that the content is sensitive, strategic, or potentially suspicious.

glosses: to improve; to make progress; to get better at
explanations: To become more skilled or proficient at something through practice or experience. Used for skills, abilities, and performance.

glosses: leaving an institution; discharge; departure from a facility
explanations: The act of leaving or being discharged from an institution such as a care facility, detention center, or research institute. The opposite of 入所.
A reservation or booking made ahead of general availability, typically offered to members, fans, or priority customers before tickets or products go on sale to the public.
A dietary approach that limits the intake of sugars and carbohydrates. Widely popular in Japan as a weight-loss and health management method.

glosses: new business venture; new enterprise; new project
explanations: A newly launched business, project, or line of work within an existing company or as a startup. Common in corporate and business contexts.
The systematic management of cleanliness and sanitary conditions, especially in food service, healthcare, and workplace settings.
The highest speed that a vehicle, object, or system can reach. Used in traffic regulations, vehicle specifications, and physics.
Development carried out jointly by two or more parties, such as companies, countries, or research institutions. Common in business, technology, and international relations.
Clothing designed for adult women. Commonly seen as a department or floor label in department stores and shopping malls.
A person who creates and arranges dance movements for performances. Used in theater, film, music videos, and traditional Japanese performing arts.

glosses: nepotism; favoritism toward one's own people
nepotism; favoritism toward family or close associates
explanations: The tendency to give unfair preferential treatment to one's own family members, relatives, or inner circle. Generally carries a negative connotation.
Refers to people, matters, or activities outside one's own company or organization. The opposite of 社内.

glosses: mental concentration; focusing one's mind; composing oneself
explanations: The act of focusing all mental energy on a single point, clearing distractions. Used in martial arts, sports, meditation, and before important tasks.
Supernatural powers or practices involving spells and incantations. Also used for stage magic and illusions, though 手品 is more common for that meaning.
A glass-fronted cabinet or case used to display merchandise, food items, or collectibles. Common in bakeries, jewelry stores, museums, and retail shops.

glosses: display shelf; display rack; exhibition shelf
explanations: A shelf or rack used to display merchandise in stores, museums, or exhibitions. Unlike a showcase, it is typically open without glass enclosure.
An organ or group of cells in the body that produces and secretes substances such as hormones, sweat, or saliva. Used in medical and biological contexts.
An intersection where one road ends by meeting another at a right angle, forming a T shape. Named after the kanji 丁, which resembles the letter T.
Literature from the modern era, generally referring to works from the post-World War II period onward in Japanese literary studies. The exact time boundary varies by context.

glosses: psychological description; portrayal of inner thoughts
psychological description; portrayal of inner thoughts and feelings
explanations: The depiction of a character's mental state, emotions, and inner world in literature, film, or other creative works. A key element of literary analysis.

glosses: deep psychology; subconscious mind; underlying psychology
explanations: The hidden or unconscious aspects of a person's psychology that influence behavior and emotions without their awareness. Used in psychology, everyday conversation, and media.

A defensive player in baseball who is not the pitcher or catcher. Refers collectively to the seven position players in the field: first baseman, second baseman, shortstop, third baseman, left fielder, center fielder, and right fielder.

glosses: commemorative ceremony; memorial ceremony; anniversary event
explanations: A formal ceremony held to mark an anniversary, milestone, or significant event. Common for school anniversaries, company milestones, and national commemorations.
A tool used to remove corks from wine bottles. The ～抜き pattern (remover/opener) is productive in Japanese.

glosses: nape hairline; hair at the back of the neck
explanations: The hairline at the back of the neck, or the hair growing in that area. Important in hairstyling and traditionally considered an attractive feature in Japanese aesthetics.

glosses: character formation; personality development; character building
explanations: The process of developing one's character and personality, especially during childhood and adolescence. A common topic in education and psychology.
A small, narrow vase designed to hold a single flower or a small branch. A traditional element of Japanese interior decoration, reflecting the aesthetic of appreciating beauty in simplicity.

glosses: you (very formal, used in written correspondence)
explanations: A highly formal second-person pronoun used primarily in business letters, official documents, and formal written communication. Traditionally used to address men of equal or lower status, but in modern usage the gender restriction has loosened.

glosses: pre-order bonus; reservation perk; booking privilege
explanations: A special bonus item or benefit given to customers who reserve or pre-order a product. Common in the gaming, entertainment, and retail industries.
A vessel or appliance used to boil water. Can refer to a stovetop kettle, an electric kettle, or a hot water heater.
The main perpetrator of a crime who planned or led the criminal act. Distinguished from accomplices and accessories.
Soldiers who fight on horseback, or a military unit composed of such soldiers. Historically important in warfare, now largely ceremonial or used in historical and fantasy contexts.
The movement of troops toward a destination or enemy position. Also used figuratively for determined forward progress.

glosses: returning home for the Obon festival; going back to one's hometown during Obon
explanations: The custom of returning to one's hometown during the Obon period (mid-August) to visit family and honor ancestors. One of the peak travel periods in Japan alongside New Year and Golden Week.
The construction or building of a castle or fortress. A key concept in Japanese history, particularly during the Sengoku (Warring States) period.

glosses: narrow escape from death; surviving against all odds
explanations: An idiom meaning to barely survive a life-threatening situation. Literally "one life out of nine deaths," expressing that the chance of survival was only one in ten.
Singing casually with the mouth closed or half-open, typically while doing something else. Implies a relaxed, happy mood.
Sitting or lying in a sunny spot to enjoy the warmth. A leisurely, relaxed activity rather than intentional tanning.
