A personality trait of being reluctant to step forward or assert oneself. Describes someone who holds back in social situations.
The middle of the day when the sun is at its highest. Often emphasizes the brightness or openness of daytime, especially when contrasted with something unexpected happening.
A strong prohibition, often seen on signs and in rules. Stronger than 禁止, conveying zero tolerance.
A man who behaves with courtesy, dignity, and good manners. Also used more broadly to refer to men in formal or polite contexts.

glosses: lady; gentlewoman; woman of refined character
explanations: A woman of good breeding and graceful manners. Used in formal or literary contexts to describe an elegant, well-mannered woman.

glosses: trump card; ace up one's sleeve
trump card; ace up one's sleeve; decisive measure
explanations: The strongest card in a card game that can beat other cards.
A secret weapon, final resource, or decisive advantage held in reserve. The figurative usage is much more common than the literal card game meaning.
A large-scale orchestral composition, typically in multiple movements. The formal Japanese term for a symphonic work.
A public performance of music, typically classical or traditional. The standard formal term for a concert in Japanese.
Confessing one's sins or wrongdoings and expressing remorse. Used in both religious contexts (Buddhist and Christian) and everyday situations where someone admits fault.
The look and feel of a material or surface — how something feels to the touch or appears in terms of material quality. Commonly used in fashion, design, and product descriptions.
Payment that has not yet been made, especially one that is due. Used for bills, wages, taxes, and other financial obligations.

glosses: setting a question; posing a problem
setting a question; posing a problem; giving a quiz
explanations: The act of creating and presenting questions or problems, especially in exams, quizzes, or competitions.

glosses: difficult problem; tough question; hard challenge
explanations: A problem or question that is very hard to solve or answer. Used for academic questions, puzzles, and also figuratively for real-world challenges.

glosses: giving in; losing patience; being worn down by persistence
explanations: Yielding because the other party's persistence outlasts your resistance. Losing not on merit but because you run out of stamina or patience to keep refusing.

glosses: secret informing; tip-off; informing on someone
explanations: Secretly reporting someone's wrongdoing to the authorities or to someone in power. Carries a negative connotation of betrayal or disloyalty.
Stealing someone else's creative work (writing, music, art) and presenting it as one's own. A serious accusation in both academic and professional contexts.

glosses: Go; the board game of Go
explanations: A strategic board game played with black and white stones on a 19×19 grid, where players compete to control territory. One of the oldest and most respected board games in East Asia.
Visually striking and beautiful in a lively, colorful way. Describes things that are eye-catching and full of vitality, whether physical appearance, atmosphere, or lifestyle.

glosses: to sympathize; to feel sorry for; to empathize
explanations: To share in another person's suffering or misfortune; to feel pity or compassion for someone.

glosses: youthful; looking young; full of youthful energy
explanations: Appearing or feeling young, especially for one's age. A compliment suggesting vitality, freshness, and energy.
Of the highest moral, intellectual, or spiritual value. Describes ideals, purposes, or experiences that inspire awe and reverence.

glosses: attracting customers; drawing a crowd; customer acquisition
explanations: The act of drawing people to a business, event, or venue. A key concept in marketing and business management.

glosses: exchange of gifts; gift-giving; presenting and receiving gifts
explanations: The formal practice of giving and receiving gifts, especially as part of social customs and seasonal traditions.
Describes something that is morally or spiritually impure and offensive. Stronger than simply 'dirty' — implies deep revulsion and contamination.
A black carbon material made by burning wood in a low-oxygen environment. Used for fuel, art, water purification, and deodorizing.
Letters, packages, and other items sent through the postal system. The standard term for physical mail.

glosses: once only; one-off; just one time
once only; just one time; one-off
explanations: Something that happens only once and will not be repeated. Emphasizes the singularity and finality of the occurrence.

glosses: ready consent; willing agreement; cheerful acceptance
explanations: Agreeing to something willingly and without hesitation. Implies that the person is pleased to accept rather than merely tolerating the request.
Writing done quickly and carelessly, resulting in messy, hard-to-read text. The image is of striking the paper rather than carefully forming characters.
Help or assistance offered to someone in trouble or distress. Often used figuratively to describe timely aid that saves a dire situation.
The state of ideas, feelings, or information flowing smoothly between people. Emphasizes the successful exchange and mutual comprehension rather than the act of speaking itself.

glosses: leading; prominent; one of the best
leading; prominent; one of the best; top-ranking
explanations: Among the very best in a group or field. The image is of counting the top items on one's fingers — so few that they can be counted on one hand.
The literal act of counting by folding fingers, often while eagerly anticipating something.
Of superior quality or craftsmanship. Used to describe products, services, and materials that meet a high standard.

glosses: to pour into; to invest heavily in
to pour into, to fill by pouring
to invest, to devote, to channel into
explanations: To pour a liquid into a container or space.
To put a large amount of money, time, effort, or emotion into something. Implies concentrated, intensive investment.

A container, space, or system that has reached its maximum capacity and cannot hold any more. Used both literally for physical containers and figuratively for schedules, facilities, and similar things.

glosses: this much, to this extent, to this degree
explanations: Indicates a degree or extent that is being pointed to or emphasized. Often used with surprise, admiration, or emphasis to highlight that something is remarkable in its degree.

glosses: to be interrupted, to break off, to pause
explanations: Something continuous (conversation, signal, flow of people, etc.) stops temporarily or permanently. An intransitive verb describing the state of being cut off or disrupted.

An advance notification given privately before an official announcement is made. Most commonly refers to personnel transfer notices in Japanese companies, where employees are told of upcoming transfers or promotions before the formal announcement.

glosses: rehabilitation, turning over a new leaf
rehabilitation, reform, turning over a new leaf
explanations: Returning to a normal, productive life after criminal behavior, addiction, or other serious problems. Often used in legal and social welfare contexts.

glosses: to be soothed, to feel at ease, to soften
to be soothed, to feel at ease, to be calmed
explanations: To become relaxed and feel a warm, gentle sense of comfort. Often describes the feeling when seeing something cute, heartwarming, or peaceful.
An atmosphere or mood becoming gentler, less tense, or more relaxed.

glosses: to value, to prize, to revere
to value, to prize, to hold in high regard
explanations: To consider something important and treat it with respect. Used for abstract values, principles, and things worthy of respect.

glosses: to close up, to be in bud, to narrow
to close up, to be in bud
to narrow, to purse, to pucker
explanations: For flowers or petals to be closed or not yet open. The opposite of blooming.
For something to become smaller or narrower, like pursing the lips or an opening becoming smaller.

glosses: to harm, to impair, to damage
to fail to do, to miss doing (as a verb suffix)
explanations: To cause damage or deterioration to something valuable — health, reputation, trust, beauty, etc. Often used for abstract damage rather than physical destruction.
When attached to the stem of another verb (V-stem + {損|そこ}なう), it means failing to do the action or doing it incorrectly.

glosses: to catch one's eye, to stand out
to catch one's eye, to stand out, to be noticeable
explanations: Something draws attention, either because it is prominent or because it keeps happening. Can be positive (something eye-catching) or negative (something annoyingly conspicuous).

glosses: to worry about, to be concerned about
to worry about, to be concerned about, to care about
explanations: To keep something on one's mind out of concern or care. Implies ongoing mental attention to someone or something, often with a caring or worried nuance.

glosses: going into service (of a ship or aircraft)
going into service, entering service on a route
explanations: A ship, aircraft, or other transport beginning regular service on a route. Also used for the launch of a new route or service.

glosses: ability to respond, adaptability, coping ability
explanations: The capacity to handle situations, respond to changes, or deal with problems effectively. Commonly used in business and personal development contexts.

glosses: suffrage, right to participate in government
suffrage, political rights, right to participate in government
explanations: The right of citizens to participate in political processes, including the right to vote and the right to run for office.
A counter used to count large animals such as cattle, horses, elephants, whales, and other sizable creatures. Generally used for animals larger than a person's arms can hold.
A formal counter used to count fish, shrimp, and similar aquatic creatures. More formal and technical than {匹|ひき}, commonly used in fisheries, markets, and news reporting.
A small establishment serving tea, coffee, and light refreshments. In modern usage, often refers to a traditional-style coffee shop (kissaten type) rather than a chain café.

glosses: to suffer, to sustain, to incur
explanations: To receive or sustain damage, loss, harm, or other negative consequences. A formal word typically used in written or official contexts.

glosses: to make stand out, to highlight, to accentuate
explanations: To cause something to become more prominent, noticeable, or distinctive. The causative form of {際立|きわだ}つ (to stand out).

glosses: third (in a series), C (in a grading system)
explanations: The third of the ten Heavenly Stems (天干), used as an ordinal marker meaning 'third' in traditional ranking systems. Equivalent to 'C' in Western A/B/C grading. Part of the sequence 甲 (A) → 乙 (B) → 丙 (C).
A table or desk surface used for dining, working, or playing games. Often appears in compound words. Also used as a counter for tables at mahjong or similar games.

glosses: issuance, issuing (of passports, visas, certificates, etc.)
explanations: The official issuing of documents by a government or authorized body. Used specifically for formal documents like passports, visas, and certificates.
The process of mixing or blending different substances together. A technical term used in chemistry, pharmacy, cooking, and manufacturing.
Regaining weight after a diet ends. This is the most common meaning in everyday Japanese. The word implies that restricting intake led to a bounce-back effect.
In basketball and other sports, catching the ball after a missed shot bounces off the backboard or rim.

glosses: good or bad luck, fortune and misfortune
explanations: The concept of whether something will turn out well or poorly. Often used in the context of divination, fortune-telling, and traditional customs.
An establishment licensed for hair cutting, shaving, and grooming services. In Japan, legally distinct from a beauty salon (美容室), as barbershops are licensed for shaving with razors.
Devices and equipment that operate using electronic circuits. A general term covering computers, smartphones, tablets, and similar devices.

glosses: hardship of making a living, financial difficulty in daily life
explanations: The suffering and difficulty that comes from not having enough money or resources to live comfortably. Often used in news and social discussions about poverty.

glosses: returning double the amount, repaying twofold
explanations: Giving back twice what was received, whether in gifts, money, or figuratively in revenge. In gift-giving culture, returning a gift worth double the original. Also used for retaliating doubly.
Something hidden or latent becoming visible, obvious, or real. The opposite of 潜在 (latent, potential).
A chemical substance added to food, wood, or other materials to prevent decay, rot, or spoilage.
Neither acidic nor alkaline; having no electrical charge. Used in scientific contexts for pH balance or electrical neutrality.
Neither distinctly masculine nor feminine. Used in grammar for neuter gender, and in modern usage for androgynous or gender-neutral qualities.
A military branch or soldier specialized in operating large-caliber weapons such as cannons and howitzers. Can refer to either the branch of the military or an individual soldier.
Substances that are not derived from living organisms and generally do not contain carbon-hydrogen bonds. Includes minerals, metals, water, and salts. The opposite of organic matter (有機物).

glosses: I am deeply sorry (very formal apology)
I am deeply sorry; I sincerely apologize
explanations: A very formal and polite way to apologize. More formal than 申し訳ありません, which is itself more formal than すみません. Used in business settings, customer service, and when speaking to superiors.

glosses: excuse me; pardon me (when entering, leaving, or interrupting)
explanations: A very formal version of 失礼します, used when entering or leaving a room, passing in front of someone, or excusing oneself. Common in business settings and when addressing superiors.

glosses: vicious cycle; negative spiral; chain of negative events
explanations: A situation where one bad outcome leads to another, creating an ongoing cycle of negative consequences. Used in discussions of social problems, economics, and personal struggles.

glosses: reduced working hours; shortened work schedule
explanations: A work arrangement where an employee works fewer hours than the standard full-time schedule. Common for parents of young children, employees returning from leave, or as part of work-life balance policies.
The part of the mind that influences thoughts and behavior without conscious awareness. Used in psychology, self-help, and everyday conversation about hidden motivations or feelings.

A building occupied by various unrelated businesses such as bars, restaurants, offices, and clinics, typically found in entertainment and commercial districts. Often older buildings with narrow stairways and multiple small tenants on different floors.
Items that have been formally decided in a meeting or discussion. A standard business term used in minutes, agendas, and organizational communication.

glosses: to rack one's brains; to think hard
to rack one's brains; to think hard; to squeeze out every idea
explanations: To exert maximum mental effort to come up with a solution or idea. The image is of wringing out wisdom like wringing out a cloth. Used when a difficult problem requires creative thinking.
The official, gender-neutral term for airline cabin crew in Japanese. Replaced the older terms スチュワーデス (stewardess) and スチュワード (steward).

glosses: on-board sales; trolley service on trains
explanations: The service of selling food, drinks, and souvenirs from a cart pushed through the aisles of trains, especially Shinkansen and limited express trains. This service has been declining in Japan due to changing passenger habits.
Government or central bank actions to control the money supply and interest rates. In Japan, this is primarily carried out by the Bank of Japan (日本銀行). A key term in economic news.
Playing a supporting role in a film, play, or other performance. Most commonly seen in the context of awards and film credits.
The practice of managing and investing financial assets such as savings, stocks, and bonds to grow wealth. A common topic in Japanese personal finance and business contexts.

The international humanitarian organization, or its national branches. In Japan, the Japanese Red Cross Society (日本赤十字社) is a major organization involved in disaster relief, blood donation services, and hospital management.
Having the ability to speak persuasively and fluently. Can carry a slightly negative nuance of being overly smooth or glib, depending on context.
Containing foreign substances or elements that compromise purity. Used for physical substances like water or metals.
Having hidden, selfish, or morally questionable motives. Often used to describe relationships or intentions that are not sincere.

glosses: to peel; to remove the skin, rind, or bark
explanations: To remove the outer layer of fruits, vegetables, or other items. A basic cooking and everyday expression.

glosses: careful selection; hand-picking; selecting the best
explanations: The act of carefully choosing only the best items from a larger group. Often used in product descriptions and book titles to emphasize quality curation.

glosses: handouts; distributed materials; printed materials for distribution
explanations: Documents, flyers, or other materials that are given out at meetings, classes, events, or other gatherings.
Transportation systems available to the general public, including trains, buses, subways, and ferries. Japan is renowned for its extensive and reliable public transportation network.
The formal Japanese name for the United Nations, the international organization founded in 1945. In everyday use, the abbreviation 国連 (こくれん) is far more common.

glosses: the reason is; because; that is because
explanations: A conjunction used to introduce an explanation or reason for something previously stated. Often followed by からだ or ためだ at the end of the explanatory sentence. Less formal than なぜなら.

glosses: winning someone over by crying; tearful persuasion
winning someone over by crying; tearful persuasion; using tears to get one's way
explanations: A persuasion tactic where someone cries or makes an emotional plea to get what they want. Often implies manipulation or insincerity.

A literary or formal way to say 'many' or 'numerous,' emphasizing a large but unspecified number of things. Conveys a sense of weight and significance, often used when looking back on experiences or challenges.

glosses: to gather around the dining table
to gather around the dining table; to sit together for a meal
explanations: To come together as a family or group to share a meal. Emphasizes the warmth of communal dining and togetherness, rather than just the act of eating.

glosses: masculine; manly; having qualities associated with men
explanations: Describes qualities, appearance, or characteristics traditionally associated with masculinity, such as strength, boldness, or a strong physique.

An abbreviation of 国連安全保障理事会. The principal organ of the United Nations responsible for international peace and security. Consists of five permanent members with veto power and ten rotating non-permanent members.

glosses: biased view; seeing through rose-colored glasses
biased view; partial perspective; seeing favorably due to personal attachment
explanations: Looking at something or someone in an overly favorable way because of personal fondness, loyalty, or connection. Acknowledges that one's judgment may not be objective.

glosses: to focus; to narrow down the focus
to focus; to narrow down the focus; to zero in on
explanations: To concentrate attention or discussion on a specific point or topic, narrowing from a broader scope. Used in discussions, research, investigations, and presentations.

A weather front where a mass of cold air advances and pushes under warmer air. Often brings sudden drops in temperature, strong winds, and heavy but short-lived rain. A standard meteorological term frequently heard in Japanese weather forecasts.

glosses: crude drug; herbal medicine ingredient; natural medicinal material
explanations: Natural substances — typically plants, but also minerals and animal products — used as ingredients in traditional medicine, especially in kampo (漢方). These are the raw or minimally processed materials from which medicines are prepared.
A plant that contains substances harmful or fatal to humans or animals if ingested or touched. Japan has several well-known poisonous plants including トリカブト (monkshood) and ドクゼリ (water hemlock).

glosses: prohibition; ban; interdict; decree forbidding something
explanations: An official order or law prohibiting something. Can refer to both historical edicts and modern regulations. More formal and authoritative than simply 禁止.
A competitive swimming event where swimmers may use any stroke, though the front crawl is universally used due to its speed. Races are held at distances of 50m, 100m, 200m, 400m, 800m, and 1500m.

glosses: developing new business; new market development
developing new business; new market development; finding new customers
explanations: The activity of finding and developing new customers, markets, or business opportunities. A key concept in sales and business strategy.
Refers to Chinese-style cooking as served in Japan. In Japanese usage, 中華料理 typically refers to higher-end, more authentic Chinese restaurant food, while 中華 alone is used more casually.

glosses: cleaning by wiping; wiping down surfaces
explanations: The act of cleaning floors, tables, or other surfaces by wiping them with a cloth, usually a damp one. A traditional Japanese cleaning method, especially for wooden floors.

The tendency to believe that others are out to get you or that you are being unfairly targeted. Can refer to the clinical condition or be used colloquially to describe someone who reads hostility into neutral situations.

glosses: singing ability; vocal ability; singing skill
explanations: The overall ability to sing well, encompassing pitch accuracy, vocal range, tone quality, and expressiveness. Often used when evaluating or praising singers.

glosses: for overseas; intended for foreign markets
for overseas; intended for foreign markets; export-oriented
explanations: Describes products, services, or content designed or adapted for markets outside Japan. The suffix ～向け indicates the intended target or audience.

glosses: to be moved to tears; to feel tears welling up
explanations: Literally 'the inner corners of one's eyes become hot.' Describes the physical sensation of being on the verge of tears due to being deeply moved, touched, or emotionally stirred. More restrained than actually crying.

glosses: to stand alongside; to rival; to be on par with
to walk side by side; to stand alongside
to rival; to be on par with; to equal
explanations: Literally, to line up one's shoulders with someone — to walk or stand next to each other.
Figuratively, to be at the same level as someone in skill, status, or achievement. Often used to describe reaching the level of a superior competitor.

glosses: to broaden one's horizons; to widen one's perspective
explanations: To expand one's outlook or way of thinking by gaining new experiences, knowledge, or perspectives. Commonly used in educational and personal growth contexts.
Transportation services available to the general public, such as trains, buses, and subways. Often used in the longer form 公共交通機関.
An animal that primarily eats meat. Used in biology and everyday conversation about animals. Contrasts with 草食動物 (herbivore) and 雑食動物 (omnivore).
Describes something designed or suitable for many different purposes. Commonly used to describe rooms, facilities, and equipment.

glosses: literary work; copyrighted work; creative work
explanations: A work that is the product of creative expression and is protected by copyright law. Includes books, music, art, software, and other original creations.

glosses: proceeding simultaneously; running in parallel; concurrent progress
explanations: Multiple tasks, events, or processes advancing at the same time. Used in work, project management, and everyday situations involving multitasking.

glosses: meeting at the venue; assembling on-site
meeting at the venue; assembling on-site; gathering at the destination
explanations: An arrangement where participants travel independently and meet directly at the destination rather than gathering at a departure point first. Common for group outings, field trips, and events.

glosses: bonesetting clinic; osteopathic clinic; chiropractic-style clinic
explanations: A clinic run by a licensed judo therapist (柔道整復師) that treats bone fractures, dislocations, sprains, and muscle injuries through manual therapy. Very common in Japan and covered by health insurance for certain treatments.

glosses: standing room; standing section; standing-room-only area
explanations: A section in a theater, concert venue, or stadium where audience members stand rather than sit. Often the cheapest ticket option.

glosses: one's go-to song; signature song; favorite song to sing
explanations: A song that a person always sings, especially at karaoke. Can also refer to a professional singer's signature number.
A flat kitchen utensil used for flipping and turning food while cooking, such as pancakes, eggs, or fish. The name literally means 'fry-flipper.'
Eating utensils such as knives, forks, and spoons. A loanword from English 'cutlery,' commonly used in homeware shops and restaurants in Japan.

glosses: kitchenware; kitchen supplies; kitchen utensils and goods
explanations: A general term for items used in the kitchen, including cooking utensils, pots, pans, cutting boards, and other kitchen tools and supplies.
A disruption to train timetables causing delays or cancellations. ダイヤ is short for ダイヤグラム (diagram), referring to the graphical train schedule used in railway operations.

glosses: sense of belonging; group identity; feeling of attachment to a group
explanations: The psychological feeling of belonging to and identifying with a particular group, organization, or community. Important in Japanese social and workplace culture.
Describes a person or behavior focused primarily on one's own interests, needs, or perspective without regard for others.

glosses: altruistic; selfless; concerned with the welfare of others
explanations: Describes actions or attitudes motivated by concern for others rather than self-interest. Originally from Buddhist terminology where 利他 means benefiting others.

glosses: business trip allowance; travel per diem
business trip allowance; travel per diem; travel stipend
explanations: A monetary allowance paid to employees to cover expenses incurred during business trips, such as meals and incidental costs.

glosses: omission (in a document); failure to include
omission; failure to include in a document; something left out of a written record
explanations: An item or piece of information that should have been written down or recorded but was accidentally left out. Commonly used in business and administrative contexts.

glosses: waiting on tables; serving food and drinks
explanations: The act of serving food and drinks to guests or customers.
A person who serves food and drinks, especially in a formal or traditional setting.
Vegetables grown primarily for their edible leaves, such as spinach, lettuce, cabbage, and komatsuna. A common category in grocery shopping and cooking.

glosses: traditional New Year games; New Year's pastimes
explanations: Traditional games played during the Japanese New Year holiday period. These include activities like kite flying, spinning tops, playing karuta, and battledore and shuttlecock.

glosses: battledore; wooden paddle used for hanetsuki
explanations: A wooden paddle used in the traditional New Year game hanetsuki (similar to badminton without a net). Also refers to elaborately decorated paddles sold as good-luck ornaments.

glosses: cutting-edge technology; state-of-the-art technology; advanced technology
explanations: The most advanced and newest technology available. Commonly used in discussions about innovation, research, and industry.

glosses: king of beasts; king of the jungle
explanations: An epithet for the lion, referring to its status as the most powerful and majestic of all animals. Also used figuratively to describe someone who dominates their field.
Large waves on the ocean, especially those caused by wind. A formal or technical term commonly used in weather reports and maritime contexts.

glosses: probability; likelihood; chance of something occurring
explanations: The degree to which something is likely to happen. A formal and somewhat literary term used in academic, legal, and philosophical contexts. In everyday speech, 可能性 is more commonly used.

glosses: sensual; sensuous; voluptuous; appealing to the senses
explanations: Describes something that strongly appeals to the physical senses, especially in a way that is pleasurable or seductive. Often used to describe art, music, fragrance, or physical beauty.
A child enrolled in a kindergarten or nursery school. Used in both casual and official contexts to refer to young children in pre-elementary education.
A large, expensive, and impressive private residence. Emphasizes grandeur and luxury rather than mere size.
The sum total calculated over an entire period or career. Commonly used in sports statistics, work experience, and other contexts where a running total is meaningful.
Food, flowers, or other items placed before a deity, Buddha, or the spirits of the deceased as a religious or commemorative offering.

glosses: luxury food or drink; indulgence item
explanations: Items consumed for pleasure rather than nutrition, such as coffee, tea, tobacco, alcohol, chocolate, and sweets. The term carries no negative judgment — it simply categorizes items enjoyed for taste or stimulation rather than sustenance.
The process of adapting a novel, true story, or other source material into a screenplay, stage play, or other dramatic format.
Adding dramatic flair or exaggeration to a story or account, making it more interesting or impressive than the reality. Often implies the speaker is stretching the truth.

glosses: to squeeze out; to come up with
to squeeze out; to wring out
to come up with; to devise with effort
explanations: To physically twist or squeeze something to extract its contents.
To produce an idea, answer, or solution through great mental effort, as if wringing it out of one's brain. Implies difficulty and strain.
The sixth planet from the Sun, known for its prominent ring system. Named after the element earth (土) in the Chinese five-element system used for naming planets.
The first and smallest planet in the Solar System, closest to the Sun. Named after the element water (水) in the Chinese five-element system.

glosses: lap blanket; lap robe; throw blanket
explanations: A small blanket or throw used to cover the legs and lap while sitting, commonly used in offices, on airplanes, or when sitting on a sofa.
A long pillow designed to be embraced while sleeping. In everyday use, it is a sleeping aid. In otaku culture, body pillow covers featuring anime or game characters are popular collectibles.
Deep, selfless love and compassion, especially the kind shown by a parent toward a child, or by a figure of authority toward those in their care. Carries a warm, nurturing quality.

The act of recognizing or appreciating something anew, often after taking it for granted or seeing it from a new perspective. Commonly used when someone gains a deeper understanding of something they already knew.

A colorful bell pepper, typically red, yellow, or orange. In Japanese, パプリカ specifically refers to the thick-fleshed, sweet varieties imported or grown for salads and cooking, distinguishing them from the thinner-walled ピーマン.

glosses: hand (of cards); cards in one's hand
explanations: The cards a player is currently holding during a card game or trading card game. Also used figuratively for the options or resources one has available.
An artificial body of water created to store water for drinking, irrigation, or industrial use. May refer to large outdoor reservoirs or smaller storage facilities.

glosses: spring water; water from a natural spring
explanations: Water that flows naturally from the ground. Valued in Japan for its purity and taste, spring water sites are often tourist destinations and sources of local pride.
The act of intentionally ending a life to relieve suffering, whether human or animal. A frequent topic in medical ethics discussions and news. In Japan, active euthanasia for humans remains illegal.
Describes products, materials, or goods that are of low quality, poorly made, or substandard. A fairly strong negative assessment, stronger than simply 'cheap.'
The total distance a vehicle has traveled, typically measured in kilometers. A key factor when buying or selling used cars, and commonly displayed on the odometer.

A stage in the blooming of flowers, especially cherry blossoms, where about half the buds have opened. Part of a scale used in Japanese weather reports and cherry blossom forecasts to describe the progress of blooming.

The formal procedure of preparing and serving matcha in the Japanese tea ceremony. Encompasses all the prescribed movements, from handling utensils to whisking the tea. Also used to compliment someone's skill at making tea.
A literary or poetic word for a kiss. More elegant and romantic than the loanword キス, and typically used in fiction, poetry, and formal or artistic contexts.
On or above the surface of water. Used as a prefix or modifier to describe activities, transportation, or structures that take place on water.

glosses: stationing; being posted (abroad or at a location)
stationing; being posted; residing for duty
explanations: Being assigned to live and work at a particular location, especially overseas, for work purposes. Commonly used for diplomats, company employees on overseas assignments, and police officers assigned to local posts.
The part of a chair, sofa, or seat designed to support the arm. Found on office chairs, airplane seats, theater seats, and sofas.

A public facility found in neighborhoods across Japan, used for community events, classes, meetings, and cultural activities. Operated by local governments and available for residents to use, often for free or at low cost.

The legal right to use reasonable force to protect oneself or others from an imminent threat. In Japanese law, an act of self-defense that meets certain conditions is not punishable. Also used loosely in everyday speech.

glosses: copying verbatim; wholesale copying; transcribing in full
explanations: Copying something exactly as it is, word for word, without any changes or original input. Often carries a negative connotation, implying laziness, plagiarism, or lack of effort.

glosses: dead honest; completely straightforward; utterly sincere
explanations: An intensified form of 正直 (honest), meaning someone is honest to a fault — so honest that it can sometimes work against them. The まっ prefix adds emphasis, like 'dead' or 'completely' in English.
The act of hitting or striking someone, especially as an act of violence. A formal word commonly used in legal, police, and news contexts to describe physical assault.

glosses: epidemic prevention; disease control; quarantine measures
explanations: Measures and activities aimed at preventing the spread of infectious diseases. Includes quarantine, vaccination campaigns, disinfection, and public health monitoring.
Death that occurs abruptly and unexpectedly, without prior warning or prolonged illness. Used in both medical and general contexts.

glosses: running side by side; running parallel
running side by side; running in parallel
explanations: Moving alongside something or someone at the same speed, whether literally (vehicles, runners) or figuratively (projects, processes running concurrently).
The residents or citizens of a town (町). Used in official and administrative contexts to refer to the people living in a municipality classified as a 町.
A substance used to add sweetness to food or drinks. Covers both natural sweeteners like sugar and honey, and artificial ones like aspartame and stevia.

glosses: place of stay; where one is staying
explanations: The location where someone is staying, especially when away from home. Used for hotels, host families, or any temporary lodging during travel or business trips.

glosses: hearing loss; hardness of hearing; hearing impairment
explanations: A medical condition in which a person's ability to hear is reduced. Ranges from mild difficulty to profound deafness. Used both as a medical term and in everyday conversation.

glosses: snow removal; snow clearing; snow plowing
explanations: The act of clearing accumulated snow from roads, sidewalks, rooftops, and other surfaces. A common winter activity in snowy regions of Japan, especially in Hokkaido and the Japan Sea side.
Describes someone or something that inspires warm affection through their cuteness or innocence. Stronger and more heartfelt than かわいい, often implying a desire to cherish or protect.
Describes food or drink that has a sweet taste. Used especially for sake, wine, curry, and sauces to indicate the sweeter end of the flavor spectrum.
For dishes like curry, indicates a mild, non-spicy level. Japanese curry products are typically graded from sweet (甘口) through medium (中辛) to hot (辛口).
The act of giving up one's own interests, comfort, or well-being for the sake of others. Often discussed in moral, philosophical, and literary contexts.
A respectful way to refer to the Buddha or Buddhist deities. The さま suffix adds reverence.
A respectful, euphemistic way to refer to a person who has died. Rooted in the Buddhist belief that the deceased becomes a buddha. Common in conversation about funerals and death.

glosses: serving a prison sentence; imprisonment; doing time
explanations: The act of serving time in prison as punishment for a crime. A formal term commonly used in news and legal contexts.
A deep, dark shade of brown resembling the color of something scorched. Literally 'burnt brown.' Used for colors of clothing, hair, furniture, and other items.
Describes a person or manner that tends to hold back, be restrained, or avoid imposing on others. Conveys a habitual tendency toward reserve rather than a single instance.

glosses: to share; to share with one another
to share; to divide and share; to share with one another
explanations: To share something among people, especially abstract things like feelings, experiences, joy, or sorrow. Implies mutual sharing and emotional connection. More literary and heartfelt than simply 分ける.

glosses: end of work; end of the business day; closing
explanations: The conclusion of work or business hours for the day. Used in both workplace and school contexts. The opposite of 始業 (start of work).

Describes speech, writing, or methods that are unnecessarily indirect and take a long time to get to the point. Always carries a negative connotation — implying the speaker or method should be more direct.

glosses: Vernal Equinox Day; Spring Equinox Day
explanations: A Japanese national holiday that falls around March 20-21, on the date of the vernal equinox. It is a day for appreciating nature and showing love for living things. Also traditionally a day for visiting family graves.

glosses: to flutter down; to fall dancing
to flutter down; to fall gently; to drift down
explanations: Describes something light falling slowly and gracefully through the air, as if dancing. Used for things like leaves, petals, snowflakes, and feathers. A poetic, evocative word.

glosses: vaguely; dimly; obscurely; in a hazy way
explanations: Describes a state where something is unclear, undefined, or lacking concrete form. Used for thoughts, feelings, memories, and impressions that are not sharply defined.

glosses: to expose; to reveal; to disclose
to expose; to reveal; to disclose; to unmask
explanations: To bring hidden or secret information to light, especially wrongdoing, scandals, or things someone wanted to keep secret. Often implies the revelation is damaging to the person exposed.

glosses: before it happens; in advance; beforehand
explanations: Describes preventing something bad from occurring before it actually happens. Almost always used with verbs meaning 'to prevent' or 'to stop.' A formal expression common in written language and official contexts.

glosses: sensitivity to cold; poor circulation; tendency to feel cold
explanations: A constitutional tendency to feel cold easily, especially in the hands, feet, and lower body. Recognized in Japanese and East Asian medicine as a condition requiring treatment. Much more commonly discussed in Japan than in Western cultures.

glosses: behind the scenes; background; hidden side
explanations: The area behind a person or thing. More formal and literary than 後ろ.
The hidden forces, motives, or circumstances behind an event or situation. Often used in news and investigative contexts.
A piece of cloth or knitted fabric worn around the neck for warmth. A slightly old-fashioned or literary word; マフラー is more common in everyday speech.

glosses: outward journey; the way there; outbound route
explanations: The trip going to a destination, as opposed to the return trip. Used in travel, sports (relay races), and transportation contexts.

glosses: living a life of leisure; carefree retirement
living a life of leisure; carefree and self-sufficient living
explanations: A four-character compound (四字熟語) describing a relaxed, unhurried lifestyle free from worldly pressures. Typically used to describe retirement or a life of comfortable independence.

glosses: solo trip; traveling alone; solo travel
explanations: A trip taken by oneself without companions. Can refer to both short day trips and longer journeys. Often carries a positive connotation of freedom and self-discovery.
A reduced price offered to students for transportation, admission, services, and products. Short for 学生割引. Very common in Japan for train tickets, museum admission, movie theaters, and more.

glosses: somehow; vaguely; in some indefinable way
explanations: Expresses a feeling or impression that is hard to pinpoint or articulate clearly. The speaker senses something but cannot identify exactly what or why.

glosses: mock exam; practice test; trial examination
explanations: A practice examination designed to simulate the format and difficulty of a real test. Very common in the Japanese education system, especially for university entrance exams and professional qualification tests.
A woman who is married to one's father but is not one's biological mother. The reading ままはは is the most common; the kanji 継 means 'to succeed' or 'to inherit.'
Describes a person whose personality is warm, calm, and gentle. Implies someone who is not easily angered and treats others with kindness. A consistently positive descriptor.
A vast expanse of clouds viewed from above, typically from a mountaintop or airplane. The clouds spread out below the viewer like an ocean. A popular sight for hikers and photographers in Japan.

Describes something that looks awkward, unshapely, or lacking in grace. Can refer to physical appearance, posture, movements, or the shape of objects. Often used affectionately or self-deprecatingly rather than harshly.

glosses: to keep watch; to stand guard
to keep watch; to stand guard; to look out
explanations: To watch carefully over a place, person, or situation in order to protect, monitor, or prevent something from happening. Implies sustained, vigilant observation.

A style of painting based on traditional Japanese artistic conventions, techniques, and materials such as mineral pigments, ink, and washi paper or silk. Distinguished from Western-style painting (洋画) as a category in the Japanese art world.

glosses: vertically long; tall and narrow; portrait-oriented
explanations: Describes an object or shape that is longer in the vertical direction than the horizontal. Used for physical objects, windows, screens, images, and document layouts. The opposite of 横長 (landscape-oriented).
A person stationed at the entrance of a building, campus, or facility to check visitors and maintain security. Commonly found at schools, hospitals, office buildings, and government facilities.

A flat mat woven from rushes (igusa) or similar plant materials. Used for sitting or lying on outdoors, at festivals, picnics, and traditional events. Also refers to the woven surface layer of tatami.

A member of the clergy in Protestant Christianity who leads a congregation, conducts worship services, and provides spiritual guidance. Specifically refers to Protestant ministers, not Catholic priests.
A solemn promise or formal commitment, often made publicly or in a binding context. Used for both personal vows and official agreements.
A family unit or household, especially in the context of managing daily life, finances, and domestic affairs. Often carries the nuance of the practical side of running a home.

glosses: to misjudge; to think less of
to misjudge; to misgauge; to make a wrong assessment
to lose respect for; to think less of; to be disappointed in
explanations: To judge someone or something incorrectly, especially to underestimate or fail to see their true nature.
To become disillusioned with someone after seeing their bad behavior or poor character. Often used when expressing strong disappointment.

glosses: to let wither; to kill (a plant)
to let wither; to cause to dry up; to kill (a plant)
explanations: To cause a plant to wilt and die, typically through neglect (not watering) or by using chemicals. The transitive counterpart of 枯れる (to wither).
A work of writing, especially a book or scholarly publication. Refers to the finished product.
The act of writing and publishing written works. Often used in compounds related to intellectual property and copyright.
An explanation using diagrams, charts, or illustrations to make something easier to understand. Also refers to the diagram itself.
A person who secretly gathers information about another country, organization, or group. Also used loosely for a traitor or informant within a group.
Having a pure, unspoiled quality free from malice or cunning. Describes someone, typically a child, who acts naturally without hidden motives. Generally positive or endearing.
Having a pure and uncorrupted heart or character. Describes someone whose feelings and intentions are genuine and free from worldly calculation. Slightly literary in tone.

glosses: to feel ashamed; to be embarrassed
to feel ashamed; to be embarrassed; to feel disgrace
explanations: To feel shame about one's own actions, behavior, or shortcomings. A more introspective and literary word than 恥ずかしい.

glosses: agreement; same feeling; sympathy; sharing someone's view
explanations: The feeling of agreeing with someone's opinion or sharing their sentiment. Used to express that one feels the same way about something.

glosses: good or bad; merits and demerits
good or bad; right or wrong; merits and demerits; quality
explanations: The relative merit or quality of something, encompassing both its good and bad aspects. Used when evaluating or judging something from multiple angles.
Being completely focused on one thing or one person with unwavering dedication. Often used positively, especially about love, passion, or effort.
Refusing to change one's mind or yield to others' opinions, even when it would be reasonable to do so. Carries a negative connotation.
Completely eliminating something undesirable so that it cannot recur. Used for diseases, social problems, crime, and harmful practices.

glosses: back side; reverse side; hidden aspect
back side; reverse side; back surface
hidden side; behind the scenes; hidden aspect
explanations: The back or reverse surface of a physical object such as paper, a card, fabric, or a sign.
The unseen or concealed aspect of a situation, person, or event. The side that is not publicly known.

glosses: heavy snowfall; extreme snow; blizzard-level snow
explanations: An exceptionally large amount of snowfall, significantly beyond normal levels. Used in weather reports and when describing regions or events affected by extreme snow.

glosses: to ask again; to ask back
to ask again; to ask someone to repeat
explanations: To ask someone to say something again because you didn't hear or understand it the first time.
To respond to a question with another question, turning it back on the person who asked.

glosses: prophetic dream; dream that comes true
explanations: A dream whose content later becomes reality. In Japanese folk belief, dreams seen in the early morning hours are said to be more likely to come true.

A humble expression for giving someone a gift or present. The speaker lowers themselves by using this word, making it appropriate when offering something to a superior, customer, or someone deserving respect.

glosses: bereavement; parting by death; being separated by death
explanations: The experience of losing someone close through death. Focuses on the separation and loss felt by the surviving person.

Lacking propriety or showing poor judgment about what is appropriate in a given situation. Often used to criticize behavior that is disrespectful or tasteless, especially during serious or solemn occasions.
The ability to control one's emotions, impulses, and desires. A valued personal quality in both personal and professional settings.
A web of personal and professional relationships that can be drawn upon for information, opportunities, or support. An important concept in Japanese business and social culture.
Detecting or perceiving something through the senses or through a device. Used both for human perception and for machines or sensors that detect changes.

glosses: sacred place; holy land; holy ground
explanations: A place of religious significance or spiritual importance. Refers to sites considered sacred in any religion.
A place strongly associated with a particular activity, interest, or fandom. In modern Japanese, commonly used for locations connected to anime, manga, or other pop culture.

glosses: to bend; to flex; to be supple
to bend; to flex; to be supple; to spring
explanations: To bend smoothly under force and spring back, like a flexible branch or fishing rod. Describes an elastic, resilient bending motion rather than a permanent deformation.

glosses: proper course of action; right way; proper procedure
explanations: The logical flow or coherent sequence of an argument, explanation, or course of action. Implies things should proceed in a reasonable, orderly manner.
The correct or socially expected way of handling a situation. Implies there is a right process to follow.

glosses: airtight seal; hermetic seal; sealed shut
explanations: Sealing something completely so that no air, moisture, or contaminants can enter or escape. Used for food storage, packaging, and containers.
A name used to conceal one's true identity. Often implies deceptive intent, unlike pen names or stage names which are openly acknowledged.

glosses: dual income; both spouses working; two-income household
explanations: A household where both husband and wife work and earn income. A common arrangement in modern Japan, increasingly discussed in the context of work-life balance and childcare.
The person or organization that plans and takes responsibility for an event, conference, competition, or gathering.
The act of starting or launching a computer, application, or system. Used broadly for any device or software that powers on or initializes.

glosses: to look after; to take care of
to look after; to take care of; to attend to
explanations: To provide care, supervision, or assistance to someone. Often used for caring for children, elderly family members, or subordinates.
The quality of being round or having curved edges. Used for physical shapes.
A figurative sense describing a softened or gentler quality in personality, tone, or flavor.

glosses: to look away; to avert one's eyes
explanations: To deliberately turn one's gaze away from something. Often implies avoidance, embarrassment, or unwillingness to confront something.

glosses: host city; venue; place where an event is held
explanations: The location where an event, competition, or conference takes place. Commonly used for large-scale events like the Olympics, World Cup, or international conferences.
To walk around an area checking for problems or ensuring safety. Used for security guards, police, or anyone conducting inspections.
To move one's eyes around a space to take in the surroundings.
A ticket purchased before the day of an event, typically at a discounted price compared to tickets sold at the door.
The amount of something that is left. Commonly used for battery charge, ink, fuel, and other consumables.

glosses: to fall silent; to clam up
to fall silent; to clam up; to become quiet
explanations: To suddenly stop talking and remain silent, often because of shock, sadness, anger, or not knowing what to say. The ～{込|こ}む suffix adds a sense of sinking into or becoming absorbed in the state of silence.

glosses: a group; a party; a troupe; a band
explanations: A group of people who are together for a shared purpose, such as travelers, performers, or workers. Implies a cohesive unit moving or acting together.
A person who possesses an enormous fortune. Literally means 'a person of hundreds of millions,' emphasizing vast wealth. Used somewhat colloquially and often in aspirational or storytelling contexts.
Describes a person or lifestyle characterized by vigorous activity and energy. Used for people who are always doing things, as well as for lively or dynamic situations.

glosses: shared room; room shared with another person
explanations: A room that is shared between two or more people who are not traveling together. Common in hostels, ryokan, hospitals, and dormitories.

glosses: three-day weekend; three consecutive days off
explanations: Three consecutive holidays, typically formed when a national holiday falls on a Monday or Friday, creating a long weekend. Japan's Happy Monday system creates several three-day weekends per year.

glosses: old model; old type; outdated version
explanations: A previous version or model of a product, machine, or system that has been replaced by a newer one. Commonly used for electronics, vehicles, and equipment.
A small repair, correction, or improvement made to something that is mostly complete. Implies the changes are minor rather than a complete overhaul.

glosses: observation deck; lookout point; viewing platform
explanations: A platform or area, usually at a high elevation, designed for people to enjoy a panoramic view. Found on tall buildings, mountains, and scenic spots.
Describes an attitude or manner that uses authority or pressure to force compliance. Used for people, organizations, or communication styles that intimidate others into submission.

glosses: to browse; to view; to read
to browse; to view; to inspect; to read through
explanations: To look through or read documents, websites, or materials. Originally used for inspecting official documents, now very common for browsing the internet.
In biology, living on or in another organism and obtaining nourishment from it. Used for insects, plants, and microorganisms.
Figuratively, relying on someone else for one's livelihood without contributing in return.
A sound in the low frequency range. Used for music, voices, and audio equipment.
Describes a person, face, or performance that shows a rich variety of emotions. Used positively to praise someone's expressiveness.
The act of leaving a room, meeting, building, or online space. More formal than simply 'leaving' and often used in official or digital contexts.

glosses: look of the sky; way things are going
look of the sky; movement of clouds
way things are going; signs; outlook; developments
explanations: The appearance of the sky based on how clouds are moving, especially as an indication of approaching weather.
Figuratively, the direction a situation is heading, especially when it seems to be turning unfavorable.

glosses: short time; brief period; short duration
explanations: A relatively brief span of time. Often used as a modifier with で or の to describe doing something quickly or in a limited time.

glosses: outpouring; surge; flood (of complaints, problems, etc.)
explanations: The forceful release of liquid, gas, or material from an opening. Used for volcanoes, geysers, pipes, and other physical phenomena.
Figuratively, a sudden and overwhelming emergence of problems, complaints, or other abstract things.

glosses: one's place; one's station; one's standing; one's limits
explanations: One's social position, abilities, or means. Often used in expressions about knowing one's limits or acting within one's means.
The sport of table tennis. Japan has a strong table tennis tradition and has produced world-class players. Also called ピンポン in casual speech.

glosses: to crouch down; to squat down; to huddle up
explanations: To bend the body low and curl up close to the ground. Often implies being in pain, feeling cold, or trying to hide. Can also be written as 蹲る in kanji.

glosses: captain; skipper; master of a ship
explanations: The person in command of a ship or boat. Responsible for the vessel's navigation, safety, and crew.

glosses: brown sugar; unrefined sugar; raw sugar
explanations: Dark, unrefined cane sugar with a rich, molasses-like flavor. A specialty product of Okinawa and other southern Japanese islands.
Sugar pressed into small cube shapes for convenient use in drinks like coffee and tea.
The supreme governing authority of a state or the ultimate power held by the people in a democratic system. A fundamental concept in political science and international law.

glosses: plain; easy; simple; easy to understand
explanations: Describes language, writing, or explanations that are clear and simple, avoiding difficult or technical expressions. Often used to praise clear writing or speaking.

glosses: to outwit; to outsmart; to catch off guard; to do the unexpected
explanations: To act in a way that the other party does not expect, thereby gaining an advantage. Often used in strategy, competition, and negotiations.
A person with exceptional intellectual ability or talent, especially in academics. Carries a positive connotation of natural brilliance.

glosses: ordinary person; average person; mediocre person
explanations: A person of average ability with no outstanding talents. Can be used self-deprecatingly or to contrast with exceptional people.
Food that remains uneaten after a meal. The most common usage.
Items remaining after the main selection has been taken. Can imply lesser quality or being unwanted.
A flower made from fabric, plastic, paper, or other materials to imitate a real flower. Used for decoration.
A noisy disturbance or a situation where people are making a big deal out of something. Can refer to both literal noise and figurative overreaction.
A negative evaluation or reception of something. Used when a product, decision, or action is poorly received by others.
A feeling of love, devotion, and attachment to one's country. In Japanese discourse, this term can carry complex connotations due to Japan's modern history.

glosses: application; filing (for admission, a patent, or a license)
explanations: The formal act of submitting an application, most commonly for university admission or patent registration. More formal and specific than 申し込み.

glosses: leave of absence; temporary leave from work
explanations: A period during which an employee is temporarily away from work, typically due to illness, childcare, or personal reasons, while maintaining their employment status.
A research study conducted with human participants to evaluate the safety and efficacy of new drugs or medical treatments before they are approved for general use.
The bony framework of a human or animal body. In everyday usage, often refers to a skeleton model or a skull-and-crossbones image.
A line made up of a series of dots or short dashes. Used in diagrams, maps, forms, and documents to indicate boundaries, cutting lines, or areas to fill in.
A fence or boundary made of closely planted shrubs or trees. A traditional feature of Japanese residential gardens.

glosses: feeling of inferiority; sense of inadequacy
feeling of inferiority; sense of inadequacy; self-consciousness
explanations: A feeling of being inferior to others or not measuring up. Often used with を感じる (to feel).
Meat or other food cut into small, thin pieces. Commonly seen on food packaging.
Describes time or activities broken up into small, discontinuous segments.

glosses: point-blank range; very close distance; close proximity
explanations: An extremely short distance between two things. Originally a military/firearms term for the distance at which a bullet travels in a nearly flat trajectory, now commonly used to mean simply 'very close.'
A lack of trust or confidence in someone or something. Commonly used in political and institutional contexts.
Acting without good faith or sincerity in dealings with others.
Being of the same sex or gender. Used in social, legal, and relationship contexts.
Having or appearing to have length, width, and depth. Used in science, technology, and everyday language.
In otaku culture, refers to the real world and real people, as opposed to the two-dimensional world of anime, manga, and games.
An Olympic track and field event in which athletes walk as fast as possible while maintaining continuous contact with the ground. One foot must always be on the ground.

glosses: snap decision; prompt judgment; quick decision
explanations: Making a decision immediately without lengthy deliberation. Can be viewed positively (decisive action) or negatively (hasty judgment) depending on context.
A feeling of sorrow and concern for the suffering or misfortune of others. Can carry a slightly condescending nuance depending on context.
Pain in the stomach area. Can refer to both physical stomach pain and, figuratively, stress-induced discomfort.

glosses: perfect synchronization; tacit understanding; unspoken coordination
explanations: The ability of two people to act in perfect harmony without needing verbal communication. Implies a deep, intuitive mutual understanding built through long experience together.
A small hill or rise in the ground. Can refer to a natural elevation or a man-made mound.
A system where customers serve themselves rather than being served by staff. Common in gas stations, restaurants, and stores.
Techniques and skills for protecting oneself from physical attack. Encompasses various martial arts and defensive methods.

glosses: new ground; new frontier; new territory; new realm
explanations: A previously unexplored area of activity, thought, or creative expression. Used when someone breaks into a new field or achieves something unprecedented.
A thin, absorbent paper used for Japanese calligraphy (書道). Standard size is approximately 24cm × 33cm. Named because it is roughly half the size of a full sheet of traditional Japanese paper.
Not subject to taxation. Used for goods, services, income, or transactions that are exempt from tax by law.

glosses: the strong; powerful person; dominant party
explanations: A person or entity with power, strength, or a dominant position. Often used in abstract or social contexts to discuss power dynamics.

glosses: low table (for sitting on the floor)
low table; floor table; Japanese-style table
explanations: A low table designed to be used while sitting on the floor (on tatami mats or cushions). A staple of traditional Japanese living rooms.

glosses: case (of a disease); clinical case; instance of illness
explanations: An individual occurrence of a disease or medical condition. Used in medical reports, research, and news coverage of health topics.

glosses: to go overboard; to cut loose; to get carried away
to go overboard; to cut loose; to get carried away; to go too far
explanations: To lose self-control and behave excessively, especially in the context of having fun or celebrating. Implies going beyond reasonable limits.
A line that curves up and down in a wave-like pattern. Used in documents, diagrams, and proofreading marks.

A warship designed to escort and protect other vessels. In modern Japanese usage, this is the official designation for Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force (JMSDF) destroyers, since the postwar constitution avoids overtly military terminology.
An exceptionally fast pitched ball in baseball. Emphasizes overwhelming speed and power beyond a regular fastball.

glosses: peerage; title of nobility; rank of nobility
explanations: A hereditary or granted rank within a system of nobility. In Japan, the peerage system (華族制度) existed from 1869 to 1947.
The flat bone at the center of the chest that connects the ribs. An important anatomical landmark in medical and first-aid contexts.
The deepest, most hidden aspects of a subject or discipline. Often refers to knowledge or truths that are not easily accessible and require deep study to understand.
A literary and somewhat classical term for a beautiful woman. More refined and elegant in nuance than everyday words like 美人.

glosses: a-un; unspoken mutual understanding; perfect synchronization
explanations: Originally a Buddhist term representing the first and last sounds of the Sanskrit alphabet (like alpha and omega), symbolizing the beginning and end of all things. In modern usage, most commonly refers to the tacit, wordless coordination between two people who understand each other perfectly.
The property of transmitting or receiving signals, sound, or energy more effectively in a particular direction. Used in audio engineering, telecommunications, and antenna design.
Shifting an entire piece of music or passage to a different key while preserving the intervals between notes. A fundamental concept in music theory and performance.
A book used alongside the main textbook in school education to provide additional material or different perspectives on a subject. Often produced by local governments or educational boards.

glosses: circuit board; printed circuit board; substrate
explanations: A flat board made of insulating material on which electronic components are mounted and connected by conductive pathways. Also refers more broadly to any base plate or substrate in manufacturing.
A material that allows electric current or heat to flow through it easily. Metals like copper and aluminum are typical conductors.

glosses: national polity; national structure; form of government
explanations: The fundamental character or political structure of a nation. Historically significant in prewar Japan as an ideological concept centering on the emperor system.
Short for 国民体育大会 (National Sports Festival), an annual multi-sport competition held in a different prefecture each year. Renamed to 国民スポーツ大会 in 2024, but the abbreviation 国体 remains in common use.

glosses: redness; erythema; reddening of the skin
explanations: Abnormal redness of the skin caused by inflammation, irritation, allergy, or infection. A medical term used in clinical descriptions and pharmaceutical instructions.
One's capability and proficiency in swimming. Used to assess or describe how well someone can swim, often in instructional or competitive contexts.

The total or overall amount of something, as opposed to a relative proportion or ratio. Often used when emphasizing that the sheer volume of something is insufficient or significant regardless of percentages.

glosses: desire for possession; possessiveness; acquisitive desire
explanations: The desire to own things or to have something exclusively for oneself. Can refer to material possessions, relationships, or abstract things.

glosses: all manner of abuse; torrent of insults
all manner of abuse; torrent of insults; stream of invective
explanations: A barrage of abusive language and insults. A four-character compound (四字熟語) that emphasizes the indiscriminate and relentless nature of the verbal attacks.

glosses: breakup of a family; family scattered apart
explanations: A situation where the members of a family are forced to separate and go their own ways, typically due to financial ruin, war, disaster, or other dire circumstances. Carries a tragic, irreversible connotation.

glosses: crawling forward; belly crawl; low crawl
explanations: Moving forward on one's stomach with elbows and knees, keeping the body as low as possible. Originally a military technique for advancing under enemy fire, but also used figuratively for any painstakingly slow progress.

glosses: bare-handed; empty-handed; with nothing; from scratch
explanations: Literally, having no weapons or tools — fighting with bare fists. Figuratively, starting from nothing with no resources, connections, or advantages. Often used admiringly to describe someone who built something through sheer effort.
The tiny, flat, overlapping structures that cover the wings of butterflies and moths (Lepidoptera). These scales create wing patterns and colors, and feel like fine powder when touched.
A shirt or garment style with the collar worn open, without a tie or buttoned-up neckline. Refers especially to the open-collar dress shirts commonly worn in summer in Japan.
A warm, reddish-brown color resembling polished copper. Used to describe skin tanned by the sun, metallic surfaces, or autumn foliage.
The surface of a floor. Used in construction, architecture, and interior design when discussing flooring materials, finishes, or specifications.
A mid-level military officer rank. In the army and air force, equivalent to major; in the navy, equivalent to lieutenant commander. Ranks above captain (大尉) and below lieutenant colonel (中佐).
A senior military officer rank. In the army and air force, equivalent to lieutenant colonel; in the navy, equivalent to commander. Ranks above major (少佐) and below colonel (大佐).

glosses: one by one; one at a time
one by one; one at a time; one each
explanations: Indicates doing or distributing something one unit at a time. The counter 個 is used for small, discrete objects.
A device that uses electromagnetic fields to propel charged particles to high speeds and energies. Used in physics research, medical treatment, and industrial applications.
A playing piece used in mahjong. A standard set contains 136 tiles divided into suits (萬子, 筒子, 索子) and honor tiles (字牌). Also written as 牌 in other tile-based games.

glosses: paper feed; paper feeding; paper supply
explanations: The mechanism or process of feeding paper into a printer, copier, or other machine. A common term in office equipment and printing.

The total volume of all cylinders in an internal combustion engine, typically measured in cc (cubic centimeters) or liters. A key specification for cars and motorcycles that also determines tax and licensing categories in Japan.

glosses: person in need; the destitute; the needy
explanations: A person suffering from severe poverty or hardship. A formal term used in social welfare, government policy, and news reporting.

glosses: morale visit; encouragement gift; visit to those working hard
explanations: A visit or gift given to encourage people in the midst of an intense effort, such as during an election campaign, a major project, or long working hours. Originally referred to visiting soldiers at their camp.

glosses: stick gum; slab gum; flat chewing gum
explanations: Chewing gum in the traditional flat, rectangular stick form, as opposed to pellet-type gum (粒ガム). A common everyday product in Japan.
Attaches to the stem of a verb (masu-stem) to indicate that the action is easy to perform. The resulting word conjugates as an i-adjective.
Indicates a natural tendency or susceptibility toward the action. Often used to describe inherent characteristics of people or things.
Attaches to the masu-stem of a verb to indicate that the action is difficult to perform, often with a nuance of psychological or emotional difficulty. The resulting word conjugates as an i-adjective.
Attaches to the masu-stem of a verb to indicate that the action has been completed in its entirety. Emphasizes that the process reached its endpoint.
Attaches to the masu-stem of a verb to indicate the beginning of an action. The resulting compound conjugates as an ichidan verb.

glosses: to do ~ over again; to redo ~
explanations: Attaches to the masu-stem of a verb to indicate repeating an action from the beginning, usually to correct or improve the result. The resulting compound conjugates as a godan verb.

glosses: covered in ~; full of ~; riddled with ~
explanations: Attaches to nouns to indicate being covered in or full of something undesirable. Almost always carries a negative connotation. Functions as a no-adjective when modifying nouns.
A conjunction pattern meaning "not only A but also B." Indicates that the scope extends beyond A to include B as well. Often paired with ～も at the end of the clause.

glosses: thank you for your hard work (to a subordinate)
thank you for your hard work; good job
explanations: An expression used to acknowledge someone's effort or labor. Importantly, it is typically used by a superior toward a subordinate or by someone receiving a service. Using it toward a social superior is considered rude.

glosses: to oversleep; to sleep past one's alarm or intended wake-up time
explanations: To sleep longer than planned, typically resulting in being late. A compound of 寝る (to sleep) and 過ごす (to pass/exceed).

glosses: to be absorbed in; to be immersed in
to be absorbed in; to be immersed in; to devote oneself to
explanations: To concentrate so deeply on an activity that one loses awareness of everything else. Often used for work, study, hobbies, or creative pursuits. Takes the particle に for the activity.

glosses: to wail; to cry loudly; to sob uncontrollably
explanations: To cry loudly and openly, with audible sobbing. Stronger than simply crying (泣く). Often used in dramatic or emotional contexts.

glosses: to trigger; to induce; to cause
to trigger; to induce; to cause; to provoke
explanations: To cause something (usually negative) to occur as a consequence. Often used in medical, scientific, and news contexts for events that set off a chain reaction or bring about an undesirable outcome.

glosses: to cross; to intersect; to associate with
to associate with; to have relations with
explanations: For lines, roads, or paths to cross each other at a point. Used for physical intersections.
To interact or socialize with people. Often used in somewhat formal or literary contexts to describe personal or social relationships.

glosses: to crunch; to break down into simple terms
to crunch; to chew up; to bite into pieces
to explain in simple terms; to break down (an explanation)
explanations: To break food or other objects into small pieces by biting. The literal meaning of chewing something hard until it breaks apart.
To make a complex topic easy to understand by simplifying it. A figurative extension of the literal meaning.

glosses: to barricade oneself in; to hole up
to barricade oneself in; to hole up; to shut oneself in
explanations: To take refuge inside a building or enclosed space and refuse to come out, often in a standoff situation. Commonly used in news reports about hostage situations or sieges. Can also be used more casually for shutting oneself in a room.

glosses: to leave alone; to leave as is; to neglect
to leave alone; to let be; to leave someone/something as is
explanations: To deliberately not interfere with or attend to someone or something. Can imply either benign neglect (giving space) or irresponsible neglect depending on context.

glosses: to leave as is; to defer; to keep unchanged
to leave as is; to keep unchanged; to hold at the current level
explanations: To maintain something at its current state or level without changing it. Commonly used for prices, interest rates, taxes, and other quantitative measures that could be raised or lowered.

glosses: to mature; to come to fruition (figurative)
explanations: For fruit or crops to reach the stage where they are ready to eat or harvest. Used for the natural ripening process.
For a plan, idea, skill, or situation to develop to the point where it is ready or complete. A figurative extension of the ripening metaphor.

glosses: to frolic together; to play-fight; to romp
to frolic together; to play-fight; to romp; to roughhouse
explanations: For two or more people or animals to play together in a physical, lighthearted way — wrestling, chasing, tumbling. Implies affection and playfulness. Commonly used for young animals, children, or couples.

glosses: commonly called; what is popularly known as
commonly called; what is popularly known as; so-called
explanations: An expression used to introduce a common name, colloquial term, or popular label for something. Indicates that the term that follows is informal, colloquial, or widely used but not necessarily official.

glosses: to be on the defensive; to fall behind
to be on the defensive; to fall behind; to be reactive rather than proactive
explanations: To end up in a position where one can only react to events rather than control them. Originally from shogi/go terminology where 後手 means the second player (who moves second). Implies a disadvantageous position.

glosses: difficult to read; hard to decipher
explanations: Describes text, kanji, or names that are difficult to read correctly. Most commonly used in the compound 難読漢字 (hard-to-read kanji) referring to kanji with unusual or rare readings.

glosses: to fall into a trap; to be ensnared
explanations: To be caught in a trap, either literally (an animal caught in a physical trap) or figuratively (a person deceived by a scheme or trick). The figurative usage is more common.

glosses: to keep in mind; to bear in mind
to keep in mind; to bear in mind; to be mindful of
explanations: To consciously maintain awareness of something when making decisions or taking action. A somewhat formal expression used in both spoken and written Japanese.

glosses: to make the first move; to take the initiative
to make the first move; to take the initiative; to act preemptively
explanations: To take action before the other party does, gaining a strategic advantage. Originally from shogi/go terminology where 先手 is the player who moves first.

glosses: to stand out from the crowd; to be outstanding
to stand out from the crowd; to be outstanding; to be head and shoulders above
explanations: To be exceptionally superior compared to others in a group. Literally means "to pull out from the herd/group." Used as high praise for someone or something far exceeding the norm.

glosses: to pay attention; to exercise caution
to pay attention; to exercise caution; to take care
explanations: To be careful and attentive about something. More deliberate and formal than simply 気をつける. The verb 払う (to pay) is used metaphorically here, as in English "to pay attention."

glosses: to take advantage of; to multiply
to take advantage of; to exploit (an opportunity or weakness)
explanations: To seize upon a situation, moment of weakness, or confusion to act in one's favor. Often implies cunning or opportunism.
