To perform multiplication. A formal/literary alternative to 掛ける in mathematical contexts.

glosses: to eat greedily; to devour; to be desperate for
to eat greedily; to wolf down; to devour
to be desperate for; to be overly eager
explanations: To eat voraciously, without manners or restraint. Implies hunger or lack of self-control around food.
To show excessive eagerness or desperation, especially regarding money, romantic attention, or opportunities. Carries a negative connotation of being too hungry or aggressive in pursuing something.

glosses: to triumph; to gloat; to exult in victory
explanations: To display pride and satisfaction after winning. Often implies showing off one's victory in a way that may be smug or arrogant. Commonly used as a modifier in the form 勝ち誇った (triumphant).

glosses: and so on; etcetera; and more
explanations: A casual emphatic repetition of など, used at the end of a list to indicate that there are more items. More emphatic and conversational than a single など, suggesting that the list could go on considerably.

glosses: reaching the summit; summiting; climbing to the top of a mountain
explanations: The act of successfully reaching the peak of a mountain. Used specifically for mountaineering achievements. Can also be used as a suru-verb (登頂する).

glosses: orally; verbally; by word of mouth
explanations: Doing something through spoken words rather than in writing. Used to specify that communication, instructions, or agreements are made verbally. 口頭 alone is a noun meaning "oral/verbal."

glosses: to reply; to answer; to respond
to reply; to answer; to respond (to a question, survey, or inquiry)
explanations: To provide an answer or response, especially to a formal question, survey, questionnaire, or official inquiry. More formal than 答える and implies a considered or official response.

glosses: non-renewal of contract; termination of employment
non-renewal of a fixed-term employment contract; termination by not renewing
explanations: When an employer decides not to renew a temporary or fixed-term worker's contract at its expiration, effectively ending their employment. A significant labor issue in Japan, especially for non-regular workers.

A small shelter or lodge built on a mountain, used by hikers and climbers for rest or overnight stays. In Japan, many mountain huts are commercially operated and offer meals and bedding during hiking season.
A bag designed to be carried by hand, typically with short handles. Used for shopping bags, small tote bags, and similar portable bags.
The younger sister of one's spouse, or the wife of one's younger brother.
A younger female sibling by remarriage of a parent, not related by blood.
A speech sound produced by partially or fully obstructing airflow, as opposed to a vowel. In Japanese linguistics, consonants combine with vowels to form syllables in the kana system.
The act of staying in a place when others have left, or continuing to remain in a position or organization.
Substances or effects that remain after a process, especially chemicals or contaminants that persist in food, soil, or the body.
The design or practice of letting natural light into a building through windows, skylights, or other openings. An important consideration in architecture and interior design.
Describes things that are independent or unrelated to each other. Used to emphasize that two or more items should be treated as separate matters.
A stretched cord on a musical instrument such as a guitar, violin, or koto that produces sound when plucked or bowed.
The string of a bow used in archery.
Physical or mental suffering caused by hard work or difficult circumstances. A somewhat literary or formal word emphasizing the burden of effort.
The quality of food or drink that sustains health and promotes growth. Often used to describe foods that are particularly nutritious or health-giving.
The amount of medicine or substance to be taken or administered at one time or over a period. Commonly seen on medicine packaging and in medical instructions.

glosses: first public showing; debut exhibition; unveiling
explanations: The first time something is shown or revealed to the public, such as a film, artwork, product, or building.

glosses: traditional boys' school uniform with stand-up collar
explanations: A black, military-style uniform with a stand-up collar (Prussian collar) and brass buttons, traditionally worn by male students in Japanese middle and high schools. Still used at many schools today.
The ability or capacity to handle and process tasks, data, or work. Used for both technological systems (computers, servers) and human or organizational capability.
A substance that pollutes or contaminates the environment, including air, water, and soil. Commonly used in environmental science and public health discussions.

glosses: having no distinct national character; cosmopolitan; borderless
explanations: The condition of not being a citizen of any country. A legal status recognized in international law.
Used figuratively to describe food, music, fashion, or spaces that blend elements from multiple cultures without belonging to any single one.
Any device or structure used to block sunlight, such as an awning, parasol, shade cloth, or sun visor. Used for both architectural elements and portable shade devices.
The outermost surface of the earth. Used in geography, science, and general descriptions of things on or near the ground level.
A shell-less land mollusk that moves slowly and leaves a slimy trail. Common in gardens and damp areas, especially during the rainy season.

glosses: to stick in one's ears; to get on one's nerves (a sound)
to linger in one's ears; to be catchy
to get on one's nerves; to be annoying to hear
explanations: A sound, melody, or phrase that stays in one's mind after hearing it, whether pleasantly or not.
A sound, voice, or repeated phrase that becomes irritating through repetition or unpleasantness.

glosses: to frame someone; to falsely accuse
to frame someone; to falsely accuse; to pin the blame on
explanations: To make an innocent person appear guilty of something they did not do. Literally means "to put wet clothes on someone" — an idiom originating from the idea of being unjustly burdened.

A comment or action that indirectly criticizes or mocks someone without naming them directly. The speaker implies criticism through a seemingly general statement that the target (and often the audience) can recognize as aimed at them.
Not yet fully developed or matured. Used for physical growth, technology, infrastructure, or cognitive/emotional development.
A state of being out of harmony. Used in music to describe clashing tones, and figuratively for conflict or inconsistency between people, ideas, or elements.

glosses: second by second; down to the second; extremely tight schedule
second by second; down to the second; in increments of seconds
explanations: Measuring or tracking time in units of seconds. Used to describe an extremely packed or precisely timed schedule, or literal second-by-second measurement.
A wild rabbit or hare, as opposed to a domesticated pet rabbit. In Japan, the Japanese hare (ニホンノウサギ) is native and changes its coat color with the seasons in snowy regions.

glosses: boisterous revelry; noisy partying; rowdy merrymaking
explanations: Loud, exuberant celebration or partying, typically involving drinking, singing, and general noise. Often implies excessive or disruptive merriment.

glosses: rare and curious; strange; exotic; outlandish
explanations: Something that is both rare and unusual, often attracting curiosity. Can describe objects, animals, plants, or behaviors that are strikingly different from the norm.

glosses: some; some kind of; in some way
explanations: Indicates an unspecified or vague something. Used when the speaker cannot or does not need to specify exactly what kind or in what manner.

glosses: full stomach; bellyful; to one's heart's content
to one's heart's content; as much as one wants
explanations: The state of having eaten enough to be completely full. A direct, somewhat casual way to describe satiety.
Doing something to the fullest extent, without restraint.
The act of pressing one's lips against someone or something. A formal and literary word for kiss; in everyday conversation, キス is far more common.
Tailored trousers with a crease, typically worn as part of business or smart-casual attire. Distinguished from jeans or casual pants by their neat, pressed appearance.
A court ruling where a prison sentence is imposed but its execution is delayed for a specified period. If the offender commits no further crimes during that period, the sentence is waived.

glosses: the poor; impoverished class; poverty-stricken population
explanations: The segment of a population living in poverty. Used in news, sociology, and policy discussions about economic inequality.

glosses: source (of a signal, information, or transmission)
explanations: The origin or starting point of a signal, message, broadcast, trend, or piece of information. Used both for technical transmissions and figuratively for the origin of ideas, trends, or rumors.

A small, affordable paperback book format standard in Japanese publishing. Bunko editions are typically A6 size (105×148mm) and are how most novels and classic literature are republished for wide distribution.
A curated collection of books or literary works, or a small library. Often used in the names of publishing imprints or special collections.

glosses: another world; parallel world; fantasy world
explanations: A world different from the real one, especially a fantasy or parallel universe. Widely used as a genre term in Japanese fiction (anime, manga, light novels) where a character is transported to or reborn in a different world.
A hairstyle made by interweaving three strands of hair. Can also refer to braided cord or rope using the same three-strand technique.

Clothing worn for formal ceremonies and occasions such as weddings, funerals, and official events. In everyday Japanese usage, it most often refers to the black formal suit worn at funerals and memorial services.

A medical term for disorders affecting mental health, including conditions such as depression, anxiety disorders, schizophrenia, and bipolar disorder. This is the standard formal/clinical term used in medical and official contexts.

glosses: to get heated; to become passionate; to warm up
to become warm; to heat up
to get heated; to become passionate or intense
explanations: Literally, to take on heat. Used for physical objects that become warm or hot.
Figuratively, used when a discussion, debate, competition, or atmosphere becomes more intense, passionate, or emotionally charged.
A critical assessment or commentary on a work, idea, event, or policy. More formal than simply stating an opinion, it implies structured evaluation and analysis.
Used to describe something that is clear, obvious, or unmistakable. Almost always appears in the negative form 判然としない (not clear, unclear), which is far more common than the affirmative.

glosses: role; part (in a play or situation)
role; part (in a play, film, or performance)
role; function; part to play (in a situation)
explanations: The specific character or part that an actor plays. Implies the nature and importance of the role.
One's role or expected function in a group, project, or situation. Used figuratively beyond the performing arts.

glosses: foil; supporting role that makes others look better
foil; person or thing that makes another look better by contrast
explanations: A person, character, or element whose purpose is to highlight or enhance the qualities of another, often the main figure. Equivalent to a 'foil' or 'straight man' in English.
Keeping something stored or preserved over a long period. Used for food storage, data archiving, document preservation, and other contexts where durability over time is important.

glosses: settlement; reaching an agreement; conclusion of negotiations
explanations: The successful conclusion of negotiations or discussions in which both sides reach a mutually acceptable agreement. Used primarily in formal, business, legal, and diplomatic contexts.
A string of beads used in Buddhist prayer and meditation, traditionally used to count recitations of sutras or mantras. In Japan, they are also commonly held during funerals and memorial services.
The central office or location from which a military operation, organization, or large-scale effort is directed and controlled. Most commonly used in military contexts.
A state of not yet being developed or civilized. Historically used to describe societies or regions considered primitive, though this usage is now seen as problematic and ethnocentric.
Not yet explored, utilized, or developed. Used for land, resources, markets, or fields of study that have potential but remain untouched.

A reference book that catalogs kigo (seasonal words) used in haiku, organized by season. Each entry explains the word's seasonal association and often includes example haiku. An essential tool for haiku composition.
Literally 'ten thousand thunderclaps.' Used almost exclusively in the set phrase 万雷の拍手 (thunderous applause) to describe extremely loud, enthusiastic clapping from an audience.
Apes that closely resemble humans, including chimpanzees, gorillas, orangutans, and gibbons. The scientific term for the primate group most closely related to humans.

The order of mammals that includes humans, apes, monkeys, and prosimians (such as lemurs). The Japanese term literally means 'chief of spirits/souls class,' reflecting the traditional view of primates as the most intelligent animals.
An exclamation of frustration, anger, or annoyance. Originally from 畜生 (beast/brute), a Buddhist term for animals as one of the lower realms of existence. Now used as a mild to moderate swear word.
A derogatory or dismissive term for a young, inexperienced person. Implies the person is immature, naive, or not yet worthy of respect. Typically used by older people referring to younger men.

A second-person pronoun expressing strong anger, contempt, or hostility toward the listener. Despite its kanji containing 貴 (noble) and 様 (honorable), it has shifted to become one of the most aggressive ways to say 'you' in modern Japanese. Commonly heard in anime, manga, and period dramas.
A toilet that uses water to flush waste into a sewage system. Distinguished from non-flush toilets (汲み取り式) that were common in rural Japan until recent decades.

A person who pulls a jinrikisha (人力車), a two-wheeled passenger cart. Historically a common occupation in the Meiji through early Shōwa periods. Today, rickshaw pullers can still be seen in tourist areas like Asakusa, Kyoto, and Kamakura.
The measurement from the crotch to the bottom of the leg, used primarily when buying or tailoring pants. Also refers to the corresponding part of a garment.

glosses: telling on someone; tattling; reporting someone's wrongdoing
explanations: An instruction or order given by a person in authority, such as a parent, teacher, or boss.
The act of informing an authority figure (parent, teacher) about someone else's bad behavior. Commonly used among children.
A horizontal line drawn through text to indicate deletion or correction. Used in both handwritten documents and digital text formatting.
A musical instrument played by pressing keys on a keyboard, such as the piano, organ, harpsichord, or synthesizer.

The traditional Japanese name for July (the seventh month). Part of the set of twelve traditional month names (和風月名) that predate the adoption of the Western calendar. Still used in formal writing, poetry, and seasonal greetings.
Lack of sincerity, honesty, or faithfulness. Often used to describe someone who is unfaithful in a relationship, or who acts dishonestly or without integrity.

glosses: round cushion; sitting in a circle
round straw cushion; circular seat cushion
sitting in a circle; forming a circle to sit together
explanations: A traditional round cushion, originally made of woven straw or rush, used for sitting on tatami floors. Also refers to modern circular cushions.
The act of people sitting together in a circular arrangement, typically for conversation, drinking, or a meeting.
A knitted head covering that exposes only the eyes (and sometimes the mouth), worn for warmth in cold weather or to conceal one's identity. The name literally means 'eye-exposing hat.'

glosses: education for gifted children; elite education
education for gifted children; elite early education
explanations: Specialized education designed to develop the talents of gifted or high-ability children. In common usage, it also broadly refers to intensive early education or training a child receives from a young age in a specific field such as music, sports, or academics.

A loud shout or cry, often expressing strong emotion such as alarm, urgency, or excitement. Distinguished from 歓声 (cheers of joy) by being more general and often carrying a sense of alarm or intensity.

glosses: medicine taken as needed (not on a regular schedule)
medicine taken as needed; on-demand medication
explanations: Medicine that is taken only when symptoms appear, rather than at regular intervals. Common examples include pain relievers, anti-anxiety medication, and fever reducers. The term is widely used in medical and pharmacy contexts.
The formal act of sitting down in one's designated or assigned seat. Used in formal settings such as ceremonies, classrooms, meetings, and performances. The opposite of 起立 (standing up).
A goal or ambition that one holds in their heart and intends to achieve. Often used when stating plans or resolutions for the future, especially at the start of a new year, job, or role.
A wheeled platform used to transport heavy or bulky items. Common in warehouses, factories, moving operations, and retail stores.

Insurance that covers medical expenses. In Japan, enrollment in a public health insurance system is mandatory for all residents. The two main types are employee health insurance (社会保険) and National Health Insurance (国民健康保険).
The hours during which a store, restaurant, office, or other business is open to customers. Commonly displayed on signs and websites.

glosses: to coat; to sprinkle over; to cover with
explanations: To coat the surface of food with powder, flour, breadcrumbs, or other dry ingredients by tossing or rolling. Primarily a cooking term.
A small, typically ceramic cup used for drinking sake. Usually holds about 30-50 ml. A staple item at izakaya and traditional Japanese restaurants.
Deep sorrow or anguish, especially in response to loss, tragedy, or suffering. As a な-adjective, describes something that conveys or expresses such grief.

A structure built into a wall where a fire can be lit for warmth. While not common in typical Japanese homes, fireplaces appear in Western-style buildings, lodges, and are familiar through foreign movies and literature.

glosses: to crowd; to flock; to swarm
to crowd together; to flock; to swarm; to gather in groups
explanations: For animals or people to gather together in large numbers. When used about people, it can carry a slightly negative nuance of mindlessly clustering together.

glosses: hard to come by; rare; invaluable
hard to come by; rare; invaluable; precious
explanations: Describes something that is difficult to obtain or encounter, and therefore precious or valuable. Often used to express appreciation for rare opportunities or irreplaceable people.

glosses: reluctant; unwilling; not in the mood
reluctant; unwilling; not in the mood for
explanations: Expresses a lack of enthusiasm or willingness to do something. Literally 'one's spirit does not advance.' Used when one feels unenthusiastic about an activity without necessarily having a strong reason to refuse.

A company that engages in import/export and international trade. Japanese trading companies (especially 総合商社) are distinctive corporate entities that trade in a vast range of goods and invest globally.

glosses: Tokyo metropolitan area; greater Tokyo; capital region
explanations: The region centered on Tokyo, generally including the surrounding prefectures of Kanagawa, Saitama, Chiba, Ibaraki, Tochigi, Gunma, and Yamanashi. Home to approximately 36 million people.

glosses: drunk driving; driving under the influence
drunk driving; driving under the influence (DUI)
explanations: Operating a motor vehicle after consuming alcohol. A serious criminal offense in Japan, with penalties applying not only to the driver but also to those who provide alcohol to the driver or ride as passengers.

glosses: hitting the mark; direct hit; striking the target
explanations: Successfully hitting a target with a projectile, shot, or thrown object. Also used figuratively for predictions or guesses that turn out to be correct.
A level of spiciness between mild and hot. Commonly used to label the spice level of curry roux, instant noodles, and other food products in Japan.

glosses: pet cat; domestic cat (that has an owner)
explanations: A cat that is kept as a pet, as opposed to a stray or feral cat. Formed from 飼う (to keep/raise an animal) + 猫 (cat).

glosses: prompt decision; snap judgment; deciding on the spot
explanations: Making a decision immediately without deliberation. Can be positive (decisive) or negative (hasty) depending on context.
The very best quality or option among alternatives. More formal than 一番いい and often used in written or formal contexts.

Creating a copy that imitates the appearance of a genuine article. Often carries a negative connotation when referring to counterfeit goods, but can be neutral when referring to reproductions or replicas.
The act of replacing one thing with another, or exchanging items. The noun form of the verb 取り換える (to replace, to exchange).

glosses: releasing fish or animals into the wild; stocking
explanations: The practice of releasing fish, fry, or other aquatic creatures into rivers, lakes, or the sea. Often done for conservation, fishing industry purposes, or as part of environmental restoration.
The controlled release of water from a dam or reservoir.
Valuable possessions such as gold, jewels, and precious objects. Often associated with stories of hidden or buried treasure, historical artifacts, or pirate lore.
Describes something that is certain to occur as a natural or logical consequence. Implies that the outcome could not have been otherwise given the circumstances.
An action or plan taken in advance to prevent something undesirable from happening, such as disease, accidents, or problems.

glosses: making a fortune at a stroke; striking it rich
making a fortune at a stroke; striking it rich; getting rich quick
explanations: Gaining a large amount of money or wealth all at once through a single opportunity. A four-character idiom (四字熟語). Literally means 'grab a thousand gold pieces in one swoop.'

glosses: relying on others; dependence on others
relying on others; dependence on others; leaving things to others
salvation through Amida Buddha's power (Buddhist term)
explanations: In everyday usage, describes the attitude of depending on others to do things for you rather than making an effort yourself. Carries a negative connotation of laziness or lack of initiative.
The original Buddhist meaning: the belief in Pure Land Buddhism that salvation comes through the power (他力) and original vow (本願) of Amida Buddha, rather than through one's own efforts.
A situation, decision, or statement that changes direction multiple times. Often carries a negative nuance of inconsistency or unreliability.
Describes someone's appearance or manner that conveys pride or satisfaction. Formed from 誇らしい (proud) + the suffix ～げ (appearing to be, looking like).

glosses: landing a catch; unloading; sales revenue
landing a catch; unloading fish from a boat
explanations: The act of bringing caught fish or seafood from a fishing boat to the harbor. Also refers to the quantity or value of fish landed.
The total amount of money earned from sales, especially in retail or market contexts.

glosses: branch office; local office; field office; agency
explanations: A smaller satellite office of a larger organization, typically a government agency or company, set up in a different location to provide services closer to the local population.
A mistake in judgment, planning, or execution, especially one with significant consequences. More formal than ミス and implies a strategic or political error.
A fielding mistake in baseball that allows a batter or runner to advance. The official statistical term for an error in Japanese baseball.

glosses: shellfish gathering; clamming; digging for clams at low tide
explanations: A popular recreational activity in Japan, typically done in spring, where people gather clams and other shellfish on tidal flats during low tide.
A person authorized to act on behalf of another in legal, business, or official matters. Can refer to legal representatives, sports agents, or anyone acting with delegated authority.

glosses: cutting in two with one stroke; decisive action
cutting something in two with a single stroke; making a clean, decisive judgment
explanations: A four-character compound (四字熟語) describing the act of resolving something swiftly and decisively, like cutting through an object with one stroke of a sword. Often used with する to describe making a bold, unequivocal decision or dismissal.

glosses: splitting evenly; dividing in half; going halves
explanations: Dividing something, typically a cost or expense, equally between two parties. Very commonly used when splitting a bill or sharing expenses.

glosses: central pillar of a traditional Japanese house
explanations: The main structural pillar in a traditional Japanese building, typically the thickest and strongest column supporting the entire structure.
Figuratively, the person who is the main support of a family, organization, or team. The one everyone depends on.

glosses: urgent; immediate; prompt; as soon as possible
explanations: Describes something that needs to be done quickly and without delay. Often used in business and formal contexts to convey urgency.

glosses: to hum; to croon; to sing softly
to hum; to croon; to sing softly to oneself
explanations: To sing or hum a melody quietly, often unconsciously or absent-mindedly. Implies a casual, relaxed mood.

glosses: policy; measure; initiative; plan of action
explanations: A concrete plan or action taken by a government, organization, or company to address a problem or achieve a goal. More specific and action-oriented than 政策 (broad policy direction).

glosses: locked room; closed room; secret chamber
locked room; sealed room; closed room
explanations: A room that is sealed or locked from the inside, especially in the context of mystery fiction where a crime is committed in a seemingly impossible setting.
Used figuratively to describe decisions or discussions conducted in secret, without public scrutiny or transparency.

glosses: mandatory vehicle inspection; periodic car inspection
explanations: The legally required periodic safety inspection that all registered vehicles in Japan must undergo. New cars must pass their first inspection after three years, then every two years thereafter.
The act of officially taking away someone's property or possessions, usually as a penalty or by authority. Also used in everyday contexts like a teacher confiscating a phone.
A portable frame used for carrying a sick or injured person, typically carried by two people. Used in medical emergencies, sports injuries, and disaster response.
A silent signal conveyed through eye contact, used to communicate something secretly or discreetly to another person without speaking.

glosses: perception; sensation; awareness through the senses
explanations: The ability to perceive through the senses (sight, hearing, touch, taste, smell), or the act of perceiving something. Used in both everyday and scientific/medical contexts.

glosses: absence from a competition or event; withdrawal; sitting out
explanations: Used when someone who was expected to participate in a sporting event, competition, or performance is unable to attend, usually due to injury or illness.
An electric charge that builds up on the surface of objects, commonly experienced as a small shock when touching metal objects or other people, especially in dry winter weather.

glosses: auction; sale by auction; public sale
explanations: A public sale in which items are sold to the highest bidder. Used for both voluntary auctions and court-ordered forced sales of property.

glosses: dreamlike state; dreamy feeling; trance; ecstasy
explanations: A blissful, dreamlike state of mind where one feels as if they are in a dream. Used to describe being so happy, enchanted, or overwhelmed that reality feels unreal.
The act of keeping watch over something, or the person assigned to keep watch. Used in both literal security contexts and more casual situations.

glosses: suspicion of a crime; charge; accusation
explanations: Suspicion that someone has committed a crime, or the formal charge brought against them. A legal and journalistic term frequently seen in news reports.
The act of making corrections or adjustments to fix errors or improve accuracy. Used in technical, budgetary, and everyday contexts.

glosses: Honshu; the main island of Japan
explanations: The largest and most populous of Japan's four main islands, home to major cities including Tokyo, Osaka, Kyoto, and Nagoya. Located between Hokkaido to the north and Shikoku and Kyushu to the south.

glosses: shy person; easily embarrassed person; someone who gets flustered easily
explanations: A person who is easily embarrassed or gets flustered, especially when praised or put in the spotlight. Often used affectionately to describe this trait.

glosses: beginning of the month; first days of the month
explanations: The first few days of a calendar month. Commonly used in business contexts for deadlines, reports, and scheduling.
An onomatopoeic word describing the sound and appearance of liquid simmering or boiling in a pot. Suggests steady, continuous bubbling at moderate heat.

glosses: to be deeply impressed; to admire greatly
to be deeply impressed; to admire greatly; to be filled with admiration
explanations: To feel deep admiration or respect for someone's skill, effort, character, or achievement. A somewhat formal expression that conveys genuine, heartfelt admiration.

glosses: extraordinary; off the charts; far beyond normal; outrageous
explanations: Describes something so extreme that it goes beyond the normal scale or range. Can be used for both positive qualities (extraordinary talent) and negative ones (outrageously expensive).

glosses: rejuvenation; looking or feeling younger; renewal
explanations: The process of becoming or looking younger, or of being refreshed and renewed. Used for both physical appearance and for organizations or systems being revitalized.
A condition where blood accumulates in a part of the body, making it appear red. Most commonly used to describe bloodshot eyes, but can refer to any area with excessive blood flow.
A small, rounded amount of liquid, such as a raindrop, teardrop, or dewdrop. Evokes a poetic, somewhat literary image.

glosses: to awaken; to become alert; to be aroused
to awaken; to wake up; to become alert
to awaken to a talent or power; to be aroused
explanations: To wake from sleep or become sharply alert and aware. Also used figuratively for becoming aware of a truth or reality.
To discover or activate a hidden ability, potential, or awareness. Common in fiction and self-improvement contexts.
A person who tends and herds sheep. While not a common occupation in Japan, the word appears frequently in stories, fables, religious texts, and cultural references.
Describes something that is unclear, indistinct, or hard to see, as if obscured by mist or fog.
Describes a state of diminished consciousness where one's awareness is clouded, as when half-asleep, feverish, or exhausted.
An expression meaning that something will happen eventually regardless of timing. Implies inevitability — whether it happens early or late, the outcome is certain.

glosses: being buried; submergence; sinking into the ground
falling into obscurity; being overlooked; going unnoticed
explanations: The physical state of being buried or submerged under earth, sand, snow, or other material.
Used figuratively for talent, achievements, or individuals that are buried or overlooked, failing to receive proper recognition.
A telephone connected by a physical line to a fixed location, as opposed to a mobile phone. Increasingly uncommon in Japanese households but still used in business settings.

glosses: jumble; hodgepodge; mishmash; all mixed together
explanations: A state where different things are mixed together in a disorderly way. Often implies a chaotic or haphazard combination without clear organization.

glosses: a small number; a select few; a tiny minority
explanations: The amount that can be held in one hand when gripped. A physical quantity measurement.
Figuratively, a very small number of people or things out of a larger group. Emphasizes how few they are.

glosses: protracted war; long-drawn-out battle; long haul
explanations: A prolonged conflict, competition, or effort that extends over a long period. Used both for actual military conflicts and figuratively for any extended struggle or effort.
A line drawn or running horizontally. Used in drawing, writing, mathematics, and everyday descriptions.
Describes an abundant harvest or the state of being rich and productive. Used literally for agricultural abundance and figuratively for cultural or creative richness.
The youngest daughter in a family. Often carries connotations of being spoiled or pampered, as the baby of the family.
A form of gambling where numbered tickets are sold and winners are selected by drawing. Also refers to the ticket itself.
A newspaper edition published and delivered in the afternoon or evening, as opposed to the morning edition.
In a state of disorder where things are scattered about without organization.
A wide, well-traveled street that is the primary thoroughfare in an area, as opposed to back streets or side streets.
The act of supplying fuel to a vehicle, aircraft, or machine. Used with する to form a verb.

glosses: kun reading; reading kanji by native Japanese meaning; reading classical Chinese in Japanese word order
kun reading; reading a kanji using its native Japanese meaning; reading classical Chinese texts in Japanese word order
explanations: Reading kanji with the native Japanese word that matches the character's meaning, as opposed to the on'yomi (Sino-Japanese reading). Also refers to the practice of reading classical Chinese texts with Japanese word order.
The player who scores the most points or goals in a league or tournament. A title used primarily in team sports like soccer and basketball.

glosses: rookie of the year; best newcomer
explanations: An award given to the most outstanding first-year player or newcomer in a sport, league, or other competitive field.
A period of reduced economic activity, declining business, or financial hardship.
Used figuratively to describe a gloomy atmosphere, a lack of energy, or a depressing state of affairs.
A mathematical relationship where one quantity increases as another decreases at a proportional rate. Also used figuratively to describe opposing trends.
A person who is sent to run errands or do minor tasks for someone else. Often carries a negative nuance of being treated as a subordinate.
The act of going somewhere to carry out small tasks on behalf of someone else.
A tall structure or tower used to display advertisements, typically found in urban areas.
A person who serves as the public representative of an organization or cause, often implying they are being used mainly for promotional purposes.
An informal meeting or assembly where people come together to discuss matters. Has a traditional, community-oriented nuance.

glosses: idiom from a historical story; historical proverb
idiom derived from a historical story; proverb originating from classical Chinese or Japanese history
explanations: A fixed expression or saying that originated from a specific historical episode or classical text, typically from ancient Chinese literature. Studied as part of Japanese language education.

glosses: writing on someone's behalf; scrivener's work
writing on someone's behalf; ghost-writing; scrivener's work
explanations: The act of writing documents, letters, or other text for someone who cannot or does not wish to write it themselves. Historically, a common service for those who were illiterate or unfamiliar with official forms.

glosses: the nations; the powers; countries of the world
explanations: A collective term for the nations of the world, especially in the context of international relations or diplomacy. Often implies major or influential countries.
Making one's own decision about one's fate or actions without external interference.
A euphemistic term for suicide, particularly used in historical or military contexts to describe taking one's own life rather than surrendering.

glosses: covered in dirt; muddy; caked with soil
explanations: The state of being covered or smeared with dirt or soil, typically from physical activity outdoors.

glosses: land sold in lots; subdivided land
land sold in lots; subdivided land for sale
explanations: A tract of land that has been divided into individual lots and sold to buyers, typically for building houses. A key concept in Japanese residential real estate.

glosses: at most; at the most; no more than
explanations: Sets an upper limit on a quantity or degree. Indicates the maximum possible amount.

glosses: both sexes; both male and female
hermaphroditic; having both male and female characteristics
explanations: Refers to both the male and female sex, used in formal, legal, or scientific contexts.
In biology, describes an organism that has both male and female reproductive organs.
A placeholder pronoun used when referring to unspecified people or when listing names without specifying who exactly. Used like 'so-and-so' or 'Mr./Ms. X' in English.
The act of applying oil to machinery, hinges, chains, or other mechanical parts for maintenance and smooth operation.
In Christianity, the third person of the Trinity, together with the Father and the Son. A central concept in Christian theology.

glosses: leisure; having time to spare; being at leisure
explanations: The state of having free time and not being occupied with work. Often implies wealth or social status that allows for a leisured lifestyle.

glosses: swarm of mosquitoes; column of gnats
explanations: A swirling column of small flying insects, typically midges or mosquitoes, that cluster together in the air. Named because the swarm resembles a pillar.

glosses: large number of people; many people
large number of people; many people; large group
explanations: A noun referring to a large group of people, often used when discussing group activities, seating capacity, or crowd management.
A flat surface used for playing board games such as go, shogi, or chess.
A flat, broad object. Used in compounds to refer to various flat objects including trays, discs, and platforms.

glosses: two rounds; two sizes (bigger/smaller); 24 years apart in the zodiac
two sizes (bigger or smaller); much larger/smaller
two cycles of the zodiac; 24 years apart
explanations: Used to describe a noticeable difference in size, typically saying something is two sizes bigger or smaller than expected or than something else.
In the Chinese zodiac system, one cycle is 12 years. Two cycles means a 24-year age difference.
A formal conjunction indicating that what follows is a logical result or conclusion of what precedes. Used primarily in written and formal contexts.

glosses: the likes of; someone/something as insignificant as
explanations: A literary and formal expression meaning 'like' or 'resembling,' used to draw comparisons. Modifies the following noun.
Used dismissively to belittle someone or something, implying they are unworthy of consideration.

glosses: behind the scenes; in secret; covertly
explanations: Doing something out of public view or without others knowing. Often implies hidden or underhanded actions.

glosses: spread of fire from an adjacent building; being burned by a neighboring fire
spread of fire from an adjacent building; damage from a neighboring fire
explanations: Fire damage suffered when a fire that started in a nearby building spreads to one's own property. An important concept in Japanese fire insurance and urban fire prevention.
An academic discipline encompassing the study of the languages, history, cultures, philosophies, and religions of East and Southeast Asia.

glosses: making a living; livelihood; scraping by
explanations: A literary term for earning just enough to survive. Literally 'pasting the mouth shut' — having just enough food to eat. Often implies a meager or modest existence.

glosses: must be; there is no doubt that; certainly
explanations: Expresses strong conviction or certainty about something. Attaches to verbs (plain form), adjectives, and nouns (+に). More formal than ～に決まっている and softer than ～はずだ.
Describes someone or something that looks impressive, attractive, or admirable. Can refer to physical appearance, behavior, or style. Very common in spoken Japanese.

glosses: ashamed; embarrassed; unable to face someone
explanations: Expresses deep shame or embarrassment, especially when one feels unable to face others due to a failure or mistake. Often used as an apology when one has let someone down.

glosses: to make a mistake in writing
to make a mistake in writing; to write incorrectly; to botch writing
explanations: To fail at writing something correctly, resulting in an error. Often used for handwritten documents, addressing envelopes, or calligraphy. The ～損じる pattern means 'to fail at doing ~'.

glosses: to twist and turn; to wind; to meander
to twist and turn; to wind; to meander; to zigzag
explanations: Describes a road, river, or path that bends repeatedly. A compound of 曲がる (to bend) and くねる (to twist), emphasizing continuous winding movement.
Describes something that is unclean or unkempt in an understated, casual way. The 小～ prefix softens the directness of 汚い, but the word still carries a negative nuance.

glosses: to beat down; to thrash; to pummel
explanations: To strike someone repeatedly and violently, knocking them down. Can also be used figuratively to mean thoroughly defeating someone in an argument, competition, or debate.
The physical sensation of being tickled or being sensitive to touch in a way that makes one want to squirm or laugh.
A figurative sense describing the uncomfortable, squirming feeling when receiving excessive praise or flattery.
Describes a person who tends not to trust others or who is inclined to doubt what they are told. Formed from 疑い (doubt) + 深い (deep).
A position that is across and to one side — not directly opposite but at an angle. Commonly used to describe locations of buildings, seats, or rooms relative to a reference point.
Describes a person or situation where things turn out favorably by chance. A common everyday expression using 運 (luck) + が + 良い (good).

glosses: to maneuver; to act shrewdly; to manage skillfully
to move about; to go around (a place)
explanations: To conduct oneself cleverly in a social or political situation, navigating around people and obstacles to achieve one's goals.
To move from place to place, especially as part of an investigation, search, or official duty.

glosses: to run away; to run off
to run away; to run off; to dash away
explanations: To leave a place quickly by running. A compound of 走る (to run) and 去る (to leave), emphasizing both the speed and the departure.

glosses: to start moving; to get going
to start moving; to begin to move; to get into motion
explanations: To begin moving after being still. Used for physical objects, vehicles, and figuratively for projects, plans, or situations that begin to progress.
A person with the ability to judge the quality or authenticity of things — especially art, antiques, food, or other specialized items. Also refers to the ability itself.

glosses: one's circumstances; one's lot in life
one's circumstances; one's fate; one's personal history
explanations: Refers to a person's life situation, personal background, or the circumstances they find themselves in. Often carries a nuance of hardship or sympathy.

Describes a person who tends to argue using logic and reasoning in an excessive or annoying way. Carries a negative connotation — implying the person is difficult to deal with because they always insist on logical explanations.

glosses: to rehabilitate; to turn over a new leaf
to rehabilitate; to reform; to turn over a new leaf
explanations: To change one's ways and start living a proper life, especially after criminal behavior, addiction, or a troubled past. Often used in legal and social welfare contexts.

glosses: to strip away; to pare down
to shave off; to pare away; to strip away
explanations: To remove something by shaving or cutting at an angle. Literally used for food preparation (shaving off thin slices), and figuratively for removing excess or unnecessary elements to achieve simplicity or efficiency.

glosses: to purr; to smack one's lips
to smack one's lips; to lick one's lips in anticipation
explanations: Describes the sound a cat makes when content, vibrating its throat to produce a rumbling purr.
To make sounds of eager anticipation, especially when seeing or thinking about delicious food.

glosses: to speak one's true feelings; to reveal one's real thoughts; to let one's true feelings slip out
explanations: To express what one truly thinks or feels, often after holding back. Implies that the true feelings were previously hidden behind a polite or official front (建前).

glosses: to start sliding; to get off to a start
to start sliding; to begin to slip
to get off to a start; to launch; to get underway
explanations: To begin sliding or slipping on a surface. Used for physical sliding motion.
Figuratively, to begin a new venture, season, or period. Often used with adjectives like 好調 (strong) or 順調 (smooth) to describe how something has started.

glosses: to roll up; to turn up; to flip up
explanations: To fold or push something upward, such as rolling up sleeves, turning up a skirt hem, or flipping up a cover. Combines めくる (to flip/turn) with 上げる (upward).

glosses: chewy; firm; having a good bite; al dente
explanations: Describes noodles, mochi, or other starchy foods that have a pleasantly firm, springy texture — not soft or mushy. A desirable quality in Japanese noodle culture.

glosses: to issue; to grant; to deliver (an official document)
explanations: To officially issue or grant a document such as a passport, visa, certificate, or permit. Used in formal and administrative contexts.

glosses: to liven up the atmosphere; to energize the mood; to get things going
explanations: To make a gathering, party, or event more exciting and fun through one's actions, words, or entertainment. A socially valued skill in Japanese group settings.
With a negative predicate, means that no person performs or is affected by the action. The negative verb is required.
With an affirmative predicate, means all people or any person. Often appears as 誰もが.
In a way that makes little or no noise. Used as a command to tell someone to be quiet, or to describe actions done without making sound.
In a calm, undisturbed manner. Describes doing something without haste, excitement, or agitation.

glosses: varied; full of variety; rich in change; diverse
explanations: Describes something that has abundant variation or diversity. Used for landscapes, climates, experiences, content, and other things characterized by richness and variety.

glosses: to teach and guide; to mentor
to teach and guide; to mentor; to lead and instruct
explanations: To both teach knowledge and guide someone in the right direction. Implies a deeper, more personal form of education than simply teaching facts. Often used for mentoring, parenting, and spiritual guidance.
A rough, rude way to say 'who' or 'which one,' referring to a person. Used when angry, frustrated, or speaking very casually among close friends. Should not be used in polite company.

glosses: to turn pages; to leaf through
to turn pages; to leaf through; to flip through
explanations: To turn the pages of a book, magazine, or document. The verb 繰る means to turn or draw something through one's hands, giving a sense of moving through pages one by one.

glosses: sociable; good at keeping company; willing to go along with others
explanations: Describes someone who readily joins social activities, accepts invitations, and is easy to spend time with. Highly valued in Japanese workplace and social culture.

glosses: to cool down; to dampen enthusiasm
to cool something down; to let the heat dissipate
to dampen enthusiasm; to pour cold water on; to cool someone's passion
explanations: To reduce the temperature of something, such as food, a fever, or a heated situation.
To reduce or extinguish someone's excitement, interest, or enthusiasm. Often used when something ruins the mood or kills motivation.

glosses: to involve danger; to be fraught with risk
to involve danger; to be fraught with risk; to carry risk within
explanations: To contain inherent danger or risk within something. The verb 孕む literally means 'to be pregnant with,' giving the sense that danger lurks within and may emerge. Used in formal or written contexts.
Music from Western countries, especially pop, rock, and other popular genres from the English-speaking world. Used in contrast to {邦楽|ほうがく} (Japanese music).

glosses: living away from one's family for work
living away from one's family for work; solo work transfer
explanations: When an employee is transferred to a distant workplace and moves there alone, leaving their family behind. A common phenomenon in Japanese corporate culture where employees are reassigned to branch offices in other cities.
A dramatic, rapid change in a situation, environment, or condition. Often used for large-scale societal, economic, or environmental shifts.

glosses: student preparing for entrance exams; exam candidate
explanations: A student who is studying for and planning to take entrance examinations, typically for high school or university. In Japan, this usually refers to students in their final year before the exam.
A walk-through attraction at amusement parks, festivals, or cultural events designed to scare visitors with ghostly or horror-themed elements.

glosses: decentralization; distribution of resources or risk
explanations: The act or state of things being spread out or scattered across a wide area or among multiple points.
Deliberately spreading out resources, functions, or risk across multiple locations or areas to reduce concentration.
The arrangement of people or things according to their rank, status, or importance. Commonly used in organizational, political, and social contexts.
The hard, pointed mouth part of a bird. Can also be written as {嘴|くちばし} in kanji, though the kana form is more common.

glosses: personnel change; staff transfer; organizational reshuffle
explanations: Changes in personnel assignments within an organization, including transfers, promotions, demotions, and departmental reassignments. A routine practice in Japanese companies, typically occurring in April.

glosses: mental fatigue; emotional exhaustion from social strain
explanations: Tiredness caused not by physical exertion but by mental or emotional effort, especially from being considerate of others, navigating social situations, or dealing with interpersonal tension.
A product that has been recently developed and released onto the market.
Items that come with or can be added to a main product, such as cables, adapters, cases, or other supplementary components.

glosses: sold separately; available as a separate purchase
explanations: Indicates that an item is not included with the main product and must be purchased independently.
The price at which something was bought, or the price a buyer is willing to pay. Contrasts with {売|う}り{値|ね} (selling price).
Providing hands-on assistance to people who need help with daily activities due to age, disability, or illness. Focuses on physical support such as helping with movement, eating, and bathing.
Taking a photo or filming a scene again because the first attempt was unsatisfactory.

glosses: board of directors; board of trustees; board meeting
explanations: The governing body of an organization, or a meeting of that body. Used for corporations, associations, condominiums, universities, and other organizations.
Describing something arranged or carried out according to a coherent system or logical structure, rather than being random or piecemeal.
Insurance that provides a monetary payout upon the policyholder's death or after a specified period. One of the most common types of insurance in Japan.
The major transformation of manufacturing and industry that began in Britain in the late 18th century. Also used more broadly to describe any large-scale industrial transformation.
A large retail store carrying a wide variety of goods organized into departments. The formal term for what is more casually called デパート.
Taking charge of and managing the practical aspects of running a business, household, or organization. Implies hands-on, day-to-day management.

glosses: ignorance; lack of knowledge or awareness
explanations: The state of not knowing about something, especially when one should. Can describe a lack of general knowledge or ignorance about a specific topic.
Acting or speaking without thinking carefully about the consequences. Describes careless, hasty behavior.

glosses: ardent desire; fervent wish; burning aspiration
explanations: An intense, passionate desire for something. Stronger than {希望|きぼう} (hope) or {願望|がんぼう} (wish), conveying urgency and emotional intensity.
The gate or entrance at the back of a building, school, temple, or other property. Contrasts with {正門|せいもん} (main gate) or {表門|おもてもん} (front gate).

glosses: coward; timid person; someone who is overly cautious
explanations: A person who is easily frightened, overly cautious, or lacks courage. Often used self-deprecatingly or to tease someone gently.
Having a timid, hesitant disposition. Describes someone who lacks assertiveness or is easily discouraged.
Forming a judgment or conclusion before having all the facts. Most commonly appears in the negative expression {予断|よだん}を{許|ゆる}さない (unpredictable; cannot be taken for granted).
The act of removing unwanted plants (weeds) from a garden, field, or other area. Can be done manually or with chemicals.
Using something again, either for its original purpose or a new one, rather than discarding it. A key concept in environmental sustainability.
Allowing some light to pass through but not fully transparent. Objects behind a translucent material can be vaguely seen but not clearly.

glosses: genuine; authentic; undeniable; the real deal
explanations: Emphasizes that something is absolutely genuine and beyond any doubt. A four-character compound ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}) used for strong emphasis.

glosses: the slightest bit; not at all (in negative expressions)
explanations: An extremely small piece or particle. Often used in cooking to describe finely chopped ingredients (みじん{切|ぎ}り).
Used with negative expressions to emphasize the complete absence of something — not even the tiniest amount.

glosses: affected area; diseased part; injured area
explanations: The specific part of the body that is injured, infected, or afflicted with disease. A medical term commonly used by doctors and in everyday health contexts.
Vinegar used in cooking. The polite prefix お makes this the standard everyday form; plain 酢 sounds blunt in conversation.
A small to medium-sized parrot, especially species commonly kept as pets in Japan such as budgerigars and cockatiels.
A system of government in which power is held by elected representatives and the people, as opposed to a monarchy. Most commonly encountered in the compound 共和国.
A state of physical or mental comfort and freedom from pain or hardship. Often used in formal or literary contexts.
An official endorsement on a passport permitting entry to or exit from a country. The formal Japanese term for what is commonly called ビザ in everyday speech.

glosses: junior and senior high school students
junior and senior high school students; middle and high schoolers
explanations: A collective term for students in both junior high school (中学生) and senior high school (高校生), roughly ages 12-18.
Fat stored in the body. Commonly discussed in health, fitness, and medical contexts, especially in relation to body fat percentage.
The annual income from an investment expressed as a percentage of its cost or current value. Used in finance for bonds, stocks, real estate, and other investments.
The outer surface or appearance of a building, vehicle, or object.
The outermost layer of packaging for a product, as opposed to the inner packaging.
A large or important church or religious building, especially one serving as the principal church of a diocese. Also used for Confucian temples in Japanese historical contexts.
A person who has prior experience in a particular field, activity, or situation. Frequently used in job listings and recruitment.
The activity of risking money or valuables on an uncertain outcome. A general term covering all forms of gambling.
The original painting, drawing, or artwork from which reproductions are made.
In anime production, the main drawings that define the start and end points of a movement, from which in-between frames are created.

glosses: haniwa; clay figure from ancient Japan
explanations: Unglazed terracotta figures that were placed on and around burial mounds (古墳) during the Kofun period (3rd-6th century). They depict humans, animals, houses, and other objects.
Vegetables that are in season during summer, such as tomatoes, cucumbers, eggplants, and bell peppers.

glosses: simmered and soaked dish; vegetables lightly simmered in broth
explanations: A Japanese cooking technique and dish in which ingredients (typically vegetables) are briefly simmered in a seasoned broth and then left to soak and absorb the flavors as they cool.

glosses: mixed blood; mixed race; mixed heritage
explanations: Having parents of different racial or ethnic backgrounds. Can refer to the state of being mixed-race or to a person of mixed heritage.
A traditional Japanese pipe with a small metal bowl and long bamboo stem, used for smoking finely shredded tobacco.

Slang for riding a train while only paying for the first and last portions of the journey, skipping the fare for the middle section. Named because a kiseru pipe has metal at both ends and bamboo in the middle — like a ticket that only covers the endpoints.
The process of making a solution or substance less concentrated by adding water or another solvent.

The pursuit of or devotion to beauty and sensuous pleasure, especially in art and literature. In modern Japanese pop culture, also refers to a genre featuring beautiful, often romantic depictions of male characters.
The traditional Japanese name for the first month of the year. Originally referred to the first month of the lunar calendar but is now associated with January in the modern calendar.
The vertical distance from the surface of a body of water to its bottom. Used in geography, navigation, diving, and pool measurements.
Describing someone, especially a child, who is quick-witted and sharp in understanding. Carries a positive, somewhat literary nuance.
A precious silvery-white metal used in jewelry, catalytic converters, and various industrial applications. The Japanese name literally means 'white gold'.

glosses: first half; first half of a fiscal year; first half of a business period
explanations: The first half of a fiscal year or accounting period. In Japan, where the fiscal year typically runs April to March, the first half is April to September.

glosses: second half; second half of a fiscal year; latter half of a business period
explanations: The second half of a fiscal year or accounting period. In Japan, where the fiscal year typically runs April to March, the second half is October to March.
The original meaning: a temporary, palliative measure that does not address the root cause of a problem.
The widely used modern meaning: acting in a petty, cowardly, or underhanded way to avoid direct confrontation. This usage arose from the negative connotation of avoiding proper solutions.

glosses: differentiation; distinction; setting apart from competitors
explanations: The process of distinguishing a product, service, or brand from others, especially in business and marketing contexts. Unlike 差別 (discrimination), this term has no negative connotation.
A lens or device that makes objects appear larger than they are. Includes handheld magnifying glasses, loupes, and digital magnification tools.
Having many functions or capabilities. Used as a modifier (多機能の/多機能な) to describe products, devices, or systems with multiple features.

glosses: day shift; daytime work; daytime duty
explanations: Working during the daytime hours, as opposed to night shifts. Common in workplaces that operate around the clock, such as hospitals, factories, and security.

glosses: mine tunnel; gallery; underground passage in a mine
explanations: A horizontal or inclined passage dug underground for mining or military purposes.

glosses: bookmaker; the house; gambling organizer; banker
explanations: The person or entity that organizes and runs a gambling operation, collecting bets and paying out winnings. By extension, can refer to the organizer or behind-the-scenes operator of any venture.

glosses: continued rise; further advance; continued gain
explanations: A continued upward movement, especially in stock prices, market indexes, or other numerical measures. Used primarily in financial and economic reporting.
A humble way to refer to one's own younger brother. An older, formal expression.
A subordinate or junior member in a hierarchical organization, especially in yakuza or gang contexts. Refers to someone who serves under a senior figure.
The act of dividing something into smaller, more manageable portions. Commonly used when packaging food or organizing items into smaller groups.

glosses: to wipe off; to wipe away
to wipe off; to wipe away; to clean by wiping
explanations: To remove dirt, liquid, or other substances from a surface by wiping with a cloth or tissue.

glosses: to drive back; to send away
to drive back; to send away; to chase off
explanations: To force someone to leave or go back, often by refusing them entry or driving them away.

glosses: to tease; to keep in suspense; to tantalize
explanations: To deliberately make someone wait or withhold something they want, causing them to feel impatient or frustrated.
A childbirth that proceeds without complications or difficulty. Often used as a wish or prayer for expectant mothers.

glosses: to empty; to make room; to vacate
to empty; to make room; to clear out
explanations: To remove the contents of something, making it empty or creating space.
To leave a position, seat, or place unoccupied. Also used for making time available.

glosses: to sign a contract; to conclude an agreement
explanations: To formally enter into a contractual agreement with another party. A standard business expression.

glosses: to become familiar with; to get accustomed to
to become familiar with; to grow accustomed to
explanations: To become thoroughly familiar with something through long exposure, developing a sense of comfort and attachment.
Indicates a rate or frequency of once per second, or something that occurs each second.

glosses: to underestimate; to take lightly; to not take seriously
explanations: To assume something is not a big deal and underestimate its importance or difficulty. Often used when someone's casual attitude leads to unexpected trouble.

glosses: to recommend; to endorse; to advocate
explanations: To formally recommend something as good or suitable. More formal than すすめる, often used in official or institutional contexts.

glosses: to come untied; to come undone
to come untied; to come undone; to unravel
explanations: For something that was tied, knotted, or bound to become loose and come apart on its own.
For tension, a stiff expression, or a guarded attitude to ease and become relaxed. Used figuratively.

glosses: to let pass; to wait out; to overdo
to let pass; to wait out
to overdo; to go too far
explanations: To let something pass by without acting, or to wait for something unpleasant to end.
To do something to excess, beyond what is appropriate.

glosses: to get a job; to take up a position
to get a job; to take up a position; to enter employment
explanations: To begin working at a job or to assume an occupational position.

glosses: to be frozen with fear; to have one's legs go weak
explanations: To become unable to move one's legs due to fear, anxiety, or shock. Describes the physical sensation of legs becoming stiff or weak from fright.

glosses: to stand frozen; to be rooted to the spot
explanations: To stand motionless, unable to move, due to fear, shock, or overwhelming emotion.
To disappear without a trace. Stronger and more emphatic than simply {消|き}える. Can also be used as a harsh command meaning 'get lost.'

glosses: to spare time; to find time for
to spare time; to make time for; to find time
explanations: To allocate or set aside time from a busy schedule for something. Implies that one is busy and making an effort to find time.

glosses: to assign; to allocate; to set aside for
to assign; to allocate; to set aside for a purpose
explanations: To designate something (money, time, resources, personnel) for a specific purpose or use.

glosses: always; habitually; on a daily basis
always; habitually; on a daily basis; at all times
explanations: Describes something done regularly as a matter of course, or a habitual state of affairs. Somewhat formal.

glosses: very small amount; negligible quantity; trifling
explanations: An extremely small quantity or degree. Used in formal or written contexts to describe something minimal.
Approaching or involving something from multiple perspectives or directions. Used in both analytical and business contexts.

glosses: to misunderstand; to misinterpret; to confuse
to put on the wrong shoes; to mix up footwear
to misunderstand; to misinterpret; to get wrong
explanations: To accidentally wear someone else's shoes or put shoes on the wrong feet.
To fundamentally misunderstand or misinterpret the meaning or purpose of something. Used figuratively.

glosses: to take shelter with; to stay with someone
to take shelter with; to stay with; to go to for refuge
explanations: To go to live with or take refuge with someone, typically a relative or trusted person, when one has nowhere else to go.

glosses: burnt to a crisp; completely charred
burnt to a crisp; completely charred; burnt black
explanations: The state of something being entirely burned and blackened. Used for food, buildings, or other objects.

glosses: to be in want of; to lack; to go without
explanations: To experience a shortage or lack of something necessary. Often used in the negative ({不自由|ふじゆう}しない) to mean having plenty.

glosses: communication power; ability to spread a message
communication power; ability to influence through messaging
explanations: The ability to effectively communicate and spread one's message or ideas, especially through media or social platforms.

glosses: adding water; water added while cooking
explanations: The act of adding cold water to a pot during cooking, especially when boiling noodles or beans, to prevent them from boiling over or to control the cooking process.

glosses: to oust; to dethrone; to drive out of a position
to oust; to dethrone; to topple from power
explanations: To force someone out of a position of power or authority. Often used in political and competitive contexts.

glosses: to share; to experience together; to partake in together
explanations: To share an experience, state, or activity with someone. Often used for sharing both joys and hardships.

glosses: to reveal one's true colors; to show one's real nature
explanations: For someone's hidden or disguised true nature, identity, or intentions to become apparent. Often implies the revealed truth is negative.

glosses: numerous; a great number of; many
explanations: A somewhat formal way to express that there are many of something. Functions as a modifier before nouns.

glosses: enshrinement; laying to rest; placing (a body or sacred object)
enshrinement; placing a sacred object or statue
laying out a body; keeping a body before burial
explanations: To place a Buddhist statue, sacred object, or religious artifact in a designated location for worship.
To place a deceased person's body in a designated area before funeral rites are performed.

glosses: rushing about busily; running around everywhere
rushing about busily; running around in all directions
explanations: To run about busily from place to place trying to get things done. A four-character idiom (yojijukugo) expressing energetic but hectic activity.

glosses: to fall into a predicament; to find oneself in a tight spot
to fall into a predicament; to find oneself in a desperate situation
explanations: To end up in a very difficult or desperate situation from which it is hard to escape.

glosses: to squeeze out; to extract; to milk
to squeeze out; to extract; to press out
explanations: To extract liquid or essence from something by applying pressure. Used for juicing fruit, pressing oil, extracting flavor, etc.
To draw milk from a cow or other animal.

glosses: to shrink; to shorten; to contract
to shrink; to contract; to become smaller
explanations: For something to decrease in size, length, or volume. Used for physical objects shrinking as well as abstract gaps or distances narrowing.

glosses: to see through; to detect; to expose
explanations: To perceive or discover a hidden truth, lie, trick, or disguise. Implies successfully uncovering something that was meant to be concealed.

glosses: to decay; to rot; to crumble
to decay; to rot; to crumble away
explanations: For something (typically wood, buildings, or organic matter) to deteriorate over time and fall apart. Often carries a literary or evocative tone. Can also be used figuratively for reputations or names fading into obscurity.

glosses: to pierce through; to carry through; to stick to
to carry through; to stick to; to persist in
explanations: To pass completely through something from one side to the other. Used for physical objects like arrows, bullets, or roads that run through an area.
To maintain a belief, principle, or course of action without wavering. Implies strong determination and consistency.

glosses: to separate; to keep apart; to place between
to separate; to set apart; to place a distance or barrier between
to treat differently; to be distant toward
explanations: To create physical or temporal distance between things. Often used with を to mark the barrier or space, and with に/にして to indicate time or space intervals.
To create emotional distance or show discrimination between people. Used when someone treats others unequally or keeps them at arm's length.

glosses: to tell; to narrate; to indicate
to tell; to narrate; to recount
to indicate; to show; to be evidence of
explanations: To tell a story or recount events. A somewhat literary or formal way of saying 'to tell.'
For facts, data, or circumstances to clearly show or demonstrate something. The subject is typically an inanimate thing (data, expression, results) that 'tells' or reveals a truth.

glosses: to be respectful; to humbly do
to respectfully do; to humbly offer
explanations: To perform an action with deep respect and humility. Used in very formal contexts such as official announcements, New Year's greetings, and formal letters. Almost always appears in the form 謹んで (respectfully).

glosses: to lower; to reduce; to bring down
explanations: To make something lower in level, degree, volume, or position. Used for physical height, sound volume, risk levels, standards, etc.

glosses: to tighten; to become firm; to be taut
to tighten; to become taut; to be firm
to be disciplined; to become focused; to shape up
explanations: For something to become tight or taut physically. Used for knots, screws, muscles, body, etc.
For an atmosphere, attitude, or person to become more serious, disciplined, or well-organized. Often used for situations where slack or looseness is corrected.

glosses: to see through; to foresee; to see all the way
to see through; to see all the way to the end
to foresee; to predict; to see through (a plan or intention)
explanations: To be able to see from one point to a distant point without obstruction. Used for long straight roads, clear views, etc.
To anticipate a future outcome or to perceive someone's hidden intentions or the true nature of a situation.
A person who is learning a skill or trade by watching and imitating experienced workers. Also used as a prefix meaning 'trainee' or 'apprentice.'
The act or period of learning by watching and imitating others in a workplace or craft.
The practice of predicting the future or reading a person's fate through various methods such as astrology, palm reading, tarot cards, etc. Also refers to the result of such a reading.
Going out to buy something or deliver something on behalf of someone else. Commonly used when a parent sends a child to the store, or when someone runs errands for the household.
The act of paying money. Often used in compounds to specify payment methods or timing.
A sweeping or brushing action to remove something. In Shinto contexts, refers to ritual purification to ward off evil spirits or impurity.
A state of having lost honor or reputation. Can function as a noun (a disgrace) or as a na-adjective (dishonorable, disgraceful).
The origin or means from which income or revenue is generated. Used for individuals, businesses, and organizations.

glosses: how filling food is; staying power of food
how filling food is; how long food keeps you full
explanations: The quality of food in terms of how long it keeps you feeling full after eating. Almost always used with がいい (filling, keeps you full) or がわるい (not filling, wears off quickly).
When a device, system, or mechanism operates incorrectly or activates when it should not. Commonly used for electronic equipment, sensors, alarms, and software.

glosses: local area; localized spot; specific part
explanations: A limited, specific area or part of a larger whole. Frequently used in medical and technical contexts to describe something affecting only a particular area rather than the whole.
The underground storage organ of certain plants, from which the plant grows. Includes true bulbs (like tulips and onions), tubers, corms, and rhizomes in general usage.

glosses: adult insect; imago; fully grown insect
explanations: An insect that has completed all stages of metamorphosis and reached its final, mature form. Contrasts with larva and pupa stages.
Something that conclusively determines an outcome. Originally from sports (a decisive hit or play), now widely used figuratively for the final factor that settles a matter.
A person who analyzes information, data, or situations as a profession or by disposition. Used for financial analysts, political analysts, and also in psychology for psychoanalysts.

glosses: inseparable bond; relationship that persists despite one's wishes
explanations: A relationship or connection that continues even though the people involved may not always want it to. Often used with a tone of resignation or wry humor about a long-standing tie that simply cannot be severed.

glosses: superficial; surface-level; outward; on the surface
explanations: Pertaining only to the surface or appearance, without touching on the deeper substance or reality. Often carries a negative connotation, suggesting something lacks depth.
To a striking or notable degree. The adverbial form of the i-adjective 著しい. Used in formal and written contexts to describe changes, differences, or developments that are clearly evident.

An intensifier used to emphasize the degree of an adjective or verb. Widely used in casual spoken Japanese. Originally the adverbial form of the adjective すごい, but now functions independently as an adverb.

glosses: many; much; a large number; mostly
many; much; a large number; the majority
mostly; for the most part; in many cases
explanations: A large number or amount of something. Functions as a noun, often followed by の (多くの = many) or used with が/は as a subject meaning 'most' or 'the majority.'
Used adverbially to indicate that something is true in the majority of cases.

glosses: strict; upright; serious; rigid in character
explanations: Firmly held, secured, or established. Used for things that are reliably solid, like a firm handshake, solid defense, or secure promise.
Describes a person or behavior that is strict, serious, principled, or inflexible. Can be positive (reliable, upright) or negative (stiff, uptight).

glosses: carrot and stick; reward and punishment
carrot and stick; reward and punishment; the soft and hard approach
explanations: A strategy of using both incentives (rewards) and deterrents (punishment) to achieve a desired outcome. Literally 'candy and whip.' Equivalent to the English expression 'carrot and stick.'

glosses: in an instant; instantaneously; in a flash
explanations: Happening in an extremely short amount of time, almost immediately. Emphasizes the speed at which something occurs.

glosses: cannibalism among animals; eating one's own kind
infighting; undermining allies; competing destructively within the same group
explanations: The behavior of animals eating members of their own species. A natural phenomenon observed in many animal species.
Used figuratively for situations where members of the same group, party, or industry harm each other through competition, rather than cooperating against external rivals.
Having graduated from a prestigious or high-level educational institution, typically a well-known university. In Japanese society, often specifically refers to having attended a top-tier university.

glosses: healthy body; state of good health
healthy body; state of good health; clean bill of health
explanations: A body that is in good physical health with no medical problems. Often used when describing someone who has been medically cleared or is in excellent physical condition.

glosses: section; segment; interval (of a route or range)
explanations: A defined portion of a route, track, or range, often used for transportation routes, distance measurements, or mathematical intervals.
Describes something exceptionally large in size, used for products, portions, and items that exceed the standard large size.
Sake produced by a local brewery, typically associated with a particular region and reflecting its water, rice, and brewing traditions. Valued for regional character and artisanal quality.
The act of detecting or identifying something, typically by a sensor, device, or system. Often used in technical contexts for automated detection of substances, signals, or conditions.
