It is commonly applied to daily routines, heartbeats and pulses, the arrangement of buildings or plantings, scientific observations, and grammatical conjugations. The opposite is {不規則|ふきそく} ('irregular').

glosses: wild; primal; untamed; rough-hewn (in personality or appearance)
having the rough, raw, unrefined quality of a wild animal or something that has not been domesticated; wild, untamed, primal, rough-hewn
explanations: Describes a person — or sometimes an animal — whose appearance, voice, manner, or attitude feels raw, instinctive, and uncivilized in an attractive or impressive way. Often applied to actors, athletes, and models whose looks give a sense of animal energy, sharp features, deep tans, or a muscular build. Unlike {野蛮|やばん} ('barbaric'), which is strongly negative, {野性的|やせいてき} typically has a positive or admiring tone — it praises the subject as charismatic, masculine, or primally attractive.

glosses: real number (math); actual number / actual count
in mathematics, any number that can be represented as a point on the number line, including rational numbers (such as 1/2 or -3) and irrational numbers (such as √2 and π); a real number
the actual number or actual count of people, things, or events, as opposed to an estimated, listed, or nominal figure; the real number, the actual count
explanations: The mathematical term for the full set of numbers on the continuous number line, excluding only the imaginary and complex numbers. The real numbers include integers, fractions, and non-terminating decimals such as π and √2. Introduced in Japanese high-school mathematics when the number system is extended beyond rationals. The set is written ℝ, which in Japanese textbooks is usually explained as 'the set of all {実数|じっすう}.'

In everyday usage, {実数|じっすう} refers to the real, actual count of something — how many people actually showed up, how many copies were actually sold, how many cases actually occurred — as opposed to planned, rounded, publicly announced, or rate-based figures. Often contrasted with percentages, ratios, or official estimates.

glosses: a desk; a piece of furniture used as a workspace, typically for writing, reading, or computer work in an office, school, or home study
a desk editor; a senior journalist at a newspaper or broadcaster who supervises reporters and edits their stories
explanations: The English loanword for a work desk. In Japanese it usually refers to a Western-style office or study desk used in workplaces and modern homes, as opposed to the traditional low writing table {机|つくえ}, although the two words overlap heavily in everyday speech. デスク is especially common in business contexts and product names.

A specialized journalism sense. The desk editor at a Japanese newspaper or TV news department is the mid-level editor who reviews articles, gives assignments, and oversees a group of reporters from a desk in the newsroom. The role is roughly equivalent to a city editor or section editor in English-language news organizations.

glosses: a flyer; a leaflet; a small printed advertisement, often for a sale, event, or local business, distributed by hand, mailed, or inserted in newspapers
explanations: The everyday word for a single-sheet printed advertisement. Japanese チラシ are most often associated with supermarket sale notices, real-estate listings, restaurant menus, and political or cultural event announcements. They are typically delivered to mailboxes (ポスティング), inserted into newspapers as {折|お}り{込|こ}みチラシ ('newspaper inserts'), or handed out on the street. The word is written in katakana for visibility, although the kanji {散|ち}らし (from the verb {散|ち}らす, 'to scatter') is the historical origin.

glosses: the area around the eyes; one's eyes (as a feature of facial expression)
the area around the eyes; the part of the face surrounding the eyes, including the eyelids, lashes, and skin near the corners of the eyes
explanations: Refers to the region of the face surrounding the eyes, rather than the eyeballs themselves. This is a useful word in beauty and skincare contexts (eye creams, makeup), in descriptions of facial features and expressions, and in everyday talk about tired eyes or wrinkles. It often carries an implicit sense of how someone looks, since the area around the eyes is one of the most expressive and noticeable parts of the face.

glosses: a drawing study, especially one done in pencil, charcoal, or another monochrome medium as practice for capturing form, proportion, light, and shadow
explanations: Borrowed from French 'dessin' rather than English 'drawing'. In Japanese, デッサン specifically refers to a study drawing made for art training — typically a black-and-white rendering of a still life, plaster bust, model, or human figure that focuses on accurate observation of shape, volume, and shading. It is the standard word in the Japanese art-school context for the foundational practice of drawing from life. デッサン can be used as a noun, and as a する-verb meaning 'to do a study drawing'.

glosses: earplugs; small soft inserts worn in the ear canal to block out noise or keep water out of the ears
explanations: The everyday Japanese word for earplugs of any kind: the foam, silicone, or wax inserts used to reduce noise while sleeping, studying, or working in loud environments, as well as the rubber or silicone plugs used by swimmers to keep water out of their ears. Like its English counterpart, {耳栓|みみせん} is generally used as a plural concept, even though Japanese makes no plural distinction. They are sold inexpensively in pharmacies, convenience stores, and 100-yen shops.

glosses: a break room; a lounge or rest area in a workplace, school, hospital, or public facility where people can sit, relax, eat, or take a break
explanations: Refers to a dedicated room or space for taking breaks, distinct from the main work, study, or activity area. {休憩室|きゅうけいしつ} can be found in offices, factories, hospitals, schools, museums, shopping centres, train stations, and highway service areas. In a corporate setting it usually means an employees-only break room with chairs, tables, vending machines, and possibly a microwave; in a public facility it usually means a free rest area open to all visitors.

glosses: bouquet (small bunch of flowers, especially as carried by a bride)
a bouquet; a small, decoratively arranged bunch of cut flowers, especially the type held by a bride at a wedding or given as a gift on a special occasion
explanations: Borrowed from French 'bouquet' (via European convention rather than English). In Japanese, ブーケ very strongly evokes the wedding context and is the standard word for the bridal bouquet, but it is also used more broadly for any small, hand-tied arrangement of flowers given as a present, used as a stage prop, or sold in flower shops. Larger arrangements in vases or baskets are usually called {花束|はなたば} or by other names rather than ブーケ.

glosses: toaster oven; small countertop oven (esp. for toasting bread and reheating food)
a small countertop electric oven with heating elements above and below, used for toasting bread, reheating leftovers, and baking small dishes
explanations: A wasei-eigo compound combining 'oven' and 'toaster'. Refers to the small box-shaped electric oven that is a standard kitchen appliance in nearly every Japanese household. It is used primarily for browning toast in the morning, but also for melting cheese on gratin, reheating fried foods to restore crispness, baking small pizzas, and cooking simple oven dishes. Unlike a Western 'toaster', it has an open interior space and a glass door, more like a small oven, but it is generally smaller and simpler than the larger {電子|でんし}{オーブンレンジ} (microwave-oven combo).

glosses: gluten-free; (of food, ingredients, or a diet) not containing gluten, the protein found in wheat, barley, and rye
explanations: The English-derived loanword for 'gluten-free'. It is used both as a noun and as an attributive modifier, often before another noun (e.g. グルテンフリーの{食事|しょくじ} 'a gluten-free meal', グルテンフリー{食品|しょくひん} 'gluten-free foods'). It can also be used predicatively, meaning that something 'is gluten-free'. In Japan it commonly refers to specialty foods made without wheat for people with celiac disease, wheat allergies, or those choosing the diet for health or fitness reasons.

glosses: to talk (someone) into; to persuade by clever talk; to deceive with words
to talk someone into accepting something through clever or specious reasoning; to persuade by words in a way that bypasses the listener's better judgement, often involving deception or manipulation
explanations: A compound verb meaning to use skilful talk to lead someone into agreeing with something, typically against their own interest or against what they would have decided if they thought it through. The action almost always carries a negative or critical nuance: the speaker is implied to be cunning or dishonest, and the listener is implied to have been outmanoeuvred or fooled. It is commonly used about salespeople, swindlers, or smooth talkers, but also more lightly about a clever child who 'talks their parent around'.

glosses: to wipe away; to dispel (doubts, fears, an impression); to remove completely
to wipe (something) away completely; to remove a stain, smudge, mark, or moisture from a surface so that no trace remains
to dispel; to wipe away (an impression, doubt, fear, suspicion, or sad memory); to make a feeling or perception disappear
explanations: The literal physical sense: to use a cloth, hand, or similar action to wipe something off a surface so thoroughly that nothing is left behind. The added {去|さ}る ('to leave, to be gone') intensifies the basic verb ぬぐう ('to wipe') and emphasises that the wiped substance is completely gone. Less common in modern speech than the figurative sense (sense 2).

The figurative and far more common sense. With abstract objects such as {不安|ふあん} ('anxiety'), {疑|うたが}い ('doubt'), {印象|いんしょう} ('impression'), {汚名|おめい} ('disgrace'), or {悲|かな}しみ ('sadness'), ぬぐい{去|さ}る means to remove the feeling or perception completely so that nothing of it remains. It is a literary, slightly formal verb common in journalism, essays, and speeches.

glosses: sweet and lovable; pretty in a delicate way; dainty (esp. of girls, flowers, small creatures)

(of a girl, a young woman, a small child, a flower, or a small animal) sweet and endearing in a delicate, fragile way that arouses tenderness and a wish to protect; lovely in a small, gentle, or unassuming manner
explanations: A literary adjective describing a particular kind of beauty: small, delicate, slightly fragile, and stirring the viewer's protective affection. It is most often applied to young girls or young women, to wildflowers and other small flowers, and occasionally to small animals like birds or kittens. Unlike きれい ('pretty, clean') or {美|うつく}しい ('beautiful'), {可憐|かれん} specifically combines an impression of physical daintiness with a sense of vulnerability or innocence. It is much more common in writing than in casual speech.

glosses: the Arctic Circle; the Arctic region
the Arctic Circle; the imaginary line of latitude at about 66°33′ north, marking the southern limit of the area where the sun does not set on at least one day a year
explanations: Refers to the parallel of latitude that defines the boundary of the Arctic. North of this line, there is at least one day per year on which the sun does not set (the midnight sun) and at least one on which it does not rise (polar night). The same word is also used loosely to mean the entire region inside that line — the high-latitude lands and seas of the far north, including parts of Russia, Canada, the United States (Alaska), Greenland, Iceland, and the Scandinavian countries.

glosses: mailing (a letter); posting (in a mailbox); dropping into a box

the act of mailing a letter or postcard by dropping it into a public mailbox or post-office collection box; the act of dropping a slip into a designated collection box (e.g. a comment box, raffle box, or election ballot box)
explanations: The standard formal word for the action of putting a letter, postcard, application form, or similar item into a collection box. Most often used about postal mail dropped into a {郵便|ゆうびん}ポスト (street mailbox), but it also covers ballot voting, prize-draw entries, and any context in which something is dropped into a labelled box. Used as a noun and as a する-verb ({投函|とうかん}する 'to mail, to post').

glosses: (one's) sense of ethics; moral sense; ethical values
a person's or group's sense of ethics; the personal values or moral standards by which someone judges right and wrong
explanations: Refers to a person's or group's internalized sense of what is morally right and wrong, especially as it influences their behaviour. The word focuses on the value system itself, not on a specific moral judgement, and is therefore often used in contexts that comment on the strength, weakness, or character of someone's morals (e.g. saying that a politician 'lacks ethics' or that a profession 'demands a strong sense of ethics'). Common in news commentary, social criticism, and discussions of professional ethics.

glosses: the lower lip; the lower of the two lips of the mouth
explanations: The straightforward word for the lower lip, used in anatomy, beauty/cosmetic descriptions, dental contexts, and in describing facial expressions. It contrasts with {上唇|うわくちびる}, the upper lip. In casual speech, the simple word {唇|くちびる} ('lips') is used unless it is necessary to distinguish between the two.

glosses: clothing made of light, breathable material designed to be worn in summer; the lighter version of a school or workplace uniform worn during the warm months
explanations: Refers to clothes intended to be worn in hot weather — usually thin, light-coloured, and short-sleeved. In a Japanese context, the word most often appears in two settings: (1) ordinary summer wardrobes that are taken out and put away with the seasons, and (2) the formal seasonal change of school and workplace uniforms. Japanese schools and many companies have a regulated date in May or June when employees and students switch to {夏服|なつふく}, and another date in autumn when they switch back to {冬服|ふゆふく}. This seasonal switch is called {衣替|ころもが}え.

glosses: a shortened form of a word, phrase, or expression; a contraction or abbreviation that is in common use as a substitute for the full version
explanations: A general grammatical/linguistic term for any shortened version of a longer word or expression. It covers English-style contractions like 'don't' for 'do not', Japanese colloquial contractions like 〜じゃない for 〜ではない, abbreviated names like スマホ for スマートフォン, and the various ways that nouns or technical terms get shortened in everyday speech. Common in language-learning materials, dictionaries, and grammar explanations.

glosses: window sash; window frame (esp. an aluminum sliding-window frame)
the metal (typically aluminum) frame holding the glass of a sliding window or door, or by extension the entire factory-made window unit; a window sash
explanations: Borrowed from English 'sash'. In Japanese, the word almost always refers to the aluminum frame of a sliding window — by far the most common type of window in Japanese houses and apartments — and by extension to the whole prefabricated window unit (frame plus glass plus rails). Wooden or steel frames are sometimes also called サッシ but the strong default is aluminum. The phrase アルミサッシ ('aluminum sash') is so closely associated with the basic word that the two are often used interchangeably.

glosses: curl (in the hair); curl (of an object); to curl
a curl, especially in the hair; a section of hair shaped into a wave or ring; a curling treatment that gives the hair such waves
explanations: Borrowed from English 'curl'. The most common everyday use is in beauty contexts: hair curls created by a curling iron, perm, or hair rollers, ranging from loose waves to tight ringlets. The word can refer to a single curl, the overall curly look of someone's hair, or the technique of curling. Used both as a plain noun and as a する-verb (カールする 'to curl'), and is also frequently combined with アイロン (curling iron) and similar terms.

glosses: well...; let me see...; um...; uh...

a hesitation marker used to fill the silence while the speaker is thinking, recalling something, or searching for the right word; the rough Japanese equivalent of English 'well...', 'let me see...', or 'um...'
explanations: One of the most common Japanese filler words. Speakers use ええと at the start or in the middle of an utterance when they need a moment to think — to recall a fact, choose a word, or organize their thoughts. It is a polite, neutral filler that does not carry any particular emotional colour, and is appropriate in almost any situation, from chatting with friends to answering a teacher's question. Often spelled with one or two long vowels (ええと, えーと, えっと); the spoken form can range from a brief 'eto' to a drawn-out 'eee...to' depending on how long the speaker pauses.

glosses: coffee cup; coffee mug; (in an amusement park) a teacup ride
a coffee cup; a small cup, usually with a saucer, designed for drinking coffee
a teacup ride; a spinning amusement-park ride in which riders sit inside large, saucer-mounted cups and spin them by turning a wheel in the centre
explanations: Refers to the standard small ceramic cup with a handle that is used for serving coffee, typically together with a matching saucer. Japanese speakers tend to use コーヒーカップ specifically for the formal, smaller, saucer-paired type used for hot black coffee or espresso, in contrast to the larger handled mug (マグカップ) used for casual everyday drinks.

By visual analogy, コーヒーカップ also refers to the classic amusement-park ride in which riders sit in large oversized 'coffee cups' that rotate around a centre pivot. The same ride is called 'teacups' in English-speaking parks; in Japanese, the loanword 'coffee cup' is used instead. It is a staple ride at theme parks like Disneyland, Sanrio Puroland, and family amusement parks across Japan.

glosses: a brass band; a musical ensemble made up mainly of brass and percussion (and often woodwind) instruments, especially the wind ensembles common in Japanese schools
explanations: Borrowed from English. In strict music terminology, ブラスバンド refers to an ensemble of brass instruments only, but in everyday Japanese it commonly covers school and amateur wind ensembles that include flutes, clarinets, saxophones, and other woodwinds in addition to trumpets, trombones, and percussion. School ブラスバンド clubs ({吹奏楽部|すいそうがくぶ}) are one of the most popular and visible extracurricular activities in Japanese junior high and high schools, performing at sports events, school festivals, and competitions.

headword: ダイレクトメッセージ
glosses: direct message; DM (a private message sent on social media)
a direct message; a private message sent on a social-media or messaging service from one user to another, away from public posts or comment threads
explanations: Borrowed from English. Refers to the private one-to-one (or small-group) message function built into social media platforms such as Twitter (X), Instagram, TikTok, LINE, and Facebook. It is used in contrast to public posts and public replies — when someone is asked to 'send a DM' (DMください or DMで{連絡|れんらく}してください), it means they should write a message that only the recipient can see. The shortened form DM (ディーエム) is at least as common as the full term in everyday speech.

glosses: lowering a fever; bringing down a fever; antipyresis
the lowering of a fever by medication or other means; the action of bringing a feverishly raised body temperature back down toward normal
explanations: A medical/health term referring specifically to the act of reducing a fever, not the natural disappearance of fever as a person recovers. Most often used in the context of fever-reducing medication ({解熱|げねつ}{剤|ざい} or {解熱|げねつ}{薬|やく}), in pediatric and home medicine, and on packaging for over-the-counter cold and flu drugs. Used both as a plain noun and as a する-verb ({解熱|げねつ}する 'to bring down a fever / for a fever to come down').

glosses: preheating; warming up (an oven, an engine, etc.) in advance
the act of heating an oven, machine, or engine in advance to a desired temperature before use; preheating
explanations: Refers to warming something up to its working temperature before the actual operation begins. The most familiar use is for ovens in baking and cooking — Japanese recipes typically include the instruction オーブンを 200 {度|ど}に{予熱|よねつ}しておく ('preheat the oven to 200°C'). The word also covers preheating in industrial contexts (engines, kilns, manufacturing equipment) and figuratively in expressions about warming up the body before exercise. Used as a noun and as a する-verb ({予熱|よねつ}する 'to preheat').

glosses: decoration; an ornamental addition designed to make something look more festive, attractive, or special; the act of adding such decorations
explanations: Borrowed from English 'decoration'. Used in Japanese for any added ornamental element placed on cakes, rooms, shop windows, walls, holiday displays, gifts, or personal possessions. Also used as a する-verb (デコレーションする 'to decorate'). It is especially associated with food (デコレーションケーキ 'decorated cake') and with the Japanese subculture of decorating phones, nails, and gadgets with rhinestones and stickers (デコ).

glosses: a portrait painting; a painted (occasionally drawn or printed) representation of a specific person, usually showing the face and upper body, intended to capture the appearance and character of the subject
explanations: Refers to a fine-art portrait — typically a painting in oils, watercolour, or another traditional medium. The Japanese word emphasises the painted/drawn nature of the work; for photographic portraits, {肖像写真|しょうぞうしゃしん} or simply {写真|しゃしん} is used. The term is the standard one in art history, museum labels, and historical writing about kings, samurai, religious figures, and historical leaders.

glosses: a blouson; a short jacket that is loose and bloused around the upper body but gathered tightly at the waist with a band or elastic, including styles such as bomber jackets, MA-1s, and similar casual outerwear
explanations: Borrowed from French 'blouson'. In Japanese fashion vocabulary, ブルゾン denotes a category of short jackets characterised by a fitted waist (with elastic or a knit band) and a loose, slightly puffed body. It includes bomber jackets, MA-1 military jackets, sukajan-style jackets, and many similar casual jackets, but excludes longer coats, suit jackets, blazers, and tailored cardigans. ブルゾン is the standard everyday word in Japanese clothing stores and fashion magazines for this jacket type.

glosses: a leading question; a question framed in a way that suggests or implies the answer the questioner wants, often used to manipulate the respondent into agreeing with or revealing something
explanations: Originally a legal term referring to a type of question that is generally not allowed during direct examination of a witness because it puts words in the witness's mouth. In everyday Japanese the word is used much more broadly: about journalists asking leading questions of politicians, parents trying to extract a confession from a child, or even friends fishing for a particular response in conversation. The word almost always carries a negative or wary nuance — a 誘導尋問 is something to watch out for or to call out.
A collective term for edible marine and freshwater creatures including fish, shellfish, crustaceans, squid, octopus, and other aquatic organisms used as food.
A keigo (honorific language) term meaning to receive something, used to show deep respect toward the giver. It lowers oneself to elevate the person who gave or sent the item.
Refers to a range of different things or circumstances. A formal word used primarily in written Japanese to indicate multiple factors or considerations.

glosses: bad weather; inclement weather; adverse weather conditions
explanations: A formal compound noun used to describe unfavorable weather conditions that interfere with planned events, travel, or outdoor activities.

glosses: food stall village; cluster of food stalls
food stall village; cluster of food stalls; hawker center
explanations: A designated area where multiple food stalls or small eateries are gathered together, typically in an outdoor or semi-outdoor setting. Common in cities across Japan, especially in entertainment districts.
The act of protecting an important person or location from danger, typically carried out by police, security personnel, or bodyguards.
Describes branches that hang downward in a graceful, drooping manner. Most commonly used as a prefix for tree varieties whose branches grow downward, especially cherry and willow trees.
A Chinese-origin dish of eggplant stir-fried with ground meat in a spicy bean paste sauce. A popular adaptation of mapo tofu, substituting eggplant for tofu.
The electrical cable that connects an appliance or device to a power outlet. An everyday item found on most electronic devices.
Chicken meat that has been finely chopped or passed through a grinder. A common ingredient in Japanese cooking, especially for meatballs, dumplings, and simmered dishes.
Pork meat that has been finely chopped or passed through a grinder. One of the most commonly used ground meats in Japanese and East Asian cooking.
A seasoned mixture of ground meat and other ingredients, prepared as a base or filling for dishes such as dumplings, meatballs, hamburger steaks, and stuffed vegetables.
Sesame seeds that have been dry-roasted to bring out their nutty flavor and aroma. A ubiquitous condiment and garnish in Japanese cooking.

glosses: used tea leaves; spent tea leaves
explanations: Tea leaves that remain after brewing tea. In Japan, these are sometimes repurposed for cleaning, deodorizing, or as cooking ingredients rather than simply being discarded.

glosses: written instructions; directive document; instruction sheet
explanations: A document containing specific instructions or directions for performing a task, following a procedure, or complying with requirements. Used in workplaces, medical settings, and official contexts.
A mechanical device for transporting people or goods between floors of a building. A formal or technical term for what is commonly called エレベーター in everyday speech.

The polite form of {餅|もち} (mochi), a traditional Japanese food made from glutinous rice that has been pounded into a sticky, chewy mass. A staple of New Year celebrations and used in many traditional sweets and dishes.
Underwater diving using a self-contained underwater breathing apparatus (SCUBA). In Japanese, the word refers both to the equipment and the activity itself.

glosses: semi-voiced sound; p-sounds in Japanese kana
explanations: The set of Japanese syllables beginning with the 'p' sound (ぱ{行|ぎょう}), indicated by a small circle (゜) added to the は{行|ぎょう} kana. The five semi-voiced sounds are: ぱ (pa), ぴ (pi), ぷ (pu), ぺ (pe), ぽ (po).
Sesame seeds with a pale cream to white hull. The most commonly used variety of sesame in Japanese cooking, with a mild, delicate flavor.
Sesame seeds with a dark black hull, known for their strong nutty flavor and aroma. Widely used in Japanese sweets, as a garnish, and in health-conscious cooking.

glosses: arrowroot starch; kudzu starch; kuzu powder
explanations: A fine white starch extracted from the root of the kudzu plant ({葛|くず}). Used as a thickener in Japanese cooking and as the base for traditional sweets. Prized for the smooth, glossy texture it gives to sauces and desserts.
The act of planting crops in a field, or the plan for what crops to plant in which fields. Used in agriculture and news reporting about farming.

glosses: voiceless sound; clear sound (in Japanese phonetics)
voiceless sound; clear sound; unvoiced kana
explanations: In Japanese phonetics, the basic, unmarked kana syllables that have no voicing diacritic. Includes the sounds represented by か, さ, た, は, and other rows written without dakuten (゛) or handakuten (゜).

glosses: point of contention; issue in dispute
point of contention; issue in dispute; contested point
explanations: A specific issue or topic that is the focus of a debate, disagreement, or legal dispute. Often used in formal discussion, academic writing, and legal contexts.

glosses: to season; to flavor; to add seasoning
to season; to flavor; to add seasoning to food
explanations: To add salt, soy sauce, spices, or other seasonings to food during cooking to enhance or adjust the taste.
The state or degree of feeling physically tired or worn out.
The degree to which something is mentally or emotionally taxing or difficult to endure.
A disease or medical condition that persists over a long period of time, as opposed to an acute condition. Includes conditions such as diabetes, hypertension, and asthma.

glosses: column; vertical row; things arranged in a line from front to back
explanations: A line of people, vehicles, or objects arranged one behind the other, extending in depth rather than width. Also used for vertical columns in tables and charts.

glosses: straining; sieving; passing through a sieve
straining; sieving; passing food through a fine mesh
explanations: A cooking technique in which food is pressed through a fine mesh sieve to create a smooth, uniform texture. Used to make purees, smooth sauces, and strained soups.

glosses: sacred object of worship enshrined in a Shinto shrine
sacred object; object of worship; divine body
explanations: A physical object enshrined in a Shinto shrine that is believed to house or represent a deity (kami). Common examples include mirrors, swords, jewels, stones, and natural objects such as mountains or trees.

glosses: contracted sound; palatalized syllable (e.g., きゃ, しゅ, ちょ)
explanations: In Japanese phonetics, a syllable formed by combining a consonant-i kana (き, し, ち, に, ひ, み, り, ぎ, じ, び, ぴ) with a small ya, yu, or yo (ゃ, ゅ, ょ) to produce a single palatalized syllable. Examples: きゃ (kya), しゅ (shu), ちょ (cho).

glosses: nasal sound; the syllabic 'n' (ん) in Japanese
nasal sound; the moraic nasal 'n' (ん/ン)
explanations: In Japanese phonetics, the nasal syllable ん (hiragana) or ン (katakana), which is the only kana that represents a consonant without an accompanying vowel. Its actual pronunciation varies depending on the sound that follows it.

glosses: drinker; sake lover; person who prefers alcohol over sweet things
drinker; sake lover; person who favors alcohol
explanations: A person who enjoys drinking alcohol, especially sake. Contrasted with people who prefer sweets. Used in a lighthearted or self-deprecating way.

glosses: one's own book; one's own written work
one's own book; one's own publication; a book one has written
explanations: A book or written work authored by the person being discussed. Used when referring to someone's own published writing, especially in literary, academic, or media contexts.

glosses: set temperature; target temperature; thermostat setting
explanations: The temperature that a device such as an air conditioner, heater, oven, or refrigerator is set to maintain or reach.
A room designed to be used for various activities rather than a single fixed purpose. Found in public facilities, schools, community centers, and commercial buildings.

glosses: merit pay; ability-based pay; performance-based salary
explanations: A compensation system in which an employee's pay is determined by their skills, abilities, or performance rather than by seniority or a fixed scale.

glosses: operating revenue; business income; revenue from core operations
explanations: The income a company earns from its main business activities, excluding non-operating income such as investment gains or interest. A key figure in financial statements and business reporting.

glosses: busy period; busy season; peak period
busy period; busy season; peak season
explanations: A time of year or period when work, business, or activity is particularly intense and demanding.

glosses: charm; taste; artistic sentiment; refined atmosphere
charm; taste; refined atmosphere; artistic sentiment
explanations: An elegant or emotionally evocative quality that appeals to one's aesthetic sensibility. Used to describe the subtle beauty, mood, or emotional resonance of a scene, object, or experience.

glosses: battle formation; military formation; tactical arrangement
formation; lineup; arrangement of players or team members
explanations: The arrangement or positioning of troops or forces for battle. Used in historical and military contexts.
By extension, the tactical arrangement of players in sports or the positioning of participants in games. Common in gaming and sports contexts.

glosses: headquarters; main camp; base of operations
explanations: The central command post or main base from which operations are directed. Originally a military term for the commander's main camp, now also used figuratively for any central base of activity.

glosses: business rival; trade competitor; commercial rival
explanations: A person or business that competes directly in the same trade or market. Carries a sense of personal rivalry, not just impersonal market competition.

glosses: the entire sky; the whole sky; across the sky
the entire sky; the whole sky; all across the sky
explanations: Describes the sky in its entirety, typically when it is completely covered or filled by something — clouds, stars, a sunset glow, etc.

glosses: to one-up; to assert dominance; to act superior
to one-up; to assert dominance; to act superior over someone
explanations: To demonstrate or assert one's superiority over another person, often in a boastful or competitive way. Derived from the martial arts concept of taking the 'mount' position (sitting on top of a downed opponent).

glosses: oily skin; oily constitution; greasy complexion
explanations: A skin type characterized by excessive sebum (oil) production, resulting in a shiny or greasy appearance. Used in skincare and cosmetics contexts.

glosses: fruit vegetable; vegetable grown for its fruit (e.g., tomato, cucumber, eggplant)
fruit vegetable; vegetable cultivated for its fruit
explanations: A category of vegetables where the edible portion is the fruit of the plant, as opposed to the leaves, roots, or stems. Examples include tomatoes, cucumbers, eggplants, peppers, and squash.
A general, somewhat casual term for any leafy green vegetable such as spinach, komatsuna, or bok choy. Used in everyday cooking and conversation rather than in formal or scientific contexts.

A paved or maintained path designed for walking, typically found in parks, along rivers, or through scenic areas. Unlike ordinary sidewalks, a {遊歩道|ゆうほどう} is specifically intended for leisurely walking and enjoyment of the surroundings.

glosses: number of years; duration in years
explanations: The count or span of years involved in something, such as a period of service, the age of a building, or the time required to complete a process.

glosses: visiting a grave; paying respects at a grave
explanations: The act of visiting a family grave or memorial to pay respects to the deceased. This is an important cultural practice in Japan, especially during Obon, the spring and autumn equinoxes, and the New Year.
The components or elements that make up a substance, material, or system. Used in scientific, industrial, and analytical contexts to describe what something is made of and in what proportions.

glosses: pupil; disciple; student (of a master or school)
explanations: A person who studies under a particular master or teacher, or the group of such students collectively. Used in traditional arts, martial arts, academic lineages, and similar contexts where there is a clear master-student relationship.
A person who works at a bank. The term covers all bank staff from tellers to office workers, but does not include executive management.
The surgical removal or deactivation of reproductive organs in an animal or, historically, in a person. In modern Japanese, most commonly used in the context of pet care and livestock management.
Used figuratively to describe stripping someone or something of power, influence, or vitality.
A person sent on a specific diplomatic or official mission, typically by a head of state or government. Distinguished from a regular ambassador by the temporary and focused nature of the assignment.

glosses: walking path; strolling route; usual walk
explanations: A path or route that one regularly walks for pleasure or exercise. Unlike {遊歩道|ゆうほどう}, which refers to a purpose-built walkway, {散歩道|さんぽみち} can be any route — streets, riverbanks, park paths — that someone habitually uses for their daily walk.
A person who works aboard a ship, especially one engaged in manual labor on deck rather than in a commanding or navigating role. The word has a somewhat traditional or literary flavor.

glosses: art world; art circles; painting establishment
explanations: The collective community of painters and the institutional world of fine art, including exhibitions, critics, art associations, and the social networks surrounding painting. Often used when discussing trends, influence, or standing within the painting community.

The sun as it rises in the early morning. Refers both to the physical sun visible at dawn and to the light it casts. A word with poetic and cultural resonance in Japanese, evoking freshness, new beginnings, and the beauty of dawn.
Beer that has not been heat-pasteurized, served on tap or in unpasteurized bottles and cans. In everyday restaurant and bar usage, it typically refers to beer served from a tap (on draft).
A medicine or drug that reduces or eliminates pain. The most common everyday word for over-the-counter and prescription pain medication.

glosses: to wake up; to awaken; to come to one's senses
to come to one's senses; to have one's eyes opened
explanations: To transition from sleep to a waking state. An intransitive expression describing the natural process of waking up, as opposed to being woken by someone else.
To suddenly realize the truth of a situation, snap out of a delusion, or become aware of something one was previously blind to. Used figuratively for moments of realization or disillusionment.

The return of money that was overpaid or is owed back, especially in official or administrative contexts such as tax refunds, insurance reimbursements, and government payments. More formal than everyday words for refunds.

glosses: start of a performance; curtain up
start of a performance; curtain up; showtime
explanations: The moment when a theatrical show, concert, or other live performance begins. Used for scheduled start times and the actual commencement of performances.

glosses: fraction; remainder; odd amount; fractional amount
explanations: A partial or leftover amount that does not form a round number, especially in the context of money, measurements, or calculations. Commonly refers to amounts below a convenient rounding unit, such as the yen below a hundred-yen mark.

A seasonal greeting card or message sent during the hottest part of summer (roughly mid-July to early August) to inquire after someone's well-being. One of several traditional seasonal greeting customs in Japan, along with New Year's cards.
A third molar tooth, the last teeth to emerge in the back of the mouth, typically appearing in late adolescence or early adulthood. Often associated with dental problems requiring extraction.

glosses: numbered ticket; number tag; queue ticket
explanations: A small ticket, tag, or token with a number on it, used to manage waiting order at service counters, restaurants, government offices, and similar places. The customer takes a number and waits to be called.

glosses: without; excluding; leaving out (as a suffix)
explanations: Used as a suffix attached to a noun to mean "without that thing" or "with that thing removed." Extremely common in food ordering, daily conversation, and written instructions.
The act of leaving something out or cutting corners in a process or task. Often used in the expression {手抜|てぬ}き (cutting corners, doing a sloppy job).

glosses: destination address; recipient address; shipping address
explanations: The address to which something is being sent — a package, letter, or shipment. The place or person on the receiving end of a delivery.

A loanword from English "drink," used widely in restaurants, cafes, menus, and vending machines to refer to any drink or beverage. Often appears in compound terms for drink-related services and products.

glosses: navigation system; car nav; GPS navigation
explanations: An abbreviated form of ナビゲーション (navigation). Refers primarily to car navigation systems (カーナビ), but also used more broadly for any GPS or map-based navigation on smartphones and other devices.

glosses: disaster preparedness supplies; emergency supplies; disaster kit
explanations: Items kept on hand in preparation for natural disasters such as earthquakes, typhoons, and floods. Includes food, water, flashlights, first-aid kits, batteries, and other survival essentials. A culturally important concept in disaster-prone Japan.
The act of attaching, installing, or mounting equipment, fixtures, or appliances into place. Commonly used for air conditioners, shelves, lighting, and other household or industrial equipment.

The identifying number or code of a scheduled transport service, most commonly an airline flight (e.g., JL123, NH456). Can also refer to bus or ferry service numbers, though airline usage is dominant.

A record of events, activities, or observations kept on a daily basis, typically in a professional, institutional, or organizational context. Unlike a personal diary, a {日誌|にっし} is usually an official or work-related record.
A person who has been physically injured, whether from an accident, disaster, or other incident. Used in news reports, emergency contexts, and everyday conversation about accidents.
Corn kernels that have been heated until they burst open into light, fluffy pieces. A popular snack at movie theaters, theme parks, and festivals in Japan.
A Buddhist temple, used with the polite prefix お. The standard everyday form when referring to temples in conversation.
A flat receptacle used for carrying or displaying items. From English 'tray'. Widely used in restaurants, cafeterias, and fast food shops in Japan.
A device that measures and displays a quantity such as speed, distance, electricity usage, or gas consumption. From English 'meter'.
The fare meter in a taxi that calculates and displays the fare based on distance and time.
A person or figure in a story, anime, manga, game, or other fictional work.
A designed character used as a mascot or brand representative, including corporate mascots, regional mascots, and product characters.
A ride or entertainment feature at a theme park or amusement park. From English 'attraction'. In Japanese, this word almost exclusively refers to physical rides and attractions at leisure facilities.

glosses: ordinary savings account; regular deposit account
explanations: The most common type of bank account in Japan, allowing deposits and withdrawals at any time. Equivalent to a basic checking/savings account in English-speaking countries.
Mail sent to or received from another country. Covers letters, parcels, and other postal items crossing international borders.

glosses: convenience store payment; paying bills at a convenience store
explanations: A payment method where bills, online shopping orders, or other charges are paid in cash at a convenience store counter using a payment slip or barcode.

A school that teaches Japanese as a foreign language, primarily to international students and residents. Many foreign students attend these schools to prepare for university entrance or to improve their Japanese for work.
The rate at which one currency can be exchanged for another. A key concept in international finance and travel.
A waste sorting category in Japan for items that cannot be incinerated, such as metals, ceramics, glass, and certain plastics. Collection days and accepted items vary by municipality.

glosses: residence card (for foreign residents in Japan)
explanations: An identification card issued to foreign nationals residing in Japan with a period of stay exceeding three months. It serves as the primary form of identification for non-Japanese residents.
A rechargeable contactless smart card used primarily for public transportation and electronic payments. Major brands include Suica, Pasmo, and ICOCA.
A label used in housing listings, hotels, and other facilities to indicate that pets are permitted. Very commonly seen in real estate advertisements and apartment search websites.
A portable audio device or app that provides recorded commentary and explanations at museums, tourist sites, historic buildings, and other cultural venues.
A company that provides insurance products including life insurance, health insurance, auto insurance, and property insurance.
A company that manages residential or commercial properties on behalf of the owner. Handles maintenance, tenant relations, rent collection, and building upkeep.

glosses: consultation counter; inquiry desk; help desk
explanations: A service counter or contact point where people can seek advice, ask questions, or get help with procedures. Found at government offices, hospitals, banks, and other institutions.

A professional service company that helps people move their belongings from one residence to another. In Japan, moving companies offer various service levels from basic transport to full packing and unpacking.
Japan's basic public pension system that covers all residents aged 20-59. It is the first tier of Japan's pension system and provides a basic old-age pension.
An amusement park ride consisting of a fast train that travels along a track with steep drops, loops, and sharp turns. A Japanese-English coinage from 'jet coaster', not used in English.
A small chip card inserted into a mobile phone to connect to a cellular network. Essential for phone service in Japan, available from major carriers and budget providers.
A rendering of text from one language into another. Used as both a standalone noun and as a suffix indicating the language translated into.
The polite/honorific form of {挨拶|あいさつ}, used in formal contexts such as business, ceremonies, and official communication. Covers spoken greetings, formal speeches, and written salutations.
A measured duration of time, especially in sports and competitions. Used for race results, personal records, and performance measurements.
A pause or break in a game or activity, called by a player, coach, or participant.
An electronic mail address used for sending and receiving email. Often abbreviated to メアド in casual speech.

glosses: shared area; common area; common-use space
explanations: Areas in an apartment building or condominium that are shared by all residents, such as hallways, lobbies, elevators, and parking lots. Contrasted with the individual units owned or rented by each resident.

glosses: organizing committee member; executive committee member
explanations: A member of a committee responsible for planning and carrying out an event, festival, or project. Common in schools, universities, and community organizations.

glosses: in a horizontal line; in a row side by side
horizontal line; single row; side by side in a line
explanations: A formation where people or things are arranged in one line from left to right (as opposed to a vertical column). Used for physical arrangements and figuratively for equal status.
The polite/honorific form of {確認|かくにん}, used in business correspondence, customer service, and formal requests to ask someone to check or confirm something.

glosses: from a long time ago; for ages; traditionally
from a long time ago; for ages; traditionally; since the old days
explanations: Indicates that something has been the case continuously from a distant past up to the present. Used to describe long-standing customs, personal traits, relationships, or facts that have not changed for a long time.

glosses: extremely; excessively; to an extreme degree
explanations: Indicates that something is at a level far beyond what is normal, reasonable, or expected. Often carries a negative nuance, suggesting that the degree is unbalanced or unhealthy, though it can also be used neutrally to emphasize extreme values or behavior.

glosses: dinner party; meal gathering; get-together over a meal
explanations: A social gathering centered on sharing a meal together, typically at a restaurant or in someone's home. Less formal than a banquet ({宴会|えんかい}) and usually smaller in scale, often held to celebrate an occasion, welcome or farewell someone, or simply deepen relationships.

A machine that produces paper copies of documents or images. Common in offices, convenience stores, schools, and public libraries in Japan. Modern devices usually combine copying, printing, scanning, and faxing functions.

An informal or affectionate name used instead of one's real name, typically by friends, family, or within a specific community. In Japanese, ニックネーム most commonly refers to the display name used on websites, apps, and games, as well as nicknames given among classmates or friends.

glosses: private car; personal automobile; family car
explanations: A car owned by a private individual or household for personal use, as opposed to a company car, taxi, or rental vehicle. In Japan, private cars have white-background license plates, distinguishing them from commercial vehicles, which use green-background plates.

glosses: safety management; safety oversight; safety administration
explanations: The systematic effort by an organization to identify hazards, prevent accidents, and protect workers, users, and the public. In Japan, {安全|あんぜん}{管理|かんり} is a legally required activity in construction, manufacturing, transportation, schools, and many other fields, typically coordinated by a designated safety manager.

In mathematics, a number that can be expressed as the ratio of two integers (a fraction), where the denominator is not zero. Includes all integers, finite decimals, and repeating decimals. Contrasted with {無理数|むりすう} (irrational numbers) such as π and √2.

glosses: ethics; moral philosophy; the study of ethics
explanations: The branch of philosophy concerned with questions of right and wrong conduct, moral values, and the nature of the good life. Studied as an academic discipline at universities and in philosophy departments, distinct from the everyday sense of {倫理|りんり} (ethics, morals) that one might apply to personal conduct.

glosses: carpentry tools; carpenter's tools; woodworking tools
explanations: The set of hand and power tools used by carpenters and woodworkers, such as saws, hammers, chisels, planes, and measuring tools. The term emphasizes tools traditionally used in Japanese house-building and wooden furniture making, though it is also used for the modern carpenter's kit.

The awareness a person has of their own character, abilities, emotions, and position, including both accurate self-understanding and the image one holds of oneself. Used in psychology, education, business, and everyday discussion of personal growth.

glosses: sound equipment; audio system; PA system
explanations: The collection of equipment — speakers, amplifiers, microphones, mixers, and related devices — installed in a venue to handle sound production and amplification. Used for concerts, theaters, conference rooms, wedding halls, schools, and public facilities.

The branch of medicine that applies medical knowledge to legal questions, most commonly by examining deceased bodies to determine cause and time of death in criminal investigations. In Japan, {法医学|ほういがく} is taught in medical schools and practiced by specialists at universities and police-affiliated institutes.

glosses: replacement; swap; changing (one attached part for another)
explanations: The act of removing a part, fitting, accessory, or attachment and putting a different one in its place. Used for items that are meant to be installed and removed, such as light fixtures, phone cases, name tags, straps, and belts. Distinct from pure replacement ({交換|こうかん}) in that the item is physically attached/detached.

In mathematics, a positive integer that divides two or more given integers without leaving a remainder. For example, 6 is a common divisor of 12 and 18. The greatest such number is called the {最大|さいだい}{公約数|こうやくすう} (greatest common divisor).

By extension, something shared by multiple parties — a point of agreement, a shared trait, or a common ground. Often used in the phrase {最大|さいだい}{公約数|こうやくすう} to mean "the greatest common ground" among different people or groups.

glosses: curriculum; educational program; course of study
explanations: The overall plan of subjects, content, and activities that make up a school's instructional program. Used for both compulsory education and higher education in Japan. Organized by the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT) for public schools, with each school adapting the national curriculum to its own context.

glosses: attached document; supporting document; accompanying papers
explanations: Documents that are attached to an application, report, or main document as supporting evidence or required supplementary information. Commonly used in official procedures, business correspondence, tax filings, and job applications.

glosses: order of numbers; numerical order; in number order
explanations: The arrangement of items, people, or documents according to their assigned number, typically ascending. Used for calling patients at clinics, processing applications, seating students, and organizing files.

glosses: condolence visit; call of condolence; visit of mourning
explanations: A formal visit to a bereaved family to express condolences after someone's death. In Japan, a {弔問|ちょうもん} visitor may come to the family's home before the funeral or to the funeral venue itself to offer incense, prayers, and sympathy to the family of the deceased.

The quality of being contrary to reason or logic, or of not conforming to rational thought. Used both as a noun describing irrationality itself and as a na-adjective describing things that defy reasoning — emotions, customs, behaviors, or social structures that cannot be justified by logical analysis alone.

The obligation or practice of keeping sensitive information — business data, client information, trade secrets, or government secrets — from being disclosed to unauthorized parties. A key concept in employment contracts, government work, and corporate governance.

headword: よろしくお願いします
glosses: please treat me well; I look forward to working with you; please (take care of this for me)
please treat me kindly; pleased to meet you; I'm counting on you
explanations: A standard set phrase used at the start of relationships, collaborations, or any interaction where one is asking for goodwill or cooperation. It has no single English equivalent, and is often translated according to context (e.g., 'nice to meet you' at introductions, 'I look forward to working with you' in professional settings, or 'please take care of it' when delegating a task).

glosses: excuse me for intruding; pardon my intrusion; hello (on entering someone's home)
excuse me for intruding; pardon the interruption; (said upon entering someone's home or workspace)
explanations: A polite set phrase said when entering someone else's home, office, or private space. It acknowledges that the speaker is imposing on the host, and is expected etiquette in Japan — going without saying it would seem rude. Literally, 'I will be a bother.'

glosses: thank you for having me; sorry for intruding; I'll be going now
thank you for having me; sorry for the intrusion; (said when leaving someone's home or space)
explanations: The past-tense counterpart of お{邪魔|じゃま}します. It is said when leaving someone's home, office, or other private space to thank the host and acknowledge the imposition. Literally, 'I was a bother' — functionally closer to 'thanks for having me.'

headword: お世話になっております
glosses: thank you for your continued support; I am indebted to you (business greeting)
thank you for your continued support; I appreciate your ongoing help; (standard business greeting)
explanations: A fixed greeting used at the beginning of phone calls and emails between business parties who have an ongoing relationship. It acknowledges that the speaker or their company is being looked after by the listener's company, and is said regardless of whether any recent interaction took place. The literal meaning is 'I am in your care.'

headword: つまらないものですが
glosses: it's just a small thing, but...; please accept this humble gift
it's just a small thing, but...; it's nothing special, but...; please accept this humble gift
explanations: A humble set phrase used when presenting a gift. It literally means 'it is a trifling thing, but [please take it],' and is a conventional way of downplaying a gift out of modesty. The speaker is not saying the gift is actually worthless — the humility is formulaic.

glosses: to take off one's shoes; to remove one's footwear
explanations: A basic everyday collocation. In Japan, the phrase is especially bound up with the custom of removing shoes at the entrance of a home and at many other interior spaces (traditional restaurants, temples, schools, etc.).
The standard collocation for washing the face, typically as part of the morning or evening routine. Uses the generic verb {洗|あら}う ('to wash'), which covers any kind of washing done with water.

glosses: to dry one's hair; to blow-dry one's hair
explanations: The standard collocation for drying wet hair after a bath or shower. The verb {乾|かわ}かす is the causative 'to make dry,' and is used for any object that is actively dried (hair, laundry, etc.), as opposed to things that dry passively.

glosses: (please) help me; give me a hand
explanations: A cry for help in an emergency. Grammatically the te-form of {助|たす}ける ('to save, rescue, help'), used on its own as a complete utterance. It is the standard Japanese equivalent of shouting 'help!' in English.
A casual request for assistance with a task. In this softer use, the speaker is asking for cooperation or support rather than calling for rescue. Often said to friends or family.

glosses: water (polite/soft form); a glass of water
explanations: The polite/softened version of {水|みず} ('water'), formed by prefixing the honorific お. Especially common in service contexts (restaurants, cafes, hospitals), in women's speech, and when speaking to children. The meaning is the same as {水|みず}, but the tone is more courteous or gentle.

glosses: the next station (along a rail or subway line); the upcoming stop
explanations: Refers to the station that comes next on a given route, typically in the context of trains or subways. Frequently heard in station announcements and in everyday travel conversation.

glosses: (I'm sorry to bother you) when you are busy; at this busy time
(while you are) busy; at such a busy time (a polite preface acknowledging the listener's busyness)
explanations: A polite set phrase used to preface a request, thanks, or imposition on someone who is presumed to be busy. It softens the request by acknowledging that the listener's time is valuable. Almost always followed by a phrase like すみません, {申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ありません, ありがとうございます, or a request verb.

glosses: groundbreaking ceremony (marking the start of a construction project)
explanations: A formal ceremony held at the start of a major construction project — typically a building, bridge, railway line, or other large piece of infrastructure. It usually involves dignitaries, developers, and contractors and may include a shovel-turning gesture or a Shinto purification rite.

glosses: to line up in a single row/line
to line up in a single row; to form a single line / queue
explanations: A standard expression for people or things arranging themselves in one line. Frequently used as an instruction in schools, ticket queues, and public transit, and to describe orderly formations.
The principal course of a meal, typically served after appetizers and before dessert in Western-style dining. In Japan the term is used mainly for Western or restaurant-style meals.
An armed exchange of gunfire between opposing parties, such as police and criminals, rival groups, or soldiers. Commonly seen in news reports and action films.
A train that carries passengers, as opposed to one that carries freight. The standard technical term used by railway operators, contrasted with {貨物列車|かもつれっしゃ} (freight train).

The transfer of thermal energy through a material by direct contact between particles, without the material itself moving. A physics and engineering term that also appears in discussions of cookware and building materials.
A plastic tape coated with a magnetizable layer, used to record audio, video, or computer data. Though largely replaced by digital storage, it is still used for long-term data archiving.
A semiconductor device that emits light when an electric current flows through it. The full Japanese term for what is usually abbreviated as LED.
A symbol or keyword that represents an operation on one or more values, such as + and - in arithmetic, AND/OR in logic, or = and == in programming languages.
A small booklet issued by a bank in which deposits, withdrawals, and the running balance of a savings account are recorded. Still widely used in Japan alongside digital banking.

Life as a student, including studies, friendships, club activities, and school events. Typically refers to the overall experience at a high school or college, especially in the context of fiction or nostalgia.
The act of identifying oneself to a computer system, website, or application with a user name and password. Functions as a noun and, with する, as a verb.
A plant that grows from an underground bulb and overwinters as the bulb stores nutrients. Typical examples include tulips, lilies, and daffodils.

Government or private efforts to boost the economy and population of a local area, often through tourism promotion, subsidies, or new industry development. A common term in Japanese policy, news, and local politics, especially in the context of depopulated rural areas.
The process of making something uniform in composition, quality, or character. Used in science and industry (e.g., of milk or materials) and metaphorically about society, products, and culture.

glosses: passbook update; printing transactions in a bankbook
explanations: Having recent deposits, withdrawals, and the running balance printed into a bank passbook. Typically done at an ATM, which has a dedicated slot for feeding in the passbook.
The processing of calculations in a computer, including arithmetic, logical, and numerical operations performed by the CPU or GPU. A technical term used in hardware specifications and programming.

glosses: bankrupt person; person who has filed for or been declared bankrupt
explanations: A person who has been legally declared bankrupt by a court, or who is in the process of bankruptcy proceedings. Used in legal, financial, and news contexts rather than everyday conversation.
A medical term for inflammation of the skin, covering a range of conditions such as eczema, contact dermatitis, and atopic dermatitis. Used in medical contexts and health reporting.

glosses: light brown sugar; sanontou (a Japanese sugar with a caramel-like color and flavor)
explanations: A Japanese type of brown sugar produced by repeatedly heating the sugar syrup that remains after white sugar is extracted. It is pale brown with a mild caramel flavor and is used widely in home cooking, especially for simmered dishes.

glosses: ethnic; national; pertaining to a people or ethnic group
ethnic; national; relating to a particular people or ethnic group
explanations: Describes something that relates to, or is characteristic of, a particular ethnic group or people. Commonly used in discussions of culture, identity, conflict, and tradition.

glosses: attendee; visitor; person who enters a venue or event
explanations: A person who enters a ticketed or ticket-like venue — a museum, stadium, exhibition, theme park, concert, or similar event. Used especially in official counts and announcements of attendance figures.

glosses: mountain pass road; winding road through a mountain pass
mountain pass road; winding road that climbs up and over a mountain pass
explanations: A road that crosses a mountain pass, typically narrow, winding, and climbing steeply to a summit before descending the other side. Often used when describing scenic drives, difficult driving conditions, or traditional travel routes between regions.
The small, triangular bone at the bottom of the spine, the vestigial remnant of the human tail. Used in medical contexts and when describing injuries from falling on the lower back.

glosses: person with parental authority; legal guardian (parent)
person with parental authority; parent with legal custody of a minor child
explanations: A legal term referring to the parent or parents who hold {親権|しんけん} (parental authority) over a minor child — the right and duty to care for the child, manage their property, and represent them legally. Especially important after divorce, when one parent is often designated as the sole {親権者|しんけんしゃ}.

glosses: official name; formal name; full official designation
explanations: The full, official name of an organization, law, product, or other entity, as opposed to a common abbreviation or nickname. Often used when introducing a new item or when clarifying what a commonly used short name actually stands for.

glosses: discoverer; finder; the person who first discovered or found something
discoverer; finder; the person who first discovered or noticed something
explanations: The person credited with discovering something — a scientific fact, a new species, an archaeological site, or simply the person who first noticed a lost item, an accident, or a body. Used in both scientific and everyday news contexts.

glosses: sales office; business office; branch office
sales office; business office; (local) branch office
explanations: A local office of a company that handles sales, customer service, or regional operations — typically smaller than a headquarters or {支店|してん} (branch), and often focused on logistics, pickups, deliveries, or regional clients. Common for shipping companies, utilities, and sales-driven businesses.

An egg cell that has been fertilized by a sperm cell — used in biology, reproductive medicine, and everyday discussion of pregnancy, IVF, and animal breeding. Also used for fertilized eggs of birds (e.g., chickens) that will develop into chicks if incubated.

glosses: closing time (of a shop or restaurant)
closing time; the time at which a shop, restaurant, or other business closes for the day
explanations: The time at which a retail shop, restaurant, or similar business stops operating for the day. Posted on shop signs and websites, and commonly discussed when planning visits.

glosses: city council; city assembly; the elected legislative body of a Japanese city
explanations: The elected legislative body of a Japanese {市|し} (city). City council members ({市議会|しぎかい}{議員|ぎいん}) debate local ordinances, approve the city's budget, and oversee the mayor's administration. Parallel bodies exist at other levels: {町議会|ちょうぎかい} for towns and {県議会|けんぎかい} for prefectures.

Electricity generation that uses the flow of water (typically from a dam or river) to turn turbines. Discussed in news, school textbooks, and policy debates about energy sources, climate change, and renewable energy.

glosses: irrealis form; imperfective form (of a Japanese verb or adjective)
explanations: One of the six traditional conjugation bases ({活用形|かつようけい}) of Japanese verbs and adjectives, used as the stem for negative forms (〜ない), volitional forms (〜う/〜よう), and passive/causative forms (〜れる/〜せる). For example, the {未然形|みぜんけい} of {書|か}く is {書|か}か- (as in {書|か}かない).

glosses: terminal form; conclusive form; dictionary form (of a Japanese verb or adjective)
terminal form; conclusive form; dictionary form
explanations: One of the six traditional conjugation bases ({活用形|かつようけい}) of Japanese verbs and adjectives: the form used to end a plain-style sentence. This is the form listed in dictionaries — e.g., {書|か}く, {食|た}べる, {高|たか}い.

glosses: attributive form; adnominal form (of a Japanese verb or adjective)
explanations: One of the six traditional conjugation bases ({活用形|かつようけい}) of Japanese verbs and adjectives: the form that directly modifies a following noun. In modern Japanese this form is identical to the {終止形|しゅうしけい} for verbs and i-adjectives, but differs for na-adjectives (e.g., {静|しず}かな{部屋|へや}) and the copula.

A grammatical category referring to the addressee — the "you" of a conversation. In English it corresponds to "you" and "your"; in Japanese it is expressed by words like あなた, {君|きみ}, お{前|まえ}, or, very often, by the addressee's name or title rather than a pronoun.

glosses: below-floor flooding; flooding that reaches under the floor but not into the living space
below-floor flooding; flooding under the floor
explanations: A classification used in Japanese disaster reporting for flooding in which water enters the space beneath a house's floor but does not rise above the floor level into the living space. This is the less severe of the two standard damage categories, the other being {床上浸水|ゆかうえしんすい}.

glosses: above-floor flooding; flooding that rises above floor level into the living space
above-floor flooding; flooding above floor level
explanations: A classification used in Japanese disaster reporting for flooding in which water rises above floor level and enters the living space of a house. This is treated as the more serious of the two standard damage categories, the other being {床下浸水|ゆかしたしんすい}, and it typically qualifies for disaster assistance.

The buttocks or gluteal region of the body. A clinical/anatomical term used in medicine, fitness, and formal writing. In everyday speech Japanese speakers use the much more common お{尻|しり} (or plain {尻|しり}).

glosses: the insured; insured person; policyholder (of an insurance policy)
explanations: The person covered by an insurance policy — that is, the person whose life, health, property, or circumstances are the subject of the contract. Distinguished from the {契約者|けいやくしゃ} (the policyholder who signs the contract and pays the premiums) and the {受取人|うけとりにん} (the beneficiary who receives any payout).

glosses: money paid on someone else's behalf; advance payment (to be reimbursed)
money advanced/paid on someone else's behalf; advance payment to be reimbursed
explanations: Money that one party pays on behalf of another party, with the expectation of later reimbursement. In everyday contexts it refers to, for example, an employee paying for business travel out of pocket and later reclaiming it; in accounting it is a standard balance-sheet item (current asset) for receivables arising from such advances.

glosses: contrast agent; contrast medium (for medical imaging)
explanations: A substance administered before or during a medical imaging procedure (X-ray, CT, MRI, or ultrasound) to make certain tissues or blood vessels show up more clearly on the resulting images. Common examples include iodine-based agents for X-ray/CT and gadolinium-based agents for MRI.

Describes a substance, drug, or effect that reduces inflammation in the body. Used mainly in medical, pharmaceutical, and health-food contexts, often as a modifier in compounds like {抗炎症薬|こうえんしょうやく} (anti-inflammatory drug) or {抗炎症作用|こうえんしょうさよう} (anti-inflammatory action).

glosses: body fat scale; body fat meter
body fat scale; body fat meter; body composition monitor
explanations: A household device that measures body fat percentage, usually a bathroom scale that also estimates body composition by passing a weak electrical current through the body. Many modern models also report muscle mass, visceral fat, basal metabolic rate, and similar metrics.

glosses: stadiometer; height meter; height measuring device
explanations: A device used to measure a person's height, typically a vertical ruler with a sliding horizontal arm that rests on the top of the head. Found in schools, clinics, hospitals, and sometimes in homes, especially for tracking children's growth.

The track-and-field event in which the athlete swings a metal ball attached to a wire handle inside a throwing circle and releases it for maximum distance. One of the four throwing events in athletics, alongside shot put, discus, and javelin.

glosses: person radical (亻); the left-hand "person" radical in kanji
explanations: The kanji radical {亻|にんべん}, a stylized form of {人|ひと} (person) that appears on the left side of many kanji. It is one of the most common left-side radicals ({偏|へん}) and generally signals that the kanji has some connection to people or human activity, as in {休|やす}む, {作|つく}る, {住|す}む, and {使|つか}う.

glosses: tree radical (木); the left-hand "tree" radical in kanji
explanations: The kanji radical {木|き}, the {偏|へん} (left-side) form of the character for tree. It appears in many kanji related to trees, wood, and wooden objects, such as {林|はやし}, {森|もり}, {村|むら}, {机|つくえ}, {板|いた}, and {柱|はしら}.

glosses: right-hand component of a kanji; tsukuri
right-hand component of a kanji; the right-side radical element
explanations: The right-hand element of a kanji that has a left-right structure. It contrasts with {偏|へん}, the left-side element. For example, in {時|じ} (time), {日|ひ} is the {偏|へん} and {寺|じ} is the {旁|つくり}. The {旁|つくり} often carries a phonetic hint, while the {偏|へん} carries semantic meaning.

glosses: ink pad (for rubber stamps); stamp pad
explanations: A flat, ink-soaked pad used with rubber stamps to apply ink before stamping. Usually a rectangular plastic case with a fabric or felt pad inside, sold in colors such as black, red, and blue. Distinct from {朱肉|しゅにく}, the specialized vermilion pad used with formal {印鑑|いんかん} seals.

A large industrial furnace used in steelmaking to smelt iron from ore. Iron ore, coke, and limestone are loaded from the top, and hot air is blown in from the bottom, producing molten pig iron. A core facility of heavy industry, often shown as a symbol of steel manufacturing.

A pyramid with a quadrilateral base (typically a square or rectangle) and four triangular faces meeting at an apex. A standard solid figure introduced in middle-school geometry, familiar as the shape of the Pyramids of Giza.

A device or subsystem that processes signals, data, or materials. In computing, it refers to a CPU or similar processing component ({中央処理装置|ちゅうおうしょりそうち} = CPU). In industry, it refers to a plant or machine that processes a substance, such as a {水処理装置|みずしょりそうち} (water processing unit).

glosses: skeletal specimen; mounted skeleton (for study or display)
explanations: A prepared and often reassembled skeleton used as a specimen for biology study, education, or museum display. Common examples include animal skeletons in natural history museums and small-animal or human-anatomy skeletons in school biology classrooms.
The number 20,000, expressed as {二|に} (two) × {万|まん} (10,000) in the Japanese numbering system. A common round figure in everyday contexts — mid-range yen amounts, attendance figures, and so on.

The age of nineteen. In Japan, this is the final year before legal adulthood ({成人|せいじん}) at age 20, though the legal age of majority for most civil-law purposes was lowered to 18 in 2022. Nineteen-year-olds are usually first- or second-year university students, or young workers in their second post–high-school year.

The killing of a large number of people, typically in a single incident or by a single perpetrator or group. Used in news reporting, criminal-law discussions, and historical descriptions of atrocities and terror attacks.

The highest-ranking diplomatic representative a state sends to another country, authorized to act with full authority on behalf of the head of state. The formal, official title used in diplomatic protocol, treaties, and news coverage of ambassadorial appointments.

glosses: required items; prescribed items (on a form)
explanations: The items that must be filled in or recorded as specified by rules, regulations, or a form's instructions. A bureaucratic term used on application forms, contracts, and official notices to indicate fields the user is required to complete.

glosses: not applicable; not relevant; does not fall under (a category)
explanations: A checkbox or dropdown label meaning that a given item, rule, or category does not apply to the person or case in question. Common on government forms, applications, and legal documents as the opposite of {該当|がいとう} (applicable).

A specific procedure or algorithm used to perform a calculation, especially in scientific, engineering, financial, or statistical contexts. Used when discussing the choice or comparison of methods rather than the act of calculating itself.

A legal term meaning a crime that has been fully carried out, with all elements of the offense completed. Contrasted with {未遂|みすい} (attempted but not completed). Used in criminal law, court judgments, and news reporting on criminal cases.

glosses: principal (offender); person who commits the crime directly
explanations: A legal term for the person who personally carries out the criminal act, as opposed to an accomplice or accessory. Under Japanese criminal law, the principal is distinguished from those who merely aid, abet, or instigate the crime, and is generally subject to the full penalty.

glosses: stealing someone away from their partner; poaching a lover
explanations: A tabloid-style term describing the act of making someone leave their existing partner (spouse, boyfriend, girlfriend) to start a romantic relationship with oneself. Typically carries a sensational or moralizing tone and is common in entertainment news about celebrity affairs and in women's magazines.

A meteorological term for a period of unseasonably warm air flowing into a region, causing temperatures well above normal for several days. Used in weather forecasts and climate reports as the counterpart of {寒波|かんぱ} (cold wave).

glosses: modified word; head word (the word that a modifier modifies)
explanations: A linguistic term referring to the word that receives modification from another word (the modifier). In the phrase "red apple," "apple" is the modified word and "red" is the modifier. Used in grammar textbooks, linguistics papers, and Japanese-language teaching.

glosses: person who gives orders; director; person in charge
explanations: The person whose job is to direct others — issuing instructions, assigning tasks, and overseeing how work is carried out. Can describe a formal supervisory role, but more often appears in a slightly critical or teasing tone, suggesting someone who bosses others around without doing the hands-on work themselves.

glosses: inner rind; inner skin (of fruit, seeds, etc.)
explanations: In anatomy and medicine, the thin layer of cells lining the inside of blood vessels, the heart, and other hollow organs. Contrasted with {外皮|がいひ} (outer skin) and {中皮|ちゅうひ} (mesothelium).
In botany and cooking, the thin white or translucent membrane found just inside the outer peel of citrus fruits, chestnuts, and similar foods. Often removed for a better texture or flavor.

glosses: post-dating (writing a future date on a document)
post-dating; writing a future date on a document
