explanations: The practice of putting a date later than the current one on a document — most commonly a check or a contract — so that it takes effect from that later date. Used in banking, accounting, and business contexts.

glosses: self-defensive; for self-protection; defensive in nature
explanations: Describes an action, measure, or attitude that is intended to protect oneself — one's body, rights, interests, or organization — from harm or attack. Applies both to physical self-defense and to more abstract situations like protective political, legal, or business measures.

glosses: a woman picking up a man (for a date or hookup)
explanations: A slang term for the reversed version of ナンパ (nampa, a man striking up a pickup with a stranger) — specifically, when a woman approaches a man on the street or in a venue to start a romantic or sexual encounter. The term is often used with a sense of surprise or amusement, since men-initiating is more culturally expected.

glosses: tipping feature; donation function (on a live-streaming or social media platform)
tipping feature; donation function (on a live-streaming platform)
explanations: An online feature that allows viewers to send money to a streamer, creator, or performer in real time while watching or reading their content. Common on live-streaming sites, video platforms, and social media, where it serves as direct viewer-to-creator financial support.

A traditional Japanese food made from wheat gluten that has been kneaded, shaped, and then baked or toasted until dry and light. Sold in hard, spongy pieces (rounds, sticks, or small flower shapes) that are rehydrated and added to soups, stews, sukiyaki, and simmered dishes.

glosses: nama-fu; fresh wheat gluten (soft and chewy)
explanations: A traditional Japanese food made from wheat gluten mixed with glutinous rice flour, steamed to produce a soft, chewy texture. Eaten as a refined ingredient in Kyoto-style cuisine, Buddhist vegetarian cooking, and high-end Japanese restaurants.
The age of eight; used to state someone's age in years. Also written {8|はっ}{歳|さい} in numerals. Appears in questionnaires, forms, medical records, and everyday conversation.

glosses: repatriate; person evacuated home from overseas
explanations: A Japanese national who returned to Japan from overseas, especially from the former colonies and occupied territories (Korea, Taiwan, Manchuria, Sakhalin, etc.) at the end of World War II. The term most commonly refers to the roughly six million civilians and demobilized soldiers repatriated between 1945 and the early 1950s.

glosses: birthday celebration; birthday festival (esp. for an idol or fictional character)
explanations: A formal-sounding word for a birthday celebration, used especially in fan culture for events that honor the birthday of an idol, anime/manga/game character, or other beloved figure. Often accompanied by hashtags, fan art, special merchandise, and themed cafés or events.

A small rodent of the species Mus musculus, the common house mouse. The Japanese name reflects the old folk belief that the mouse's gestation period is about twenty days. Widely kept as a laboratory animal and pet, and the basis of the white mouse used in scientific research.

The biological order Rodentia, comprising mammals such as mice, rats, squirrels, beavers, and porcupines that share continuously growing front incisors used for gnawing. Used both as a technical zoological term and in everyday writing about animals.

The biochemical stiffening of the muscles that occurs in a body within hours after death and gradually subsides over the next day or two. A key piece of evidence used in forensic medicine to estimate time of death.

A dedicated video-game machine designed to be connected to a television or monitor at home, as opposed to handheld systems, smartphones, arcade cabinets, or PCs. The standard industry term in Japanese for products such as PlayStation, Nintendo Switch (in dock mode), and Xbox.

glosses: ENT (ear, nose, and throat) department; otolaryngology
explanations: The medical specialty and the corresponding department of a hospital or clinic that treats diseases of the ear, nose, throat, and adjoining areas of the head and neck. Patients visit it for problems such as ear infections, hearing loss, sinusitis, sore throat, hoarseness, dizziness, and hay fever.

glosses: intravenous infusion; IV drip; infusion fluid
explanations: The medical procedure of administering large volumes of fluid (saline, glucose, electrolytes, nutrients, or medication) into a patient's vein over a sustained period, or the fluid itself that is administered. Used to correct dehydration, restore electrolyte balance, deliver drugs, or provide nutrition to patients who cannot eat or drink.

An extinct group of large, long-necked marine reptiles (order Plesiosauria) that lived from the late Triassic to the end of the Cretaceous, alongside the dinosaurs. Famous for their swan-like necks, paddle-shaped flippers, and small heads. The supposed Loch Ness Monster is most often imagined to be a surviving plesiosaur.

glosses: reply postcard; pre-addressed reply card (esp. of an ōfuku-hagaki)
explanations: The reply half of an {往復|おうふく}はがき (round-trip postcard), or any pre-addressed postcard included with an invitation, survey, or business correspondence so that the recipient can write a reply and mail it back. Frequently used for wedding invitations, alumni-association notices, and formal business RSVPs.

A company whose ownership and/or management is concentrated in the hands of a single family or a small number of related families. The term covers everything from small neighborhood shops to large publicly listed corporations in which the founding family retains a controlling stake or holds key executive posts.

A triangle in which all three sides are of equal length and, equivalently, all three interior angles are equal at 60°. The most symmetric of the triangle types and a foundational figure in elementary and middle-school geometry.

The twenty-three special wards ({特別区|とくべつく}) that together make up the central, urban core of Tokyo, distinct from the rest of Tokyo Metropolis (which includes outer cities such as Hachioji and the Tama region). Each ward functions as an independent municipality with its own elected mayor and assembly, but together they correspond to what is loosely called 'central Tokyo' or simply 'Tokyo' in casual English.

glosses: chin strap (of a hat, helmet, or mask)
explanations: A strap or cord attached to a hat, helmet, kasa, mask, or similar headgear that passes under the chin to keep the item securely on the wearer's head. Found on construction helmets, military helmets, riding helmets, traditional sedge hats ({菅笠|すげがさ}), kindergarten hats, and elementary-school yellow safety hats.

glosses: skim milk powder; nonfat dry milk
explanations: Powdered milk produced by removing the fat from cow's milk and then dehydrating it. Used as an inexpensive long-shelf-life dairy product, in baking, in food processing, and historically as a key ingredient in postwar Japanese school lunches.

glosses: high image quality; high resolution; high definition
explanations: A high level of visual quality in a photo, video, display, or camera — sharp, clear, and with fine detail. Used both as a noun and, with の, as a modifier meaning high-quality or high-resolution.

glosses: low image quality; low resolution; poor picture quality
explanations: A low level of visual quality in a photo, video, or display — blurry, pixelated, or lacking detail. Used both as a noun and, with の, as a modifier meaning low-quality or low-resolution.

glosses: floor plan; plan view; plan drawing
explanations: A drawing that shows a building, room, or site as seen from directly above — with walls, doors, furniture, or other features drawn flat on a two-dimensional plane. Used in architecture, real estate, and interior design.

glosses: elevation drawing; elevation view; front/side elevation
explanations: A drawing that shows a building as seen from the front, back, or side — representing the exterior as a flat, two-dimensional image. Used in architecture alongside plan views and cross-sections.

glosses: primeval forest; virgin forest; old-growth forest
explanations: A forest that has developed naturally without significant human intervention — never logged, cleared, or planted. Used in ecology, geography, and nature writing to describe ancient, undisturbed forests.
A forest that has grown naturally rather than being planted by humans. Contrasted with {人工林|じんこうりん} (plantation forest). Used in forestry, ecology, and environmental discussions.

glosses: how; in what way; in what manner
explanations: A somewhat formal way to ask "how?" or "in what way?" Built from どの (which) + ように (like, in the manner of). Used to ask about the manner, method, or process by which something is done. More polite and written-style than the casual どう.

glosses: self-sufficiency; self-supply; producing for one's own use
explanations: Supplying something — especially food, energy, or resources — by oneself rather than depending on outside sources. Often used in economic and policy contexts about a country or household producing what it consumes.

A mathematical relationship in which one quantity increases (or decreases) in the same ratio as another — if one doubles, the other doubles. Contrasted with {反比例|はんぴれい} (inverse proportion). Also used in everyday Japanese to describe any situation where two things rise and fall together.
A newspaper that covers news of a particular local area — a prefecture, city, or community. Contrasted with national newspapers ({全国紙|ぜんこくし}). Used in news, media, and journalism contexts.

glosses: accidental death; death by accident; death in an accident
explanations: Dying as a result of an accident — a traffic accident, a workplace accident, a fall, or any similar unintended event. Contrasted with natural death, disease death, suicide, or homicide. Used in news reports, legal contexts, and insurance documents.

glosses: history (as an academic discipline); historical studies
history (as an academic discipline); historiography; historical studies
explanations: The academic field that studies and interprets the human past through documentary, archaeological, and other evidence. Distinguished from {歴史|れきし} (history as a subject or the past itself) by emphasizing the systematic, scholarly study of history.

glosses: magic trick; conjuring; sleight of hand
magic trick; conjuring; sleight of hand; stage magic
explanations: The art or performance of stage magic — making objects appear, disappear, or transform in ways that seem impossible. A somewhat formal or old-fashioned word compared to the common loanword マジック.

glosses: desire for career advancement; ambition (for success); drive to get ahead
explanations: A strong personal desire to rise in rank, status, or position — especially at a company or in society. Has a mildly negative or neutral nuance; "ambition" in a pure, positive sense is more often expressed with {向上心|こうじょうしん}.

glosses: documents to be submitted; required paperwork
documents to be submitted; required paperwork; submission documents
explanations: The set of documents or forms that a person is required to submit — for example, for a job application, school admission, a visa, or an official procedure. A compound noun, not a verb phrase. Common in formal, administrative, and workplace contexts.
Any wind instrument made of metal and played by buzzing the lips into a cup-shaped mouthpiece — for example, trumpet, trombone, horn, or tuba. Contrasted with {木管楽器|もっかんがっき} (woodwind instrument).

glosses: self-sufficiency; being content with what one has
self-sufficiency; meeting one's own needs; being content with what one has
explanations: Supplying one's own needs or being satisfied with what one already has — without seeking more from outside. Most commonly seen in the four-character compound {自給自足|じきゅうじそく} (self-sufficiency).

glosses: low quality; poor quality; inferior quality
explanations: A low standard of quality — of goods, services, content, or work. Used both as a noun and, with の, as a modifier meaning low-quality or inferior.

glosses: for advanced users; aimed at advanced learners
for advanced users; intended for advanced learners; aimed at experts
explanations: Designed for or aimed at people who already have a high level of skill or experience. Commonly seen as a label on textbooks, courses, tutorials, products, or ski slopes. Contrasted with {初級者向|しょきゅうしゃむ}け (for beginners).

glosses: for beginners; aimed at beginner learners
for beginners; intended for beginner learners; entry-level
explanations: Designed for or aimed at beginners — people who are just starting to learn a skill or subject. Seen as a label on textbooks, classes, apps, tutorials, and equipment. Contrasted with {上級者向|じょうきゅうしゃむ}け (for advanced users).

glosses: intermediary; go-between; the person or thing that connects; bridging role
explanations: Someone — or occasionally something — that serves to connect, link, or bridge two sides. Often used for a person who mediates between two parties, or a figure who links an older and newer generation, or someone filling a temporary connecting role.

glosses: the rewarding aspect of work; sense of fulfillment at work
the rewarding aspect of one's work; sense of fulfillment or meaning from one's job
explanations: The feeling that one's work is worth doing — that it produces satisfaction, meaning, or a sense of accomplishment. A common topic in job-hunting, workplace surveys, and discussions of career values.

A fixed, well-established expression — a phrase or idiom whose wording has been stable over time and whose meaning cannot always be predicted from its parts. Often refers to four-character compounds ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}) and proverbs drawn from Chinese classics.

glosses: ventilation; sending air; blowing air (without heating or cooling)
explanations: The act of sending a stream of air through a space or machine — for ventilation, cooling, or drying. In household contexts, particularly the "fan" (air-circulation only) mode on an air conditioner, which moves air without heating or cooling it.

glosses: differentiation; making something distinct; clearly distinguishing
explanations: The act of making something distinct from something else — often used in business (differentiating a product from competitors) or in conceptual discussion (drawing a clear line between two ideas, categories, or groups).

glosses: business partner; affiliated company; tie-up partner
business partner; affiliated company; tie-up partner; partner organization
explanations: A company, organization, or store with which one has a formal business alliance or tie-up — the "other side" of a business partnership. Common in corporate, financial, and travel-industry contexts.

glosses: way of taking something (mentally); interpretation; reaction
way of taking (something said or done); way of interpreting; way of reacting to
explanations: How a person mentally or emotionally takes in something — news, criticism, an event, or another person's words. Emphasizes that different people may react or interpret things in different ways.

glosses: water tower; elevated water storage tank
explanations: A tall structure that holds water at height so that it can be supplied to buildings and water pipes by gravity pressure. A standard element of municipal water supply and of large apartment or industrial complexes.

glosses: to pay a price; to pay compensation
to pay a price (for something); to pay compensation; to give something in return
explanations: Collocation meaning to hand over money or another form of value in exchange for a good, service, or benefit. Often used in the literal, commercial sense, but also figuratively for "paying a price" in effort, sacrifice, or consequences.

Expenses connected with holding meetings or conferences — room rental, drinks and light refreshments, materials, and so on. A standard accounting category in Japanese corporate bookkeeping, distinct from entertainment expenses ({接待|せったい}{交際|こうさい}{費|ひ}).

glosses: Chinese person; Chinese national; a person from China
explanations: A person whose nationality is Chinese (the People's Republic of China), or who is ethnically Chinese. The term is used in the same neutral way as {日本人|にほんじん} or {アメリカ{人|じん}}.
The permanent end of menstruation, generally occurring naturally in women between their late 40s and early 50s. Also used as a suru-verb ({閉経|へいけい}する) meaning 'to reach menopause'.
Elastic material obtained from the latex of rubber trees (mainly {パラゴムノキ}, Hevea brasiliensis). Contrasts with synthetic rubber ({合成|ごうせい}ゴム) made from petrochemicals.

An elastic polymer made artificially from petrochemicals, used as a substitute or supplement for natural rubber. Comes in many varieties (SBR, nitrile, silicone, etc.) tailored to different heat, oil, or weather requirements.
One of the ten standard cloud genera: puffy, cotton-like clouds with flat bases and rounded tops, typically forming on fair-weather days by thermal convection in the lower atmosphere.

One of the ten standard cloud genera: a flat, featureless, low-altitude cloud sheet that covers large areas of sky, often producing drizzle or mist. Distinguished from cumulus by its uniform layered appearance.
The biological system consisting of the brain, spinal cord, and nerves, which transmits signals throughout the body and coordinates sensation, movement, and thought.

glosses: synthetic leather; artificial leather; imitation leather
explanations: A material made to look and feel like real leather, typically consisting of a fabric base coated with polyurethane or polyvinyl chloride. Used in clothing, furniture, bags, and automotive interiors as a cheaper, more uniform, and animal-free alternative to natural leather.
A green organelle found in plant cells and algae that carries out photosynthesis. Contains chlorophyll, which captures light energy and uses it to produce sugars from carbon dioxide and water.

A group of mammals whose young are born at a very early stage of development and continue to grow in a pouch on the mother's abdomen. Includes kangaroos, koalas, wombats, and opossums; mostly native to Australia and the Americas.

glosses: to face each other; to sit / stand opposite one another
explanations: For two or more people or things to be positioned facing one another directly. Also used figuratively for confronting or dealing squarely with a person, problem, or one's own feelings.

glosses: to be cornered; to be in a tight spot
to be driven into a corner; to be in a desperate situation; to run out of options
explanations: To reach a point where there is no more time or no way out, and one must act urgently. Describes deadlines, financial trouble, personal crises, and similar situations where all easier options have been exhausted.

glosses: to automatically debit (money from an account); to draw (a payment) from a bank account
to pull down; to drag down; to knock down from above
explanations: For a bank, credit card company, or service provider to withdraw funds directly from a customer's bank account, typically as a scheduled recurring payment for utilities, rent, or credit card bills. Most commonly encountered in personal finance contexts.
To physically pull something down from a higher position, or to force a person down from where they were standing or sitting. Less common than sense 1 in modern everyday Japanese.

glosses: credit limit; usage limit (amount); spending cap
explanations: The maximum amount that a user is permitted to charge, withdraw, or spend — most commonly the credit limit on a credit card, but also used for debit cards, prepaid cards, point services, and other usage-based accounts.

glosses: My Number Card (Japan's national ID card)
My Number Card; Individual Number Card (Japan's national ID card)
explanations: The official plastic ID card issued by the Japanese government that carries a resident's 12-digit {個人番号|こじんばんごう} (Individual Number, commonly called 'My Number'). It shows the holder's name, photo, date of birth, and address, and contains an IC chip used for online government services, tax filing, and health insurance.

glosses: unlimited time plan; free time (as a service pricing option)
unlimited time plan; all-you-can-use time; free-time package
explanations: A pricing plan for time-based services under which a customer pays a set fee for unlimited or extended use within a given session — most commonly advertised at karaoke boxes, internet cafés, billiards halls, and manga cafés. Despite the English loan, this is a wasei-eigo term not used this way in English.

glosses: user card; library card; patron card
explanations: A registration card issued to the users of a facility or service — most typically a public library card, but also used at sports centers, community centers, and other membership-based public facilities. It identifies the holder as a registered user and is shown when borrowing items or using services.

An office or counter at a station, airport, public facility, or police jurisdiction where items lost by the public are received, held, and returned to their owners. The formal term seen on signs at train stations and on railway websites.

glosses: from partway through; from the middle (of)
from partway through; starting from the middle; from partway along
explanations: A set phrase meaning 'starting from some point partway through' something — an event, a story, a route, a process, or a period. Combines the noun {途中|とちゅう} (on the way; partway) with the starting-point particle から (from).

The reference interest rate used as a baseline for setting the rates on loans, mortgages, and other financial products. A bank's advertised loan rate is typically expressed as 'the benchmark rate plus/minus X percentage points'.

glosses: seasonal event; seasonal observance; seasonal tradition
explanations: A recurring event, custom, or observance tied to a particular time of year — such as {花見|はなみ} in spring, {花火|はなび}{大会|たいかい} in summer, {月見|つきみ} in autumn, or {正月|しょうがつ} in winter. Includes both traditional cultural observances and modern seasonal promotions at schools, shops, and community groups.

glosses: averaging; leveling (out); smoothing out; standardization (toward an average)
explanations: The process of reducing variation across items, people, or values so that they become closer to a common average. Used both in technical/statistical contexts (smoothing data, leveling workload) and in social ones (standardization of wages, service quality, or abilities).

A device that records audio or video for later playback. In everyday Japanese usage, most often refers to a television/video recorder (especially a Blu-ray or hard-disk recorder) or an audio recording device such as a voice recorder or digital audio recorder.

A device for making audio recordings. Historically referred to tape and reel-to-reel machines; today the word is still used generically for audio recorders, though in casual conversation about handheld digital recorders speakers usually say {ボイスレコーダー} or ICレコーダー instead.

glosses: to brush (hair, clothes, teeth, etc.); to apply a brush to
to brush (hair, clothes, a surface); to give (something) a brushing
explanations: A verb phrase meaning to apply a brush to something — most commonly one's hair, clothes, pets, or shoes. The combination of ブラシ (brush) with かける ('to apply, to run over') expresses the action of using a brush in one smooth movement across a surface.

A line that runs vertically, or more precisely a line that meets another line or plane at right angles. Used in geometry, physics, and architecture, as well as in everyday descriptions of shapes on screens and paper.

A line that crosses or intersects another line or path. Used in geometry and technical drawing for lines that share a common point with another line, and more broadly for any line that cuts across something — for example, lines drawn through text or crosshatched patterns in illustrations.

The service provided to customers by a company — both the department or staff dedicated to handling customer inquiries and complaints, and the broader concept of how a company treats its customers before, during, and after a purchase.

An observable pattern of thought, feeling, perception, or behavior studied by psychology — including cognitive biases, optical illusions, group dynamics, and other regular effects that appear across people under similar conditions.

A facility where eggs — most commonly those of fish, chickens, or other birds — are incubated and hatched under controlled conditions. Used in fisheries, poultry farming, and conservation programs for releasing young fish or birds into the wild.
A device that keeps eggs at the right temperature and humidity so that they will hatch. Used on poultry farms, in schools for educational observation, and by hobbyists who breed birds or reptiles.

A fine-grained, dark-colored volcanic rock formed from rapidly cooled lava. It is the most common rock on the Earth's surface and covers large areas of the ocean floor, as well as many volcanic regions in Japan. In everyday Japanese, the word appears mainly in geology, geography, and tourism contexts.

A fine-grained sedimentary rock formed from hardened mud — a mixture of clay and silt particles deposited in still water such as lakes or the deep sea. Often contains fossils and, in some regions, petroleum or natural gas.

glosses: imprisonment without labor (as a criminal sentence)
explanations: A form of imprisonment under Japanese criminal law in which the convict is confined to a prison but, unlike {懲役刑|ちょうえきけい}, is not required to perform compulsory labor. Historically given for crimes considered to involve no moral turpitude, such as some negligence offenses. Under criminal-law reforms that take effect from 2025, {禁固刑|きんこけい} is being unified with {懲役刑|ちょうえきけい} into a single sentence called {拘禁刑|こうきんけい}.

glosses: member (of a group, troupe, or organization)
member of a group / troupe / corps / squad
explanations: A person who belongs to an organized group whose name ends in -{団|だん} — for example a theater troupe, orchestra, children's sports team, fire brigade, scout group, or boys' and girls' club. The word identifies the person as one of the members, without specifying rank.

glosses: outer frame; outer border; outer framework
explanations: The outermost frame of a structure, such as a window, picture, table, or screen layout. In contrast with {内枠|うちわく} (inner frame), {外枠|そとわく} encloses the whole object on the outside. Also used figuratively for the outer limits or overall framework of a plan, budget, or rule.

A device or appliance that mixes liquids, pastes, or powders by rotating blades or a paddle. Found in kitchens (food mixers, blenders), laboratories (magnetic stirrers, vortex mixers), construction (mortar mixers), and industrial plants (large tanks with powered impellers).

An acute viral infectious disease spread by mosquitoes, occurring in tropical regions of Africa and South America. Causes high fever, jaundice (hence the "yellow" in the name), bleeding, and in severe cases organ failure. Travelers to endemic areas are often required to show proof of vaccination.

One of the three main types of muscle tissue in the body. Skeletal muscles are attached to bones by tendons and, unlike smooth or cardiac muscle, are under voluntary control — they contract when we choose to move. They make up roughly 40% of body weight in healthy adults.
Eggs beaten and cooked in a pan with stirring, usually served as a breakfast dish. A common Western-style breakfast item in Japan, often paired with bacon, sausage, or toast.

A unit of length equal to one hundredth of a meter. The everyday unit of length in Japan for small-to-medium measurements such as clothing sizes, furniture, and body measurements. Often shortened to センチ in casual speech.

A piece of bedroom furniture consisting of a table with a large mirror and drawers, used for applying makeup, styling hair, and storing cosmetics and accessories. In Japanese usage, ドレッサー most commonly refers to this vanity table, not a chest of drawers.
Salt-cured eggs (roe) of sturgeon, served as a luxury delicacy. Widely known in Japan as one of the 'three great delicacies of the world' along with foie gras and truffles.

glosses: boiler (for heating water or generating steam)
explanations: A closed vessel that heats water or produces steam, used for building heating, hot water supply, baths, or industrial power. Commonly found in apartment buildings, factories, public baths, and hotels.

A brass instrument with a circular coiled tube and a wide, flared bell, played by buzzing the lips into a funnel-shaped mouthpiece. Known for its warm, mellow tone and used in orchestras, wind ensembles, and brass bands. In Japanese, ホルン most commonly refers specifically to the French horn.
A headwear item with a brim but no crown on top, worn to shade the eyes and face from the sun. Popular for outdoor sports like tennis and golf, as well as gardening and walking.
The flip-down panel mounted above the windshield inside a car, used to block sunlight while driving.

A person who goes on hikes, typically walking for recreation in nature, mountains, or trails. In Japanese usage, ハイカー usually refers to casual day hikers, as opposed to serious mountain climbers ({登山家|とざんか}).
A thin, non-slip mat used during yoga practice to provide cushioning for the body and grip for the hands and feet. Also widely used for general home stretching, pilates, and core exercises.

The transmission of video and audio over the internet in real time, typically via platforms such as YouTube, Twitch, Instagram, or TikTok. Covers streamed performances, gaming broadcasts, events, and personal broadcasts by influencers.

glosses: channel subscription; subscribing to a channel
explanations: Subscribing to a content creator's channel on a video platform such as YouTube, so that the viewer is notified of new uploads and the channel appears in their subscription feed. Heard constantly in YouTuber videos in the standard appeal to viewers.

A battery that can be recharged and reused multiple times, as opposed to a single-use disposable battery. Includes both standard-shaped (AA/AAA) rechargeable cells and built-in batteries in devices such as smartphones and laptops.

glosses: surcharge; premium; extra fee added to a base price
explanations: An additional amount added to the regular fee under specific conditions — late-night hours, holidays, oversized or overweight items, overtime work, peak seasons, and the like. Appears on taxi receipts, delivery invoices, utility bills, and airline tickets.

glosses: electric hot water dispenser; electric thermos pot
explanations: A countertop appliance that boils water and keeps it hot at a set temperature, dispensing it on demand with a pump or lever. A common fixture in Japanese homes and offices, used throughout the day for making tea, instant coffee, instant noodles, and baby formula.

glosses: family care leave; leave of absence from work to care for a family member
explanations: A statutory leave of absence in Japan that allows employees to stop working temporarily in order to care for a family member who requires nursing care due to illness, injury, or old age. Under Japanese law, eligible workers may take up to 93 days of {介護休業|かいごきゅうぎょう} per family member needing care.

glosses: browned surface; sear marks; golden-brown color on grilled or fried food
explanations: The browned, slightly charred color and surface texture that develops on food when it is grilled, seared, or fried at high heat. A key element of both appearance and flavor in Japanese cooking, especially for fish, meat, and grilled vegetables.

glosses: to take (someone) along; to bring (someone) with you
to take someone along; to bring someone with you (to a destination)
explanations: To accompany someone by taking them from the current location to another place. The subject physically leads or brings the other person, who is normally a human or animal (not an inanimate object — for inanimate objects use {持|も}っていく). Direction is away from the speaker's reference point.

glosses: test kit; testing kit (typically for medical or home diagnostic testing)
explanations: A packaged set of tools and reagents for carrying out a specific test, especially medical tests done at home or on-site. Became widely familiar to the general public during the COVID-19 pandemic, when self-administered antigen test kits ({抗原|こうげん}{検査|けんさ}キット) were sold over the counter.

glosses: margin of error; error range; error tolerance
explanations: The range within which measured or estimated values are considered to deviate from the true value, treated as acceptable or expected variation. Used in statistics, polling, science, and engineering, and also colloquially to mean 'close enough' or 'negligible difference'.

News coverage or an interview obtained by a single media outlet with no access granted to competitors. A common selling point on magazine covers and in TV news promotion, signaling that the content cannot be seen or read elsewhere.

glosses: individually; separately; one by one; case by case
explanations: Adverbial form of the na-adjective/noun {個別|こべつ} ('individual, separate'). Indicates that an action applies to each person or item one at a time rather than collectively. Common in business, educational, and administrative contexts for describing tailored handling of cases, requests, or instruction.

glosses: those (things or people far from both speaker and listener)
those; those things; those people (at a distance from both speaker and listener)
explanations: Plural form of the demonstrative pronoun あれ ('that, over there'). Refers to multiple things or people that are spatially or conceptually distant from both speaker and listener. Relatively uncommon in everyday speech; speakers more often repeat あれ or restate the referent noun. It shows up most in written or slightly formal contexts.

glosses: breaking and entering; home invasion; burglary (using force)
breaking and entering; home invasion; forced-entry robbery
explanations: Forced entry into a residence or business, typically to commit robbery, often while the occupants are inside. Also refers by extension to the person who does this. A standard term in crime news reports.

glosses: to spin round and round; to go round in circles
to spin round and round; to rotate continuously; to go round in circles
explanations: To turn repeatedly in a circular motion, whether literally (a wheel, a top, a carousel) or figuratively (one's thoughts, a conversation that gets nowhere). The mimetic adverb ぐるぐる suggests multiple continuous rotations rather than a single turn.

glosses: breach (in a levee or embankment); break point
breach in a levee, dike, or embankment; the point where a barrier has given way
explanations: The physical gap where a levee, dike, or other water-retaining structure has collapsed under pressure, allowing water to flow through. Appears often in disaster and flood reporting, especially after heavy rain or typhoons in Japan.

glosses: irreplaceable; one of a kind; having no substitute
explanations: Describes something or someone that cannot be replaced, because no substitute of equal value exists. The phrase is essentially a fixed collocation built on {代|か}わり ('substitute, replacement'), and is used to express deep emotional value, especially for people and meaningful things.

glosses: peeping (Tom); voyeurism (illegal act of secretly watching someone)
a peek; a quick glance (neutral sense)
explanations: The act of secretly watching someone — typically through a window, gap, or small hole — especially in a sexual or invasive context. Used as a legal and news term for the crime of voyeurism, and also as a noun for the person who does this (a 'Peeping Tom').
A brief or partial look at something through a small opening or from around a corner. Neutral usage, often appearing in compounds like {覗|のぞ}き{穴|あな} ('peephole') or {覗|のぞ}き{見|み} ('a peek').

glosses: internal; in-house; relating to the inside of an organization or system
explanations: Describes something confined to the inside of an organization, group, system, or entity — as opposed to being external or public. Commonly used in business, legal, and technical writing to contrast with {外部的|がいぶてき} ('external').

glosses: creator; producer; maker (of a creative or media work)
explanations: A person (or group) who makes a creative work — including films, videos, TV programs, games, websites, artworks, or other media. Emphasizes authorship or hands-on involvement in the creation process. Written in formal, credit-line, or descriptive contexts.

glosses: the high seas; international waters (sea areas beyond any nation's jurisdiction)
explanations: The parts of the ocean that lie outside any country's territorial waters or exclusive economic zone, and are therefore open to navigation, fishing, and other uses by all nations under international law. A formal term in international law, maritime affairs, and news reporting.

glosses: overnight train; night train (a train that runs through the night, often with sleeper cars)
explanations: A train that travels during the night, allowing passengers to make long-distance trips while sleeping. In Japan, the category traditionally includes sleeper express trains ({寝台|しんだい}{特急|とっきゅう}), though most such services have been discontinued in recent decades.

glosses: mechanical pencil; propelling pencil (with refillable leads)
explanations: A pencil with a thin lead that can be extended or retracted using a mechanism, typically by clicking the end. Refill leads are replaceable. In casual speech, almost always shortened to {シャーペン}. The full form {シャープペンシル} sounds slightly formal or old-fashioned.

glosses: entering a garage/warehouse; stocking in; returning to depot
warehousing; putting goods into a warehouse; stocking in
(a train, bus, etc.) returning to the depot/garage; (a car) entering a parking garage
explanations: The act of bringing goods or inventory into a warehouse or storeroom and registering them as stock. Standard logistics and retail term; contrasts with {出庫|しゅっこ} ('shipping out; stock out').

The act of a vehicle going back into its garage, depot, or parking structure. Used for trains returning to rail yards at the end of service, buses going back to the depot, or a car entering a parking garage.

A dedicated facility for playing baseball, ranging from a simple public field with a backstop and dirt infield to a major league-sized stadium with stands and lights. The standard generic term for any baseball-playing venue.

glosses: a quotation; quoted passage; cited text
explanations: A sentence or passage taken verbatim from another source and used in one's own writing or speech. Standard term in academic writing, journalism, and book reviews. Contrasted with original prose and with paraphrase.

glosses: quotation marks; quote marks (punctuation marking quoted text)
explanations: Punctuation marks used to enclose a direct quotation, dialogue, or word being referred to as a word. In Japanese this most commonly means 「 」 (single brackets) and 『 』 (double brackets); in Western-style writing it refers to " " and ' '.

glosses: film adaptation; making into a movie
explanations: The act or result of adapting a novel, manga, stage play, or other work into a feature film. Commonly used with する to form a verb meaning 'to adapt (something) into a film.'
The central or innermost portion of a geographical area, city, object, or region. Often used of the downtown core of a city, the inner zone of a typhoon, or the central part of a body or structure.

glosses: charge; responsibility; the area or task one is in charge of
one's charge; assigned responsibility; the people or area one is in charge of
explanations: The specific class, patients, territory, or task that has been assigned to a particular person. Commonly used for a homeroom teacher's class, a nurse's assigned patients, or a salesperson's sales territory.
A situation in which the available supply of food is insufficient to meet needs. Used in discussions of famine, wartime rationing, refugee situations, disaster relief, and global food security.

glosses: broad daylight; the middle of the day
explanations: The bright middle hours of the day. Characteristically used in contexts where something surprising, shocking, or bold happens despite the clear visibility of daytime — crimes committed in public view, hallucinations occurring when one should be lucid, etc.

The ability to hold a conversation — typically referring to skill in a foreign language, but also used for the social skill of conversing well with others. Commonly discussed in language study and communication training.

glosses: sociability; friendliness; ability to get along with others
explanations: The personality trait of enjoying and being skilled at interacting with other people. Frequently discussed as a desirable quality in job applicants, children, and well-adjusted adults.

glosses: crimson; deep red; the red of safflower dye (beni)
explanations: A warm, vivid red with slight orange undertones — the traditional color of {紅|べに} ('rouge'), made from safflower petals and long used as a dye, lipstick, and pigment. Associated with Japanese aesthetic tradition, kimono, and the ink used on hanging scrolls and seals.

glosses: windbreak; wind shield; protection against the wind
windbreak; wind shield; something used to block or shelter from the wind
explanations: A fence, wall, row of trees, tarp, or other barrier placed to block wind. Also used of clothing or gear designed to protect the body from wind.

glosses: plants and animals; flora and fauna
plants and animals; flora and fauna; wildlife
explanations: A collective term covering both animals ({動物|どうぶつ}) and plants ({植物|しょくぶつ}). Used in discussions of biodiversity, ecosystems, nature conservation, and regional wildlife.

A person who has acquired a high level of skill through long practice or training, typically in a trade, craft, or technical field. Contrasted with {初心者|しょしんしゃ} ('beginner') and {未熟者|みじゅくもの} ('an unskilled person').

glosses: dining car; a train car fitted out as a restaurant
explanations: A passenger train car equipped with tables and a kitchen, where passengers can order and eat meals while traveling. Once common on long-distance Japanese trains, now rare except on luxury tourist services.
The soft paper on a roll used in bathrooms. Everyday word used at home, in stores, and in product packaging.
A toilet facility in a park, train station, street, or other public space, available for general use. Distinct from toilets inside stores, restaurants, or private buildings.
A bomb that releases energy through nuclear fission or fusion, capable of massive destruction. An umbrella term covering both {原子爆弾|げんしばくだん} ('atomic bomb') and {水素爆弾|すいそばくだん} ('hydrogen bomb').

glosses: mailing address; destination address (for shipping or forwarding)
mailing address; shipping address; recipient's address
explanations: The address to which documents, parcels, or other materials are to be sent. Standard term on shipping labels, order forms, and business correspondence.

The department within a company or organization responsible for general administrative matters — office management, facilities, company-wide events, supplies, and other functions not handled by specialized departments.

glosses: forerunner; pioneer; harbinger; the first of its kind
forerunner; pioneer; the first of its kind
explanations: The earliest example of something — a person, work, event, or phenomenon — that precedes and paves the way for others. Commonly used of pioneers in a field, early signs of a trend, or seasonal firsts such as the first flowers of spring.

A wild, typically four-legged mammal — a deer, boar, bear, fox, and the like. Carries a wilder, more primitive connotation than the neutral {動物|どうぶつ} ('animal'), and is often used in figurative or literary contexts.

glosses: subspecies; biological variant below the species level
explanations: In biology, a taxonomic rank immediately below species, distinguishing populations that are geographically or morphologically distinct but still able to interbreed. By extension, used metaphorically for a variant or subtype of any category.

glosses: same kind; same species; of the same type
same kind; same type; of the same species
explanations: Belonging to the same category or type. Used in biology to mean 'the same species,' in law and business for 'the same kind of offense / product / case,' and in everyday speech for 'the same type' generally.

glosses: archery; the art of the bow (as a traditional Japanese martial art)
explanations: The classical Japanese martial art of shooting with a bow. Historically referred to battlefield archery practiced by samurai; today the related modern discipline {弓道|きゅうどう} is more widely practiced, with {弓術|きゅうじゅつ} retaining its older, traditional associations.
The individual elements that together make up a whole. Used across fields — grammar, chemistry, software, systems engineering, social theory — to refer to the parts of which something is composed.

glosses: shoulder wrap; shawl; shoulder bag (item slung over the shoulder)
a shawl or wrap worn over the shoulders; (also) something designed to be slung over the shoulder, such as a shoulder bag
explanations: Originally a piece of cloth such as a shawl draped over the shoulders for warmth. Extended in compounds to mean 'worn over the shoulder,' as in {肩掛|かたか}けカバン ('shoulder bag').

A carboxylic acid with a long hydrocarbon chain. Fatty acids are the building blocks of fats and oils and play key roles in nutrition, metabolism, and the chemistry of food and skincare products. Commonly discussed in terms of {飽和|ほうわ}{脂肪酸|しぼうさん} ('saturated fatty acids') and {不飽和|ふほうわ}{脂肪酸|しぼうさん} ('unsaturated fatty acids').

glosses: sexual; erotic; relating to sex or sexuality
explanations: Describes something as pertaining to sex, sexuality, or sexual activity. Used in a neutral, often clinical or formal register in medical, legal, and social-science contexts (sexual orientation, sexual harassment, sexual violence), but also applies to everyday discussion of sexual desire, attraction, and erotic content.

glosses: sleeping outdoors; camping out in the open
sleeping outdoors; camping out (without a tent or proper shelter); roughing it
explanations: Spending the night outside without staying at an inn, house, or formal campsite. The image is of sleeping on the ground, under the stars, in a park, a {河原|かわら} ('riverbed'), a mountain, or a {駅|えき} ('station'). It does not require a tent; pitching a tent at a designated campground is usually called {キャンプ|} rather than {野宿|のじゅく}. Can be chosen (travelers, adventurers) or unavoidable (hikers caught by darkness, people without a place to stay).

Unable or unwilling to accept views, behaviors, or people different from one's own; lacking generosity of spirit. Describes a person's disposition or an institution's attitude, often in critical or reflective writing. More formal and literary than {心|こころ}が{狭|せま}い, which is the everyday equivalent.

Containing poison or producing harmful effects on living organisms. Used in chemistry, biology, medicine, environmental science, and food-safety contexts to describe substances, gases, plants, and animals that can injure or kill. A neutral scientific/formal term — not metaphorical ('toxic' relationship, 'toxic' behavior). Functions as both a na-adjective and a no-adjective; also very common as a prefix in compound nouns: {有毒|ゆうどく}ガス ('toxic gas').

A formal, on-site check conducted by an authority to verify compliance with laws, regulations, treaties, or internal rules. Typical contexts include tax audits by the National Tax Agency, nuclear non-proliferation inspections by the IAEA, workplace safety inspections, and internal-audit visits by a company headquarters to a branch. The nuance is of an authority coming in to look, not merely reviewing documents from afar.

glosses: predecessor; forerunner; those who came before
predecessor; forerunner; those who came before; our forebears
explanations: People who lived or worked in the past, especially those whose achievements, wisdom, or example serve as a legacy to later generations. Typically collective rather than pointing to one individual, and carries a tone of respect. Often appears in essays, speeches, and commemorative writing in phrases like '{先人|せんじん}の{知恵|ちえ}' ('the wisdom of our forebears') or '{先人|せんじん}の{努力|どりょく}' ('the efforts of those before us').

glosses: coma; deep unconscious state from which a person cannot be awakened
explanations: A medical term for the most severe level of impaired consciousness: the patient does not open their eyes, cannot speak, and does not respond even to strong painful stimuli. Distinct from ordinary sleep or fainting. Frequently appears in medical reports and news about serious illness, injury, or overdose. Used as a verbal noun with する ({昏睡|こんすい}する 'to fall into a coma'), but the phrase {昏睡|こんすい}{状態|じょうたい} ('comatose state') is by far the most common form.

A person known for publicly putting forward strong, clearly reasoned opinions on political, social, or cultural issues. A {論客|ろんきゃく} is someone whom others recognize as articulate and hard to argue against — whether a newspaper columnist, a TV commentator, or an active participant in academic debate. The term is mildly honorific in tone but can be used with a touch of irony when the person is overly fond of arguing.

glosses: obscene; indecent; lewd (especially in a legally or socially unacceptable way)
explanations: Describes sexual content, acts, or depictions considered a violation of public decency. In Japanese, {猥褻|わいせつ} is primarily a legal and news-media term: it appears in criminal-law names of offenses ({強制|きょうせい}{猥褻|わいせつ}{罪|ざい} 'indecent assault', {猥褻|わいせつ}{物頒布|ぶつはんぷ}{罪|ざい} 'distribution of obscene materials') and in reports of arrests for indecent exposure, groping, or sexual molestation. Much more formal and more strongly negative than everyday words like エッチ or いやらしい.

The drive or appetite for sexual activity. A neutral term used in medical, psychological, and everyday contexts to discuss one of the basic human appetites. Often listed alongside {食欲|しょくよく} ('appetite for food') and {睡眠欲|すいみんよく} ('desire for sleep') as one of the '{三大|さんだい}{欲求|よっきゅう}' ('three great desires') of human life.

Describes a tool, machine, facility, or material that can serve many different uses. Primarily attaches to a noun as a modifier either directly ({多用途|たようと}{機|き} 'multi-purpose machine') or with の ({多用途|たようと}の{布|ぬの} 'versatile cloth'). Common in product descriptions, marketing copy, defense news, and technical contexts.

glosses: drawing a figure; geometric construction; drafting
drawing a figure; geometric construction; drafting (a diagram or plan)
explanations: The act of producing a geometric figure, diagram, technical drawing, or plan — typically following a set of rules or requirements. Most often encountered in (a) school mathematics, where it refers to classical ruler-and-compass constructions, and (b) engineering/architecture, where it refers to producing technical drawings. Used as a verbal noun with する: {作図|さくず}する ('to draw a figure; to draft').

glosses: the art of the staff (a Japanese martial art)
bōjutsu; the martial art of fighting with a staff
explanations: A traditional Japanese martial art that uses a wooden staff, typically around 180 cm long (the {六|ろく}{尺|しゃく}{棒|ぼう}, 'six-foot staff'), as its principal weapon. Techniques include strikes, thrusts, sweeps, and blocks, and {棒術|ぼうじゅつ} is one component of classical weapons training ({古武道|こぶどう}), often taught alongside or within schools of {柔術|じゅうじゅつ} or {剣術|けんじゅつ}. Also refers to the broader category of staff-based martial techniques.

glosses: conceptual; abstract; pertaining to concepts rather than concrete reality
explanations: Describes something that exists at the level of ideas or general notions rather than in concrete, observable form. Often contrasts with {具体的|ぐたいてき} ('concrete; specific') and is used in academic, philosophical, and business discussions to characterize frameworks, models, or explanations that remain abstract.

Describes something that arises or is produced from a more fundamental thing, rather than existing in its own right. Used of concepts, meanings, products, effects, and problems that branch off from a primary source. Often contrasts with {本来|ほんらい}の ('original; intrinsic') or {主|おも}な ('main; primary').

glosses: local; localized; limited to a small area
localized; limited to a particular place or part
explanations: Describes a phenomenon, problem, or effect that is confined to a small or specific area rather than spread widely. Common in weather reports, medicine, engineering, and discussions of systems or regions. Usually contrasts with {全体的|ぜんたいてき} ('overall; general') or {広範|こうはん}な ('wide-ranging').

glosses: pioneering; groundbreaking; ahead of its time
explanations: Describes a person, work, idea, or initiative that leads the way in a field, doing something before others do. Usually carries positive evaluation: praises originality and vision. Common in reviews of art, research, technology, and social movements.

Describes reasoning, arguments, statements, or actions that do not follow logical principles. Typically used negatively to criticize reasoning that is inconsistent, unreasoned, or based on emotion rather than analysis. The direct antonym is {論理的|ろんりてき} ('logical').

glosses: irrational; contrary to reason; not conforming to rational principles
explanations: Describes behavior, beliefs, systems, or decisions that go against reason or rational judgment. Frequently used in economics, psychology, and philosophy to label actions that maximize neither efficiency nor logic. The direct antonym is {合理的|ごうりてき} ('rational; reasonable').

glosses: emotional; sentimental; driven by feelings rather than reason
explanations: Describes reactions, judgments, or atmospheres that are grounded in feeling. When applied to a person's response it often carries a mildly critical nuance of being overly swayed by emotion rather than thinking calmly. When applied to places or scenes it can be neutral or positive, evoking an evocative, atmospheric mood.

Describes an atmosphere, attitude, or relationship characterized by goodwill and cooperation rather than hostility. Often used in formal settings — diplomacy, business, and public statements — to describe relations between countries, companies, or groups. Carries a more measured, official tone than the everyday word {親切|しんせつ} ('kind').

glosses: phenomenology (the philosophical study of structures of experience and consciousness)
explanations: A branch of twentieth-century philosophy founded by Edmund Husserl that investigates phenomena as they appear in conscious experience, setting aside presuppositions about their underlying reality. Subsequent figures — Heidegger, Merleau-Ponty, Sartre — developed the method in different directions. In Japan, {現象学|げんしょうがく} is a standard topic in philosophy departments and in the history of Western thought.

A fence or barrier installed to protect people, vehicles, or property from danger. The term covers a wide range of structures, from steel guardrails along roads ({ガードレール}) to fencing around construction sites, power substations, train platforms, animal enclosures, and restricted areas. The key nuance is purpose: the barrier exists to prevent harm or intrusion, not merely to mark a boundary.

glosses: fit-like; impulsive; on a sudden impulse
impulsive; seizure-like; happening on a sudden, uncontrollable urge
explanations: Describes behavior or emotional reactions that erupt suddenly, like a fit or seizure, and which the person cannot easily control. Used mostly of urges, rage, weeping, or impulsive actions — often the kind the speaker later regrets. The underlying noun {発作|ほっさ} literally refers to a medical attack or seizure (e.g., asthma or epilepsy), which gives the adjective its nuance of uncontrollable, sudden onset.

glosses: number of visitors; customer count; attendance
number of visitors; customer count; number of people who come to a place
explanations: A numerical count of visitors, guests, or customers coming to a business, event, facility, or home. Common in retail, hospitality, and event management to track attendance. Can describe shop customers, exhibition attendees, or household visitors depending on context.

glosses: drop in water level; decrease in water volume
a drop in water level; decrease in water volume (of a river, reservoir, lake, etc.)
explanations: A fall or reduction in the water level or stored volume of a body of water. Used of rivers, reservoirs ({ダム}), lakes, and ponds, typically during droughts or dry seasons. Often appears in news about water shortages alongside {渇水|かっすい} ('water shortage') and {節水|せっすい} ('water conservation'). The antonym is {増水|ぞうすい} ('rising water').

glosses: photo studio; room equipped for taking photographs
explanations: A dedicated room or small studio for taking photographs, typically equipped with backgrounds, lighting, and a camera setup. Found inside department stores, hotels, schools, hospitals, and government offices, {写真室|しゃしんしつ} is often used for ID photos, portraits, and commemorative pictures. Distinct from the freestanding commercial {写真館|しゃしんかん} ('photo studio'), which is a whole shop rather than a room within a larger facility.

glosses: life-size; life-sized; in the same dimensions as a real human body
explanations: Describes an object — most often a statue, doll, poster, or mannequin — that is made in the exact proportions and size of a real human. Literally 'in the size of one's (whole) body'.
Figurative use: describes a portrayal or self-image that presents a person honestly, without exaggeration or idealization. Common in talking about fiction, memoirs, and public personas.

glosses: co-pilot; first officer; second-in-command pilot of an aircraft
explanations: The pilot who assists and serves under the captain on the flight deck. In commercial aviation the {副操縦士|ふくそうじゅうし} is the licensed pilot who occupies the right-hand seat, shares flying duties with the {機長|きちょう} ('captain'), and is qualified to take over the controls if needed. English 'first officer' and 'co-pilot' both correspond to this term.

glosses: mollusk; a member of the phylum Mollusca
explanations: The biological phylum that includes snails, slugs, clams, oysters, octopuses, and squid. Characterized by a soft, unsegmented body, typically protected by a hard shell. {軟体動物|なんたいどうぶつ} is the standard Japanese equivalent of the scientific term 'Mollusca'.

glosses: luxury cruise ship; luxury passenger liner
explanations: A large, richly appointed passenger ship that carries tourists on multi-day cruises, typically equipped with restaurants, theaters, swimming pools, and premium cabins. The term is used especially in travel advertising and news coverage of tourism.

glosses: tea whisk; bamboo whisk used to prepare matcha
explanations: A small whisk carved from a single piece of bamboo, with fine tines splayed outward, used in the Japanese tea ceremony to whisk powdered green tea ({抹茶|まっちゃ}) into hot water. The splitting of the bamboo into many thin tines is what gives the whisk its characteristic shape and frothing ability.

glosses: tea scoop; bamboo scoop for matcha
tea scoop; slender bamboo scoop used to measure matcha powder
explanations: A narrow, slightly curved utensil — usually carved from a single piece of bamboo — used in the Japanese tea ceremony to scoop powdered green tea ({抹茶|まっちゃ}) from the caddy into the tea bowl. Although simple in appearance, {茶杓|ちゃしゃく} are valued as art objects, often given poetic names ({銘|めい}) by their makers or owners.

glosses: truthful; genuine; unfeigned; free of falsehood
explanations: A set prenominal phrase used to describe a statement, feeling, attitude, or person as completely honest and free of any deception or exaggeration. Literally 'without falsehood'. It is somewhat formal and often occurs in written language, testimony, declarations, and heartfelt personal statements.

glosses: to open one's mouth; to open (a container)
to open one's mouth (to speak, yawn, or receive food, medicine, or a dental exam)
to open (a bottle, package, or other container); to unseal
explanations: The basic, literal sense: to physically open the mouth. Commonly heard at the dentist ({口|くち}を{大|おお}きく{開|あ}けてください), when feeding a baby or an animal, or when describing someone yawning or singing. Note: for the sense 'to start talking; to speak up', Japanese usually prefers {口|くち}を{開|ひら}く with the reading ひらく.

By extension from the 'mouth' metaphor for openings: to remove the cap or seal of a bottle, jar, bag, or similar container, often for the first time. Common with foods, drinks, cosmetics, and medicines.

A common over-the-counter medicine used to relieve pain, reduce fever, and suppress inflammation. Low doses are also prescribed to inhibit blood clotting in patients with cardiovascular disease. The Japanese name is a direct borrowing of the German/English trade name, which became a generic term.

glosses: web page; a single document on the World Wide Web
explanations: A document accessible through a web browser, typically written in HTML, and identified by a URL. In everyday Japanese, ウェブページ refers to an individual page, while ウェブサイト or ホームページ refers to a collection of pages making up a site.

glosses: weasel (various species of the family Mustelidae, especially the Japanese weasel)
explanations: A small, slender carnivorous mammal with a long body, short legs, and brown or yellowish-brown fur. In Japan the term most often refers to the Japanese weasel ({ニホンイタチ|にほんいたち}) and the closely related Siberian weasel ({チョウセンイタチ|ちょうせんいたち}). Weasels are widespread in fields and around houses, and have a reputation for cunning and for emitting a foul-smelling defensive odor.

Describes a person (typically a woman, child, or pet) who is appealing in a warm, likable, lightly flirtatious way — not merely pretty but pleasant to be around. The word is a loanword from English 'charming' and has a somewhat old-fashioned, gentlemanly or complimentary tone; it is more often used in writing and by older speakers than in casual conversation among young people, who prefer かわいい, {魅力的|みりょくてき}, or すてき.

glosses: wreath; garland; a circular arrangement of flowers or greenery
explanations: A ring-shaped decoration woven from flowers, leaves, or artificial flowers. In Japan, large standing {花輪|はなわ} on stands are commonly sent to shop openings, theatrical performances, and funerals as formal congratulatory or condolence gifts. The word also covers smaller hand-made flower crowns and wreaths for doors or graves.

A magnet whose magnetic field is produced by passing an electric current through a coil of wire, usually wound around an iron core. Unlike a permanent magnet, its magnetism can be switched on and off and its strength adjusted by changing the current. Widely used in motors, relays, speakers, scrapyard cranes, and maglev trains.

glosses: poster; contributor; person who submits a post or article
poster; contributor; person who submits a post, comment, or article
explanations: The person who writes and submits a post, comment, photo, or article to a magazine, newspaper, bulletin board, blog, or social media platform. Originally used of readers contributing to print publications; now the default word for someone who posts content online.

glosses: public relations activities; PR activities; publicity work
public relations activities; publicity work carried out by a company, government agency, or organization
explanations: The range of activities an organization undertakes to communicate information about itself or its services to the public — press releases, press conferences, social media posts, information pamphlets, advertising campaigns, and community outreach. The focus is on building understanding and a favorable image rather than on direct sales.

glosses: small amount; small-lot; cut end (of a log or board); edge (of a book)
small amount; small-scale; small-lot (especially of transactions)
cut end (of a log, board, or bundle); the surface where something has been cut
edge (of a book); the three non-spine edges of a bound book
explanations: Used in business and finance to describe small-sized transactions, accounts, or cash. The standard pair is {小口|こぐち} ('small-lot') vs. {大口|おおぐち} ('large-lot'), applied to orders, customers, deposits, donations, and cash handling.

The flat surface exposed when a log, piece of lumber, vegetable, bundle of paper, or similar object is cut. In cooking, {小口|こぐち}{切|ぎ}り means cutting a long item (green onions, cucumbers, etc.) crosswise into thin rounds.
In bookbinding, the three edges of a book other than the spine — top, bottom, and fore-edge. The fore-edge is sometimes specifically called the {前小口|まえこぐち}.

A formal document issued by a government agency, company, school, or other organization to inform the recipient of an official decision, status, or required action — tax assessments, examination results, insurance enrollments, court summonses, and the like. The paper is the physical letter itself; the content (the act of informing) is {通知|つうち}.

glosses: sociology; the academic study of human society, social relationships, and institutions
explanations: The scientific study of society, patterns of social relationships, social interaction, and culture. Named as an academic field, it is the most common Japanese translation of the English term 'sociology' and is used in university department names, course titles, and book titles.

glosses: sleeping car; sleeper car (on a train)
sleeping car; sleeper car (a railway car with beds for overnight passengers)
explanations: A railway car equipped with beds or berths where passengers can sleep during overnight long-distance travel. Once common on Japan's long-distance express trains, such cars have become rare, with only a few luxury 'cruise train' services now operating them.

glosses: strategy guide; walkthrough book (for a video game)
strategy guide; walkthrough book (a printed guide explaining how to clear a video game)
explanations: A printed book that explains how to progress through and complete a video game, typically including maps, item lists, enemy data, and step-by-step walkthroughs. Once a major category of gaming publication; with widespread internet access such guides are now more often found online, but printed {攻略本|こうりゃくぼん} are still released for major titles.

glosses: duet; duo (instrumental performance by two players)
duet; duo — an instrumental piece or performance by two players
explanations: A classical music term for an instrumental performance by two players, or a piece written for two instruments. Used specifically of instrumental duos; a vocal duet is more commonly {二重唱|にじゅうしょう}.

glosses: trio — an instrumental piece or performance by three players
explanations: A classical music term for an instrumental performance by three players, or a piece written for three instruments. Parallel in formation to {二重奏|にじゅうそう} 'duet' and {四重奏|しじゅうそう} 'quartet'; used only of instrumental ensembles.

glosses: aerobic; with oxygen (used attributively, especially in fitness contexts)
explanations: A prefix-like noun meaning 'with oxygen'. In everyday Japanese it is almost always seen attributively, especially in the compound {有酸素運動|ゆうさんそうんどう} ('aerobic exercise'). Contrasts with {無酸素|むさんそ} ('anaerobic; without oxygen').

glosses: headset — a device combining headphones with an attached microphone
explanations: A headphone unit with a microphone attached, worn on the head for hands-free voice communication. Used for phone calls, video meetings, online gaming, and call-center work. Distinguished from ヘッドホン ('headphones'), which has no microphone.

glosses: marina — a small harbor or dock designed for pleasure boats and yachts
explanations: A harbor facility specifically for yachts, motorboats, and other pleasure craft, typically including mooring berths, fueling stations, and clubhouse facilities. Distinguished from a general commercial or fishing port.

glosses: electrical work; electrical construction or installation
electrical work — construction, installation, or repair of electrical wiring and equipment
explanations: The trade and work of installing, maintaining, or repairing electrical systems in buildings, including wiring, outlets, lighting, and major appliances. In Japan, most {電気工事|でんきこうじ} must be performed by a licensed {電気工事士|でんきこうじし} ('licensed electrician').

glosses: derived word; derivative — a word formed from another word by adding an affix or changing its form
explanations: In linguistics, a word that has been created by attaching a prefix or suffix to an existing word, or by some other morphological process. For example, {不自然|ふしぜん} ('unnatural') is a {派生語|はせいご} of {自然|しぜん} ('natural'). Often contrasted with {複合語|ふくごうご} ('compound words').

glosses: proof; substantiation; establishing by evidence (especially in legal or scholarly contexts)
explanations: Demonstrating that a claim or fact is true by presenting evidence. Used primarily in legal proceedings, academic argument, and formal investigation. Also used as a {する}-verb, {立証|りっしょう}する ('to prove; to establish').

glosses: experiential learning; hands-on learning — education in which students learn by directly experiencing an activity
explanations: An educational approach in which students acquire knowledge and skills through direct, practical experience rather than only through lectures or textbooks. In Japan, it is widely used for elementary and junior high school field programs — farming experiences, workplace visits, traditional craft workshops, nature programs, and similar activities.

glosses: method of use; usage; directions for use
method of use; how to use; directions for use
explanations: The procedure for using a particular product, tool, or piece of equipment correctly. Commonly seen on packaging, instruction manuals, and product labels as a heading introducing usage instructions.

glosses: supporting actor — a male actor in a supporting rather than leading role
explanations: A male actor who plays a supporting role rather than the lead in a film, stage play, or television program. Most frequently encountered in the names of film-industry awards such as {助演男優|じょえんだんゆう}{賞|しょう} ('Best Supporting Actor').

glosses: guide light; exit sign; emergency guidance light
guide light; exit sign — illuminated signs that show evacuation routes in buildings
explanations: Illuminated signs installed in buildings to show the direction of emergency exits and evacuation routes. In Japan they are legally required in most public buildings and typically show the familiar green running-figure pictogram. Also used more generally for any light that guides movement (e.g., runway lights, signal lights for ships).

glosses: cuff; the end opening of a sleeve where the hand comes out
explanations: The opening at the end of a sleeve on a shirt, jacket, or other garment — the part that encircles the wrist. Refers to the opening itself as well as to any band, cuff, or trim around it.

A garment without sleeves, or the quality of being sleeveless. Functions both as a noun naming the garment type (a sleeveless top or vest) and as a descriptor indicating that a piece of clothing has no sleeves.

glosses: thyroid gland — the butterfly-shaped endocrine gland at the front of the neck
explanations: The endocrine gland located at the front of the neck, below the Adam's apple, which secretes hormones that regulate metabolism, growth, and body temperature. Most commonly encountered in medical contexts, especially in the names of disorders such as {甲状腺機能亢進症|こうじょうせんきのうこうしんしょう} ('hyperthyroidism').

glosses: lubrication — reducing friction between moving parts, or (figuratively) the smooth operation of a system
explanations: The act or state of making motion smooth by reducing friction. Used literally for machinery (oil between moving parts) and figuratively for the smooth running of organizations, communication, or relationships. Rarely appears as a standalone predicate — almost always found in compounds or in the phrase {潤滑|じゅんかつ}{油|ゆ} ('lubricating oil').

glosses: course fee; tuition for a class or lecture
course fee; the fee paid to attend a class, lecture, seminar, or training program
explanations: The fee charged to attend a non-degree class, lecture series, seminar, workshop, or other training course. Distinct from university tuition ({授業料|じゅぎょうりょう}, {学費|がくひ}), which typically refers to fees for formal schooling. Common in the context of adult education, cram schools, online courses, and professional training.

glosses: rocky mountain; a mountain or hill composed mainly of exposed rock rather than soil and vegetation
explanations: A mountain or hill where rock is prominently exposed at the surface rather than being covered by forest or soil. Often describes steep, bare mountains used for rock climbing or featured in dramatic natural scenery.

glosses: imported car — a car manufactured overseas and brought into Japan for sale
explanations: A car manufactured outside Japan and imported for sale domestically, contrasted with {国産車|こくさんしゃ} (domestically produced cars). In Japan, {輸入車|ゆにゅうしゃ} is often associated with European brands such as BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Audi, and Volkswagen, and carries connotations of higher price and prestige.

glosses: domestic car — a car manufactured in one's own country (especially, in Japan, one produced by a Japanese manufacturer)
explanations: A car made in the speaker's own country. In Japan, this specifically refers to cars produced by Japanese manufacturers such as Toyota, Honda, Nissan, or Mazda, and is contrasted with {輸入車|ゆにゅうしゃ} ('imported car'). Often associated with affordability, good fuel economy, and ease of maintenance in the local market.

glosses: sweat gland — the gland in the skin that produces perspiration
explanations: One of the glands in the skin that secretes sweat. Humans have two main types: {エクリン汗腺|かんせん} (eccrine sweat glands), distributed over most of the body and important for temperature regulation, and {アポクリン汗腺|かんせん} (apocrine sweat glands), found mainly in the armpits and groin and linked to body odor.

glosses: poop; poo — a casual, childlike word for feces
explanations: A casual, childlike term for feces. Widely used by young children, and by adults speaking to children or in humorous, unrefined, or informal contexts. Roughly equivalent in register to English 'poop' or 'poo'. Written in hiragana or katakana; there is no kanji form in common use.

glosses: small boat — a small watercraft, typically propelled by oars, poles, or a small sail, used on rivers, lakes, or along the coast
explanations: A small watercraft such as a rowboat, canoe, or skiff. {舟|ふね} evokes a traditional, human-powered vessel and is contrasted with the larger character {船|ふね}, which is used for ships and larger modern boats. Both are read ふね, but the choice of kanji conveys a difference in scale and register.

glosses: powder (especially cosmetic or fine granular material)
powder — a fine granular substance, especially cosmetic face powder, baby powder, or a fine powdered ingredient
explanations: Loanword from English 'powder'. Most commonly used for cosmetic face powder and similar fine granular substances. It is also used for powdered food ingredients (protein powder, cocoa powder) and for fine, dry snow (パウダースノー). For more traditional or native contexts, the Japanese word {粉|こな} is used instead.

glosses: how many days; what day (of the month)
how many days — asking about or referring to an unspecified number of days
what day (of the month) — asking the date of the month
explanations: Used to ask about the duration of something in days, or to vaguely refer to 'some number of days'. Formed from the question word {何|なん} and the counter {日|にち}.
When paired with the date, {何日|なんにち} asks for the day of the month (the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, etc.). Context or an accompanying word such as {今日|きょう} makes this meaning clear.

glosses: Buddhist — a person who follows or practices Buddhism
explanations: A person who professes Buddhism as their religion or practices it as a way of life. The suffix {徒|と} attaches to religions to designate an adherent (as in {キリスト{教徒|きょうと}} 'Christian', {イスラム{教徒|きょうと}} 'Muslim'). In Japan, formal religious affiliation is often loose, so {仏教徒|ぶっきょうと} is more commonly heard in news, surveys, and descriptions of other countries than as a personal self-identification.

glosses: kenpō — a style of Chinese-origin martial arts emphasizing strikes with the fists, and, by extension, various related martial arts
explanations: A martial art that emphasizes hand strikes, kicks, and throws. Originally referring to Chinese martial arts such as {少林寺|しょうりんじ}{拳法|けんぽう} (Shaolin kenpō), it is also used for Japanese-developed variants like {日本|にほん}{拳法|けんぽう} and {少林寺|しょうりんじ}{拳法|けんぽう} (a modern Japanese martial art founded in 1947). It is a homophone of {憲法|けんぽう} ('constitution') and is distinguished by kanji and context.

glosses: workbook — a book containing exercises and activities for a student or trainee to work through, often used alongside a main textbook
explanations: Loanword from English 'workbook'. Refers to a study book made up of exercises, practice questions, and fill-in activities, typically used as a companion to a main textbook. It may also refer to self-study books for language learning, business skills, or personal development.

glosses: depending on — used after a noun to say that an outcome varies according to that factor
explanations: A fixed pattern [noun] + {次第|しだい}で, meaning 'depending on [noun]' or 'according to [noun]'. It introduces a factor that will determine or influence the result of something. The related form {次第|しだい}だ ends a sentence ('it depends on X'), and {次第|しだい}では adds a stronger conditional nuance ('depending on the circumstances').

glosses: squash — a racquet sport played in an enclosed court by two players using a small rubber ball
squash — a carbonated or still fruit drink, typically made with citrus juice, sugar, and (often) soda water
explanations: The racquet sport in which players hit a small rubber ball against the walls of an enclosed court. Introduced to Japan as an imported sport, it is played at dedicated squash courts and fitness clubs.

A type of fruit-based drink, especially a citrus drink made with lemon or lime juice, sugar, and carbonated or still water. Common varieties in Japan are レモンスカッシュ (lemon squash) and オレンジスカッシュ (orange squash), usually served chilled at coffee shops and restaurants.

glosses: baseball cap — a soft cap with a stiff visor at the front, worn by baseball players and as casual headwear
explanations: A cap with a rounded crown and a stiff visor in front, originally designed for baseball players but now widely worn as casual headwear. In Japan the term is used both for the uniform caps of baseball teams and for the everyday fashion item (which is often also called キャップ in modern usage).

glosses: limit point — the point at which something reaches its limit or threshold, beyond which it can no longer continue or function normally
