explanations: The point at which something reaches its maximum capacity or tolerance, and beyond which it breaks, fails, or undergoes a qualitative change. Used for physical limits (of materials, endurance, patience) as well as abstract limits (of growth, tolerance, performance).

glosses: spoken language — the form of language used in speech, as opposed to writing; colloquial style
explanations: Language as it is actually spoken in conversation, including casual phrasing, sentence-ending particles, contractions, and rhythms of speech that differ from the more formal and tightly structured forms used in writing. Contrasts with {書|か}き{言葉|ことば} ('written language').

glosses: terminal station — the final station on a train or bus line; also used figuratively for a final destination or end point
explanations: The last stop on a rail or bus line, where the service ends and passengers must disembark. Also used figuratively in song lyrics and prose to evoke the end of a journey, a relationship, or a stage of life.

glosses: incinerator — a furnace or facility used to burn waste, garbage, or documents
explanations: A furnace or enclosed burner designed to dispose of waste material — from household garbage processed at municipal facilities to confidential documents burned at hospitals, schools, or government offices.

glosses: past tense — the grammatical form used to describe events or states in the past
explanations: The grammatical form that places an action or state in the past. In Japanese grammar, this typically refers to the {~た}-form of verbs and adjectives (e.g., {食|た}べた, {寒|さむ}かった) and {~でした} for polite noun/na-adjective predicates. The term is also used for the past tenses of English and other foreign languages in language-teaching contexts.

glosses: print shop — a business or facility where books, newspapers, flyers, and other printed material are produced
explanations: A business or workshop where printed material is produced — books, magazines, newspapers, business cards, leaflets, packaging, and so on. Ranges in scale from small neighborhood shops to large industrial printing plants.

glosses: torrential downpour — extremely heavy rain concentrated in a small area over a short time, often causing floods and landslides
explanations: Very heavy rain that falls over a limited area for a short period of time, often a few hours. Common in Japan during the rainy season ({梅雨|つゆ}) and typhoon season, and a frequent cause of flash floods, landslides, and disaster warnings.

glosses: housing for sale (as opposed to rental), for-sale housing unit
housing for sale — a residential property (typically in a development or condominium) that is sold individually to buyers, as opposed to being rented out
explanations: A home or condominium unit that is sold outright to an individual owner, typically as part of a housing development or apartment complex. Contrasts with {賃貸|ちんたい}{住宅|じゅうたく} ('rental housing'). The term is widely used in Japanese real-estate advertising.

glosses: side view — a technical drawing or illustration showing an object or building viewed from the side
explanations: A drawing that shows an object, vehicle, or building as seen from the side. One of the standard views used in technical drawing, architectural drafting, and product design, alongside {正面図|しょうめんず} ('front view') and {平面図|へいめんず} ('plan/top view').

glosses: home healthcare — medical care provided to patients at their own home, by visiting doctors, nurses, or other medical professionals
explanations: Medical care delivered at a patient's home rather than in a hospital or clinic, typically through scheduled visits by doctors ({往診|おうしん}) and nurses ({訪問|ほうもん}{看護|かんご}). Especially important for elderly people with chronic illnesses, patients recovering after discharge, and terminal patients receiving palliative care.

glosses: high-rise building — a tall building with many stories; also, the construction of such buildings
explanations: A tall building with many floors — typically an office tower, condominium, hotel, or public building. Also refers to the activity or industry of constructing such buildings. In Japan the term is often used more or less interchangeably with {高層|こうそう}ビル, though {高層建築|こうそうけんちく} has a slightly more technical or formal ring.

glosses: clever idea, bright idea, ingenious plan
clever idea — a particularly good or ingenious idea or plan, often one that elegantly solves a tricky problem
explanations: A clever, ingenious, or particularly well-suited idea — often one that resolves a problem that seemed difficult, or that is noticeably more elegant than ordinary proposals. Frequently used in phrases expressing that someone has or has not come up with such an idea.

glosses: insulator — a material that does not conduct electricity (or heat) well; e.g., rubber, glass, or ceramic used to block current flow
explanations: A substance that does not readily allow the flow of electric current (and sometimes, by extension, of heat). Examples include rubber, glass, plastics, and ceramics. Used in physics and electrical engineering in contrast to {導体|どうたい} ('conductor') and {半導体|はんどうたい} ('semiconductor').

glosses: amplifier — an electronic device that increases the strength of a signal, especially an audio or radio-frequency signal
explanations: An electronic device or circuit that increases the power, voltage, or current of a signal. Used in audio equipment, radio receivers and transmitters, instrumentation, and many other devices. In everyday audio contexts, the loanword アンプ is far more common, but {増幅器|ぞうふくき} remains the standard technical term.

glosses: second term — the second of the academic terms in a Japanese school year; in a three-term system, roughly September to December
explanations: The second of the terms ({学期|がっき}) in a Japanese school year. In the most common three-term system used by Japanese elementary, junior high, and high schools, the second term runs from around early September (after the summer break) to late December (before the winter break). In two-term systems used by some universities, it corresponds to the fall/autumn semester.

glosses: measuring instrument — a device used to measure weight, volume, length, or other physical quantities; includes scales, meters, and gauges
explanations: A general term for any device used to measure a physical quantity, such as weight, volume, length, or flow rate. In everyday use most commonly refers to weighing scales and kitchen measuring devices, but in technical and legal contexts includes electricity and gas meters, taxi meters, and many industrial instruments.

glosses: stewardess — a female cabin attendant on an airplane
explanations: Loanword from English 'stewardess'. Refers to a woman who works as cabin crew on an airplane, serving passengers and ensuring their safety. In current Japanese usage, this word is considered somewhat dated and gender-marked; the gender-neutral {客室乗務員|きゃくしつじょうむいん} or the loanword キャビンアテンダント (cabin attendant) are now standard in airline industry and news contexts.

glosses: the on-reading of a kanji — the Japanese pronunciation of a Chinese character derived from its original Chinese reading
explanations: Refers to the pronunciation of a kanji that was borrowed from Chinese, as opposed to its native Japanese reading. For example, the {字音|じおん} of {山|さん} is さん (as in {登山|とざん}), while its native reading is やま. Used in linguistic, educational, and dictionary contexts to contrast with {訓読|くんよ}み.

glosses: regulated verse (a traditional Chinese poetic form)
regulated verse — a form of classical Chinese poetry consisting of eight lines with strict tonal, rhyme, and parallelism rules
explanations: A category of classical Chinese poetry ({漢詩|かんし}) that became fully codified in the Tang dynasty. A {律詩|りっし} has eight lines, with a fixed number of characters per line (five or seven), specific rhyme positions, and required tonal parallelism in the middle two couplets. It is one of the main genres studied and composed in Japan within the {漢詩|かんし} tradition.

glosses: the number of sound units (morae) in a word, phrase, or line of verse
explanations: A linguistic and prosodic term meaning the count of {拍|はく} (morae) — the rhythmic units that make up Japanese pronunciation. Used especially in discussions of poetic meter (haiku, tanka), word length, and phonology. Each kana normally counts as one {音|おん}, with small kana like ゃ/ゅ/ょ combining with the previous kana and the long vowel mark ー and geminate っ each counting as one.

glosses: a fine piece, a superior-quality item, a particularly excellent example (of an artwork, antique, or commodity)
explanations: A written, somewhat formal word used mainly for artworks, antiques, tea utensils, and collectable goods to single out a piece of especially high quality among others in its category. Often encountered in auction catalogues, gallery descriptions, and dealer listings.

glosses: I wonder if ...?; might it be that ...? (polite)
a polite sentence-ending expression used to soften a question, express uncertainty, or make a gentle inquiry — roughly 'I wonder if...', 'could it be that...', or 'might it be...?'
explanations: Formed from the polite copula でしょう (conjectural/polite form of だ) plus the question particle か. Used to phrase a question less directly than simple ですか, giving it a more reflective or deferential tone. Appropriate when softening a potentially intrusive question, asking about something uncertain, or politely requesting information from someone of equal or higher status.

glosses: to maintain order; to observe the rules
to maintain order, to keep a peaceful and orderly state, to observe the rules or social norms that keep a group or society functioning
explanations: A common collocation of {秩序|ちつじょ} ('order, orderly arrangement') with {守|まも}る ('to protect, to observe, to keep'). Used in contexts of law, public safety, classrooms, lines and queues, international order, and any situation where a shared system of rules needs to be upheld.

glosses: to be kindly invited; to receive an invitation (humble/formal)
to be kindly invited; to receive an invitation — a formal, humble way of acknowledging that one has been invited by the addressee or by a person the speaker respects
explanations: A set phrase combining お{招|まね}き ('invitation', with the honorific prefix お) and あずかる ('to be granted, to partake of [something offered]', used humbly to receive a favor). Speakers use it to gratefully acknowledge having been invited somewhere, treating the invitation itself as a favor extended to them. Common in formal speeches, thank-you remarks at weddings, parties, and official gatherings.

glosses: onomatopoeia; a word that imitates a sound made by a person, animal, or object
explanations: A linguistic term for words that mimic actual sounds, such as animal cries, natural noises, or human voices. {擬声語|ぎせいご} covers sound-imitating vocabulary in particular; related terms include {擬音語|ぎおんご} (for non-living sound effects) and {擬態語|ぎたいご} (for words describing states or manners rather than sounds).

glosses: a large-scale disturbance or riot; a breakdown of public order in which crowds act violently
explanations: A formal word for serious public disorder — riots, mob violence, or civil unrest. Stronger than {騒動|そうどう} (a commotion) and used in news reports, legal contexts, and historical writing. The word emphasizes that the disturbance is widespread and threatens public order.

glosses: native inhabitants; indigenous people (of a region)
the original inhabitants of a region, especially before the arrival of settlers or colonizers
explanations: Refers to the people who originally lived in a place before others — typically colonists, immigrants, or invaders — arrived. In modern Japanese, this word is sometimes considered dated or inappropriate when talking about indigenous peoples' rights; {先住民|せんじゅうみん} is now preferred in respectful and academic contexts. {原住民|げんじゅうみん} is still commonly used in everyday speech, historical accounts, and travel writing.

glosses: full age; exact age in years as counted from birth
full (completed) age — a person's age counted by completed years since birth, the standard modern way of reckoning age
explanations: The modern Japanese system for counting age, in which a person is 0 at birth and adds one year on each birthday. This is the system used in law, schools, medical records, and everyday life. It contrasts with {数|かぞ}え{年|どし}, the traditional East Asian system that counts the year of birth as 1 and adds a year at the new year, producing a higher number.

glosses: a stadium — a large outdoor or covered sports venue, especially one used for baseball, soccer, or athletics
explanations: A loanword from English 'stadium'. Used for large modern sports facilities, often as part of the venue's official name (e.g., {埼玉|さいたま}スタジアム, {神宮|じんぐう}{球場|きゅうじょう}スタジアム). Distinct from {競技場|きょうぎじょう} (a more general term for a sports ground) and {球場|きゅうじょう} (specifically a baseball ground).

glosses: the previous year — the year immediately before the one being discussed, or the year before a particular reference point
explanations: A formal noun meaning 'the year before'. The reference point is usually clear from context: in business reports it usually means the preceding fiscal year, in narrative writing it means the year before the events described. Very common in economic and statistical contexts in expressions like {前年|ぜんねん}{比|ひ} (compared to the previous year).

glosses: a ski slope; the prepared runs at a ski resort where people ski and snowboard
explanations: A loanword from German 'Gelände'. Used for the groomed, lift-served slopes at a ski resort. In Japanese this word specifically evokes a resort setting — a slope with lifts, groomers, and skiers — rather than the side of a mountain in general.

glosses: a snowboard (the board itself), or the sport of snowboarding
explanations: A loanword from English. Refers to both the snowboard as an object and to the sport of snowboarding. The sport is often abbreviated as スノボ in casual speech. As a verb-like expression, 'to snowboard' is スノーボードをする.

glosses: facial tissues — soft disposable paper tissues, typically sold in a box
explanations: A loanword referring to the soft disposable paper tissues used for blowing the nose or wiping the face. Almost always means boxed or pocket-pack facial tissues; crepe paper and gift tissue paper (the English sense of 'tissue paper') are expressed differently. In everyday speech, often shortened to just ティッシュ.

glosses: distinguished family; renowned house or lineage
a distinguished or prestigious family; a household with a long history and high social standing
explanations: Refers to a family of long-established prestige — typically one known for its ancestors, social position, or achievements in a particular field (politics, the arts, business, a traditional craft). The word carries a tone of respect and often implies inherited status passed down through generations.

glosses: romaji input (method of typing Japanese using the Latin alphabet)
romaji input — the method of typing Japanese on a keyboard by entering romaji, which is then converted to kana and kanji
explanations: The most common way to type Japanese on computers and smartphones: the user types Latin letters such as 'ka' and the IME (input method editor) converts them to か, and then candidates for kanji conversion are offered. Contrasts with かな{入力|にゅうりょく}, in which each key on the keyboard is mapped directly to a kana character.

glosses: a team of trained personnel organized to rescue people in emergencies such as disasters, mountain accidents, or maritime incidents
explanations: A group of trained rescuers — firefighters, coast guard members, mountain rescuers, or military personnel — dispatched to save lives in emergencies. Common compounds specify the context: {山岳|さんがく}{救助隊|きゅうじょたい} (mountain rescue), {海上|かいじょう}{救助隊|きゅうじょたい} (sea rescue), {災害|さいがい}{救助隊|きゅうじょたい} (disaster rescue).

glosses: mechanization (replacement of manual labor by machines)
mechanization — the process of replacing human or animal labor with machines in production, work, or daily life
explanations: Refers to the introduction of machinery to perform tasks that were previously done by hand. Used broadly in discussions of agriculture, manufacturing, office work, and even warfare. Functions as a noun on its own and combines with する to form the verb {機械化|きかいか}する ('to mechanize').

glosses: white cane (used by visually impaired people)
a white cane — the long white stick used by blind or visually impaired people to detect obstacles and to signal their condition to others
explanations: The standard mobility tool used by visually impaired people. In Japan, the white cane also functions as a legal and visual symbol: under the road traffic law, drivers and passersby are required to assist or give way to people holding a white cane. The word appears in public awareness campaigns and in signs at train stations.

glosses: a horn — a simple wind instrument originally made from an animal horn, used for signaling or as a musical instrument
explanations: Refers to a horn instrument, traditionally made from the horn of an animal such as an ox or goat. In Japanese it evokes images of shepherds, hunters, or pre-modern European settings. Modern metal horns such as those in orchestras are usually called {ホルン} instead.

glosses: toothpick — a small pointed stick of wood (or sometimes plastic) used to clean between the teeth or to pick up small pieces of food
explanations: An everyday item commonly found at Japanese restaurants and in households. The word is written in kanji as {爪楊枝|つまようじ} but is very often written in hiragana as つまようじ or even shortened to {楊枝|ようじ} in casual speech.

glosses: rhinitis; inflammation of the nasal mucosa
rhinitis — inflammation of the mucous membrane of the nose, causing sneezing, a runny nose, or congestion; includes allergic rhinitis and hay fever
explanations: A medical term used for inflammation of the nose, whether caused by allergy, infection, or other irritation. The most common compound encountered by learners is {アレルギー{性|せい}{鼻炎|びえん}} (allergic rhinitis), which overlaps heavily with {花粉症|かふんしょう} (hay fever).

glosses: an iron pot or pan — cookware made of cast iron or wrought iron, valued for even heat retention and durability
explanations: Refers to any cooking pot or pan made of iron. Often used in Japanese cooking for dishes that benefit from high heat or long simmering, such as {すき{焼|や}き} or {餃子|ぎょうざ}. Also commonly seen at restaurants as a serving vessel that keeps food hot at the table.

glosses: a person who mediates between two parties — arranging a deal, smoothing a negotiation, or acting as a neutral go-between in a dispute or transaction
explanations: Refers to any individual who stands between two sides and helps them reach an agreement or complete a transaction. The word is broad: it covers real-estate agents, business brokers, diplomatic mediators, and informal go-betweens in personal or social matters.

glosses: participant; contestant; entrant (in a competition or event)
a person who takes part in a competition, contest, tournament, or public performance — a participant or contestant who actually appears on the field, stage, or event
explanations: Used specifically for people participating in an organized event where they appear before others — sports matches, tournaments, speech contests, TV shows, beauty pageants, and the like. Contrast with {参加者|さんかしゃ} (a general "participant"), which covers casual events and meetings too.

glosses: a bento box delivered from a caterer or restaurant — typically ordered in bulk for meetings, funerals, film shoots, or other events rather than individual consumption
explanations: Refers to bento meals prepared by a catering service and delivered to the customer, rather than bento bought at a store or made at home. Usually ordered by offices, event organizers, or families for gatherings, and often more elaborate than convenience-store bento.

glosses: fish meat; fish flesh (as food product)
the flesh of fish, considered as a food ingredient — especially used as a generic or categorical term, or in processed-food names
explanations: A slightly technical or categorical word for fish as meat, in contrast to {肉|にく} when it refers to livestock meat. Commonly seen on food labels and in processed-food names like {魚肉|ぎょにく}ソーセージ (fish sausage) or {魚肉|ぎょにく}ハム. Much less common in everyday cooking speech, where people simply say {魚|さかな}.

glosses: classical vocalist; classical singer; vocal artist
a professional singer in the classical or art-music tradition — typically an opera singer, lieder singer, or trained soloist, as distinguished from a popular or rock singer
explanations: Refers specifically to someone trained in the art of {声楽|せいがく} (classical vocal music) — opera, art song, oratorio, or church music. The word carries an image of formal concert halls, Western classical training, and sustained academic study, and would not be applied to a J-pop singer or street musician.

glosses: accidental discharge (of a firearm); sudden outburst; unplanned eruption
accidental discharge of a firearm — a gun going off unintentionally
a sudden and unplanned outburst; an unprovoked eruption of tension, emotion, or conflict
explanations: The most specific use: a gun firing without the shooter intending it. Typical in news reports about mishandled firearms, training accidents, or hunting incidents.

An extended use for any eruption that breaks out unexpectedly — pent-up anger, a wave of protests, or a conflict that flares up without formal declaration. The nuance is of something latent suddenly breaking out of control.

glosses: dressing as a man; male attire (on a woman); cross-dressing (female-to-male)
the act of a woman dressing in men's clothing, or the male appearance thus produced — includes theatrical cross-dressing, cosplay, and everyday fashion
explanations: Refers specifically to a woman adopting a male appearance through clothing, hairstyle, and sometimes binding or makeup. The word is neutral and covers a wide range of contexts: the all-female {宝塚|たからづか} revue where actors play male roles, anime and manga characters, historical disguise, cosplay, and gender-expression fashion.

glosses: stratified society; class society; hierarchical society
a society structured around distinct layers or classes — with people divided by wealth, occupation, education, or social rank, and limited mobility between the layers
explanations: A sociological term for any society in which social classes ({階層|かいそう}) are clearly differentiated. It can describe historical class-based societies (feudal Japan, Victorian Britain), contemporary societies with sharp inequalities, or ideal-type models in the social sciences.

glosses: an introductory chapter or book that lays out the groundwork of a subject — used especially in academic titles and in the openings of scholarly works
explanations: Found most often in book titles in the humanities, sciences, and philosophy — e.g., 「{哲学|てつがく}{序説|じょせつ}」 ("An Introduction to Philosophy"). More formal and more scholarly than {入門|にゅうもん} or {概論|がいろん}, and typically emphasizes foundational concepts or preliminary arguments that prepare the reader for fuller treatment.

Describes a person, performance, or expression filled with strong, intense emotion — especially devotion, enthusiasm, or romantic feeling. Used in writing and formal speech more than casual conversation, and often describes speeches, performances, love, or dedication to a cause.
A chemistry term for a compound formed when a substance combines with oxygen. Commonly encountered in science textbooks, material science, and articles about rust, corrosion, and batteries.

A literary, bookish word meaning "nothing else compares." Almost always appears attached to another noun as a compound modifier, often in set phrases praising quality, strength, or beauty. Sounds elevated or old-fashioned; common in advertising copy, reviews, and written descriptions of masterworks.

glosses: dealer; pusher; illegal seller (especially of drugs)
explanations: In contemporary Japanese this word almost always refers to someone who sells illegal drugs on the street. It carries strong negative connotations and appears in news reports about drug busts, crime novels, and films. The older general sense of "trader, merchant" has largely faded from everyday use.

glosses: far right; extreme right wing (in politics)
explanations: A political label for the extreme right end of the ideological spectrum — parties, groups, or individuals associated with strong nationalism, anti-immigration positions, or hardline conservatism. Used in news reporting, commentary, and academic writing about politics worldwide.

glosses: far left; extreme left wing (in politics)
explanations: A political label for the extreme left end of the ideological spectrum — groups, parties, or individuals associated with radical socialism, revolutionary communism, or militant leftist activism. Common in news coverage and political commentary.

glosses: refueling; fuel supply; act of supplying fuel to a vehicle, aircraft, or ship
explanations: Supplying fuel — gasoline, jet fuel, bunker oil, and so on — to a vehicle or vessel. Common in aviation, shipping, military, and road-transport contexts. The word can also be used metaphorically for refilling other "reserves."

glosses: handshake event; meet-and-greet (where fans line up to shake hands with celebrities, idols, or authors)
explanations: A fan event where performers — most famously idol group members, but also authors, voice actors, and athletes — line up to greet fans one by one with a brief handshake and a few words. Attendance is typically limited by ticket, often bundled with CD or book purchases. A well-established fixture of Japanese pop culture.

glosses: "girl power"; a woman's collection of feminine skills and charm (cooking, fashion sense, grooming, thoughtfulness, etc.)
explanations: A popular buzzword that arose in the 2000s and remains widely used. It refers to the traditionally "feminine" skills and qualities a woman (or anyone) is seen to possess — polished appearance, stylish clothes, cooking, manners, attentiveness, and attention to detail. Often used half-jokingly by women about themselves or each other.

glosses: female college student; female university student
explanations: A woman currently enrolled at a university or four-year college. A very common everyday word — much more frequent in speech than the formal equivalents — and often used as a demographic label in advertising, media, and casual conversation.

glosses: language ability; linguistic competence; proficiency in understanding and using language
explanations: A person's capacity to understand, produce, and use language — whether their native language or a foreign one. The word is common in educational, psychological, medical (language development or impairment), and linguistic discussions; it also appears in job postings about required foreign-language skills.

glosses: market capitalization; market cap; total market value
market capitalization; total market value (of a company, calculated as share price × shares outstanding)
explanations: A finance term for the total market value of a company's outstanding shares. It is the standard yardstick in news reports for ranking companies by size, comparing global firms, and tracking changes in a company's valuation over time.

glosses: subtropics; subtropical zone; the climatic region between the tropics and temperate zones
explanations: A geographic and climatic term for the zones lying between the true tropics and the temperate belts. In Japan, Okinawa and the Amami Islands are often described this way. Common in weather reports, geography class, and travel writing.

A person who studies or writes philosophy. Used for both academic researchers of philosophy and historical thinkers such as Socrates or Kant. Can also be used loosely, and sometimes playfully, to describe someone who reflects deeply on life.

glosses: receiver; receiving device (for radio, television, or other signals)
explanations: An electronic device that receives and decodes transmitted signals — radio, television, telemetry, satellite, GPS, or other wireless communication. A technical but widely understood word, common in user manuals, news about broadcasting, and explanations of wireless technology.

glosses: daycare child; preschooler at a nursery school
daycare child; a child enrolled at a nursery school / daycare center
explanations: A child between roughly 0 and 6 years old who attends a {保育園|ほいくえん} — a Japanese daycare center that cares for infants and preschool-age children while parents work. Distinguished from kindergarten-goers, who are called {幼稚園児|ようちえんじ}.

glosses: all directions; every direction; omnidirectional (360-degree) coverage
explanations: "In every direction," "on all sides," or "360 degrees." Used literally for cameras, microphones, or sensors that cover all angles, and figuratively for policies, marketing, or attention directed at every possible audience or threat. It often functions as a prefix-like element in compound modifiers.

glosses: excessively; overly; to an undue or unhealthy degree
explanations: The adverbial form of {過剰|かじょう} (excess), used to mark an action or state as going beyond what is appropriate, necessary, or healthy. It usually carries a negative or cautionary tone — reacting too strongly, consuming too much, or worrying more than the situation warrants.

glosses: big ovation; thunderous applause; great acclaim
big ovation; thunderous applause; enthusiastic acclaim
explanations: A large, enthusiastic response of applause, cheering, or praise from an audience or crowd. Most often used for the reaction to a performance, speech, or sporting achievement, but also figuratively for strong public approval of an idea or announcement.

glosses: scrap material; waste wood; discarded building material
scrap material; waste lumber; discarded construction material
explanations: Material — most commonly wood from demolished buildings or offcuts from construction and carpentry — that is no longer needed for its original purpose. Often emphasized in contexts of recycling, upcycling, or disposal, and extended to scrap metal, pallets, and other reusable leftovers.

glosses: namer; person who gives a name; name-giver
namer; name-giver; the person who bestows a name on something or someone
explanations: The individual credited with choosing and giving the name of a person, place, product, species, building, or other entity. Most common in news articles and official contexts (e.g., ship launches, new species descriptions, naming-rights contracts) rather than everyday conversation.

glosses: changing every month; monthly rotation; monthly special
explanations: A schedule or arrangement in which the content, menu, or featured item is replaced with something new each month. Very common in restaurant menus, subscription boxes, magazine features, and display rotations.

glosses: during the period; throughout the period
during the period; throughout the period; while the specified period is ongoing
explanations: Specifies a time frame that begins and ends with a particular period — typically a sale, campaign, exhibition, event, or contract term. Functions both as a noun and, very commonly, as an adverbial modifier placed at the start of a sentence.

glosses: dual citizenship; dual nationality; the condition of holding two nationalities at once
explanations: The status of a person who legally holds the citizenship of two countries simultaneously. A frequent topic in Japan because Japanese law in principle does not allow dual nationality for adults, and individuals with two nationalities are required to choose one before a set age.

glosses: foreign-made; made overseas; of foreign manufacture
explanations: Indicates that a product was manufactured outside of Japan. Used on labels, catalogs, and in conversation to contrast with {国産|こくさん} ('domestic / Japanese-made'). Often functions as a noun modifier ('foreign-made car', 'imported watch'), and can also take の to attach to another noun.

glosses: number of pages; page count; total pages
explanations: The total count of pages in a book, document, report, thesis, or printed material. Used when referring to the length or volume of written content, often in contexts like publishing, academic writing, printing, and office work.

glosses: marking; putting a mark or sign on something for identification
explanations: The act of placing a visible mark, label, or identifying sign on an object, document, surface, or body. Used in manufacturing (product coding), logistics (labeling parcels), sports (player marking), and office work (highlighting passages).
Used especially of cats, dogs, and other mammals spraying urine or rubbing scent to claim territory. A common word in pet-care contexts.

glosses: defensive; protective; aimed at defending or preserving
explanations: Describes an attitude, action, strategy, or posture that is oriented toward defense rather than offense. Used both literally (military, security) and figuratively (psychology, business, sports tactics, debate), often with a mildly critical nuance when it implies being overly cautious or unwilling to take risks.

glosses: notional; theoretical; ideational; divorced from reality
notional; theoretical; ideational; based on abstract ideas rather than concrete reality
explanations: Describes thinking, argument, or planning that stays at the level of ideas without reference to concrete facts or practical considerations. Often carries a negative nuance of being 'armchair' or 'out of touch'. Contrasts with {具体的|ぐたいてき} ('concrete') and {実際的|じっさいてき} ('practical').

glosses: only in the case of; precisely when; of all things, just when
(limiting) only; only in the case of; limited to
(unexpected coincidence) of all times; precisely when; just when it was that
(confident denial) ... of all people; surely not X
explanations: Marks a specific case or a restricted group as the only one that applies, excluding all others. Equivalent to 'only' or 'exclusively' and often used in formal notices and announcements.

Used to express that a negative or inconvenient event happens at exactly the worst possible moment, or that someone normally reliable does something out of character. Conveys surprise, frustration, or irony about the timing or actor.
Used with a negative or a rhetorical question to express strong confidence that the person or thing named would not do the thing in question. Often paired with はずがない or そんなことはない.

glosses: gloss; glossy finish; shiny surface quality
explanations: A cosmetic applied to the lips to add shine, moisture, and a lightly tinted finish. In everyday Japanese, グロス by itself most often refers to lip gloss, with the fuller form リップグロス also used.
A shiny, reflective finish on paint, printed material, photos, nails, or other surfaces. Contrasts with マット ('matte'). Used in printing, design, cosmetics, and product descriptions.

glosses: previous model; existing product; conventional product
explanations: A product that has been on sale or in use until now, implicitly being contrasted with a new, improved, or different version. Typical in product marketing, press releases, and technical comparisons where a manufacturer emphasizes what the new product does better than the previous lineup.

glosses: oily skin; a skin type that produces excess sebum
explanations: One of the standard skin type categories in Japanese cosmetics and dermatology. Describes skin that secretes a large amount of sebum, giving it a shiny appearance and making it prone to clogged pores and breakouts. Contrasts with {乾燥肌|かんそうはだ} ('dry skin') and {混合肌|こんごうはだ} ('combination skin').

glosses: combination skin; a mixed skin type (oily in some areas, dry in others)
explanations: A skin type in which different parts of the face have different characteristics — most commonly oily in the T-zone (forehead, nose, chin) and dry or normal on the cheeks. Standard category in Japanese skincare, alongside {脂性肌|しせいはだ}, {乾燥肌|かんそうはだ}, and {敏感肌|びんかんはだ}.

The formal closing of a meeting, session, conference, ceremony, or similar gathering. Used for official or structured events — Diet sessions, conferences, sports tournaments, academic symposia — rather than casual gatherings. Often paired with its opposite, {開会|かいかい} ('opening').
The act of breathing in — drawing air into the lungs. Used in medical, physiological, and exercise contexts. The opposite is {呼気|こき} ('exhalation').
Air drawn into an engine, ventilation system, or other mechanical device. Common in automotive and HVAC contexts, often combined with {口|こう} or {弁|べん} to name specific parts.

glosses: texture (of food); feel on the teeth; mouthfeel
explanations: The physical sensation a food gives when bitten into — how crisp, soft, chewy, or crunchy it feels against the teeth. A standard term in food writing, product descriptions, and restaurant reviews, focusing specifically on the tactile experience of chewing rather than on taste.
A large warship designed to serve as a seagoing airbase, carrying, launching, and recovering aircraft. The full formal term for what is usually abbreviated in conversation as {空母|くうぼ}.

Using a product, service, or system on a trial basis, typically before committing to full adoption, purchase, or employment. Common in software free trials, product demo programs, and employment probation contexts.

The government function of regulating the entry of foreign nationals into a country — checking passports and visas, issuing residence permits, and enforcing immigration law. Also used to refer to the system or agency responsible for these tasks. Frequently shortened to {入管|にゅうかん}.

glosses: self-publishing; publishing at one's own expense; vanity publishing
self-publishing; publishing at one's own expense
explanations: Publishing a book by paying the production and distribution costs oneself rather than through a commercial publisher's normal contract. In Japan the term covers both author-funded arrangements with specialty {自費|じひ}{出版|しゅっぱん} companies and fully independent self-publishing. Historically carried a vanity-publishing connotation, though digital platforms have broadened its image.

glosses: game record (shogi, go, chess); score sheet of a board game
game record (of shogi, go, or chess); notation of moves
explanations: A written or digital record of the moves played in a game of shogi, go, or (less often) chess. Kept for later study and analysis, and a central part of how professional and amateur players learn. Published for major professional matches in magazines, newspapers, and online databases.

glosses: old age; one's later years; senescence
explanations: The stage of life corresponding to old age, typically beginning around age 65 in Japanese usage. Used in medical, welfare, psychological, and developmental contexts as one of the named life stages ({幼年期|ようねんき}, {少年期|しょうねんき}, {青年期|せいねんき}, {壮年期|そうねんき}, {老年期|ろうねんき}).

A person who earns a living by working for an employer, especially in the context of labor law, economics, or social class. The standard term in legal and political discourse and in statistics; in Japan's Labor Standards Act, a {労働者|ろうどうしゃ} is legally defined as someone employed and paid wages.

The physical, social, or infrastructural environment around a particular location — a house, school, facility, or station — including what businesses, transport, noise levels, and amenities are nearby. Standard in real estate listings, urban-planning reports, and product/site descriptions.

glosses: polishing; giving a shine; adding gloss
explanations: The action or product of making a surface shiny and glossy — applied to furniture, cars, shoes, floors, nails, and also to food finishes in cooking. Refers both to the process (polishing) and to the substance used to achieve it (polish).

glosses: characterization; character description; portrayal of a person
characterization; depiction of a character; portrayal of a person
explanations: The way a person is portrayed in a novel, film, drama, or other work — covering appearance, personality, background, and behavior. Standard in literary criticism, film reviews, and writing guides; used to praise a work for its vivid portrayal of characters or to criticize it as flat or shallow.

glosses: the curtain rises; to begin; to get underway
to begin; to get underway; to open (of a major event or era)
explanations: Literal use: the stage curtain goes up at the start of a play, concert, or similar performance.

Figurative use: a significant event, era, or contest begins — a tournament, a new political era, a project, a campaign. Carries a ceremonial or dramatic tone, framing the beginning as a public unfolding.

The counter {羽|わ} is used for birds of all kinds and, by traditional convention, for rabbits. {一羽|いちわ} counts one such animal. The reading of {羽|わ} changes depending on the number attached to it (e.g., {三羽|さんば}, {六羽|ろっぱ}).

glosses: slugger; heavy hitter; power hitter (especially in baseball)
explanations: A batter known for hitting the ball hard and often driving in runs with extra-base hits and home runs. Used primarily in baseball commentary and sports writing.

In baseball, a player who bats in place of the pitcher in the lineup but does not play a defensive position. The rule is used in Japan's Pacific League and in Major League Baseball. Often abbreviated DH (from the English 'designated hitter').

glosses: manner; mode; way something appears or behaves
explanations: The observable state or condition of something, most commonly a patient's medical condition. In clinical and news contexts, often used in phrases describing how someone is doing after injury or illness.

A more technical sense meaning the manner or mode in which something occurs. Used in grammar ({様態|ようたい}の{助動詞|じょどうし}, 'modal auxiliary of appearance', e.g., そうだ meaning 'looks like') and in academic or scientific descriptions of behavior or form.
A saw powered by an electric motor, typically used for cutting wood, metal, or other materials. An everyday household/DIY term encompassing handheld reciprocating saws, jigsaws, and similar tools.

A martial-arts technique that applies pressure to an opponent's joint (elbow, shoulder, knee, ankle, etc.) to force submission or incapacitate. A core category of techniques in judo, jujitsu, sambo, mixed martial arts, and professional wrestling.

Describes something that is clearly visible, surfaced, or made evident, as opposed to something latent or hidden. A written, analytical term frequent in academic, business, and policy writing, usually paired as a contrast with {潜在的|せんざいてき} ('latent; potential').

The removal of a company's shares from a stock exchange, ending their public trading. Can occur voluntarily (e.g., after a management buyout) or involuntarily (e.g., for financial trouble, falsified reports, or failure to meet listing criteria).

In astronomy, a star of apparent magnitude 1 — one of the brightest stars visible in the night sky. The magnitude system divides visible stars into six classes, with {一等星|いっとうせい} the brightest category regularly taught in schools.
The thin stick used by an orchestra or choir conductor to keep time and direct the ensemble. The Japanese word is borrowed from German 'Taktstock' ('beat stick'), shortened to タクト.
By metaphorical extension, the act of leading or directing a group or project. Most common in the set phrases タクトを{振|ふ}る ('to take the lead; to direct') and {指揮|しき}のタクト.

glosses: inauguration ceremony; launch ceremony; kickoff ceremony
explanations: A formal ceremony held to mark the start of a new organization, committee, project, or system. Common for new government agencies, research institutes, associations, and corporate initiatives.
Fruit whose moisture has been removed through sun-drying, hot-air drying, or freeze-drying. The formal, written-Japanese equivalent of the more common everyday term ドライフルーツ.

A deciduous tree of the genus Morus, whose leaves are the sole food of silkworms. Historically central to Japan's silk industry, and the source of edible mulberry fruit (berries) and mulberry-bark paper.

Sharp, often shooting pain that runs along the course of a nerve, typically triggered by cold weather, pressure, or nerve damage. A common complaint associated with aging, and often discussed in everyday conversation about aches and pains.

A division of a hospital or clinic organized around a medical specialty, such as internal medicine, pediatrics, or orthopedics. The term appears on hospital directories, signage, and insurance paperwork to direct patients to the appropriate doctor.

A small, slender, translucent-white fish (Salangichthys microdon) that runs up rivers from the sea in early spring to spawn. Traditionally eaten whole, raw or lightly cooked, and prized as a harbinger of spring in Japanese cuisine.

To discuss a matter in a formal, institutional setting — typically in a legislature, board meeting, or committee — with a view to reaching a decision. Restricted to written and formal contexts; replaced in everyday speech by {議論|ぎろん}する or {話|はな}し{合|あ}う.

Romantic or sexual attraction between people of the same sex. A neutral, standard term used in journalism, academic writing, and legal and policy discussion; the default Japanese word when English 'homosexuality' is translated.

glosses: deputy department head; assistant manager; vice-captain (of a club)
explanations: The person who supports and acts as deputy to a {部長|ぶちょう} — a department head in a company, or the captain of a school or university club. Responsibilities typically include deputizing for the head when absent and handling day-to-day coordination within the unit.

A school administrator who assists the {校長|こうちょう} (principal) and carries out duties delegated by the principal. The position was formally established in Japanese public schools by a 2007 revision of the School Education Act, sitting between the principal and the older {教頭|きょうとう} rank.

Pure white sugar with fine, uniform crystals, drier and more free-flowing than ordinary Japanese table sugar ({上白糖|じょうはくとう}). Preferred in baking, confectionery, and coffee, where its neutral flavor and easy measurement are valued.

glosses: clamp (tool or fixture for holding parts together)
explanations: A mechanical device that uses screws, springs, or levers to hold two objects firmly together. Widely used in woodworking, metalwork, engineering, and medicine; the loanword is standard technical vocabulary across these fields.

Small drop-shaped or bead-shaped pieces of chocolate formulated to hold their shape when baked. Used in cookies, muffins, scones, ice cream, pastries, and sweet breads. The standard Japanese term, matching the English product category.

In botany and ecology, a group of plants of the same or related species growing together in a specific location and forming a distinct natural grouping. Roughly equivalent to the English terms 'plant community' or 'stand', depending on context.

glosses: relative by marriage; in-law; affinity by marriage
explanations: A relative connected not by blood but by marriage — the family and relatives of one's spouse, and by extension the network of kinship ties created by marriage. A formal term used in legal, genealogical, and literary contexts rather than everyday family conversation.

glosses: sutra text; passage from a sutra
sutra text; the text or passages of a Buddhist sutra
explanations: The written text of a Buddhist sutra, or the passages chanted from it during a ritual. Refers specifically to the verbal/written content of the scripture, as distinct from the physical scroll or volume that contains it.

The inclusion of extra or duplicate components in a system — whether data, equipment, or wording — beyond the minimum required. In engineering and IT, redundancy is a positive property that provides fault tolerance; in writing, it is often a negative property indicating wordiness.

glosses: perpendicular line; perpendicular (from a point to a line or plane)
explanations: In geometry, a straight line that meets another line or plane at a right angle, especially one drawn from a given point perpendicular to a reference line or plane. Standard terminology in school mathematics and technical drawing.

glosses: diagram; chart (visual representation of data or relationships)
explanations: A visual diagram used to illustrate relationships, processes, or data. Used in technical, business, and academic contexts. Often shortened to ダイヤ.

In the context of railways, buses, and other scheduled transport, refers to the operating schedule — the plan of when each train or bus runs. Usually shortened to ダイヤ in this sense, as in {運行|うんこう}ダイヤ (operating schedule) or ダイヤの{乱|みだ}れ (schedule disruption).

Protection against dust entering a device, space, or product. Used attributively (often as {防塵|ぼうじん}~) to describe products, masks, equipment, or rooms designed to keep dust out. Common on product specifications for cameras, smartphones, and industrial equipment.

glosses: spouting (of a whale); water spout; blowhole spray
spouting (of a whale); the spray of water and air a whale releases from its blowhole
explanations: The act of a whale or dolphin expelling a spray of water vapor and air from its blowhole at the surface. The visible spout is a well-known characteristic of whale-watching and is sometimes used by observers to identify different whale species by its shape.

glosses: tax-inclusive price display; displaying the total price
tax-inclusive price display; showing the final all-inclusive total on price tags and advertisements
explanations: The practice of displaying the full, tax-included price on price tags, menus, and advertisements — rather than the pre-tax price. Under Japan's Consumer Tax Act, businesses selling to consumers are required to use {総額表示|そうがくひょうじ} so that the shopper can see at a glance what they will actually pay.

glosses: exploded view; breakdown diagram showing the component parts of a product
explanations: A technical illustration that shows the individual parts of a product separated out along the lines they fit together, so that the viewer can see how everything is assembled. Used in manuals, parts catalogs, repair guides, and engineering documentation.

glosses: uniqueness; singularity; the quality of being one of a kind
uniqueness; singularity; the quality of being the only one of its kind
explanations: The abstract quality of being unique — the property that nothing else is equivalent or a substitute. Used in philosophy, business, mathematics, database design, and identity-related discussions to describe the one-of-a-kind nature of a thing or value.

glosses: (mobile phone) coverage area; service area; area within signal range
explanations: The geographical area in which a mobile phone or other wireless device can make and receive calls through a carrier's network. Going outside this area results in dropped calls or no signal.

glosses: water supply; pumping of water; water transmission
water supply; pumping or sending of water through pipes or hoses
explanations: The action of sending water from one place to another through pipes, hoses, or other conduits. Used for municipal water systems (sending water from a treatment plant to consumers), firefighting (pumping water through a hose to a fire), and industrial contexts. Can be used as a する verb.

glosses: resolution; resolving power; the smallest difference a measuring instrument can detect
explanations: A technical term for the finest distinction a measuring or observational instrument can make — for example, the smallest angular separation a telescope can distinguish, the smallest change in temperature a sensor can detect, or the pixel density of a digital display. Different from file or screen "resolution" in consumer contexts, which is usually {解像度|かいぞうど}.

A new edition of a book in which additional content has been added to the original text — for example extra chapters, updated data, new illustrations, or a supplementary appendix. Distinct from a mere reprint, and usually advertised on the cover as evidence that the book has grown since its first publication.

The cap or lid that seals a bottle — whether a twist-off plastic cap on a PET bottle, a metal crown cap on a beer bottle, or a screw-top lid on a glass jar. A general term covering all types of bottle closures.

A researcher who studies human beings — their cultures, societies, languages, biological evolution, or material remains. Covers both cultural anthropologists working with living communities and physical or archaeological anthropologists studying human origins and artifacts.

glosses: in practice; practically; from a practical standpoint
explanations: Used to contrast what theoretically or officially ought to be the case with what actually happens in real-world practice. Signals that the speaker is describing how things function on the ground, as opposed to how they are defined on paper.

The screen of a device on which information is shown to the user — for example the panel of a smartphone, the monitor of a PC, or the LCD readout of an appliance. Often used in technical manuals and UI documentation to refer to whatever layout is currently visible on the screen.

The administrative office of a village ({村|むら}) — the smallest unit of Japanese local government. Handles residence registration, tax, welfare benefits, and other daily administrative services for village residents, paralleling the role of a {市役所|しやくしょ} in a city or a {町役場|まちやくば} in a town.

glosses: pale pink; light crimson; soft rose
explanations: A soft, slightly warm pink — a lightened version of the traditional color {紅|べに} ('crimson; safflower red'). Evokes cherry blossoms, peach blossoms, and the delicate tones of traditional Japanese cosmetics and kimono, and is felt as a distinctly refined, classical color name rather than a modern industrial color term.

glosses: foot bath; soaking one's feet in hot water
explanations: Soaking the feet and lower legs in warm or hot water, either as a relaxing home practice or as a therapeutic and nursing procedure. Popular at hot-spring resorts as a {足湯|あしゆ} facility and also used in healthcare settings to warm patients who cannot take a full bath.

glosses: startup sound; startup chime; boot sound
explanations: The short audio cue that a computer, smartphone, game console, or other electronic device plays when it is powered on, confirming that the device has successfully started. Also used for the jingles that apps and operating systems play when they launch.

glosses: diurnal habit; being active during the day
explanations: The biological habit of being active during daytime and resting at night — applied to animals as a classification of their activity pattern. Directly contrasted with {夜行性|やこうせい} ('nocturnal habit'). Used mainly in biology, zoology, and nature writing.

glosses: lesson plan; teaching plan; course plan
explanations: A written plan outlining what will be taught in a class or course — the sequence of topics, teaching methods, learning objectives, and materials to be used. Prepared by teachers for a single lesson, a unit, or a whole semester, and often submitted to supervisors or shared with students.

Eyewear worn to protect the eyes from physical or chemical hazards — flying debris, splashing liquids, dust, sparks, UV light, or lasers. Used in laboratories, factories, construction sites, DIY work, and some sports.

glosses: affiliated store; group store; chain store within a corporate group
explanations: A shop or outlet that belongs to the same corporate group or distribution network as a parent company — for example a car dealership operating under a single manufacturer, or a convenience store within a chain. Used especially when explaining that a store is part of a larger business network rather than an independent one.

The network of high-voltage lines, towers, and substations that carries electricity from power plants to distribution areas and ultimately to homes and businesses. A national-scale infrastructure term, frequently discussed in the context of energy policy, renewable energy, and disaster response.

Strong sexual or carnal desire for another person, often viewed as something that overrides reason or moral judgement. The word carries a literary, sometimes religious, tone and is rarely used in casual conversation. It often appears in novels, essays, religious texts (especially Buddhist writings), and serious journalism about scandals or human nature.

glosses: to make a (corny) pun; to crack a bad joke based on wordplay
explanations: To produce a pun — typically a deliberately groan-worthy joke that exploits the similar sound of two words. The verb is colloquial and usually carries a slightly affectionate or teasing tone, often associated with stereotypical 'dad jokes' (おやじギャグ). Used both about the act of telling such jokes and about a habitual tendency to do so.

glosses: formalism; emphasis on form over substance; bureaucratic adherence to procedure
explanations: An attitude or approach that places excessive importance on outward form, procedure, or formality at the expense of substance or actual results. Often used critically about organizations, schools, or governments where rigid rule-following obstructs practical action. The word also has a more neutral, technical sense in fields such as art, literature, philosophy, and law, where it refers to schools of thought that emphasize form (e.g., Russian Formalism in literary theory).

glosses: barren land; wasteland; (figuratively) area devoid of activity or productivity
barren land; wasteland; an area where vegetation cannot grow
(figuratively) area or field devoid of activity, talent, or productivity
explanations: A geographical region — desert, frozen tundra, or rocky terrain — where the soil and climate make farming or natural plant growth impossible. Used in physical geography and travel writing.

Used metaphorically to describe a domain where something expected is missing — a field with no notable talent, a market with no products, a region with no industry, etc. Common in journalism and commentary, often paired with the area in question (e.g., {政治|せいじ}の{不毛地帯|ふもうちたい} 'political wasteland'). Famously the title of a popular novel and TV drama by Yamasaki Toyoko.

glosses: vehicle inspection certificate; vehicle registration document
explanations: The official document issued after a Japanese vehicle passes its mandatory periodic inspection ({車検|しゃけん}). It records the make, model, registration number, owner's name and address, weight, dimensions, and the next inspection due date. Drivers are legally required to carry it in the vehicle at all times. The full official name is {自動車検査証|じどうしゃけんさしょう}, of which {車検証|しゃけんしょう} is the everyday short form.

Snow that contains a high amount of liquid water, making it heavy, dense, and sticky. Common in coastal regions and during warmer parts of winter, especially on the Sea of Japan side. Wet snow tends to cling to power lines, branches, and roofs, often causing damage and traffic disruption. Used in weather forecasts, news reports about snowstorms, and skiing/avalanche discussions.

A general term for various species of marine bivalves whose inner shell is lined with a layer of nacre (mother-of-pearl) and which can produce pearls — most notably the Akoya pearl oyster ({アコヤガイ}), used for the cultured pearl industry that Japan helped to pioneer. Used in news about pearl farming, marine biology articles, and aquariums.

glosses: other people (polite); other families; people outside one's own household
explanations: A polite, slightly old-fashioned way of referring to people or families other than one's own — outsiders, neighbours, strangers, or members of another household. The honorific suffix さま signals respect or social distance. Often used by parents to teach children to behave properly toward people outside the family ('don't trouble {余所様|よそさま}'), or in formal apologies and self-deprecating speech.

glosses: phenomenal; on the surface; relating to the appearance rather than the essence
explanations: Describes something pertaining to phenomena — that is, what is observed or appears on the surface — as opposed to underlying causes, essence, or substance. Common in academic writing (philosophy, sociology, science) and in serious commentary, often paired in contrast with {本質的|ほんしつてき} ('essential'). The English 'phenomenal' meaning 'remarkable; outstanding' is a separate sense not normally expressed by this word.

glosses: serving plate; large plate for arranging food
explanations: A plate, often larger and shallower than an individual dish, used to display or serve food that has been arranged on it — sashimi, fruit, sweets, side dishes, or hors d'oeuvres. Found in Japanese restaurants, izakaya, home dining, and as a sales unit ('plate of X') in food shops.

glosses: manzai duo; comedy duo (performing manzai stand-up)
explanations: A pair of comedians who perform {漫才|まんざい}, the classic Japanese stand-up style consisting of fast-paced comic dialogue between two performers — typically a {ボケ} ('the funny one; one who says silly things') and a {ツッコミ} ('the straight man who corrects them'). Common in entertainment news, audition contests like M-1 Grand Prix, and discussions of Japanese popular culture.

The act of removing ice that has built up on a surface — most commonly the wings and body of an aircraft before takeoff, or the rotor blades of a wind turbine, ship hulls, and road surfaces. Used in aviation, transport, and engineering contexts. Often appears as a する-noun ({除氷|じょひょう}する 'to de-ice') and in compounds such as {除氷|じょひょう}{装置|そうち} ('de-icing equipment').

Objects that have been scattered or strewn about — typically debris on a road after an accident, items dropped from a truck, broken glass on a station platform, or litter left in a public space. Frequently used in traffic news, road safety announcements, and reports on disaster cleanup.

glosses: site area; lot area; total area of land on which a building stands
explanations: The total area of a piece of land (a building lot, factory site, school grounds, etc.), normally measured in square metres or {坪|つぼ} (a traditional unit of about 3.3 m²). A standard item in real-estate listings, building plans, and construction documents, often shown alongside the building footprint and total floor area.

An orchard where apples are grown commercially. Common throughout the apple-producing regions of Japan, especially Aomori, Nagano, and Iwate. Often appears in tourism contexts, since many orchards offer pick-your-own apple experiences ({りんご{狩|が}り}) in the autumn harvest season.

A farmer or farming family whose main crop is apples. Like other 〜{農家|のうか} ('X-growing farmer') terms, the word can refer to either the farmer as an individual or to the household / business as a whole. Often used in news about agriculture, weather damage, harvest seasons, and rural tourism, especially in apple-producing regions like Aomori, Nagano, and Iwate.

The large innermost toe on the foot. In Japanese, toes are usually referred to using the names of the fingers of the hand prefixed with {足|あし}の ('of the foot'), so the big toe is literally 'the thumb of the foot.' Frequently mentioned in medical, sports, and footwear contexts.

Used as a modifier or adverbial phrase meaning 'throughout recorded history' or 'from a historical perspective.' Commonly attached to nouns with の ({歴史上|れきしじょう}の...) to mean 'historical ~' and used adverbially with verbs to mean 'in the course of history' or 'as a matter of historical record.' Frequently used in claims about how rare, important, or unprecedented an event is.

glosses: in the end, at the end, ultimately
explanations: A sentence adverbial used to mark the final outcome of a sequence of events or situations, often after describing intervening struggles or changes. Similar to English 'in the end,' 'eventually,' or 'at last.' Frequently signals a conclusion that contrasts with earlier expectations.

The age range from 40 to 49 years old. Used to describe a person's approximate age or to refer to this demographic group as a whole. In Japan this is often regarded as the period of peak responsibility at work and in the household.

An organic compound that serves as a building block of proteins. Commonly encountered in contexts such as nutrition, health foods, supplements, cosmetics, and biology. Twenty amino acids make up the proteins of the human body, and a subset ({必須|ひっす}アミノ{酸|さん}) must be obtained from food.

glosses: Faculty of Letters, Faculty of Humanities
Faculty of Letters; Faculty of Humanities; School of Humanities
explanations: A division of a university dedicated to the study of literature, linguistics, philosophy, history, and related humanistic fields. In Japan, the {文学部|ぶんがくぶ} is one of the oldest faculties in traditional universities and typically covers language and literature (both Japanese and foreign), philosophy, psychology, history, and area studies.

The first and larger of the two main divisions of the Christian Bible, containing the scriptures inherited from Judaism: the books of Moses, historical books, prophets, and wisdom literature. The Japanese name literally means 'the scripture of the old covenant,' contrasting with {新約聖書|しんやくせいしょ} ('New Testament').

The second of the two main divisions of the Christian Bible, recounting the life and teachings of Jesus, the early Christian church, and the letters of the apostles. The Japanese name literally means 'the scripture of the new covenant,' the covenant that Christians believe God established through Jesus.

glosses: writing style; manner of writing; tone (of writing)
explanations: The distinctive way in which someone writes — encompassing tone, word choice, sentence rhythm, and overall manner. Often used when commenting on someone's article, letter, or essay to describe the feel of the prose rather than its content.

glosses: to strum; to play loudly (a stringed instrument)
to strum; to play loudly; to bang out (on a stringed instrument)
explanations: To play a stringed instrument — especially a guitar, mandolin, or traditional Japanese instrument like the biwa — by sweeping or scraping the strings vigorously to produce bold, continuous sound. Suggests energetic, often rough or expressive playing rather than careful plucking.

glosses: raising (an issue); bringing up; filing (a lawsuit)
raising (an issue); bringing up; presenting (a question or problem) for consideration
explanations: Putting forward a topic, question, or problem so that others must consider or discuss it. Typical of meetings, debates, articles, and policy discussions where someone formally introduces a matter for attention.
In legal contexts, the act of formally initiating a court case or other legal action. Most commonly appears in the fixed expression {訴訟|そしょう}を{提起|ていき}する ('to file a lawsuit').

glosses: overturning; capsizing; derailment (of a vehicle, boat, or train)
explanations: The physical event of a vehicle or vessel turning upside down or being knocked off its proper position. Typical subjects include trains, boats, cars, and trucks. Used both for accidents (intransitive sense) and deliberate sabotage (transitive sense).
Figurative use referring to the violent or political downfall of a government, regime, or established order. Often appears in news reports about coups, revolutions, and conspiracies.

glosses: forensics; expert appraisal; the eye for judging quality
forensic investigation; crime scene examination; the forensics team
expert appraisal; connoisseurship; an eye for quality
explanations: The technical, scientific examination of physical evidence by police — fingerprints, blood, hair, footprints — to identify suspects or reconstruct events. By extension, refers to the police forensics unit itself, often mentioned in news reports and crime dramas.

The trained ability to judge the authenticity, value, or quality of art, antiques, gems, or other items. Also refers to a person's discerning eye — the capacity to distinguish what is genuine or excellent from what is not.

glosses: risky; involving significant danger or uncertainty
explanations: Describes an action, plan, or situation that carries a high chance of failure, loss, or harm. The English loanword feels lighter and more modern than the Sino-Japanese {危険|きけん}, and is common in business, finance, and everyday casual contexts.

glosses: gambling; wagering money or valuables on games of chance
explanations: The act of staking money or valuables on the outcome of a game, race, or other event of chance, especially in legal, news, and formal contexts. Most casual conversation uses ギャンブル or {博打|ばくち} instead; {賭博|とばく} appears most often in connection with crime, law, and prohibition.

glosses: dome; rounded vaulted roof or building
explanations: A hemispherical roof or building with a rounded top, whether a religious structure (cathedrals, mosques), a sports stadium with a fixed or retractable roof, or a smaller covering such as a planetarium. In modern Japan, the word is most associated with large covered stadiums.

glosses: offense and defense; attack and defense
offense and defense (in sports); both attacking and defensive aspects of play
attack and defense (figurative); both sides of a contest or argument
explanations: A short Sino-Japanese compound covering both halves of competitive play. Frequently used in baseball, soccer, basketball, and other sports to talk about a team or player who must handle both roles.
Used metaphorically for any situation involving alternating attack and defense — a debate, a court case, a business negotiation, or a strategic struggle.
The bony prominence in the upper part of the cheek, beneath the outer corner of the eye. Often referenced when describing facial features, anatomy, or the effects of aging or weight loss.

glosses: an urgent issue; a pressing problem that must be addressed
an urgent issue; a pressing matter; a top-priority problem
explanations: A set phrase used in formal speech, government statements, business reports, and editorials to label a problem that demands immediate attention. It carries weight and seriousness — appropriate for high-stakes policy or organizational matters, not for everyday concerns.

glosses: bleak; grim; harsh and lifeless (atmosphere or scene)
bleak; grim; harsh and devoid of warmth (of an atmosphere, scene, or human relations)
explanations: A pre-noun modifier formed from the {タリ}-adverb {殺伐|さつばつ}と + {した} (the past form of する). It describes a setting or mood that feels cold, hostile, or stripped of human warmth — a battle-scarred landscape, a tense workplace, or a society in which people no longer care for one another.

glosses: on-street parking; parking on a public road
on-street parking; parking a vehicle on a public road
explanations: The act — usually unauthorized — of parking a car on a public street rather than in a parking lot or garage. In Japan, this is heavily restricted in cities and is a frequent target of police enforcement and fines.

glosses: rear-end collision; an accident in which one vehicle hits the back of another
explanations: A traffic accident in which the front of one vehicle strikes the rear of the vehicle ahead — typically because the following driver failed to maintain enough distance or did not notice that the vehicle ahead had stopped. One of the most common types of car accident in Japan.

glosses: faction; clique; gang (with a negative nuance)
explanations: A group of people who band together to pursue a common — usually questionable or harmful — purpose. The word carries clearly negative connotations: secrecy, factionalism, plotting against others. Most commonly heard in the set phrase {徒党|ととう}を{組|く}む ('to form a faction').
The south-facing exit of a train station, building, or other public facility.
The east-facing exit of a train station, building, or other public facility.
Having the properties of oil, or made with an oil base rather than water.
A small grain-like particle, or a product in granulated form such as medicine or instant food.
A part of an object designed to be grasped by hand, such as a door handle, pot handle, or drawer pull.
An outline of the most important points, rules, or procedures, typically in an official or administrative document.
The reduction or complete waiving of taxes, fees, penalties, or other financial obligations.
Water escaping from pipes, roofs, walls, or other structures where it should be contained.
The power or authority that comes with a particular official position or role.
The process of adding quantities together over time to obtain a total.
The calculation of projected costs for a construction or engineering project based on materials, labor, and other factors.
A large, stately residence, especially one associated with nobility or feudal lords. Also used figuratively or humorously for any impressively large house.
The higher portion of a layered structure, whether physical (atmosphere, soil, water) or social (class, organization).
The industrial process of producing iron from ore, or the iron and steel manufacturing industry in general.
A bond issued by a corporation to raise funds, with the company promising to repay the principal plus interest to the bondholder.
The art or craft of carving objects from wood, or a carved wooden object.
The act of applying pressure to compress, squeeze out liquid, or condense something.
Communication or contact from a person, especially letters or messages that indicate someone is alive and well.
Relating to the third power in mathematics, or a three-dimensional cube shape. Used as a prefix for cubic measurements.
An additional issue of a magazine or periodical published outside the regular schedule, often on a specific theme.
The reduction of a nation's military forces, weapons, or defense spending, typically through international agreements.
A fortified structure including its walls, moats, and surrounding defensive works. Often used to refer to the entire castle complex rather than just the main tower.

glosses: fight to the death; desperate battle
explanations: An extremely fierce and intense battle or struggle where the participants fight as if their lives depended on it.
A formal dinner party or banquet setting, including the occasion, the seating arrangement, and the gathering itself.
Visiting someone who is suffering, hospitalized, or in difficult circumstances to offer comfort and encouragement.
A game or activity where one shoots at targets, especially the cork-gun shooting stalls found at Japanese festivals and hot spring towns.

glosses: arts and sciences; learning and the arts
explanations: The combination of academic learning and creative arts, or scholarly and artistic pursuits in general.
The state of being morally pure, unsullied, or untainted, especially in relation to sexual virtue or moral integrity.

glosses: chivalry; gallantry; code of honor among outlaws
explanations: A code of conduct emphasizing loyalty, justice, and protecting the weak, historically associated with yakuza and itinerant gamblers in Japanese culture.
Preparations and arrangements made to protect against attack, including fortifications, guard positions, and defensive measures.
The process of reducing pressure, whether in a physical system, industrial process, or medical/diving context.
Describes something that is absolutely necessary and cannot be omitted or removed. Derived from the potential-negative form of the verb 欠く (to lack), literally meaning 'cannot be made to lack.'
Previously owned items that are resold. A legal and commercial term covering anything from used clothing to electronics.
Old objects valued for their age, craftsmanship, or historical significance. Overlaps with sense 1 but emphasizes the collectible or aesthetic value.

glosses: day trip; excursion without an overnight stay
explanations: A trip to a destination and back within the same day, without staying overnight. Common for sightseeing, hot springs, hiking, and other leisure activities.

glosses: yellow light; warning sign; caution signal
explanations: The yellow light on a traffic signal that appears between green and red, indicating that drivers should prepare to stop.
A figurative signal that something is heading in a dangerous or problematic direction. Used for health, relationships, business situations, and other domains where trouble is brewing.

glosses: foreigner; person from another land; stranger
explanations: A person from a foreign country or unfamiliar place. A literary and somewhat poetic term, often carrying a sense of being out of place or belonging to a different world.

glosses: good results; excellent performance; strong record
good results; excellent performance; strong showing
explanations: Outstanding or better-than-expected results in academics, sports, business, or other measurable endeavors.

glosses: lost property; lost article; missing item
explanations: An item that has been lost or misplaced. Used in official, administrative, and everyday contexts when reporting or inquiring about something that has gone missing.

glosses: calligraphy and painting; written and visual art
calligraphy and painting; works of brush art
explanations: The combined art of calligraphy (brush writing) and painting, traditionally viewed as closely related disciplines in East Asian culture. Also refers to individual works or collections that include both calligraphic and pictorial pieces.

Industries rooted in historical craft techniques and local materials, typically producing goods such as pottery, textiles, lacquerware, and paper. In Japan, many are officially designated and supported by local and national government programs.

glosses: by item; by category; broken down by heading
explanations: Organized or classified according to individual items, categories, or headings. Used when data, expenses, tasks, or other information is separated and presented per item rather than as a lump sum or aggregate.
The power or ability to control, dominate, or exert decisive influence over people, organizations, markets, or situations.
A shop or store that is authorized to sell, service, or handle a particular product or brand. Commonly seen on signs and advertisements to indicate where specific products are available.

A building design that uses strong, rigid structural elements to withstand earthquake forces without collapsing. One of three main approaches to earthquake engineering in Japan, alongside seismic isolation and vibration damping.

A traditional form of manual therapy that treats bone fractures, joint dislocations, sprains, and musculoskeletal injuries through manipulation rather than surgery. In modern Japan, practiced by licensed judo therapists at clinics called 整骨院.

glosses: rate of return; profit rate; yield
explanations: The ratio of profit or income generated relative to the amount invested or the revenue earned. A key metric in finance, investment, and business management.

The act of defending or protecting oneself from physical harm, psychological attack, or adverse situations. Encompasses both physical self-defense and broader protective measures such as information security and emotional boundaries.

glosses: rights holder; person with legal rights
rights holder; person entitled to legal rights
explanations: A person or entity that holds specific legal rights, such as property rights, copyrights, patent rights, or other legally recognized entitlements.
