Used figuratively to describe something done perfectly or someone's ideal performance or qualities.

glosses: monthly installment; monthly proration; monthly basis
explanations: Dividing a total amount into monthly portions, or calculating something on a per-month basis. Commonly used for payments, fees, and accounting.
A warm golden-brown color resembling ripe wheat. Often used to describe sun-tanned skin or hair color.

glosses: sure hit; certain to hit the mark
sure hit; hitting without fail; certain to strike the target
explanations: Hitting a target with certainty. Used in archery, martial arts, military contexts, and figuratively for plans or strategies that are bound to succeed.

glosses: one gulp; drinking in a single swallow
one gulp; drinking in a single swallow; downing in one go
explanations: The act of drinking something all at once without pausing. Can also mean something is so easy it can be consumed or dealt with effortlessly.
A wide, deep bowl specifically designed for preparing and drinking matcha in the tea ceremony. Valued both as functional ware and as art objects.

glosses: pest bird; harmful bird; nuisance bird
explanations: A bird species that causes damage to agriculture, property, or the ecosystem. The designation depends on context — a bird may be considered a pest in farmland but not elsewhere.
A large black waterbird that dives to catch fish. Found along rivers and lakes throughout Japan, and closely associated with the traditional practice of cormorant fishing.
A very dark shade of brown, close to black. A traditional Japanese color name used to describe clothing, hair, furniture, and other objects.

glosses: sideways glance; looking to the side
explanations: The act of looking to the side rather than straight ahead. Can imply casual observation, distraction, or a furtive glance.
The state of not wearing a hat or cap. Often noted as a contrast to the norm when headwear would be expected.

glosses: backwardness; underdevelopment; slow progress; lagging behind
explanations: The state of progressing slowly or falling behind compared to others. Used for economic development, technology adoption, policy implementation, and other measurable domains.

glosses: sauce yakisoba; stir-fried noodles with Worcester sauce
sauce yakisoba; stir-fried noodles seasoned with Worcester-style sauce
explanations: The most common type of yakisoba in Japan, where stir-fried noodles are flavored with a thick, sweet-savory Worcester-style sauce and topped with ingredients like cabbage, pork, and pickled ginger.
Fertilizer mixed into the soil before planting seeds or transplanting seedlings. Provides essential nutrients for the early growth stage of plants.
Fertilizer in liquid form, diluted with water before application. Quickly absorbed by plants and commonly used for houseplants, container gardening, and hydroponics.
A coin-operated device installed at the roadside that allows temporary paid parking for a set duration, typically 60 minutes in Japan.
Shoes or boots with wheels attached to the sole, used for gliding over smooth surfaces. Also refers to the activity of skating with such shoes.
Boots with a blade attached to the sole, worn for gliding on ice. Includes figure skates, speed skates, and hockey skates.
The solid matter left after liquid has been pressed or strained from a substance. Most commonly refers to sake lees (酒粕) or the residue from tofu production (おから).
Figuratively, something of no value — the leftover after everything good has been taken. Often used in the expression 絞りかす or 出がらし to describe someone or something drained of worth.

glosses: bang-bang; slam-slam; with repeated loud banging
explanations: The sound or manner of doors, shutters, or heavy objects slamming shut or being struck repeatedly. Conveys forceful, noisy, repeated impact.

glosses: loungewear; clothes for relaxing at home
explanations: Comfortable clothing designed for wearing around the house. A wasei-eigo term (room + wear) widely used in Japanese fashion and retail. Positioned between everyday clothes and pajamas — presentable enough for answering the door but comfortable for relaxing.
Reducing the amount of waste generated, typically by consuming less or using resources more efficiently. One of the 3Rs (リデュース・リユース・リサイクル) promoted in Japanese environmental policy.

glosses: side mirror; wing mirror; door-mounted mirror
explanations: The exterior mirror mounted on a car door for checking the rear and side views while driving. A wasei-eigo term (door + mirror) that is standard in Japanese automotive vocabulary.

glosses: all items; all products; every item
explanations: Every single product or item in a given category or location. Frequently used in retail, shopping, and restaurant contexts to indicate that something applies to the entire selection.

glosses: to enter; to trespass; to get involved in
to enter; to trespass; to go into a restricted area
to get involved in; to pry into; to delve into
explanations: To physically enter a place, especially somewhere that is restricted, prohibited, or off-limits. Often carries the nuance that entry is unauthorized or unwelcome.
To go deeply into someone's personal affairs, a sensitive topic, or the details of a matter. Suggests overstepping boundaries.
A country in North America, south of the United States. Known in Japanese media for its food culture, natural landscapes, and historical civilizations.

glosses: cover letter; transmittal slip; covering note
explanations: A brief document attached to materials being sent — such as faxes, documents, or packages — that identifies the sender, recipient, and contents. Standard in Japanese business communication.
The act of translating Japanese text into English. Commonly encountered as a section in English language textbooks and exams in Japan.

glosses: bending backward; leaning back; arching the body backward
explanations: The action or posture of bending the upper body backward, away from something. Can describe a physical posture, a startled recoil, or an exaggerated backward lean.

Cosmetic treatment of the toenails, including filing, polishing, and decorating. In Japanese usage, often refers specifically to toenail polish or nail art applied to the toes, rather than the full foot-care treatment.
A soft, creamy French cheese with a white rind. Very popular in Japan, where domestically produced versions are widely available in supermarkets and convenience stores.
Clothing designed for sleeping. A fashion-industry loanword that positions sleepwear as a product category distinct from casual loungewear.
A video game designed to scare or unsettle the player through atmosphere, jumpscares, or disturbing themes. Japan has been a major producer of the genre since the 1990s.
A synthetic fabric widely used in clothing, bedding, and other textiles. Known for being wrinkle-resistant, quick-drying, and affordable.
Ice cream flavored with vanilla. The most basic and popular ice cream flavor in Japan, served at restaurants, convenience stores, and ice cream shops.

glosses: clothes drying rack; hanging out laundry
clothes drying rack; laundry drying stand
hanging out laundry to dry; drying clothes
explanations: A rack or stand used for hanging laundry to dry, typically placed on a balcony or in a room.
The act of hanging washed clothes on a line or rack to air-dry.
The standard way to express taking a shower in Japanese. Uses the verb {浴|あ}びる (to bathe in; to be showered with) rather than a direct translation of 'take.'
A photograph used to represent oneself on social media, messaging apps, business profiles, or official documents.

glosses: digital nomad; nomad worker; location-independent worker
explanations: A person who works remotely from various locations such as cafés, coworking spaces, or while traveling, rather than commuting to a fixed office.
Publishing a book or other work independently, without going through a traditional publishing house. The author handles or arranges editing, design, printing, and distribution.

glosses: caller ID; number display; number notification
explanations: A telephone feature that displays the caller's phone number on the recipient's screen before the call is answered.
The act of smoothing and polishing fingernails or toenails using a buffer or file to give them a natural shine.
A tool used to smooth and polish the surface of nails.
A social media relationship where two users follow each other's accounts. A common concept on platforms like X (Twitter) and Instagram.
The branch of anthropology that studies human cultures, social structures, beliefs, and practices through fieldwork and comparative analysis.
A formal ceremony marking the start of an event, project, season, or facility. Used for events ranging from sports seasons to construction projects.
A label or designation indicating that a container or item can be safely used in a microwave oven.
A paper voucher issued by a local municipality that entitles a resident to receive a specific vaccination, typically free of charge or at a subsidized rate.

glosses: notification form; official written notice; registration document
explanations: A formal document submitted to a government office, employer, or institution to officially notify them of a change in status, a request, or a declaration.
A machine that automatically dispenses items such as drinks, food, or tickets after a customer inserts money or uses electronic payment.

glosses: New Year deity; god of the incoming year
explanations: A Shinto deity believed to visit each household at the start of the new year, bringing blessings of good harvest and prosperity. Many New Year traditions are rooted in welcoming this deity.

glosses: laundry room; utility room for laundry
explanations: A dedicated room or space in a home, apartment building, or facility equipped for washing, drying, and sometimes ironing clothes.
The Olympic sport of gymnastics involving routines on apparatus such as floor, vault, bars, and beam, scored by judges on difficulty and execution.
The action of pressing a computer mouse button twice in quick succession, typically used to open files, launch applications, or select text.
A service or department that assists customers with questions, problems, complaints, and technical issues related to a product or service.

glosses: status update; personal news message; recent-activities write-up
explanations: A brief written message informing others about one's recent activities, life changes, or current situation. Common in letters, social media posts, and alumni newsletters.

glosses: serial drama; TV series; ongoing television drama
explanations: A television drama that airs weekly over a set number of episodes, typically one season (one cour) of 10-12 episodes in Japan. Distinguished from single-episode specials or movies.

glosses: thrill ride; scream machine; extreme amusement park ride
explanations: An amusement park ride designed to be thrilling and frightening, such as roller coasters, free-fall towers, and spinning rides. The name literally means 'screaming machine.'

glosses: car insurance; automobile insurance; motor vehicle insurance
explanations: Insurance that covers damages, liability, and injuries related to motor vehicles. In Japan, this includes both mandatory government insurance and optional private insurance.

glosses: question setter; examiner; person who creates test questions
explanations: The person responsible for composing questions for an examination, quiz, or test. Used in academic, certification, and entertainment (quiz show) contexts.

glosses: original author; creator of the source work
original author; creator of the source material
explanations: The author or creator of an original work that is later adapted into another medium, such as a novel adapted into a film, or a manga adapted into an anime.
A member of the Japanese Cabinet who serves as head of a ministry or holds a special portfolio. Appointed by the Prime Minister and collectively responsible for government policy.

glosses: white sugar; refined sugar; granulated white sugar
explanations: Refined sugar that has been processed to remove molasses and impurities, resulting in white crystals. The most commonly used type of sugar in everyday Japanese cooking and baking.
Individual parts used in electronic circuits and devices, such as resistors, capacitors, transistors, and integrated circuits. A key term in Japan's electronics manufacturing industry.

glosses: location conditions; site conditions; locational factors
explanations: The various characteristics and advantages of a particular location, especially as they relate to opening a business, building a home, or developing property. Includes factors like transportation access, surrounding amenities, and neighborhood environment.

glosses: coordination of interests; balancing of interests
coordination of interests; balancing of competing interests; interest mediation
explanations: The process of mediating between parties with different or conflicting interests to reach a workable compromise. A core concept in Japanese politics, business negotiations, and organizational management.

glosses: preparing baby formula; making up powdered milk
explanations: The process of mixing powdered infant formula with hot water to prepare a bottle for a baby. Involves specific temperature and hygiene requirements.
The industry and practice of processing raw fish and other marine products into preserved, prepared, or packaged food items. Includes smoking, drying, canning, and freezing of seafood.

The period of life roughly from the late thirties to the mid-fifties, considered a person's most productive and vigorous adult years. In Japanese usage this often emphasizes capability and maturity rather than decline.
A point that lies exactly or approximately in the middle between two ends, stages, or positions. Used both for physical locations and abstract progress through a process or project.

The policy or practice of a country extending control over foreign territories, exploiting their resources, and governing their people. Used in historical and political discourse to describe imperial expansion and its legacy.
The second-in-command pilot of an aircraft who assists the captain and is qualified to take over if needed. Officially ranks directly below the captain in the cockpit crew.
A player who enters a game to replace another player on the field. Used across team sports including soccer, baseball, basketball, and others.
A vehicle equipped to tow or haul other vehicles, typically broken-down or illegally parked cars.
A powered vehicle designed to pull trailers, heavy equipment, or other loads. Includes agricultural tractors and the cab units of articulated trucks.

The visual appearance and character of a city or urban area, including its buildings, streets, greenery, and overall aesthetic. Often discussed in the context of city planning, architecture, and preservation.
A chemical compound containing chlorine bonded to another element or group. Chlorides are extremely common in nature and everyday life, from table salt (sodium chloride) to industrial chemicals.
A person who gathers, organizes, and edits material into a systematic reference work such as a dictionary, encyclopedia, anthology, or historical chronicle.

A rhythmic pattern in Japanese poetry where lines alternate between five and seven morae (syllable units). This meter forms the foundation of traditional Japanese verse forms including tanka and haiku.
A speech sound produced with vibration of the vocal cords. In Japanese, the voiced consonants include the g, z, d, b, and n series, typically marked with the dakuten (゛) diacritic.
A speech sound produced without vibration of the vocal cords. In Japanese, the voiceless consonants include the k, s, t, h, and p series, written with basic kana without diacritical marks.
The pattern of lines, ridges, and creases on the surface of a person's palm. Used in forensic science for identification and in palmistry for divination.
The raised platform on which an orchestra conductor stands during a performance or rehearsal. Elevates the conductor so that all musicians can see the baton and gestures clearly.
The routine, scheduled operation of public transportation such as buses, trains, ferries, or flights, running on a fixed timetable along established routes.

Describes an object manufactured from porcelain, a hard, white, translucent ceramic fired at high temperatures. Used as a noun modifier to indicate the material of tableware, decorative items, and other objects.
A person who has withdrawn from active work or public life to live quietly. Traditionally referred to a household head who had handed over authority to a successor.
A person who has chosen to withdraw from society and live a quiet, secluded life, often with connotations of contentment and simplicity.

A professional who designs, builds, and maintains gardens, parks, and other outdoor spaces. In Japan, this requires specialized knowledge of plants, stone arrangement, and traditional garden aesthetics.

glosses: confidential (within a company); for internal use only
explanations: A classification label indicating that a document or piece of information is restricted to employees of the company and must not be shared externally. Commonly stamped or printed on sensitive business documents.
A small gland in the male reproductive system located below the bladder. It produces fluid that forms part of semen. Medical issues related to the prostate are common in older men.

The state or fact of residing in a foreign country. Used as a noun modifier (with の) or in compound expressions to describe people, experiences, or situations related to living outside one's home country.

glosses: exit door (of a bus or train); alighting point
explanations: The designated door or area on a bus, train, or other public transport vehicle through which passengers exit. On Japanese city buses, passengers typically board at the rear and exit at the front, where the fare is paid.
A device used to measure physical quantities such as temperature, pressure, distance, or weight. Covers a broad range from simple gauges to sophisticated electronic instruments.

glosses: for young children; aimed at toddlers
explanations: Describes products, content, services, or activities designed or intended for young children, typically ages one to five. Functions as a noun modifier with の or as a compound modifier before another noun.

glosses: change of route; change of course; policy shift
change of course; policy shift; change of direction
explanations: A physical change in the path or route of transportation such as a bus line, train line, or road.
A figurative change in strategy, policy, or overall direction. Commonly used in business and politics to describe a significant shift in approach.

glosses: genuine parts; OEM parts; original manufacturer parts
explanations: Replacement parts made by or authorized by the original equipment manufacturer. Distinguished from aftermarket or third-party parts, genuine parts are guaranteed to match the original specifications.

glosses: individual customer; private customer; retail customer
explanations: A customer who is a private individual rather than a business entity or corporate client. Used in hospitality, banking, retail, and service industries to distinguish individual clients from corporate or group customers.

glosses: semi-finished product; work in progress; intermediate product
explanations: A product that has gone through some stages of manufacturing but is not yet a finished good ready for sale. It may be sold to another manufacturer for further processing or stored as inventory.

The period of human history before the invention of writing systems. In Japanese history, this generally refers to the time before the earliest written records, ending roughly with the introduction of Chinese characters.
The level of the ocean's surface, used as a reference point for measuring altitude and depth. Also refers to the physical surface of the sea.

glosses: light vehicle; non-motorized vehicle (bicycles, carts, etc.)
explanations: A legal category in Japanese traffic law that includes bicycles, animal-drawn carts, rickshaws, and other non-motorized or small vehicles. In traffic regulations, light vehicles must follow specific rules different from both pedestrians and motor vehicles.

glosses: proof of qualification; certification; credential verification
explanations: A document or process that verifies a person holds a particular qualification, license, or credential. Common in job applications, visa processes, and professional registration.

glosses: tabletop mirror; vanity mirror; desk mirror
explanations: A small mirror designed to stand on a table or desk, used for grooming and makeup application. Often has a stand or foldable design.

Thin paper coated with a dark waxy substance on one side, used to make copies when writing or typing. Placed between sheets so that pressure from writing transfers the coating to the sheet below. Still used in some multi-copy forms in Japan.

glosses: enough for the number of people; per-person portion
enough for the number of people; per-person portion; for everyone in the group
explanations: An amount or quantity sufficient for all the people present or involved. The suffix {分|ぶん} (portion, share) attaches to {人数|にんずう} (number of people) to indicate that something is prepared or available in the right quantity for the group.

glosses: message board; notice board; communication board
explanations: A physical or digital board used to post messages, announcements, and notices for a group. Common in schools, workplaces, and community settings.

glosses: received email; incoming mail; inbox message
explanations: An email that has been received, as opposed to sent mail. Also refers to the inbox or received mail folder in an email application or on a mobile phone.

glosses: noise removal; noise cancellation; noise reduction
explanations: The process or technology of eliminating unwanted sound or electronic interference from audio signals, recordings, or transmissions. Common in audio engineering, telecommunications, and consumer electronics.

glosses: flesh-and-blood human being; real person; living human
explanations: Emphasizes that someone is a real, physical, vulnerable human being with emotions and limitations, as opposed to a machine, fictional character, or superhuman ideal. Often used when reminding others that human limitations and feelings should be acknowledged.
The process or capability of reducing the force of an impact, vibration, or sudden load. Applied to materials, devices, and structures designed to protect against physical shocks.
The quality of being passed down through genes from parent to offspring. Used in medical, scientific, and everyday contexts when discussing traits or conditions that run in families.
The act of pulling or towing a vessel, vehicle, or object by another. Most commonly used in maritime contexts for ships towing other ships, but also applicable to general towing situations.

glosses: in the soil; underground; in the earth
explanations: Within or beneath the ground, referring to the interior of the earth or soil. Used in agricultural, archaeological, and scientific contexts.

glosses: original copy; official document; authenticated text
explanations: The authoritative, official version of a document or text, as opposed to copies or drafts. Used in legal, administrative, and scholarly contexts for documents that carry legal or official weight.

glosses: bare-handed; empty-handed; without tools or weapons
explanations: Using only one's hands without any implements, weapons, or equipment. Frequently used in martial arts and physical training contexts, as well as figuratively to describe undertaking something without resources.

glosses: survival; remaining from the past; vestige
explanations: Something that has survived or been preserved from an earlier time. Used in archaeological, historical, and biological contexts to describe things that persist from previous eras.
The contrast or range between cold and hot temperatures. Used in technical, engineering, and everyday contexts to discuss temperature fluctuations and their effects on materials or environments.
A fundamental building block in electronics or technology, such as a transistor, diode, or sensor. Refers to a discrete functional unit within a larger system.
The time of year when seeds are planted. An agricultural term for the optimal period to sow crops, which varies by region, climate, and crop type.
Having or using many colors. Used as a modifier to describe printing, dyeing, art, and design that involves more than one or two colors.

glosses: earth and stone; soil and rocks; debris
explanations: A collective term for soil, dirt, and rocks. Frequently appears in disaster-related contexts, particularly regarding landslides and mudflows, as well as in construction and geology.

glosses: silk thread; cocoon thread; raw silk fiber
explanations: Thread obtained from silkworm cocoons. Refers to the raw silk fiber before it is processed into fabric. An important term in the history of Japanese textile production and sericulture.

glosses: local character; regional identity; sense of locality
explanations: The distinctive qualities, customs, and cultural traits that characterize a particular region or locality. Used in discussions of regional culture, literature, cuisine, and art that reflect the unique features of a place.
The reduction or prevention of vibration, especially in engineering, construction, and equipment design. Used for measures and materials that absorb or block unwanted vibrations.

glosses: crawling on one's knees; approaching on one's knees
explanations: The act of moving forward while on one's knees, traditionally performed as a show of deep respect or humility in formal Japanese settings. Also used in Noh theater and other traditional performing arts for a specific movement technique.

glosses: protective wall; barrier wall; defensive fence
explanations: A wall or fence built to protect against wind, noise, fire, or other hazards. Used in construction, urban planning, and general descriptions of protective barriers.

glosses: heaviness in the stomach; indigestion; something to lean on
heaviness in the stomach; indigestion; feeling of fullness
backrest; something to lean on; support
explanations: An uncomfortable heavy feeling in the stomach after eating, as if food is sitting undigested. A common everyday complaint.
Something to lean one's back or body against for support, such as the back of a chair or a wall.

A fearsome demon from Buddhist and Hindu mythology that devours humans. In Japanese Buddhist tradition, these demons are sometimes depicted as protectors of the dharma after being converted by Buddhist teachings. Also used figuratively for someone extremely fierce or frightening.

glosses: praying for clear weather; wishing for good weather
explanations: The practice of praying or wishing for clear, fair weather, especially before important outdoor events. In Japanese folk tradition, this includes making てるてる{坊主|ぼうず} (handmade paper dolls hung to wish for sunshine).

A historical and literary term for romantic and sexual relationships between men. Widely documented in Japanese history, particularly among samurai, Buddhist monks, and the aristocracy from the Heian period through the Edo period.
The act of drinking a beverage quickly, whether in a competitive context, out of hurry, or as a social activity. Can refer to both alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks.

glosses: training; practice; cultivating skill through repetition
explanations: Disciplined practice aimed at mastering a skill, especially in martial arts, qigong, and traditional Chinese-influenced physical or spiritual disciplines. Emphasizes the cultivation of inner skill through sustained effort.

glosses: big-brother type; protective personality; someone who looks after others
explanations: A personality trait of being naturally protective, dependable, and willing to take care of those around you, like an older brother. Describes someone who is generous, decisive, and looks out for the group.

glosses: tea drinker; teetotaler; person who doesn't drink alcohol
explanations: A person who prefers tea or other non-alcoholic beverages over alcohol. An older, somewhat playful expression contrasting with {左党|さとう} (a drinker). Derives from the traditional association of the right hand with rice (and by extension, non-alcoholic drinks).

glosses: estrangement; driving a wedge between people; splitting apart
explanations: The act of causing two people or groups who were close to become estranged or separated, or the resulting state of being split apart. Often involves a third party deliberately creating conflict.

glosses: fee revision; rate change; price adjustment
explanations: The official adjustment or revision of prices, fees, or rates charged for a service or product. Often used for public utilities, transportation fares, and subscription services.

glosses: replacement item; exchange product; substitute goods
explanations: An item provided as a replacement for a defective, broken, or unsuitable product. Commonly used in retail, customer service, and warranty contexts.
The percentage or proportion of people absent from school, work, or an event. Used in educational, workplace, and statistical contexts.

glosses: casebook; case file; record of incidents
explanations: A book or record documenting cases, incidents, or investigations. Used both for actual case records in legal and investigative contexts, and as a title format for mystery fiction and TV shows.

glosses: provisional hiring; probationary employment; tentative appointment
explanations: A period of trial employment where the hire is not yet permanent. The employer evaluates the worker's suitability before confirming full employment. Common in both private companies and public service.
Shipping or dispatching an order on the same day it is placed. A selling point commonly advertised by online retailers and mail-order services.
The habit of sucking one's thumb or fingers, typically seen in infants and young children. Often discussed in parenting and pediatric contexts.

glosses: ordinary savings account; regular bank account
explanations: The most common type of bank account in Japan, used for everyday deposits, withdrawals, and automatic payments. Formally called 普通預金口座, this is the standard account type that individuals open for personal banking.
A specific point or aspect where statements, facts, or logic are contradictory or inconsistent. Used in argumentation, analysis, and investigation.
The last or definitive report on a project, investigation, or study. Indicates that the findings or conclusions are complete and no further updates are expected.
The amount of a drug or medication given to a patient. A key term in medical and pharmaceutical contexts, specifying how much of a substance should be taken or given.

glosses: in transit; on the move; while traveling
explanations: The state of being in the process of moving from one place to another. Used to describe someone who is traveling, commuting, or otherwise not at a fixed location.

glosses: one set; one pair; one group
explanations: A single set or pair of items that go together, such as a set of dishes, a pair of gloves, or a deck of cards.
A single group of people, or the first class/group in a school or organizational division. Japanese schools typically label classes by number: 一組, 二組, etc.

glosses: independent production; self-produced work; indie production
explanations: Creative work produced independently, without backing from a major studio, label, or publisher. Covers films, music, games, and other media made with personal or small-scale resources.
A bank account designed for frequent transactions, primarily used by businesses. Unlike ordinary savings accounts, current accounts typically allow check issuance but pay no interest on the balance.

glosses: academic advisor; thesis supervisor; supervising instructor
explanations: A professor or instructor who guides a student's research, thesis, or academic progress. Also used for supervising officers in military and professional training contexts.
A person who actively encourages or advances a cause, project, or process. Used in business, policy, and organizational contexts for someone who drives progress or change.
A formal written work submitted as a requirement for an academic degree. Encompasses both master's theses and doctoral dissertations.

glosses: storage device; memory unit; data storage
explanations: A hardware device used to store digital data. The formal Japanese term for computer storage, covering hard drives, SSDs, USB drives, and other media that retain data.
The biological instructions encoded in DNA that determine the characteristics of a living organism. Used in biology, medicine, and discussions about heredity and genetics.

glosses: state control; government administration; state management
explanations: Control, oversight, or management of industries, resources, or institutions by the national government. Often used in political and economic discussions about the role of government in regulating or operating key sectors.

glosses: in vitro fertilization; IVF; extracorporeal fertilization
explanations: A medical procedure in which an egg is fertilized by sperm outside the body, and the resulting embryo is transferred to the uterus. A major assisted reproductive technology.
The act of photographing or filming something again, typically because the first attempt was unsatisfactory. Used in photography, film production, and document processing.
Colors without hue — specifically white, black, and all shades of gray. In color theory, these are colors defined only by brightness, with no chromatic component.

glosses: individual packaging; single-dose packaging; portioned packaging
explanations: The practice of dividing and packaging items into individual portions or doses. Most commonly used in pharmacy for dividing medication into single-dose packets, but also applies to food and other products.
The inclined surface of an embankment, levee, or excavation. Used in civil engineering and construction to refer to any artificial or natural slope that has been shaped by cutting or filling earth.

glosses: obsolete word; archaic term; dead word
explanations: A word that has fallen out of common use and is no longer part of active vocabulary. Used in linguistics and language study to classify words that were once current but are now considered outdated.

glosses: full dose; full capacity; maximum amount
explanations: The maximum quantity or dose of something, particularly medication, fuel, or any substance measured by volume or weight. Commonly used in pharmaceutical and technical contexts.
The period or state before a surgical operation. Used as both a standalone noun and as a modifier (術前の) to describe examinations, preparations, or conditions that occur prior to surgery.

glosses: written reply; response document; formal answer in writing
explanations: A formal document written in response to an inquiry, request, or official communication. Used in business, legal, and administrative contexts.
Indicates that a product or item is intended for use in bathing. Commonly found on product labels for bath salts, soap, towels, and other bathing-related items.

glosses: words of praise; laudatory title; honorific appellation
explanations: A formal word or phrase used to praise or honor someone or something. Can refer to honorary titles, laudatory epithets, or expressions of commendation. Used in literary, ceremonial, and formal contexts.

glosses: consignee; recipient of goods; addressee (of a shipment)
explanations: The person or entity designated to receive shipped goods or cargo. A standard term in logistics, shipping, and trade documentation.

glosses: focusing; being in focus; achieving focus
explanations: The state of a lens or optical system being properly focused so that an image appears sharp and clear. Used in photography, optics, and camera technology.

glosses: table card; face-up card on the playing field
explanations: A card that has been played and is lying face-up on the table in a card game. Used in hanafuda, karuta, and other traditional Japanese card games, as well as modern card games.

glosses: seven spring herbs; seven herbs of spring
explanations: A set of seven edible wild herbs traditionally eaten in a rice porridge on January 7th. The seven herbs are: seri (water dropwort), nazuna (shepherd's purse), gogyo (cudweed), hakobera (chickweed), hotokenoza (henbit), suzuna (turnip), and suzushiro (daikon radish).

glosses: box tissues; tissue box; boxed facial tissues
explanations: Facial tissues sold in a rectangular box, as opposed to pocket tissues. A ubiquitous household item in Japan found in virtually every home, office, and car.

glosses: rice flour bread; bread made from rice flour
explanations: Bread made using rice flour instead of or in addition to wheat flour. Popular in Japan as a gluten-free alternative and as a way to promote domestic rice consumption.

glosses: as stated above; the above; aforementioned
explanations: A formal written expression meaning "as described above" or "the foregoing." Used in legal documents, academic papers, and formal reports to refer back to previously stated content.

glosses: delayed reply; late response; belated answer
explanations: A reply or response that comes after an expected or appropriate timeframe. Used in formal correspondence and business communication to acknowledge that one's reply is overdue.

An honorific expression used when offering food or drink to someone of higher social status or to a guest. It is the honorific form of {食|た}べる and {飲|の}む, and is commonly heard in restaurants, formal dining, and hospitality settings.
A principle or system in which people are evaluated, promoted, or rewarded based on their actual achievements and results rather than seniority, background, or other factors.
The practice of studying or learning at one's own home rather than at school or another institution. Used broadly for homework-style study, remote learning, and self-directed education.

glosses: rental conference room; meeting room for hire
explanations: A meeting room or conference space that can be rented by the hour or day, commonly found in urban business districts. Used by freelancers, small businesses, and companies that need temporary meeting space.
The process of identifying, assessing, and controlling threats to an organization or individual. Widely used in business, finance, healthcare, and disaster preparedness.
The act or obligation of keeping information secret and not disclosing it to unauthorized parties. Commonly used in legal, business, and medical contexts.
Intense fear or anxiety about performing or speaking in front of an audience. Can range from mild nervousness to a debilitating phobia.

glosses: unwanted item collection; junk removal; disposal service
explanations: A service that collects and disposes of items people no longer need, such as old furniture, appliances, and household goods. Common in Japan, where strict waste disposal rules make getting rid of large items complicated.
The act of fitting one object into another, or the resulting joint or piece. Used in woodworking, jewelry, construction, and crafts for pieces that fit snugly into prepared openings.
In photography, video, and design, the technique of inserting one image or footage into another, such as green-screen compositing or picture-in-picture effects.

glosses: to read too much; to overinterpret; to overthink
to overinterpret; to read too much into something; to overthink
explanations: To spend too much time reading, or to read an excessive amount of material.
To find meanings or intentions that are not actually there, attributing excessive significance to words, actions, or situations.

headword: 終わりよければすべてよし
explanations: A proverb meaning that as long as the final outcome is good, any difficulties or problems along the way can be forgiven or forgotten.

glosses: brotherly love; fraternal love; love for one's compatriots
explanations: A sense of love, kinship, and solidarity toward people of the same nation, community, or human family. Can refer narrowly to patriotic fellow-feeling or broadly to universal human compassion.

glosses: unfaithful; disloyal; not true to one's obligations
explanations: Lacking faithfulness or loyalty to a person, duty, or commitment. Used for romantic infidelity, professional disloyalty, and failure to honor obligations.
A public event or showing to announce and display a completed work, building, or product. Most commonly used for film premieres and building completion ceremonies.

glosses: selfishness; doing as one pleases; willfulness
explanations: Behaving according to one's own wishes without regard for others. Used both as a noun and as a na-adjective to describe selfish behavior or a self-centered personality.
Fertilizer derived from natural, organic materials such as compost, animal manure, bone meal, or plant matter, as opposed to chemically synthesized fertilizers.
A city with an excessively high population density that strains infrastructure, housing, and public services. A central concept in Japanese urban planning and social policy discussions.

glosses: hazard management; danger management; safety management
explanations: The systematic identification and control of dangers and hazards, particularly in workplaces, industrial settings, and daily life. Focuses on preventing accidents and injuries.

The process of making products, especially electronic devices, thinner and more compact. A key concept in Japanese product design and electronics manufacturing, where miniaturization is highly valued.

glosses: earnestly honest; wholeheartedly sincere; single-mindedly upright
explanations: Describes a person who is thoroughly honest and sincere in everything they do, without any pretense or calculation. Combines the ideas of honesty and wholehearted devotion.

glosses: seat category; type of seating; seating class
explanations: A classification of seats by type, price, or location, used when purchasing tickets for concerts, sporting events, theaters, and transportation.

glosses: medical history; past illness record; previous medical conditions
explanations: A record of a patient's past illnesses, surgeries, and medical conditions. Used in clinical settings when gathering patient information.

A standard-sized bottle holding 720 milliliters (four go), most commonly used for sake, shochu, and other Japanese alcoholic beverages. One of the two standard bottle sizes in the Japanese alcohol industry.
The level to which coffee beans or tea leaves have been roasted, which affects flavor, aroma, and color. Most commonly used in the context of coffee.

glosses: brand new, unused; new and unopened
explanations: A label indicating that an item has never been used or opened since purchase. Extremely common in online marketplace listings and secondhand shops in Japan.

glosses: collusive relationship; corrupt ties; cozy relationship
explanations: An improperly close relationship between entities that should maintain independence, especially between politicians and businesses, or between government agencies and private interests. Carries a strongly negative connotation.

Publishing through an established publishing house that bears the costs of production and distribution, in contrast to self-publishing where the author pays. The publisher selects manuscripts, edits, prints, and distributes the work.

glosses: performance technique; playing technique; musical skill
explanations: The technical skill and proficiency involved in playing a musical instrument or performing music. Encompasses both fundamental mechanics and advanced expressive techniques.

glosses: manufacturing cost; cost of production; cost of goods manufactured
explanations: The total cost incurred in producing goods, including raw materials, labor, and factory overhead. A key accounting term used in financial statements and business management.

glosses: relay station; repeater station; retransmission station
explanations: A broadcasting or telecommunications facility that receives a signal and retransmits it to extend coverage to areas that cannot receive the original signal directly.

glosses: grappling technique; clinch technique; locking technique
explanations: A technique in martial arts involving close-body contact such as holds, locks, throws, and pins. Used in judo, jiu-jitsu, wrestling, and other grappling arts, as opposed to striking techniques.
The fibrous tissue that forms over a wound after healing. Used as the formal medical term for scars, in contrast to the more everyday word {傷跡|きずあと}.
An engine that generates power by burning fuel inside the engine itself, as opposed to external combustion engines like steam engines. Includes gasoline engines, diesel engines, and gas turbines.

glosses: standard household; model household; reference household
explanations: A statistically defined household type used as a baseline for government statistics, tax calculations, and utility rate comparisons. Traditionally defined as a married couple with two children, though the concept is evolving as household structures change.

glosses: currency circulation; money supply in circulation
explanations: The flow and distribution of money through an economy, or the total amount of currency currently in use. Used in economic discussions about monetary policy and the money supply.

glosses: playback screen; player screen; playback view
explanations: The screen or interface displayed during audio or video playback on a device or application. Shows controls such as play, pause, and seek, along with the media content.

Fertilizer applied to plants after they have already been planted and are actively growing, as opposed to base fertilizer applied before planting. An essential practice in Japanese gardening and agriculture.
The first-born grandchild, regardless of gender. A formal term used in family contexts, inheritance discussions, and historical or literary texts.

headword: 二兎を追う者は一兎をも得ず
glosses: he who chases two hares catches neither; don't try to do two things at once
if you try to do two things at once, you will fail at both
explanations: A proverb warning against spreading one's efforts too thin. By pursuing two goals simultaneously, you risk achieving neither.

headword: 急いては事を仕損じる
glosses: haste makes waste; more haste, less speed
haste makes waste; rushing leads to mistakes
explanations: A proverb warning that acting too hastily causes errors and poor results. Patience and careful action produce better outcomes.

glosses: prior to; before; in advance of
explanations: A formal expression indicating that one action or event occurs before another. Used to set temporal context, especially for preparatory actions taken before a main event.

glosses: to dissolve; to mix into a liquid
to dissolve; to mix (a powder or solid) into a liquid
explanations: To stir or blend a substance into liquid until it dissolves or forms a smooth mixture. Commonly used in cooking for mixing ingredients like flour, eggs, or seasonings into liquid.

glosses: to spout; to gush; to erupt
to spout; to gush; to spray
explanations: For liquid, steam, or gas to burst out forcefully from an opening or source.
For a volcano to discharge lava, ash, or gas. Also used figuratively for emotions or situations that burst out uncontrollably.

glosses: one place; one spot; a single location
one place; one spot; one point
explanations: A single location, spot, or point. Used both for physical places and abstract points (such as a single error in a document or a single spot on the body).

glosses: to pay attention; to be attentive; to be considerate
to pay attention to; to be attentive to; to take care of
explanations: To direct one's awareness and consideration toward something or someone. Implies thoughtful, ongoing attention rather than a momentary glance.

glosses: left-side component of a kanji; radical
left-side component of a kanji character
explanations: The structural component that appears on the left side of a kanji character. One of the major categories of kanji components used to classify and look up characters in dictionaries.
A Japanese banknote with a face value of 5,000 yen. One of the standard denominations of Japanese paper currency.
A Japanese banknote with a face value of 10,000 yen. The highest denomination of Japanese paper currency and the most commonly used bill for large purchases.

glosses: excuse me for going first; after you; go ahead
excuse me for going first; I'll go ahead
after you; go ahead; please go first
explanations: A polite expression used when leaving before others, such as leaving the office or a gathering earlier than colleagues. Short for お{先|さき}に{失礼|しつれい}します.
Used to politely yield to someone, inviting them to go before you — for example, letting someone enter an elevator or go through a door first.

glosses: take care of yourself; get well soon
take care of yourself; get well soon; look after yourself
explanations: A set expression said to someone who is sick, injured, or about to visit a doctor. Conveys a wish for recovery and concern for the person's health.

glosses: no photography; photography prohibited; no filming
explanations: A prohibition on taking photographs or recording video. Commonly seen on signs in museums, theaters, temples, and other locations where photography is restricted.

glosses: required time; travel time; time needed
required time; time needed; time it takes
explanations: The amount of time required to complete a task, make a trip, or carry out a process. Commonly used for travel durations, cooking times, and procedure lengths.

glosses: ready to eat; ripe for eating; at its best for eating
ready to eat; at peak ripeness; at its best for eating
explanations: The ideal state or timing for eating something, especially fruit or other produce that reaches peak flavor and texture at a certain point of ripeness.

glosses: at its peak; in full bloom; height of
at its peak; in full bloom; at the height of
explanations: The point at which something is at its most intense, active, or flourishing. Used for seasons, activities, careers, and other things that have a peak period.

glosses: at its best for drinking; ready to drink
at its best for drinking; ready to drink; at the ideal drinking temperature or maturity
explanations: The optimal state for consuming a beverage, whether in terms of temperature, age (for wine), or brewing time (for tea). Often used for wine, sake, tea, and other drinks where timing or temperature matters.

glosses: outside of hours; after hours; overtime
explanations: Time that falls outside regular operating hours, business hours, or scheduled hours. Used for businesses, hospitals, offices, and other organizations.
Work performed beyond regular working hours. Often used in labor contexts to refer to overtime work and overtime pay.

glosses: to have someone look at; please take a look (humble)
to have someone (superior) look at; to show to a respected person
explanations: A humble expression used when asking or describing the action of a respected person viewing, reading, or watching something. Combines the honorific ご{覧|らん} (looking) with the humble auxiliary いただく (to receive the favor of).

glosses: thanks to you; fortunately; I'm happy to say
thanks to you; thanks to your help; owing to your kindness
fortunately; happily; I'm glad to say
explanations: A polite expression used when acknowledging someone else's help or influence in a positive outcome. Expresses gratitude for the other person's support.
Used as a polite conversational opener when reporting good news, even when the listener did not directly contribute to the outcome. A humble way of sharing positive developments.
The side of an object or surface that faces downward or is positioned below another part.

glosses: leaving a nursery school or kindergarten; withdrawal from a preschool
explanations: The act of a child being taken out of or graduating from a nursery school ({保育園|ほいくえん}) or kindergarten ({幼稚園|ようちえん}). Used for both voluntary withdrawal and planned departure.

glosses: daytime type; morning person; diurnal lifestyle
explanations: A person who is naturally active during the day and goes to bed early, or a lifestyle pattern centered around daytime hours. Contrasts with {夜型|よるがた} (night-owl type).
Classification, sorting, or presentation of data organized according to geographic region. Commonly used in statistics, reports, and administrative contexts.
A body or form that is soft and flexible, lacking hard skeletal structure. Most commonly encountered in the compound {軟体動物|なんたいどうぶつ} (mollusk), but also used independently to describe flexibility.

glosses: water column; water spout; pillar of water
explanations: A column-shaped body of water rising vertically, such as a geyser eruption, a burst water main, or a waterspout. Also used as a unit of pressure measurement (millimeters of water column).

The psychological process of encoding new information into memory. A technical term used in psychology and cognitive science, corresponding to the encoding stage of memory (as distinct from retention and recall).
Cruel and oppressive governance that abuses power and causes suffering to the people. Used in historical, political, and literary contexts.
Thread or yarn spun from cotton fibers. Used in textile manufacturing, sewing, and crafts.

glosses: quick work; nimble technique; feat of speed
explanations: An action performed with impressive speed and skill. Used to describe someone completing a task remarkably fast, a quick sleight-of-hand trick, or a rapid technique in martial arts or sports.

glosses: the side next to; the neighboring side; adjacent side
explanations: The side or area immediately next to something or someone. Used when specifying which side of an object, building, or space you are referring to.

glosses: to bring close together; to reconcile; to align
to bring close together; to press together
to reconcile; to align; to bring into agreement
explanations: To physically bring two things close together so they touch or are side by side.
To bring differing opinions, positions, or numbers into alignment. Commonly used in business and negotiations to describe the process of reconciling differences.

glosses: roll call; calling names aloud; designation
explanations: The act of calling out names one by one, as in a roll call or attendance check.
The name or label by which something is referred to. Used in technical and administrative contexts for the official or common name of an item.

glosses: doing as one pleases; acting freely and selfishly
explanations: Behaving however one wants without regard for rules, expectations, or other people's feelings. Carries a negative connotation of selfishness or inconsideration.
The state of a machine, system, or service operating continuously without interruption. Commonly used in IT, manufacturing, and infrastructure contexts.

glosses: plumbing work; water supply construction; waterworks repair
explanations: Construction, repair, or maintenance work on water supply and drainage systems, including pipes, faucets, and sewage connections. Encompasses both residential plumbing and public water infrastructure projects.
A building equipped with a wind-driven mechanism, historically used for grinding grain into flour. Often associated with European landscapes, fairy tales, and the story of Don Quixote.

glosses: member of the House of Representatives
explanations: An elected member of the House of Representatives ({衆議院|しゅうぎいん}), the lower house of the Japanese National Diet. Members serve four-year terms and are chosen through a combination of single-seat constituencies and proportional representation.

glosses: should be; is expected to; is supposed to
should be; is expected to; ought to be
is supposed to; is scheduled to
explanations: Expresses the speaker's expectation or logical conclusion that something is or should be the case, based on reasoning, evidence, or prior knowledge.
Indicates that something was planned, arranged, or supposed to happen according to a schedule or agreement.
Expresses a moral obligation, recommendation, or the speaker's judgment that something is the right or proper course of action.
Used in the past tense (べきだった) to express regret or criticism that something was not done when it should have been.

glosses: it seems; it appears; it looks like
in such a way that; so that
explanations: Expresses the speaker's judgment or inference based on what they have observed or sensed. Indicates that something appears to be a certain way.
Used to make comparisons or similes, expressing that something resembles or is similar to something else.
Used with verbs to express a desired manner or goal, indicating the way something should be done.
Used to indicate that there is no difficulty, obstacle, or cause for concern. Often used as a reassuring response.

glosses: how much; how long; to what extent
how much; how many; to what extent
explanations: Used to ask about quantity, degree, or extent of something.
Used to ask about duration of time or physical distance.
An interdisciplinary academic field that studies the relationship between human activity and the natural environment, encompassing ecology, conservation, pollution, and sustainability.
The pitcher who begins the game on the mound and pitches the first inning. In professional baseball, starting pitchers typically pitch every five or six days in a rotation.
Pottery produced during the Jomon period (approximately 14,000-300 BCE) in prehistoric Japan, characterized by distinctive cord-marked patterns and elaborate decorative designs.

glosses: great supporting actor; excellent supporting player
great supporting actor; excellent character actor
excellent supporting player; key contributor in a secondary role
explanations: An actor who excels in supporting roles, adding depth and quality to a production without being the lead.
Used figuratively for any person or thing that plays an outstanding secondary role, supporting and enhancing the main element.
An organism that lived in a past geological age, now known primarily through fossil remains. Encompasses everything from ancient bacteria to dinosaurs.
Traditional performing arts rooted in local communities and passed down through generations, including folk dances, festival performances, ritual music, and theatrical traditions.
Refers to having an above-average height. Often used to describe physical attributes, especially in contexts like dating profiles, fashion, and sports.
A photo album created to preserve memories of a special occasion such as a graduation, wedding, or school year.
The player with the highest batting average in a league or season. An important statistical title in professional baseball.

glosses: like; as if; as though; resembling
explanations: A literary or classical expression meaning 'like' or 'as if,' used to draw comparisons. More formal and literary than ようだ or みたいだ.
The spread of nuclear weapons, nuclear weapon technology, or fissile materials to states or groups that do not already possess them.
A detailed plan prepared by a teacher outlining the objectives, content, methods, and activities for a class session or series of lessons.
The legal right of a foreign national to reside in a country. In Japan, this is governed by immigration law and tied to specific visa categories.
A type of particle in Japanese grammar that connects clauses, indicating relationships such as cause, condition, concession, or sequence between them.

A way of cutting vegetables and other ingredients into stick or baton shapes, typically about 4-5 cm long and 1 cm square in cross-section. Named after its resemblance to hyoushigi (wooden clappers used in traditional Japanese performances).

glosses: new construction; newly built structure or vessel
explanations: Refers to the building of something new, especially ships, buildings, or other large structures. Most commonly used in the context of shipbuilding to mean a newly constructed ship.
An older usage referring to a newly married woman or young wife. This sense is now archaic or dialectal but appears in classical literature and historical texts.

glosses: arrival of goods; receipt of shipment
arrival of goods; receipt of a shipment
explanations: The arrival of ordered goods or cargo at their destination. Used in business and logistics contexts to indicate that a shipment has been received.

glosses: auspicious day; lucky day; favorable day
explanations: A day considered to be fortunate or propitious for important events such as weddings, business openings, or moving house. Based on the traditional Japanese calendar system that designates certain days as lucky or unlucky.
The administrative and ritual duties involved in running a Shinto shrine. Includes managing ceremonies, maintaining shrine grounds, handling visitors, and conducting daily rituals.
The protective case or sheath for a Japanese sword. An essential component of a complete sword mounting, traditionally made of wood with a lacquered finish.
The string of a bow used in archery. In the context of Japanese archery, it refers to the string of a traditional longbow.
The state of having nothing in one's hands — no weapons, tools, or resources. Used both literally to mean fighting with bare fists and figuratively to mean starting with nothing.

glosses: troops and horses; military forces; military matters
explanations: A literary term referring to soldiers and their horses, used to represent military power or warfare in general. Appears in historical texts, literary works, and formal writing.

glosses: nuts and seeds; seed and fruit
nuts and seeds; seeds and fruits
explanations: A collective term for the edible seeds, nuts, and small dried fruits of plants. Used in food science, nutrition, and botany to refer to this food category as a group.
The transmission of electrical current through a material. Used in physics and engineering to describe the ability of a substance to conduct electricity.
The process of keeping eggs warm so that the embryos inside develop and eventually hatch. Used for both natural incubation by parent birds and artificial incubation using machines.
A body of water partially enclosed by land, forming an indentation in the coastline. Used in geographical and maritime contexts.

glosses: soil quality; soil type; nature of the soil
explanations: The physical and chemical properties of soil, including its composition, texture, drainage, and fertility. Used in agriculture, construction, and earth sciences.

glosses: reckless driving; driving wildly out of control
explanations: Dangerous, uncontrolled driving of a vehicle, typically at high speed and without regard for traffic rules or safety. Often used in news reports about traffic incidents.
Running about in a disorderly or chaotic manner, without direction or control. Can refer to people, animals, or figuratively to things spiraling out of control.
The material forming the inner core of a layered or composite structure. Used in construction, manufacturing, and materials science to describe the central structural component.
The dense, dark inner wood of a tree trunk, as opposed to the lighter sapwood on the outside. Heartwood is valued in woodworking for its durability and color.

glosses: cigarette dangling from the mouth; smoking with a cigarette held in the lips
explanations: The act or state of holding a lit cigarette in one's mouth while doing something else with the hands. Often evokes a casual, rough, or nonchalant image.
A building or hall where religious ceremonies, rituals, or festivals are conducted. Used for both Shinto and Buddhist contexts, as well as more broadly for any sacred or ceremonial space.

glosses: cold and warm; both cooling and heating
explanations: Refers to both cold and warm temperatures together, especially in the context of devices or systems that can provide both cooling and heating functions.
A relatively low temperature, typically used in technical or scientific contexts to describe conditions below normal ambient temperature but above freezing.
An incorrect judgment or ruling, particularly in legal or sports contexts. Refers to a decision made by a judge, referee, or authority that turns out to be wrong.

glosses: carriage road; road for horse-drawn carriages
explanations: A road designed or historically used for horse-drawn carriages. In modern usage, often refers to historical roads or streets that preserve the name from the era of horse-drawn transportation.

glosses: leading male role; male protagonist (in kabuki)
leading male role; male protagonist in traditional theater
key player; central figure; leading role (figurative)
explanations: The principal male role in kabuki and other traditional Japanese performing arts. The term specifically refers to serious, dignified male characters, as distinct from comic or villainous roles.
By extension, a person who plays the most important or central part in an event, project, or achievement.
A small wheeled cart pushed or pulled by hand, used for transporting goods or materials. Common in markets, warehouses, and construction sites.
A hinged control surface on the trailing edge of an airplane wing, used to control the aircraft's roll. Ailerons on the left and right wings move in opposite directions to tilt the plane.

The transfer of heat through a material by direct contact between molecules, without bulk movement of the material itself. One of the three main modes of heat transfer, alongside convection and radiation.

glosses: releasing fish; fish stocking; restocking fish
explanations: The act of releasing fish into rivers, lakes, or the sea, typically as part of conservation efforts, fishery management, or cultural practices. Includes both restocking programs and ceremonial releases.

glosses: summer insect; insect drawn to fire
summer insect; bugs that appear in summer
insect drawn to fire; moth drawn to a flame
explanations: A general term for insects that are active during the summer months, such as beetles, cicadas, fireflies, and moths.
An insect, typically a moth, that flies toward a light or flame and is burned. Used figuratively to describe someone who rushes headlong into danger or destruction.

glosses: point sticks; scoring sticks used in mahjong
explanations: Narrow stick-shaped tokens used to keep score in mahjong. Each player starts with a set number of points represented by these sticks, which are exchanged when a hand is won or lost.

glosses: transfer to a different facility; relocation
transfer to a different facility; relocation of placement
explanations: The act of transferring a person from one facility, institution, or care center to another. Commonly used in welfare, medical, and institutional contexts for transfers between care homes, hospitals, or detention facilities.

glosses: preliminary figure; flash estimate; initial report value
explanations: A provisional numerical value released quickly after data collection, before thorough verification. Commonly used for economic indicators like GDP, trade statistics, and employment figures that are published in stages — first as a preliminary estimate, then revised.

Describes a building that has three above-ground floors. Formed from the counter 三階 (three floors) plus 建て (built, constructed), this is part of the productive ～階建て pattern used to describe the number of stories in any building.

glosses: second choice; second preference; backup option
explanations: One's second-ranked preference, typically when applying for schools, universities, jobs, or other competitive selections. Used in the context of ranking multiple options in order of desirability.

glosses: sushi platter; assorted sushi; sushi assortment
explanations: An arrangement of various pieces of sushi served together on a plate or tray. Commonly ordered at sushi restaurants or purchased at supermarkets as a pre-made assortment, typically containing a variety of nigiri and sometimes maki rolls.

glosses: consecutive work days; working without a day off; continuous duty
explanations: Working for multiple days in a row without rest days in between. Often discussed in the context of labor regulations, overwork, and work-life balance in Japan.

glosses: neologism; newly coined word; new coinage
explanations: A word that has been recently created or invented, either by combining existing elements in a new way or by introducing an entirely new term. Used in linguistic and media discussions about language evolution.

glosses: heroine; female protagonist; female lead character
explanations: The main female character in a novel, film, drama, manga, anime, or other narrative work. Distinguished from 主人公 (protagonist, which is gender-neutral but often assumed male) by the prefix 女 to specify the character is female.

glosses: reload; refresh; re-loading of data or a page
explanations: The act of loading content again, most commonly used for refreshing a web page or reloading data in a software application. The Japanese equivalent of 'reload' or 'refresh' in computing contexts.

glosses: one-person company; sole-member corporation; single-owner business entity
explanations: A legally incorporated company where a single individual serves as the sole shareholder, director, and often the only employee. Distinct from sole proprietorship in that it is a registered corporate entity with limited liability.

glosses: light gray; pale gray; ash gray
explanations: A muted, pale shade of gray. Used to describe colors in fashion, design, interior decoration, and nature. Formed with the prefix 薄 (light, thin) added to 灰色 (gray).

glosses: dark gray; charcoal gray; deep gray
explanations: A dark shade of gray approaching black. Used to describe colors in fashion, materials, and natural phenomena. Formed with the prefix 濃 (dark, deep, concentrated) added to 灰色 (gray).

glosses: bedwetting; wetting the bed; nocturnal enuresis
explanations: Involuntary urination during sleep, typically referring to children who have not yet outgrown the habit. Used in everyday conversation about child development as well as in medical contexts.

glosses: popular literature; mass-market fiction; entertainment literature
explanations: Literature written primarily for entertainment and broad popular appeal, as opposed to serious or highbrow literary fiction. Encompasses genres like mystery, romance, adventure, and historical fiction aimed at a general readership.

glosses: external; outward; pertaining to outward appearance
explanations: Relating to the outward appearance or external look of something, as opposed to its internal substance, function, or character. Used when discussing how something appears on the surface.

glosses: biweekly publication; fortnightly; published every other week
explanations: A publication schedule or format in which issues are released once every two weeks. Used as both a noun and a prenominal modifier to describe the frequency of magazines, newspapers, and other serial publications.

glosses: three years ago; the year before the year before last
explanations: More formal equivalent of {三年前|さんねんまえ}. Used in written and formal spoken contexts.

glosses: enka singer; a singer who performs enka (traditional Japanese popular ballads)
explanations: Refers to professional singers who specialize in the enka genre.

glosses: policy interest rate; the benchmark interest rate set by a central bank to guide monetary policy
explanations: Used in economics and finance contexts. In Japan, this refers to the rate set by the Bank of Japan.

glosses: purchase bonus; special gift or benefit included with a purchase
explanations: Common in retail, especially for books, games, CDs, and online shopping.

glosses: get-well gift; a gift brought when visiting someone who is ill or hospitalized
explanations: The お prefix is standard and almost always included.

glosses: monetary tightening; a policy of raising interest rates or restricting the money supply to curb inflation
explanations: Used in economic and financial reporting.

glosses: swimming goggles; underwater goggles; diving mask
explanations: Covers both competitive swim goggles and snorkeling/diving masks.

glosses: Gothic typeface; sans-serif font (in Japanese typography)
explanations: In Japanese typography, ゴシック{体|たい} refers to sans-serif fonts, which is different from the Western meaning of Gothic.

glosses: rarely seen in recent years; unprecedented in modern times; remarkable (used to modify a noun)
explanations: Functions as a pre-noun modifier. Often used in news reporting and formal writing to emphasize the exceptional nature of something.

glosses: special news bulletin; breaking news; emergency broadcast
explanations: Used when regular programming is interrupted for urgent news.

glosses: potluck party; a party where each guest brings a dish or drink to share
explanations: Common in both casual and semi-formal social gatherings.

glosses: to roll dice; to throw dice
explanations: Used literally in games, and occasionally figuratively to mean taking a chance.

glosses: imitation crab meat; surimi sticks shaped and flavored to resemble crab
explanations: Often abbreviated to カニカマ in casual speech.
In everyday Japanese, often refers to any bottled water, not just water with mineral content.

glosses: professional; a person with specialized expertise or someone who does something for a living
explanations: Can be used as a noun (a professional) or as a na-adjective (professional-quality).
A horizontal or vertical line of text in writing, printing, or on a screen. Used when referring to specific positions in documents, code, or printed material.
A row of the Japanese syllabary chart (五十音図), grouping kana that share the same consonant.
A prefix attached to nouns to indicate only one of a pair or set, or that something is incomplete or one-sided. Often implies an imbalance or that the counterpart is absent.

A traditional Japanese sweet consisting of three rice dumplings on a skewer, each a different color: pink (or red), white, and green. Strongly associated with cherry blossom viewing (hanami) and spring.

glosses: foreigner; person from another country; stranger from a foreign land
explanations: A literary or somewhat old-fashioned term for a person from a different country. Carries a more romantic or exotic nuance than the neutral 外国人, often evoking historical or literary contexts.

glosses: resource collection; recyclable collection; recycling pickup
explanations: The organized collection of recyclable materials such as paper, cans, bottles, and plastic for reuse or recycling. A routine part of waste management in Japanese communities, with designated collection days and sorting rules.

glosses: number of votes; vote count; ballot count
explanations: The total number of votes cast in an election, poll, or any kind of voting process. Frequently used in news reporting about elections and surveys.
The price at which goods are sold in bulk by a wholesaler to a retailer, before being marked up for sale to the end consumer. Lower than the retail price.
Nitrogen in its liquid state, kept at extremely low temperatures (around −196°C). Used in science, medicine, food processing, and industrial applications for rapid freezing and cooling.
A fictional or hypothetical being from the planet Mars. Used in science fiction and popular culture, and sometimes figuratively to describe someone who seems completely out of touch or alien.
A victory in which the opposing team or player scores zero points or runs. Used primarily in baseball and other sports where preventing the opponent from scoring entirely is a notable achievement.

glosses: maritime nation; seafaring state; ocean nation
explanations: A country whose identity, economy, or strategic interests are strongly tied to the sea. Used in discussions of geopolitics, history, and national identity, especially regarding island nations and countries with major naval or trade traditions.

A camera with a single lens system used for both viewing and capturing images, typically with interchangeable lenses. Covers both traditional single-lens reflex (SLR) cameras and modern mirrorless interchangeable-lens cameras.
A person who provides aid, assistance, or support to others. Used in contexts ranging from international humanitarian aid to personal help and social welfare.

glosses: term of endearment; pet name; nickname word
term of endearment; pet name; affectionate nickname
explanations: A word or name form used to express affection or familiarity, such as shortened names, diminutives, or special nicknames. A linguistic term that also appears in everyday discussions about how people address loved ones.
The fleshy back part of the lower leg between the knee and the ankle. Most commonly encountered in the compound こむら返り (leg cramp).

glosses: frequent; repeated; occurring in many instances
explanations: Describes events or phenomena that happen many times or in many locations. Often used in news and formal reporting to characterize incidents, accidents, or outbreaks that occur repeatedly.

Relating to the entire Earth or affecting the whole planet. Used when discussing issues, phenomena, or perspectives that span the globe, especially in environmental, scientific, and geopolitical contexts.

The second-in-command in a professional kitchen, directly below the head chef. Responsible for overseeing kitchen operations when the head chef is absent and assisting with menu planning and staff management.
An interrogative expression used to ask about the number of small, round, or compact objects. Combines the question word 何 with the general-purpose counter 個.

glosses: vinyl sheet; plastic tarp; ground sheet
explanations: A large flat piece of vinyl or plastic material used as a ground cover, protective sheet, or tarp. Commonly used for picnics, outdoor events, construction sites, and disaster preparedness.

glosses: sukiyaki pot; shallow iron pot for sukiyaki
explanations: A wide, shallow, heavy iron or cast-iron pot specifically designed for cooking sukiyaki. Its flat bottom and low sides allow ingredients to be simmered in a thin layer of sweet soy-based broth at the table.

glosses: classic film; old movie; classic cinema
explanations: A film widely recognized as a masterpiece or an important work from an earlier era of cinema. Can refer to both Japanese and Western films, typically from roughly the 1920s through the 1970s.

The turn to make a move in a board game or strategy game. Primarily used in shogi, go, chess, and similar turn-based games. Can also refer to the advantage of having the initiative or the right to move.

The result of having expected or predicted something that turned out to be wrong. Refers to the letdown when reality fails to meet one's assessment or hopes, especially regarding people, investments, or outcomes.

glosses: latest model; newest version; current model
explanations: The most recently released version of a product, especially cars, electronics, appliances, or other manufactured goods. Emphasizes that this is the most up-to-date version available.

The process of organizing, prioritizing, and tracking tasks and to-do items, especially in a work or project context. Encompasses both the concept and the tools (apps, boards, lists) used to manage tasks.
