glosses: receipt; written acknowledgment that something has been received
explanations: A document confirming that goods, money, or documents have been received. Used in both commercial transactions and official procedures.

glosses: hair dye; hair coloring; hair color treatment
explanations: A product or salon service used to change the color of one's hair. Refers to both the product itself and the act of coloring hair.

glosses: sea breeze; ocean wind; breeze blowing from the rocky shore
explanations: A wind that blows from the sea or the rocky coast, carrying the scent of salt and seaweed. A poetic and evocative word associated with the Japanese coastline.

glosses: bamboo pole; long bamboo stick used for hanging laundry or as a tool
explanations: A long pole made of bamboo, traditionally used for hanging laundry to dry outdoors. Also used for reaching high places, fishing, and other purposes.

glosses: to tweet; to post on social media
to tweet; to post on X (formerly Twitter)
explanations: To publish a short message on the social media platform X (formerly Twitter). By extension, sometimes used loosely for posting on other social media platforms.

glosses: wreath; decorative ring of flowers or foliage
explanations: A contract for the long-term rental of equipment, vehicles, or property. Common in business for acquiring expensive assets without purchasing them outright.
A circular decoration made of flowers, leaves, or other materials, hung on doors or walls. Associated with Christmas and other occasions.

glosses: morning service; breakfast set offered at cafes at a discount
morning coat; cutaway coat; men's formal daywear
explanations: A special breakfast deal offered by cafes and coffee shops, typically in the morning hours. The customer orders a drink and receives toast, eggs, or other breakfast items for free or at a reduced price.
A formal men's coat with tails tapering from the front waist to the back knee, worn at weddings, funerals, and formal daytime ceremonies.

glosses: with a tapping or knocking sound
explanations: Describes doing something with patient, sustained effort over time, often involving repetitive small actions that accumulate into significant results.
Mimics the sound of hard objects striking a surface repeatedly, such as knocking on a door, footsteps on a hard floor, or tapping with a tool.
A formal written document submitted to resign from a position, typically used in the context of employment or public office.

glosses: wavelength; compatibility; being on the same page
explanations: The distance between successive crests of a wave, used in physics to describe light, sound, and other wave phenomena.
Used figuratively to describe how well two people's personalities, thinking styles, or communication mesh together.

glosses: once upon a time; long, long ago
explanations: A formulaic opening for traditional Japanese folktales and fairy tales, equivalent to English 'once upon a time.' Signals that a story set in the distant, unspecified past is about to begin.
An emphatic reflexive pronoun that stresses the person themselves, as opposed to others. Combines {自分|じぶん} (self) with {自身|じしん} (itself) for emphasis.

glosses: condescending attitude; looking down on others
condescending attitude; looking down on others; talking down to someone
explanations: An attitude or manner of speaking that comes across as superior or patronizing, as if the person is literally looking down from above. Always carries a negative connotation.
Describes something so minor or unimportant that it does not merit attention or discussion. Literally 'not sufficient to take up.'
The act of firing a gun at a target, or the gunfire itself. Used both as a noun and as a suru verb.

glosses: to feel rough; to be coarse to the touch
to feel rough; to be coarse; to have a gritty texture
explanations: Describes a surface or texture that feels rough, gritty, or unsmooth when touched. Derives from the onomatopoeia ざらざら.

glosses: complexion; color of one's face; skin color as indicator of health
explanations: The color or hue of a person's face or skin, particularly as an indicator of their health or physical condition. Literally 'blood color.'

glosses: resourcefulness; quick wit; talent for practical problem-solving
means of raising money; financial resourcefulness
explanations: The ability to think quickly and find clever solutions, especially in practical or business matters. Implies a combination of intelligence and pragmatic adaptability.
The ability to procure money or resources when needed, often through clever or industrious means.
An area of low-lying, waterlogged land where the ground is soft and wet. May have standing water and characteristic wetland vegetation.
An organized arrangement of people standing or moving in orderly lines, especially in military or ceremonial contexts.
A post-secondary educational institution offering two- or three-year programs, shorter than a four-year university. Often abbreviated as {短大|たんだい}.

glosses: putting one's affairs in order; tidying up one's personal matters
putting one's affairs in order; tidying up personal matters
explanations: The act of organizing, sorting, and settling one's personal belongings and affairs, typically in preparation for a major life change such as moving, retirement, or in anticipation of death.

glosses: good news; glad tidings; a welcome development
explanations: The Christian Gospels — the teachings of Jesus Christ or the books of the New Testament that record them (Matthew, Mark, Luke, John).
Used more broadly to mean welcome or uplifting news, especially something that brings hope or relief to people in difficulty.
A state where law and order do not prevail, or behavior that defies rules and social norms.
Behavior that is excessively aggressive, unreasonable, or reckless, disregarding consequences or propriety.
A small rural community or settlement, typically with a close-knit population engaged in agriculture. More formal and academic than {村|むら}.

glosses: children's center; community center for children
children's center; children's hall; community center for children
explanations: A public facility for children (typically ages 0-18) providing a safe space for play, learning activities, and after-school care. Run by local governments across Japan.
A commercial entertainment facility with coin-operated video games, crane games, purikura (photo booths), and other amusement machines.

glosses: lack of preparation; inadequate preparation; being unprepared
explanations: The state of not having prepared sufficiently for something. Often used to explain or criticize a poor outcome.

glosses: work arrangement; employment format; work style
work arrangement; employment format; working pattern
explanations: The type or style of employment, including factors such as full-time vs. part-time, shift schedules, remote work, and contract type.

glosses: to install (software, an application, or a program)
explanations: To set up software on a computer, smartphone, or other device so that it is ready to use.
Lasting psychological damage caused by a deeply distressing or disturbing experience. The formal Japanese term for what is commonly called 'trauma' in everyday speech.

glosses: integrity; decisiveness; grace in accepting outcomes; dignified resolve
explanations: The quality of being clean-cut and decisive, especially in accepting defeat, taking responsibility, or making difficult decisions without clinging or complaining. A highly valued quality in Japanese culture.

glosses: Boys' Day doll; samurai warrior figure displayed for Children's Day
Boys' Day doll; warrior figure for Children's Day
explanations: Decorative dolls or figurines displayed in Japanese homes during the period around Children's Day (May 5th), typically depicting samurai warriors, historical heroes, or other martial figures. Displayed to wish boys healthy growth and strength.

glosses: person in charge; attendant; clerk; staff member
explanations: Refers to a person responsible for or assigned to a particular task or area, often seen in public facilities, transportation, and customer service contexts.

glosses: stopping off partway; getting off at an intermediate station (on a longer journey)
explanations: Commonly used in the context of train travel, where a passenger breaks the journey at an intermediate station before continuing to the final destination.

glosses: always having on hand; keeping in stock; standing (army, equipment)
explanations: Used for items or resources kept available at all times for regular or emergency use.

glosses: to become bright and lively; to become gorgeous; to become festive
explanations: An intransitive verb describing a scene, atmosphere, or appearance becoming vibrant and glamorous.

glosses: oral tradition; oral transmission; passing down knowledge by word of mouth
explanations: Refers to knowledge, techniques, or teachings transmitted verbally rather than in writing, often in traditional arts, crafts, or religious practices.

glosses: to dig up; to unearth; to excavate
to discover; to find (something valuable or rare); to uncover
explanations: Physically digging something out of the ground.
Figuratively finding something hidden or overlooked, such as a bargain, talent, or rare item.
Somewhat formal term for a friend from school or university days.

glosses: reading room (in a library or archive)
explanations: A designated room in libraries, archives, or institutions where visitors can read or consult materials.

glosses: way of grilling; cooking method (for roasting, baking, or frying)
explanations: Refers to the method or degree of cooking by heat, including grilling, roasting, baking, and pan-frying.
A market specializing in fish and seafood, ranging from wholesale markets to smaller retail fish markets.
A formal term for someone who writes professionally, encompassing novelists, essayists, and other literary figures.

glosses: warring states; period of civil war and rival feudal lords (especially the Sengoku period, c. 1467–1615)
explanations: Most commonly refers to the Sengoku period of Japanese history, an era of near-constant military conflict among feudal lords.

glosses: localized; local; limited to a specific area
explanations: Often used in weather reports, news, and technical contexts to describe something confined to a particular area.

glosses: utterance; speech; speaking (the act of producing speech)
explanations: Used in linguistics, education, and technical contexts to refer to the act or product of spoken language.
Most commonly refers to thick Japanese-style omelette (厚焼き卵), but can also describe thick-grilled versions of other foods.

glosses: likeness (of a face); portrait; facial resemblance
explanations: Most commonly encountered in the compound 似顔絵 (caricature/portrait sketch).

glosses: going to bed late; staying up late
explanations: Describes the habit or act of going to sleep at a late hour.

glosses: curriculum vitae; resume; career history document
explanations: A formal document detailing one's career and educational history, used in job applications.
The place or address where goods are to be delivered.
A designated spot for viewing scenery, typically at scenic locations, parks, or tourist attractions.

glosses: penetration rate; adoption rate; rate of spread
explanations: The percentage or proportion showing how widely something has spread or been adopted in a population.
Used to describe things that form a contrast or are being compared with each other.

glosses: memorial service; ceremony to console the spirits of the dead
explanations: A formal ceremony held to honor and comfort the spirits of deceased persons, often those who died in wars, disasters, or accidents.

glosses: Japanese food restaurant; Japanese cuisine restaurant
explanations: A restaurant specializing in Japanese cuisine.

glosses: branding iron; brand mark; burn mark (stamped with a heated iron)
explanations: A mark made by pressing a heated metal stamp onto a surface, or the tool used to make such marks.
Used to describe attractive, well-formed handwriting, and also as a category for handwriting improvement courses and books.

glosses: re-entry (into a country); returning to a country after leaving
explanations: Used in immigration and visa contexts, referring to the process of entering a country again after having left.

glosses: "herbivore" type; passive, gentle, unassertive type (especially regarding romantic relationships)
explanations: A slang term originating in the late 2000s to describe people (especially men) who are not aggressive in pursuing romantic relationships.

glosses: manual labor at a temple; cleaning and maintenance work (in Zen Buddhism)
explanations: Originally a Zen Buddhist term for daily physical work considered part of spiritual practice.

glosses: putting into writing; documenting; converting into written form
explanations: The act of expressing ideas, rules, or information in written form.
The country where one was born or where one's ancestors originated. Carries a strong emotional and patriotic tone, often used in contexts of longing, loyalty, or sacrifice.
A mistake or misunderstanding arising from incorrect perception or judgment. Often used in formal or written contexts, and most commonly encountered in the compound {試行錯誤|しこうさくご} (trial and error).
The formal act of giving property, money, or other assets to another person, especially in legal and financial contexts. Distinct from casual gift-giving.
A tree cultivated for its edible fruit. Used in agricultural and horticultural contexts.
An honorific title used to address or refer to high-ranking officials such as heads of state, ambassadors, and ministers. Used in diplomatic and extremely formal contexts.
A small pocket of air or gas trapped in a liquid, solid, or other material. Used in both everyday and scientific contexts.
The specific rules or provisions in a law, regulation, or contract that prescribe punishments for violations. Often used in legal, regulatory, and business contexts.
A physical position of readiness, especially in martial arts, sports, or combat. The way one positions the body in preparation for action.
A mental state of readiness or a particular attitude toward something. Used figuratively to describe being prepared or on guard.
The external appearance or imposing size of a building or establishment.
A pattern of irregular spots or patches of different colors. Describes something with an uneven mix of colors or shades.
Used figuratively to describe something that is inconsistent or uneven in quality, distribution, or degree.

glosses: lake surface; surface of a lake
explanations: The surface of a lake. Often used in descriptive or literary contexts when discussing the appearance, conditions, or reflections on a lake.

glosses: practice hall; training room; rehearsal space
explanations: A place where traditional arts, martial arts, dance, or theater are practiced and rehearsed. Strongly associated with traditional Japanese arts and sumo.

The principle or practice of rejecting the use of violence as a means of achieving social or political change. Associated with the philosophy and movements of figures like Gandhi and Martin Luther King Jr.

glosses: selection; choosing what to keep and what to discard
explanations: The act of deciding what to accept and what to reject. Literally 'taking and discarding.' Most commonly used in the compound {取捨選択|しゅしゃせんたく} (selection, sorting out).
The shape or form of a wave, whether physical (sound, light, water) or as displayed on instruments and screens. Used in scientific, technical, and audio contexts.
A painting technique using oil-based pigments, or a work of art created using this technique. Refers to both the method and the finished work.
Severe difficulty, distress, or suffering, especially over a prolonged period. A literary and formal word emphasizing endurance through difficult circumstances.
Having no poison or toxicity. Used to describe substances, animals, or plants that are not harmful or dangerous.

glosses: lack of a plan; absence of measures
lack of a plan; absence of policy; having no strategy
explanations: The state of having no plan, policy, or countermeasures. Often used critically to describe a government, organization, or person's failure to take action.
A male deer, especially one with antlers. The counterpart of {雌鹿|めじか} (female deer, doe).
A female deer. The counterpart of {雄鹿|おじか} (male deer, stag).
The older, more complex forms of kanji that were in standard use before the postwar script reform of 1946. These were replaced by simplified {新字体|しんじたい} (new-form kanji) for everyday use.
The simplified forms of kanji adopted as standard in Japan after the 1946 postwar script reform. These replaced the more complex {旧字体|きゅうじたい} (old-form kanji) for everyday use.
Doing or considering things separately, paying attention to each item rather than the whole.
The practice of buying goods cheaply and reselling them at a higher price, originally referring to used books but now covering any product.

glosses: person with a disability; disabled person
explanations: A person who has a physical, intellectual, or mental disability.
A round, flat Japanese cake made from batter cooked in a circular mold and filled with sweet bean paste or other fillings.

glosses: set phrase; fixed expression; stock phrase
explanations: A conventionalized phrase or expression that is used repeatedly in a particular context, often without variation.
A feeling of opposition or animosity toward someone, often manifesting as a desire to resist or confront them.
A person who has been physically injured, especially in an accident, disaster, or conflict.
Written or presented in a way that ordinary people can easily understand, as opposed to specialized or academic content.
Lacking refinement or depth; appealing to mass taste rather than intellectual or artistic merit.
A category of polite Japanese speech that makes words sound more refined or elegant, primarily through the prefix お or ご.

glosses: various conditions; multiple requirements; several terms
explanations: A collection of different conditions, requirements, or terms that must be considered together.

glosses: breakthrough power; ability to break through
breakthrough power; ability to break through obstacles
explanations: The force, ability, or drive needed to overcome barriers, whether physical, strategic, or figurative.

glosses: person of refined taste; sophisticate; connoisseur
explanations: A person who is worldly-wise and has cultivated aesthetic sense, especially regarding pleasure, entertainment, and the arts.
Carried out in a planned, coordinated manner with clear structure and roles.
Relating to or involving an organization as a whole rather than individuals.
Focused on real-world application and usefulness rather than theory or ideals.
Done regularly as a habit or established custom, rather than as a one-time action.
Not making the best use of time, resources, or effort; failing to achieve maximum output with minimum waste.
A design or mechanism that allows something to be moved, adjusted, or repositioned.
Related to or limited to a particular geographic area or region.
The person who first established or created something, such as a company, organization, school of thought, or movement.
Information or news passed from person to person through spoken conversation rather than written communication.
The practice of passing down knowledge, stories, or techniques verbally from one generation to the next.

glosses: most important; of the highest importance; top priority
explanations: The superlative form of {重要|じゅうよう}, indicating something that is of the greatest significance or urgency among all options.

glosses: facing each other; sitting opposite; face to face
explanations: A seating or spatial arrangement where two people or things are positioned directly across from each other.

glosses: to show off; to try to look cool
to show off; to try to look cool; to put on airs
explanations: To deliberately behave or dress in a way intended to impress others, often with the implication of being somewhat vain or pretentious.
A country with a large, influential economy that plays a significant role in global markets and trade.
People who have been killed or injured in an accident, disaster, attack, or conflict. Encompasses both fatalities and those who survived with injuries.
The powerful rush of air and pressure generated by an explosion, capable of causing destruction over a wide area.

glosses: thundercloud; cumulonimbus cloud that produces lightning
explanations: A large, dark cloud that generates thunder and lightning, typically accompanied by heavy rain. Technically a type of cumulonimbus cloud.

glosses: internal information; insider information; confidential information
explanations: Information that is known only within an organization and not intended for public disclosure. Often refers to proprietary business data or confidential details.
Time off from work during which the employee does not receive salary or wages. Taken for personal reasons, extended absences, or when paid leave has been exhausted.

glosses: emergency meeting; extraordinary meeting; ad hoc meeting
explanations: A meeting convened outside the regular schedule to address an urgent or unexpected matter that requires immediate discussion.

glosses: economic effect; economic impact; economic benefit
explanations: The measurable influence that an event, policy, or project has on the economy, typically expressed in monetary terms.
A massive, towering cloud formation that develops vertically and produces heavy rain, thunder, lightning, and sometimes hail or tornadoes. The formal meteorological term.

glosses: autumn rain front; fall stationary front
explanations: A weather front that brings prolonged rainy weather to Japan in September and October, similar to the rainy season front ({梅雨前線|ばいうぜんせん}) but occurring in autumn.
A fire-resistant door installed in buildings to prevent the spread of fire and smoke between sections. Required by building codes in many structures.

glosses: regular meeting; periodic meeting; standing meeting
explanations: A meeting held at fixed, recurring intervals such as weekly, monthly, or quarterly, as part of an organization's routine operations.

glosses: vegetable dish; vegetable cooking; vegetable cuisine
explanations: A dish or style of cooking that features vegetables as the main ingredient. Can refer to a single dish or to vegetable-based cooking in general.

glosses: to become hoarse; to lose one's voice
explanations: For the voice to become rough, raspy, or weak due to overuse, illness, or strain on the vocal cords.
The organizational structure and framework of formal education in a country, including the levels of schooling, years of study, and progression from elementary through higher education.
A device installed at intersections and pedestrian crossings that uses colored lights to control traffic flow.
More broadly, any mechanical or electronic device used to send signals, such as railway signals.

glosses: evening; early night; dusk to late evening
explanations: The period from early evening until around midnight, especially the hours after sunset when it is fully dark but still relatively early in the night.
An aquatic plant with large round leaves and distinctive pink or white flowers. Deeply significant in Buddhism and Japanese culture.
Activities, study, or events that take place outside of regular class hours or the standard curriculum.
The act of threatening someone with harm or negative consequences to force them to do something. Used in both everyday and legal contexts.

glosses: to threaten; to intimidate; to menace
to threaten; to intimidate; to menace; to coerce
explanations: To use threats of harm or negative consequences to frighten someone or force them into compliance.
A person who is excessively kind and trusting, often to the point of being naive or easily taken advantage of. Can be used affectionately or critically.

An error in procedure or handling, especially one that arises from miscommunication, carelessness, or a breakdown in coordination. Implies the mistake was unintentional and administrative rather than a moral failing.

glosses: to give up on; to abandon; to see through
to give up on; to abandon; to write off
to see through; to judge fully; to size up
explanations: To conclude that something or someone is hopeless and decide to stop investing effort, money, or attention.
To assess something or someone completely and reach a decisive conclusion about their true nature or value.
The criminal act of threatening someone in order to obtain money, property, or other advantages. A specific legal term in Japanese criminal law.

glosses: spring tide; exceptionally high and low tides
explanations: The tides that occur around new moon and full moon when the gravitational pull of the sun and moon align, producing the largest tidal range. The opposite of neap tide.

glosses: athlete's foot; tinea pedis; ringworm of the foot
explanations: A common fungal infection of the skin on the feet, causing itching, peeling, and sometimes blisters. Medically known as foot ringworm.
An official act by the government forgiving or reducing the punishment of convicted individuals. In Japan, granted by the Cabinet with the Emperor's attestation.

glosses: freeloader; sponger; dependent lodger; person living off someone else
explanations: A person who stays at someone else's home without paying rent or contributing to expenses. Carries a mildly negative nuance of imposing on another's hospitality.

glosses: pretending to be out; feigning absence
explanations: The act of being at home but pretending not to be, typically to avoid answering the door or dealing with a visitor.

glosses: all for nothing; a waste; come to nothing
all for nothing; a waste; come to nothing; futile
explanations: An idiomatic expression meaning that effort, time, or investment has been wasted and come to nothing, like bubbles on water that quickly disappear.

glosses: haphazard; unplanned; playing it by ear
haphazard; unplanned; playing it by ear; random; improvised
explanations: Acting without a plan or preparation, just dealing with things as they come. Can describe either a carefree attitude or reckless disorganization.

glosses: trivia; fun facts; useful tidbits of knowledge
explanations: Small pieces of interesting or useful knowledge that are not essential but good to know. Often presented as entertaining or surprising facts.

glosses: you reap what you sow; suffering from your own actions
you reap what you sow; suffering the consequences of your own actions; brought it on yourself
explanations: A proverb meaning that one's misfortune or suffering is the result of one's own past behavior or mistakes. Literally, rust that comes from the blade itself.

glosses: ulterior motive; hidden agenda; secret intention
explanations: A concealed intention or selfish motive behind seemingly innocent or kind behavior, especially romantic or sexual interest.

glosses: snatching away; stealing; intercepting; seizing what belongs to another
explanations: The act of taking something that rightfully belongs to someone else, especially by swooping in from the side. Implies unfairness and opportunism.

glosses: sneaking a taste; nibbling; pilfering food
explanations: Secretly eating small amounts of food, especially before a meal is ready or from food that isn't meant for you.
Figuratively, trying things only partially or selectively without committing to any one thing.

glosses: opening shot; trigger; spark that starts something
explanations: Originally, the small fire used to ignite a cannon or firearm. The literal ignition source.
Figuratively, the initial action or remark that triggers a larger event, discussion, or movement.

glosses: scheme; plot; ulterior motive; hidden agenda
explanations: A secret plan or calculated intention, usually with a selfish or dishonest purpose. Implies deliberate strategic thinking to achieve a hidden goal.
Deliberately extending the duration of something, often to avoid a decision or outcome. Usually carries a negative nuance of unnecessary delay.
Making something physically larger, especially enlarging a photograph or image.

glosses: off the mark; wrong guess; irrelevant
off the mark; wrong guess; irrelevant; wide of the mark
explanations: A guess, estimate, or response that completely misses the point or is far from the correct answer.

glosses: arrogance; conceit; overestimation of oneself; presumption
explanations: An inflated sense of one's own abilities or importance. Having an exaggerated opinion of oneself that goes beyond what is warranted.

glosses: accepting uncritically; swallowing whole; taking at face value
explanations: Accepting information, claims, or instructions without questioning, analyzing, or verifying them. Always used negatively, warning against a lack of critical thinking.

glosses: retaliation; payback; tit for tat; getting even
explanations: Striking back immediately after being wronged. Implies a swift, proportional response to an offense, like hitting back right away.
Originally, a samurai without a sword at the waist. Now used literally for being without weapons or figuratively for being unprepared or defenseless.
Figuratively, going into a situation without the tools, knowledge, or preparation needed. Entering a confrontation or negotiation at a disadvantage.

glosses: dependence on others' indulgence; spoiled behavior; presuming on goodwill
dependence on others' indulgence; presuming on goodwill
spoiled behavior; self-indulgence; lack of self-discipline
explanations: The expectation or desire that others will be tolerant, forgiving, or accommodating. A key cultural concept describing the psychology of relying on another's benevolence, famously analyzed in Doi Takeo's 'The Anatomy of Dependence.'
Acting in a way that takes advantage of lenient conditions or avoids facing difficulties. Often used critically to describe someone who is not taking responsibility.

glosses: to fall asleep; to go to sleep
explanations: A somewhat literary or gentle expression for falling asleep. More elegant than simply {寝|ね}る, often used in narrative, bedtime contexts, or when describing someone drifting off peacefully.
The systematic act of seeking out and collecting information on a topic. Used broadly in everyday, business, academic, and military/intelligence contexts.

glosses: physical stance of readiness; defensive posture
mental readiness; bracing oneself; being on guard
explanations: A body posture taken in preparation for a physical confrontation, attack, or sudden movement. Used in martial arts and sports.
A figurative stance of psychological preparedness or wariness, as when anticipating difficulty, criticism, or an uncomfortable situation.
A device that projects images or film onto a screen. Traditionally refers to a film projector, but also used for modern digital projectors.
A document listing one's employment history, job responsibilities, and professional experience. In Japanese job hunting, this is typically submitted alongside a {履歴書|りれきしょ} (personal history form).
A personality or character type that is intellectual, studious, and methodical. Describes someone who approaches things analytically and values knowledge, even if they are not an actual scholar.

A round cake made by filling batter in a circular mold and cooking it with a sweet filling, typically red bean paste. This is the Kansai and western Japan term for what is called {今川焼|いまがわや}き in the Kantō region.
The middle area or section of a physical space, region, object, or structure. Used for geographical locations, buildings, documents, and other things that have a discernible center.
Indicates that a registration process has been completed. Used for accounts, products, documents, and any official registration. Functions as a no-adjective to modify nouns.
Indicates that a task, process, or action has been fully completed. Commonly used in administrative, technical, and digital contexts as a status label.
The seventh planet from the Sun in the solar system. An ice giant with a distinctive blue-green color, known for its extreme axial tilt.
Indicates something continuing without end. Used for genuine permanence, emotional emphasis, or hyperbolic expressions of a very long duration.
Indicates something lasting indefinitely without change or reversal. More factual and formal than {永遠|えいえん}に, often used for official, legal, or scientific permanence.

glosses: like this; in this way; this is how
like this; in this way; by doing this
in this manner; when things are like this
explanations: Refers to a method or manner being demonstrated, described, or already known from context. Often accompanies physical demonstrations or step-by-step explanations.
Refers to a current situation or state of affairs, reflecting on how things have turned out or how one finds oneself in the present circumstances.
When followed by a negative verb, means 'not in any place' or 'not to any place.' This is the most common usage.
When followed by a positive verb, means 'in/to every place without exception.' Less common than the negative usage.

glosses: busy farming season; peak agricultural period
explanations: The time of year when farming work is most intensive, particularly during planting (spring) and harvesting (autumn). The opposite of {農閑期|のうかんき} (slack farming season).
The quality or state of being indifferent or uninterested. The noun form of the na-adjective {無関心|むかんしん}, used when referring to indifference as a thing or concept itself.
Describes something so extreme in its unpleasantness — pain, heat, noise, boredom, sadness — that one cannot endure it. The negative potential form of {耐|た}える (to endure).

glosses: treasure house; treasury; repository of valuables
treasure house; treasury; storehouse for valuables
explanations: A building or room where valuable objects, artifacts, or treasures are kept. Often found at temples, shrines, castles, and museums in Japan.
Used figuratively to describe a place, collection, or resource that is exceptionally rich in valuable content.

glosses: photo developing lab; film processing facility
explanations: A facility where photographic film is chemically processed to produce negatives and prints. While declining due to digital photography, some still exist for professional and film enthusiast use.
A body position where the upper body leans forward. Used in sports, ergonomics, physical therapy, and figuratively for an aggressive or eager attitude.
The period before a child enters compulsory education (elementary school in Japan, age 6). Used in education, childcare, and policy contexts.

glosses: rare; hard to find; not easily come by
explanations: Describes something that is uncommon, scarce, or difficult to encounter. The combination of なかなか (not easily) with ない (not exist/not have) creates an expression meaning something is genuinely rare or special.

A reputation formed through personal recommendations, online reviews, and informal evaluations passed between people. Extremely common in modern Japanese consumer culture, especially for restaurants, products, and services.

glosses: in a natural manner; without affectation
explanations: Describes something happening without deliberate action, force, or artificial intervention. The process or result occurs on its own.
Describes behaving, speaking, or appearing in a way that is relaxed and unforced, without seeming artificial or stiff.

glosses: for free; at no charge; free of cost
explanations: Indicates that something is provided or available without requiring payment. Very common in commercial, service, and everyday contexts.

glosses: fully; thoroughly; to a great extent
explanations: Indicates that something meets or exceeds the required level or amount. Used to confirm that a condition has been satisfactorily met.
Emphasizes completeness or thoroughness of an action. Conveys that something was done without cutting corners.
A liquid secreted by organs in the digestive system that breaks down food. Includes gastric juice, bile, pancreatic juice, and intestinal fluids.
Describes something that deviates from what is considered normal or standard. Can be neutral, negative (something is wrong), or positive (something is exceptionally good).
The act of welcoming and caring for guests, visitors, or customers. Encompasses service, food, atmosphere, and attentiveness.

glosses: sorry to keep you waiting; thanks for waiting
explanations: A set phrase used when arriving late or when someone has been waiting for you. Also used by service staff when bringing food or completing a task.
A situation where no progress can be made because opposing sides are evenly matched or unwilling to compromise. Used for negotiations, conflicts, competitions, and political situations.
Describes something or someone that is thickly coated with dust. Uses the まみれ pattern meaning 'covered with' or 'smeared with' something undesirable.

glosses: business trip destination; place one is posted to
business trip destination; place one is sent to for work
explanations: The location where someone goes for a business trip. Refers to the destination itself, not the journey.

glosses: tastes and preferences; hobbies and inclinations
tastes and preferences; personal inclinations and hobbies
explanations: A four-character compound referring to a person's overall tastes, preferences, and leisure interests taken together. Often used in contexts discussing personality, marketing, or compatibility.

glosses: the other shore; the far bank; the opposite side
the other shore; the far bank; the opposite side of a river or body of water
explanations: The bank or shore on the opposite side of a river, lake, or other body of water from where the speaker is. Can also be used figuratively for something that feels distant or unreachable.

glosses: business failure; corporate collapse; management breakdown
explanations: The failure or collapse of a business, typically due to financial difficulties. A formal term frequently used in news and business contexts.

glosses: to make comfortable; to ease; to relax
to make oneself comfortable; to relax; to be at ease
to ease; to relieve; to make easier
explanations: Used reflexively to mean making oneself comfortable or relaxing one's posture or attitude. Often said as an invitation to someone to relax.
To reduce difficulty, pain, or burden for someone or something.

glosses: to bring to the surface; to make public; to show openly
to make public; to reveal; to bring out into the open
to bring outside; to put out front
explanations: To reveal something that was hidden, private, or internal. Used for information, feelings, or matters that are brought to public attention.
To physically move something from inside to outside or to the front. Literal usage.

glosses: flashback; vivid involuntary recollection of a past experience
explanations: A sudden, vivid memory of a past event that feels as if it is happening again. Often associated with traumatic experiences, but also used more casually for any sudden, vivid memory.
A storytelling device in film, literature, or other media where the narrative shifts to depict events from an earlier time.

glosses: boarding entrance; boarding door; entrance for passengers
boarding entrance; boarding door; place where passengers get on
explanations: The designated entrance for boarding a bus, train, or other vehicle. Commonly seen on signs at stations and bus stops.

glosses: leader; guide; one who leads the way
explanations: A person who goes ahead and leads others, either literally (guiding a group) or figuratively (pioneering a field or movement).

glosses: tastelessness; lack of flavor; having no taste
explanations: The state of having no taste or flavor. Used literally for food and drink, and figuratively for things that lack interest or appeal.

glosses: recovery from illness; complete healing; recuperation
explanations: Full recovery from an illness or injury. A formal word often used in written communication such as get-well cards and formal wishes for recovery.

glosses: ventilation opening; air vent; vent hole
explanations: An opening in a wall, ceiling, or floor designed to allow air to circulate for ventilation. Found in buildings, vehicles, and underground spaces.
Flour ground from buckwheat seeds. The primary ingredient for making soba noodles and galettes. Important in Japanese cuisine and relevant for allergy awareness.

glosses: older sister (informal); big sis; young woman (familiar)
explanations: An informal, affectionate way to refer to or address one's older sister. Warmer and more casual than お{姉|ねえ}さん.
Used to address or refer to a young woman who is not one's sister, typically by children or in a friendly, informal manner.

glosses: independent travel; individual travel; traveling on one's own
independent travel; individual travel; non-group travel
explanations: Travel arranged and undertaken by an individual or small group independently, as opposed to organized group tours. The traveler plans their own itinerary, transportation, and accommodation.
The deposit of pigment in the skin, resulting in darker patches or spots. A common dermatological concern caused by sun exposure, inflammation, aging, or hormonal changes.

glosses: collection of famous sayings; book of quotations
collection of famous sayings; book of quotations; anthology of notable quotes
explanations: A compiled collection of memorable or wise sayings from famous people. Available as books, websites, or social media content.

glosses: to eliminate; to remove; to erase
to eliminate; to remove; to erase; to cancel
explanations: To completely remove or cancel something, especially in legal, administrative, or formal contexts. Often used for removing registrations, records, or rights.

glosses: to leave over; to leave (something) remaining; to have to spare
to leave (something) over; to leave remaining
explanations: To leave a portion of something unused, unfinished, or unconsumed. The transitive counterpart of {余|あま}る.
Used in fixed expressions like {〜|〜}を{余|あま}して to mean 'with (time/distance) to spare' before reaching a deadline or destination.
The player at bat in baseball or softball — the offensive player who tries to hit the ball thrown by the pitcher.

glosses: Boston bag; soft-sided travel duffel bag
explanations: A medium-sized, soft-sided travel bag with handles on top and often a shoulder strap, roughly cylindrical or rectangular in shape. The Japanese name comes from the bags used by Boston University students in the early 20th century.
A musician who plays the violin, either professionally or as a serious performer. From English "violinist".

glosses: coil (electrical or wire wound in loops)
explanations: A length of wire (usually copper) wound in loops, used in electrical circuits, motors, transformers, and electromagnets. Also refers to other coiled objects such as heating coils.
A shop offering haircuts, shaves, and related grooming services, traditionally aimed at male customers. Distinguished from {美容院|びよういん} (beauty salon), which traditionally serves women.
A man who tends cattle on horseback, especially in the American West. In Japanese it almost always evokes the image from American Westerns rather than referring to actual modern ranch workers.

glosses: playboy; man who dates many women casually
explanations: A man, typically wealthy or charming, who pursues many casual romantic relationships rather than committing to one partner. Often carries mildly negative or teasing nuance.

A man one is dating in a romantic relationship. Loanword from English. In modern Japanese, {彼氏|かれし} is more commonly used in everyday conversation; ボーイフレンド sometimes implies a less serious or more casual male friend.
The international youth organization for boys focused on outdoor activities, citizenship, and character development. Also refers to an individual member of the organization.

glosses: soccer ball; football (the ball used in association football)
explanations: The round ball used in soccer/football, traditionally with a black-and-white pentagon-and-hexagon pattern.
A small boat propelled by an engine, used for recreation, fishing, or short transport. In Japan also strongly associated with the public sport of {競艇|きょうてい} (motorboat racing).
A small boat made of rubber or rubberized fabric and inflated with air. Used for recreation, fishing, life rafts, and emergency rescue.
A narrow, lightweight boat propelled by a double-bladed paddle, with the paddler seated facing forward. Used for recreation on rivers, lakes, and the sea.

glosses: geographical; relating to geography or physical location
explanations: Pertaining to physical location, terrain, or geographic distribution. Used to describe factors, conditions, or characteristics that are determined by where something is located on the earth.

glosses: parking brake; hand brake (in a car)
explanations: The brake used to keep a parked car from rolling, operated by a hand lever or foot pedal independent of the regular foot brake. The Japanese term is wasei-eigo; in modern English, "hand brake" or "parking brake" is more common.

glosses: foot brake; service brake (on a car)
foot brake; the main brake pedal
explanations: The main brake pedal on a car, operated by the foot — used during normal driving to slow down or stop the vehicle. Distinguished from サイドブレーキ (parking brake) and エンジンブレーキ (engine braking).

glosses: engine braking (slowing a vehicle using the engine)
explanations: The technique of slowing a vehicle by releasing the accelerator and/or downshifting, so that the engine's resistance helps decelerate the car without using the foot brake. The Japanese term is wasei-eigo.

glosses: door chime; doorbell that plays a chime tone
explanations: A doorbell device that produces a melodic chime when pressed, typical of Japanese homes and apartments. The term is also used for the chime sound that plays when train or shop doors open.

glosses: time signal; hourly chime; time announcement
explanations: A signal — typically a series of beeps, a chime, or a recorded voice — that announces the exact time, especially on the hour. Used by radio and TV broadcasts, telephone services, and clock towers.
A soft, mild, spreadable fresh cheese made from cream and milk. Used in Japan most often for cheesecake, bagels, and as a spread on bread or crackers.

glosses: natural cheese (cheese that is not processed cheese)
explanations: Cheese made directly from milk by curdling, draining, and ripening, without further melting and reblending. Distinguished in Japanese supermarket labeling from プロセスチーズ (processed cheese).
A hamburger with a slice of melted cheese, typically served in fast-food restaurants. A standard menu item at McDonald's, Mos Burger, and similar chains in Japan.

The formal ceremony held at the start of an event such as a sports tournament, school athletic festival, conference, or international competition. Typically includes speeches, parading of participants, and an official declaration that the event has begun.
The conventional heart symbol — used in decoration, emoji, design, and as a card suit.
One of the four suits in a standard deck of playing cards, marked with a red heart.
Used loosely in Japanese for emotional feelings, warmth, or mental strength. Distinct from {心臓|しんぞう} (the physical heart organ) and from {心|こころ} (more native term for mind/heart).

glosses: spades (suit in a deck of playing cards) ♠
explanations: One of the four suits in a standard deck of playing cards, marked with a black spade symbol.

glosses: down coat (long winter coat insulated with down)
explanations: A long winter coat insulated with down feathers, typically reaching to the hip or knee. Distinguished from a shorter ダウンジャケット (down jacket).

glosses: down jacket (puffy winter jacket insulated with down)
explanations: A short winter jacket insulated with down feathers, typically reaching the waist or hip. Distinguished from the longer ダウンコート.

glosses: tart (open pastry with sweet or savory filling)
explanations: A baked dish consisting of a shortcrust or pâte sablée base filled with cream, custard, fruit, jam, or savory ingredients. From French "tarte"; in Japan, the dessert version (especially fruit tarts) is most familiar.

glosses: dress code (rules about what clothing is appropriate)
explanations: The expected or required style of dress for a particular setting, such as a fine restaurant, formal event, club, or workplace.

glosses: dressing up; getting dressed up (in formal/special clothing)
dressing up; putting on more formal or fancy clothes
explanations: Wearing more formal, glamorous, or special-occasion clothing than usual. Can be used as a noun or with する as a verb.

glosses: old coin; antique coin (especially as a collectible)
explanations: Coins that are no longer in circulation, or coins from a previous era valued by collectors. Includes pre-modern Japanese coins, foreign coins, and older Japanese yen denominations no longer issued.

glosses: blizzard; severe snowstorm with strong winds
explanations: A meteorological term for a severe winter storm combining heavy snow with strong, often dangerous winds. The formal term used in weather warnings and news in Japan.

glosses: the normal / regular state (noun, often as 通常の or 通常通り)
explanations: Used to describe what typically happens or what is the standard situation. Slightly more formal than {普通|ふつう} or いつも.
Used as a noun-modifier or adverbial phrase meaning "normal" or "as usual," especially in business and announcements: {通常|つうじょう}{通|どお}り (as usual), {通常|つうじょう}{営業|えいぎょう} (regular business hours).

glosses: everyday use; (of an item) suitable for daily use rather than special occasions
explanations: Refers to items — clothing, dishes, accessories, bags, etc. — that are intended or appropriate for ordinary daily use, as opposed to being kept for special occasions. Often paired with の as a noun modifier: {普段使|ふだんづか}いの〜.
Engineering and policy efforts to control rivers and floodwaters — including dams, levees, channel improvements, and watershed management — so that flooding is reduced and water resources are usable.

glosses: to dent; to make concave; to bring (someone) down emotionally
to dent; to make a dent in (something); to push in
to make (someone) feel down; to dishearten; to take down a peg
explanations: To physically deform something by pushing or striking it inward, creating a concave area. The transitive counterpart of {凹|へこ}む.
To cause someone to feel discouraged, embarrassed, or psychologically deflated — often by criticism, defeat, or a sharp comeback. The transitive counterpart of {凹|へこ}む in its emotional sense.

glosses: to make resound; to cause to echo; to spread (one's name/fame)
to make (a sound) resound; to cause to echo
to spread (one's name, fame, voice) far and wide
explanations: To deliberately produce a sound loud enough to fill or echo through a space. The causative/transitive counterpart of {響|ひび}く (to resound).
Used figuratively in expressions about reputation, fame, or one's name spreading widely — e.g., {名|な}を{響|ひび}かせる (to make a name for oneself).

glosses: knob (a round handle on a door, drawer, or appliance)
explanations: A round handle that one turns or pulls — most commonly a door knob, but also drawer knobs and tuning knobs on devices.

glosses: blush; rouge (cosmetic applied to the cheeks to add color)
explanations: A cosmetic in powder, cream, or liquid form applied to the cheeks to give them a healthy, rosy color. The native Japanese term, slightly more old-fashioned than the loanword チーク.

glosses: one's own home (especially a privately owned house)
one's own home; a house one has bought (as opposed to renting)
explanations: A house or condominium that one personally owns — typically used in the context of the dream of buying one's first home. Wasei-eigo: in English, "my home" simply means "my house," but in Japanese, マイホーム specifically connotes home ownership.

glosses: homestay; staying with a host family while studying abroad or traveling
explanations: An arrangement in which a student or traveler — often abroad — stays in a private home with a host family rather than in a hotel or dormitory. Especially common for short-term language study programs.

glosses: pendant (a hanging ornament worn on a necklace chain)
explanations: An ornamental piece — often a stone, locket, or charm — that hangs from a necklace chain or cord. Also used for similar hanging ornaments such as pendant lights.
The stone monument placed at a grave, usually inscribed with the family name or a Buddhist posthumous name. The standard formal term in Japan.
A pattern, image, or design carved or engraved into a surface — wood, stone, metal, etc. Refers both to the act of carving and to the resulting artwork.

An older / native term for a tattoo, traditionally associated with elaborate Japanese-style designs (irezumi). The term has cultural baggage in Japan due to historical associations with criminals and yakuza, though it is also used neutrally to refer to traditional tattoo art.

glosses: dugout (the bench area for a baseball team)
explanations: The roofed enclosure beside a baseball field where players, coaches, and equipment wait when the team is not on the field. Also used loosely for the bench area of a softball or other field-sport game.

Colloquial term meaning that someone has been divorced two times. Formed from バツ (the X mark for "wrong") and {二|に} ("two"). The metaphor comes from the X marks once placed on a person's family register entry when they were removed after a divorce. Part of the series バツイチ (divorced once), バツニ (twice), バツサン (three times).

glosses: bench press (a weight-training exercise performed lying on a bench)
explanations: A common upper-body strength exercise in which the lifter lies on their back on a bench and pushes a weighted barbell or dumbbells upward, primarily working the chest, shoulders, and triceps. Used both as the name of the exercise and, by extension, as a する verb meaning "to do bench presses."

glosses: cowboy hat (the wide-brimmed felt or straw hat traditionally worn by American cowboys)
explanations: A wide-brimmed hat with a tall crown, typically made of felt, leather, or straw, originally worn by cowboys in the western United States. In Japan the word denotes both the actual western hat and any costume hat in that style — for example at theme parks, Halloween, or country-music events.

glosses: (baseball) walk; base on balls; four balls
explanations: In baseball, the situation in which the batter is awarded first base after the pitcher throws four pitches outside the strike zone (balls). The Japanese term is a wasei-eigo coinage from English "four" + "ball" — in real English baseball usage this is called a "walk" or "base on balls."

In baseball, the count when the batter has taken three pitches called as balls. From this count, one more ball results in a walk (フォアボール), so a スリーボール count puts the pitcher under pressure. Often used as part of the full count phrase スリーボール・ツーストライク (a 3-2 "full" count).

In baseball, the count when the batter has accumulated two strikes. From a ツーストライク count, one more strike results in a strikeout ({三振|さんしん}), so the batter is under pressure to protect the plate by fouling off or making contact with anything close to a strike.

glosses: rowing by hand; oar-powered; manually rowed/paddled
rowing by hand; powered by hand-operated oars (as opposed to a motor)
explanations: Used as a noun and as a noun-modifier (with の) to describe boats, vehicles, or simple machines that are propelled by human muscle power — typically by oars or paddles — rather than by an engine or motor. Most often heard in {手漕|てこ}ぎボート ("rowboat").

glosses: the "hand" radical (扌); left-side hand radical in kanji
the kanji radical {扌|てへん} ("hand"), as it appears on the left side of a character
explanations: The {扌|てへん} radical is a stylized form of {手|て} ("hand") used as the left-side ({偏|へん}) component of many kanji. Most kanji that contain てへん relate in some way to actions of the hand — pushing, pulling, holding, hitting, etc. Examples include {打|う}つ ("to hit"), {持|も}つ ("to hold"), {押|お}す ("to push"), and {投|な}げる ("to throw").

glosses: the "grass crown" radical (艹); top kanji radical for plants
the kanji radical {艹|くさかんむり} ("grass crown"), placed above the rest of a character
explanations: The {艹|くさかんむり} radical is a stylized form of {草|くさ} ("grass"), placed across the top ({冠|かんむり}) of many kanji. It indicates a connection with grasses, plants, or vegetation. Examples include {花|はな} ("flower"), {草|くさ} ("grass"), {茶|ちゃ} ("tea"), and {葉|は} ("leaf").

glosses: Parmesan cheese (a hard, aged Italian-style cheese)
explanations: A hard, granular cheese with a sharp, savory flavor, originally from Italy (Parmigiano-Reggiano). In Japan, パルメザンチーズ usually refers to the powdered version sold in green-topped shaker bottles for use on pasta, salads, and gratins, but it also covers genuine block Parmesan cheese.

glosses: cheese fondue (a Swiss dish of melted cheese eaten communally with bread, vegetables, etc.)
explanations: A communal Swiss/French dish in which cheese is melted in a small pot (typically with white wine and seasonings) and kept warm at the table. Diners use long forks to dip pieces of bread, boiled potatoes, vegetables, or sausage into the molten cheese. In Japan, チーズフォンデュ is a popular dinner-party and restaurant dish, especially in winter.

glosses: but; however; though (a slightly more emphatic variant of だけど)
explanations: A casual conjunction used to introduce a statement that contrasts with or qualifies what was just said. Functionally close to だけど, but with the extra も giving a slight feeling of "and yet…" or "…even so." Common in conversational and online writing; rare in formal documents.

glosses: but; although; however (slightly more formal than だけど)
explanations: A conjunction used to introduce a statement that contrasts with or qualifies what was just said. Sits between casual だけど and formal だけれども on the formality scale. Common in everyday writing such as essays, blog posts, and messages where the writer wants a slightly more careful tone than だけど without going as far as the literary しかし or だけれども.

glosses: dessert menu (the menu listing desserts at a restaurant or café)
explanations: The separate menu (or section of the menu) that lists the desserts and sweets offered at a restaurant, café, or hotel. Customers typically request it after finishing the main course.

glosses: wedding dress (the white bridal gown worn for a Western-style wedding)
explanations: The white, often long and elaborate, bridal gown worn by the bride at a Western-style wedding ceremony. Distinct from {白無垢|しろむく} or {色打|いろう}ち{掛|か}け, which are traditional Japanese bridal kimono. Brides at Japanese weddings often change between a ウェディングドレス and a Japanese bridal kimono during the reception.

glosses: yen coin (used after a denomination, e.g. 100{円玉|えんだま} "100-yen coin")
yen coin; coin of a given yen denomination
explanations: A noun used to refer to a yen coin of a specified value. Almost always preceded by a numeric denomination — the standard ones are {一円玉|いちえんだま} (¥1), {五円玉|ごえんだま} (¥5), {十円玉|じゅうえんだま} (¥10), {五十円玉|ごじゅうえんだま} (¥50), {百円玉|ひゃくえんだま} (¥100), and {五百円玉|ごひゃくえんだま} (¥500). On its own, {円玉|えんだま} just means "yen coin" generically, in contrast to {お札|おさつ} ("bills").

glosses: encoding (the process of converting information into a particular code or representation)
explanations: A technical term used in mathematics, information theory, telecommunications, and computer science. {符号化|ふごうか} refers to converting data — text, audio, video, or signals — into a coded representation suitable for transmission, storage, or processing. Common examples include character encoding (e.g., UTF-8), audio/video codecs (MP3, H.264), and error-correcting codes.

glosses: punctuation marks (collectively); the formal term for punctuation symbols
explanations: A formal collective term for the punctuation marks used in written Japanese — the period (。), comma (、), question mark (？), exclamation mark (！), brackets (「」『』), middle dot (・), and so on. {句読符号|くとうふごう} appears in style guides, school grammar instruction, and editorial discussion; in everyday speech, the more common term is {句読点|くとうてん}, although strictly that refers only to ， / 。 and , / 、.

glosses: two steps; (shogi) the illegal move of placing two pawns on the same file
two steps; two paces (a literal pair of footsteps)
(shogi) nifu — the illegal move of placing two unpromoted pawns on the same file
explanations: Two steps measured by walking. {歩|ほ} is the counter for steps in walking, so {二歩|にほ} = "two steps." Used both literally (two paces forward, back, or sideways) and metaphorically as a small distance or unit of progress.

In shogi (Japanese chess), {二歩|にほ} is the foul of dropping a pawn ({歩|ふ}) onto a file (column) that already contains one of your unpromoted pawns. It is an immediate-loss rule violation, and is one of the most common and most embarrassing illegal moves a player can make.

The interrogative form of the {歩|ほ} ("step") counter, used to ask how many steps. Combines {何|なん}- ("how many," the question marker for counters) with the counter {歩|ほ}, with the doubled-consonant reading change ぽ. Used both literally for footsteps and figuratively for amounts of progress.

The opening at the top of a volcano (or on its flanks) from which lava, ash, and gases are ejected during an eruption. {噴火口|ふんかこう} refers specifically to the active vent, while the broader bowl-shaped depression that may form around it is more often called {火口|かこう}.

A large-scale volcanic eruption, typically one significant enough to be reported in the news or remembered historically. Formed by prefixing {大|だい}- ("big, major") to {噴火|ふんか} ("eruption"). Frequently used both for currently occurring large eruptions and for historical references such as {富士山|ふじさん}の{大噴火|だいふんか}.

glosses: to be struck by; to be afflicted with (disaster, misfortune, illness)
to be struck by; to be afflicted with (a disaster, misfortune, illness, or unwelcome event)
explanations: The passive form of {見舞|みま}う ("to inquire after, to visit a sick person; to befall"). In its most common modern use, {見舞|みま}われる means to suffer or be hit by something unpleasant — typhoons, earthquakes, accidents, illness, financial troubles. Almost always used with {に} marking the misfortune.

glosses: outside the group; outside one's department; nonmember
outside the group; outside one's department or organization
explanations: A formal noun used in administrative and corporate contexts to refer to people, things, or matters that are outside a particular department, division, or organization. The most common collocation is {部外者|ぶがいしゃ} ("outsider, nonmember"). Combines {部|ぶ} ("section, department, group") with {外|がい} ("outside").

glosses: training; instruction (especially for skills like driving)
explanations: Formal instruction or training, most strongly associated in modern Japanese with driving schools ({自動車|じどうしゃ}{教習所|きょうしゅうじょ}). Combines {教|きょう} ("teach") with {習|しゅう} ("learn, practice"). Although it can in principle apply to any structured training, in everyday speech it almost always evokes driving instruction unless context specifies otherwise.

An ancient genre of Japanese court music and dance, performed at the Imperial Court and certain shrines and temples for over a millennium. {雅楽|ががく} encompasses both purely instrumental music and accompanied dances ({舞楽|ぶがく}), and includes pieces of both Japanese origin and pieces transmitted from Tang-dynasty China and ancient Korea. It is one of the oldest continuously performed musical traditions in the world.

The middle portion of a calendar month, roughly the 10th to 20th. Combines {月|つき} ("month") with {半|なか}ば ("middle, halfway point"). Used both as a time expression in itself and to anchor schedules: "by mid-month," "around the middle of the month," etc.

glosses: decimal; decimal number (a number with a fractional part written after the decimal point)
explanations: A mathematical term for a number expressed in decimal form — that is, with a decimal point and a fractional part, such as 0.5, 3.14, or 12.034. Combines {小|しょう} ("small") with {数|すう} ("number"). Beware the homophone {少数|しょうすう} ("small number, minority"), which is unrelated.

glosses: bank seal (a personal seal registered with one's bank)
bank seal — a personal hanko registered with a bank for authorizing transactions
explanations: In Japan, a personal seal ({印鑑|いんかん}/{はんこ}) that has been formally registered with a bank as the seal authorized to approve transactions on a particular account. Withdrawals over the counter, account changes, and other major bank business have traditionally required impressing the registered {銀行印|ぎんこういん}. Distinct from the everyday {認印|みとめいん} used for casual signing and from {実印|じついん}, the seal registered with city hall for legal purposes.

glosses: rotation on its own axis (esp. of a celestial body)
explanations: In astronomy, the rotation of a body — most often a planet, moon, or star — about its own axis. Distinct from {公転|こうてん}, which refers to revolution around another body. Earth's daily rotation is the canonical example: the Earth's {自転|じてん} produces day and night.

glosses: revolution; orbital motion of one body around another
explanations: In astronomy, the orbital motion of one body around another — typically a planet around its star or a moon around its planet. Distinct from {自転|じてん} ("rotation on the body's own axis"). Earth's annual {公転|こうてん} around the Sun produces the seasons.

glosses: air current; airflow (esp. in the atmosphere)
explanations: A flow of air on a meteorological scale — a current or stream of air in the atmosphere. Used in weather reports, aviation, and discussions of climate. The most familiar example for travelers is {乱気流|らんきりゅう} ("turbulence"), the patches of disturbed airflow that buffet aircraft.

glosses: the number of patients (with a particular illness, at a hospital, in a region, etc.)
explanations: A statistical noun for a count of patients. Combines {患者|かんじゃ} ("patient") with the productive suffix ~{数|すう} ("number of, count of"). Heard most often in news reports and medical statistics — for example, the number of patients with a contagious disease, the number of patients at a hospital, or the number of patients in a particular age bracket.

glosses: air conditioning; climate control (HVAC, in buildings)
explanations: The general term for the equipment and systems that regulate the temperature, humidity, and circulation of air inside a building. Short for {空気調和|くうきちょうわ} ("air conditioning," literally "air harmonization"). {空調|くうちょう} typically refers to the whole system at a building or facility level — covering both heating and cooling — whereas the everyday loanword エアコン usually refers to a single residential unit.

The (typically passive) flow of air through a space, garment, or piece of equipment. {通気|つうき} emphasizes that air can pass through — for example, a room where air moves freely, fabric that breathes, or vents in a building's structure. Less active than {換気|かんき}, which refers to deliberately exchanging stale air for fresh air.

glosses: commentary (audio/video commentary track; running explanation of an event)
explanations: A running spoken explanation accompanying an event, broadcast, film, or game. コメンタリー most often refers to sports/event play-by-play, audio commentary tracks on DVDs and streaming releases, or behind-the-scenes commentary by directors and creators. As a loanword it has a slightly modern, media-industry feel and is more common than {解説|かいせつ} in entertainment contexts.

glosses: spin (rotation of a ball, skater, etc.); spin-off
spin; rotation (of a ball, skater, vehicle, etc.)
spin-off (work derived from a main story or series)
explanations: Rotation imparted to a ball in sports, the rotational figure performed by a figure skater or dancer, or the uncontrolled rotation of a vehicle. Often used with {する} as a verb.
A derivative work — a manga, novel, drama, or film that focuses on side characters or settings from a main franchise. Often appears in compounds like スピンオフ.

glosses: modern; stylish; contemporary (in design and aesthetic sense)
explanations: Of a stylish, contemporary aesthetic — clean lines, fashionable, up-to-date in look and feel. モダン applies most often to design, architecture, fashion, interiors, and art. Unlike English "modern," which can mean "of the present era" in general, モダン in Japanese is almost always evaluative — implying a sleek, refined, or cosmopolitan style rather than simply "of the current time." For the temporal sense, Japanese uses {現代的|げんだいてき} or {現代|げんだい}.

glosses: custom; customization; customized version (of a product, vehicle, software setting, etc.)
explanations: Modification or configuration of a product to suit individual taste or needs. Used heavily in tech (custom UI/settings), automotive (custom cars and bikes), gaming (custom controllers, builds), and merchandise. Often used with {する} as a verb meaning "to customize."

glosses: angle (camera angle, viewpoint, perspective in photography/film)
angle (in photography, film, broadcasting); viewpoint; perspective
explanations: The angle from which a camera frames its subject, or by extension the perspective from which a topic is approached. Used heavily in photography, film, TV broadcasting, and journalism. For ordinary geometric angles, Japanese uses {角度|かくど}, not アングル.

glosses: monitoring; ongoing observation/measurement of a system or condition
explanations: Ongoing observation, measurement, or tracking of a process, system, environment, or person's condition. Used in business, IT, healthcare, environmental science, and consumer-product testing. Often combined with {する} as a verb (モニタリングする = to monitor).

glosses: sweets; desserts (a stylish, modern-feeling word for confections, especially Western-style)
sweets; desserts; pastries (Western-style or modern Japanese-style confections)
explanations: Sweet foods, especially Western-style desserts such as cakes, tarts, parfaits, and pastries, but also stylishly presented Japanese sweets. The word entered everyday Japanese in the 2000s and now strongly implies fashionable, café-style confections suitable for posting to social media. It is more upscale and trendy in feel than {お菓子|おかし}, which can mean any kind of snack or sweet.

glosses: owned home; a house one owns (as opposed to a rental)
explanations: A house owned by the resident, as contrasted with a rental property ({賃貸|ちんたい}). The word appears regularly in housing surveys, real-estate advertisements, life-planning articles, and discussions of household finances. It implies a single-family home or detached house but is often extended to include owned condominiums.

glosses: pop (music genre); pop-style (cheerful, contemporary aesthetic); point-of-purchase display card
pop-style; cheerful, bright, modern in feel (used adjectivally)
POP (point-of-purchase display card or shelf-talker in retail)
explanations: Pop music as a genre, especially mainstream contemporary pop. Often appears as Jポップ (J-pop, Japanese pop music) or in the compound ポップミュージック.
An aesthetic descriptor for designs, illustrations, fashion, or interiors with bright colors, cute shapes, and a contemporary mood. Used as a な-adjective: ポップな + noun.

A small advertising card or sign placed near a product on a store shelf to attract attention or describe the item. Borrowed from English "POP" (point of purchase). Common in Japanese retail and bookshop contexts; written in katakana but often in all-caps as POP.

glosses: song (typically a classical art song or formally composed song with lyrics)
song (especially an art song, classical song, or formally composed vocal piece)
explanations: A composed song, often in a classical or formal context. {歌曲|かきょく} is the standard Japanese term for art songs (e.g., German Lied, French mélodie, English art song) and is also used in formal music criticism for any song that is the work of an identifiable composer. In ordinary conversation about pop or folk music, the everyday word {曲|きょく} or {歌|うた} is far more common; {歌曲|かきょく} carries a literary, classical-music feel.

glosses: end-of-life preparations; activities to prepare for one's own death
end-of-life preparations; preparing for one's own death
explanations: The deliberate practical, emotional, and legal preparations a person makes for their own death. Typical {終活|しゅうかつ} activities include writing a will, drafting an {エンディングノート} ("ending note"), pre-planning one's funeral and grave, decluttering possessions, organizing finances, and discussing wishes with family. The word emerged in Japan in the late 2000s and is now firmly established in everyday use. Often used with {する} as a verb (= to do end-of-life preparations).

glosses: atmospheric pressure; air pressure (in meteorology and physics)
explanations: The pressure exerted by the weight of the Earth's atmosphere on a surface. {大気圧|たいきあつ} is the standard term in meteorology, physics, and engineering. The everyday weather word {気圧|きあつ} is essentially the same thing in popular usage; {大気圧|たいきあつ} is more precise/scientific.

glosses: barometer; instrument for measuring atmospheric pressure
explanations: An instrument that measures atmospheric pressure, used in meteorology, aviation, mountaineering, and home weather stations. {気圧計|きあつけい} is the standard term, covering everything from old-fashioned mercury and aneroid barometers to digital sensors built into watches and smartphones.

glosses: weather-related illness; physical symptoms triggered by changes in weather (especially atmospheric pressure)
weather-related illness; symptoms (headaches, dizziness, fatigue, joint pain, etc.) caused or aggravated by weather changes
explanations: A general term for physical complaints — most commonly headaches, dizziness, neck and shoulder stiffness, joint pain, fatigue, and mood changes — that flare up in response to changes in weather, particularly drops in atmospheric pressure during the rainy season or when typhoons approach. {気象病|きしょうびょう} is widely discussed in Japanese health media but is not strictly a medical diagnosis; it is recognized as a real phenomenon under terms such as "{天気痛|てんきつう}."

glosses: to return (to a starting point, principle, or original state); to go back (to one's roots, the basics)
to return to (a starting point, original principle, basic stance, or earlier state)
explanations: To go back to a starting point — typically a fundamental principle, the original purpose of a project, the basics of a discipline, or an earlier mental or emotional state. {立|た}ち{返|かえ}る is more abstract than plain {帰|かえ}る ("to go home, to return") and almost always concerns ideas, intentions, attitudes, or methods rather than physical movement. The {立|た}ち- prefix adds a sense of "making oneself return," giving the verb a deliberate, reflective tone.

glosses: goldfish bowl; (figuratively) a setting where one is constantly observed
goldfish bowl; small round glass tank for keeping a goldfish
goldfish-bowl situation; a setting in which one is on constant display (figurative)
explanations: A small, typically round or globular glass container for keeping a goldfish or two. The classic image is a clear glass sphere holding water, a goldfish, and perhaps a sprig of water plant — strongly associated with summer in Japan, when goldfish-scooping ({金魚|きんぎょ}すくい) at festivals brings home small fish that need a temporary container.

A figurative use, in expressions like {金魚鉢|きんぎょばち}の{中|なか} ("inside a goldfish bowl"), describing a situation where one is fully visible and observed by everyone — for example, in a small workplace, public-figure life, or surveillance-heavy environment.

glosses: water temperature (of a body of water, an aquarium, a hot bath, an engine cooling system, etc.)
explanations: The temperature of water in any context — the sea, rivers, swimming pools, fish tanks, hot baths, kettles, or the cooling systems of cars and machinery. {水温|すいおん} is a neutral, technical-flavored term used wherever water temperature needs to be specified.

glosses: graduated, progressive (esp. of taxation, fees, or rates that increase by tier)
progressive / graduated (increase in steps, typically of taxation or fees)
explanations: A system in which a rate, charge, or punishment increases in stages or tiers as some underlying quantity (income, usage, severity) rises. Most commonly seen in compounds: {累進|るいしん}{課税|かぜい} (progressive taxation), {累進|るいしん}{税率|ぜいりつ} (progressive tax rate), {累進|るいしん}{制|せい} (graduated/progressive system). Bare {累進|るいしん} on its own is rare in conversation; it almost always appears in such compounds in tax, finance, legal, and policy writing.

glosses: a fixed amount; a set amount of money
a fixed amount of money; a set sum
explanations: A predetermined, set sum of money — for example, a fixed monthly allowance, a flat fee, a fixed deductible, or a threshold below which special rules apply. {一定額|いっていがく} appears constantly in financial, legal, tax, and contractual writing where a numeric amount is held constant or compared against a threshold.

glosses: desired amount; requested amount of money
explanations: The amount of money one wishes to receive, borrow, charge, or be paid. {希望額|きぼうがく} is a standard term in salary negotiations, loan applications, fundraising, donation requests, sales price negotiations, and similar contexts where one party states their preferred figure.

glosses: preferred date; date one wishes (for delivery, an appointment, a reservation, etc.)
explanations: The date that a customer or applicant wishes to be selected — for a delivery, hospital visit, hotel reservation, interview, viewing, or service appointment. Standard label on Japanese order forms, booking sites, and request emails.

headword: シンガーソングライター
glosses: singer-songwriter (a musician who writes and performs their own songs)
singer-songwriter; a musician who writes and performs their own songs
explanations: A musician who both composes and performs their own songs — typically writing their own lyrics and music and singing them themselves. The term entered Japanese music journalism in the 1970s with the rise of folk and adult-contemporary singer-songwriters and is now standard vocabulary for anyone whose performances feature their own original material.

glosses: unlucky; out of luck; having bad luck
explanations: Colloquial expression for being unlucky, especially on a particular day or in a particular situation. The negative form of ついている ("to be lucky"), originally from {運|うん}がつく ("luck attaches to one").

glosses: packing tape; duct tape; cloth tape
explanations: Wide, strong adhesive tape used for sealing cardboard boxes, bundling items, and general repairs. A wasei-eigo coinage from "gum" + "tape"; refers mainly to paper-backed kraft tape and cloth-backed duct tape, not the narrow transparent {セロハンテープ|せろはんてーぷ}.

A clear sugar syrup served alongside iced coffee or tea to sweeten cold drinks (sugar does not dissolve well in cold liquid). Usually provided in single-serve plastic packets at cafes and restaurants. Often shortened to ガムシロ.
A large indoor commercial complex housing many retail stores, restaurants, and entertainment facilities under one roof. Often shortened to モール in casual speech.
