glosses: boning (fish or meat); watering down; gutting
watering down; gutting (a plan or proposal)
explanations: Taking the bones out of a fish or piece of meat in preparation for cooking or eating.
Removing the essential or strongest content from a plan, bill, or proposal so that little of substance remains.
A professional player of shogi or go who competes in title matches for a living.
A style of painting that uses only black ink, expressing form and depth through gradations of shading rather than color.

glosses: to be rested; to feel at ease
explanations: Of the body, mind, or feelings, to be relieved of strain and grow calm and rested.

glosses: to say everything; to express fully; to exhaust words
explanations: To express something completely, leaving nothing unsaid. Most often used in the negative potential form, describing feelings too great to put fully into words.

glosses: to use up completely; to exhaust; to consume entirely
explanations: To use something until none of it is left. Applies to physical resources, money, energy, or time.

glosses: to recommend; to endorse; to put forward
explanations: To suggest a particular person, book, product, or option to someone as being good or suitable. Written 薦める when vouching for a specific thing or candidate.

glosses: to decoct; to boil down; to brew (herbs, tea)
explanations: To extract the essence of herbs, medicinal plants, or tea leaves by simmering them in water. Associated with traditional herbal medicine and tea preparation.
Television and radio operated by private companies and funded by advertising, as distinguished from public broadcasting. An abbreviation of {民間|みんかん}{放送|ほうそう}.
The meal eaten in the evening. A common, slightly casual everyday word for dinner.
The pair of small strokes written at the upper right of a kana to mark a voiced consonant, as in が, ざ, だ, and ば.
Poetry and verse considered together as a literary form, covering both Chinese-style poems and Japanese forms such as waka and haiku.
A hidden place where criminals, wrongdoers, or undesirable things gather and base themselves. Almost always used with a negative tone.
The cylinder of muscle a bivalve uses to open and close its shell. As food, it most often refers to the prized adductor muscle of the scallop.
The central administrative office of a prefecture, and by extension the prefectural government as an organization.

glosses: within the prefecture; inside the prefecture
explanations: The area inside the boundaries of a particular prefecture. Often used with の to modify another noun.
A banknote that is brand new and unwrinkled. Crisp new bills are customarily used as gift money for celebratory occasions.
A large domesticated bovine with broad, curved horns, kept in warm regions of Asia for farm work, milk, and meat.
A cabinet or boxlike piece of furniture for storing books.

glosses: shoulder width; breadth of the shoulders
explanations: The distance across a person's shoulders. Used when describing build, fitting clothes, or body measurements.
The quality of being good; the good points or appeal of something. The noun form of the adjective {良|よ}い.
Alcoholic drinks of Western origin, such as whisky, wine, and brandy, as distinguished from sake and other traditional Japanese drinks.
Imitating someone else superficially, without understanding the reason or substance behind what is copied. Always used disparagingly.

glosses: mountain village; secluded village in the hills
explanations: A small village set deep in the mountains, away from towns. The word carries a quiet, remote, somewhat poetic image.
The length of a garment's sleeve, measured from the shoulder seam to the end of the cuff. A standard clothing measurement.
The practice sword used in kendo, made from four strips of split bamboo bound together. It stands in for a real sword in training and matches.

glosses: to hire; to take on; to employ
explanations: To formally bring someone on as a worker or staff member. More deliberate and formal than plain {雇|やと}う, often used of a company taking on new personnel.

glosses: to yield to one another; to give way mutually; to compromise
explanations: For two or more parties to each defer to the other, whether physically making room or backing down in a dispute. Carries a positive sense of mutual consideration.

glosses: to be divisible; to be satisfied; to feel settled
to feel settled about; to come to terms with
explanations: Of a number, to divide evenly leaving no remainder.
To resolve one's feelings about something and accept it, leaving no lingering doubt or dissatisfaction. Often used in the negative to mean 'unable to fully accept'.

glosses: to be content; to be fully satisfied; to want for nothing
explanations: To feel complete satisfaction, with nothing lacking. Describes a deep, settled sense of fulfillment rather than momentary pleasure.

glosses: to attract; to draw; to captivate
to attract; to draw (interest, attention); to captivate
explanations: To draw someone's interest, attention, or feelings toward something. Written {惹|ひ}く specifically for attracting attention or the heart, distinguishing it from the general verb {引|ひ}く.

glosses: to study; to master; to cultivate
to study; to master; to cultivate (learning, conduct)
explanations: To pursue a field of study to completion, or to cultivate and discipline one's skills or moral conduct. Written {修|おさ}める for the senses of learning and self-cultivation.

glosses: to be checkmated; to be cornered; to be stuck
to be checkmated; to be cornered; to have no way out
explanations: Originally a shogi/chess term for the king being checkmated. By extension, used colloquially to mean a situation is hopeless and there is no escape.

glosses: to take (measures); to devise; to work out
to take (measures); to devise (a plan, countermeasure)
explanations: To work out and put into effect a plan or countermeasure to deal with a problem. A formal verb used mostly with words like {対策|たいさく} or {措置|そち}.

glosses: to mix together; to blend; to combine
explanations: To stir or fold two or more substances together so they form a single uniform mixture. The {合|あ}わせる element stresses bringing the parts together into one.

glosses: enviable in a resentful way; jealous; galling
enviable in a resentful way; galling; arousing jealousy
explanations: Describes someone or something that stirs bitter envy — wanting what another has, mixed with resentment that they have it. Stronger and more negative than {羨|うらや}ましい.
Describes something striking in scale, force, or degree — so much so that it is almost overwhelming. Can be positive or negative depending on context.
Describes a problem or choice that causes worry and is hard to resolve, leaving one torn. The most common modern usage.
Describes something that stirs the senses or desire, especially a captivating, sensual quality. A more literary, less frequent sense.

glosses: gentle; mild; even-tempered (of a person or climate)
explanations: Describes a calm, gentle quality with no harshness — used both for a mild, agreeable climate and for a calm, even-tempered personality.

glosses: separated; apart from one another; scattered
explanations: The state of people (or things) who were once together being apart and unable to be together. Most often used of family or close friends who become separated.
The horn of an automobile, sounded to warn or signal others. From the brand name 'Klaxon'.

glosses: outskirts of town; edge of town
explanations: The area at the edge of a town where buildings thin out and the countryside begins.
A person who breaks a rule, regulation, or law. Common in traffic and administrative contexts.
A harmful event or trouble that brings suffering. More literary and weighty than everyday words for trouble, often used in proverbs and set phrases.

glosses: shoe polishing; the act of shining shoes; a shoeshiner
explanations: Cleaning and polishing shoes to make them shine, or the tools or person that does this.

glosses: afternoon sun; the low sun shining from the west
explanations: The strong, low sunlight that comes from the west in the late afternoon. Often felt as glaring or uncomfortably hot.
A small bed for an infant, typically one that can be rocked. Also used figuratively for the place where something originates or is nurtured.

glosses: body slam; throwing oneself wholeheartedly into something
body slam; ramming with one's body; body check
tackling something wholeheartedly; an all-out, fearless approach
explanations: Striking an opponent or object by hurling one's whole body against it.
Figuratively, throwing oneself into a task or challenge with one's whole being, holding nothing back.

glosses: firefly viewing; going out to enjoy or catch fireflies
explanations: The traditional summer pastime of going out on early-summer evenings to watch or catch fireflies near rivers and rice fields.

glosses: onsen egg; egg slow-cooked at a low temperature
explanations: An egg cooked slowly in hot water around 65–70°C so that the yolk stays creamy while the white turns soft and custard-like. Originally made using hot-spring water.
The standard greeting used in the evening, after dark, when meeting or addressing someone.
A first-year or newly debuted player or member, especially in professional sports. From English 'rookie.'
A thick, strong cord made of twisted fibers, wire, or synthetic material, used for tying, pulling, or securing things.
Describes a person who is habitually lazy and makes no effort, or such behavior. As a noun it refers to such a person. Colloquial and mildly critical in tone.
The use of physical violence against another person. In legal contexts it refers to the crime of using force on someone, and it is sometimes a euphemism for sexual assault.
A thin, shimmering sphere of soapy water blown into the air, popular as a children's plaything. シャボン derives from the Portuguese word for soap.

glosses: mechanical; like a machine; done without thought
explanations: Describes actions or responses done automatically and without thought or feeling, like a machine. Can also literally mean 'relating to machines.'

glosses: steaming in a covered pan; baking in foil
steam-baking; cooking in a sealed covering
explanations: A cooking method in which food is heated in a closed pot, foil, or wrapping so that it cooks gently in its own steam and moisture.

glosses: to comb out and smooth (hair); to disentangle
explanations: To run a comb through hair to remove tangles and smooth it. The reading とく is shared with the homophones {解|と}く (to undo) and {溶|と}く (to dissolve).
The pupil of the eye — the black, adjustable opening at the center of the iris that lets light in. A medical and anatomical term.

glosses: koban; oval gold coin of the Edo period
explanations: A flat, oval gold coin used as currency in Japan during the Edo period (1603–1868), and a familiar symbol of old wealth.
A cat with black fur. In Japan it carries superstitious associations — unlucky in some traditions, but a charm against evil in others.

glosses: watching vigilantly for a chance; lying in wait
explanations: Watching closely and patiently for the right moment to pounce, the way a tiger eyes its prey. A four-character idiom, used adverbially with と.

glosses: Year of the Tiger (in the zodiac)
explanations: The Year of the Tiger, one of the twelve years of the Chinese/Japanese zodiac ({十二支|じゅうにし}). A person born in such a year is said to be 'a tiger.'
The peregrine falcon, a fast-flying bird of prey famous for its high-speed dives. The name is also used for fast trains and vehicles.
A common brown bird of prey often seen circling and crying overhead near coasts and rivers in Japan, known for snatching food from people.
The traditional sport of hunting game with a trained hawk or falcon, historically practiced by nobles and samurai.
The Japanese macaque, the native monkey of Japan, famous abroad as the 'snow monkey' that bathes in hot springs.
The paulownia tree and its lightweight, fine-grained wood, prized for chests, boxes, and musical instruments.
Contemporary poetry, especially free verse written in modern colloquial Japanese, as opposed to classical or fixed-form poetry such as tanka and haiku.
A cleaning tool with a long handle and an absorbent or fibrous head, used for wiping and cleaning floors.
An expression of welcome said to someone who has come or arrived, equivalent to English 'welcome.'
The academic study of nutrition — how the nutrients in food affect health and bodily function.

glosses: the whole face; (with a smile) beaming
explanations: The entire face. Used especially in {満面|まんめん}の{笑|え}み ('a beaming smile') to describe an expression spread across the whole face.

glosses: to appear in print; to be listed; to be loaded on
to appear in print; to be listed; to be carried (in a publication)
explanations: Of an article, photo, name, or piece of information: to appear in a newspaper, book, website, or other published medium. Also used of cargo or an object resting on or loaded onto something.

glosses: to suffer from (an illness); to be ill
explanations: To be afflicted with a disease or long-term medical condition. More formal and literary than {病気|びょうき}になる, and usually implies a serious or prolonged illness.

glosses: to roll; to tumble; to roll over
explanations: Of a person or object: to roll, tumble, or roll over, often suddenly or repeatedly. Frequently describes someone rolling around on the ground or floor.

glosses: to sever; to cut off; to give up
to sever; to cut off; to break off; to give up
explanations: To deliberately end or break off something ongoing — a relationship, a supply, a route, or a habit. Often implies a decisive, final break.

glosses: to be imminent; to draw near; to press in
to be imminent; to draw near; to press close
explanations: Of a deadline, the year's end, or an event: to be close at hand and pressing. Conveys a sense of mounting urgency as the time approaches.

glosses: to harm; to injure; to damage
to harm; to injure; to damage; to hurt (feelings, health)
explanations: To cause harm or damage to something, especially health, feelings, or interests. Common in formal or written contexts and in fixed expressions.

glosses: to find (someone) bothersome; to keep at a distance
to find (someone) bothersome; to feel awkward around; to keep at a distance
explanations: To regard a person as a nuisance or as someone whose presence makes one uncomfortable, and to want to avoid them — often a senior, strict, or overbearing figure.

glosses: to cite; to name; to hold (a ceremony); to achieve
to cite; to name; to give (as an example); to raise (a hand)
to hold (a ceremony); to achieve; to produce (results)
explanations: To put something forward for attention — to name or enumerate an example, reason, or candidate, or to raise one's hand or voice.
To carry out a formal event such as a wedding, or to attain a concrete result, profit, or record through effort.

glosses: to point out; to indicate; to identify
to point out; to indicate; to identify (a problem, error)
explanations: To draw attention to a specific point — typically a mistake, problem, or noteworthy fact — by explicitly naming it. Common in discussion, criticism, and analysis.

glosses: old custom; long-standing convention; entrenched practice
explanations: A custom or practice handed down from the past, usually carrying a negative nuance of something outdated that hinders progress. Often the target of criticism or reform.

glosses: gold bar; gold ingot; gold nugget
gold bar; gold ingot; lump of gold
explanations: A solid mass of gold, whether a refined bar or ingot held as an asset, or a natural nugget. Used for gold held as a store of value or recovered from mining.
A state of calm rest in which the mind and body are at ease, free from worry or labor. A somewhat literary word, often with spiritual or religious overtones.

glosses: victim of an accident; person in distress
person in distress; accident victim; stranded person
explanations: A person who has met with disaster — typically lost, injured, or stranded in the mountains, at sea, or in another dangerous situation, and in need of rescue.
A junior academic rank at a Japanese university, below {准教授|じゅんきょうじゅ} (associate professor). The position carries both teaching and research duties.
The point from which something arises — literally the headwaters of a river, or figuratively the origin or root cause of an idea, energy, problem, or culture.

glosses: labor and management; workers and employers
explanations: Workers (labor) and employers (management) considered together as the two parties in employment relations. Used mainly in discussion of negotiations, disputes, and agreements.

glosses: assembly hall; chamber; floor (of a legislature)
assembly hall; legislative chamber; the floor
explanations: The hall or chamber where a legislative or deliberative body meets, such as a parliament or council. Also refers to the floor where members debate and vote.
The large intestine — the final section of the digestive tract, which absorbs water and forms waste. Contrasts with the {小腸|しょうちょう} (small intestine).
An organic acid produced by fermentation and by muscles during intense exercise. Familiar from fermented foods and from the discussion of muscle fatigue.
A medical treatment that filters waste and excess fluid from the blood when the kidneys can no longer do so. Usually refers to {人工透析|じんこうとうせき} (artificial dialysis).
Legal matters between private parties — disputes over contracts, money, property, or damages — as opposed to criminal matters. Contrasts with {刑事|けいじ} (criminal).
A pair of people who work together as a team, especially a comedy duo or any well-matched partnership. Short for English "combination."

glosses: receipts and disbursements; accounting of money
receipts and payments; cash accounting; bookkeeping of money
explanations: The taking in and paying out of money, and the keeping of records of those transactions. Used mainly in accounting and administrative contexts.
A pattern of parallel lines or bands, as on cloth, an animal's coat, or any surface. Most often used of textiles and clothing.

glosses: always; habitually; for some time now
explanations: On an ongoing, habitual basis. Used especially to introduce a thought or opinion one has held all along, as in "I've always thought that…"
A non-alcoholic drink such as juice, cola, or tea, typically offered as an alternative to alcoholic beverages.

glosses: softball (the sport, or the ball used in it)
explanations: A bat-and-ball sport similar to baseball but played with a larger, softer ball on a smaller field. Popular in Japanese schools, especially for girls.

glosses: blueberry (the small dark-blue fruit or its plant)
explanations: A small, round, dark-blue berry eaten fresh or used in jam, sweets, and drinks. Often associated with eye health in Japan.

glosses: apricot (the orange fruit or its tree)
explanations: A small, soft, orange stone fruit with a tart-sweet flavor, eaten fresh or dried and often made into jam. Also written {杏|あんず}.
The stimulant found in coffee, tea, and many soft drinks that helps keep one awake and alert.
A young cow that has not yet matured. Also written {仔牛|こうし}.
A coiling, circular pattern or motion turning in toward a center, as in water swirling down a drain or a spiral shape.
A swirling current in the sea, formed where strong tides meet in a narrow channel. The whirlpools of Naruto are especially famous.

glosses: thicket; copse; woods of mixed trees
explanations: A small wood made up of various kinds of ordinary broadleaf trees rather than planted timber, often found near villages and farmland.
A wood made up of pine trees, often seen along the coast where pines are planted as windbreaks.
A museum with hands-on exhibits about science and technology, often aimed at letting visitors learn through experiments and displays.
A person who smokes tobacco, especially as a habit. A somewhat formal term used in health and public-policy contexts.
The ability to produce new ideas or original things, valued in art, design, and problem-solving.
A traditional Japanese fishing method using trained cormorants to catch sweetfish, performed at night by torchlight on rivers.

glosses: second cousin; child of a parent's cousin
explanations: A relative who shares a great-grandparent: the child of one's parent's cousin. Also called またいとこ.
The quality of being beautiful. The noun form of the adjective {美|うつく}しい, used for visual, natural, and abstract beauty alike.
Idle talk or rumors about other people's private lives, especially scandalous stories about celebrities reported in the media.
A leisure activity of going to an orchard to pick and eat apples, popular as an autumn outing.
The quality or degree of being weak — in strength, will, ability, or intensity. The noun form of the adjective {弱|よわ}い.
The quality of being young or childlike, whether an endearing innocence or an immaturity in attitude. The noun form of {幼|おさな}い.

glosses: to become muddy; to be miry
explanations: Of ground or a road, to turn soft and muddy so that feet sink in, typically after rain or snowmelt.
A small yellow songbird kept as a pet and prized for its singing. Often used figuratively as an early warning of danger.
A percentage added to a bill at restaurants, hotels, and bars to cover service. Common in higher-end establishments and often shown as a fixed rate such as 10%.
A small towel for drying the hands, often carried in a bag for use in public restrooms, which frequently lack paper towels or dryers.
Clear adhesive tape used for wrapping, mending paper, and sticking things together. Originally a brand name that became the everyday word for the product.
A magnetic tape in a small plastic case, used to record and play back sound before CDs and digital media became standard.
Easily peelable paper tape. Besides its original use in painting, decorative versions (often shortened to マスキングテープ／マステ) are popular in Japan for crafts and journaling.
Television service delivered over a wired cable network rather than over the air, often offering local channels and extra programming for a subscription fee.
A thin, flat television using LCD, LED, or similar panel technology, as opposed to the bulky cathode-ray-tube sets that came before.

glosses: principal (of a kindergarten or preschool); director
principal of a kindergarten or nursery; director
explanations: The head of a 幼稚園 (kindergarten) or 保育園 (nursery). Also used for the director of facilities ending in 園, such as a botanical garden or zoo.
A small finch with a gray body, white cheeks, and a thick pink beak, popular in Japan as a hand-tamed pet bird.

glosses: way of making; how to make; recipe
way of making; how to make; method of preparation
explanations: The method or procedure for making something. Used for recipes, crafts, and any process of producing or building a thing.
The thick cotton jacket, trousers, and belt worn for judo. Made sturdy enough to withstand the gripping and throwing of the sport.
A station, base, or hub. In Japanese it rarely means a train station ({駅|えき}); instead it appears in names of service points, broadcasting bases, and facilities.
A method of treating an illness or condition. Covers medical procedures, drug regimens, and other approaches to curing or managing a disease.
A device that detects danger such as fire or smoke and sounds an alarm. Most often refers to a fire alarm or smoke detector.
A basic swimming style in which the head stays above water and the hands paddle in short strokes, like a swimming dog. Often the first stroke beginners learn.

glosses: good guy; hero; the good party
explanations: A virtuous character or person, contrasted with a villain. Often used of clear-cut heroes in stories or of the 'good side' in a dispute.
In health and nutrition, bacteria that benefit the body, especially in the gut. Usually said as 善玉菌.

glosses: bad guy; villain; the bad party
explanations: A villain or wrongdoer, contrasted with a hero. Also used for whoever or whatever is cast as the cause of a problem.
In health and nutrition, bacteria that harm the body, especially in the gut. Usually said as 悪玉菌.

glosses: lending and borrowing; debts and credits
explanations: The act of lending and borrowing, taken together. Often used of money or favors, and of keeping such accounts balanced between people.
The biological process by which organisms produce offspring. A technical term used in biology and reproductive health, often in compounds.
A written expression that shows how a value is calculated, using numbers and operators. Used for arithmetic problems as well as formulas in spreadsheets.

glosses: to pass (an exam, inspection); to qualify
explanations: To pass a test, examination, or inspection by meeting the required standard. Used for school and license exams, job screenings, and quality checks.

glosses: right to vote; voting rights; suffrage
explanations: The legal right to cast a vote in an election. In Japan it is granted to citizens aged 18 and over.
A play, film, or TV drama set in the past and based on historical events or figures. In Japan, samurai-era stories are a common subject.
A hard casing applied around a broken bone or injured limb to hold it still while it heals.
A person who travels into unknown or dangerous regions to investigate them, such as polar, jungle, or deep-sea explorers.
A brush for grooming and styling the hair. From English 'hair brush'.

glosses: sports towel; long thin towel for exercise
explanations: A long, narrow towel designed to be draped around the neck during sports or workouts. From English 'sports towel'.
The common currency of the eurozone countries of the European Union. From English 'euro'.
The currency of the United Kingdom (pound sterling). From English 'pound'.
The unit of weight equal to about 454 grams, used mainly when referring to overseas measures.
A presenter who hosts a TV or radio news program, often adding commentary rather than just reading the news. From English 'newscaster'.
A small wheel attached to the bottom of furniture or carts so they can be rolled. From English 'caster'.
A person who gathers information on location and reports it on TV or radio, often interviewing people at the scene. From English 'reporter'.
A guest on a TV program, often an expert or celebrity, who offers opinions and analysis on the news or topics being discussed. From English 'commentator'.
A person who provides the spoken narration for a program, film, or documentary, usually off-screen. From English 'narrator'.
A motorcycle. A somewhat older or colloquial word, originally distinguishing a solo motorcycle from one with a sidecar.
A proposed plan for a project, event, or product, typically written up for review and approval. Compound of {企画|きかく} (planning) + {案|あん} (proposal, draft).
A proposed plan for fixing or improving an existing problem, process, or situation. Compound of {改善|かいぜん} (improvement) + {案|あん} (proposal, draft).

glosses: to be angry; to be enraged
explanations: To feel and show strong anger. A literary, somewhat dramatic word for the everyday {怒|おこ}る, often suggesting intense or dignified anger.

glosses: wheeled bag; rolling carry-on; carrier bag
explanations: A bag or case with wheels and an extendable handle, pulled along rather than carried. From English 'carry bag'. Also used for a soft carrier for pets.
A sandwich of a cooked patty served in a round bun, typically with toppings. From English 'hamburger'.

glosses: being fed up; being sick and tired (of)
being fed up; being sick and tired of
explanations: The state of being thoroughly bored or fed up with something after too much of it. A reduplicated, emphatic form of {飽|あ}きる (to grow tired of). Most often used as {飽|あ}き{飽|あ}きする.

glosses: unhulled rice; rice in the husk
unhulled rice; rice in the husk; paddy
explanations: Rice grains that still have their outer husk on, as harvested from the plant before threshing and hulling.

glosses: paddy rice; rice grown in flooded fields
explanations: Rice cultivated in flooded paddy fields, as opposed to rice grown in dry fields. The standard method of rice farming in Japan.
A hand farming tool with a flat blade and a long handle, used to dig and turn over soil. Historically also a plow drawn through a field.

headword: スーパーコンピュータ
explanations: An extremely high-performance computer used for large-scale scientific and technical calculations such as weather forecasting and simulations. From English 'supercomputer'.
Visual images produced by a computer, or the field and technology of creating them. From English 'graphics'.

glosses: faculty of commerce; school of commerce
explanations: The university department that teaches commerce, business, accounting, and marketing. Compound of {商学|しょうがく} (commerce studies) + {学部|がくぶ} (faculty).

glosses: riding double; riding two on one vehicle
riding two people on one vehicle; riding double
explanations: Two people riding together on a vehicle meant primarily for one, such as a bicycle or motorcycle. Compound of {二人|ふたり} (two people) + {乗|の}り (riding).
The realm of the afterlife in religious belief. Also used figuratively for any place or situation that feels blissful or ideal.
A traditional Japanese unit of area equal to about 3.3 square meters, or two tatami mats. Still widely used for land and real estate.
Half of a day — either a morning or an afternoon, or simply a stretch of roughly four to six hours.

glosses: somewhat late; on the late side
somewhat late; on the late side; a bit slow
explanations: Formed from {遅|おそ}い plus the suffix め. Indicates being later or slower than average, but not extremely so — 'a bit late.'
An adnominal meaning 'unknown' or 'unfamiliar,' placed directly before a noun. Most often describes a person one has never met.

glosses: ginger pork; pork sautéed with ginger
explanations: A home-style and diner dish of thinly sliced pork pan-fried in a sauce of grated ginger, soy sauce, and mirin. Short for {豚|ぶた}の{生姜焼|しょうがや}き.
A loanword from English 'expert.' A person with advanced skill or deep knowledge in a particular field.
A designated region of the sky, especially as controlled or restricted for aviation, defense, or air-traffic purposes.
Along or facing the sea — the strip of land running beside the coast. Often used attributively with の.

glosses: number of books; number of volumes
explanations: The count of books or bound volumes — for example, how many books a library lends or a person owns.
Each and every weekend; recurring on Saturdays and Sundays. Combines {毎|まい} (every) with {週末|しゅうまつ} (weekend).

glosses: to stop raining; to stop falling (of rain or snow)
to stop raining; to stop (of rain or snow)
explanations: Of rain, snow, or hail, to cease falling. A compound of {降|ふ}る (to fall as precipitation) + {止|や}む (to stop).

glosses: to be startled; to be taken aback; to be shocked
explanations: To feel a sudden jolt of surprise or alarm, often at something unexpected, unpleasant, or frightening. ぎょっ is mimetic of a sharp inner shock.
The night of two days ago — the evening preceding last night.

glosses: metropolitan; run by the Tokyo Metropolitan Government
explanations: Established and operated by the Tokyo Metropolitan Government ({都|と}). Used before institutions such as schools, hospitals, and parks.
An argument or quarrel between a married couple. Combines {夫婦|ふうふ} (married couple) + {喧嘩|けんか} (quarrel).
A commissioned officer in the military — someone holding the rank of second lieutenant or above, who commands enlisted personnel.
A member of Japan's Self-Defense Forces ({自衛隊|じえいたい}) — the term used in place of 'soldier' for Japan's uniformed personnel.

glosses: to update; to renew; to break (a record)
explanations: To replace something with a newer version or state — updating data or software, renewing a contract or license, or setting a new record that surpasses the previous one.
One's own personal or private business, as opposed to public or work matters. Often used to preface a personal remark.

glosses: dinner (often a special or upscale evening meal)
explanations: A loanword from English 'dinner.' An evening meal, especially a somewhat formal, special, or restaurant-style one.

glosses: square (of a number); square (in area units)
explanations: Square — used to form units of area (square meters, etc.) and, in mathematics, the square of a number (a number multiplied by itself).
A pen with a flexible, brush-like tip and a built-in ink supply, used to write in a calligraphic brush style without grinding ink.

glosses: to ignite; to catch fire; to light
explanations: To start burning, or to set something burning. Used for fires, fuel, fireworks, burners, and the like.
A voucher or coupon exchangeable for a meal. Often given as a perk, prize, or welfare benefit, or included with hotel and event packages.
A voucher redeemable toward travel costs such as transport, lodging, or tour packages. Popular as a prize or gift.
A red flag used as a signal, especially to warn of danger or to stop traffic, races, or swimming. Also a long-standing symbol of socialist and communist movements.

glosses: dog and monkey; (figuratively) two parties who get along badly
explanations: Literally "dog and monkey," animals proverbially said to fight on sight. Used almost exclusively in the idiom {犬猿|けんえん}の{仲|なか} to describe two people on extremely bad terms.

glosses: red clay; red soil; reddish earth
explanations: Reddish-brown soil or clay colored by iron oxides. Common on volcanic terrain and used for pottery, bricks, and athletic-field surfaces.
A slender wasp with long, dangling hind legs that builds open, honeycomb-shaped nests under eaves. Less aggressive than hornets but capable of a painful sting.
A topical cream, lotion, or oral medicine that relieves itching from insect bites, rashes, or allergies.
The instinctive, protective love a mother feels for her child. Sometimes used more broadly for a nurturing affection toward those weaker than oneself.
The everyday shortened name for the photo- and video-sharing app Instagram. Standard in casual speech and online.

glosses: side shoot; axillary bud; lateral bud
explanations: A bud or shoot that grows from the angle between a leaf and the stem, rather than at the tip. Gardeners often pinch these off to direct the plant's energy.
A person who paints or draws pictures, especially as a profession. A casual, everyday word compared with {画家|がか}.
A closed-in, narrow space with little room to move, such as an elevator, a small windowless room, or an MRI tube. Most often seen in {閉所恐怖症|へいしょきょうふしょう} (claustrophobia).

glosses: temple bell; large hanging Buddhist bell
explanations: A large bronze bell hung in a Buddhist temple and struck from the outside with a wooden beam. Best known for being rung 108 times on New Year's Eve.
A low degree or level of something, especially of an illness, injury, disability, or symptom. Used as a noun and, with の, as a modifier.
The handing over of something from one party to another — money, goods, documents, or information. A formal word, common in legal, business, and grammar contexts. Takes する.
A hazy condition of the air caused by fine dust, smoke, or pollutants that reduce visibility. A meteorological term, drier and dustier than fog.

glosses: official use; official business; public use
explanations: Use for governmental, public, or company business rather than private purposes. Often contrasts with {私用|しよう} (personal use).
A native speaker's command of Japanese — reading comprehension, vocabulary, writing, and the ability to express thoughts clearly. Discussed especially in education.

glosses: session; term (of a legislature or conference)
session; term; period of a meeting
explanations: The set period during which a legislative body, assembly, conference, or exhibition is in session. Defines when business can be conducted.

glosses: complete recovery; full healing (from injury or illness)
explanations: Full healing of an injury or illness to the point of complete cure. Most often stated as a length of time, as in {全治|ぜんち}{二週間|にしゅうかん} ("two weeks to fully heal"). Takes する.

glosses: monaka; wafer-shell sweet filled with bean paste
explanations: A traditional Japanese confection of sweet adzuki-bean paste sandwiched between two thin, crisp wafer shells made from glutinous rice.
A map showing only outlines such as borders and coastlines, with place names and other details left blank. Used in geography classes for students to fill in.

glosses: independent study project; free research assignment
explanations: A school assignment, classically over summer vacation, in which a student chooses a topic and investigates it freely — through experiments, observation, crafts, or fieldwork.
Thick, strained yogurt with a high protein content and a creamy texture. Widely sold in Japanese supermarkets and used in both sweet and savory dishes.

headword: インフルエンザワクチン
explanations: A vaccine that protects against seasonal influenza, typically given by injection in autumn before flu season begins.
A person whose job is to drive a taxi, transporting passengers for a fare.
A serving format in which diners help themselves freely from a spread of dishes, often for a fixed price.
Natural materials such as oil, coal, natural gas, and renewables that can be used to produce energy.

glosses: in an instant; in a flash; instantly
explanations: Describes something happening in an extremely short moment. Formed from {一瞬|いっしゅん} (a moment) plus the particle で marking the span of time over which something occurs.

glosses: the distant future; the far future
explanations: A point in time far ahead from now. Often contrasted with {近|ちか}い{将来|しょうらい} (the near future).
Refers to the very recent past, often to stress that something feels surprisingly recent. The adverb つい means "just (now)" or "only a moment ago."
Goods that are indispensable for daily life, such as food, water, and fuel, especially during emergencies or shortages.
A group that goes ahead of the main body to prepare the way, scout, or set things up. Used in military, expedition, and business contexts.

glosses: the prewar generation; prewar school (of thought)
the prewar generation; people of the prewar era
explanations: People who were born and grew up before World War II, or whose values and outlook were shaped in that era. Often contrasted with the postwar generation.
The green pigment in plants and algae that absorbs light to drive photosynthesis.
An aircraft designed to operate from a warship, especially an aircraft carrier.
An average found by multiplying n values together and taking the nth root. Used for rates of growth and ratios, where it suits the data better than the ordinary (arithmetic) mean.

glosses: jojutsu; staff fighting; art of the staff
jojutsu; the art of the short staff
explanations: A Japanese martial art that uses a short wooden staff ({杖|じょう}) for striking, thrusting, and blocking, often practiced against a sword.
Secretly watching others, especially for sexual gratification. A formal, somewhat clinical term used in legal and psychological contexts.
A surface or view produced by cutting straight across an object, perpendicular to its long axis. Used in engineering, anatomy, and geology.

glosses: skin-beautifying effect; benefits for the skin
explanations: The effect of making skin smoother, clearer, or more attractive. A common marketing phrase for cosmetics, foods, and treatments.
A cosmetic or medicinal substance intended to lighten the skin or reduce dark spots and pigmentation.
How often something happens within a given period or population. Common in statistics, medicine, and quality control.

glosses: overall record; cumulative record; career stats
explanations: A total tally of results accumulated over a whole career or period, rather than for a single season or game. Common in sports.
Oil burned to produce heat or power, such as the heavy oil used in ships, boilers, and power plants.
The whole of Japan, or everywhere within the country. Formed from {日本|にほん} (Japan) plus the suffix 〜{中|じゅう} (throughout).
Describes a claim or expression that overstates the truth, making something seem greater or better than it really is. Carries a critical, negative tone.

glosses: to mislead; to confuse; to lead astray
explanations: To cause someone to lose clear judgment through deception, temptation, or distraction. The transitive counterpart of {惑|まど}う (to be perplexed).

glosses: air conditioning and heating; climate control
explanations: Equipment or systems that both cool and heat indoor spaces; collectively, indoor climate control. Compound of {冷房|れいぼう} (cooling) and {暖房|だんぼう} (heating).
The way something gets under way, especially its initial momentum or success. Often used of projects, sales, seasons, or careers.
The hospital department or medical specialty dealing with disorders of the nervous system. The suffix 〜{科|か} designates a medical specialty.

glosses: to get excited; to be worked up; to be on edge
explanations: Of emotions or nerves, to become heightened or aroused, often in a way that is hard to calm. Also written {昂|たか}ぶる.
Something whose outcome cannot be predicted and depends heavily on luck or circumstance, such as a contest, election, or business venture.
A male child. A formal or official word used on documents, in news, and in set phrases rather than in casual speech.
A person who runs a business or makes a living through trade. Often implies someone shrewd and skilled at making money.
A newly developed pharmaceutical, especially one recently approved or brought to market.

glosses: to be injured; to be wounded
explanations: To suffer a physical injury, especially in an accident, disaster, or conflict. A formal word common in news reports.
The state of being infected with or having a condition while displaying no symptoms. The prefix {無|む}〜 means "without."
A female child. A formal or official word used on documents, in news, and in set phrases rather than in casual speech.
The common name for Japan's government-run public employment security offices, which help people find jobs and claim unemployment benefits.
The summer period, viewed especially with regard to its heat or its effect on activity, business, or health.
An amusement-park ride with seats, often shaped as horses, mounted on a rotating platform that moves up and down.
A large amusement park built around a unifying theme, with rides, shows, and attractions.
A person known for developing and expressing original ideas, especially about society, politics, or human life.
A writer who composes plays for the stage.
Walking long distances through mountains or natural terrain for recreation, typically more rugged than ordinary hiking.
A group of people traveling or acting together as a unit, often a delegation or the people accompanying a central figure.
The governmental power to make laws. In Japan it belongs to the Diet, as one of the three separated powers.
Describes doing or deciding something before the right time has come. Almost always appears in the set phrase {時期尚早|じきしょうそう}.
The polite form of {迷惑|めいわく}, used to refer to trouble or inconvenience caused to others. Very common in apologies and set business expressions.
Colloquial i-adjective from エロ (a clipping of 'erotic'). Describes something sexually suggestive or raunchy, or a person who is perverted.
The adverbial form of the na-adjective {楽|らく} (ease, comfort). Describes doing something without difficulty or strain, or being in a relaxed, comfortable state.
Noun formed from {速|はや}い (fast), referring to how fast something moves or happens. Also used for speed as a magnitude in everyday and scientific contexts.
The person who is speaking, as contrasted with the listener. Can also describe someone skilled at talking or telling stories.
The German language. Formed with the suffix {語|ご} (language) attached to ドイツ (Germany).

glosses: nursing home; retirement home; old people's home
explanations: A residential facility where elderly people live and receive care and meals. ホーム is from English 'home'.
A facility that provides nursing and daily-living assistance for elderly or disabled people who need help. {介護|かいご} means long-term care; {施設|しせつ} means facility.
A novel centered on solving a crime or puzzle through reasoning, typically a murder investigated by a detective. {推理|すいり} means deduction or reasoning.
A company that plans and produces advertising and buys media space on behalf of client businesses. Composed of {広告|こうこく} (advertisement) + {代理店|だいりてん} (agency).
The Japanese imperial era name for the reign of Emperor {昭和|しょうわ} (Hirohito), spanning 1926 to 1989. Years are counted from the start, so {昭和|しょうわ}{50年|ねん} is 1975.
The historical period of Emperor Meiji's reign, 1868–1912, when Japan rapidly modernized and Westernized after the end of the feudal Edo period.
The amount of time still left before a deadline, the end of a game, or the completion of an activity.
A strap or handle that hangs from above for standing passengers to hold on a train or bus; also a hanging handle on a bag or fixture.
The amount of time that has passed since a starting point, such as the start of an event, a stopwatch, or a process.
Going from bar to bar drinking, or making a habit of going out to drink. The noun form of {飲|の}み{歩|ある}く.

glosses: to zip up; to do up a zipper
to zip up; to close a zipper
explanations: To close a zipper. チャック is a common everyday word for 'zipper' (originally a brand name).

glosses: to expect something in return; to seek a reward
to expect something in return; to seek a reward or favor back
explanations: To do something while expecting a benefit, favor, or compensation in return. {見返|みかえ}り means a return favor or reward.

glosses: person who sees someone off; well-wisher at a departure
person who sees someone off; well-wisher
explanations: A person who goes to see off a traveler or guest at a station, airport, or port to bid them farewell.
Perceiving depth and three dimensions, either through normal binocular vision or by viewing specially prepared images such as stereograms or 3D displays. Can take する.

Lying about one's personal history — education, work experience, or qualifications — typically on a résumé or job application. {経歴|けいれき} is one's background; {詐称|さしょう} is false representation. Can take する.

glosses: gateway to success; stepping stone (to a career)
explanations: A difficult barrier or contest that, once passed, opens the way to success or advancement in a field.

glosses: first class; first place; first prize
first class; first place; first prize; top grade
explanations: The highest grade, rank, or prize among several levels. Used for prizes, travel classes, and ranks.

glosses: elite; member of a select, highly capable group
explanations: A person belonging to a select, highly capable or privileged group, especially in education, business, or government.

glosses: the following; the next (day, morning, year, etc.)
explanations: A prenominal word meaning 'the next' that attaches directly to a time noun. It cannot stand alone or take particles.
A deep-fried, panko-breaded pork cutlet, usually served with shredded cabbage, rice, and a thick sauce.
The thigh — the upper part of the leg between hip and knee. Also names the thigh as a cut of meat, especially poultry.
Flowers cut from the plant with their stems, used for arranging in a vase or as a bouquet, as opposed to potted or growing plants.
A felt-padded eraser used to wipe chalk off a blackboard. A familiar object in Japanese classrooms.
Mimetic word for the sound of loud snoring or, by extension, for sleeping very deeply.

glosses: suddenly and completely; all at once; easily
explanations: Mimetic adverb for a sudden, complete change of state — falling asleep at once, an abrupt change of mind, or being easily fooled. Often suggests the change happens easily or unexpectedly.

glosses: hardship; painfulness; how hard something is to bear
explanations: The quality of being emotionally or physically hard to bear, and the suffering that comes with it. The noun form of {辛|つら}い.
A small ball or beanbag, as used in the traditional game お{手玉|てだま}. In everyday Japanese it appears mostly in the idiom {手玉|てだま}に{取|と}る.
A hollow cylindrical object open at one or both ends, such as a tube, pipe, or barrel-like container.

glosses: drink diluted with hot water (esp. shochu)
explanations: An alcoholic drink, most often shochu, mixed with hot water; also the practice of diluting a drink this way. Popular in colder months.
A somewhat literary or emphatic word for the eye, more evocative than the everyday {目|め}. Appears in set expressions and descriptive writing.

glosses: waist cord (used when putting on a kimono)
explanations: A thin cloth cord tied around the waist, used mainly to hold a kimono in place while dressing, before the {帯|おび} is added.

glosses: kokuji; a kanji invented in Japan
explanations: A character made in Japan in the style of Chinese characters but not found in Chinese, such as {峠|とうげ} or {畑|はたけ}. Many have only a kun'yomi and no on'yomi.

glosses: plot of land; landed property; premises
plot of land; landed property; estate
explanations: A piece of land, especially one owned as property — a lot, plot, or estate. Somewhat formal; emphasizes land as a possession or asset.
A grass-like rush plant whose dried stems are woven into the facing of tatami mats.
A small room measuring four and a half tatami mats (about 7.3 square meters), a classic size for a modest Japanese room.
A team game in which players throw small balls into a tall basket, common at Japanese school sports festivals.

glosses: the five elements (wood, fire, earth, metal, water)
explanations: The five fundamental elements of traditional Chinese natural philosophy, thought to generate and overcome one another in cycles. Widely used in East Asian thought.
The point in the tidal cycle when the sea level is at its highest. The native ({訓読|くんよ}み) reading of {満潮|まんちょう}.
A softer, more literary way of saying that someone has died. Often carries a tone of quiet acceptance or respect. Also read {逝|ゆ}く.
An interjection used when about to begin something decisive, expressing resolve. Also forms the fixed phrase いざという{時|とき} (when the time comes; in an emergency).

glosses: to hold up; to hold out; to wave (over a reader)
to hold up; to hold out over something
explanations: To hold something up or out, especially over or toward something — over a fire for warmth, over one's eyes to shield them, or over a card reader. Now commonly used for tapping an IC card to a reader.

glosses: to resolve; to make up one's mind
to resolve; to make up one's mind; to be determined
explanations: To firmly decide to do something, with strong determination. Weightier and more deliberate than {決|き}める, implying a considered, serious commitment.

glosses: contrail; vapor trail (left by an aircraft)
explanations: The white trail of condensed water vapor that forms behind a high-flying aircraft. Literally {飛行機|ひこうき} (airplane) + {雲|くも} (cloud).
Pain in a tooth or teeth. The Sino-Japanese ({音読|おんよ}み) reading; the same kanji are also read {歯痛|はいた} in everyday speech.
An organized body of soldiers, ranging from a small squad to a large force. By extension, any organized team dispatched for a task.

glosses: to speak to; to address; to talk to
explanations: To speak to someone, often gently or warmly and in a way that invites a response. Also used of works of art or media that 'speak to' the audience emotionally.
A bullet or projectile fired from a gun. When read {弾|たま}, the character refers to ammunition; the same character is read {弾|だん} in compounds such as {弾丸|だんがん} (bullet).
A positively charged subatomic particle found in the nucleus of an atom, together with neutrons.
An electrically neutral subatomic particle found in the nucleus of an atom alongside protons.
A firmly established habit of doing something, almost always something undesirable or illegal. Most often appears in compounds about repeat offenders.
Something good received as a gift or blessing, or a favorable outcome achieved through effort. Always positive in tone; somewhat formal and literary.

glosses: roadside; wayside; side of the road
roadside; wayside; edge of the road
explanations: The edge or side of a road or street, especially the strip just beside where people walk or drive.

glosses: to input; to enter (data); to type in
to input; to enter (data); to key in
explanations: To enter data, text, or commands into a computer or device. The opposite of {出力|しゅつりょく}する (to output).

glosses: kanji numerals ({一|いち}, {二|に}, {三|さん} …)
explanations: Numbers written with kanji characters rather than Arabic numerals (1, 2, 3). Standard in vertical writing and formal documents.

glosses: first dan; first-degree rank (martial arts, go, shogi)
explanations: The first and lowest {段|だん} (dan) rank in martial arts, go, shogi, and similar disciplines, reached after clearing the {級|きゅう} (kyū) grades. In martial arts it corresponds to the first-degree black belt.
The Fahrenheit temperature scale, used mainly in the United States. Japan uses {摂氏|せっし} (Celsius) for everyday temperatures.

glosses: gym clothes; PE uniform; sportswear (for school PE)
explanations: The clothing students change into for physical education ({体育|たいいく}) class at Japanese schools, typically a T-shirt and shorts or a tracksuit.
A casual first-person pronoun used mainly by women and girls. A softened, colloquial form of わたし that sounds friendly and informal.
An affectionate, casual word for grandmother. Can also refer more broadly to any elderly woman.
An affectionate, informal word for one's father, warmer and more homey than おとうさん.
The arctic deer known in English as reindeer or caribou. Like many animal names, it is conventionally written in katakana.

glosses: rice husk; rice chaff; rice hull
explanations: The dry, papery outer hull separated from rice grains during hulling. Often used as mulch, fuel, or packing material.

glosses: shell mound; shell midden; kitchen midden
explanations: An archaeological site formed from accumulated shells and refuse left by prehistoric people, valuable for studying ancient diet and life.
A major port city in Kanagawa Prefecture just south of Tokyo, and Japan's second-largest city by population.
The capital and largest city of Hokkaido, known for snowy winters, its Snow Festival, ramen, and beer.
Japan's main conservative political party, abbreviated from {自由民主党|じゆうみんしゅとう}. It has governed Japan for most of the postwar era.
A short word for something served cold or unheated. Refers to cold water (especially お{冷|ひ}や at a restaurant) or to sake served at room temperature rather than warmed.
A drawn-out sound expressing hesitation, thinking, or mild reluctance while one considers a question or problem.
A short, sharp exclamation of sudden surprise, alarm, or realization—often the first reaction before saying more.
The country and continent in the Southern Hemisphere. A popular destination for Japanese travelers and students.
The northernmost prefecture of Honshu, famous for apples, the Nebuta Festival, and heavy winter snow.
Literally 'ten thousand years.' Used as a prefix in compounds to mean 'perpetual' or 'perennial,' and often, half-jokingly, 'forever stuck in one state.'

glosses: what kind of; what sort of
explanations: A prenominal expression asking about the nature, type, or meaning of something. It always precedes a noun.
Literally 'only this place.' Most often appears in ここだけの{話|はなし}, used to mark information as confidential—something that should not leave the present conversation.
The polite form of いくつ, made with the honorific お-. Used to ask someone's age, or sometimes a quantity, courteously.
Describes an older style, model, or method that has been superseded by newer ones. Often used for machines and equipment, and frequently with の before a noun.
Describes a newer style, model, or method as opposed to an older one. Frequently used with の before a noun.
A major or important discovery. The intensifying prefix {大|だい} emphasizes its significance; also used lightly in conversation for any exciting find.
A soft food spread on bread or crackers, such as jam, butter, or cream cheese. From English 'spread.'
Paint, or (with する) the act of painting or coating a surface. From English 'paint.' Common in DIY, automotive, and design contexts.
A small square of terrycloth carried like a handkerchief, popular in Japan for drying the hands and wiping away sweat.
Typing on a keyboard without looking at the keys. A wasei coinage; English uses "touch typing."

glosses: faculty of pharmacy; school of pharmacy
explanations: The division of a university that teaches pharmaceutical science and trains pharmacists.

glosses: faculty of education; school of education
explanations: The university division that studies education and trains teachers.
A type of municipality with city-level powers; in practice refers to Tokyo's 23 wards, each with its own mayor and assembly.
A scheduled transport service such as a plane flight, bus, or delivery run. Also used as a counter for such services.
Money paid in excess of what was actually owed. Most often refers to interest overpaid on consumer loans that the borrower can legally reclaim.
An educational system in which students earn credits by passing courses and graduate once they accumulate the required number, rather than advancing by fixed year-groups.
A payment method in which the buyer pays the courier for the goods at the moment of delivery. Often abbreviated 代引き.
A senior Japanese cabinet minister who heads the Cabinet Secretariat, coordinates government policy, and acts as the government's chief spokesperson.
A short form of {外務大臣|がいむだいじん}, the cabinet minister in charge of foreign affairs. Common in news headlines and reporting.
The entire school, meaning every student (and often the staff) of a single school taken together.
The silver-colored coin worth 100 yen, one of the most commonly used coins in everyday transactions.

glosses: moving work; touching film or book
explanations: A film, novel, or other creative work that deeply moves its audience. Frequently used in advertising and reviews.
In Buddhism, the accumulated effect of one's past actions that shapes one's destiny. By extension, a deep-rooted nature or burden one cannot escape.
A position one occupies, especially a coveted post, rank, or title. Carries a sense of authority or prestige attached to the spot.
A graded level of skill or quality. As a suffix it marks ranks in proficiency tests and martial arts, or a class within a category.
A suffix attached to nouns to form the word for a fee or charge paid for a service or for the use of something.
A state of being incomplete or not functioning fully. Most often appears in medical compounds naming the failure of an organ or bodily function.
Two or more factors reinforcing one another so that their combined result exceeds the simple sum. Almost always used in compounds, above all {相乗効果|そうじょうこうか}.
Describes a crime, criminal, or violent act that is extremely cruel and serious. Almost always used of grave offenses.
A person trained to travel and work in outer space aboard a spacecraft.
A shop that sells jewelry such as rings, necklaces, and precious stones.
A persuasive or seductive remark that wins someone over completely. Often a line that captures another's heart or seals a sale.

glosses: conversion to cash; cashing in; liquidation
explanations: Turning goods, securities, or other assets into money by selling them. Used as a noun and with する as a transitive verb.
A celebrated, unforgettable scene in a film, drama, sports match, or other performance that audiences remember and replay.
Describes an outcome so unlikely or fortunate that it seems like a miracle. Often used of narrow escapes and recoveries.

glosses: to push through; to part (a crowd)
to push through; to part; to shove aside
explanations: To push or sweep things aside with the hands or body in order to move forward, as through a crowd, undergrowth, or branches.
A large crowd of people moving like waves, especially the flow of a dense throng in a busy place.
Three children born to the same mother at one birth.
A young child of about three. This older sense survives mainly in the proverb below.
Two children born to the same mother at one birth. A formal, technical word; everyday speech uses {双子|ふたご}.

glosses: laziness; not bothering to do something; slovenliness
explanations: The trait of finding effort troublesome and neglecting to do things one should. Used as a noun and as a na-adjective. Also written {無精|ぶしょう}.

glosses: abolition; eradication; doing away with entirely
explanations: Completely abolishing or wiping out something undesirable so that it ceases to exist. Often used of weapons, discrimination, and harmful customs.

glosses: useful tool; convenient device; sharp instrument
explanations: A handy implement or technology that makes work easier. Most often appears in the set phrase {文明|ぶんめい}の{利器|りき} (the conveniences of civilization).
The general direction or course that a plan, project, organization, or piece of work is taking or should take.

glosses: home visit (by a teacher to a pupil's family)
explanations: A Japanese school custom in which a teacher visits each pupil's home, usually early in the school year, to meet the family and learn about the home environment.
A gathering held after an event or project to look back on what happened, discuss what went wrong, and draw lessons for next time.
An inner urge to resist or defy authority, rules, or those above oneself. Often used of adolescents toward parents and teachers.

glosses: the real culprit; the true criminal
the real culprit; the true perpetrator
explanations: The person who actually committed a crime, as opposed to someone wrongly suspected or falsely accused.

glosses: white ballot; vote in favor (in the Diet)
explanations: A ballot cast with nothing written on it, used to record turnout without choosing any candidate or option.
In Japan's Diet, a white voting slip indicating approval of a motion, as opposed to a blue slip for opposition.

glosses: travel destination; place one is traveling
travel destination; place one travels to
explanations: The place one goes to or is staying at on a trip. The suffix {先|さき} marks the destination or place where an action occurs.
A painting or drawing whose subject is natural scenery such as mountains, rivers, fields, or townscapes.
A physics term for the pulling force transmitted along a string, rope, or surface, or the force resisting being stretched.
A method or system of cultivating crops, such as organic or traditional farming.
A frog — a small jumping amphibian that lives in or near water. Usually written in katakana as カエル, though the kanji {蛙|かえる} also exists.
A powerful enemy or opponent. Very often used figuratively for anything that poses a serious threat or obstacle to a goal or condition.

glosses: prime working age; peak of one's working life
prime of one's working life; peak working years
explanations: The period when a person is at the peak of their energy and productivity at work, typically one's 30s and 40s.
The state of working too much or too hard. Formed from {働|はたら}く (to work) plus the suffix 〜{過|す}ぎ (excess, too much).
Not following the normal or expected pattern. Used especially for unsettled weather and for irregular bodily cycles.
A wish to harm or an intention behind a hurtful act. Most often used in the negative — {悪気|わるぎ}はない — to say that no harm was meant.
A permanent wave — a salon treatment that gives the hair lasting curls or waves. Shortened from English 'permanent (wave)'.
An unspecified span of a few years, typically two to five or so. The prefix {数|すう} means 'several' or 'a number of'.

glosses: range of swing; amplitude; range of variation
range of swing; amplitude; breadth of variation
explanations: The width over which something swings or varies, from one extreme to the other. Used literally for a pendulum's swing and figuratively for the range of someone's moods, performances, or ability.

glosses: price range; range of price movement
explanations: The difference between the high and the low of a price, especially in stock and commodity markets. Composed of {値|ね} (price) plus {幅|はば} (width).
A needle used for hand sewing, with an eye at one end for thread. From {縫|ぬ}う (to sew) plus {針|はり} (needle).
A long needle used for knitting, usually in pairs. From {編|あ}む (to knit) plus {針|はり} (needle).
A barbed hook for catching fish, tied to a fishing line. From {釣|つ}る (to fish) plus {針|はり} (needle, hook).

glosses: to go off the scale; to swing to the limit
to swing past the maximum; to peg the meter; to go off the scale
explanations: Of a needle or gauge, to swing all the way to the end of its scale; figuratively, for a value or feeling to reach an extreme. Intransitive counterpart of {振|ふ}り{切|き}る.

glosses: outside the range; out of scope; out of bounds
outside the range; out of scope; beyond the limits
explanations: Outside a defined range, area, or scope. Composed of {範囲|はんい} (range, scope) plus the suffix {外|がい} (outside).

glosses: points to reflect on; areas for improvement
points for reflection; areas needing improvement
explanations: Aspects of one's own conduct or a project that should be reconsidered and done better. From {反省|はんせい} (self-reflection) plus {点|てん} (point).
Marked by great suffering or a disastrous outcome. From {悲劇|ひげき} (tragedy) plus the suffix 〜{的|てき} (-like, -al).

glosses: the most; the greatest number; highest count
the most; the largest number; highest count
explanations: The greatest in number or frequency. From {最|さい} (most) plus {多|た} (many). The opposite is {最少|さいしょう} (the fewest).
Four children born together from a single pregnancy. From {四|よ}つ (four) plus {子|こ} (child), which voices to ご.

glosses: way of holding; how to hold; grip
way of holding; how to hold something; grip
explanations: The manner in which something is held or gripped. From the verb stem {持|も}ち (holding) plus the suffix 〜{方|かた} (way of doing).
The property of emitting radiation; used attributively to mean 'radioactive'. From {放射|ほうしゃ} (radiation) plus the suffix 〜{性|せい} (property, -ness).

glosses: this fiscal year; this academic year
this fiscal year; this business or school year
explanations: The current {年度|ねんど} — the business or academic year, which in Japan normally runs April 1 to March 31, not the calendar year.

glosses: next fiscal year; next academic year
next fiscal year; next business or school year
explanations: The {年度|ねんど} after the current one — the business or academic year that begins next April in Japan, not simply the next calendar year.

glosses: land route; overland travel; by land
explanations: A route over land, as opposed to by sea or air. Often used adverbially to mean 'by land'. From {陸|りく} (land) plus {路|ろ} (route).

glosses: fashion; trend; the current craze; what's in style
explanations: What is currently popular or in fashion. The noun form of the verb {流行|はや}る (to be popular, to catch on). Often written {流行|はや}り in kanji.

glosses: national defense; defense of a country
explanations: The protection of a nation's territory, people, and sovereignty against external military threats. Covers armed forces, defense policy, budgets, and related institutions.
Reducing a set sum of money such as a fee, salary, budget, or payment. The opposite of {増額|ぞうがく} (increasing an amount). Often used with する as a verb.
Evaluating something again, often leading to a revised, frequently higher, opinion or value. Applies to people, artworks, policies, or assets. Used with する as a verb.

glosses: judge (of a contest); examiner; judging-panel member
explanations: A person who evaluates entries in a competition, contest, or examination and decides on results or scores. Common for contests, auditions, art exhibitions, and qualification screenings.

glosses: hair ornament; hair accessory; hair decoration
explanations: A decorative accessory worn in the hair, such as a clip, comb, ribbon, or flower. Often associated with traditional dress like {着物|きもの} and {浴衣|ゆかた}, but also everyday clips and barrettes.

glosses: automatic ticket gate; fare gate (at a station)
explanations: The automated gate at a train or subway station that passengers pass through by inserting a ticket or touching an IC card. The machine checks the fare and opens or closes the barrier.
A practice exercise in which people rehearse evacuating a building or area safely in case of fire, earthquake, or other emergency. Routinely conducted at schools, workplaces, and public facilities.
Literary works from earlier eras regarded as having lasting value, especially the classical literature of Japan such as Heian-period works. May also refer to the classics of any country.

glosses: popular song; hit song of an era
explanations: A song that is widely popular at a particular time, especially the popular songs of earlier decades. Somewhat dated; the word evokes the popular music of the past rather than current pop.
A person given to daydreaming or unrealistic fancies, often someone whose ideas are impractical. Can be mildly critical (out of touch with reality) or admiring (imaginative).

glosses: activation; invocation; bringing (a power or rule) into effect
explanations: Setting a power, authority, right, or special rule into operation. Used for invoking legal powers and emergency measures, and in games for triggering an effect or skill. Used with する as a verb.

glosses: bundling; selling items together as a set; tie-in sale
explanations: Selling a desirable item only together with a less popular one, or combining products as a set. In commerce, {抱|だ}き{合|あ}わせ{販売|はんばい} (tie-in selling) is a way to move slow stock and is sometimes viewed negatively.

glosses: vegetation; the plant cover of an area
explanations: The collective plant cover of a particular area or region, considered as a whole. A term used in ecology, geography, and environmental science.
The very best or most excellent, especially as awarded in competitions and evaluations. Almost always used attributively with の or in compound award names like {最優秀|さいゆうしゅう}{賞|しょう} (grand prize).
Examining or trying a legal case again. A formal legal term for reopening proceedings to reconsider a matter. Used with する as a verb.

glosses: livestock industry; animal husbandry (as an industry)
explanations: The industry of raising domestic animals such as cattle, pigs, and chickens for meat, milk, eggs, and other products. One branch of agriculture.

glosses: to drink up; to drink it all
to drink up completely; to drink the last of
explanations: To drink something until none is left. The compound suffix {尽|つ}くす adds the sense of doing the action completely, to exhaustion or until nothing remains.

glosses: to forget to write; to leave unwritten
to forget to write (something); to neglect to write down
explanations: To fail to write something because one forgot. Formed from {書|か}く (to write) plus {忘|わす}れる (to forget), following the common 〜{忘|わす}れる pattern of forgetting to do an action.

glosses: dreamy; visionary; given to fanciful ideas
explanations: Describes a person, idea, or mood that is detached from reality, idealistic, or lost in fancy. Can suggest impracticality or, more positively, imaginative idealism. A な-adjective.

glosses: hit rate; accuracy rate; percentage of hits
explanations: The proportion of attempts that hit a target, expressed as a rate or percentage. Used for shooting, sports, predictions, and similar contexts where success is measured against attempts.

glosses: to get separated from; to lose sight of (one's group)
to get separated from; to lose sight of (one's companions)
explanations: To become separated from a group or companion one was with, typically by accident in a crowd or while moving. The person or animal one loses is marked with と or から.

glosses: to switch over; to change over; to be switched
to switch over; to change over (to a new state or mode)
explanations: For a system, display, signal, or mode to change from one state to another. The intransitive counterpart of {切|き}り{替|か}える; the change happens by itself or automatically rather than being done to an object.

glosses: to comb (hair); to run a comb through
to comb (hair); to run a comb or brush through
explanations: To pass a comb or brush through hair to untangle and smooth it. Written {梳|と}かす in kanji, but the kana spelling is far more common in everyday writing.

glosses: to go along; to run down (a surface)
to move along; to run down (following a surface)
explanations: To move along the length of something, using it as a path or support. Often used of liquid (tears, sweat, rain) running down a surface, or of a person making their way along a wall, rope, or ledge. The surface followed is marked with を.

glosses: to blush; to flush (one's face) red
to make (one's face) turn red; to blush
explanations: To cause one's face to redden, typically from embarrassment, shame, or anger. The object is almost always {顔|かお} (face). The intransitive counterpart is {赤|あか}らむ.

glosses: to paste together; to glue together
to paste together; to glue (two things) face to face
explanations: To join two sheets or pieces together by applying adhesive between them, so that their surfaces stick face to face. Common with paper, boards, photos, and layered materials.

glosses: to kick (the ball) into; to kick in
to kick into; to kick (a ball) in
explanations: To send something into a target or enclosed space by kicking. Most often used in sports of kicking a ball into the goal. The destination is marked with に.
Describes a person of keen, well-balanced intelligence who grasps things quickly and judges wisely. A refined, complimentary word, often used of someone admirable rather than merely clever.
Describes handling a matter strictly and fairly by the rules, without bias or leniency. Common in formal contexts such as judging, screening, and examinations where impartiality must be guaranteed.

Describes something that gives an impression of coolness or refreshing breeziness to the eye, such as summer clothing, glassware, or wind chimes. The げ suffix means 'looking/seeming', so it conveys appearance rather than actual temperature.

A mimetic word describing something that is soft, full, and pleasantly rounded — such as well-cooked rice, freshly baked bread, a sun-dried futon, or rounded cheeks. Usually appears as ふっくら(と)する or ふっくらした.

glosses: unavoidably; having no choice but to; inevitably
explanations: Indicates that something is done because circumstances leave no alternative. Almost always appears in the pattern 〜を{余儀|よぎ}なくされる ('be forced to do ~') or 〜を{余儀|よぎ}なくさせる ('force someone to do ~'). Formal, common in news and writing.
A single grain of rice. Also used figuratively as an image of something extremely tiny.

glosses: rainbow colors; the colors of the rainbow; iridescent
explanations: The band of colors seen in a rainbow, or something that shows many shifting colors like a rainbow. Often used with の to modify a noun.

glosses: bedside; the area by one's pillow
explanations: The space right beside the head of a sleeping person, near the pillow. The spot where one keeps things to reach while lying down or where someone sits to attend to a sleeper.

The heating unit that warms the water in a Japanese bathtub, typically fueled by gas. It heats and circulates the bath water, and is often what is meant when a household talks about the bath 'breaking down'.

glosses: cedar forest; grove of cedar trees
explanations: A wood or plantation consisting of Japanese cedar ({杉|すぎ}). Large planted cedar forests are common in Japan and are a major source of springtime pollen.

The ceremonial entrance that top-division sumo wrestlers perform before a day's bouts, in which they step up onto the ring in their decorative aprons. The yokozuna (grand champion) performs a special solo version with attendants.
A person who has been formally invited to an event such as a wedding, party, ceremony, or premiere, as opposed to a paying customer or uninvited attendee.
The thin, hollow needle attached to a syringe, used to inject medicine into or draw blood from the body.
A fence or boundary wall built from wooden boards, traditionally seen enclosing houses and gardens in Japan.

glosses: endangered species; species at risk of extinction
explanations: A species in danger of dying out. A shortened form of {絶滅危惧種|ぜつめつきぐしゅ}, used in conservation and news contexts to refer to plants and animals threatened with extinction.
A small domesticated finch (Lonchura striata domestica) kept as a pet in Japan since the Edo period. Known for its sociable nature and willingness to foster the chicks of other finch species.
The number 10,000,000. Composed of {千|せん} (thousand) + {万|まん} (ten thousand).

glosses: fourth-year student; fourth grader; final-year student (university)
explanations: A student in their fourth year of a school. In elementary school refers to a 9–10-year-old, and in a four-year Japanese university refers to a final-year student preparing for graduation.

glosses: to have no objection; to have no different opinion
explanations: A formal expression used to indicate agreement or non-opposition to a proposal, decision, or arrangement. Composed of {異存|いぞん} (a differing opinion or objection) + ない (none).

glosses: the four classical arts: zither, Go, calligraphy, and painting
the four classical arts of the East Asian scholar
explanations: A four-character compound referring to the four traditional accomplishments of an educated person in classical East Asian culture: playing the {琴|きん} (zither/koto), the board game {棋|き} (Go), {書|しょ} (calligraphy), and {画|が} (painting).
A cord or strap worn around the neck to hold something such as an ID card, key, smartphone, or whistle.
The foot or leg on the right side of the body. As with {足|あし} in general, this can refer to either the foot only or the whole leg depending on context.
Refers to events, relationships, or conditions that occur inside the home or among family members, as opposed to those involving the outside world.
An approximate amount in the range of roughly two to nine million yen (about US$15,000–60,000). Uses the prefix {数|すう} (several) to give a rough estimate rather than an exact figure.
The fifth grade in the {段|だん} ranking system used in martial arts, board games like {碁|ご} (Go) and {将棋|しょうぎ} (shogi), and traditional arts.
In Japanese grammar, a class of verbs whose endings shift across all five rows of the {五十音|ごじゅうおん} table when conjugated. Examples include {書|か}く, {読|よ}む, and {話|はな}す.

glosses: LP record; vinyl album; long-playing record
explanations: A 33⅓ rpm vinyl record, typically 12 inches in diameter, holding around 20 minutes of music per side. Abbreviation of English "long-playing".
A male performer in film, television, or theater. Used mainly in formal contexts and award names where the distinction between male and female performers is relevant.

glosses: one united body; unity; acting as one
explanations: A group acting together with a single purpose. Almost always appears in the fixed pattern {一丸|いちがん}となる ("to become as one") or {一丸|いちがん}となって ("acting as one").

glosses: ritual clapping at a Shinto shrine
explanations: The ceremonial clapping performed when worshipping at a Shinto shrine, typically two claps with the palms slightly offset to produce a clear, resonant sound that calls the attention of the {神|かみ}.

glosses: range of increase; margin of rise; amount of gain
