explanations: The magnitude by which something rises, particularly a price, stock value, temperature, or numerical figure. Often contrasted with {下|さ}げ{幅|はば} (range of decrease).

glosses: cyber-; related to computers and the internet
explanations: A prefix borrowed from English "cyber-", attached to other words to indicate something related to computers, networks, or the internet — especially issues of security and crime.
Any substance or device capable of producing a violent explosion, including bombs, grenades, and industrial blasting agents.
The country in northwestern Europe consisting of England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. In casual speech often used loosely to mean England specifically.
A grammatical category that locates an event in time, marking past, present, or future. A core term in linguistics and language teaching.
A grammatical sentence type that expresses an order, instruction, or request, such as English "Sit down" or Japanese {座|すわ}れ. Used in language instruction and grammar analysis.
A species of plant or animal whose population is small enough to be considered uncommon or at risk. Used in biology, conservation, and environmental policy.
A paradoxical statement or question used in Zen Buddhism (especially the {臨済|りんざい} school) as an object of meditation, aimed at provoking insight beyond ordinary logical thought.

glosses: Obon holidays; summer holiday around the Bon festival
Obon holidays; summer break around the Bon festival
explanations: The mid-August holiday period centered on the Buddhist {お盆|ぼん} festival honoring ancestral spirits, during which many businesses close and people return to their hometowns.
Loanword from English 'long', most often attached to clothing, hair, or other items to indicate a longer-than-standard version. Used as a modifier rather than a standalone noun.

glosses: to load (cargo); to publish; to post
to publish; to print; to post; to carry (an article)
explanations: To place cargo, freight, or goods onto a vehicle, vessel, or surface for transport.
To include text, an image, an article, or information in a publication, on a website, or in another medium.

glosses: to postpone; to extend (a deadline or period)
to postpone; to put off; to defer
to extend; to lengthen (a period of time)
explanations: To move a scheduled event or deadline to a later time.
To make the duration of something — a stay, contract, or deadline — longer than originally planned.

glosses: to measure (time); to plan; to scheme
to plan; to plot; to scheme
explanations: To measure time, duration, or numerical intervals — typically using a clock, stopwatch, or counter.
To devise or attempt something, often with a calculated or strategic intent. In set phrases this sense can carry either neutral or negative connotations.

glosses: to weigh; to measure (volume or weight)
to weigh; to measure (weight or volume)
explanations: To measure how much something weighs or its volume, typically using a scale or measuring vessel.
Goods or baggage being carried or transported. Often appears in compounds such as {荷物|にもつ} (luggage) rather than as a standalone word in modern speech.
Figuratively, a weight of responsibility or worry that one must bear. Used in set expressions about feeling burdened or relieved.

A formally imposed restriction forbidding some activity. Standalone use is largely confined to set expressions; the kanji is more commonly seen in compounds such as {禁止|きんし} (prohibition) or {禁酒|きんしゅ} (abstaining from alcohol).
The on'yomi reading of the kanji {乳|にゅう}, used almost exclusively in compounds referring to milk products or the mammary glands. The standalone kun'yomi form is ちち.

glosses: America; the United States; US (prefix/compound element)
explanations: The on'yomi reading of {米|べい} used as an abbreviated reference to the United States, derived from the historical transliteration {亜米利加|あめりか}. Mostly used in compounds, especially in news writing about US politics, military, and trade.
Describes something that relates to people as a resource, casualty group, or factor — most often used in news, business, and policy contexts. Typically modifies a following noun as {人的|じんてき}＋noun.

glosses: whether or not; whether ... or not
explanations: An embedded-question particle pattern used to indicate uncertainty about whether something is the case. It introduces a yes/no question as the object of verbs like {知|し}る (to know), {分|わ}かる (to understand), {確認|かくにん}する (to confirm), or {決|き}める (to decide).

glosses: China (the country); the People's Republic of China
explanations: The standard Japanese name for China.

The western region of Japan's main island Honshu, comprising Tottori, Shimane, Okayama, Hiroshima, and Yamaguchi prefectures. To avoid ambiguity with the country name, this region is sometimes called {中国地方|ちゅうごくちほう}.
An immensely long, essentially endless span of time, originally from Buddhist cosmology (kalpa). In modern Japanese it almost always appears in the set phrase {未来永劫|みらいえいごう}.
A vehicle with runners that slides over snow or ice, used for transport or play. Sometimes written with the kanji {橇|そり}, but the kana form is much more common in everyday writing.
A grammatical term for a sentence that expresses negation — in Japanese, typically marked by ない, ません, or じゃない. The opposite of {肯定文|こうていぶん} (affirmative sentence).

glosses: complete denial; total negation; flat rejection
explanations: A categorical denial of all of something — a claim, a person's value, a possibility, or a group of options. Often used as {全否定|ぜんひてい}する 'to deny completely' or {全否定|ぜんひてい}される 'to be totally rejected'.
The act or state of denying one's own value, abilities, identity, or past. Used in psychological, philosophical, and everyday contexts, often with a negative connotation of low self-esteem.
Organized work aimed at protecting something vulnerable — wildlife, the environment, cultural heritage, animals, or people. Common in NGO and government contexts.
Sheets of paper dyed in various colors, used for origami, school crafts, and decoration. Typically sold in square sheets in packs of mixed colors.

glosses: place one returns to; return destination
place where one is going back to; return destination
explanations: The address or location someone is heading home to — used in shipping forms, travel arrangements, and questions about where someone is staying. Compound of {帰|かえ}る (to return) + {先|さき} (destination).

glosses: hot spring resort area; spa town
explanations: A locality known for its hot springs, typically with multiple inns, bathhouses, and tourist facilities centered on bathing.

glosses: low doorway; small wicket door; crawl-through door
explanations: A small, low door set within or beside a larger gate or wall, low enough that a person must stoop or duck to pass through. Common in traditional Japanese architecture, tea houses, and temple gates.

glosses: right next to one's ear; close to the ear
explanations: The area immediately beside someone's ear. Typically used in expressions about whispering, shouting close by, or sounds heard from very near.
The activity of growing crops, especially through tilling the soil. Often used in historical, anthropological, or formal contexts rather than for modern industrial farming.
A circular control that is rotated to make a selection — historically on telephones, and still on radios, safes, ovens, and other equipment. Also used as a verb (suru) for dialing a phone number.

Persimmons that have been peeled and air-dried until they shrivel and develop a sweet, chewy texture coated with a natural white frost of sugars. A traditional Japanese preserved food and seasonal winter treat.

A decorated evergreen tree (real or artificial) displayed indoors as part of Christmas celebrations. Adopted from Western tradition and widely seen in Japanese homes, schools, and commercial spaces during December.
A mark or stain left by blood, typically on clothing, a floor, or another surface. Especially common in crime, forensic, and medical contexts.
An object that has been stolen, viewed especially from a legal or law-enforcement perspective. Knowingly buying, selling, or possessing such items is itself a crime.

glosses: to sell off; to dispose of by selling
to sell off; to sell out; to dispose of (a large quantity) by selling
explanations: To sell goods—often a large quantity, leftover stock, or illicitly obtained items—until they are gone. Implies skillful or aggressive distribution, and is frequently used for clearing inventory or fencing stolen items.

glosses: shrewd; not missing a trick; sharp
shrewd; not missing a trick; sharp; calculating
explanations: Describes someone who is alert, calculating, and never lets an opportunity slip — especially when it comes to gaining advantage or profit. Often carries a mildly negative or wry tone.
The outer husks of buckwheat seeds, separated from the grain during milling. Traditionally used in Japan as a pillow filling because they are light, firm, and breathable.

glosses: sleeping in peace; resting easy; freedom from worry
explanations: A tall, raised pillow. The literal meaning, much less common in everyday speech than the idiomatic use.
An idiom meaning to sleep soundly and without anxiety, by extension to be free of worry. Used especially in the expression {高枕|たかまくら}で{寝|ね}る/{眠|ねむ}る.
White, lightning-bolt-shaped paper strips attached to sacred ropes ({注連縄|しめなわ}), wands ({御幣|ごへい}), and other Shinto ritual objects to mark off purified or sacred space.

The imaginary line at roughly 180° longitude that marks where the calendar date changes. Almost always appears in the full form {日付変更線|ひづけへんこうせん}; the short form is used only after the full term has been established.
The physical field produced by moving electric charges and time-varying currents, encompassing both electric and magnetic components. A core concept in classical electromagnetism.
The field of gravitational force produced by mass-energy in classical mechanics and general relativity. Describes how a mass at a given point experiences gravitational acceleration.
A device that shows or signals a state or direction. Most commonly refers to a vehicle's turn signal, but also covers gauges and indicator lamps in machinery.

glosses: sound of an explosion; blast; loud bang
explanations: The noise produced by an explosion or sudden violent burst. Commonly used in news reports, witness accounts, and descriptions of accidents or fireworks.
The sharp report made by a firearm being discharged. Often used in news reports, crime descriptions, and witness accounts of hearing distant gunfire.

Differences or unevenness among items that are supposed to be similar — in measurements, product quality, individual abilities, performance, etc. Common in technical, statistical, and everyday contexts.

A volcano that has not erupted in recorded history but is not considered extinct and may erupt again. In modern geology this classification is largely obsolete in favor of {活火山|かっかざん}/non-active, but the word remains common in general usage.

glosses: fee; bill; charge for a service or item
explanations: Suffix attached to nouns to indicate the cost, fee, or bill associated with that thing or service.

glosses: for the sake of; in order to; because of
for the sake of; for the benefit of; in order to
because of; due to; as a result of
explanations: Indicates a purpose or beneficiary. Attaches to nouns (with の) or to dictionary-form verbs to express the goal or reason for an action.
Indicates a cause or reason, typically for an unintended or negative outcome. Often used with past-tense verbs.
Archaic and literary first-person pronoun, surviving in modern Japanese almost exclusively in fixed idioms. Refers to the self, especially one's own desires or will.
Suffix attached to a noun or adjective stem to describe a person's inborn nature, temperament, or physical constitution. Distinct from 〜{性|せい}, which forms abstract -ness/-ity nouns.
Suffix attached to a noun or stem to indicate transformation into the state expressed by the base word. Forms abstract nouns and, with する, action verbs meaning 'to turn into X'.
Suffix attached to a noun to form a word naming a category of physical objects or substances. Common in formal, technical, and legal vocabulary.
Prefix attached to a noun to mean 'the entire' or 'all of'. Common in formal and journalistic vocabulary expressing comprehensive scope.
Attaches to a quantity word to mean 'every one' of the group counted, including both or all members without exception. The set must already be specified in context.
Suffix attached to a noun to form a word for a person who specializes in or is committed to that field. Equivalent to English -ist, -ian, or 'expert in'.

glosses: precisely because; all the more because
explanations: Compound particle attached to a clause to express that the following outcome or feeling is intensified or particularly fitting because of the stated reason. Combines the limiting particle だけ with cause-marker に.
Literary first-person pronoun referring to oneself, mainly preserved in proverbs, classical writing, and a small set of formal expressions about self-reflection.
A literary expression meaning 'a hundred battles' or, more broadly, 'many encounters or contests'. Used almost exclusively in fixed phrases and compounds.
Suffix attached to a noun to mean the charge or payment for that service or thing. Especially common for transport fares, rent, and labor wages.

Used with の to mark something as 'real', 'actual', or 'by blood'. Appears in a small set of common patterns including biological-family terms and rhetorical phrases that contrast the actual with the apparent.

glosses: happiness; blessing; bounty (of land or sea)
bounty; produce (of the sea or mountains)
explanations: Literary word for happiness or good fortune. Rare in everyday speech but common in formal writing, classical poetry, and fixed expressions.
The natural bounty yielded by the sea or mountains, used in the fixed expressions {海|うみ}の{幸|さち} (seafood) and {山|やま}の{幸|さち} (mountain produce).
Suffix attached to a noun to name a specific match, contest, or campaign. Common in sports, board-game titles, military history, and political races.
Suffix attached to a noun to mean the raw material, lumber, or substance used for something. Common in construction, cooking, and manufacturing vocabulary.
By extension, a person regarded as a useful asset or human resource, as in {人|じん}{材|ざい} (human resources) and {逸|いつ}{材|ざい} (an outstanding talent).
The visual rear portion of a picture, photograph, or scene — what lies behind the main subject.
The circumstances, history, or context underlying an event, decision, or person. Often used to explain why something happened.

glosses: due to; by means of; according to
due to; caused by; resulting from
by; by means of; through (a method or means)
explanations: Attaches to a noun to indicate the cause or origin of an event. The cause is presented as the agent or reason for the result that follows.
Indicates the means, method, or instrument by which an action is performed.
Attributes information to a source. Typically used in news writing or formal reports.
Very formal adverb expressing sincere or heartfelt emphasis. Common in business apologies, thank-yous, and ceremonial speech.

Standard first-person plural pronoun. Polite enough for most situations: classroom, workplace, and public-facing speech. Inclusive when the listener is part of the group; otherwise refers to the speaker and others.
Suffix attached to a noun to name a certified or licensed professional. Implies the field requires a formal qualification or examination.
Indicates that something cannot be done or is impossible. Most commonly used as a suffix attached to a noun (especially Sino-Japanese stem) to mean 'un-V-able' or 'impossible to V'.

glosses: precisely because; it is exactly because
explanations: Compound particle that emphatically asserts the reason for something. Combines the cause-marker から with the emphasis particle こそ, conveying 'this and no other is the reason'.
A garden or grounds designed for recreation and play. Rarely used on its own in modern Japanese; almost always appears as part of {遊園地|ゆうえんち} (amusement park).

glosses: faction; school; sect; group sharing a position
explanations: A group of people sharing a position, ideology, style, or affiliation. Used both as a standalone noun and very often as a suffix attached to a name, stance, or trait.
Used as a modifier to indicate that an action, skill, or attitude is directed toward or involves other people. Almost always attached to another noun rather than standing alone.

glosses: for the first time in (a span of time)
for the first time in; after an interval of
explanations: Suffix attached to a time expression to say that something has happened for the first time after that span. Highlights the gap between the previous occurrence and the present.
Ordinal counter attaching to a number plus {年|ねん} to mark the Nth year since something started, such as a job, a marriage, or any ongoing situation.
States that a claim, rumor, or accusation has no basis in fact. Used almost exclusively in the set phrase {事実|じじつ}{無根|むこん} "completely without basis."

Prefix attached to nouns to mean either "pure / unmixed" (free of impurities or qualifications) or "net" (after subtracting other amounts). The financial "net" sense is common in business and accounting.
Suffix attaching to an -ism noun ({主義|しゅぎ}) to label someone who holds or champions that ideology, principle, or way of life. The English equivalent is the "-ist" ending.
Refers to an unspecified small number of countable things — typically more than two but not many. Functions as a noun-like quantity expression and can stand on its own or modify a noun with の.

glosses: melodic style; way of singing; intonation
melodic style; way of singing; characteristic intonation
explanations: The distinctive way a singer or speaker shapes a melody or vocal line — the melodic contours, ornaments, and timing that give a performance its personal flavor. Often used for traditional Japanese music and for distinctive speech delivery.
A person who has placed high enough in a contest or competition to receive a prize or award. Includes not only the top winner but anyone awarded a recognized rank or honor.

glosses: the three Cs (closed spaces, crowded places, close-contact settings)
explanations: A public-health term coined in Japan during the COVID-19 pandemic for the three conditions believed to raise infection risk: {密閉|みっぺい} (poorly ventilated spaces), {密集|みっしゅう} (crowded places), and {密接|みっせつ} (close-range contact). "Avoid the {三密|さんみつ}" was the central slogan.

A volcano considered no longer capable of erupting. The traditional classification opposed {死火山|しかざん} to {活火山|かっかざん} (active) and {休火山|きゅうかざん} (dormant), though modern Japanese geology has largely abandoned this three-way split.

glosses: loss on difference; exchange loss; trading loss
loss arising from a price or rate difference; exchange loss
explanations: An accounting term for a loss that arises from the difference between purchase and sale prices or between exchange rates at different times. Most often appears in compounds such as {為替|かわせ}{差損|さそん} (foreign exchange loss).

glosses: densely; lushly; thickly (of trees or vegetation)
explanations: Describes vegetation growing thickly enough to block out light and create a shadowy atmosphere. Almost always paired with verbs of growing or covering.
A pencil with a colored wax or pigment core, used for drawing, coloring, and marking. Usually sold in sets of various colors.
The amount of time a person spends sleeping, typically measured per night. A common topic in discussions of health, work-life balance, and study habits.

glosses: to tie down; to bind tightly to
to tie down; bind firmly to (something)
explanations: To fasten something or someone tightly to a fixed object with rope, string, or restraints. Also used figuratively for being held in place by obligations, rules, or circumstances.
A wall built from precast concrete blocks, commonly used around houses and properties in Japan. Frequently discussed as an earthquake hazard because poorly reinforced walls can collapse.
A wall or boundary fence built of stones, often surrounding a traditional house, temple, or castle grounds. Older and more decorative than concrete block walls.

glosses: to run all the way; to finish running
to run all the way (to the end); to finish running a distance
explanations: To run from start to finish without stopping, completing the entire intended distance. Emphasizes seeing the run through to its end rather than the speed or quality of running.

The native Japanese word for ten, the final element in the {一|ひと}つ, {二|ふた}つ, {三|みっ}つ ... {十|とお} counting sequence. This series stops at ten; from eleven onward, Japanese uses the Sino-Japanese system ({十一|じゅういち}).

glosses: several billion yen; billions of yen
explanations: An indefinite sum on the order of a few billion yen. Combines {数十|すうじゅう} (several tens) with {億円|おくえん} (hundreds of millions of yen). Common in news about large business deals, investments, or losses.
Short for {職業安定所|しょくぎょうあんていじょ}, a public employment office where job seekers register, receive counseling, and apply for unemployment benefits. Commonly known as ハローワーク.
The dead body of an animal or insect, viewed as a physical object. For humans, it is harsh and clinical; the neutral term is {遺体|いたい}.
A licensed technician who inspects, repairs, and maintains vehicles, aircraft, or other machinery. The suffix {士|し} indicates a certified professional.
The classical Japanese dance form that developed from kabuki and noh, performed in kimono to {三味線|しゃみせん} or {長唄|ながうた} music. Often shortened to {日舞|にちぶ} when spoken among practitioners.

glosses: several kinds; several types; a few varieties
explanations: An indefinite small number of distinct categories, typically two to nine. Combines {数|すう} (several) with {種類|しゅるい} (kind, type). Used adverbially with の to modify a noun.

glosses: the whole town; all over town; throughout the town
explanations: The entire town or every part of it. The suffix {中|じゅう} attaches to time/place nouns to mean "throughout" or "everywhere within." Note that {町中|まちなか} (read differently) means "downtown" instead.

The closing portion of the current month — roughly the last week or so, or the final day depending on context. Combines {今月|こんげつ} (this month) with {末|まつ} (end). Standard in business and scheduling contexts.
A horrific event that causes major loss of life or suffering, especially an accident or violent incident. Formal and emotive; common in news headlines.

glosses: to befall; to fall upon; to come down on
to fall onto; to come down on (rain, ash, dust)
to befall (misfortune, trouble); to fall upon (a person)
explanations: Of small particles or liquid, to fall from above and land on something. Used for rain, snow, ash, leaves, and the like.
Figuratively, of misfortune or trouble, to come down on someone unexpectedly. The affected person is marked with に, and the trouble is the grammatical subject.
A professional who takes photographs or films video. Unlike English "cameraman," the Japanese word covers both still photographers and video camera operators of any gender.

glosses: infected person; patient with an infection
explanations: A person who has contracted a contagious disease, especially a viral or bacterial infection. Standard term in medical and public health reporting.
The craft of making decorative or practical objects from wood, especially as a traditional art form. Encompasses joinery, carving, lacquered wares, and similar techniques.
Belonging to the national government, especially in reference to land, railways, forests, or enterprises. Almost always used attributively as {国有|こくゆう}の or in compounds like {国有地|こくゆうち}.
A piece of lumber sawn into a square or rectangular cross-section, used as a structural member in carpentry and DIY work. The opposite of round timber ({丸太|まるた}).
A person or business that buys and sells lumber. The suffix {商|しょう} marks a merchant or commercial dealer in the named goods.
A historic district in northeast Tokyo, famous for {浅草寺|せんそうじ} temple, the Nakamise shopping street, and a traditional {下町|したまち} atmosphere. One of Tokyo's most-visited sightseeing areas.
A district in northeast Tokyo centered on Ueno Park and Ueno Station, known for its museums, zoo, cherry blossoms, and the lively Ameyoko market. A major transit hub for trains to northern Japan.
A district in Sumida Ward, eastern Tokyo, known as the home of sumo. Site of the {国技館|こくぎかん}, where the Tokyo grand sumo tournaments are held three times a year.

glosses: before (it becomes too late); while still
explanations: Attached to a verb, adjective, or noun + の, marks the period while a condition holds. The action in the main clause should be completed before that condition changes.
With a negative verb (〜ないうちに), means 'before (something happens).' Implies the speaker should act before the state changes.

glosses: people of old; ancient sages; ancestors
people of old; the ancients; ancient sages
explanations: People who lived in the distant past, often viewed as a source of wisdom. Used in literary and reflective contexts, especially when quoting old sayings or comparing the present with the past.

glosses: two doors down; two houses away
two doors down; two houses over
explanations: The second house from one's own, counting along a row of houses or shops. Used to locate a neighbor or nearby establishment.

glosses: faculty of agriculture; school of agriculture
explanations: The division of a university that teaches and researches agriculture, including crop science, animal science, forestry, and food science.

glosses: as; in proportion to; along with (a change)
explanations: Marks a parallel change: as the first situation progresses, a second situation changes accordingly. Both clauses describe gradual, related shifts.
A duration of 100 years. Used both literally for measured time and figuratively for 'a very long time' in set expressions.

glosses: to discuss; to argue; to debate (formal)
to discuss; to argue; to debate
explanations: To take up a topic and present reasoning, opinions, or analysis about it. The formal, classical-flavored variant of {論|ろん}じる; common in academic and editorial writing.

glosses: fearfulness; terror; dreadfulness; how frightening (something) is
explanations: The quality or degree of being frightening. Formed by attaching the noun-forming suffix さ to the i-adjective {恐|おそ}ろしい (frightening, terrible).
The quality of being charming, sweet, or endearing. Formed from the i-adjective {可愛|かわい}らしい (cute, lovely) with the noun-forming suffix さ.
The customs, arts, beliefs, and lifestyle practices associated with Japan. Used in both casual references and academic discussion.

glosses: don't need; don't want; no thanks
explanations: The plain negative of {要|い}る (to need, to be required). Used colloquially to decline an offer or to say something is unnecessary.
Even larger than {巨大|きょだい} (huge). The prefix {超|ちょう} (super-, ultra-) intensifies the size beyond ordinary scale.

glosses: to come to (do); to become able to
to come to (do); to start (doing) — change in behavior or state
explanations: Marks a change to a new habitual action or state. With a plain present verb, it expresses that a person has come to do something they did not used to do.
With the potential form of a verb, it expresses newly gained ability.

glosses: so; well, that being the case; with that
well, that being the case; so; with that (set expression marking a wrap-up)
explanations: A set transition phrase used to draw a conclusion based on what has just been said, or to wrap up a topic and move on. Common at the end of an explanation or before saying goodbye.
A word used with a precise, specialized meaning within an academic discipline, profession, or art form. Often opaque to non-specialists.

glosses: childish; immature; unbecoming of an adult
explanations: Describes behavior that is petty, irritable, or undignified in a way that is inappropriate for a grown-up. Often used self-critically or as a mild rebuke.

glosses: back cover (of a book or magazine)
explanations: The cover at the back of a book, opposite the front cover. Often carries the barcode, blurb, or a closing illustration.
The academic study of law — statutes, legal principles, court decisions, and their theory. Refers to the field as a discipline, not to law itself.

glosses: outdoors; the open air; outside (a building)
explanations: The space outside the doors of a building. Formal and literary; common in written instructions, signage, and academic prose.
A recognized type or breed of dog, distinguished by physical traits and ancestry (e.g., Shiba, Poodle, Labrador).
The number of live births per a given population over a set period, usually expressed per 1,000 people or as the average number of children per woman. Central to demographic discussion.

glosses: to read and compare; to compare by reading
to read and compare; to read several texts side by side
explanations: To read two or more texts (articles, books, drafts, translations) in order to compare them. The objects compared are typically marked with を or と.

glosses: to re-cover; to replace (paper, fabric); to re-paper
to re-cover; to replace a stretched surface (paper, fabric, leather)
explanations: To remove an existing paper, cloth, leather, or screen surface and replace it with a fresh one. Common with shoji screens, wallpaper, sofa upholstery, and tatami covers.
An error or fault on one's own part — something for which one should accept responsibility. Most often appears in the fixed expression {非|ひ}を{認|みと}める (to admit one's fault).
The act of writing books or scholarly works, or the written work itself. Formal; primarily used for books, academic writing, and the profession of writing.

glosses: a bit more; somewhat more; on the larger side
explanations: An amount or quantity that is slightly larger than usual or than what is strictly required. The suffix め attaches to adjectives or quantity words to mean 'on the X side.'

glosses: to distort; to twist; to warp
to distort; to twist; to warp (something)
explanations: To bend or contort the shape of something out of its normal form. Also used figuratively for distorting facts, expressions, or the truth.
The feeling or degree of being embarrassed, ashamed, or shy. Formed by attaching the noun-forming suffix さ to the i-adjective {恥|は}ずかしい.

glosses: pressure point; the right spot; the key point
the right spot; the key point; what makes (someone) tick
explanations: A specific point on the body used in acupuncture, acupressure, and massage to relieve tension or pain. Often written in katakana.
Figuratively, the precise point that hits the mark — what triggers laughter, what works, or the essential point of a topic. Common in the idiom ツボに{嵌|は}まる.

glosses: to crack; to become cracked; to split
explanations: For a surface or material to develop visible cracks, especially from dryness, age, or stress. Common for skin, walls, ceramics, and dried earth.

glosses: to rub against; to chafe; to become worn
to rub against (something); to chafe; to become worn
explanations: For two surfaces to rub against each other, often resulting in friction, irritation, or wear. The intransitive counterpart of {擦|こす}る (to rub something).
Women's shoes with tall, narrow heels. A loanword from English 'high heel.' Usually used in the singular form even when referring to a pair.

glosses: way of walking; gait; how to walk
explanations: The manner in which someone walks, or instructions for how to walk. Formed from {歩|ある}く (to walk) + the suffix 〜{方|かた} (way of doing).

To draw the eyebrows together, typically expressing displeasure, worry, or concern. Almost always used with {眉|まゆ} as its object. Written {顰|ひそ}める in older texts, but the kanji is rare and the verb is normally written in hiragana.

glosses: bite; dental occlusion; alignment of upper and lower teeth
meshing; engagement (of gears or interlocking parts)
explanations: The way the upper and lower teeth fit together when the mouth is closed. A common dental term.
By extension, the fit or engagement of any two parts that mesh together, such as gear teeth. Also used figuratively for how two parties or arguments line up.

glosses: first volume; upper volume (of a two- or three-part work)
explanations: The first volume of a book or work published in two or three parts. The pairing is {上巻|じょうかん} / {下巻|げかん} for two-part works, or {上巻|じょうかん} / {中巻|ちゅうかん} / {下巻|げかん} for three.

glosses: second volume; last volume (of a two- or three-part work)
explanations: The final volume of a book or work published in two or three parts. The pair of {上巻|じょうかん} (first volume).
A formal or trade term for leather and animal hides, especially in industrial and manufacturing contexts. The everyday word for leather is {革|かわ}.

glosses: to ripple; to become choppy; to be disturbed
(for a water surface) to ripple; to become choppy
to be disturbed; to be in turmoil (figuratively)
explanations: For a body of water to develop waves or ripples, typically due to wind or other disturbance.
Used figuratively for emotions, atmosphere, or a situation becoming agitated or unsettled, like a calm surface being disturbed.

glosses: attendee; guest (at a ceremony such as a wedding or funeral)
explanations: A person present at a formal ceremony such as a wedding, funeral, or memorial. Used in formal contexts; the everyday word for a guest is {ゲスト} or {お{客|きゃく}さん}.

glosses: to draw; to paint; to depict
explanations: To produce a picture or image with lines, brushes, or a pen. The everyday reading of {描|か}く; the kanji is the same as {描|えが}く, but かく is more colloquial and used for concrete acts of drawing.
An image of what is currently shown on a computer or smartphone screen. A loanword from English; the abbreviated form スクショ is very common in casual conversation.
The act of appearing and disappearing — often unexpectedly or sporadically. Typically used for wild animals, criminals, ghosts, or anything that turns up in a place from time to time without warning.
A person who is cowardly, unfair, or sneaky — someone who avoids confronting things directly or who uses unfair tactics. A strongly insulting term.

glosses: food and drink; food and beverages
explanations: A collective noun for things to eat and drink. Common on signs and in formal contexts; in casual speech, {食|た}べ{物|もの}と{飲|の}み{物|もの} is more typical.

glosses: large room; shared (hospital) room; communal dressing room
explanations: A spacious room shared by multiple people. Most often refers to a shared hospital ward, but also used for the communal dressing room of junior actors or for any large multi-person room.
Tiny grains of iron-bearing mineral (mostly magnetite) found mixed with ordinary sand on beaches and riverbeds. Magnetic, and historically used in Japan as a raw material for tatara iron-making.
A pointed length of wood, metal, or concrete driven into the ground as a support, marker, or foundation.
The small, dimpled ball used in the game of golf. A compound of ゴルフ (golf) + ボール (ball).

glosses: bento shop; bento restaurant; takeout lunch shop
explanations: A shop that makes and sells boxed lunches ({弁当|べんとう}) for takeout. Common near train stations, offices, and busy streets in Japan.
A faithful copy of an original object, especially of artwork, historical artifacts, sports jerseys, or trophies.

glosses: medical certificate; doctor's note; diagnostic report
explanations: An official document issued by a physician stating a patient's diagnosis. Often required by employers, schools, or insurance companies to verify illness or injury.
People connected by blood, marriage, or other ties — including extended family and in-laws. More formal and broader than just blood relatives.

glosses: new idea; new design; utility model (patent)
new idea; new design; novel proposal
explanations: A newly devised idea, plan, or design. Also used in patent law as part of {実用|じつよう}{新案|しんあん} (utility model), a category of intellectual property covering minor inventions.
In Japanese grammar, a sentence containing one main clause and at least one subordinate clause. Contrasts with {単文|たんぶん} (simple sentence) and {重文|じゅうぶん} (compound sentence).

glosses: main clause (grammar); main text; operative part of a ruling
operative part of a court ruling; main text
explanations: In grammar, the principal clause of a complex sentence, which can stand alone as a sentence. Contrasts with {従属節|じゅうぞくせつ} (subordinate clause).
In legal usage, the portion of a court judgment stating the actual ruling (acquittal, sentence, damages awarded), as distinct from the reasoning that supports it.
A pricing system in which the manufacturer sets the retail price and retailers cannot discount it. In Japan, this is legally permitted for certain categories such as books, newspapers, and music CDs.
Living, freshly cut bamboo, distinguished by its bright green color and flexibility. Used for crafts, garden fences, and traditional decorations.
A long, straight section of bamboo used as a pole — for laundry, fishing, vaulting, or supporting plants. Often written {竹竿|たけざお} with kanji.
Indicating that a product was manufactured in Japan. Often used as a quality marker, since 'Made in Japan' has strong positive connotations both domestically and abroad.
Indicating that a product was manufactured in China. Frequently seen on consumer goods sold in Japan.

glosses: made of metal; metal- (as a material modifier)
explanations: Indicating that an object is made of metal. Used to specify material, often in contrast to {木製|もくせい} (wooden) or {プラスチック製|プラスチックせい} (plastic).
The geographic region of Central Asia, typically including Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan.
Three times some quantity, value, or size. Formed with the counter {倍|ばい} (times).
Used to refer to the fifth day of a calendar month.
A span of five days, often in the form {五日間|いつかかん}.
Designating something modeled on Western (especially European or American) conventions, in contrast to {日本式|にほんしき} or {和式|わしき} (Japanese-style).

glosses: Japanese-style; done in the Japanese manner
explanations: Designating something done in a distinctly Japanese way, in contrast to {西洋式|せいようしき} or {洋式|ようしき} (Western-style).
An imposing power or presence that inspires awe, respect, or fear in others. Usually associated with rulers, leaders, or institutions of authority.

glosses: heaven; sky; the heavens; Heaven (as deity)
Heaven; providence; fate (as a personified force)
explanations: The sky above, or the heavens in a poetic or religious sense. Often invoked in literary, religious, or proverbial contexts.
An impersonal higher power or fate that governs human affairs — comparable to 'Heaven' in classical Chinese thought. Used in set phrases about destiny and divine will.

glosses: bamboo cutter; person who gathers bamboo
explanations: A person whose occupation is cutting and gathering bamboo. Almost always encountered today in the title of the classical tale {竹取物語|たけとりものがたり} ('The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter').
Attaches to nouns to indicate type, lineage, or category. Used for ethnic/national descent, family lines, scientific systems, and stylistic categories of fashion, music, or character.
Suffix attaching to nouns to form the name of a formal written document, certificate, or record. Common in business, legal, and administrative vocabulary.
Suffix attaching to a noun to name an organized exhibition or art/cultural show. Used widely in titles of museum, gallery, and trade-show events.

glosses: for a period of; over the span of
explanations: Suffix attaching to a time-unit phrase to express duration ('for X days/weeks/years'). Makes the time expression explicitly a span rather than a point in time.
Suffix attached to a number, yen amount, or percentage to express a price reduction. The rendaku form of {引|ひ}き (pulling, subtracting).
Suffix attaching to a noun to form the name of a historical field or written history. Common in academic, journalistic, and book-title vocabulary.
Suffix attaching to a noun to mark a part or installment of a book, course, video series, or themed collection.
A house or building constructed with only one floor, no upper stories. Often used in real estate listings and discussions of housing preference.
A building constructed with five stories. A standard example of the 〜{階|かい}{建|だ}て counter pattern, which describes how many floors a building has.

glosses: ten people; a group of ten
explanations: Ten as a count of people. Uses {人|にん}, the standard counter for people, attached to {十|じゅう} (ten). Note: 1 person is {一人|ひとり} and 2 people is {二人|ふたり} (irregular), but 3 onward use ~{人|にん}.

glosses: the three wise monkeys (see-no-evil, hear-no-evil, speak-no-evil)
explanations: The famous trio of monkeys covering their eyes, ears, and mouth, representing the maxim 'see no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil'. Most strongly associated with the carving at Nikko's Tosho-gu shrine.

The outer edge or boundary of an object, typically the strip of material running along the perimeter. Used for the fabric border of tatami mats, the rim of dishes, the edges of pools and roofs, and similar perimeter areas.

glosses: land price; cost of land; price paid for land
explanations: The monetary cost or price of a piece of land, especially in the context of purchase or rental. Distinguished from the cost of the building itself.

glosses: to mingle; to be mixed in (people, group)
to mingle; to join in; to be mixed in
explanations: Intransitive verb meaning one element joins or blends into a group. Uses {交|まじ}わる-related kanji to emphasize joining people or distinguishable elements, rather than the chemical-style blending of {混|ま}ざる.

glosses: to mix in; to add (people, distinguishable items)
to mix in; to include; to let join
explanations: Transitive verb meaning to add or include something within a larger group, while keeping it distinguishable. Uses the {交|まじ}わる kanji to emphasize joining or including, especially for people or visibly distinct items.

glosses: three mon (old coin); a pittance; cheap
three mon (old copper coin unit); a pittance; trifling amount
explanations: Literally 'three mon' — three units of an old copper coin worth almost nothing. Now used figuratively in idioms to mean 'a trifle', 'a cheap thing', or 'a small but real benefit'.
Legal-jargon noun meaning 'causing bodily injury'. Attaches to other criminal-act nouns to form aggravated offense names — e.g., 'robbery resulting in injury'.
Casual contraction of ではない, the negative form of the copula だ/である. Attaches to a noun or na-adjective to express 'X is not Y'.
With rising or emphatic intonation, expresses confirmation, surprise, or mild disagreement — 'isn't it!', 'don't you think?'. Similar to a tag question in English.

glosses: all; entirely (used as prefix or in compounds)
explanations: A long pole with a flat blade at one end, used to row a boat by pulling against the water. From English 'oar'.
From English 'all'. Used as a prefix in compounds like オールラウンド (all-around), and casually to mean 'staying out / staying up all night' as in {オール}する.

glosses: Japanese era calendar; Japanese imperial calendar
explanations: The traditional Japanese way of counting years based on imperial reign names ({元号|げんごう}), e.g., {令和|れいわ} 8 for 2026. Used alongside the Western calendar ({西暦|せいれき}) in official documents and daily life.
An official order or decree banning a specific activity, behavior, or item. Issued by governments, organizations, or individuals (often a parent or boss) with authority over the subject.
The quantity of particles—most commonly pollen—dispersed into the air over a given area and time. Frequently reported in weather forecasts during {花粉症|かふんしょう} (hay fever) season.
Mimetic word for the repeated motion of light, bouncy hops or jumps—typical of rabbits, frogs, small children, and similarly springy movement. Often paired with {跳|は}ねる, {跳|と}ぶ, or {飛|と}び{回|まわ}る.
Rice that has been processed to remove the bran layer at the factory, so it does not need to be rinsed before cooking. Saves water and time but slightly more expensive than regular white rice.

The edible seed of the {銀杏|いちょう} (ginkgo) tree, eaten in autumn. Has a distinctive smell when fresh but a delicate, slightly bitter flavor when roasted, and is a classic ingredient in {茶碗蒸|ちゃわんむ}し and other Japanese dishes.

glosses: personal data leak; leak of personal information
explanations: The unauthorized release of personally identifiable information—names, addresses, ID numbers, account details—often as the result of a security breach, lost device, or insider misuse. A staple topic of corporate apologies and news headlines.

A variety of peach with pale, cream-colored flesh and a delicate, sweet flavor. The most common type of {桃|もも} sold in Japan, prized for its softness and aroma; contrasts with {黄桃|おうとう} (yellow peach).

Chestnuts roasted with sugar—classically the Tianjin ({天津|てんしん}) variety from China, with peelable shells and a soft, sweet flesh. Sold ready-to-eat at supermarkets, convenience stores, and street stalls in autumn and winter.

glosses: chestnut in its spiny husk; close-cropped (spiky) hair
explanations: A chestnut still enclosed in its prickly green outer burr ({毬|いが}). The fully ripe form that drops from the tree before being opened.
By metaphor, a very short hairstyle that resembles the bristly burr of a chestnut. Often used affectionately for young boys.

glosses: sweetened chestnut paste; mashed sweet potato with chestnuts
explanations: A traditional Japanese sweet dish made by mashing sweet potatoes (or yams) with sugar and mixing in whole boiled chestnuts. The bright yellow color symbolizes gold, so it is a customary New Year's ({お正月|おしょうがつ}) {おせち料理|おせちりょうり} dish wishing for wealth in the coming year.

A large, showy flowering plant in the peony family, valued for its full, fragrant blooms in late spring and early summer. The herbaceous counterpart to {牡丹|ぼたん} (tree peony). Its dried root is also a classic ingredient in Chinese and {漢方|かんぽう} medicine.
A single box of something. Formed by attaching the {一|ひと}- prefix to the counter {箱|はこ} (boxes). The counter {〜箱|はこ} is used for tissues, fruit, sweets, cigarettes, and similar boxed items.

A professional performer of {落語|らくご}, the traditional Japanese art of comic storytelling. The performer kneels alone on stage in a kimono, narrates a long humorous story, and plays all characters by changing voice and direction of gaze.

A short comic skit performed by one or more comedians in character, typically with a clear setting (school, office, restaurant) and a punchline. Distinguished from {漫才|まんざい}, which is performed by stand-up duos as themselves.

A rapid exchange of words, lines, or musical phrases between two parties—a comedy duo's banter, the call-and-response of a festival chant, or the give-and-take in a negotiation. Emphasizes rhythm and reaction more than the literal content of what is said.

The quality of being interesting, fun, or amusing. Formed by attaching the abstract-noun suffix 〜さ to the い-adjective {面白|おもしろ}い. Refers to the inherent attractiveness or interest-value of something — a book, a sport, an activity, a person's talk.

A person who plays the guitar, usually professionally or seriously. From English "guitarist." Used for any genre — rock, jazz, classical, flamenco — though it tends to imply a band or solo performer rather than a casual hobbyist.

glosses: playing and singing at the same time (esp. solo)
explanations: A solo performance in which one person both plays an instrument (typically guitar or piano) and sings. The performer accompanies themselves, with no separate vocalist or backing band.
A small woodwind instrument shaped like a flute but pitched one octave higher, producing a bright, piercing sound. Common in orchestras and marching bands. From Italian {piccolo} ("small").

A simple woodwind instrument with a whistle-style mouthpiece and finger holes. Standard equipment in Japanese elementary and junior high school music classes, where students learn pieces on the soprano ({ソプラノ}) or alto ({アルト}) recorder.

Classical music written for a small ensemble (typically 2–9 players), one player per part, intended to be performed in a small room rather than a concert hall. Includes string quartets, piano trios, and similar groupings.

A person who plays the drum kit, especially in a rock, pop, jazz, or similar band. From English "drummer." Usually does not refer to players of traditional Japanese drums like {太鼓|たいこ}, who are called {太鼓奏者|たいこそうしゃ}.

A large classical orchestra of around 70–100 musicians from the strings, woodwinds, brass, and percussion sections, organized to perform symphonies and other orchestral works. The standard formal name for an orchestra in Japanese; appears in the official names of most professional groups (e.g., NHK{交響楽団|こうきょうがくだん}).
A person who plays the flute, especially professionally. From English "flutist." Usually refers to classical or orchestral performers rather than casual hobbyists.

glosses: gidayū; narrative chanting for bunraku puppet theater
explanations: A style of dramatic narrative chanting accompanied by shamisen, developed in the late 17th century by Takemoto Gidayū. It is the vocal element of bunraku puppet theater and is also performed independently as a concert form.

glosses: nagauta; long-song shamisen genre for kabuki
explanations: A traditional Japanese vocal genre sung to shamisen accompaniment, developed in the Edo period as music for kabuki dance scenes. Now also performed independently in concert settings.

glosses: komusō; mendicant Zen monk who plays shakuhachi
explanations: A Zen Buddhist monk of the Fuke sect who wandered while playing the {尺八|しゃくはち} shakuhachi flute as a form of spiritual practice. Recognizable in period dramas by a large basket-like straw hat ({天蓋|てんがい}) that covers the whole head.

Refers to a philharmonic orchestra, typically as part of the proper name of an ensemble (e.g., {東京|とうきょう}フィルハーモニー{交響楽団|こうきょうがくだん}). From German "Philharmonie." Often shortened to フィル in casual reference.

Competitive gymnastics performed on apparatus such as the vault, parallel bars, rings, horizontal bar, balance beam, and uneven bars. Distinguished from rhythmic gymnastics ({新体操|しんたいそう}) and general floor-based exercise.
The act or quality of producing foam or bubbles, as with soap, shampoo, beer, or whipped ingredients. Often used to describe how well a product foams up.

Unwanted bacteria or microbes, especially the kind that contaminate food, water, or surfaces and may cause spoilage or illness. The {雑|ざつ} ("miscellaneous") implies unspecified, undesirable microorganisms.

glosses: sprinkling water on the ground (to cool an area or settle dust)
explanations: The traditional practice of sprinkling water on streets, gardens, or entryways during hot weather. The evaporating water cools the surroundings and also keeps down dust. Common in summer and often associated with traditional shops, ryokan entrances, and tea ceremony preparation.

glosses: mountain closing (end of climbing season); mine closure
end of the climbing season; closing of a mountain to climbers
mine closure; shutting down of a mine
explanations: The official end of the period during which a mountain (especially a popular peak like {富士山|ふじさん}) is open to climbers. Marks the seasonal cutoff after which trails, huts, and facilities are closed for winter.
The closing down of a mining operation, whether temporarily or permanently. Often appears in economic and historical contexts.
A narrow wooden veranda attached to the outside of a traditional Japanese house, projecting beyond the eaves and so exposed to rain. Contrasts with the covered, interior-side {縁側|えんがわ}.
A tree that has lived for many years, typically with a thick trunk, gnarled branches, and a sense of long history. Often used reverently for trees in temple grounds, shrines, or scenic spots.

glosses: sacred tree (at a shrine or temple)
sacred tree at a shrine or temple
explanations: A tree on the grounds of a Shinto shrine (or sometimes a Buddhist temple) that is regarded as sacred, often believed to house or attract a divine spirit. Typically marked off with a {注連縄|しめなわ} (sacred rope) tied around the trunk.

glosses: to cut down (a tree); to fell
explanations: To cut through the base of a tree (or similar standing object) so that it falls over. Used both for forestry work and for removing individual trees in gardens or construction sites.
A small enclosed room or booth equipped with a shower but no bathtub. Common in business hotels, gyms, and compact apartments where a full bathroom is impractical.
An absorbent robe worn after bathing, typically made of toweling material. Mostly seen in hotels, spas, and Western-style home settings.
Cleaning something thoroughly with water or another liquid, often in medical, industrial, or hygienic contexts. Also used as the label for the bidet/rinse function on a washlet toilet.

A small device installed in many Japanese women's restrooms that plays a continuous flushing sound on demand. Designed to mask the sounds of using the toilet without actually flushing water, saving water that would otherwise be used to provide the same cover.
A person of outstanding ability in a particular skill or art—especially performing arts, sports, board games, or crafts. Conveys real admiration; not used casually.
A book that gathers several short stories, usually by a single author. May also refer to a collection of short films or other brief works.
The act of pressing clothes or fabric with an iron to remove wrinkles. Can be used on its own as a noun or with する as a verb.
Silk fabric or fiber. Loanword from English, used especially in the context of fashion, lingerie, and modern products; the native word {絹|きぬ} is more traditional.

glosses: phase; stage (of a project, process, or development)
explanations: A distinct stage in a process, project, or sequence of events. Most common in business, engineering, and project-management contexts.
Casual loungewear or athletic clothing made from thick, soft fleece-backed fabric. Refers to the garment (top or bottom) or to the fabric itself. Often used for at-home or workout wear.
A tailored jacket, typically single-breasted, worn as part of a school uniform or as semi-formal/business-casual wear. In Japan, strongly associated with school uniforms.

glosses: cut-and-sewn top; knit top; T-shirt-style top
explanations: A top made by cutting and sewing knit fabric — covering T-shirts and other casual knit tops that are not a buttoned shirt or a sweater. A Japanese-coined fashion term (from English "cut and sewn").

glosses: food (esp. in compounds and brand-style names)
explanations: A hood attached to a jacket, parka, or hoodie. Pulled up over the head against rain or cold.
Food, used mostly in fixed compounds such as ファストフード, ペットフード, ベビーフード. Rare on its own.

glosses: place one has gone out to; destination when out; where one is while out
place one has gone out to; destination when out; while out
explanations: Where someone is when they're out of the house or office — the workplace they've visited, a café, a station, etc. Often appears with で to mean "while out and about."
The leading player on a sports team, or by extension the most reliable person in a group. Most commonly used for the starting pitcher in baseball.
The ace in a deck of playing cards.

glosses: missing person; person whose whereabouts are unknown
explanations: A person whose whereabouts have become unknown — used in news reports about disasters, accidents, runaways, and police searches.
A dog trained to work with police — for tracking suspects or missing people, detecting drugs and explosives, and other operational duties.
Alzheimer's disease, a progressive form of dementia. Usually appears in the full form アルツハイマー{病|びょう} but is frequently shortened to just アルツハイマー in speech and headlines.

glosses: group home; small-scale residential care facility
explanations: A small residential facility where a few people with dementia, disabilities, or other care needs live together with support from staff. Distinct from a large nursing home in scale and atmosphere.
A recording of the heart's electrical activity, used to diagnose heart problems. Refers both to the test itself and to the printed/displayed trace.
Casual abbreviation of デジタルカメラ (digital camera). Refers specifically to a standalone digital camera, as distinct from a smartphone camera.
A camera that records images electronically rather than on film. Used for the full category, from compact point-and-shoots to mirrorless and DSLR cameras.
A camera designed for recording moving video. Typically refers to handheld consumer camcorders used for events like school recitals or family trips.
A condition in which the heart cannot pump blood effectively enough to meet the body's needs. A serious illness and a frequent cause of death listed in news reports and obituaries.
Chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart muscle, typically due to narrowed coronary arteries. Often triggered by exertion or stress.

glosses: phone photo; phone snapshot; photo sent by phone
explanations: A photo taken with a mobile phone, especially a casual one shared with friends. Originally short for {写真|しゃしん}メール (photo message), the term still feels somewhat dated and is mostly used by older speakers.

glosses: work of art; art object; artwork (esp. as an item)
explanations: An item recognized as a work of art — paintings, sculptures, ceramics, lacquerware, and the like. Treats the work as a physical object that can be owned, displayed, insured, or stolen.

glosses: for emergency use; emergency (used as a modifier)
explanations: Designating equipment, supplies, or facilities meant to be used in an emergency rather than in normal operation. Usually attaches to another noun with の or as a prefix-like element.

glosses: shawl; wrap worn over the shoulders
explanations: A rectangular or triangular piece of fabric worn loosely over the shoulders or upper body for warmth or as a fashion accessory.
A tube-shaped fabric piece worn around the neck for warmth. Unlike a scarf, it has no loose ends and is pulled on over the head.
The physics concept of light waves oscillating in a single plane. Commonly seen in compounds describing products that filter or use polarized light.
A wearable device worn on the wrist that connects to a smartphone and tracks fitness data, notifications, and time.
A short necklace worn tightly around the neck, often made of velvet, leather, beads, or chain.
A long-barreled firearm with grooves cut inside the barrel to spin the bullet for accuracy. Used in hunting, military operations, and target shooting.
The numerical result of a game, match, test, or assessment. Used for sports scores as well as test results like TOEIC.
Something limited to family members, close friends, or members of the same group. Often used to describe gatherings or matters not shared with outsiders.
An emperor who has abdicated the throne. The formal title for a Japanese emperor after retirement, reinstated in 2019 when Emperor Akihito abdicated.

glosses: time card; punch card for tracking work hours
explanations: A paper or digital card used to record the times an employee starts and ends work. Inserted into a time clock that stamps the time.

glosses: clocking in/out; stamping the time on a record
explanations: The act of recording one's start or end of work time, traditionally by stamping a time card and now often by scanning a card or using a smartphone app.

glosses: letter of resignation (formal request to resign)
explanations: A formal document submitted to request resignation. Phrased as a request (not a declaration), it can be withdrawn before the employer accepts it.

glosses: to restrain; to pin down; to apprehend
explanations: To physically subdue and hold a person, typically a fleeing or violent suspect, to prevent their movement or escape.
An enclosed structure of bars or wire for confining animals or, by extension, people. Used for zoo animals, livestock, and figuratively for confinement.

glosses: to come to an end; to be exhausted; to perish
to come to an end; to finish; to be exhausted
(as suffix) to do completely; to ~ utterly
explanations: For a long process, struggle, or one's energy to reach a complete end. Has a literary, definitive feel — stronger than {終|お}わる.
Attached to the conjunctive form of another verb, indicates the action has been carried out to the point of exhaustion or complete depletion. Often written 〜はてる in kana.

glosses: to close up completely; to shut tight
to close up completely; to keep shut
explanations: To close doors, windows, or curtains completely and leave them that way, often for an extended period. Implies sealing a space off from the outside.
To wake a sleeping person by physically shaking them — typically the shoulder. Implies more vigor than simply calling their name.

glosses: to make known; to make widely known
to make known; to inform; to make widely known
explanations: To cause something to become known to many people. A formal, somewhat literary verb often used in declarations, announcements, or when describing how a person or thing gained recognition.
Modifies verbs of refusing, denying, or maintaining a position to express that someone will not budge or compromise. Carries a sense of inflexibility — sometimes admiring, often critical.
A person walking along a street or path. Often used in news reports about incidents involving uninvolved bystanders or witnesses on the road.
Describes performing an action that looks heavy or difficult as if it were no effort at all. Often used for lifting, carrying, or accomplishing demanding feats.
Waste materials produced by metabolism in the body, such as urea, carbon dioxide, and toxins, that need to be eliminated. Common in health, fitness, and beauty contexts.
Casual slang for サングラス (sunglasses), formed by reversing the order of the syllables. Used in informal speech and writing.

Classical or literary word for war and armed conflict, especially associated with the samurai and pre-modern eras. In modern Japanese it appears mainly in historical writing, period dramas, set phrases, and idioms.
A mathematical expression or formula — a written combination of numbers, variables, and operators. Used in mathematics, physics, chemistry, and other technical fields.
A formal ceremony or ritual occasion. Often appears as a suffix on the names of specific ceremonies (e.g. {結婚式|けっこんしき} wedding ceremony, {卒業式|そつぎょうしき} graduation ceremony).

glosses: all ages; ancient and modern times
all ages; ancient and modern; throughout history
explanations: Literary noun combining {古|こ} (old) and {今|こん} (now), referring to all eras from antiquity to the present. Almost always used in fixed expressions or titles rather than as a free-standing word.

glosses: Tokyo University; the University of Tokyo (abbreviation)
explanations: Common abbreviation for {東京大学|とうきょうだいがく}, the University of Tokyo. Japan's most prestigious public university and a shorthand for academic elite status.

glosses: feel; sense; impression; quality of being ~
explanations: Suffix attached to nouns and na-adjective stems to mean 'a feeling/sense of ~' or 'the quality of being ~'. Highly productive in both formal writing and casual speech, especially in product descriptions, reviews, and impressions.

glosses: is nothing but; is none other than
is nothing but; is none other than; is precisely
explanations: Fixed pattern used to emphatically identify one thing as the sole or true essence of another. Frequently used in formal writing, essays, and speeches to make a definitive claim.

glosses: guest of honor; VIP guest; invited guest
explanations: A formally invited guest at a ceremony, reception, or official event — especially one whose status warrants special acknowledgment. Used in announcements, programs, and seating arrangements at weddings, graduations, and official functions.

glosses: during a trip; while traveling; on a trip
explanations: The period while someone is on a trip. Formed from {旅行|りょこう} (trip) + {中|ちゅう} (in the middle of). Used to specify when something happens or to explain someone's absence.
Heat originating from inside the Earth, especially the heat used as an energy source via volcanic and hot-spring activity. In Japan, often discussed as a source of renewable power.
The nutritive substances contained in food, soil, or other materials. More technical than {栄養|えいよう} alone — it refers to the constituent nutrient components rather than nutrition as a whole concept.
Biological species — the basic unit of taxonomy. Also used more loosely as a noun or counter for 'kind' or 'type', especially in technical writing.

glosses: hotspot; concentrated area of activity or risk
explanations: From English 'hotspot'. Used in several technical fields: biodiversity hotspots (areas with concentrated species), Wi-Fi hotspots, geological hotspots, and figuratively for areas of concentrated activity or danger (infection hotspots, crime hotspots).
From English 'spotlight'. Refers literally to a focused stage light, and figuratively to public attention or media focus on a person or topic.

A mental health condition characterized by alternating episodes of mania ({躁|そう}) and depression ({鬱|うつ}). The current medical term is {双極性障害|そうきょくせいしょうがい}, but {躁鬱病|そううつびょう} remains common in general usage.

glosses: way of teaching; teaching method; teaching style
explanations: The manner in which something is taught — covering approach, sequence, and pedagogical style. Formed from {教|おし}える + {方|かた} (way of doing).

glosses: monthly salary system; salaried payment system
explanations: A wage system in which an employee receives a fixed sum each month, as opposed to hourly or daily wages. The standard arrangement for full-time {正社員|せいしゃいん} in Japan.
Wages paid on a weekly basis. Less common in Japan than monthly salaries, but used in some part-time and short-term arrangements, especially in retail and food service.

glosses: usable in both sun and rain; all-weather
usable in both sun and rain; all-weather (umbrella, etc.)
explanations: Describes an item — most often an umbrella or parasol — that can be used both as a sunshade and for rain. Standard product-category label in Japanese shops.
Describes a material that is thicker than the standard version — typically used for fabrics, paper, cardboard, and ceramic dishware. Usually appears as {厚手|あつで}の + noun.
The part of the leg just below the kneecap, or — most commonly — the length of clothing or footwear that reaches to just below the knee. Used in clothing measurements and fashion descriptions.
A vertical line of broken threads in stockings, pantyhose, or tights — what English speakers call a 'run' (US) or 'ladder' (UK). Also used as a する verb: {伝線|でんせん}する 'to get a run/ladder.'
A product label and ingredient description meaning 'containing no added salt.' Common on butter, nuts, crackers, and processed foods marketed to people on low-sodium diets.
A thick blended drink made from fruit or vegetables, often with yogurt, milk, or ice. The term and the drink itself spread in Japan from the late 1990s as part of the health-food boom.
A small, cylindrical charcoal cooking brazier traditionally made of diatomaceous earth ({珪藻土|けいそうど}). Used in homes and restaurants for grilling fish, meat, and vegetables one piece at a time.
A product label meaning 'salt has been added.' Most commonly seen on butter, where {有塩|ゆうえん}バター is the default supermarket variety; contrasts with {無塩|むえん} (unsalted).

glosses: game of tag; game of chase
explanations: A children's chasing game, or any reciprocal chasing activity. Formed from {追|お}いかける (to chase) + the suffix っこ that turns the verb into a playful reciprocal action.
The decision-making body of a Japanese company composed of its {取締役|とりしまりやく} (directors). Also refers to the actual meeting at which directors deliberate and vote on company matters.
A conference attended by participants from multiple countries — used for academic, business, diplomatic, and intergovernmental meetings alike.
The hinged cover over a car's engine compartment. The primary meaning of the word in modern Japanese — covering both UK 'bonnet' and US 'hood'.
The act of turning something into a legal or institutional requirement. Frequently used in news and policy contexts: マスク{着用|ちゃくよう}の{義務化|ぎむか} (mandating mask-wearing), etc. Functions as a する verb.

Porcelain produced in and around the town of {有田|ありた} in Saga Prefecture. Japan's first true porcelain, with a 400-year tradition, known for fine white clay and intricate cobalt-blue or polychrome decoration.

A thin strand or cable of metal. Most often refers to flexible steel cable used in construction, vehicles, and brakes, as well as wire used in jewelry, art, and crafts. ⚠️ For an electrical wire, Japanese uses {電線|でんせん} or コード, not ワイヤー.

glosses: reserve army; (figurative) at-risk group; pool of potential cases
at-risk group; borderline cases; pool of potential X
explanations: Literally, military reserves — soldiers held back from active deployment but available if needed.
Figurative and now far more common: a group of people not yet diagnosed or classified as X, but on track or at risk to become so. Standard in health and social-policy reporting.
A flat pad placed on a desk under a computer mouse to provide a smooth tracking surface and protect the desktop.

glosses: to hang down; to dangle; to droop
explanations: For a thin or flexible object — a rope, hair, branch, sleeve, drop of liquid — to extend downward under its own weight. Intransitive.

glosses: wheel; rim (of a car or bicycle)
explanations: The metal wheel structure — usually the hub and rim onto which a tire is mounted. Distinct from タイヤ (the rubber tire itself).
The front wheel(s) of a vehicle — most often a car, motorcycle, or bicycle. Contrasts with {後輪|こうりん} (rear wheel).
The rear wheel(s) of a vehicle — most often a car, motorcycle, or bicycle. Contrasts with {前輪|ぜんりん} (front wheel).
A physically attractive woman. Slightly literary or formal compared to neutral {美人|びじん}; often used in set phrases, news headlines, and entertainment-industry contexts.

glosses: delicate, understated facial features; soft, gentle look
explanations: A modern slang term for a face with soft, fine, low-contrast features — pale skin, slim eyes, and a generally subdued appearance. Coined as a contrast to {醤油顔|しょうゆがお} (classic Japanese features) and {ソース顔|そーすがお} (deep, sharp features).
Reflecting the style, ideas, or technology of the present age. Often used to contrast something with traditional or old-fashioned forms.
Suffix attached to nouns to mean 'including ~' or 'with ~ included'. Most often seen in prices ({税込|ぜいこみ}, {送料込|そうりょうこみ}), but also used for general bundling.
The percentage at which a tax is levied. Applies to consumption tax, income tax, corporate tax, and any other tax with a rate.

glosses: tax not included; before tax; pre-tax
explanations: Indicates that a displayed price does not include consumption tax. Often appears on menus, signs, and packaging, especially after tax-display rules changed.

glosses: having few children; declining birthrate (in compounds)
having few children; few children; declining birthrate (in compounds)
explanations: {少|しょう} (few) + {子|し} (children). Appears almost exclusively as a bound element in compounds such as {少子化|しょうしか} (declining birthrate) and {少子高齢化|しょうしこうれいか} (declining birthrate combined with an aging society).

Productive prefix meaning 'super-' or 'ultra-'. In compounds it conveys exceeding the normal or expected level, while in casual speech it works as an intensifier roughly equivalent to 'super' or 'really'.
A chemical substance with a pH below 7, the opposite of an alkali (base). Used as a general noun and as a suffix in names of specific acids ({硫酸|りゅうさん} sulfuric acid, {塩酸|えんさん} hydrochloric acid).
A substance with a pH above 7, the opposite of an acid. Used in chemistry, in product descriptions (alkaline batteries, alkaline water), and in nutrition discussions of alkaline-forming foods.
Describes a person who is quiet and unsmiling, often appearing to be in a bad mood. Used as an adverb (with する) or to describe a personality.

glosses: to be offended; to feel annoyed; to bristle
to feel stuffy; to be muggy
explanations: To suddenly feel angry or annoyed in response to someone's words or behavior. The reaction is usually short and visible on the face rather than expressed openly.
Used of air or atmosphere — to feel oppressively warm, humid, or stuffy. Less common than the first sense.
Describes a soft, watery object that quivers or jiggles when moved, like pudding, jelly, or skin with a healthy moist look. Often used positively in food and cosmetic contexts.
Describes a small, rapid trembling of the body or limbs, typically caused by cold, fear, anger, or muscle fatigue.
Describes a texture that is soft, yielding, and pleasant to press — like a baby's cheeks, soft toys, or memory foam. Almost always used positively or affectionately.

glosses: to melt; to dissolve in the mouth; to be enchanted
to melt; to dissolve in the mouth
to be entranced; to be melted (by pleasure, beauty, or affection)
explanations: Of food, especially fatty or rich food, to soften and melt smoothly — often used as a sign of high quality.
Figurative use: to be so charmed, moved, or relaxed that one feels one's body or mind is melting. Common in descriptions of music, faces, hot springs, and romantic moments.

glosses: dry and unkempt; frizzy; disheveled (especially of hair)
explanations: The sound or motion of dry, light material moving in the air — a bird's wings flapping, papers being shuffled, or a curtain rustling in a breeze.
Describes hair, fur, or grass that is dry, rough, and lacks moisture or care. Almost always negative — implies neglect or poor condition.

glosses: clingy; unable to let go; pathetic about lingering attachment
explanations: Describes someone whose behavior visibly shows they cannot accept that something is over — most often a relationship, a missed chance, or a past defeat. Strongly negative and often pejorative.

The period during which a war is being fought. In Japanese contexts most often refers to World War II (specifically the wartime years from the late 1930s to 1945), but can also describe any ongoing war.
A person skilled in formulating strategies, whether in business, politics, sports, or warfare. Carries a positive connotation of foresight and skill at planning.
The act of building a feature into software or hardware so it actually functions. In a hardware context, it can also mean physically mounting a component. Frequently used as a する verb.
A high-speed, always-on internet connection, in contrast to older dial-up service. The term covers fiber, cable, and high-speed mobile connections.
A five-a-side variant of soccer played on a smaller, hard court with a low-bounce ball. Popular in Japan as a casual after-work and weekend sport.

Refers to football codes other than soccer — most often American football, but also Australian rules football or rugby league depending on context. The bare word サッカー is preferred for soccer in Japanese.

headword: コストパフォーマンス
explanations: The ratio of what you get to what you pay. Used positively (good value) or negatively (poor value), and applied to products, services, or experiences. Commonly abbreviated as コスパ.
Yoga practiced in a room heated to around 35–40°C and kept at high humidity, intended to promote flexibility and sweating. Widely offered as a class-based studio service in Japan.
Stretchy, sweat-wicking clothing designed for yoga practice. The term covers both studio-only outfits and athleisure pieces worn casually.
A practice facility where golfers hit balls into a netted or open field. In Japan, often multi-tiered, with stations along the edge of a city or suburb.
A construction finish in which poured concrete is left visible rather than covered with paint, tile, or other cladding. Often associated with modernist architecture.
A legal right to use a club's facilities, especially a golf course, resort, or fitness club. In Japan often a transferable asset that can be bought, sold, or inherited.
A camera that develops and prints a photograph immediately after the picture is taken. In Japan, Fujifilm's Instax line is the dominant brand.
The team's main catcher, who plays the position most regularly. The prefix {正|せい} ("main; regular") contrasts with backup or rotating players.

glosses: valvular heart disease; heart valve disease
explanations: Any disorder of the heart's valves in which they fail to open or close properly. Most often the full phrase is {心臓弁膜症|しんぞうべんまくしょう}, but {弁膜症|べんまくしょう} alone is common.

An older Japanese clinical term for dementia. Officially replaced in 2004 by {認知症|にんちしょう} because the kanji {痴|ち} carries strongly pejorative connotations. Now mostly seen in pre-2004 writing or as a slur.

glosses: sense of orientation (to time, place, person)
orientation; awareness of time, place, and person
explanations: The cognitive ability to know what day it is, where one is, and who is around. A standard clinical assessment item; its loss ({見当識障害|けんとうしきしょうがい}) is a hallmark of dementia and other cognitive impairment.
Extremely rapid and out-of-control price inflation — typically monthly rates well above 50%. The full form is ハイパーインフレーション but the clipped form is far more common.
A sustained drop in general price levels in an economy, the opposite of inflation. The full loanword is mostly used in formal economic writing; in everyday speech, the clipped form デフレ is preferred.
Of an experience, defeat, or treatment that destroys one's pride or dignity. Implies a public or socially-visible loss of face, not just private embarrassment.

glosses: to torment; to afflict; to plague
explanations: To cause persistent mental or physical suffering. Usually the subject is an emotion, illness, or memory, and the object is a person — often in the passive ({苛|さいな}まれる).
An interest rate expressed on a per-year basis. The standard unit for advertising loan and deposit rates in Japan.

glosses: to escape from; to break out of; to get out of
to escape from; to break out of; to extricate oneself from
explanations: To get free of a difficult situation, state, or place. The thing one escapes is marked with から or, more commonly in this formal register, を. Often used about crises, hardships, or constraining categories.
A severe, prolonged economic downturn marked by bank failures, plunging prices, and mass unemployment. Standard term in economic history for events like the 1929 crisis.
A sudden burst of fear and chaos that grips a crowd or an individual. Mostly used in the phrase {恐慌|きょうこう}{状態|じょうたい} (a state of panic).
The philosophical position that life, morality, or knowledge has no inherent meaning, value, or foundation. The standard Japanese translation of the European philosophical term.
Describing a feeling, atmosphere, or outlook that everything is meaningless or hollow. Less technical than {虚無主義|きょむしゅぎ}{的|てき} — applies to moods, gazes, and worldviews, not just philosophy.
Paid items, currency, or upgrades bought from within a smartphone game or app after the initial install. Almost always appears as part of the longer phrase アプリ{内課金|ないかきん}.
A building with many stories, especially as a category. The 〜{建|だ}て suffix indicates how many stories a building has; {高層建|こうそうだ}て groups together all the tall ones.
