A formal Sino-Japanese prefix marking that something has already occurred or is already in place. Common in administrative, legal, and academic writing.
Doing or being something ahead of others, either in order of action or in arrival. The standard polite phrase when leaving the office early is お{先|さき}に.
Referring back to a recent earlier time. Often replaces this morning, yesterday, or last week when the exact time is irrelevant.
The て form of {向|む}かう (to face, to head toward), used like a postposition: ～に{向|む}かって 'toward, facing, addressed at'. Marks the direction of motion, of attention, or of speech.

glosses: to do completely; to go and do; to mess up
to finish doing; to get done; to go ahead and do
to mess up; to blow it; to do something one regrets
explanations: やる plus the ～てしまう aspect marker. The neutral reading is completion: 'get the thing done', often with a sense of resolving to do it now rather than later.
The same form takes on a negative emotional reading depending on context, especially in the past tense (やってしまった): 'I did it (and now I regret it)'. Contracted to やっちゃう / やっちゃった in casual speech.

glosses: head slightly bowed; looking down a little
(with one's) head slightly tilted down; looking down a little
explanations: A posture or facial set in which the head is bowed somewhat — often expressing shyness, sadness, or thoughtfulness. Common as a description of demeanor in narration.

glosses: a mountain of; huge piles of; an enormous amount of
a mountain of; piled high; an enormous amount of
explanations: A simile likening a large quantity to a mountain. Used with concrete things stacked up ({書類|しょるい}, {洗濯物|せんたくもの}) and with abstract ones (work, complaints).

glosses: to come to a punchline; to wind up predictably; to find a fitting end
to reach a punchline; to wind up with a fitting (often funny or ironic) ending
explanations: Used of stories, situations, or chains of events that resolve in a way that feels like the punchline of a joke — often the predictable or ironic ending the listener could see coming.

glosses: to grow accustomed through practice; to get used to doing
to grow accustomed to (something) through repeated learning or practice
explanations: A compound verb combining {習|なら}う (to learn) with {慣|な}れる (to get used to). Describes reaching a state where a skill or routine feels natural after enough practice.

glosses: to turn awkward; to become stiff or stilted
to turn awkward; to become stiff (in movement or speech)
explanations: The adverbial form of the i-adjective ぎこちない (awkward, clumsy) plus なる. Describes a shift from natural to unnatural — often in conversation, body language, or movement when someone gets self-conscious.

glosses: just by; merely from; simply because
just by; merely from; with only
explanations: The limit particle だけ followed by で. Marks a single action, condition, or quantity as sufficient cause for what follows: 'just by doing X, Y happens' or 'with only X, Y is enough'.
A casual masculine exclamation of resolve, satisfaction, or psyching oneself up. Used the moment a decision is made, a task is started, or a victory is scored.

glosses: having a stomachache; hilarious enough to hurt
having a stomachache; one's stomach hurts
so funny it hurts; gut-bustingly funny
explanations: Casual i-adjective form of 'stomach hurts', built from {腹|はら} (stomach) + {痛|いた}い (painful). Used as a direct complaint about an upset stomach.
Colloquial figurative use, said when something is so hilarious that one's stomach actually aches from laughing. Equivalent to English 'my stomach hurts from laughing'.

glosses: one or the other; either one; one of (two things)
one or the other (of two options); either one
explanations: Combines どちら (which of two) with the indefinite particle か. Picks out an unspecified one from a pair — usually translated as 'either one', 'one of the two', or 'whichever'.

glosses: either is fine; whichever; I don't mind either way
either is fine; whichever; I don't care which
explanations: Casual version of どちらでもいい. The speaker has no preference between two options. Tone ranges from genuinely easy-going to annoyed (couldn't care less), depending on delivery.

glosses: to be silly; to slip up; to be vacant-witted
to be silly; to look foolish; to slip up in an absent-minded way
explanations: Describes acting in a way that misses the point or looks dopey. Most often used in the past form {間抜|まぬ}けた as a noun modifier ({間抜|まぬ}けた{顔|かお} 'a vacant face').

glosses: to exaggerate a story; to embellish; to add embellishments
to exaggerate a story; to add embellishments; to dramatize
explanations: Idiom literally meaning 'to attach a tail and fins'. Used when a story or rumour gets enlarged each time it's passed along, with details added that were not in the original.

glosses: let alone; much less; even more so
let alone; much less; (and) even more so
explanations: Literary conjunction used after a milder case to introduce a stronger one. 'If even X is the case, then certainly Y too' — typically marking the second item as a more extreme example of the same point.

glosses: handwriting with personal quirks; idiosyncratic penmanship
explanations: Handwriting whose individual style — slant, loops, oversized characters — makes it noticeably personal, often at the cost of legibility. Carries a slightly negative or apologetic nuance.
A night when the moon is shining brightly enough to light the surroundings. Often used in literary or poetic contexts.

glosses: to grow dark at dusk; to be in decline; to look pensive
to grow dark at dusk; for twilight to fall
to be in decline; to be past one's prime
to look lost in thought; to space out wistfully
explanations: For the sky to dim as the sun sets. Literary or poetic; in everyday speech {暗|くら}くなる is more common.
Figurative: for a person, career, or era to be fading toward its end. Often used self-deprecatingly or about an industry.
Colloquial: to sit absentmindedly with a pensive, melancholy expression. Common in casual speech and manga.

glosses: to wash up on shore; to crash against; to surge in
to wash up on shore; to beat against; to break (of waves)
explanations: For waves to roll in and strike the shore, rocks, or a boat. Also used figuratively for crowds or emotions surging forward.
Wood that has been carried along by a river or washed up on a shore. Often used decoratively in aquariums and gardens.
A harbor with natural conditions favorable for ships — deep water, shelter from wind and waves, and safe access. Often appears in geography and history discussions.
A disease of the tissues surrounding the teeth, including the gums and bone. Caused by plaque buildup and can lead to tooth loss if untreated.
Medication taken to induce or maintain sleep. In Japan most types require a prescription.
The nausea and vomiting some pregnant people experience, typically in the first trimester. Despite the English name, it can occur at any time of day.

glosses: severe degree; serious level (esp. of illness or disability)
explanations: A noun used attributively (with の) to qualify illnesses, injuries, or disabilities as severe. Standard in medical and welfare contexts.

glosses: peashooter; pea gun (toy that shoots beans)
explanations: A simple toy gun, traditionally bamboo, that fires small beans or pellets. Mostly encountered today in the idiom {鳩|はと}が{豆鉄砲|まめでっぽう}を{食|く}ったよう.
A black cricket native to Japan, famous for the clear, bell-like sound the males produce in late summer and early autumn. Sometimes kept as a pet for its song.
The activity of catching and preserving insects, traditionally a popular summer hobby for Japanese children, often as a school break project.
A climbing vine whose large white flowers open in the evening. Its fruit is used to make {干瓢|かんぴょう} (dried gourd strips, often eaten in sushi).

glosses: field bindweed (Calystegia japonica); related Calystegia species
explanations: A creeping vine with pale pink, trumpet-shaped flowers that open during the daytime. Common as a wildflower along roadsides and field edges in Japan.

glosses: kudzu vine (Pueraria montana); the plant itself
explanations: A vigorous climbing vine native to East Asia. One of the {秋|あき}の{七草|ななくさ} (seven autumn flowers) in Japan; the root is harvested for food and medicine.
A fine white starch made from the root of the kudzu plant. Used in traditional Japanese sweets and to thicken sauces. Sometimes labeled in English as "kuzu".
A thin, ropy edible seaweed (Cladosiphon okamuranus and related species). Famous as a specialty of Okinawa, where it is widely cultivated.

glosses: Japanese tea (typically green tea); Japanese-style green tea
explanations: Tea produced and prepared in the Japanese style — almost always green tea ({緑茶|りょくちゃ}), in contrast to Chinese tea ({中国茶|ちゅうごくちゃ}) or black tea ({紅茶|こうちゃ}).
A small mesh strainer used to filter tea leaves when pouring brewed tea. Sometimes built into the spout of a {急須|きゅうす} (Japanese teapot).

glosses: vinegar-miso dressing (miso mixed with vinegar and sugar)
explanations: A classic Japanese dressing made by mixing miso, vinegar, and sugar (often with mirin). Used on simmered greens, seafood, and {和|あ}え{物|もの} (dressed dishes).

glosses: small fish; small fry (used as food)
explanations: Small fish such as anchovies, sardines, and whitebait, often eaten whole and prized for their calcium content. Also a general term for any small fish.
A traditional seasonal festival held on May 5, originally celebrating boys' growth and health. Now a national holiday under the name {こどもの日|こどものひ} (Children's Day).
A beach made up of pebbles or small stones rather than sand. Contrasts with a sand beach ({砂浜|すなはま}).
An intercom system installed at the front door of a home or apartment, often with audio and/or video, used to speak with visitors before opening the door.
Synthetic material used for clear plastic sheets, paints, and fibers in clothing. From English "acryl(ic)."
A unit of digital information storage equal to 1,000 gigabytes (or 1,024 GB in binary). Also functions as a counter when paired with a number.
A unit of volume equal to one thousandth of a liter. Used as both a noun and a counter after numerals.
An animal whose body temperature varies with the surrounding environment, such as reptiles, amphibians, and fish.
A kitchen or laboratory tool with a fine mesh used to separate fine particles from coarser ones, especially for sifting flour or straining liquids.
The thick, slightly sticky consistency of a sauce, soup, or stew, typically produced by starch or reduction. A desired texture in many Chinese-style and Japanese dishes.
A formal or technical term for the potato. Common in agricultural, scientific, and food-labeling contexts rather than everyday speech.
An amphibian similar to a frog but with drier, warty skin and a stockier body. Commonly appears in folklore and traditional medicine references.
An amphibian with a long body, tail, and short legs, living in cool, damp environments. The giant salamander of Japan is a protected national treasure.
The aquatic larval stage of a frog or toad, with a round body and tail but no legs.
A playful colloquial term for the round-headed notes on a musical staff, which resemble tadpoles.
The respiratory organs on the sides of fish (and some other aquatic animals) that allow them to extract oxygen from water.
Fish that live in rivers, lakes, and other freshwater bodies, as opposed to those in the sea.
A popular Japanese-style breaded and deep-fried shrimp dish. The shrimp is coated in flour, egg, and panko before frying, then served with tartar sauce or tonkatsu sauce.
A pungent yellow mustard paste made from ground mustard seeds, used as a condiment with natto, oden, tonkatsu, and other Japanese dishes. Sharper and hotter than Western mustards.

glosses: to enrich (soil); to fatten (livestock); to line one's own pockets
to line one's pockets; to enrich oneself (figurative)
explanations: To add nutrients to soil so that crops grow well. Used in agricultural contexts.
To raise the body weight of an animal, especially livestock, by feeding it well.
Used in the idiom {私腹|しふく}を{肥|こ}やす to mean enriching oneself unfairly, usually through one's official position.

glosses: backing out; reneging on a deal (slang)
explanations: A direct, coarse word for urine or urinating. Common in everyday male speech and informal writing, but considered crude in polite contexts.
Used in expressions like {小便|しょうべん}する to mean breaking a promise, walking away from a deal, or pulling out of an arrangement. Rough, informal register.

glosses: hundreds; several hundred; how many hundreds
explanations: An indefinite expression for an unspecified number in the hundreds. Typically used with も to emphasize how many there are.

glosses: to catch; to capture; to seize
to catch; to capture; to seize (an animal, fish, criminal)
explanations: To physically catch or capture a moving creature or person — most often fish, insects, or game animals, or sometimes criminals. Used when the action involves chasing or grabbing.
A warm, fragrant spice from the inner bark of cinnamon trees, used in baking, hot drinks, and curries. Sold as powder, sticks, or essential oil.
Used after a number to count individual pieces of sushi, typically nigiri. Standard in sushi restaurants and on menus.

glosses: shishito pepper; small wrinkled green pepper
explanations: A small, slender, mostly mild green pepper popular in Japanese cuisine. Usually grilled, fried, or simmered. Occasionally a single pepper turns out spicy.
A tropical or subtropical biome of grassland with scattered trees, typically associated with Africa. Home to many large mammals such as lions, elephants, and giraffes.
The hard, woody fruit of a pine tree, with overlapping scales that open to release seeds. A common natural object found on the ground in pine forests.

glosses: tatsuta-age; chicken or fish marinated in soy and fried with starch coating
explanations: Bite-sized pieces of chicken or fish marinated in soy sauce, mirin, and ginger, then dusted in potato starch and deep-fried. The reddish-brown color of the surface is said to resemble autumn leaves on the Tatsuta River.
Genuine mirin made by fermenting glutinous rice and rice koji with shochu. Contains about 14% alcohol, distinguishing it from low-alcohol mirin-style seasonings.

glosses: to drizzle in a circular motion; to pour around
explanations: To pour a liquid (oil, sauce, dressing) over food while moving the container in a circle so the liquid covers the surface evenly. Common cooking instruction.

glosses: unroasted sesame oil; pale sesame oil
explanations: Sesame oil pressed from raw (unroasted) sesame seeds. Pale and almost colorless, with a mild flavor — unlike the dark, fragrant roasted-sesame oil used as a finishing seasoning.
Wheat flour with a medium protein (gluten) content, between cake flour and bread flour. Typically used for udon noodles, takoyaki, and some baked goods.

glosses: to be deep-fried; to come out crispy
to be deep-fried; to come out (well) fried
explanations: For food being deep-fried to finish cooking, especially with a desirably crisp result. The intransitive partner of {揚|あ}げる.

glosses: dish topped with thick starchy sauce
dish topped with thick starchy sauce; ankake
explanations: A preparation in which a dashi- or broth-based sauce thickened with potato starch is poured over food such as tofu, fish, noodles, or rice. Also refers to the sauce itself.
A family of stout, often metallic-colored beetles whose larvae feed on plant roots and whose adults eat leaves. Familiar garden pests in Japan.
An aquatic beetle that swims in ponds and rice paddies using paddle-like hind legs. Once common in Japanese countryside, now an endangered species due to habitat loss.

glosses: Mito; capital city of Ibaraki Prefecture
explanations: A city northeast of Tokyo, known historically as the seat of the Mito branch of the Tokugawa clan and today famous for {納豆|なっとう} (fermented soybeans) and the {偕楽園|かいらくえん} plum garden.
A general term for any of several pure-white heron species found in Japan, including the great egret, intermediate egret, and little egret. Common around rivers, paddies, and coastal mudflats.
Japan's largest native heron, a tall blue-grey bird found year-round near rivers, lakes, and paddies. Hunts fish, frogs, and small mammals by standing still in shallow water.

glosses: leg (of a person or animal); limb
explanations: The whole limb from the hip to the foot — what supports the body and is used for walking. Distinct from {足|あし} (foot), though the readings are identical and the words overlap in casual writing.
The supporting parts under a table, chair, camera tripod, or similar object.
An ingredient, mix, or concentrate that serves as the base for making something else. Especially common in food product names like だしの{素|もと} (dashi base) or ラーメンの{素|もと} (ramen base).
The country in South Asia. Also forms compounds for things of Indian origin or association, such as インドカレー (Indian curry) and インド{洋|よう} (Indian Ocean).
Pepper as a seasoning, especially black or white pepper. Loanword from English; appears mostly in cooking product names and compounds, while {胡椒|こしょう} is the everyday word.
Energetic, all-out effort in action. Rarely used alone; appears almost exclusively in the four-character idiom {獅子|しし}{奮迅|ふんじん} (charging like a lion).

A child-rearing approach of deliberately exposing a child to hardship to make them stronger. The image comes from the legend that a lion pushes its cub off a cliff and raises only the one that climbs back up.
A warm dipping sauce for tempura, made from {出汁|だし}, soy sauce, and mirin. Usually served with grated daikon stirred in.
A flour milled from regular (non-glutinous) short-grain rice, used to make {団子|だんご}, {柏餅|かしわもち}, and other Japanese sweets that need a firm, springy texture.
A deciduous conifer native to the central Japanese mountains, distinctive for being one of the few Japanese conifers whose needles turn yellow and fall in autumn.
A traditional Japanese sweet made from white bean paste mixed with a small amount of {求肥|ぎゅうひ} (mochi-based binder), then kneaded, tinted, and shaped by hand — often into flowers or seasonal motifs.
Japanese sweets with a moisture content between fresh ({生菓子|なまがし}) and dry ({干菓子|ひがし}) wagashi. Includes most {最中|もなか} and many bean-jam-filled pastries; keeps longer than fresh wagashi.
A water-loving iris that grows in shallow ponds and wet ditches, producing deep purple flowers in May and June. Long celebrated in Japanese poetry and art.
A tall, large-flowered iris with sword-shaped leaves, planted in damp gardens and along stream banks. Blooms June through early July in a wide range of cultivated colors.
The softer red glow that follows {夕焼|ゆうや}け in the western sky after the sun has set. Used mainly in the fixed pair {夕焼|ゆうや}けこやけ rather than on its own.
An astronomical object whose gravity is so strong that nothing, including light, can escape from it. Often used figuratively for places or systems that absorb resources without trace.
A contemporary story of unverified origin that spreads as if it were true. Often spooky, surprising, or moralistic, and circulated by word of mouth or online.
The eighth planet from the Sun, the farthest of the solar system's planets. Composed of {海|かい} (sea) + {王|おう} (king) + {星|せい} (star/planet).
A dwarf planet beyond Neptune, classified as a planet until 2006 when it was reclassified as a dwarf planet ({準惑星|じゅんわくせい}).

glosses: sense of justice; sense of right and wrong
explanations: An inner conviction about what is fair or right, and a willingness to act on it. Often praised as a character trait.
Across or between different generations. Used as a modifier (often with の) before nouns like gap, transfer, or communication.

glosses: each going their own way; scattered every which way
each going their own way; scattered in every direction
explanations: Describes people or things acting or moving individually in different directions, with no coordination. Often emphasizes a lack of unity or organization.

glosses: crumpled; crushed; in a wrinkled mess
sopping wet; soggy and falling apart
explanations: Describes paper, fabric, or other pliable items that have been crushed, wrinkled, or wadded up into a disordered shape. Often used with する or なる.
Describes something soaked through and reduced to a wet, mushy state — clothes drenched in rain, food fallen apart in liquid.

glosses: to get tired; to wear out
to get tired; to be worn out; to be exhausted
explanations: To become physically or mentally exhausted, especially after sustained effort. Slightly literary or old-fashioned, with a worn-down nuance compared to {疲|つか}れる.
For an object — typically clothing, shoes, or a bag — to become shabby and aged through long use.

glosses: with a thud; flopping down (lying or rolling)
explanations: Onomatopoeia for a single, heavy action of lying down or rolling over. Captures the moment of dropping onto a surface, as opposed to the continuous ごろごろ.

glosses: somen; thin wheat noodles (usually served cold)
explanations: Very thin Japanese wheat noodles, typically eaten cold in summer with a dipping sauce ({めんつゆ}). Often written in kana, sometimes as {素麺|そうめん}.

glosses: wax (for floors, cars, hair, skis, etc.)
explanations: A wax product applied to surfaces for shine or protection — floor wax, car wax, ski wax — or styling product for hair.

glosses: riverbed; dry stony area beside a river
explanations: The flat, often rocky or sandy area along a river that is dry except during high water. A popular spot for picnics, fireworks, and camping in Japan.
A free-reed wind instrument with 17 bamboo pipes mounted on a small cup-shaped chamber, used in {雅楽|ががく} (Japanese court music). Produces an ethereal, sustained chord.
A simple side-blown bamboo flute used in folk music and festival music ({祭|まつ}り{囃子|ばやし}). Sweeter and lighter than the more formal {龍笛|りゅうてき} of gagaku.
A general term for musical instruments of Western origin (piano, violin, guitar, etc.), used in contrast to {和楽器|わがっき} (traditional Japanese instruments).
A staged dramatic work in which much or all of the text is sung, with orchestral accompaniment. Includes both individual works and the genre as a whole.
Singing in which each part is performed by a single voice, in contrast to {合唱|がっしょう} (chorus) where each part has multiple singers. Used in classical music for duets and small ensembles.
The square or circular fighting area used in boxing, professional wrestling, and similar combat sports.
A ring-shaped object — finger ring, key ring, gymnastic rings, etc. — often used as a modifier.
Pro wrestling as a sport and entertainment form. Abbreviation of プロフェッショナル・レスリング (professional wrestling), used as the standard term for the sport in Japanese.
A person who surfs (rides ocean waves on a surfboard). Sometimes used loosely for someone with a beachy, surf-culture lifestyle.
The board used in surfing — a long, narrow board, typically made of foam coated in fiberglass, that the surfer rides on the wave.
A person who dives — scuba diver, competitive (springboard/platform) diver, or skydiver. Context determines which kind.

A class of synthetic gases formerly used as refrigerants and in aerosol sprays, now phased out because they damage the ozone layer. The Japanese term covers CFCs and related halogenated coolants in general usage.
A streak of ore or mineral running through surrounding rock. Also used figuratively for a rich source of something valuable, such as information or talent.
The network of vessels visible on a leaf that carries water and nutrients between the stem and the leaf tissue.
A form of oxygen (O₃) with a distinctive sharp smell, found in the upper atmosphere and produced by electrical discharges such as lightning.
A close-fitting suit made of neoprene worn for warmth and protection during diving, surfing, and other water sports.
A display screen that detects and responds to direct touch input from a finger or stylus, used in smartphones, tablets, kiosks, and other devices.
A quick sliding gesture on a touchscreen, especially the input method used in Japanese smartphone keyboards where the user slides from a base kana in one of four directions to select related kana.

glosses: original language; original word; source language
explanations: The language in which a text was originally written or spoken, as contrasted with a translation. Also refers to a word in its source language before being translated or borrowed.
A key combination or icon that lets you perform an action more quickly, such as Ctrl+C for copy, or a desktop icon that links directly to a program.
A short hairstyle, typically referring to women's hair cut to around the ears or shorter.
An ancient pole weapon with a blade or pointed head, used in Japan and elsewhere before firearms. Largely a historical or literary term in modern Japanese.

glosses: melon bread (sweet bun with cookie crust)
explanations: A popular Japanese sweet bread with a soft interior and a thin, crisp cookie-dough crust scored on top to resemble a melon's rind. Most varieties do not actually contain melon.
The long hair growing along the neck of certain animals, most prominently lions and horses.
Thin strips of ginger pickled in plum vinegar, dyed a bright red color. Served as a topping for dishes such as gyudon, yakisoba, and okonomiyaki.
A thin sushi roll filled with cucumber, wrapped in nori and rice. One of the simplest and most familiar sushi roll varieties.

glosses: amber color; caramel color; honey color
explanations: A translucent golden-brown color resembling that of traditional Japanese hard candy. Commonly used to describe slowly caramelized onions, varnished wood, or aged objects.
Describes something that is old, worn, and in poor condition — clothes, buildings, vehicles, equipment. Casual and somewhat blunt in tone.

glosses: pi; ratio of circumference to diameter
pi (π); ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter
explanations: The mathematical constant pi (π), approximately 3.14159, representing the ratio of any circle's circumference to its diameter.
The mathematical function that gives the exponent to which a base must be raised to produce a given number. Common in high-school math, science, and engineering contexts.
Describes something extreme enough to constitute a record — most often used in news contexts about weather, heat, rainfall, sales figures, or other measurable values.

glosses: negative consequences shifted onto someone else; spillover burden
burden shifted onto others; ripple-effect strain
explanations: The negative side-effects of a decision, problem, or policy that end up falling on people other than those responsible. Literally "pushing wrinkles together," as when smoothing one part of cloth bunches up another.
A long-distance pleasure ride, typically on a motorcycle and sometimes on a bicycle, taken for the experience of riding through scenic areas.
A heated styling tool used to straighten or curl hair. The same word covers both flat-iron (straightening) and barrel (curling) types.
A fabric made by bonding or felting fibers together rather than weaving them. Used in surgical masks, wet wipes, cleaning cloths, filters, and disposable products.
A Shinto shrine enshrining {徳川家康|とくがわいえやす} as the deity {東照大権現|とうしょうだいごんげん}. The most famous is in {日光|にっこう}, a UNESCO World Heritage site, but Toshogu shrines exist throughout Japan.

A large white wading bird with pinkish-white plumage and a long, downward-curving black bill. Once widespread in Japan but driven to near extinction in the 20th century; now the focus of a major reintroduction program on {佐渡島|さどがしま}.

glosses: competition; contest (esp. in music, art, or performance)
explanations: A juried competition in which participants are evaluated and ranked, especially in music, dance, photography, or other arts. From French 'concours'.
In choral music, refers to an ensemble that includes both men's and women's voices. Almost always appears in compounds describing choir types.

glosses: steam (esp. as a function on appliances)
explanations: Steam, especially as a feature or function on home appliances such as irons, ovens, cleaners, and beauty devices. From English 'steam'. The native word {湯気|ゆげ} is used for visible steam in everyday contexts.
A flat outdoor space adjoining a building, typically at ground level. Used for cafés, restaurants, and homes as an outdoor seating or dining area. From English 'terrace'.

glosses: side effect; adverse reaction (esp. to a vaccine)
explanations: An unintended bodily reaction to a vaccine. Distinguished in Japanese medical usage from {副作用|ふくさよう}, which is reserved for side effects of medications. The term became widely known during the COVID-19 vaccination campaign.

A contagious viral infection causing a mild rash and fever, particularly dangerous to fetuses if contracted in early pregnancy. Largely controlled in Japan by routine MMR-style vaccination, though periodic outbreaks occur among unvaccinated adult men.

In everyday Japanese usage since 2020, refers to COVID-19 and the social impact of the pandemic. Used as a casual shorthand where English would more often say 'COVID'. The formal name is {新型|しんがた}コロナウイルス.
A hospital designated to accept emergency patients around the clock. In Japan, hospitals are officially classified into tiers ({一次|いちじ}、{二次|にじ}、{三次|さんじ}) based on the severity of cases they handle.

glosses: dispatch; deployment; mobilization (of emergency services or police)
explanations: The action of police, fire, ambulance, or military personnel being sent out to a scene. Used with する as a verb. Almost exclusively associated with organized response units, not ordinary travel.
A police vehicle used for patrolling and responding to calls. The full form of the much more common abbreviation パトカー. From English 'patrol car'.

glosses: spring cabbage (early-spring variety, softer and sweeter)
explanations: A type of cabbage harvested mainly in spring, with softer, lighter-colored leaves and a sweeter, milder taste than ordinary cabbage. Especially prized for raw use such as in salads.

glosses: wakegi; Welsh onion; bunching onion (Allium × wakegi)
explanations: A perennial onion that grows in clumps from a small bulb, with slender green stalks and a mild flavor. A hybrid of {葱|ねぎ} and shallot, popular in western Japanese cooking, especially in {ぬた} (vinegar-miso dishes).

A casual real-time video conversation conducted over the internet, typically one-on-one or in small groups via apps like LINE, Zoom, or FaceTime. Suggests informal use rather than formal business meetings.

glosses: number of cases; count (of incidents, orders)
number of cases; number of items; count
explanations: The count of discrete instances of something — incidents, orders, accidents, complaints, dispatches, etc. Used when {件|けん} (case, matter) is the natural counter for the things being counted, especially in statistics and business reporting.

A round, flat cake cooked on a griddle, typically eaten for breakfast or as a dessert with butter, syrup, fruit, or whipped cream. Distinguished in Japanese usage from {ホットケーキ}, which is the older term and tends to refer to a thicker, simpler version.
A round white steamed bun with a savory pork filling. A staple winter snack sold hot at convenience stores in Japan. The Japanese adaptation of Chinese baozi.

A small, soft, cake-like steamed bun, typically lightly sweet and made with wheat flour. Popular as a snack and as homemade food for small children because of its light texture and the fact that it can be made without an oven.

A two-year (occasionally three-year) post-secondary institution in Japan, granting an associate degree ({短期大学士|たんきだいがくし}). Short for {短期大学|たんきだいがく}. Historically dominated by women's institutions emphasizing practical fields; the number of {短大|たんだい}s has declined sharply since the 1990s.

glosses: to feel a sudden chill; to feel a momentary shiver of fear
to feel a sudden chill; to have a heart-stopping moment; to feel a shiver of fear
explanations: To experience a brief sensation of cold or shock, often in response to a close call, narrow escape, or scary realization. The chill is more about the inner reaction than literal cold.

glosses: drag (computing); dragging with mouse or finger
drag (computing); dragging an item with mouse or finger
explanations: The action of holding down a button or touching a screen and moving an item across the display. Used for moving files, scrolling, selecting text, or operating on-screen objects.
The leisure activity of going to stores, malls, or browsing online to buy clothing, accessories, gifts, and similar items. Carries a more recreational nuance than the everyday {買|か}い{物|もの}.

glosses: clear plastic folder; clear file sleeve
clear plastic folder; clear A4-size file sleeve
explanations: A thin, transparent plastic folder, usually A4-sized and open on two sides, used to hold loose documents flat without binding. A ubiquitous office and school supply in Japan.

glosses: arousing; calling to attention; evoking (interest, awareness, opinion)
explanations: The act of bringing something to public attention or drawing out a feeling, awareness, or memory. Used in formal contexts about opinion, concern, or interest.
A Chinese-origin dish of shredded vegetables and meat wrapped in a thin wheat skin and deep-fried. A staple item on Chinese restaurant menus in Japan and a common bento side.
The act or state of eating more than is good for one's health or comfort. Used both for a single occasion (eating too much at one meal) and a habitual pattern.

glosses: dubious story; something fishy; suspect claim
explanations: Something that sounds too good or too strange to be true, and therefore should be doubted. Often used about rumors, get-rich-quick claims, or exaggerated stories.

glosses: nearest; closest (especially of a station, store, or facility)
explanations: The one geographically closest to a given location, usually one's home, workplace, or current spot. Almost always used attributively before a noun, especially {駅|えき} (station).

glosses: bathroom; bathing area (the wet room with the tub)
explanations: The room in a Japanese house where one washes and bathes — containing the bathtub and a tiled washing area. Distinct from the toilet, which is a separate room.
A unit of length equal to one-thousandth of a meter. Short for ミリメートル and overwhelmingly the everyday spoken form.
The metric prefix meaning one-thousandth, attached to other units such as grams, liters, or seconds.
A metric unit of area equal to a 100 m × 100 m square (10,000 m²). The standard unit for large land areas such as farmland, forests, and parks. Abbreviated 'ha' in writing.

glosses: grainy bumps; tiny round particles; bumpy texture
explanations: Many small round bumps or grains on or in something — used for textures of food (orange juice with pulp, strawberry seeds, tapioca) and skin (acne, goosebumps, hives).

glosses: tottering; staggering; unsteady on one's feet
explanations: Describes a wobbling, unstable walk — as of a toddler, an elderly person, a drunk, or someone too exhausted to keep their balance. More emphatic than よろよろ, often suggesting a precarious, almost-falling gait.

glosses: with a flat plop; flatly; sitting flat on the ground
with a flat plop; flatly; sitting or sticking flat
explanations: Describes something making full, flat contact with a surface in a single soft motion — a person flopping down to sit, a sticker pressed flat, or a hand laid flat against something.

glosses: sports club; athletics club (at a school)
explanations: A school extracurricular club for a sport such as baseball, soccer, tennis, or kendo. One of the two big categories of Japanese school clubs, alongside {文化部|ぶんかぶ} (cultural clubs).

A school extracurricular club focused on a cultural or intellectual activity rather than sports — for example brass band, drama, art, tea ceremony, or science. Contrasted with {運動部|うんどうぶ} (sports clubs).

glosses: school nurse; licensed school health teacher
explanations: A licensed teacher who staffs a Japanese school's {保健室|ほけんしつ} (health room), handling first aid, illness during school hours, health education, and student wellbeing concerns. Casually referred to as the {保健|ほけん}の{先生|せんせい}.
Medicine taken to relieve constipation. The everyday, consumer-facing word — packaging at pharmacies and TV ads typically use this term rather than the medical {下剤|げざい}.
A polite, euphemistic word for having a bowel movement, especially the regularity of one. Standard in medical settings, ads for digestive products, and conversation with the elderly or children.

glosses: gauze; medical gauze; soft loose-woven cotton cloth
explanations: A loose-woven cotton fabric used as a wound dressing or for soft baby and skincare items. Sold at pharmacies as squares for cuts, and in baby sections as towels, washcloths, and onesies.
Flowers or leaves dried flat under weight, used for cards, framed art, and craft. Also the craft of making them — a popular hobby for children and a long-standing decorative art.
Medicine that induces bowel movements, taken for constipation or to clear the bowels before a medical procedure such as a colonoscopy. The medical-register term, used by doctors and on prescriptions.
The elementary school student government, composed of elected representatives from upper grades who run assemblies and student-led activities. The middle/high school counterpart is the {生徒会|せいとかい}.

An organized association of students, especially the student government of a university or specialized school. Handles student-life activities, club support, and the school festival. The pre-university counterpart is {生徒会|せいとかい}.

glosses: hard worker; dedicated professional; consummate worker
explanations: A person who is highly skilled at and devoted to their job. Carries a sense of professionalism, competence, and seriousness about work.
A suffix attached to nouns to indicate something that wards off or protects against the preceding noun. Derived from the verb {避|よ}ける (to avoid).

glosses: suspension from attending school; mandatory absence
explanations: A school's order that a student must stay home, typically because of an infectious disease (flu, measles, COVID-19) or as a disciplinary measure. Distinct from voluntary sick leave — the student is not allowed to attend.
The quality of being tied to a particular season. Common as a noun modifier (used with の) for things that appear or recur seasonally, especially in medical and business contexts.

glosses: triangular bandage; arm sling; (kitchen) triangular head scarf
triangular head scarf (worn in cooking class)
explanations: A triangular cloth used in first aid to immobilize an injured arm or support a wound. A standard item in school and workplace first-aid kits.
A triangular cloth worn over the hair to keep it out of food. Standard equipment for elementary school cooking classes and school lunch duty.

glosses: wound medicine; antiseptic ointment; salve for cuts and scrapes
explanations: Topical medicine applied to cuts, scrapes, and minor wounds — usually an ointment, cream, or liquid disinfectant kept in the home first-aid kit.

glosses: playing at a rocky shore; tide pool exploration
explanations: Recreational time spent at a rocky seashore, especially looking for small creatures in tide pools at low tide. A popular family outing in spring and summer.

glosses: rock fishing; shore fishing from rocky coasts
explanations: Recreational fishing done from rocky shorelines or coastal rocks, often targeting fish like {黒鯛|くろだい} or {メジナ}. A distinct style from boat fishing or pier fishing.
A person who practices the sport of boxing, either as an amateur or a professional prizefighter. From the English word "boxer."

glosses: knife skills; knife handling; knife technique
explanations: A cook's skill at handling a kitchen knife — speed, precision, and control. Often used to praise the dexterity of a professional chef or a skilled home cook.
A round bamboo or wooden basket with a slatted bottom used for steaming food over a pot of boiling water. Used both in Japanese cuisine (steamed buns, vegetables, seafood) and in Chinese dim sum.

glosses: way of cutting; cutting technique; how to cut
explanations: The method or manner of cutting something — typically food in a cooking context, but also paper, fabric, or hair. Formed by the verb {切|き}る (to cut) + {方|かた} (way of doing).

glosses: emotional attachment; deep feeling; personal investment
explanations: Strong personal feelings tied to a particular thing, place, or activity — often based on memories, history, or long involvement. Usually positive: caring deeply about something.

glosses: to dodge; to evade; to sidestep; to deflect
to dodge; to evade (a physical attack)
to deflect; to dodge (a question, responsibility)
explanations: To move out of the way of an oncoming object or attack — a punch, ball, vehicle, or similar. Implies quick, deliberate avoidance rather than passive escape.
To avoid an awkward question, criticism, or unwanted topic by giving a vague or off-topic response. The figurative extension of the physical dodge.

glosses: to rub; to chafe; to wear thin; to become jaded
to rub against; to graze; to chafe
to wear thin; to fray; to become worn from rubbing
to become jaded; to become worldly-wise; to lose innocence
explanations: For two surfaces to come into rubbing contact, typically causing wear, irritation, or sound. Often used of clothing, skin, machine parts, or feet in shoes.
For a surface or material to gradually wear down due to friction over time — cuffs, knees of jeans, tire treads, the spine of a well-read book.
Figurative use: for a person to be ground down by experience into a cynical or cunning state. Often used of children who have grown up too quickly or adults who have lost their idealism.
Plants that grow in or on water — in rivers, lakes, ponds, or aquariums. Includes both fully submerged plants and ones whose leaves float on the surface.
The body of rules and structures by which taxes are levied and collected — including tax types, rates, exemptions, and administrative procedures. A standard term in news and policy discussion.
A fixed, oversimplified mental image of a group of people or things — typically a national, gender, occupational, or social-group stereotype. Often used critically.

glosses: mass resignation; en bloc resignation (of a cabinet)
mass resignation; en bloc resignation (especially of a cabinet)
explanations: The simultaneous resignation of all members of a body — most often a national cabinet, but also a corporate board or committee. Often takes する.

glosses: sasa dango; mugwort rice dumpling wrapped in bamboo leaves
sasa dango; mugwort rice dumpling wrapped in bamboo grass leaves
explanations: A traditional Niigata sweet: a sticky-rice dumpling kneaded with {蓬|よもぎ} (mugwort), filled with sweet bean paste, wrapped in {笹|ささ} (bamboo grass) leaves and steamed. The leaves give a fresh fragrance and serve as a natural preservative.

glosses: Tanabata bamboo decoration; decorated bamboo branch
explanations: A branch of {笹|ささ} (bamboo grass) decorated with paper streamers, origami ornaments, and {短冊|たんざく} (strips of paper bearing wishes), displayed for the {七夕|たなばた} festival on July 7.

glosses: both wheels; (figuratively) two essential elements that work together
explanations: The two wheels of a bicycle, cart, or similar two-wheeled object. The literal sense, less common in modern speech than the figurative one.
Figurative: two things that are both indispensable and only work together — like the two wheels of a cart, where one alone cannot move. A standard metaphor in business, policy, and education writing.

Describes an appliance or device that performs only one function, in contrast to a multifunctional model. Commonly used for kitchen appliances — a microwave that only heats, a printer that only prints, etc. Frequently used as a noun modifier with の.

glosses: three years; for three years; period of three years
three years; period of three years
explanations: A duration of three years. The suffix {間|かん} emphasizes a continuous span of time, distinguishing this from {三年|さんねん} which can also mean 'third year.'
A duration of two years.
The second year in a sequence, such as a school year or program. Commonly used in {二年生|にねんせい} (second-year student).
A combining form used in the names of Japan's education-and-science ministry and its minister: {文部科学省|もんぶかがくしょう} (MEXT) and {文部科学大臣|もんぶかがくだいじん} (Minister of Education). Almost never used alone.
Describes something that is disorderly, illogical, or out of control. As a na-adjective it characterizes a situation, plan, or behavior; as an adverb it intensifies.
Used adverbially in casual speech to mean 'extremely' or 'really.' Functionally equivalent to とても but much more colloquial.
The four basic arithmetic operations: addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. A grade-school math term.
Of or relating to a straight line, or to a relationship in which one quantity changes in direct proportion to another. Used in math, physics, and engineering.
The natural and physical sciences — typically mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, and earth science as an academic grouping, distinct from engineering or the humanities.
The padded glove-and-forearm protector worn in {剣道|けんどう} (kendo). Also refers to similar wrist-and-forearm guards worn with traditional armor or in other martial arts.
In kendo, a scoring strike to the opponent's wrist/forearm. Called out as 'kote!' when delivered.
In karate and several other martial arts, paired training or competition in which two practitioners exchange techniques. Contrasted with solo {型|かた} (forms) practice.
An overhead lattice or pergola built to support a {藤|ふじ} (wisteria) vine. The hanging clusters of purple flowers are a classic late-spring sight in Japanese parks and gardens.
The art and skill of calculating with a {そろばん} (abacus). Often refers to the school subject or after-school class where children learn this skill.

A four-character idiom describing someone who plunges ahead toward a goal without considering risks or alternatives. Literally 'charging like a wild boar.' Can be praising (single-minded drive) or critical (reckless), depending on context.
Refers collectively to multiple newspapers, treating each as a separate source. Standard journalism vocabulary for 'the press' considered paper-by-paper.

glosses: lost item; something one has lost
explanations: An item the owner has misplaced and whose whereabouts are unknown. Compare with {落|お}とし{物|もの} (a dropped item, typically found by someone else).
The temperature of hot water, especially of a bath being prepared or just filled. Typically used when checking or commenting on whether a bath is at a comfortable temperature.
The main shared room of a home, used for relaxing, watching TV, and entertaining guests. The full katakana form; often shortened to リビング in everyday speech.
The two opposite sides of something — a road, a body, a piece of paper, an argument. Used for spatial sides and, by extension, two opposing parties or viewpoints.

glosses: ceremony hall; wedding venue; funeral venue
explanations: A hall or facility dedicated to holding ceremonies — most often weddings or funerals, but also graduations and other formal events.

A pre-printed outline drawing meant to be filled in with colored pencils, markers, or paints. Also refers to the activity itself. Long popular as a children's pastime; adult coloring books became widely popular in the 2010s.
Strong, visible happiness — typically used to describe someone's reaction to good news or a welcome surprise. The {大|おお} prefix intensifies {喜|よろこ}び.

glosses: to apologize (polite); to offer one's apologies
explanations: A polite humble verb for offering an apology, especially in business, customer service, and formal correspondence. The honorific お + {詫|わ}び + する pattern makes it more formal than {謝|あやま}る.

glosses: one year; for one year; period of one year
one year; period of one year
explanations: A duration of one year. The {間|かん} suffix emphasizes a continuous span of time, distinguishing this from {一年|いちねん}, which can also mean 'first year.'

glosses: two years; for two years; period of two years
two years; period of two years
explanations: A duration of two years. The {間|かん} suffix emphasizes a continuous span of time, distinguishing this from {二年|にねん} which can also mean 'second year.'

glosses: truth; the real thing; (prefix) true; genuine
explanations: Used as a noun for 'the truth' or 'the real essence' of something. Mostly appears in set phrases and formal/literary contexts.
Used as a noun-modifier or prefix meaning 'true' or 'real' — emphasizing that something is the genuine, authentic version. Attaches to many nouns to form compounds.

glosses: many rebirths across past and future lives
explanations: A Buddhist concept referring to the many lifetimes a soul passes through in the cycle of rebirth. Used almost exclusively in the proverb {袖|そで}{振|ふ}り{合|あ}うも{多生|たしょう}の{縁|えん}.

glosses: flat side; flat surface; flat part
explanations: The flat side or face of an object, especially of something with both flat and edged sides like a sword or palm. Often appears in compounds rather than as a standalone noun.
Swimming at or near the water's surface while using a snorkel and mask to view underwater life. A common leisure activity at tropical beaches and around coral reefs.
A small graphic image used on a computer or smartphone to represent a program, file, or function. Also commonly refers to a user's profile picture on social media.
Holding down a button, key, or touchscreen element for an extended moment instead of a quick tap. Often used to access secondary menus or context-sensitive options on smartphones.
A prefix attached to nouns to indicate that something is of Western (European or American) style or origin, in contrast to {和|わ} (Japanese-style). Common in food, clothing, room, and music terms.

Abstract beauty, especially as an aesthetic ideal or quality to be appreciated in art, nature, or design. Used as a one-character noun in formal and literary writing, and as a productive suffix in many compounds.

glosses: the usual; a predictable pattern; one's standard order
explanations: Something fixed, predictable, or routinely the same. Often refers to a familiar pattern (an お{決|き}まりのパターン) or, at restaurants and cafes, to a customer's regular order.
A country other than one's own. Often used in writing, news, and formal speech as a slightly more abstract alternative to {外国|がいこく}.

glosses: cone shape; ice cream cone; traffic cone
explanations: A cone-shaped object. Covers geometric cones, the wafer cones used for ice cream, and the bright safety cones used to mark off areas on roads and construction sites.
A sphere in the geometric sense — a perfectly round three-dimensional shape. Used in math, science, and the names of round objects. Distinct from ボール, which refers to balls used in sports.
A pyramid in the geometric sense — a solid with a polygonal base and triangular faces meeting at a single point. Used for the abstract shape; the Egyptian monument is called ピラミッド.
The country of Greece. Also functions as a prefix in compounds for things of Greek origin (Greek language, Greek philosophy, etc.). Sometimes written ギリシア.
The total area covering the outside of a three-dimensional object. Used in mathematics, physics, chemistry, and engineering to describe how much exterior a solid has.
In geometry, a prism — a solid with two identical, parallel polygonal faces connected by rectangular faces. Also used outside math for square-cross-section pillars in buildings.
A six-sided polygon. Used in mathematics, and as a description for honeycomb cells, nuts and bolt heads, snowflake patterns, and other six-sided objects.

glosses: inside corner of the strike zone (baseball)
explanations: In geometry, the angle formed inside a polygon at one of its vertices. The interior angles of a triangle sum to 180°; for an n-gon the sum is 180°×(n−2).
In baseball, the side of the strike zone closer to the batter. Pitchers throw a {内角|ないかく} to back the batter off the plate.
One example among many; a single illustrative case. Used in writing and presentation to introduce a specific instance that demonstrates a broader pattern.
A plant with thick, fleshy leaves or stems that store water, such as cacti, aloe, and echeveria. Popular as low-maintenance houseplants.
A candle, especially a decorative or scented one. Loanword from English "candle" — used mostly for ornamental, aromatherapy, and ceremonial candles rather than utility ones.
A stapler — the office tool that binds papers together with metal staples. A formal/technical loanword; in everyday speech ホチキス is far more common.

glosses: to reflect (light or heat); to glare back
explanations: Of a surface, to bounce back light or heat that strikes it. Often describes asphalt, snow, water, or walls sending sunlight or heat back into the surroundings.

glosses: to sharpen; to point; to purse (lips)
to sharpen; to make pointed; to purse (lips)
explanations: To make something pointy at the tip. Also used figuratively with {口|くち} (mouth/lips) to mean pouting or sulking, and with {神経|しんけい} (nerves) to mean being on edge.

glosses: (spirits) cut with hot water; hot-water highball
explanations: An alcoholic drink, typically {焼酎|しょうちゅう} or whisky, diluted with hot water. Commonly drunk in winter to warm up. The base spirit is usually named: {焼酎|しょうちゅう}の{湯割|ゆわ}り.

glosses: words of resentment; reproach; bitter complaint
explanations: Words expressing a grudge or accumulated resentment toward someone, usually delivered face-to-face or in a letter. Implies a personal grievance rather than general complaining.
Rainfall made unusually acidic by air pollution — primarily sulfur and nitrogen oxides from factories and vehicles. A common topic in environmental discussions.
Having a slightly acidic pH (roughly 4–6.5). Often appears on skin-care, shampoo, and cleaning-product labels because skin's natural pH is mildly acidic.
A formal, respectful term for someone else's son, used in writing or polite speech. Often appears in news, invitations, and business correspondence. Frequently prefixed with ご as ご{子息|しそく}.
A family's sole male child. Implies no other male siblings — there may still be daughters.
A condominium building of roughly 20 stories or more. Common in urban Japan since the 2000s. Often shortened to タワマン in casual speech.
Money set aside regularly for a specific future purpose — building repairs, retirement, a child's education, etc. Common contexts include condominium reserve funds and monthly savings plans.

glosses: thin skin; thin peel; thin membrane
explanations: A thin outer layer — the skin of a fruit, the membrane around a peanut or section of citrus, or a thin pastry skin around a bun or dumpling.
Light-colored, mildly sweet miso made with a high ratio of rice koji and a short fermentation period. Associated with Kyoto and Western Japan; the standard miso for ozōni in those regions.

Dark reddish-brown miso fermented for a longer period (often a year or more). Saltier and stronger in flavor than {白味噌|しろみそ}. Associated with the Tōhoku and Aichi regions; Nagoya's {八丁|はっちょう}{味噌|みそ} is a famous variety.

Boasting about something one has done or owns. Comes from the old practice of each household making and praising its own miso. Most often appears in the set phrase {手前味噌|てまえみそ}ですが/{手前味噌|てまえみそ}ながら, used as a humble preface before saying something positive about oneself or one's family or company.
A {鍋|なべ} dish in which chicken and vegetables are simmered in water (no seasoning broth) and eaten with ponzu sauce. Particularly associated with Hakata (Fukuoka) and Kansai cuisine.

glosses: to beg; to ask for; to entreat
explanations: To earnestly request something — help, forgiveness, or mercy — from someone in a more powerful or favorable position. Literary in tone; in everyday speech replaced by {頼|たの}む or お{願|ねが}いする.

A warrior or samurai of the pre-modern era. In modern use, appears in historical contexts, festival names (the Boy's Day {五月人形|ごがつにんぎょう}), and set expressions such as {武者震|むしゃぶる}い (a thrill of anticipation before a challenge).

glosses: to collapse; to come to nothing; to be dashed
explanations: Of hopes, plans, dreams, or armies — to be destroyed or fall apart, leaving nothing. A literary intransitive verb, common in news and written Japanese for crushed dreams or defeated forces.

glosses: to bend (one's back, body); to stoop
to bend (one's back or body); to stoop down
explanations: To bend a part of one's own body — usually the back, knees, or whole body — to lower oneself or duck under something. The object is one's own body part.

A grand, far-reaching goal for one's life — bigger than ordinary career or personal goals. A formal, somewhat literary word, famous from William S. Clark's saying {少年|しょうねん}よ、{大志|たいし}を{抱|いだ}け ("Boys, be ambitious").
Both feet or both legs taken together, in contrast to {片足|かたあし} (one foot/leg). Used in everyday descriptions of posture, movement, sports, and medical contexts.

glosses: the interior of a country; inland area
explanations: In modern Japanese, mostly used by people from Hokkaido or Okinawa to refer to the main island of Honshu (and sometimes Honshu plus Shikoku and Kyushu). Roughly "the rest of Japan" from the speaker's perspective.
An inland part of a country, away from the coast or frontier. Less common; appears in some formal or older texts.

A graded level in a system of ranking — used for beef, wine, hotel rooms, paychecks, insurance, and judo/karate. Implies an ordered scale with clear criteria, distinguishing top grades from lower ones.
Intense physical or mental suffering — writhing in pain, or being torn by inner torment. A literary, fairly heavy word, common in novels, news reports, and medical descriptions.
A small to medium cooking pot with a single long handle, used for boiling small portions, heating sauces, or making instant noodles. The everyday Japanese term for a Western-style saucepan.
The most common variety of mandarin orange grown and eaten in Japan. Seedless, easy to peel by hand, and harvested in autumn and winter.
A variety of mandarin orange originally from India, now grown in Japan (especially Kyushu and Shikoku). Sweeter and more aromatic than common mandarins, with a slightly bumpy rind.
A large, very sweet citrus variety identified by a distinctive bump (デコ) at the top. A hybrid of ponkan and a Kiyomi orange, mostly grown in Kumamoto and Ehime.
Miso made by combining two or more types (usually white and red, or rice and barley miso). Balances the flavors of each kind and is widely sold as a general-purpose miso.
A cooking pot with handles on both sides, lifted with both hands. Typically used for boiling pasta, simmering stews, or making stock, where the pot is too heavy or wide for a single handle.
A hot pot dish featuring beef or pork intestines (もつ) simmered with cabbage, garlic chives, and other vegetables in a soy or miso-based broth. A specialty of Fukuoka.
A hot pot dish with a spicy, sour broth made from kimchi, simmered with pork, tofu, mushrooms, and vegetables. Adapted from Korean cuisine and popular in Japanese winters.

glosses: Kokugikan; sumo arena (esp. in Ryōgoku, Tokyo)
explanations: An arena built for sumo wrestling. By default refers to the {両国|りょうごく}{国技館|こくぎかん} in Tokyo, the main venue for grand sumo tournaments in eastern Japan.
A sleeveless shirt with shoulder straps, worn as a casual summer top or as inner/sports wear. Used by men and women alike.
A handheld battery-powered light. Used in everyday Japanese to refer to small, often high-power LED lights, particularly outdoor or tactical models.
A small flashlight in the shape of a pen, slim enough to fit in a pocket. Used for inspections, medical exams, and as an emergency light.
A stick-shaped, often color-changing LED light waved by fans at concerts and idol events. Strongly associated with otaku and idol fan culture.
The total quantity of muscle tissue in the body, usually expressed as a weight or proportion. Commonly cited in fitness, dieting, and health contexts.

A wedding performed in a Shinto shrine before the gods, typically with the bride in a white kimono ({白無垢|しろむく}) and the groom in formal hakama. Features rituals such as the three-cup sake exchange ({三三九度|さんさんくど}).

A wedding performed in a Christian church or church-style chapel, with vows, an exchange of rings, and a minister officiating. The most popular wedding style in modern Japan, often chosen regardless of religion.
A non-religious wedding ceremony in which the couple makes their vows in front of the assembled guests, who serve as the witnesses. Allows free design of the ceremony's content and style.
A professional photographer, especially in commercial, fashion, wedding, or freelance contexts. The loanword has a more contemporary, creative-industry feel than the native term {写真家|しゃしんか}.
A prefecture on the Sea of Japan coast in the Hokuriku region. Bordered by the Tateyama mountain range and known for Toyama Bay seafood, pharmaceuticals, and the Kurobe Gorge.

glosses: pairing (e.g., wine and food, or Bluetooth devices)
explanations: A pair of matching rings worn by a couple, usually identical in design. Worn as a symbol of being together; distinct from engagement or wedding rings.
Combining two things so they go well together. Used both for wine/food pairing and for connecting two electronic devices via Bluetooth.

glosses: tomb raider; grave robber; illegal excavator
explanations: A person who illegally digs up tombs, ancient ruins, or protected sites to steal artifacts or valuables. Also used for those who illegally collect plants or minerals from protected land.
The principal home where someone lives, as distinguished from a vacation home, secondary house, or company-provided dwelling. Often used in legal or administrative contexts.

headword: ショッピングセンター
explanations: A large retail complex housing many shops, restaurants, and often a supermarket under one roof, usually with a parking lot. Common in suburban areas.
The fee charged for household or commercial gas usage. Typically billed monthly, combining a base fee and usage-based charges.
A noticeable difference between two things, especially in brightness, color, or qualities being compared. Used for images, displays, and figurative comparisons.

glosses: yin and yang; light and dark duality
yin and yang; positive and negative; light and dark duality
explanations: The classical East Asian concept of complementary opposites that together form a balanced whole. Used in philosophy, divination, traditional medicine, and figuratively for contrasting pairs.

glosses: morning and evening; both morning and night
explanations: A compound noun referring to both ends of the day. Often used adverbially to mean 'twice daily' or to describe routines done morning and evening.

glosses: temperature difference; gap in attitude or enthusiasm
gap in enthusiasm; difference in attitude
explanations: A literal difference in temperature between two places, times, or substances.
Figurative use describing how strongly different people feel about something — typically a noticeable mismatch in interest, concern, or commitment.

glosses: right and wrong; good and evil
right and wrong; good and evil; justice and injustice
explanations: A formal compound contrasting the morally correct ({正|せい}) with the morally wrong ({邪|じゃ}). Used in writing and serious discussion to refer to the distinction itself.

glosses: norm; usual state; what is ordinary
explanations: What is normal, customary, or to be expected. Often appears in set patterns describing how things typically are, or as {常|つね}に (always) adverbially.
A person who currently holds or maintains something — typically a record, championship, license, or other formal status. Often preceded by what is held.
The business practice of contracting work to outside companies rather than handling it internally. Often used as a する-verb.

The central point or core message of a statement, document, or argument. Largely interchangeable with {趣旨|しゅし}, but emphasizes the 'main' ({主|しゅ}) aspect — what is principal — rather than purpose or intent.

glosses: Tanabata decorations; ornamental strips and streamers for the Star Festival
explanations: Colorful paper decorations — primarily {短冊|たんざく} (paper strips with wishes), origami cranes, and streamers — hung on bamboo branches for the July 7 Tanabata festival.

glosses: seventh death anniversary; memorial service held in the sixth year after a death
explanations: A Buddhist memorial service marking the seventh observance of someone's death. In Japanese tradition, it is held six years after the death (counted inclusively, so the death year is year 1).

glosses: thirteenth death anniversary; memorial service held in the twelfth year after a death
explanations: A Buddhist memorial service marking the thirteenth observance of someone's death, held twelve calendar years after the death (counted inclusively).

glosses: bride and groom; the newly married couple
explanations: A formal compound referring to a couple at their wedding or shortly after. Combines {新郎|しんろう} (groom) and {新婦|しんぷ} (bride).

glosses: entertainment (at a party or ceremony); sideshow
entertainment at a party or ceremony; performance for guests
explanations: Performances, games, or skits presented for guests at events like weddings, banquets, year-end parties, and company gatherings. Not the main event but a supplementary entertainment segment.

glosses: costume change at a wedding reception
explanations: The bride's (and sometimes groom's) midway change of outfit during a wedding reception, typically from a traditional white kimono or white dress to a colored kimono, gown, or other festive outfit.

glosses: to pose (a question); to cast (a glance, a shadow); to throw at
to pose (a question, an issue); to direct toward
to cast (a glance, a smile, a shadow)
to throw toward; to hurl at
explanations: Figurative use: to direct a question, doubt, or topic at someone or at the public. The most common modern usage.
To send out something intangible — a look, expression, or light/shadow — in a particular direction.
Literal sense: to throw an object in someone's direction. Less common than the figurative senses in modern usage.
A commercial service that introduces clients to potential marriage partners through profiles, interviews, and arranged meetings. A modern descendant of traditional matchmaking.

glosses: personal profile for an arranged-marriage meeting
personal profile for arranged-marriage meeting; matchmaking résumé
explanations: A written profile prepared for お{見合|みあい} (matchmaking meetings), traditionally listing the candidate's family background, education, work, hobbies, and other particulars. Exchanged in advance through the matchmaker or marriage agency.
A fee paid to whoever introduces a customer, client, or candidate — common in real estate, recruiting, marriage agencies, and various brokered services.
The individual stitch or the overall pattern of loops in knitting, crochet, or weaving. Also used more broadly for any mesh or interlocking pattern.

glosses: to cut off; to lop off; to chop off
explanations: To cut something so it falls away from the main body — a branch, hair, finger, edge of paper, etc. Implies a clean, complete separation.

glosses: to cut down (with a sword or blade); to slash
to cut down (with a sword or blade); to slash; to slay
explanations: To strike or cut with a sword or other bladed weapon, especially as an act of combat. The {斬|き} kanji distinguishes this from the general {切|き}る (to cut).
Figurative use: to attack or criticize with cutting words. Most common in journalism and commentary.
Describes a clean, decisive cut — like one sword stroke or a single snip — with no jagged edge or hesitation.
Figurative extension: making a clean break with a habit, a relationship, or a desire — quitting once and for all, without lingering attachment. The most common modern usage.
Being so absorbed in an activity or emotion that one forgets oneself. Most commonly seen in the set phrase {無我夢中|むがむちゅう}.
The Buddhist doctrine that there is no permanent, independent self — one of the three marks of existence. Used in Buddhist and philosophical contexts.

glosses: unanimous; unanimous agreement; with the whole assembly in agreement
explanations: A four-character compound meaning that everyone present agreed. Used to describe decisions, votes, and approvals where there is no dissent.
Describes a person, group, or attitude that refuses to help or work together. Formed by adding {非|ひ}〜{的|てき} to {協力|きょうりょく} (cooperation).

glosses: trend; tendency; the way things are heading
explanations: The general direction in which a situation, society, or industry is moving. A formal, literary word often used in analytical or journalistic writing.
A painting or pictorial work executed directly on a wall, whether ancient cave art, religious imagery in temples, or modern street murals.

glosses: standpoint; viewpoint; perspective from which to consider something
explanations: The position or angle from which one considers an issue. Used in formal contexts to indicate the framework or set of values guiding analysis.
The official document presented to a student at graduation, certifying completion of a course of study. Traditionally handed out one by one at the graduation ceremony.

glosses: welcoming fire (lit at start of Obon)
welcoming fire (lit at the start of Obon)
explanations: A small fire lit at the entrance of the home on the first evening of Obon to guide the spirits of ancestors back to the family. Traditionally made by burning ogara (hemp stalks).

glosses: tea drinking; consumption of tea or coffee
explanations: The act of drinking tea or coffee, especially in a leisurely or social context. In contemporary Japanese it appears mostly as part of compound words denoting cafes.

glosses: Hiroshima (city and prefecture in western Japan)
explanations: A major city and prefecture in the Chugoku region. Known worldwide for the August 6, 1945 atomic bombing and its postwar peace memorial sites, as well as for local specialties like oysters and okonomiyaki.

glosses: land reclamation (by draining wetlands or tidal flats)
explanations: Reclaiming usable land from a wetland, lake, or tidal flat by enclosing it with dikes and draining the water. Distinct from filling water in with soil, which is called {埋|う}め{立|た}て.
The sound or manner of large, heavy drops falling. Compared to ぽたぽた, the drops are bigger and the impact heavier, suggesting thick or viscous liquid.

glosses: in a thin trickle; on and on (complaining)
in a thin trickle; dripping continuously
on and on (of complaints, excuses, etc.)
explanations: The manner of a thin, continuous flow of liquid—sweat, blood, oil, or sauce—running rather than falling in discrete drops.
A figurative extension: going on at length with complaints, grumbling, or excuses in a tiresome way.

glosses: oinking (a pig); honking (a horn or buzzer)
explanations: The manner of grumbling, muttering complaints, or expressing dissatisfaction in a sustained, irritating way.
A low buzzing or honking sound—pigs oinking, a car horn, or a buzzer signaling a wrong answer on a quiz show.

glosses: buzzing; humming; whirring (a sustained low sound)
explanations: A drawn-out buzzing or humming sound—an insect flying by, a motor running, a small drone passing overhead.

glosses: after all; you see; the thing is
explanations: Introduces a key explanatory fact or reason that makes the speaker's point understandable. A more casual, conversational variant of なにしろ.

glosses: above all; most importantly; without a doubt
explanations: Used to single out the most outstanding or decisive point in an argument or description. Literally "no matter what one says," it dismisses other considerations and asserts the main point.
Describes something or someone that seems suspect, untrustworthy, or obviously made up. A casual word used when something doesn't ring true, whether a story, an advertisement, or a person's behavior.

glosses: heel (of a shoe); high heels; villain
villain; bad guy (in wrestling or media)
explanations: The raised back portion of a shoe, especially the elevated heel of women's dress shoes. Often used as shorthand for high-heeled shoes.
The villainous character in pro wrestling or, by extension, any narrative. Opposite of ベビーフェイス (the hero).

glosses: stiff; hard; frozen up (with cold or tension)
explanations: Describes something rigid and hard—rock-frozen food, sun-baked clay, or a body stiff with cold or nerves. Also applies figuratively to inflexible people or attitudes.
The crisp ticking sound of a small clock or watch.
The sound or manner of chewing a hard, dry food—senbei, raw vegetables, biscuits—with audible crunching.
The sound or motion of vigorously scratching an itchy spot—the head, back, or arm—often with the fingernails.

glosses: in one bite; with a snap
in one bite; with a single quick snap of the mouth
explanations: The action of opening the mouth wide and taking something in with one bite. Used for both animals snapping at food and people eagerly biting into something.
The sound or manner of someone or something moving through water and making splashes—a child playing in puddles, hands washed under a tap, fish thrashing in a net.
The sound or manner of small, light splashes—a cat lapping water, raindrops hitting a puddle, or someone walking through a shallow film of water.
Describes hair that is unkempt and sticking out in every direction; can also describe other fibrous things (a worn-out broom, dry grass) that have come apart.
Describes someone hanging around blankly without doing what they should be doing. Often used in a scolding tone.
A story or speech in which the speaker brags about their own accomplishments, possessions, family, or experiences. Usually carries a negative tone — listeners find it tedious or off-putting.
Doing something carelessly, arbitrarily, or without proper justification. Often appears on signs and in regulations prohibiting an action without due cause.
Curry in the Indian style, as opposed to Japanese-style curry (カレーライス). Typically thinner, more aromatic, and eaten with naan or basmati rice.
An unpleasant bitter or sharp taste, often associated with raw vegetables like bamboo shoots, spinach, or eggplant. Removed by blanching, soaking, or other preparation.
A prefecture in the northwest of Shikoku, facing the Seto Inland Sea. Known for mikan oranges, Dōgo Onsen, and Matsuyama Castle.
A prefecture on the Kii Peninsula in the Kansai region, facing the Pacific Ocean. Known for mikan oranges, umeboshi plums, and the sacred Kumano Kodō pilgrimage routes.
The ratio of the height to the width of a rectangular image, screen, or object. Used for displays, photos, video formats, and printed materials.
The quality of being uniform throughout, with no variation in composition or properties. Used in materials science, sociology (cultural homogeneity), and statistics.

glosses: worth listening to; engaging to hear
explanations: Said of a story, speech, music, or interview that has enough substance, skill, or depth to reward the listener. The opposite of dull or shallow.

glosses: for what purpose; why; what for
explanations: Asks the purpose or reason for an action, focused on intended outcome rather than cause. Often used rhetorically to question whether something is worthwhile.

glosses: asking after someone's recent situation; checking in
explanations: A polite act of asking how someone has been doing recently. Often the framing of a letter, postcard, or message intended to reconnect with someone the writer has not contacted for a while.

glosses: dramatic pose (in kabuki); striking a pose
explanations: A stylized, frozen pose held by a kabuki actor at a climactic moment, often with crossed eyes and an exaggerated expression. By extension, any showy or boastful display of resolve.
The commercial business of storing other parties' goods for a fee. In Japan, a regulated industry under the Warehousing Business Act ({倉庫業法|そうこぎょうほう}).
Used before a number of years to express how long ago a building was built. Almost exclusively seen in real estate listings: {築|ちく}10{年|ねん} = "built 10 years ago."

glosses: a little while ago; a bit earlier; just before
explanations: Refers to a short time before the present or before some specified moment. Can describe minutes, hours, days, or weeks earlier depending on context.
An area where there is significant risk to safety or life — due to natural hazards, conflict, crime, or industrial conditions. Used literally on warning signs and figuratively in casual speech.
A protective mask worn to filter out poisonous gases, harmful chemicals, or toxic dust. Used in military, industrial, and emergency response contexts.

glosses: destination of transmission; recipient; To: address
explanations: The address or party to which an email, fax, or other electronic communication is sent. The label of the To: field on forms and email clients.
A person who looks after a warehouse — receiving deliveries, managing inventory, and watching over stored goods. Also the Japanese name of the puzzle video game known internationally as Sokoban.
Containers (bottles, cans, boxes) and packaging (wrappers, films) used to hold or protect goods, considered collectively. Common term in recycling and waste-management regulation.
A real number that cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers — examples include π (pi), √2, and e. Contrasted with rational numbers ({有理数|ゆうりすう}).
The height of a person, measured from feet to head. The everyday way of referring to how tall someone is.

glosses: if that's the case; if it is; then
if that's the case; if it is; in that case
explanations: Casual conditional expression formed from だった (past of だ) plus ら. Follows nouns and na-adjective stems. Often used as a discourse connector meaning 'in that case' or 'if so', and can open a new clause in response to something just said.

glosses: smooth and dry (of texture or feel)
explanations: Describes a texture that is dry, smooth, and non-sticky — the opposite of sticky or damp. Often used of skin, fabric, sand, or powder.
Describes doing something in a smooth, unfussy way — saying something offhandedly, skimming through a text quickly, or handling a situation without making a fuss.

glosses: soggy; wet and mushy; soaking wet
explanations: Mimetic word describing something unpleasantly wet, soggy, or soaked — food that has absorbed too much liquid and lost its texture, or a surface or object that is dripping wet or sticky.

glosses: french fries; fried potato strips or wedges
explanations: Deep-fried potato strips or wedges, equivalent to what is called 'french fries' in American English or 'chips' in British English. In Japan, the term most commonly refers to the thin, elongated style served at fast-food restaurants.

glosses: person who founded a company or business
explanations: The person who started or established a company, shop, or organization. Formed from 創業 (founding a business) and 者 (person). Often used when referring to the original founder by name or legacy.
The quality of being morally right, logically justified, or socially acceptable. Often used when questioning or asserting whether an action, decision, or claim is properly grounded.

glosses: to be crestfallen; to lose spirit; to be dejected
to be crestfallen; to be dejected; to lose one's spirit
