explanations: To become visibly discouraged or downcast, typically after a failure, scolding, or disappointment. Suggests a sudden loss of energy or confidence, often shown through slumped posture or a subdued demeanor.
The hand tightly closed with fingers curled into the palm. Used literally when describing a physical gesture, and figuratively to convey determination, anger, or readiness to fight.

The hips or buttocks as a body part or clothing measurement. Commonly used in clothing sizes alongside バスト (bust) and ウエスト (waist). Also used informally to refer to the shape of the hips and buttocks.

Operating or existing without the required official approval, license, or certification. Formed from 無 (without) and 認可 (official approval/license). Most commonly appears as a prenoun modifier before a noun.

glosses: lactose; the sugar naturally present in milk
explanations: The sugar naturally present in milk and dairy products. Formed from 乳 (milk) and 糖 (sugar). Relevant in discussions of food ingredients, nutrition, and lactose intolerance.

glosses: mixed rice; rice mixed with toppings after cooking
mixed rice; rice stirred together with cooked ingredients
explanations: A rice dish made by mixing cooked rice with separately prepared ingredients such as vegetables, mushrooms, seafood, or meat. Distinguished from 炊き込みご飯, where the ingredients are cooked together with the rice from the start.

glosses: pie; pastry with a filling in a flaky or shortcrust shell
explanations: A baked dish with a pastry crust and sweet or savory filling, from English 'pie'. Also refers to the pastry dough itself (パイ生地). Common in compound names for specific pies and pastry products.

glosses: snap; click; single sharp snapping sound
snap; click; sound of a single sharp snap or click
explanations: Mimetic word for a single crisp snapping or clicking sound — a rubber band breaking, a clasp latching shut, a finger snap, or a light slap. The single-occurrence counterpart to ぱちぱち (repeated).

glosses: stuffed to capacity; bulging; packed full
stuffed full; bulging; packed to capacity
explanations: Mimetic word describing something stretched or filled to its limit — a bag packed until it bulges, a stomach so full it is taut, or a schedule with no free slots. Suggests the thing is about to burst or has no more room.

glosses: to face; to tackle; to be present at
to face; to tackle; to be present at (an occasion)
to face; to overlook (a view or location)
explanations: To face an event, challenge, or formal occasion, often with a sense of readiness or resolve. Used for competitions, exams, ceremonies, or any important occasion one is about to participate in.
Of a building, room, or location: to face onto or overlook something such as the sea, a plaza, or a mountain. Used in formal or descriptive writing.

Mimetic adverb describing a pleasingly slender figure or shape. Used for people's builds (waist, legs, arms) and occasionally for thin objects. Has a positive nuance, suggesting graceful thinness rather than unhealthy thinness.

glosses: academic harassment; abuse of power in academic settings
explanations: Harassment or abuse of authority within academic institutions, typically by faculty, supervisors, or senior researchers against students, junior researchers, or staff. Abbreviated from アカデミックハラスメント. Includes unfair grading, withholding academic support as punishment, or demeaning treatment.

glosses: alcohol harassment; pressuring others to drink
alcohol harassment; coercing or pressuring someone to drink
explanations: Harassment through alcohol — forcibly offering drinks to someone who has declined, mocking non-drinkers, or pressuring someone to keep drinking until ill. Abbreviated from アルコールハラスメント. Common in discussions of Japanese workplace drinking culture.

glosses: glass marble; small glass ball used as a toy
explanations: A small glass ball used as a children's toy, often in games where players flick or roll the marbles. The name likely comes from ビードロ (glass, from Portuguese vidro) plus 玉 (ball/sphere).
The quality of being original, unique, or creatively independent. Borrowed from English 'originality'. Often used in contexts of art, writing, business ideas, or personal style.
Describes something that provokes irritation or frustration. Used for situations, behaviors, or circumstances that make one feel agitated and impatient.

glosses: activities aimed at conceiving; fertility efforts
activities and efforts aimed at becoming pregnant
explanations: Informal abbreviation of {妊娠|にんしん}{活動|かつどう} (pregnancy activities). Refers to the lifestyle adjustments, medical consultations, and fertility treatments a couple undertakes when trying to conceive.

glosses: to collapse onto; to fall into; to tumble in
to collapse onto or into something; to fall and land heavily
explanations: To fall or collapse in a way that results in ending up on or inside something — a bed, a chair, a room, or a person. The ～込む suffix emphasizes the completeness of falling in or into a space.

glosses: with a cool draft; with a cold airy feeling
with a cool, airy, or drafty sensation; with a tingling cool feeling
explanations: Mimetic word (擬態語) describing the sensation of cool air flowing over or through something — like wind through a gap, mint on the tongue, or cold air on the skin. Can feel refreshing or unpleasantly chilly depending on context.

glosses: with a sudden cold sensation; with a startling chill
with a sudden unpleasant cold sensation; with a chilling start
explanations: Mimetic word describing a sudden, unpleasant cold sensation — touching something unexpectedly cold, stepping onto a cold floor, or feeling a chill of fear. Also used figuratively for the psychological 'chill' of a near-miss or frightening moment.

glosses: iron fist; hard punch; a blow with a clenched fist
explanations: Literally 'iron fist'. Refers to a powerful punch or blow with the fist. Used figuratively for forceful, authoritarian control or discipline.

glosses: eating in large bites; heart pounding
eating greedily in large bites; munching away
explanations: Mimetic word describing the action of eating large mouthfuls quickly and enthusiastically, often suggesting a big appetite.
Describes the sensation of the heart beating fast and hard, as from excitement, anxiety, or physical exertion. Used with する: {心臓|しんぞう}がばくばくする.

glosses: rummaging noisily; making a rustling, scraping sound while searching
explanations: Mimetic word for the sound and action of digging or searching through things — such as rummaging in a bag, shuffling through papers, or moving through dry leaves. Suggests both the sound and the slightly messy, searching motion.

glosses: to curl up; to roll into a ball; to become rounded
to curl up; to roll into a ball; to coil up
explanations: To become round or curl into a ball shape. Used for people, animals, or objects that take on a rounded, contracted form — like a cat curling up, a person hunching into a fetal position, or a leaf rolling up.

glosses: presentation; formal oral or visual presentation
explanations: A formal presentation of information, proposals, or ideas, typically to an audience. Usually involves slides, visuals, or structured speaking. Commonly abbreviated to プレゼン in everyday use.
An act that is morally or legally wrong. Can range from minor misconduct to serious crimes. Commonly appears in the proverb {悪事|あくじ}{千里|せんり}を{走|はし}る (bad news travels fast).
The Japanese five-yen coin. Distinctive for its brass color and the hole in the center. Often used as an offering at Shinto shrines because ごえん sounds like ご{縁|えん} (good ties, favorable connections).

glosses: postnatal; after giving birth; the postpartum period
explanations: The period following childbirth. Used as a noun or prenominal modifier to describe the physical, emotional, or lifestyle aspects of a mother's or infant's life after birth.

glosses: slightly thin; on the light side; a bit diluted
somewhat thin, light, or diluted; on the weak side
explanations: Formed from {薄|うす}い (thin, light, weak, diluted) + め (suffix indicating 'somewhat' or 'on the _ side'). Describes something that is moderately thin, light in color, diluted, or sparse — slightly below average intensity.

glosses: consultation office; advice center; counseling center
consultation office; counseling center; advice bureau
explanations: An office or center providing guidance, consultation, or advice on a specific topic. Common types include legal advice centers, child welfare consultation offices, marriage consultation agencies, and medical advisory services.

glosses: to keep saying; to continue to say
to keep saying; to continue saying without stopping
explanations: To persist in saying something — repeatedly or over a sustained period. Compound of {言|い}う (to say) + {続|つづ}ける (to continue). Emphasizes persistence or repetition of speech.

glosses: to come in; to flow in; to enter (toward the speaker)
to come in; to enter (moving toward the speaker or scene)
explanations: Compound of {入|はい}る (to enter) + くる (to come). Expresses the movement of something entering a space from outside, with the directional sense of movement toward the speaker or the focal scene. Used for people, air, light, information, or other things flowing in.

glosses: city block; urban block; block of buildings bounded by streets
explanations: A block of land bounded by streets in an urban area — the basic unit of city planning. Used in urban development, addresses, and city planning documents.

glosses: prevention law; law for the prevention of [something]
explanations: A legal act or statute aimed at preventing a specific harm or undesirable activity. Always appears in compound names specifying what is being prevented. Used across fields including public health, crime, environmental protection, and harassment.

glosses: auscultation; listening to internal body sounds
auscultation; examination by listening to internal body sounds
explanations: A medical examination in which a doctor listens to sounds from the heart, lungs, or intestines, usually through a stethoscope ({聴診器|ちょうしんき}). {聴診|ちょうしん}する means to perform this examination.
The major artery on each side of the neck that supplies blood to the head and brain. Its pulse is often checked in first aid to confirm that the heart is beating.
The arteries that wrap around the heart and supply it with blood. When one becomes blocked, the result can be a heart attack ({心筋梗塞|しんきんこうそく}).
Cancer of the pancreas ({膵臓|すいぞう}). Known for being difficult to detect early and for having a poor prognosis. The second element is often written in kana as {膵臓|すいぞう}がん.
A small sac-shaped organ beneath the liver that stores bile ({胆汁|たんじゅう}). Gallstones ({胆石|たんせき}) are a common problem associated with it.
The first section of the small intestine, just beyond the stomach. It is the site of duodenal ulcers ({十二指腸潰瘍|じゅうにしちょうかいよう}).
Tiny drops of liquid scattered into the air — from splashing water, a wave, or from coughing and sneezing. Widely known from {飛沫感染|ひまつかんせん} (droplet transmission of disease).

glosses: 70th birthday; celebration of one's seventieth year
explanations: A traditional celebration of a person's 70th birthday. The name comes from a line by the poet Du Fu, {人生|じんせい}{七十|しちじゅう}{古来|こらい}{稀|まれ}なり ("a life of seventy years has been rare since ancient times"). Also written {古稀|こき}.

glosses: 77th birthday; celebration of one's seventy-seventh year
explanations: A celebration of a person's 77th birthday. The term comes from the cursive form of the character {喜|よろこ}び (joy), whose shape resembles the figures for seventy-seven.

glosses: middle blessing; a moderately good fortune (on an omikuji)
explanations: A fortune level on an {御神籤|おみくじ} (paper fortune drawn at shrines and temples), ranking below {大吉|だいきち} (great blessing) and above {小吉|しょうきち} (small blessing).

glosses: small blessing; a slightly good fortune (on an omikuji)
explanations: A fortune level on an {御神籤|おみくじ} indicating a small amount of good luck. It generally ranks below {中吉|ちゅうきち} (middle blessing).

glosses: future blessing; good fortune that will come later (on an omikuji)
explanations: A fortune level on an {御神籤|おみくじ} meaning that good luck lies ahead rather than now — a sign to be patient. It is one of the lower-ranking blessings.

A company officer, required in many Japanese {株式会社|かぶしきがいしゃ} (joint-stock companies), who oversees how the directors perform their duties and audits the company's accounts. A statutory role distinct from an outside accounting firm.

glosses: apron; aircraft parking area (at an airport)
explanations: The area of an airport where aircraft are parked, loaded and unloaded, refueled, and boarded. Called the "apron" or "ramp" in English.

glosses: delayed arrival; arriving later than scheduled
explanations: Arrival later than the scheduled time, typically of a train, bus, plane, or delivery. {延着|えんちゃく}する means to arrive late.

glosses: to close (one's eyes); to shut (one's eyes)
explanations: To shut one's eyes. Almost always used with {目|め} (eyes) as the object: {目|め}をつぶる. Occasionally written {瞑|つぶ}る.

glosses: to insist (stubbornly); to assert firmly; to maintain
to insist (stubbornly); to assert firmly; to maintain (one's claim)
explanations: To stubbornly hold to and keep asserting one's own opinion or claim, refusing to back down even when challenged. Often carries a nuance of unreasonable stubbornness.

glosses: unprecedented and unrepeatable; the first and last of its kind
unprecedented and never to be repeated; utterly unparalleled
explanations: A four-character idiom ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}) describing something so extraordinary that nothing like it has happened before ({空前|くうぜん}, never seen before) and nothing like it will happen again ({絶後|ぜつご}, none after). Usually used with の before a noun.

glosses: chattering away; talking on and on; (speaking) fluently
rattling on; chattering; (speaking) volubly or fluently
explanations: Describes speaking rapidly, fluently, and at length. Depending on context it can be negative (blabbing, talking too much, revealing what one shouldn't) or neutral-to-positive (speaking a language fluently and effortlessly).

glosses: with heavy clumsy footsteps; clomping; stomping
with loud, heavy footsteps; clomping around noisily
explanations: The sound or manner of heavy, clumsy footsteps — people running or walking noisily, as on a wooden floor or stairs. Often suggests a lack of grace or of consideration for the noise.

glosses: seat belt; safety belt in a vehicle
explanations: A safety harness worn in a vehicle to secure the occupant in their seat. Legally required for drivers and passengers in Japan.
The feeling of longing for one's home, family, or familiar surroundings when living away from home. Often experienced by students, overseas workers, or anyone living far from their hometown.

glosses: old age; advanced age; being elderly
explanations: The state of being old or having reached an advanced age. Used in formal, legal, and medical contexts more often than conversational speech.

glosses: period of staleness; stage when a relationship loses its spark
explanations: A period in a romantic relationship when the initial excitement has faded and both partners feel boredom or indifference toward each other. Commonly discussed in the context of couples and marriage.
A small olive-brown bird native to Japan, famous for its distinctive call ホーホケキョ. Associated with spring and considered one of Japan's most beloved birds.

glosses: splish-splashing; light, gentle splashing of water
explanations: An onomatopoeic word describing the soft, rhythmic sound of water splashing gently — as when wading in shallow water, playing in a puddle, or water lapping against something.

glosses: splash; the sound of a single large object hitting water
explanations: An onomatopoeic word for a single, heavy splash — the sound and sensation of something (or someone) plunging into water with force.

glosses: thud-thud; sound of heavy, repeated thumping footsteps
explanations: An onomatopoeic word describing the heavy, rhythmic thumping sound of footsteps — typically of a large person or someone walking forcefully. Suggests weight and lack of grace.

glosses: jerky; choppy; stuttering movement or animation
explanations: An onomatopoeic word describing motion that is not smooth — moving in sharp, angular, mechanical increments rather than fluidly. Commonly used for video playback, animation, or robotic movement.
A declaration that one will not respond to a question or make a statement. Used in press conferences, interviews, and legal contexts, directly borrowed from English.

glosses: first ever in history; historical first; unprecedented achievement
explanations: A compound meaning "first time in history." Used to describe an event, achievement, or occurrence that has no precedent in recorded history.

glosses: delayed departure; a departure that is behind schedule
explanations: A departure (of a train, bus, airplane, or ship) that is delayed beyond its scheduled time. Used primarily in transportation contexts.
The medical act of removing an organ, tumor, or other tissue from the body through surgery. Also used more generally for extracting or removing objects.

glosses: ulcer; open sore on a body surface or lining
explanations: An open lesion or sore that forms on the surface of an organ or tissue, especially the lining of the stomach or intestines. Used in medical contexts.

glosses: heart sound; sound produced by the heartbeat
explanations: The sounds produced by the beating heart, heard through a stethoscope during a medical examination. Used in medical and clinical contexts.

glosses: palpation; examination by feeling with the hands
explanations: A medical examination technique in which a doctor presses or feels the body with their hands to assess organs, detect abnormalities, or check for tenderness or swelling.

glosses: bile; digestive fluid produced by the liver
explanations: A yellow-green digestive fluid produced by the liver, stored in the gallbladder, and released into the small intestine to aid in fat digestion.

glosses: gallstone; hard deposit forming in the gallbladder
explanations: A hardened deposit of digestive fluid that can form in the gallbladder or bile ducts. Gallstones can cause severe abdominal pain and may require surgical removal.
An onomatopoeic word for the chirping sound of sparrows or similar small birds. Often evokes a peaceful morning scene.

glosses: hōhokekyo; the distinctive call of the Japanese bush warbler
explanations: The onomatopoeic representation of the call of the {鶯|うぐいす} (Japanese bush warbler). This call is strongly associated with spring and is one of the most iconic bird sounds in Japanese culture.

glosses: mourning; period of mourning after a death
explanations: The period of grief and abstention from celebrations following the death of a family member or close relative. Traditionally lasting 49 days in Buddhism.

glosses: to comply with; to observe; to submit to
to observe; to comply with; to submit to (a rule, period, or authority)
explanations: To follow or observe a prescribed duty, rule, or period. Most commonly used in the phrase 喪に服す (to observe mourning). Also written 服する, the longer form.

glosses: end of the mourning period; lifting of mourning
explanations: The day or time when the formal mourning period concludes, traditionally 49 days after a death in Buddhism (四十九日). After this point, one can resume normal social and celebratory activities.

glosses: to stifle; to suppress; to bite back
to stifle; to suppress (a yawn, laugh, or impulse)
explanations: To suppress or hold back a physical or emotional response, especially a yawn or laugh. The image is of biting something to stop it from escaping.

glosses: academic success; fulfillment of one's studies
explanations: The successful completion of one's studies or academic goals. A common wish printed on good-luck charms (お守り) sold at shrines and temples, typically for students.

glosses: prayer for passing an exam; wish for exam success
explanations: A prayer or wish offered at a shrine or temple to pass an entrance exam or certification test. Expressed through visiting shrines, buying good-luck charms, or writing on votive tablets.

A type of hard igneous rock widely used in Japan for gravestones, building foundations, stone lanterns, and paving. The name comes from Mikage, a district in Kobe historically famous for quarrying this stone.

glosses: Izumo Grand Shrine; major Shinto shrine in Shimane Prefecture
explanations: One of the most important and ancient Shinto shrines in Japan, located in Izumo, Shimane Prefecture. Dedicated to Ōkuninushi no Mikoto, the deity associated with marriage and relationships. A major pilgrimage destination.

glosses: NHK New Year's Eve music special
NHK Kōhaku Uta Gassen; annual New Year's Eve singing competition on NHK
explanations: Japan's most-watched annual TV broadcast, airing on NHK every New Year's Eve (December 31). Popular singers are divided into two teams — Red (female artists) and White (male artists) — who compete in performances judged by audience and panel. A cultural milestone since 1951.
The Japanese representation of a rooster's crow. Represents the call of a rooster (おんどり), heard especially at dawn.

glosses: caw caw; cawing of a crow
caw caw; the cry of a crow
explanations: The Japanese representation of a crow's cawing sound. Crows ({カラス|からす}) are common in Japanese cities and their loud calls are a familiar urban sound.

glosses: each department; every section (in an organization)
explanations: A reference to all departments or sections within a company or organization, used when addressing or involving multiple divisions collectively.

glosses: Lego; interlocking plastic building blocks (brand name)
explanations: A brand of colorful interlocking plastic construction blocks made by the Danish company Lego. In Japanese, the full term レゴブロック (Lego blocks) is also used. One of the world's most popular toys.
A person who does bad things or has bad intentions. Used in both literal contexts (a criminal) and figurative or dramatic ones (a villain in a story).

glosses: with a self-satisfied grin; with a smug or pleased smile
explanations: Describes the expression or manner of someone smiling to themselves out of self-satisfaction, smug pleasure, or quiet delight — often when something went their way or they have a secret advantage.
Describes the sound or manner of heavy, repeated footsteps, or of a group of people or things moving into a space noisily all at once.

glosses: sparse; full of gaps; not densely packed; hollow
explanations: Describes something that is full of empty spaces, not densely filled, or lacks the expected substance. Can be used for physical objects (a bag with lots of empty space, a drawer with few items) or more figurative contexts.

glosses: crackling; snapping; the sound of sparks or larger flames
explanations: The sound of something crackling sharply and repeatedly, such as a large fire, sparks from electricity, or oil splattering. Represents a louder, sharper crackling than ぱちぱち.

glosses: to come out; to appear; to emerge
to come out; to emerge (toward the speaker or from within)
to appear; to come up (in conversation, text, or data)
explanations: To come out of an enclosed space, to emerge from somewhere, or to appear on the scene. Combines 出る (to exit) with くる (to come), indicating movement toward the speaker or present location.
To appear or turn up in a non-physical sense — such as a word appearing in a book, a name coming up in conversation, or a problem emerging.

glosses: illumination; decorative light display; Christmas lights
explanations: Decorative electric lighting displays, especially the large-scale LED light installations that appear at parks, shopping areas, and tourist spots in Japan from autumn through winter. Particularly associated with Christmas-season decoration and romantic date spots.

glosses: tending to; prone to; apt to
explanations: A suffix attached to the masu-stem of a verb, indicating a tendency or habitual inclination — often but not always with a negative connotation. The resulting form can function as a noun modifier (with な or の) or as a predicate.

glosses: to suffer; to taste; to experience (defeat, loss)
to suffer; to sustain; to experience (something negative)
explanations: To undergo or receive something unpleasant — typically defeat, a loss, or a setback. Used in formal and written contexts; the most common collocates are {敗北|はいぼく} (defeat) and {惨敗|ざんぱい} (crushing defeat).

glosses: slump; losing streak; dry spell; rut
explanations: A period of poor performance or diminished output, particularly in sports, creative work, or business. From English "slump".

glosses: throwaway price; rock-bottom price; dirt-cheap price
explanations: A price so low it is as if the item were being thrown away — used for goods sold well below market value, often in clearance sales, distressed sales, or urgent liquidations.

Traditional Japanese sandals woven from straw rope ({藁|わら}), secured to the foot with cords and worn directly against the bare foot or over tabi socks. The standard footwear for commoners, travelers, and soldiers in premodern Japan.

glosses: behind; trailing; deficit (in a competition or score)
explanations: Being behind in score or points during a sports match or competition. From English "behind". Often used with a numeric prefix indicating the number of points or runs one is trailing by.
A count of one win in a sporting or competitive context. Often used in win-loss records (e.g., 一勝一敗 = one win, one loss) or emphasizing the significance of a single victory.

The Buddhist memorial service held on the 33rd anniversary of a person's death (counted in the Japanese way, with the year of death counted as the first year). In many traditions, this is the final major memorial service, after which the deceased is considered to have fully become a Buddha or ancestral spirit.

A condition in which the body cannot properly digest lactose (the sugar in milk and dairy products) due to insufficient production of the enzyme lactase. Symptoms include bloating, diarrhea, and stomach pain after consuming dairy.
The relative importance or urgency assigned to a task, issue, or item. Used in project management, medicine, and everyday scheduling to rank competing demands.

glosses: certainty; reliability; sureness; degree of certainty
explanations: The quality of being certain or reliable — the extent to which something can be counted on to happen or be true. Used when evaluating predictions, plans, methods, or outcomes.

glosses: adaptability; flexibility; ability to adjust to new conditions
explanations: The capacity to adjust smoothly to new environments, circumstances, or demands. Can describe a person's temperament, a biological organism's response to its environment, or a system's flexibility.
The medical or formal term for nasal mucus or discharge. Used in clinical contexts. In everyday speech, {鼻水|はなみず} is far more common.

glosses: thank-you gift from a recovered patient; get-well return gift
thank-you gift from a recovered patient; return gift after recovery from illness
explanations: A gift given by a person who has recovered from illness or injury to those who sent get-well gifts or visited during their recovery. Part of the Japanese {内祝|うちいわい} (reciprocal gift) custom, sent within one month of recovery.

glosses: body composition analyzer; body composition scale
explanations: A device that measures body composition — including body fat percentage, muscle mass, bone density, and water content — in addition to weight. More advanced than a standard scale ({体重計|たいじゅうけい}).
The official legal term for motorcycles in Japan, used in vehicle registration, traffic laws, and formal contexts. In everyday speech, オートバイ or バイク are far more common.

glosses: lacking energy; dull; lifeless; not lively
explanations: An expression describing a place, atmosphere, group, or person that lacks vitality, liveliness, or bustling energy. The opposite of {活気がある|かっきがある} (full of energy, lively).

headword: パンティストッキング
explanations: Sheer nylon hosiery that covers from the waist to the feet in one piece. From English "panty stockings". Often abbreviated to パンスト in casual speech.

headword: 亭主元気で留守がいい
glosses: a wife is happiest when her husband is out
a wife is happiest when her husband is out; better when the husband is healthy and away
explanations: A humorous proverb expressing that a wife prefers her husband to be healthy enough to go to work and stay out of the house, rather than being home all day. Reflects a traditional housewife perspective on domestic life.
A gain or favorable outcome, especially financial profit or practical advantage. Appears frequently as a component in compound words.
Interest paid on borrowed money or earned on savings. Used in financial contexts, particularly in compound nouns.

glosses: by force; by brute strength; forcibly
explanations: Relying on physical strength or coercive power rather than reason, negotiation, or skill. Almost always used in the pattern {力|ちから}ずくで (by force).

glosses: swirling dust; dust cloud; sandy dust
swirling dust; cloud of fine sand or dust particles
explanations: Fine particles of sand or dust suspended or swirling in the air, typically raised by wind, vehicles, or activity on dry ground.

glosses: terms of service; terms of use
terms of service; terms of use; usage agreement
explanations: A legal agreement setting out the rules and conditions for using a service, website, or application. Users typically must agree to these terms before registering or using the service.

glosses: casual quotation particle; said that; asked that
casual topic marker; speaking of; as for
explanations: Casual spoken equivalent of と or という, marking quoted speech, thoughts, or reported information. Follows the quoted content.
Marks information received from another source rather than directly experienced. Often translated as 'they say that' or 'apparently.' Often appears as ってよ or ってさ.
Casual equivalent of は, introducing or re-introducing a topic, often with a nuance of 'what do you mean by X?' or defining/questioning a topic.

glosses: it seems; looks like; similar to
it seems; it looks like; apparently
explanations: Colloquial equivalent of ようだ. Expresses inference or appearance based on observation. Attaches to the plain form of verbs and adjectives, and directly to nouns.
Expresses a comparison or resemblance, functioning like the English 'like' or 'as if.' Used with みたいな (noun modifier) or みたいに (adverb).

glosses: that's right; yes, that's so (Kansai dialect)
explanations: Kansai (especially Osaka/Kyoto) dialect equivalent of standard そうだ. Used to confirm, agree, or affirm a statement. Also used as an exclamation of sudden recollection ('Oh right!', 'That's it!').

glosses: yeah, right; that's right, isn't it (Kansai dialect)
explanations: Kansai dialect equivalent of そうだね or そうですね. Used to agree with or acknowledge something just said, or to seek light agreement from the listener. Common in Osaka, Kyoto, and Kobe speech.

glosses: fixed-term imprisonment; prison sentence of a specified duration
explanations: A prison sentence for a defined period, as opposed to {無期懲役|むきちょうえき} (life imprisonment). Under Japanese law, the range is 1 month to 30 years, typically stated as {懲役|ちょうえき}X{年|ねん} (X years of imprisonment).
An absorbent pad worn during menstruation to absorb menstrual flow. Sold in convenience stores and drug stores in Japan, often in separate daytime and nighttime varieties.

glosses: adult entertainment establishment; sex industry business
adult entertainment establishment; business in the sex or hostess industry
explanations: A business that falls under Japan's entertainment licensing regulations ({風俗営業法|ふうぞくえいぎょうほう}), ranging from hostess bars and cabaret clubs to more explicit adult services. Commonly appears in news coverage of entertainment districts and law enforcement.

glosses: boil-and-drain cooking; cooking in hot water
boil-and-drain method; cooking by boiling in excess water
explanations: A cooking method in which food (especially rice) is cooked in a large volume of boiling water, then drained. For rice, it produces a different texture than the standard absorption method used in rice cookers.

glosses: with a thud; plop; straight down
with a thud; plop; straight down (falling sound/manner)
explanations: Describes something falling or dropping suddenly and directly, often with a sound. An intensified form of すとんと. Conveys a clean, swift drop or fall.
A cream applied to the skin to chemically dissolve and remove body hair. Applied, left for a few minutes, then wiped off along with the hair. Used as an alternative to shaving or waxing.
Formal and polite equivalent of について. Used in business correspondence, official announcements, and respectful speech when introducing the topic under discussion.

glosses: seven-five meter; alternating 7- and 5-syllable rhythmic pattern
explanations: A traditional Japanese rhythmic pattern alternating phrases of 7 and 5 syllables. Fundamental to waka poetry, enka lyrics, folk songs, and many traditional chants. Feels natural and melodious to Japanese speakers.

glosses: smooth talk; sweet words; lip service
smooth talk; glib talk; relying on words alone
explanations: Talking skillfully with words but without genuine substance or follow-through. Implies that someone's actions or character do not match their polished speech. Often used critically.

glosses: already read; read (of a message or document)
explanations: Indicates that something (a book, message, email, or document) has already been read. Used both for physical reading and digital read-receipt status in apps such as LINE.

glosses: perforation; line of small holes for tearing
explanations: A row of small holes or cuts in paper or packaging that allows a section to be torn off cleanly. Common on envelopes, receipts, stamps, tickets, and forms.

glosses: six-day calendar cycle; traditional Japanese lucky-day system
six-day repeating calendar cycle for auspiciousness
explanations: A traditional Japanese calendar system dividing days into six types with varying degrees of luck. Still widely consulted for scheduling weddings, business openings, and funerals. The six days cycle through the month.

glosses: nice; lucky you; sounds good (Kansai dialect)
nice; lucky you; that's wonderful (Kansai dialect)
explanations: Kansai dialect expression meaning 'how nice,' 'lucky you,' or 'I'd love that.' Used to express envy, admiration, or approving agreement. The Kansai equivalent of standard いいなあ.
Doing something intentionally, often with the nuance that the action is excessive or unnecessary — going out of one's way to do it.
Emphasizing that something stands out to a notable degree, more than one might expect.

glosses: to return; to be returned; to revert
to return; to be returned; to come back
to revert; to return to a previous state
explanations: Of something borrowed, lent, or taken — to come back to its owner or original place. Often used with きた to mean something has come back.
To go back to a former condition, such as consciousness returning, a situation reverting, or something going back to normal.

glosses: here you are; please go ahead; yes, certainly
explanations: A polite expression used when handing something to someone, when granting permission or inviting someone to proceed, or when responding affirmatively to a request or knock.

glosses: in order to; so as to; with the aim of
explanations: Formal expression attached to the dictionary form of a verb to indicate purpose or intent. The conjunctive form of べし. Common in formal written Japanese including news, business, and formal speech.

Classical auxiliary expressing strong obligation, appropriateness, or natural expectation. Attaches to the dictionary form of a verb. Found in formal maxims, notices, classical literature, and stiff written prose.

glosses: must; have to; be obliged to
explanations: Formal or literary contraction of 〜なければならない expressing necessity or obligation. Attaches to the nai-stem of a verb. More formal than the colloquial なきゃ or なくちゃ forms.
Colloquial contraction of 〜なければならない used in everyday spoken Japanese to express obligation or necessity. The なきゃ part contracts なければ.

glosses: to tell (someone) to; to ask (someone) to; to instruct to
explanations: Used to report an indirect command or request. The speaker conveys what they told or asked someone else to do. Follows the dictionary or nai form of a verb.

glosses: such-and-such a place; some place or other; a certain place
explanations: A reduplicated placeholder pronoun used in place of a specific location that the speaker does not specify, does not know exactly, or wants to leave vague. Often used to avoid naming a place or to keep it deliberately unspecified.
Highly polite way of asking who someone is. Used in formal service contexts such as hotels, receptions, and business settings. More deferential than どなた alone.

glosses: already; even at this stage; by this point
explanations: Formal or literary expression emphasizing that something has already happened — often at an earlier point than expected, or at the very stage under discussion. A more emphatic and literary form of すでに.

glosses: what the heck; come on; so what
explanations: Rough masculine expression conveying mild frustration, surprise, or exasperation. Used when something is unexpected, disappointing, or annoying. The tone ranges from mild complaint to reproach.

glosses: what?!; what did you say?; you don't say!
explanations: Colloquial expression used to express surprise at something just heard, or to ask someone to repeat what they said. The surprise can be genuine shock, disbelief, or simply not having caught what was said.

glosses: to achieve fame and success; to attain distinction; to make a name for oneself
to achieve fame and success; to attain distinction
explanations: Formal or literary expression meaning to accomplish great things and build a lasting reputation. Often used in biographies, formal speeches, and writing about notable achievements.

glosses: scholarly temperament; academic bent; scholar type
explanations: Describes a person whose natural disposition is toward academic study and research. Such a person is typically focused, detail-oriented, and more interested in learning than in practical or commercial pursuits.

glosses: it's fine; that's okay; no problem (Kansai)
it's fine; that's okay; no problem
explanations: Kansai dialect expression combining いい (good, fine) and the Kansai sentence-final particle やん (assertive, seeking confirmation). Used to say something is acceptable or to reassure someone that there is no problem. Equivalent to standard いいじゃないか or いいよ.

glosses: to apply; to be applicable; to fall under; to qualify
explanations: To meet the relevant criteria or conditions; to be included in a certain category or classification. Common in formal, legal, and administrative contexts.

The social and economic class between the wealthy upper class and the lower class. In Japan, commonly used in sociological and political discussion to describe the broad group of moderately prosperous working and professional people.

glosses: aerial photography; filming from the air
explanations: Photography or video recording taken from an aircraft, helicopter, or drone. Originally specialized to film and broadcast, now common with consumer drones.

glosses: rice bran; outer husk removed in milling
explanations: The outer layer of brown rice that is removed during milling to produce white rice. Used extensively in traditional Japanese pickling and as a fertilizer.

glosses: scrubbing brush; scouring pad for kitchen use
explanations: A stiff brush or abrasive pad used for scrubbing pots, vegetables, and other items. Traditionally made from palm fibers; modern versions include metal and nylon varieties.

glosses: beginner; person at the elementary level
explanations: A person who is at the elementary or beginner level of a skill, language, or activity. Often used in educational or sports contexts to describe the lowest proficiency group.

glosses: enthusiast; person who loves and pursues a particular interest
explanations: A person with a strong fondness for and interest in a particular activity, art form, or subject. More formal than ファン; often implies active participation rather than passive appreciation.

A ceremonial occasion of celebration or festivity, often with communal significance. More formal and literary than 祭り; used in contexts describing public celebrations, holidays, or commemorative events.

glosses: film adaptation; visual adaptation; adaptation to screen
adaptation to film, TV, or animation; bringing to screen
explanations: The process of adapting a story, novel, manga, or other work into a visual medium such as film, television drama, or animation. A very common concept in Japanese media culture.

glosses: new graduate hiring; recruitment of fresh graduates
hiring of new graduates; fresh graduate recruitment
explanations: The Japanese practice of companies hiring university or high school graduates all at once in spring, typically for April entry. A defining feature of traditional Japanese employment culture, contrasting with 中途採用 (mid-career hiring).

glosses: variant form of a kanji character with the same reading and meaning
explanations: An alternate written form of a kanji that shares the same reading and meaning as the standard form but differs in stroke composition. Examples include 峯/峰 and 塚/塚. Commonly encountered in names and older texts.

glosses: official booklet certifying a person's disability for welfare services
explanations: An official government-issued booklet certifying that a person has a recognized disability. It is used to access various support services, tax exemptions, discounts, and welfare benefits in Japan. There are three types depending on the kind of disability.
A state of feeling down, depressed, or discouraged. The noun form of the verb 落ち込む. Used to describe temporary low moods rather than clinical depression.
A period of reduced activity, performance, or numbers, especially in business or economic contexts. Equivalent to a slump or downturn.

glosses: driving force; propulsive power (of engine, motor, etc.)
explanations: The mechanical force that drives or propels a machine, vehicle, or device forward. Used in engineering and automotive contexts.
The force, motivation, or factor that drives progress, change, or achievement in an abstract sense. Used figuratively in business, social, and personal contexts.

glosses: competitive society; society driven by competition
competitive society; a society characterized by intense competition
explanations: A society in which individuals and organizations compete strongly for resources, status, or opportunity. Often used critically to describe pressures of academic or career competition in modern Japan.

glosses: timeliness; quality of delivering breaking news quickly
timeliness; ability to deliver news or information quickly
explanations: The quality of reporting or sharing information rapidly, especially news. Used to describe the characteristic of media, social platforms, or services that excel at delivering breaking information before others.

glosses: facilitation; structured guidance of group discussion or process
explanations: The act of guiding a group meeting, workshop, or discussion to help participants collaborate effectively and reach outcomes. The person doing this is called a ファシリテーター (facilitator). Widely used in business, education, and community settings in Japan.

glosses: high-class shop; upscale restaurant; luxury establishment
upscale shop or restaurant; luxury establishment
explanations: A shop, restaurant, or other establishment of high quality and price, catering to wealthy customers. Covers both food and retail contexts.

glosses: sense of stagnation; feeling of being stuck
feeling of stagnation; sense of being stuck or making no progress
explanations: A subjective feeling that things are not moving forward, either personally (in one's career, skills, or life) or in a broader social/economic context. The -感 suffix converts 停滞 (stagnation) into a perceived feeling.

glosses: lightning flash; the visible light of a lightning bolt
explanations: The bright flash of light produced by a lightning discharge. Distinguished from {雷|かみなり} (thunder, or lightning as a phenomenon) by focusing specifically on the visual flash of light.

glosses: rapidly; sharply; with sudden dramatic change
explanations: Describes change that happens both suddenly and to a large degree — a sharp, dramatic shift. Used for rises, falls, increases, decreases, or transformations that happen quickly and markedly.

glosses: fiercely; intensely; violently; with full force
fiercely; intensely; with great force or vigor
explanations: Describes something done with extreme force, intensity, or ferocity. Used for storms, wind, attacks, hard work, and strong emotions. Implies something overwhelming in its strength.

A cooking method and dish in which fish (especially eel) is split, skewered, and grilled while being basted with a sweet soy-based sauce. Most famously applied to eel (unagi), though also used for other fish.

glosses: tataki; seared fish or meat; finely chopped condiment
tataki; briefly seared fish or meat
finely chopped condiment or minced preparation
explanations: A dish in which the surface of raw fish or meat is lightly seared over high heat then quickly chilled, leaving the interior raw. Served sliced, often with ponzu and garnishes. Common examples include bonito tataki and beef tataki.
A chopped or minced mixture, typically of fish or vegetables with seasonings. The name comes from たたく (to pound/chop). Example: negi tataki (minced green onion).
The customs, practices, and traditions surrounding food in a society or region, including cooking methods, ingredients, dining etiquette, and the social role of meals.

glosses: wheat bran; outer layer of wheat grain
explanations: The outer fibrous coating of wheat grain that is separated from the flour during milling. Used in animal feed, as a dietary supplement for fiber, and in some baked goods.

A scale used to measure body weight, typically kept in the bathroom. A Japanese-English compound formed from 'health' + 'meter'. The standard Japanese term for what English speakers call a bathroom scale.

A suffix-like noun indicating the number of floors in a building. Always preceded by a number: 二階建て (two-story), 三階建て (three-story), etc. Describes the construction of a building in terms of its floor count.

Cheese made by melting and emulsifying natural cheese with other ingredients. In Japan, it is widely sold in individually-wrapped slices or blocks and is a common household staple used in sandwiches, cooking, and snacks.
The period in which a mother is breastfeeding her infant. Used on medicine labels, food packaging, and in medical contexts to indicate precautions for nursing mothers.

glosses: driving under the influence of alcohol; DUI
explanations: Driving while having alcohol in one's system, even if not severely intoxicated. Under Japanese law, drivers with blood alcohol above a certain threshold but below the drunk driving limit are guilty of this offense. A lesser offense than 飲酒運転 (drunk driving) but still illegal.

glosses: reckless weaving driving; lane-swerving while driving
explanations: Driving in a deliberately zigzagging or swerving manner, often as an act of road rage, intimidation, or recklessness. An illegal and dangerous behavior on Japanese roads.

glosses: no artificial coloring; free of added dyes
no artificial coloring; free from added dyes
explanations: A food label claim indicating that no artificial colorants or dyes have been added to a product. Commonly seen on Japanese food packaging alongside other natural/additive-free claims.
A closed loop or network through which electric current can flow. Studied in physics and engineering; the foundation of all electronic devices.

The price that a manufacturer recommends retailers charge for a product. Often printed on product packaging or in catalogs. Actual store prices may differ. Abbreviated as {希望|きぼう}{小売価格|こうりかかく} or sometimes as {メーカー}{希望|きぼう}{小売価格|こうりかかく} (manufacturer's suggested retail price).

glosses: ruins complex; group of archaeological sites
ruins complex; cluster of archaeological sites
explanations: A group or cluster of related archaeological remains or historical ruins in the same area. Often used in the names of UNESCO World Heritage Sites or nationally designated cultural properties.

The Romance language spoken in Portugal, Brazil, and several other countries. In Japan, Portuguese has historical significance as one of the first European languages introduced through contact with Portuguese missionaries and traders in the 16th century. Brazil's large Japanese diaspora also means Portuguese-Japanese bilingualism is notable.

Japan's primary law governing civil aviation, including regulations on aircraft operation, airspace use, pilot licensing, and more recently, drone (unmanned aerial vehicle) operation. The law was expanded in 2022 to include comprehensive drone regulations.
The highest speed achievable by a vehicle, machine, or person. Often used as a performance specification for vehicles or athletes.

A chemical product that removes unwanted hair by dissolving the protein structure of hair. Applied to skin, left for several minutes, then wiped or rinsed away. Sold at pharmacies and convenience stores.
Clothing worn for sleeping. An English loanword used in Japanese retail and fashion contexts. More formal or fashion-oriented than the older term パジャマ.
A liquid flavoring made from vanilla beans or synthetic vanillin. Used in baking and confectionery to add vanilla flavor. Sold in small bottles at supermarkets and cooking supply stores.

glosses: traditional Japanese pattern; Japanese-style design motif
explanations: A decorative pattern in the traditional Japanese style, such as those found on kimono, tenugui, and folding fans. Includes motifs like waves, cranes, and seigaiha.
The charge for delivering goods to the customer, especially in online shopping and food delivery. Often listed separately from the price of the product itself.

glosses: condolence money envelope; funeral gift envelope
explanations: A special envelope used to present money at funerals and other solemn occasions. Tied with black-and-white or silver cords and marked with somber labels, in contrast to the festive envelopes used for weddings.

glosses: input form; entry form (web or document)
explanations: The shape or way one holds and moves the body when performing a physical activity such as a sport. Good フォーム means correct, efficient technique.
A structured set of fields for entering information, especially on a website. Borrowed from English "form" in the sense of a document to fill in.
A fee charged when a contract is cancelled before its agreed term, common with mobile phone plans, rental agreements, and subscriptions.

glosses: spontaneity; acting of one's own accord
explanations: Doing something on one's own initiative, without being told or forced. Most often seen in the derived forms {自発的|じはつてき} (spontaneous, voluntary) and {自発的|じはつてき}に (voluntarily).
The time of day right now. A common label on clocks, displays, websites, and transit information showing the present moment.
A building method in which the structural frame is made of steel. A standard category in Japanese real-estate listings, often abbreviated S{造|ぞう}.
The building or wing of a larger facility that houses the offices and administrative functions, as opposed to factory, classroom, or laboratory buildings.

glosses: interior finishing material; interior trim material
explanations: Materials used to finish the inside of a building or vehicle, such as wall coverings, flooring, and ceiling panels, as distinct from structural or exterior materials.
The historical transformation, beginning in 18th-century Britain, in which manufacturing shifted from hand production to machines, factories, and mechanized industry.

glosses: timed type; time-delayed; set to a timer
timed type; time-delayed; set to go off at a preset time
explanations: Describes a device or mechanism set to activate at a predetermined time or after a set interval. Most familiar in {時限式|じげんしき}{爆弾|ばくだん} (time bomb), but also used of locks and switches.
A storage medium read and written with a laser, such as a CD, DVD, or Blu-ray disc. Data is recorded as pits on a reflective surface.

headword: パンティーストッキング
explanations: A close-fitting garment combining underwear and stockings into a single piece that covers the waist, legs, and feet. Commonly shortened to パンスト.
Paper used for printing, especially the sheets loaded into a home or office printer. Sold in standard sizes such as A4 and B5.
The traffic lane on the right side of a multi-lane road. In Japan, where cars drive on the left, the right lane is typically the passing or turning lane.
Teaching people about food, nutrition, and healthy eating habits. Carried out in schools, hospitals, and public-health settings, often by registered dietitians.

glosses: decorative paper cords; ceremonial cords tied on gift envelopes
explanations: Thin cords made of twisted, starched paper, used to tie and decorate gift envelopes and wrapped presents in Japan. The color and knot style signal the type of occasion, such as a wedding, funeral, or general celebration.

glosses: to show signs of pain; to complain of pain
to show signs of pain; to act as if in pain; to complain of pain
explanations: To outwardly express or behave as though feeling pain. Formed from the adjective {痛|いた}い plus the suffix ～がる, which describes another person's visible feelings rather than one's own.
The basic structure by which a company creates value and earns revenue — what it sells, to whom, and how it makes a profit. A loanword from English.

glosses: to stand one's ground; to hold back; to stop oneself
to stand one's ground; to stay put; to hold firm
to hold back; to restrain oneself; to stop short of doing something
explanations: To remain in place instead of retreating or giving up, often in a difficult or dangerous situation.
To check an impulse and refrain from an action one was about to take, especially something rash or regrettable.

glosses: you know; I tell you; how ...! (emotion, reflection, or emphasis)
explanations: A casual sentence-final particle that adds feeling to a statement — admiration, longing, mild emphasis, or a wish for the listener's agreement. A lengthened, more emotive form of な.

glosses: to punch and send flying; to hit hard
to punch and send flying; to strike hard; to wallop
explanations: To hit someone so forcefully that they are knocked away. The ～{飛|と}ばす component emphasizes the violence and momentum of the blow.

glosses: to ooze out; to seep out; to show through
to ooze out; to seep out; to bleed through
to show through; to be revealed gradually (of feelings or character)
explanations: For a liquid such as sweat, blood, or ink to slowly emerge and spread through a surface.
Figuratively, for an inner quality, emotion, or atmosphere to come through naturally in someone's words, expression, or work.

glosses: to gush out; to spurt out; to burst out laughing
to gush out; to spurt out; to erupt
to burst out laughing; to crack up
explanations: For a liquid, gas, steam, or the like to burst forth forcefully from an opening. Used for sweat, blood, water, lava, and similar.
To suddenly and involuntarily start laughing, especially when trying to suppress it.

glosses: even experts make mistakes; even Homer nods
even experts make mistakes; even the skilled slip up; even Homer nods
explanations: A proverb meaning that even a master of a craft can make an occasional mistake. Literally, 'even Kobo Daishi makes brush errors,' referring to the famed calligrapher-monk Kukai (Kobo Daishi).

glosses: even experts make mistakes; even the best slip up
even experts make mistakes; even a master can fail; even Homer nods
explanations: A proverb meaning that even someone highly skilled can occasionally fail at their own specialty. Literally, 'even a kappa gets swept down the river' — the kappa being a water sprite famed as an expert swimmer.

glosses: to raise (one's voice); to shout out
to raise one's voice; to shout out; to belt out
explanations: To produce a loud, forceful voice, straining it so that it carries. Almost always used with {声|こえ} as the object, describing shouting, calling out, or singing loudly.

glosses: iron rod; metal club; iron staff
explanations: A heavy bar or club made of iron or metal, used as a tool or weapon. In folklore it is the signature weapon of the {鬼|おに} (ogre), which is why it figures in the well-known idiom below.

glosses: the ocean; the open sea; the vast sea
explanations: The great, open expanse of the sea, emphasizing its vastness. A somewhat literary word that often appears in metaphors contrasting something small with the immensity of the sea.
A company that owns or controls operations, factories, or subsidiaries in more than one country. Built from {多|た} (many) + {国籍|こくせき} (nationality) + {企業|きぎょう} (enterprise).

A small organ of the lymphatic system. Strictly the correct medical term is {リンパ節|せつ} (lymph node), but リンパ{腺|せん} remains the everyday word people use, especially when describing swelling during illness.
In linguistics, the smallest unit of language that carries meaning. A word may consist of one morpheme or several, such as a root plus prefixes and suffixes.
A food product taken to supplement the diet with vitamins, minerals, or other nutrients. Built from {栄養|えいよう} (nutrition) + {補助|ほじょ} (supplementary aid) + {食品|しょくひん} (food product).
In chemistry, a compound whose molecules are based on carbon (with the conventional exception of a few simple carbon compounds such as carbon dioxide). Contrasts with inorganic compounds.

glosses: oil cake; oilseed residue (used as fertilizer or feed)
oil cake; oilseed meal; residue left after pressing oil
explanations: The solid residue that remains after oil has been pressed out of seeds such as rapeseed or soybeans. Rich in nutrients, it is widely used as organic fertilizer and as animal feed.

glosses: directly controlled territory; directly administered land
explanations: Land or territory placed under the direct control of a central authority — such as a monarch, shogunate, or national government — rather than being delegated to a local lord or regional body.
Steel whose principal alloying element is carbon, with few or no other added elements. Its hardness and strength depend mainly on its carbon content. Built from {炭素|たんそ} (carbon) + {鋼|こう} (steel).
An instrument that measures the amount of rainfall over a given period. Built from {雨量|うりょう} (amount of rainfall) + {計|けい} (measuring device).

A major historical transformation in farming methods and productivity. The term refers both to the Neolithic shift from foraging to farming and to later leaps such as the 18th-century improvements in European agriculture.
The table on which table tennis is played, divided by a net across the middle. Built from {卓球|たっきゅう} (table tennis) + {台|だい} (stand; table).

A device or machine that automatically translates between languages, typically a handheld gadget that converts speech or text from one language to another. Built from {翻訳|ほんやく} (translation) + {機|き} (machine).
The person who receives something — money, goods, a document, or a benefit. A formal term used in administrative, legal, and business contexts. Built from {受領|じゅりょう} (receipt) + {者|しゃ} (person).
Artists' paint in which the pigment is suspended in oil rather than water. It dries slowly and produces rich, durable colors. Built from {油性|ゆせい} (oil-based) + {絵具|えのぐ} (paint, pigment).
Material used to build or finish walls — for example plaster, plasterboard, tile, or wood paneling. Built from {壁|かべ} (wall) + {材|ざい} (material).

glosses: water-based paint; paint thinned with water
explanations: Paint that uses water as its solvent, so it can be thinned and cleaned up with water. Contrasts with oil-based paint.
Money belonging to a national or local government, or to a public organization, as opposed to private funds.
So wrong, offensive, or harmful that it cannot be forgiven or overlooked.

glosses: out of the question; beyond discussion; absurd
explanations: So unreasonable or unacceptable that it is not even worth discussing or considering.
A disaster caused by natural phenomena such as earthquakes, typhoons, floods, or volcanic eruptions, as opposed to a human-caused accident.
A disaster of large scale that causes extensive damage or heavy loss of life.
A self-destructive frame of mind that arises when things do not go as one hoped, leading one to give up and act without regard for the consequences.
A short phrase expressing the principle or belief by which a person, group, or organization lives or acts. From English "motto."

glosses: action before words; doing rather than talking
action before words; quietly getting things done
explanations: The attitude of doing what needs to be done quietly and steadily, without boasting or announcing it beforehand.

glosses: consistency between words and actions; practicing what one preaches
explanations: The state in which what a person says matches what they actually do.

glosses: all things in heaven and earth; all of creation
explanations: Everything that exists in the universe — the whole of nature and all the things within it.
The academic study of China, covering its language, literature, history, thought, and culture.
The branch of mathematics that studies the properties of integers and their relationships.

glosses: person entrusted with a task; mandatary
explanations: In law, the party who accepts a commission to handle a matter on behalf of another; the one who is entrusted, as opposed to the one who entrusts.
A printing method that uses several colors of ink, as opposed to single-color (monochrome) printing; also a print made this way.
The combined systems that supply clean water to and drain wastewater from a building or facility.
A disaster caused by natural forces such as earthquakes, typhoons, floods, or droughts, as opposed to one caused by human action.

glosses: mandator; party who entrusts a matter to another
explanations: In a contract of mandate or delegation, the person who entrusts a task, authority, or decision to another party. The one who accepts the entrusted matter is the {受任者|じゅにんしゃ}.

glosses: out of the question; beyond consideration
explanations: Something so unacceptable or unreasonable that it is not even worth discussing. Often used to flatly reject a proposal or to condemn behavior as inexcusable.

glosses: juggling several jobs or roles at once
holding several jobs, roles, or commitments at the same time
explanations: Taking on two or more jobs, roles, or activities concurrently and dividing one's time among them. Often used of part-time jobs, club activities, or appointments.

Matters relating to one's own personal life or situation. Most often appears in the set phrase {一身上|いっしんじょう}の{都合|つごう}, a polite, deliberately vague reason given when resigning or declining without disclosing details.
A reference book that systematically explains the grammar rules of a language. Used by learners and specialists alike.
A light, airy cake made from eggs, sugar, and flour, used as the base for many decorated cakes such as strawberry shortcake.
A facility with an ice surface for ice skating, figure skating, or ice hockey. Can refer to the ice surface itself or the whole facility.
Organic material derived from plants and animals that can be used as a renewable source of energy or raw material, such as wood, crop waste, or other organic matter.
A small case for carrying business cards, credit cards, or other cards, keeping them organized and protected.

glosses: man-made disaster; calamity caused by human action or negligence
explanations: A disaster brought about by human error, negligence, or poor planning, as opposed to a purely natural one. Often used to argue that damage blamed on nature was in fact preventable.

glosses: letter of resignation; written request to resign
explanations: A formal document in which an employee or official asks to be allowed to leave their post. Phrased as a request for permission, reflecting that the resignation must be accepted by a superior.

glosses: place of assignment; posting; department one is assigned to
place of assignment; the department or post one is assigned to
explanations: The section, branch, or location to which a new employee or transferred worker is posted. Common in corporate and bureaucratic contexts when announcing where someone will work.

glosses: the COVID-19 pandemic; the coronavirus crisis
the COVID-19 pandemic; the coronavirus crisis (as a period and its hardships)
explanations: The period of disruption caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, together with the hardships it brought. The suffix {禍|か} means calamity or misfortune, so the word frames the pandemic as a time of trouble rather than just the disease itself.
A missile carrying a nuclear warhead. Common in news reports and discussions of security, arms control, and international tensions.
An instrument that measures the distance to a target, used in photography, surveying, golf, and similar fields. Modern versions are often laser-based.

glosses: insects (as a group); the insect class
explanations: Insects considered collectively as a category of living things. The suffix {類|るい} groups the members into a class, so the word means insects in general rather than one particular bug.

glosses: Kamiarizuki; tenth lunar month (in the Izumo region)
the tenth lunar month, as called in the Izumo region
explanations: An old name for the tenth month of the lunar calendar used around Izumo. By legend the gods from across Japan gather at Izumo Shrine that month, so there the gods are present ({神在|かみあり}), in contrast to the usual name {神無月|かんなづき}, the month without gods.

glosses: critical speed; limiting speed; maximum safe speed
critical speed; the maximum speed something can sustain
explanations: The upper speed at which a vehicle, machine, or moving body can still operate safely or stably; beyond it, control or structural integrity is lost. A technical term in physics and engineering.

glosses: main part; principal section; core portion
explanations: The central or most important part of a structure, document, machine, or system. Used to single out the essential portion from secondary or peripheral ones.
A word judged especially important to learn or understand, particularly in study materials and textbooks. Often used of vocabulary that learners are expected to master.
Equipment and appliances used in a kitchen, especially the professional kitchens of restaurants and food businesses, such as stoves, refrigerators, fryers, and dishwashers.
A cat that has been abandoned by its owner, or one left to live without a home. Often used when the cat is found and taken in.

glosses: sleeping face; face of someone asleep
explanations: The face or facial expression of a person (or animal) while asleep. Often used affectionately.

glosses: memo paper; note paper; scratch paper
explanations: Small sheets of paper used for jotting down notes, reminders, or memos.
An area or spot where a vehicle can be parked, whether a marked stall or simply enough room to fit a car.
A person who draws likenesses or caricatures of people, often quickly at tourist spots, events, or street corners.
A solid figure with a triangular base and triangular side faces meeting at a single apex.
A machine part that supports a rotating shaft and reduces friction between moving parts, such as a ball bearing or roller bearing.
The act of drawing milk from a cow, goat, or other animal, by hand or by machine.
One of the small engraved tiles used to play mahjong; a standard set has 136 tiles.

glosses: pudding à la mode; custard pudding with fruit and ice cream
explanations: A Japanese café dessert of custard pudding served on a plate with whipped cream, ice cream, and assorted fruit.
The southern region of Asia, generally including India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, and neighboring countries.
The continent of Africa, the world's second-largest continent by area and population.

glosses: pest control; extermination of harmful animals
explanations: The removal or extermination of animals that damage crops, property, or daily life, such as wild boar, deer, monkeys, or rats.
A machine part that supports a rotating shaft and reduces friction so that it can turn smoothly. The native Japanese term for ベアリング.
Having a limit or an end; not infinite. Used for quantities, resources, time, and sets. The antonym of {無限|むげん} (infinite). Often appears as {有限|ゆうげん}の or {有限|ゆうげん}な.
A temperature that is low, whether of the air, an object, or a process. The antonym of {高温|こうおん} (high temperature). Common in weather, food storage, cooking, and scientific contexts.
Land at a high elevation, above sea level or above the surrounding terrain. The antonym of {低地|ていち} (lowland). Often used for plateaus and mountainous regions.

The instinct, qualities, or sense of responsibility associated with being a father. The paternal counterpart of {母性|ぼせい} (maternal instinct). Often discussed in connection with parenting and gender roles.

glosses: formal report; official reply to an inquiry
explanations: A formal report or recommendation that an advisory body returns in response to a {諮問|しもん} (official inquiry), especially in government or institutional settings.

glosses: forthcoming publication; book due out soon
explanations: A book or publication scheduled to come out soon, or one that has just been released. Common in publishing and bookstore contexts. Composed of {近|きん} (near) + {刊|かん} (publication).

glosses: escaping the winter cold; wintering in a warm place
escaping the winter cold; spending winter in a warm place
explanations: Leaving a cold region to spend the winter somewhere milder, or avoiding the worst of the cold. The winter counterpart of {避暑|ひしょ} (escaping the summer heat).

glosses: activeness; acting of one's own will; active voice
explanations: Acting on one's own initiative rather than being acted upon; also the grammatical active voice. The antonym of {受動|じゅどう} (passive). Most often seen in the form {能動的|のうどうてき} (active, proactive).

glosses: fine weather; good weather; clear skies
explanations: Pleasant, clear weather, especially weather favorable for an event or activity. The antonym of {悪天候|あくてんこう} (bad weather).
Creating something new from one's own ideas, without imitating others. Most often seen in the forms {独創的|どくそうてき} (original, creative) and {独創性|どくそうせい} (originality).

glosses: big appetite; eating a large amount
eating a large amount; big appetite; gluttony
explanations: Eating a great deal, or a person who eats a lot. The antonym of {小食|しょうしょく} (light eater). Also seen in {大食漢|たいしょくかん} (a big eater) and the colloquial reading {大食|おおぐ}い (heavy eating; eating contest).

glosses: real name; true name; one's actual name
explanations: A person's actual name, as opposed to a pseudonym or an anonymous handle. The antonym of {匿名|とくめい} (anonymity). Common in publishing, reporting, and online contexts.

glosses: outside the vehicle; outside the train or car
explanations: The space outside a train, car, or other vehicle. The antonym of {車内|しゃない} (inside the vehicle). Common in transit announcements and traffic-safety contexts.

glosses: elementary school (level or years); primary school
explanations: The elementary-school level or years, almost always used in compounds such as {小学校|しょうがっこう} (elementary school) and {小学生|しょうがくせい} (elementary-school pupil). Parallel to {中学|ちゅうがく} (middle school) and {大学|だいがく} (university).
A person who eats a large amount of food. The final character {漢|かん} means "man," so the word originally referred to men, but it is now used loosely for anyone who eats a lot.

glosses: chitose-ame; long candy given at Shichi-Go-San
chitose-ame; long red-and-white stick candy for Shichi-Go-San
explanations: A long, thin, red-and-white stick candy given to children at {七五三|しちごさん} (Shichi-Go-San). Its length symbolizes a wish for the child's long life and healthy growth. The name literally means "thousand-year candy."
At the start of a sentence, なので links to the previous statement and introduces its result or conclusion, much like "so" or "that's why" in English.
Following a noun or na-adjective, なので gives a reason (the copula な plus the particle ので). It states a cause more softly and politely than だから.

glosses: ritual burning of old charms and talismans
ritual burning of old charms, talismans, and sacred objects
explanations: A Shinto or Buddhist rite in which old {お{札|ふだ}|おふだ}, {お{守|まも}り|おまもり}, and other sacred objects are respectfully burned at a shrine or temple, returning them to the gods. It is held so that items containing spiritual power are not simply thrown away.

glosses: dried-goods store; shop selling dried foods
explanations: A shop that sells {乾物|かんぶつ}—dried foods such as kelp, dried mushrooms, dried fish, and beans. Once common in neighborhood shopping streets, such specialty stores are now less numerous.

glosses: botamochi; rice cake coated with sweet red bean paste
botamochi; sticky rice ball coated with sweet red bean paste
explanations: A traditional sweet made of pounded glutinous rice formed into a ball and covered with {あんこ|あんこ} (sweet red bean paste). It is closely associated with the spring equinox, when it is offered to ancestors.

glosses: windfall; unexpected good luck; lucky break
explanations: Good fortune that arrives with no effort on one's part. It is a shortening of the proverb {棚|たな}から{牡丹餅|ぼたもち} ("a botamochi falling from the shelf").

glosses: profound; having depth; rich in meaning
explanations: Describes food or drink with a deep, complex, satisfying taste, rather than a simple or thin one.
Figuratively, describes a work, experience, or words that reveal more the longer one engages with them—rich in subtle appeal or significance.

glosses: handling; treatment; the way one deals with people
explanations: The manner in which one receives or deals with another person, especially a customer or guest. Often appears in {客|きゃく}あしらい and {人|ひと}あしらい.
A small complementary touch added for effect—a garnish on a dish, or a decorative accent in design, dress, or flower arranging.
A small vessel for holding salt at the table or in the kitchen, whether a shaker with holes or an open cellar.

glosses: tobusuma; sliding door faced with fusuma on one side and wood on the other
explanations: A sliding door used where a Japanese-style room meets a Western-style room or hallway. One face is finished as a {襖|ふすま} to match the tatami room, while the other is a wooden door to match the adjoining space.
A woman who engages in prostitution. A clinical, somewhat formal term used in news reporting, legal contexts, and historical or literary writing.

glosses: the rings; still rings (men's gymnastics apparatus)
explanations: An apparatus in men's artistic gymnastics consisting of two rings hung from cables, on which the athlete performs swings, holds, and strength elements. Also the name of that event.

glosses: ohagi; sweet rice cake coated in red bean paste
ohagi; rice ball coated in sweetened red bean paste
explanations: A traditional confection of lightly pounded glutinous rice formed into a ball and covered with あんこ (sweet red bean paste), sometimes with きなこ or ごま instead. Customarily eaten at the autumn equinox during お{彼岸|ひがん}.

glosses: disembarking from an aircraft; getting off a plane
explanations: The act of leaving an aircraft after it lands. A formal term used mainly in aviation and airport announcements, the opposite of {搭乗|とうじょう} (boarding).

glosses: silver seat; priority seat for the elderly and disabled
explanations: A reserved seat on trains and buses for elderly, disabled, injured, or pregnant passengers. An older Japanese-coined term (from English "silver" + "seat") now largely replaced by {優先席|ゆうせんせき}.
Morally corrupt character or dishonest, unethical behavior. Frequently used attributively to label dishonest businesses and operators, as in {悪徳業者|あくとくぎょうしゃ}.
A rapid, steep fall in a quantity such as sales, population, or numbers over a short period. The opposite of {急増|きゅうぞう} (sharp increase).

glosses: soft quality; soft type (of a material)
explanations: A soft or pliable physical quality of a material, used attributively to classify a substance as the soft variety. The opposite of {硬質|こうしつ} (hard quality).
A religion that recognizes and worships a single God. Christianity, Islam, and Judaism are the principal examples. The opposite of {多神教|たしんきょう} (polytheism).

glosses: to take in; to consume (nutrients, food)
to take in; to ingest; to consume (food, nutrients, sleep)
explanations: To take something into the body, especially nutrients, food, water, or sleep. This kanji spelling distinguishes it from other verbs read とる; it often appears in health and nutrition contexts.
Opening remarks placed at the front of a book or paper, explaining its aim and background. A formal term found mainly in academic and scholarly works.

glosses: to begin with; first of all; Introduction (section heading)
to begin with; first of all; at the outset
explanations: An adverbial phrase introducing the first thing said or done, often used to open a speech, explanation, or set of instructions.
A standard heading at the front of a book or document, especially non-fiction, marking the introductory section. Equivalent to an English "Introduction" or "Preface."
A professional qualified to plan meals and give dietary guidance, working in places such as schools, hospitals, and company cafeterias. In Japan the title requires a prefectural license.

glosses: the three major; the three great
the three major ~; the three great ~
explanations: A prefix attached to a noun to name the three most important, famous, or representative members of a category, as in {世界三大|せかいさんだい}{料理|りょうり} (the world's three great cuisines).

glosses: tubers and root starches; the potato family of foods
explanations: The food category that groups starchy tubers and roots together, including {じゃがいも} (potato), {さつまいも} (sweet potato), {さといも} (taro), and {やまいも} (yam).
A colloquial clipping of {炭水化物|たんすいかぶつ} (carbohydrate), used mainly in dieting and fitness talk to refer to carb-rich foods such as rice, bread, and noodles.
A nationally licensed nutrition professional in Japan, one rank above the {栄養士|えいようし}. They plan and manage diets and give nutritional guidance in hospitals, schools, and welfare facilities.

glosses: to force a sale on; to palm off; to foist on
to force a sale on someone; to palm off; to foist on
explanations: To pressure someone into buying something, often something overpriced, unneeded, or of poor quality. The buyer is marked with に and the goods with を.
The person or team one faces in a match, game, or contest. Common in sports, board and video games, and other competitive settings.

glosses: to push down; to knock down; to shove over
explanations: To shove or thrust at a person so hard that they fall to the ground. Compound of {突|つ}く (to thrust) + {倒|たお}す (to knock down). The person pushed is marked with を.

glosses: casting pearls before swine; wasted on someone who can't appreciate it
casting pearls before swine; wasted on those who can't appreciate it
