explanations: Literally 'a gold coin to a cat.' A proverb describing the futility of giving something valuable to someone who cannot understand or appreciate its worth. The {小判|こばん} was an oval gold coin of the Edo period.

glosses: fiscal closing period; accounting period; settlement term
explanations: The period at the end of which a company closes its books and settles its financial statements, typically the end of a fiscal year or quarter. In Japan many companies use a March closing.

glosses: being frantically busy; having one's hands full
being frantically busy; having one's hands full; rushing around
explanations: A state of being so busy that one is scrambling to keep up. The {舞|ま}い part comes from the frantic dancing to fast てんてこ festival-drum rhythms. Often used with だ, で, or する.

glosses: to make a fuss; to raise a clamor; to kick up a row
to make a fuss; to raise a clamor; to sensationalize
explanations: To make a loud fuss or raise an outcry about something, often more than the matter deserves. Frequently used of the media or a crowd blowing an issue out of proportion. The topic is marked with を.

glosses: taking a story with a grain of salt; believing only half of what is said
taking a story with a grain of salt; believing only half of what one is told
explanations: The attitude of listening to a story while assuming much of it is exaggeration, so one believes only about half. Most often used in the phrase {話|はなし}{半分|はんぶん}に{聞|き}く.

glosses: uniting for a common cause; joining forces
explanations: A four-character compound ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}) meaning that different groups set aside minor differences and unite for a larger shared goal. Often used of political parties or factions forming a coalition. Used with する.
A loanword from English 'dilemma.' A situation in which one must choose between two options, both of which have undesirable consequences.

A construction technology that reduces a building's shaking during an earthquake by installing dampers that absorb seismic energy. Distinguished from {耐震|たいしん} (making the structure strong enough to resist quakes) and {免震|めんしん} (isolating the building from ground motion).

glosses: omission of courtesy; failing to send greetings
explanations: A failure or omission of an expected courtesy. Most commonly refers to not sending New Year's cards ({年賀状|ねんがじょう}) because one is in mourning ({喪中|もちゅう}). The verb is {欠礼|けつれい}する.
To become pregnant; to conceive a child. Used of the woman who is pregnant.

glosses: to create; to bring into being
explanations: To bring something new into existence — works of art, value, culture, or ideas. Often grand or abstract in scope, unlike everyday {作|つく}る.

glosses: to affirm; to acknowledge as true
explanations: To affirm something as true or acceptable; to respond positively. The opposite of {否定|ひてい}する (to deny).

glosses: to recommend; to nominate; to endorse
explanations: To recommend a person or thing to someone, often formally — a book, a candidate, an applicant. More formal than {勧|すす}める.

glosses: to plan; to organize; to devise
explanations: To plan and put together a project, event, or product — devising the concept and arranging how to realize it. Common in business and event contexts.
The dismissal of a public official or minister from their post by an authority. A formal, often political term; {罷免|ひめん}する is the verb.
A bad person; the villain in a story, or the one treated as being at fault in a situation.
A word opposite in meaning to another — the standard term for an antonym (e.g., {高|たか}い vs {低|ひく}い). The opposite concept is {類義語|るいぎご} (synonym, near-synonym).

glosses: to quell; to calm; to suppress
explanations: To bring something turbulent under control — a rebellion, a commotion, pain, or one's anger. The transitive partner of {鎮|しず}まる (to subside, to die down).

glosses: to cling to; to grab hold of
explanations: To cling or catch hold of something or someone. By extension it can mean to set to work on a task (X に {取|と}り{付|つ}く); the thing clung to or tackled is marked with に.

glosses: ending one's New Year's card custom
explanations: The practice of formally ending the custom of exchanging New Year's cards ({年賀状|ねんがじょう}), usually by sending a final card that announces one will no longer send them. A growing trend, especially among the elderly.
A {屏風|びょうぶ} (folding screen) covered in gold leaf, used as a luxurious backdrop at weddings, ceremonies, and on stages for formal speeches or {落語|らくご}.
A {屏風|びょうぶ} (folding screen) covered in silver leaf. Conceptually paired with the {金屏風|きんびょうぶ} (gold screen) but quieter in impression, used for more subdued or refined settings.
A painting executed on the panels of a {屏風|びょうぶ} (folding screen); a major format of traditional Japanese painting.
A low, usually two-panel {屏風|びょうぶ} placed behind the {風炉|ふろ} (portable brazier) and tea utensils in the tea ceremony, marking off the host's working space.

glosses: flipping the table; sudden dramatic reversal
explanations: Literally overturning a low dining table (ちゃぶ{台|だい}) in a fit of rage; figuratively, abruptly overturning a plan or decision that was nearly settled, throwing everything into disorder.
A stereotypical stubborn, old-fashioned father or older man who refuses to bend — strict, set in his ways, and gruff. Often used half-affectionately.
A word whose meaning is the opposite of another word, such as 'big' and 'small'. Used especially in language teaching and vocabulary study.

glosses: fusuma painting; painting on sliding doors
explanations: A picture painted on the paper surface of {襖|ふすま} (sliding interior doors), a traditional form of Japanese decorative art seen in temples, castles, and old residences.
A gathering at which tea is served in the tea ceremony, or the room or seat where the ceremony takes place. Often used for the occasion as a whole.

glosses: kenchin soup; vegetable and tofu soup
kenchin soup; clear vegetable and tofu soup
explanations: A clear soup made by stir-frying crumbled tofu and root vegetables such as daikon, carrot, and burdock, then simmering them in a soy-based broth. A common home and temple dish, especially in cold weather.
The essential points or basic framework of a plan, argument, or document, stripped of detail. Common in formal and written contexts such as proposals and reports.
A box made of corrugated cardboard ({段|だん}ボール), used for packing, shipping, storage, and moving.
An instrument that measures and displays speed, especially the gauge in a vehicle showing how fast it is traveling.

glosses: model sentence; sample text; example wording
explanations: An example sentence or sample passage provided as a model to follow, such as templates for letters, emails, or formal greetings.

glosses: fixed expression; set phrase; formulaic expression
explanations: A conventional, ready-made phrase used in a predictable way, such as set greetings or stock wordings in letters and business communication.
The amount subtracted from income or a payment, especially in tax and insurance contexts, such as a standard deduction or a dependent allowance.
A brown color tinged with yellow. A descriptive color term common in writing about nature, materials, and chemistry.
The body of knowledge dealing with how music works, including scales, harmony, rhythm, and notation.
A tall tower built so that visitors can enjoy a wide view of the surrounding scenery.

glosses: tail of an aircraft; tail assembly; tail fin
explanations: The tail section at the rear of an aircraft, including the vertical and horizontal stabilizers, which keeps the plane stable in flight.
A road whose surface has been paved with asphalt or concrete, as opposed to an unpaved dirt or gravel road.
A planned area where factories and related facilities are gathered together, typically developed with shared infrastructure such as roads and utilities.
Research carried out jointly by two or more people, institutions, or companies working together toward a common goal.

glosses: work history; employment history; career history
explanations: A record of the jobs and duties a person has performed over their career, especially as presented when applying for a job.

glosses: greeting message; written greeting; opening remarks
explanations: A written greeting, such as the opening lines of a letter or email, a seasonal card message, or a short address printed in a newsletter or program.
Equipment worn to protect the body from injury or hazards, such as helmets, goggles, gloves, and masks used in workplaces and sports.

glosses: company culture; corporate climate; organizational atmosphere
explanations: The distinctive atmosphere, shared values, and working style that characterize a particular company. Often discussed by job seekers when judging whether a workplace will suit them.
Getting a large amount of work done in a given time with little wasted effort. Emphasizes output and the pace of work.
Oriented toward defending or protecting rather than attacking. Used of sports tactics, business strategy, and cautious attitudes.

glosses: play; a move; performance (in a sport or game)
explanations: An action or move made by a player in a sport or game, or the overall manner of a player's performance. From English "play." Used as a verb with する.

glosses: to keep writing; to continue writing
explanations: To continue the act of writing without stopping. A compound of {書|か}く (to write) and {続|つづ}ける (to continue).
Describing people who get along well and have a warm, close relationship. A colloquial i-adjective related to the noun {仲良|なかよ}し.
A film genre built around fast-paced physical sequences such as fights, chases, and explosions.
The instrument in a vehicle that records the total distance it has traveled.
A substance, such as water or a special fluid, used to carry heat away and keep an engine, reactor, or machine from overheating.
A person who earns a living through physical labor, such as construction or factory work, rather than office work.

glosses: Japanese-language education; teaching of the national language
explanations: The teaching of reading, writing, and the Japanese language to native speakers in schools. {国語|こくご} here means the national language, i.e. Japanese, as a school subject.
An organization that has joined a larger federation, league, or alliance as a member.
The vehicles and systems—trucks, ships, trains, planes—used to move goods or people from one place to another.
A person who has diabetes, a chronic condition in which the body cannot properly regulate blood sugar.

glosses: language ability; command of foreign languages
explanations: A person's ability to use or learn foreign languages, covering reading, writing, listening, and speaking. Often mentioned in connection with study, jobs, or travel.

glosses: wetland; marshland; belt of marshy land
explanations: An expanse of low, waterlogged land such as marsh, swamp, or bog. Often discussed as important wildlife habitat or in connection with land development and conservation.
Land owned by the national government or a local authority rather than by private individuals or companies. Contrasts with privately owned land.
A parcel of land that a particular person, company, or organization legally owns. The focus is on who holds title to it.

glosses: retainer fee; initial payment; upfront fee
retainer fee; upfront fee paid when work begins
explanations: A fee paid at the start of a job, especially to a lawyer or contractor, separate from the final reward or balance. It is typically charged regardless of the outcome.
A person who has been captured and held, especially an enemy taken in battle. A formal, literary word now found mainly in writing, history, and translation.
Letters or designs carved into metal, stone, or other hard material, or the act of carving them. Also used figuratively for something engraved deeply in the heart or memory.

glosses: lecture notes; record of a lecture; transcript
written record of a lecture; lecture notes
explanations: A written or printed record of the content of a lecture or course, whether taken down by a student or published. Often compiled into booklets or course materials.

glosses: total bases (baseball); bases gained by a hit
total bases; bases reached on one's own hit
explanations: In baseball, the number of bases a batter gains on his own hit: one for a single, two for a double, three for a triple, and four for a home run. The total, {塁打数|るいだすう}, is used to compute slugging percentage. Also the base of compounds such as {二塁打|にるいだ} (double) and {本塁打|ほんるいだ} (home run).

In anthropology, the earliest stage of human ancestors, such as the australopithecines, regarded as a link between apes and humans. The oldest of the textbook stages {猿人|えんじん} → {原人|げんじん} → {旧人|きゅうじん} → {新人|しんじん}.
In mathematics, a function of the form y = a^x, in which the variable appears in the exponent. Its rapid growth is the basis of the everyday phrase 'to grow exponentially.'
Money that a person, household, or company has borrowed and must repay, especially from a bank. A common term in accounting and personal finance.

glosses: catch; volume of fish caught; haul
catch; amount of fish (or seafood) caught
explanations: The quantity of fish or other seafood taken, usually by weight, over a given period or trip. A standard term in fisheries statistics and news about the fishing industry.

glosses: water receiving tank; water storage tank
explanations: A tank that receives and stores water from the mains before it is pumped up to a building's upper floors. Common in apartment buildings, schools, and other large facilities.

glosses: speed-reading method; technique for reading quickly
explanations: A method or set of techniques for reading text quickly while still grasping its content, such as taking in several words at a glance or not subvocalizing.

glosses: terminal symptoms; signs of a final, hopeless stage
terminal symptoms; signs of a hopeless final stage
explanations: Literally the symptoms of the terminal stage of an illness. Very often used figuratively for an organization or situation in irreversible decline.

glosses: swallowtail; forked shape like a swallow's tail
explanations: The deeply forked shape of a swallow's tail, used to describe objects with a similar V-shaped split, such as a tailcoat, a pennant, or a joint in woodworking. Most often seen in compounds.

glosses: deposit interest rate; rate paid on savings
explanations: The rate of interest a bank pays on money held in deposit accounts, expressed as an annual percentage. A standard term in personal finance and banking.
A device that generates and sends out signals, especially radio waves. Contrasts with a receiver, which picks the signals up.

Matter whose atoms are arranged in a regular, repeating lattice, or the property of being so arranged. Contrasts with amorphous (non-crystalline) material such as glass. Often used attributively with の.

glosses: state-owned land; land owned by the national government
explanations: Land whose owner is the national government rather than a private individual or company. Often discussed in the context of sales to the private sector, public projects, or administrative management.

glosses: contingency fee; success fee; performance-based reward
contingency fee; success fee; reward paid only on success
explanations: A payment that is owed only when a particular result is achieved, such as winning a lawsuit, closing a deal, or recovering money. Common in legal, consulting, and recruiting work, often alongside an upfront retainer.

glosses: deposit; down payment securing a contract
deposit; earnest money securing a contract
explanations: Money paid by the buyer when a contract is concluded, confirming the agreement before the full price is paid. Common in real estate and large purchases; the buyer typically forfeits it if they back out, while the seller may owe double if they cancel.
In baseball, a hit that lets the batter reach second base or beyond — a double, triple, or home run. Valued for advancing or driving in runners more than a single does.

glosses: early human; archaic human (Homo erectus stage)
explanations: In the study of human evolution, an early human of the Homo erectus stage, more advanced than the ape-like {猿人|えんじん} but earlier than {旧人|きゅうじん} and modern humans. Often appears in the names of specific finds, such as {北京原人|ぺきんげんじん} (Peking Man).

In mathematics, a function of the form y = log_a x, the inverse of the exponential function. A standard topic in high-school and university math, used to model growth, decay, and quantities that span many orders of magnitude.

glosses: engraved mark; stamp; hallmark; (to) engrave, imprint
explanations: A mark cut or pressed into a hard surface such as metal, leather, or a seal, often to show a maker, purity, or authenticity. As {刻印|こくいん}する it means to engrave or stamp such a mark, and figuratively to leave a lasting impression on the mind.

glosses: harvest yield; amount of crop harvested
explanations: The quantity of a crop gathered in a harvest, measured by weight, volume, or area. Used when discussing farming output, the effects of weather, or year-on-year changes in production.

glosses: loan; loaned money (from the lender's side)
explanations: Money that has been lent out and is owed back, seen from the lender's side. On a balance sheet it is an asset; the same money viewed from the borrower's side is {借入金|かりいれきん}.

A slang blend of {あざとい} (calculating, sly) and かわいい (cute) describing someone — usually a woman or an idol-type figure — who is cute in a deliberate, knowing way. Often half-critical and half-admiring: the charm is transparent yet still effective.

From English "heavy." Used for things that are physically or figuratively weighty — rich food, a demanding schedule, a serious or hard-hitting topic — and as a prefix marking frequent or intense involvement, as in ヘビーユーザー (heavy user).

From English "core." As a noun it means the central or most important part of something. As a na-adjective it describes a small but deeply committed group or a niche, hardcore taste, as in コアなファン (devoted fans).

Organized, competitive video gaming, especially played for spectators and prize money. From English "e-sports" (electronic sports); covers professional leagues, tournaments, and the broader scene around them.

glosses: streamer; person who broadcasts live online
explanations: A person who broadcasts live video over the internet, especially of gameplay, talk, or events, often as a career. From English "streamer"; closely tied to platforms such as YouTube and Twitch.

From English "exciting." Describes an event, game, or experience that stirs strong excitement in those watching or taking part. Used as a na-adjective, often of sports, performances, and developments.

glosses: sensational; startling; that causes a stir
explanations: From English "sensational." Describes news, a debut, or an event so striking that it draws wide attention and stirs strong public reaction. Used as a na-adjective, often of media coverage and dramatic developments.
The count of written characters (kana, kanji, numerals, etc.) in a piece of text. Used for essays, application forms, and online posts that impose length limits.
The initial portion of a purchase price paid upfront, with the balance covered by a loan or later installments. Common when buying a house or car.

glosses: speaking voice; sound of talking; voices
explanations: The voice used in ordinary conversation, or the audible sound of people talking — as opposed to singing or shouting.
In baseball, a base hit on which the batter safely reaches first base only. Contrasted with extra-base hits such as doubles and home runs.

In the conventional four-stage scheme of human evolution, the third stage — archaic members of the genus Homo such as the Neanderthals — coming after {原人|げんじん} (Homo erectus) and before {新人|しんじん} (modern humans).

glosses: to think exhaustively; to brood over
to think exhaustively; to brood over; to ponder to the limit
explanations: To keep thinking about something intensely, often dwelling on a worry or problem until one is mentally cornered. Usually carries a sense of unhealthy over-thinking.
Goods made through industrial manufacturing, such as machinery, electronics, and vehicles — as distinct from agricultural produce or raw natural materials.
The person or party who sends out a parcel or freight shipment, as opposed to the person who receives it.

glosses: minor power; weak nation; small and weak country
explanations: A country with little military, economic, or political strength, easily swayed by larger powers. Contrasted with great powers.
A vehicle that runs on four wheels — usually an ordinary car — as distinguished from two-wheeled vehicles such as motorcycles.
The number of characters—kanji, kana, letters, and so on—in a piece of text. Most often used when there is a length limit, as in forms, essays, social media posts, and documents.

glosses: bipedal walking; walking on two legs
explanations: Moving by walking upright on two legs, as humans do, in contrast to four-legged locomotion. Common in discussions of human evolution, animals, and robotics.
Hasty, ill-considered thinking or action; making a decision without enough deliberation. A formal, somewhat literary word.
Describes a person who is honest, conscientious, and warm in dealings with others. A formal, literary word, often appearing in the idiom {温厚篤実|おんこうとくじつ}.

A large public exhibition displaying industrial, cultural, scientific, or artistic achievements, often international in scale. Visitors view exhibits gathered from many participants; a world's fair is the best-known type.
A house that one rents and lives in, rather than owns. Refers to the rented dwelling itself; しゃくや is the common reading, while しゃっか is used in formal or legal contexts.
A shop where one gets a haircut, especially a traditional barbershop catering mainly to men. Can also refer to the barber who works there. A casual, everyday word.
The building where a legislative assembly meets to deliberate. In Japan it most often refers to the National Diet Building, the {国会|こっかい}{議事堂|ぎじどう}.
A thing that someone owns; an item belonging to a particular person or organization. Emphasizes the relationship of ownership rather than the nature of the object.

glosses: poetry anthology; collection of poems or songs
explanations: A book that collects poems—especially {短歌|たんか} and other Japanese verse—or songs. In classical literature it refers to anthologies of waka such as the {万葉集|まんようしゅう}.

glosses: main argument; main discussion; the body (of a discourse)
main argument; main discussion; the body of a discourse
explanations: The central part of an argument, essay, or speech, as opposed to the introduction or digressions; also the main point one wishes to make. Common in academic and formal writing.
A mountain covered with snow; also a large heaped pile of snow, such as one left after clearing it. Read ゆきやま in everyday use; せつざん is used in mountaineering.
The male reproductive organ of a flower, which produces and holds pollen. Contrasted with the {雌|め}しべ (pistil), the female part.
The union of a male and female reproductive cell—sperm and egg—that begins the development of a new organism. A biology term applying to both animals and plants.

The state of two or more things being consistent and free of contradiction, or the act of making them agree. Common in technical, logical, and administrative contexts such as data, theories, and rules.
Something occurring unexpectedly and by chance, rather than by plan or necessity. Often used of accidents, incidents, and unforeseen events.
Being or coming very near to something in space or time. A formal word used of locations, objects, and dates, and in technical fields such as sensors and photography.
The official announcement of a law, ordinance, or constitution so that it becomes publicly known. A formal word, common in historical contexts such as the promulgation of the Meiji Constitution.

glosses: to rewrite; to transfer (a registration); to renew
to rewrite; to transfer or renew (a title, registration, or document)
explanations: To write something over again, or to update an official record by replacing the old entry with a new one. The {替|か}え here stresses substituting new content for the old; the same verb is more commonly written {書|か}き{換|か}える.
The female reproductive organ of a flower, which receives pollen and develops into the fruit or seed. Contrasted with the {雄|お}しべ (stamen), the male part.

glosses: having said that; even so; that said
having said that; even so; that said; but still
explanations: A conjunctive expression used to acknowledge what was just stated and then introduce a qualification or opposing point. It softens a shift to a contrary view, like English "that said" or "even so."

glosses: soldier; common soldier; troops; the rank-and-file
explanations: A member of the armed forces, especially an ordinary soldier rather than an officer. Also used collectively for troops, and as the lowest grade in a military rank system.

glosses: listener; member of a listening audience
explanations: A person who listens to radio, podcasts, music, or a live stream. Borrowed from English "listener," it usually refers to the audience of audio media or of a streamer.

glosses: that side; your side; your end
that side; the side near you; your side or position
explanations: The side closer to the listener, or the listener's group, position, or point of view. A casual contraction of そちら{側|がわ}, common in conversation.
The joint connecting the upper arm and the forearm. The anatomical term for the elbow as a joint, used in medicine, sports, and physical therapy.
A mid-altitude cloud type made up of white or gray patches and rolls, often arranged in regular groups. Popularly called ひつじ{雲|ぐも} (sheep clouds) for their woolly appearance.

glosses: decolorizing agent; bleach used to remove color
explanations: A chemical product that removes color from hair, fabric, or other material. Especially common for the hair bleach used to lighten hair before dyeing.

glosses: canned salmon; a can of salmon
explanations: Salmon preserved in a can. A common pantry staple used in rice dishes, salads, and sandwiches; also read さけかん or しゃけかん.

A high-altitude cloud made of small white ripples or grains arranged in regular patterns. Popularly called うろこ{雲|ぐも} (scale clouds) or さば{雲|ぐも} (mackerel clouds), and associated with a 'mackerel sky'.

glosses: requiring caution; needing attention; one to watch out for
explanations: A label meaning that something or someone needs careful attention or watching. Literally 'caution required' ({要|よう} 'need' + {注意|ちゅうい} 'caution'). Often used attributively, as in {要注意人物|ようちゅういじんぶつ}.

Formal clothing or costumes lent out for a fee, such as kimono, wedding dresses, or stage costumes. From {貸|か}す 'to lend' + {衣装|いしょう} 'clothing, costume'. Commonly used for ceremonies where expensive garments are worn only once.

glosses: black formal kimono for married women
explanations: The most formal kimono worn by married women, dyed black with family crests and a decorative pattern only along the hem. Worn by close female relatives—especially the mothers of the bride and groom—at weddings.
Paper treated with oil to make it water-resistant. Traditionally used to wrap goods, line umbrellas and raincoats, and keep out moisture before plastics became common.

glosses: way of incense; incense appreciation art
way of incense; art of incense appreciation
explanations: The traditional Japanese art of appreciating fragrant wood and incense, with its own etiquette and games. Together with {茶道|さどう} (tea ceremony) and {華道|かどう} (flower arranging), it is one of the three classical refined arts.
A Buddhist religious observance, especially a memorial service for the dead such as a funeral or a death anniversary. Covers the various rites a family holds through a temple.

glosses: before the Buddhist altar; in front of Buddha
explanations: The space in front of a Buddhist altar ({仏壇|ぶつだん}) or image of the Buddha, where offerings are made and prayers are said. Also used in {御仏前|ごぶつぜん}, the label on condolence money offered after the funeral.

In the way of incense ({香道|こうどう}), the act of savoring the fragrance of warmed incense wood. The scent is said to be 'listened to' ({聞|き}く) rather than merely smelled, reflecting the meditative attention it requires.
A chronic neurological disorder in which abnormal electrical activity in the brain causes recurring seizures. Usually written in kana, though the kanji {癲癇|てんかん} also exists.
A sudden, painful involuntary contraction of the calf muscle. From こむら (calf) + {返|がえ}り (turning over). Often strikes during sleep, swimming, or exercise, especially when one is tired or dehydrated.

A substance that dissociates into ions in solution and conducts electricity. In the body, electrolytes such as sodium and potassium regulate fluid balance and nerve and muscle function; in chemistry and batteries, the term refers to the conducting medium.
Pain felt in the chest. A clinical term covering pain from the heart, lungs, muscles, or other causes, used in medical settings and symptom descriptions.

glosses: this term; this period; current term
explanations: The current accounting term, season, or session, as opposed to the previous or next one. Used in business for the current fiscal period and more broadly for a current season of sports, broadcasting, or a legislative term.

glosses: to produce; to give rise to; to generate
explanations: To bring something new into existence as a result—profit, value, results, or consequences such as misunderstanding. Written {生|う}む, it emphasizes producing or creating, as opposed to {産|う}む, which is preferred for giving birth.
A solar eclipse in which the Moon completely covers the Sun, briefly revealing the corona and darkening the sky.
A solar eclipse in which the Moon covers only part of the Sun's disk, so the Sun appears notched rather than fully hidden.
A solar eclipse in which the Moon is too far from Earth to cover the Sun completely, leaving a bright ring of sunlight around its edge.
A lunar eclipse in which only part of the Moon passes through Earth's main shadow (umbra), darkening a section of its surface.
A lunar eclipse in which the Moon passes only through Earth's outer shadow (penumbra), so it dims slightly rather than darkening sharply.

glosses: Warm Biz; winter energy-saving dress campaign
explanations: A Japanese government-led campaign encouraging warm, layered clothing in winter so that office heating can be set lower to save energy.
The coppery-red color the Moon takes on during a total lunar eclipse, caused by sunlight bent through Earth's atmosphere; also used loosely for a strikingly red moon.
The seven bright stars of Ursa Major that form a ladle shape, widely used as a guide for finding the North Star.
A small, cross-shaped constellation visible in the Southern Hemisphere, used there as a guide for locating due south.
A chart or table laid out so that information can be found at a glance, such as conversions, fees, sizes, or schedules.
A box or case for storing and carrying hand tools.
A small cutting tool with sharp jaws for snipping wire, plastic parts, or similar thin material.
Pliers with long, tapered jaws for gripping, bending, and positioning small parts or wire in tight spaces.
A gripping hand tool, often with an adjustable joint that lets the jaws open wider to handle different sizes.
The failure of a check or promissory note to be paid because the account lacks sufficient funds, so the bill is returned unpaid.

glosses: to discount; to reduce a price; to take with a grain of salt
to discount; to reduce a price
to take with a grain of salt; to make allowances for exaggeration
explanations: To lower the price of something by a certain amount or percentage.
Figuratively, to mentally subtract exaggeration from what someone says and treat it as less than its face value.

glosses: the time being; the immediate present
explanations: The short period right now, before longer-term plans take effect; the immediate present.
A bank account used for day-to-day business payments, typically settled by check and earning no interest.
Money, especially in financial, economic, or compound contexts; a loanword that sounds more modern or technical than {お金|おかね}.
The reduction of energy use through efficient equipment and habits; the full form of the common abbreviation {省|しょう}エネ.

glosses: Cool Biz; summer light-dress energy-saving campaign
explanations: A Japanese government-led campaign encouraging light summer clothing (no jacket or tie) so that office air conditioning can be set higher to save energy.

glosses: eclipse; obscuration of a celestial body
explanations: An astronomical eclipse, in which one celestial body is wholly or partly hidden by another. A literary or technical term that most often appears in compounds such as {日蝕|にっしょく} (solar eclipse) and {月蝕|げっしょく} (lunar eclipse); the modern everyday spelling uses {食|しょく}.
The first sign of the Western zodiac, covering people born roughly March 21 to April 19. Also the constellation Aries. Used in horoscopes and casual talk about star signs.
The second sign of the Western zodiac, covering people born roughly April 20 to May 20. Also the constellation Taurus. Used in horoscopes and casual talk about star signs.
The third sign of the Western zodiac, covering people born roughly May 21 to June 21. Also the constellation Gemini. Used in horoscopes and casual talk about star signs.
The fourth sign of the Western zodiac, covering people born roughly June 22 to July 22. Also the constellation Cancer. Used in horoscopes and casual talk about star signs.
The fifth sign of the Western zodiac, covering people born roughly July 23 to August 22. Also the constellation Leo. Used in horoscopes and casual talk about star signs.
The sixth sign of the Western zodiac, covering people born roughly August 23 to September 22. Also the constellation Virgo. Used in horoscopes and casual talk about star signs.
The seventh sign of the Western zodiac, covering people born roughly September 23 to October 23. Also the constellation Libra. Used in horoscopes and casual talk about star signs.

The eighth sign of the Western zodiac, covering people born roughly October 24 to November 22. Also the constellation Scorpius. Used in horoscopes and casual talk about star signs; often written with the kana さそり{座|ざ}.
The ninth sign of the Western zodiac, covering people born roughly November 23 to December 21. Also the constellation Sagittarius. Used in horoscopes and casual talk about star signs.

The tenth sign of the Western zodiac, covering people born roughly December 22 to January 19. Also the constellation Capricornus. Used in horoscopes and casual talk about star signs; often written with the kana やぎ{座|ざ}.
The eleventh sign of the Western zodiac, covering people born roughly January 20 to February 18. Also the constellation Aquarius. Used in horoscopes and casual talk about star signs.
The twelfth and last sign of the Western zodiac, covering people born roughly February 19 to March 20. Also the constellation Pisces. Used in horoscopes and casual talk about star signs.

A hair-care product or salon service applied after shampooing to repair and condition the hair. From English "treatment." More intensive than a rinse-out conditioner ({リンス|りんす}); the everyday meaning in Japan is almost always the hair-care one.

Shaving the face, including fine facial hair and down, typically as a grooming service at a barbershop or beauty salon. Often offered to brides before a wedding to brighten the skin. Sometimes written {顔剃|かおそ}り.

An establishment that cuts hair and shaves the face, licensed under barbering ({理容|りよう}) regulations. A formal, official-sounding term; in everyday speech people more often say {床屋|とこや} or {美容院|びよういん}.

glosses: kick the can (a children's outdoor game)
explanations: A traditional children's outdoor game combining hide-and-seek and tag. An empty can is placed in the open; the player who is "it" guards it while finding the others, but anyone can free the captured players by kicking the can before being caught.
A jump-rope technique in which the rope passes under the feet twice during a single jump. A staple skill children practice and compete at on the playground.
A jump-rope game in which two people swing a long rope while several others jump together inside it. A common schoolyard and sports-day activity in Japan.

glosses: to slide down; to glide down
explanations: To move downward along a surface by sliding, as down a slide, a slope, or a pole. A compound of {滑|すべ}る (to slide) and {降|お}りる (to descend).
A ball of mud shaped by hand, a classic form of children's play. Polished versions known as {光|ひか}る{泥|どろ}{団子|だんご} (shiny mud balls) are made smooth and glossy with care.
Hand-held cutting shears used to prune branches, stems, and twigs in gardening. From {剪定|せんてい} (pruning) + はさみ (scissors), with rendaku turning はさみ into ばさみ.
A professional who tends gardens — pruning trees, shaping hedges, and maintaining plantings — or who grows and sells garden trees and plants. Refers to the trade or the person practicing it.
A piece of playground equipment consisting of a long plank balanced at its center, on which two people sit at opposite ends and rise and fall alternately. From English "seesaw."
A playground structure of metal or plastic bars joined into a cube-like lattice, which children climb on, through, and over. From English "jungle gym."

headword: スーパーボールすくい
explanations: A festival stall game in which players scoop floating rubber bouncy balls from a tub of water using a thin paper scoop (ポイ), keeping whatever they catch before the paper tears. A common alternative to {金魚|きんぎょ}すくい (goldfish scooping).
A botanical family that includes roses and many familiar fruit-bearing plants such as apples, pears, cherries, strawberries, and plums. {科|か} is the suffix for a biological family.

A botanical family of flowering plants centered on lilies and tulips. {科|か} is the suffix for a biological family. (In traditional classifications it also took in plants like onions, though modern systems often place those elsewhere.)
The joint connecting the lower leg to the foot. A technical/anatomical term used in medicine, physical therapy, and sports science.

A deep, round, open container. Used for serving or holding food, for water, and—very commonly—for growing plants (a flowerpot). Wider and deeper than a flat plate; the exact meaning depends on context.
A shallow dish set under a flowerpot to catch the water and soil that drain from the hole in its bottom, protecting the floor or shelf beneath.

glosses: prepared soil for growing plants in pots
explanations: Soil blended and enriched for raising plants, usually sold in bags for use in flowerpots and planters. It is mixed to balance nutrients, drainage, and water retention.

glosses: stones placed at the bottom of a flowerpot for drainage
explanations: Lightweight stones or gravel laid in the bottom of a flowerpot before the soil is added. They improve drainage and air flow at the base, helping prevent root rot from waterlogging.

glosses: air pressure, especially inside a tire
explanations: The pressure of compressed air, most often the air inside a vehicle or bicycle tire. Correct pressure keeps tires safe and fuel-efficient; too low or too high causes uneven wear.

glosses: winter tire that grips snow and ice without metal studs
explanations: A winter tire that grips snow and icy roads through soft rubber and a special tread pattern rather than metal studs. Standard in snowy regions of Japan, where studded tires are largely banned for damaging road surfaces.

glosses: name used online instead of one's real name
explanations: A nickname a person uses on the internet—on forums, social media, games, or chat—in place of their real name. A Japanese coinage (wasei-eigo) from English "handle" + "name"; often abbreviated HN.

glosses: fully open; full throttle; at full power
fully open; at maximum; at full power
explanations: The state of being opened all the way, with nothing held back—a window thrown wide open, or a valve, tap, or throttle at maximum. Figuratively, doing something at full intensity or energy.

glosses: pedal misapplication; stepping on the wrong pedal
pressing the wrong pedal (accelerator instead of brake)
explanations: Stepping on the wrong pedal while driving—most often pressing the accelerator when meaning to brake. A frequent cause of accidents, often discussed in connection with elderly drivers. The noun form of {踏|ふ}み{間違|まちが}える.

glosses: mon — a unit of currency in pre-modern Japan
explanations: A common small unit of currency in Japan from the medieval period through the Edo period, used until the yen replaced it in 1871. A single mon was a trivial sum, so the word often appears in proverbs and set phrases meaning "a tiny amount of money."

glosses: the Book of Han, an ancient Chinese history
explanations: A classic history of China's Former Han dynasty, compiled mainly by Ban Gu in the first century CE. One of the canonical Chinese histories, it is occasionally cited in Japanese as the source of well-known proverbs and phrases.

glosses: Lake Biwa, the largest lake in Japan
explanations: Japan's largest freshwater lake, in Shiga Prefecture northeast of Kyoto. Named for its resemblance to the {琵琶|びわ} (biwa, a lute), it is a major water source for the Kansai region and a well-known scenic and historical site.
A soil amendment made from fallen leaves that have decomposed into a soft, dark, humus-rich material. Mixed into garden soil to improve its texture and water retention.
A light, porous volcanic rock full of tiny air holes, so light that it can float on water. Used to scrub calluses off skin, clean rough surfaces, and improve drainage in potted plants.
The state of a valve, damper, door, or opening being closed all the way, leaving no gap. The opposite of {全開|ぜんかい} (fully open). Often used with する or にする to mean shutting something completely.

glosses: Records of the Grand Historian (Chinese classic)
the Records of the Grand Historian, an ancient Chinese history
explanations: A monumental history of ancient China compiled by Sima Qian around 100 BCE, covering events from legendary times to his own era. The first of the canonical Chinese histories, it is the source of many phrases and proverbs still cited in Japanese.
A hot spring that periodically erupts, shooting hot water and steam high into the air at more or less regular intervals. Found in volcanic regions.

glosses: to start getting angry; to flare up
to start getting angry; to flare up; to lose one's temper
explanations: To suddenly begin to get angry. The {出|だ}す component stresses the abrupt onset — the anger flares up, often set off by something. A compound of {怒|おこ}る (to get angry) and {出|だ}す.

glosses: evil energy; noxious influence; evil spirit
explanations: Ill feeling or harmful intent toward others. Most often heard in the negative {邪気|じゃき}のない, meaning innocent, guileless, and free of any bad intentions.
An unseen harmful force or malignant spirit, as imagined in folk belief. Something to be warded off or driven away for good health and fortune.

glosses: to distinguish by ear; to listen to reason
to distinguish by ear; to tell apart by listening
to listen to reason; to be sensible; to understand and accept
explanations: To tell sounds, voices, or words apart by listening carefully. A compound of {聞|き}く (to listen) and {分|わ}ける (to separate).
To hear an explanation and accept it — to be reasonable rather than stubborn. Often said of children who behave when things are explained to them.

glosses: senior in age; older; the eldest
explanations: Being older than others, or a person who is older. Used both as a noun and, with の, as a modifier. The opposite of {年少|ねんしょう}.
An instrument that measures the humidity of the air. Often combined with a thermometer in a single household unit.

glosses: withheld number; caller ID blocked; anonymous call
explanations: A phone call whose caller number is deliberately hidden, so the phone shows "{非通知|ひつうち}" instead of a number. Also the setting that withholds one's own number when calling.
Shaping a workpiece by cutting away material with a tool, as in turning, milling, and drilling. A standard term in manufacturing and metalworking. Takes する to form a verb.
Machining a rotating workpiece with a fixed cutting tool on a lathe ({旋盤|せんばん}). One of the main types of {切削|せっさく} (cutting), best suited to round parts. Takes する to form a verb.
Cloth woven from silk thread. A somewhat formal or literary word; everyday speech usually says {絹|きぬ} or シルク.

glosses: ridge line; the line of a ridge
ridge line; the crest line of a ridge
explanations: The continuous high line of a mountain ridge, where the slopes on either side meet. {筋|すじ} adds the sense of a line or course running along the ridge.
A historical establishment where {遊女|ゆうじょ} (courtesans) lived and entertained customers, typical of the pleasure quarters of the Edo period. A dated word tied to that era.

A grammatical term for particles such as は, も, こそ, and さえ that attach to a word and add focus or emphasis rather than marking a plain grammatical case. In classical Japanese they trigger special sentence-ending inflection ({係|かか}り{結|むす}び).
In chemistry, a compound of carbon with a metal or other element (a carbide). More loosely, any material that has been charred or carbonized.

glosses: provision of information; providing information; tip-off
explanations: Supplying information to someone. Commonly used for tips given to police or the media, and for services or companies furnishing information to their users. Takes する to form a verb.
A yellowish green, like young leaves and fresh shoots. {黄緑|きみどり} alone means the same color; adding {色|いろ} makes it explicitly "the color."
Being younger than others, especially within a group such as a family, class, or team. Often used attributively with の or in compounds.
An officially compiled, authoritative history — especially the official dynastic histories of China — as opposed to unofficial or apocryphal accounts.

glosses: to get irritated; to get annoyed
explanations: To become irritated or annoyed, typically at something mildly frustrating. A casual, colloquial verb derived from the mimetic イライラ.
An oval or elliptical shape — a closed curve resembling a flattened circle.
An orbit shaped like a circle, in which a body keeps a roughly constant distance from the object it orbits.
An orbit shaped like an ellipse, in which the orbiting body's distance from the central object varies over the course of one revolution.
The circular orbit high above the equator in which a satellite's orbital period matches the Earth's rotation, so it appears to stay fixed over one point on the ground.

glosses: pick-up artist; man who habitually hits on strangers
explanations: A man skilled at, or in the habit of, approaching and picking up people he does not know, especially women in public places. Casual and often disparaging.

glosses: person without a fulfilling offline life
person whose real (offline) life is not fulfilling
explanations: Internet slang for someone whose real, offline life — especially their social or romantic life — is not satisfying. The negation of {リア充|りあじゅう}.
Casual, internet-flavored slang for an outstanding, deeply moving song — a "god-tier tune." Formed from {神|かみ} (god, used as an intensifier) and {曲|きょく} (musical piece).
A spool or drum on which an electrical cord is wound so it can be extended and retracted; often sold as a reel-in extension cord.
Crab meat preserved in a can — a common ingredient for salads, fried rice, and other dishes when fresh crab is unavailable.

glosses: cutaneous sensation; tactile sense; intuitive feel
explanations: The sense of touch — sensations such as pressure, temperature, and pain perceived through the skin.
Figuratively, a visceral, hands-on grasp of something gained through direct experience rather than reasoning or numbers.
The geological process by which water, wind, or ice gradually wears away rock and soil and carries the material elsewhere.
The geological process by which rock is broken down in place by exposure to weather — temperature changes, water, and chemical reactions — without being carried away.
The replaceable container of powdered toner used in laser printers and photocopiers.
The hole made in the earlobe or another body part for wearing pierced jewelry.

glosses: gut feeling; intuitive sense; firsthand feel
explanations: An intuitive sense or gut feeling about something, grounded in direct personal experience rather than data or theory. Often used of a practitioner's on-the-ground grasp of a situation.

glosses: deposition; accumulation; piling up in layers
explanations: The piling up of material such as sediment, snow, or debris in layers over time. In geology, the deposition of sediment that forms strata. Usually intransitive: things {堆積|たいせき}する.
A history compiled privately rather than by the state, often preserving anecdotes and folk accounts left out of official records. Contrasted with {正史|せいし}, the authorized dynastic history.
The chemical solution used to develop exposed photographic film or paper, turning the latent image into a visible one.
Pessimistic, unfavorable, or passive in attitude or thinking. The everyday sense, and the antonym of ポジティブ.
A developed piece of film in which light and dark, and colors, are reversed. Often shortened to ネガ.
The bending of rock layers into waves under compressive tectonic forces; a geological fold. Used both for the structure and, with する, for the process.
A fee charged for using something — a facility, equipment, land, or a copyrighted work. Distinct from a fee for owning or buying it.
A fee paid for the use of intellectual property, a patent, a brand, or a franchise — usually a percentage of sales or a per-unit charge.
Examination of the eyes to measure vision and detect refractive error, typically to prescribe glasses or contact lenses.
Surgery that corrects refractive errors of the eye, such as nearsightedness or astigmatism, usually by reshaping the cornea. LASIK is one type.
Forcing others to comply through pressure or intimidation; domineering and allowing no dissent.

glosses: person of great talent; great vessel
person of great talent; person of great capacity
explanations: A person of outstanding ability and breadth, likened to a large vessel. The literal sense of a large container survives mainly in set phrases.
The act of following established rules and regulations. Common in workplace, school, and safety contexts where adherence to rules is expected.
The company or person that grants a franchise, providing the brand, business model, and support to franchisees in exchange for fees.
The company or person that operates a business under a franchisor's brand and system, paying fees in return for the right to use them.
A video game genre centered on real-time physical challenges such as running, jumping, and fighting, requiring quick reflexes and timing.
Reproduction in the full range of colors, as opposed to black-and-white or a limited palette. Used of printing, displays, and images.
An organized contest in which participants compete for a prize or ranking. Used of sports, design proposals, and business bids alike.
The lower-level professional leagues below the top league, especially in American baseball, where players develop before reaching the majors.
The handheld part of a telephone containing the mouthpiece and earpiece, or a portable communication device held in the hand.
A missile whose flight path can be steered toward its target after launch, using systems such as radar, infrared, or satellite guidance.
A missile designed to strike targets at relatively short distances, typically under about 1,000 kilometers. Contrasts with medium- and long-range missiles.
A missile designed to reach distant targets, often thousands of kilometers away. Contrasts with short- and medium-range missiles.
A thick sauce into which food such as vegetables, chips, or bread is dipped before eating.
In team sports, a player who creates scoring chances for teammates by controlling the flow of play and delivering key passes, especially in soccer or basketball.

glosses: to pour into; to wash down
explanations: To pour a liquid or fluid substance into a container, mold, or opening; also to swallow food or medicine by washing it down with a drink.

glosses: to blow away; to blow along
explanations: For wind to carry something away or make it stream in a given direction. The subject is usually the wind or a current of air.

glosses: food and drink bill; cost of eating out
explanations: The amount charged or spent on food and drink, typically at a restaurant, bar, or similar establishment.
Money spent on alcoholic drinks, especially at a bar, izakaya, or drinking party.
An arrangement to record purchases and settle the total later rather than paying each time; by extension, the negative consequences of past actions that eventually come due.

glosses: to hold back; to stop by force
explanations: To physically stop or restrain a person, movement, or action from continuing, typically by pushing against it or otherwise applying force.

glosses: to call out and stop; to hail
explanations: To make someone who is passing or leaving stop by calling out to them.
In biology, the organism on or in which a parasite, virus, or other pathogen lives and from which it obtains nourishment.
The act of crossing into or interfering with territory, airspace, sovereignty, or rights that belong to another party. Often used with する as a verb.
A unit of distance used in sea and air navigation, equal to 1,852 meters. Also used as a counter: 3{海里|かいり} = three nautical miles.

glosses: right to use; usage rights; license
explanations: The legal right to use a piece of property, land, software, or intellectual work, as distinct from owning it.
In logic and computing, the operation that returns true when at least one of its inputs is true. Corresponds to the OR operator.
Treating people unfairly on the basis of group characteristics such as race, gender, or origin; showing or involving discrimination.
A shallow, portable bowl used to hold water for washing the face or hands, common at public baths and in older bathrooms.
The energy, enthusiasm, or fighting spirit with which a person or group approaches something. Often about collective morale.

glosses: to follow along; to come along; to tag along
explanations: Compound of {付|つ}く (to attach oneself to) + くる (to come). Describes a person or animal following behind and moving together with the speaker, with the ～てくる direction indicating movement toward or with the speaker.
A casual clipped form of クラウドファンディング, referring to raising money for a project or cause by collecting small contributions from many people online. Common in everyday and social-media speech.

glosses: return; yield (on an investment or effort)
explanations: The profit, benefit, or result gained back from money, time, or effort that has been put in. Common in finance and business.
The goods, service, or benefit a backer receives in exchange for supporting a crowdfunding project. A fixed term of the クラウドファンディング world.
A casual clipped form of ブレインストーミング, referring to freely generating many ideas in a group without criticizing them. Common in workplace and creative settings.

glosses: ideation technique; method of generating ideas
explanations: A structured method for producing new ideas or ways of thinking, such as brainstorming or mind mapping. Compound of {発想|はっそう} (conception, idea) + {法|ほう} (method).

glosses: guest house; budget lodging with shared facilities
explanations: Inexpensive short-term accommodation where guests share common spaces such as kitchens, lounges, and sometimes bathrooms. Popular with backpackers and budget travelers.
Describes an optimistic, constructive attitude or mindset. Applied to people, thinking, and outlooks rather than to physical or electrical 'positive'.
Software or hardware that stores the keys used to hold, send, and receive digital money or cryptocurrency. Also used for smartphone payment apps that store electronic money.
The computational process of validating cryptocurrency transactions and generating new units as a reward. Requires heavy computing power and electricity.
The first and best-known cryptocurrency, a decentralized digital currency with no central issuer. Often abbreviated BTC.
A major cryptocurrency platform, second in scale to Bitcoin, known for supporting smart contracts and decentralized applications. Its currency unit is often abbreviated ETH.

Describes a system spread across many nodes with no single central point of control. Compound of {分散|ぶんさん} (dispersion, distribution) + {型|がた} (type). Common in IT and cryptocurrency contexts, usually used before a noun with の.
A bank card that draws money directly from the holder's account at the moment of purchase, unlike a credit card, which bills the amount later.

glosses: humanoid; human-shaped; in the shape of a human
explanations: Having the form or outline of a human body. Frequently used attributively, as in {人型|ひとがた}ロボット (a humanoid robot) or a human-shaped figure.
A robot or being with a human-like form, typically having a head, torso, two arms, and two legs. In everyday Japanese it refers almost exclusively to human-shaped robots.

glosses: serving food; setting out dishes; waiting at table
explanations: The act of arranging prepared dishes on a tray or table and bringing them to diners. Used in restaurants, banquets, hospitals, and traditional inns.
An arm-like part of a machine or device that extends, swings, or grips, such as a robot arm, a crane boom, or the tonearm of a record player. Not used for the human arm, which is {腕|うで}.
A comfortable room where people can relax, wait, or socialize, such as a hotel lobby lounge, an airport lounge, or a hotel bar lounge.
A person who works, especially in a particular style or field. Very often attached to another word as a suffix, as in ノマドワーカー (nomad worker) or ケースワーカー (caseworker).
Using a facility such as a coworking space, gym, or cafe on a casual, pay-per-visit basis without a membership or reservation.

headword: スマートコントラクト
explanations: A program stored on a blockchain that runs automatically when set conditions are met, carrying out an agreement without a human intermediary.
A robot built to look and behave like a human being. In Japanese, アンドロイド usually stresses a lifelike human appearance, in contrast to a more general or mechanical-looking robot.
Not leaning toward either side of an argument, position, or value judgment. Used of stances, opinions, colors, and tones that avoid a strong bias.
The gear position of a vehicle in which the engine is not connected to the wheels.
Compensating for one's own greenhouse-gas emissions by funding an equivalent reduction elsewhere, such as tree planting or renewable-energy projects.
A state in which the amount of carbon dioxide released is balanced by an equal amount removed or offset, giving net-zero emissions. The native-word equivalent of カーボンニュートラル.
A stand-on scooter with a footboard and handlebar, propelled by kicking off the ground with one foot. Includes both children's toys and adult commuter models.
Helping someone accomplish something, especially in a supporting role. As a suru-verb, アシストする means to assist or back up. Often used of technology or equipment that aids the user.
In team sports such as soccer or basketball, a pass or play that directly leads to a teammate scoring.
A manufacturer's collection or free repair of products found to have a defect. As a suru-verb, リコールする means to recall such products.
A procedure by which voters remove an elected official or dissolve an assembly before the end of the term.

glosses: many years; a long period; long service
explanations: A long span of years. Most often seen in set expressions praising long, continuous service or membership, and in formal or written contexts rather than everyday speech.
A quiet, unexcited, low-energy mood or manner. Describes a person who seems flat or listless rather than lively. A Japanese coinage using テンション in its Japanese sense of "mood, energy level."

Not meeting the standards required for government licensing or approval. Used especially of daycare centers ({認可外|にんかがい}{保育園|ほいくえん}) that operate without formal certification, and by extension of other unlicensed facilities.

glosses: marriage hunting; actively seeking a spouse
explanations: Deliberate effort to find a marriage partner, such as attending matchmaking events, using dating services, or being introduced to prospects. The full form of the common abbreviation {婚活|こんかつ}.
Egg whites whipped with sugar until stiff and foamy, used in baking and desserts. Also refers to baked confections made from this foam.
A small handheld electric appliance with rotating beaters, used to whip cream, beat eggs, or mix batter. Distinct from a large stand mixer.

glosses: whipped to soft peaks; whipped about 70 percent
explanations: A stage of whipping cream where it thickens and forms soft peaks that fold over, but is not yet stiff. Literally "seven-tenths whipped." Used when a soft, pourable texture is wanted.

glosses: whipped to firm peaks; whipped about 80 percent
explanations: A stage of whipping cream where it holds firm, standing peaks and keeps its shape. Literally "eight-tenths whipped." Used when the cream must stay put, as for piping or decorating.
A person who is active on the photo-sharing service Instagram, especially one with many followers and influence over trends. Often overlaps with "influencer."

A casual sentence-ending expression that seeks the listener's agreement or points out something the speaker thinks is obvious. A contraction of ではないか. Often also expresses mild surprise or a sudden realization.
A casual Kansai-dialect sentence-ending particle that seeks agreement or points out something obvious. It is the western-Japan equivalent of the Tokyo-area じゃん / standard じゃない.

glosses: headnote; note printed at the top of a page
headnote; note printed in the top margin
explanations: An annotation placed in the top margin of a page, above the main text. Common in annotated editions of classical or scholarly works, where it comments on the passage below it.

glosses: marginal note; note in the side margin
explanations: An annotation placed in the side margin, beside the main text. Used to gloss individual words or explain the passage running alongside it, especially in annotated editions and textbooks.

glosses: endnote; note collected at the back of a book
endnote; note gathered at the end of a book
explanations: An annotation collected at the back of a book rather than at the foot of each page. Numbered notes in the text refer the reader to the corresponding entry in the endnote section.

glosses: endnote; note placed after the text
endnote; note placed after the main text
explanations: An annotation gathered after the main text—at the end of a chapter or the whole work—rather than at the foot of each page. Contrasts with {脚注|きゃくちゅう} (footnote), which sits on the same page as the reference.
The authoritative written source that a statement, quotation, or word usage is based on. More formal than {出典|しゅってん} and emphasizes the reliability of the source as grounds for a claim.

glosses: original text; the source in its original form
explanations: The original text of a work, as opposed to a translation, adaptation, quotation, or commentary. Often used when stressing the value of consulting a source directly rather than through a secondary version.

glosses: to peel off; to come off; to fade
to peel off; to come off; to fade (of paint, coating, color)
explanations: For a surface layer such as paint, coating, plating, or color to come away or wear off, leaving the base exposed. Intransitive: the layer comes off by itself rather than being removed by someone.
The wall surface facing the inside of a building or room, as opposed to the {外壁|がいへき} (exterior wall). Also used technically for the inner surface of a container, pipe, or vessel.

Panel- or board-type material attached to the outside of a building as its exterior wall surface. In Japan, the most common exterior-wall finish for houses; usually sold as prefinished boards of fiber cement, metal, or resin.
A workable paste of cement, sand, and water, troweled on and left to harden. Used to join bricks and blocks, to render exterior and interior walls, and as a base for tiling.
A thin, usually square or rectangular piece of fired clay, ceramic, or stone, laid in rows to cover a wall, floor, or exterior surface. Valued for durability and easy cleaning.

glosses: heating and cooling costs; air-conditioning expenses
explanations: The cost of heating in winter and cooling in summer, usually as a household or building utility expense. Combines {冷房|れいぼう} (cooling) and {暖房|だんぼう} (heating) with {費|ひ} (expense).
Blocking or reflecting radiant heat, especially sunlight, to keep a space cooler. Common in building materials, paints, and films designed to reduce solar heat gain.
A common insulation material made from fine glass fibers, used in walls, ceilings, and roofs for thermal and sound insulation.
A foam insulation material made from polyurethane, sprayed or placed to fill gaps. Offers high insulation performance and good airtightness.

headword: セルロースファイバー
explanations: An insulation material made mainly from recycled paper treated to resist fire and pests. Blown into wall and ceiling cavities; noted for good soundproofing and humidity regulation.

glosses: water supply (for irrigation or industry); service water
water supply for a set purpose; irrigation or industrial water
explanations: Water drawn and channeled for a specific purpose such as farming, industry, or firefighting. The purpose is usually shown by a prefix, as in {農業|のうぎょう}{用水|ようすい} (agricultural water).
A man-made pond that stores water, chiefly for irrigating rice paddies and fields during dry periods. Common in regions with little rainfall or few rivers.

glosses: water use; water rights; use of water resources
explanations: The use of water resources for irrigation, transport, or industry, together with the rights and arrangements governing that use. Often concerns who may draw how much water from a shared source.
A small pale social insect that eats wood, notorious for damaging the wooden structures of houses. Despite the name (literally "white ant"), termites are not true ants.
A tiny soft-bodied insect that clusters on plant stems and leaves and sucks their sap, a common garden and crop pest. It secretes a sweet substance that attracts ants.
A small jumping insect that feeds on rice plants by sucking their sap, one of the most damaging pests of rice paddies. Large outbreaks can wither whole fields.
A disease that spreads from one person or animal to another through pathogens such as bacteria or viruses. Often used for illnesses that spread widely through a population.
A machine that converts mechanical energy into electricity, from small portable units for camping and emergencies to large machines in power plants.

glosses: on the sea; offshore; on the ocean
on the sea; offshore; on the open ocean
explanations: The area on or above the open sea. Frequently used in contexts such as offshore wind power, naval operations, and marine incidents.
A loanword meaning clean — free of dirt, pollution, or corruption. Often used figuratively for energy that does not pollute, or for honest, scandal-free conduct.
Keeping indoor humidity at a comfortable level, either passively through absorbent materials or actively with equipment. Common in descriptions of building materials and air conditioners.

glosses: restart (of a plant or reactor); resumption of operation
restart of operation (of a plant, reactor, or facility)
explanations: Restarting a facility that had been shut down, so that it resumes operating. Frequently used of nuclear reactors and factories, and prominent in news about energy policy.

glosses: decommissioning of a nuclear reactor; scrapping a reactor
explanations: Permanently shutting down and dismantling a nuclear reactor. Usually paired with にする (to decommission).
Raising water to a higher place, typically with a pump. Also refers to pumped-storage hydroelectricity, in which water is pumped uphill to store energy.

glosses: wild dancing; frenzied dancing; whirling about
explanations: Dancing wildly and without restraint, often out of great joy or excitement. Also used figuratively of things such as petals or snow whirling in the air.

glosses: ecstasy; being on cloud nine; elation
explanations: Being carried away with joy, so happy that one loses composure. Almost always used with になる. Can carry a mild negative nuance of getting carried away.
A literary word for grieving over and deploring something one finds deeply regrettable, such as social decline or injustice. More formal than {嘆|なげ}く.
The anatomical term for the part of the arm between the shoulder and the elbow. More technical than {二|に}の{腕|うで}, the everyday word for the same area.
The anatomical term for the part of the arm between the elbow and the wrist. Paired with {上腕|じょうわん} (upper arm) when describing arm anatomy.
The state of having lost tightness — sagging skin, a slack rope or wire, or, figuratively, a lapse in discipline or focus. The noun form of the verb たるむ.
A loanword from English "exercise," used especially for fitness routines and workouts done for health or beauty. Often refers to lighter or trendier workouts than {運動|うんどう}.
A loanword from English "dumbbell," the short hand-held weight used for strength training. Sold in fixed or adjustable weights.
A long metal bar loaded with weight plates on both ends, lifted with both hands. A staple of gym weight training.

glosses: humidification; adding moisture to the air
explanations: Raising the moisture level of the air, typically to counter dryness in winter or in heated, air-conditioned rooms. Takes する to become a verb.
A short hand weight held in one hand for exercise, classically a solid iron piece. {鉄|てつ}アレイ is the older native term; ダンベル (from English) is now more common.
The large muscle on the front of the upper arm that flexes the elbow; the biceps. An anatomical term that is also common in fitness contexts.
Mimetic word for speaking unclearly with the mouth barely moving, often from shyness or lack of confidence. Also describes chewing or moving something slowly inside a closed mouth.
A crack or network of fine splits in a surface such as a wall, dried ground, ceramics, or chapped skin.
The upper, arched surface of the foot, opposite the sole; the instep.
In bookkeeping, recording a transaction by classifying it into debit and credit accounts; a journal entry. Takes する to mean to make such entries.
A person who manages a business, team, or performer. In Japanese schools and clubs, also the student who handles a sports team's logistics and support rather than playing.

glosses: feed; content stream (on social media or apps)
explanations: The continuously updated stream of posts, updates, or articles shown to a user in a social media app or news reader.
Buying goods over the internet. Takes する to mean to shop online.
A performer who entertains passersby in public places such as streets and parks with juggling, magic, music, or acrobatics, typically for tips.
A case for carrying and protecting a guitar, either a soft gig bag or a rigid hard case.

glosses: Super Chat; paid highlighted live-stream message
explanations: On YouTube live streams, a paid message from a viewer that is highlighted and pinned for a time; a way of tipping and supporting the streamer.
Colloquial short form of スーパーチャット, a paid highlighted message on a YouTube live stream. Often used as a verb with する.

glosses: relationship; relatedness; nature of a connection
explanations: The nature or quality of how two or more people, things, or ideas are connected. Compared with {関係|かんけい}, it emphasizes the character and structure of a connection rather than the mere fact that one exists, and is common in academic, business, and interpersonal contexts.

glosses: pale ink; thinned sumi ink; light gray ink
pale ink; sumi ink thinned to a light gray
explanations: Sumi ink diluted with water so that it writes in a light gray rather than deep black. Used in calligraphy and ink painting for shading, and by long-standing custom for writing condolence letters and the outside of {香典|こうでん} (condolence gift) envelopes.

glosses: before the Buddha; Buddhist altar offering; condolence gift inscription (from the 49th day)
before the Buddha; offering placed before a Buddhist altar; condolence gift so inscribed
explanations: Literally "before the honored Buddha." Refers to the space before a Buddhist altar and to offerings placed there, and is the standard inscription written on the envelope of a condolence money gift ({香典|こうでん}) given at Buddhist memorial services from the 49th-day rite ({四十九日|しじゅうくにち}) onward, once the deceased is regarded as having become a Buddha.

glosses: home team; team playing on its own ground
explanations: In sports, the team playing a match at its own home stadium or ground, hosting the opposing side. Contrasted with the visiting team, and typically favored by local crowd support.
A respectful term for the son of the person one is addressing or referring to, used in formal speech, letters, and ceremonial occasions. The female counterpart is {御令嬢|ごれいじょう}.
In mathematics and physics, having a small number of dimensions, as opposed to high-dimensional. Used of spaces, data, and models.
Figuratively, describing thinking, arguments, disputes, or content as base, crude, or beneath serious attention. Usually derogatory and most often used as the na-adjective {低次元|ていじげん}な.

glosses: high-level; of a higher order; on a more advanced plane
explanations: In mathematics and physics, having a large number of dimensions, as opposed to low-dimensional. Used of spaces, data, and theoretical models.
Figuratively, describing thinking, discussion, or judgment as operating at a more advanced, sophisticated, or comprehensive level. Usually approving, most often as the na-adjective {高次元|こうじげん}な.

glosses: beet sugar; sugar from sugar beets
beet sugar; sugar refined from sugar beets
explanations: Sugar made from the sugar beet ({甜菜|てんさい}), as opposed to cane sugar. In Japan it is produced almost entirely in Hokkaido, and it is valued for a mild sweetness and for naturally containing oligosaccharides.

glosses: halftone dot; the dot pattern used in halftone printing
explanations: In printing, the array of tiny dots of varying size that reproduces continuous tones and shades of gray or color. Because ink cannot vary in density on the page, larger or denser dots read as darker areas and smaller ones as lighter.
The rotating shaft that transmits power from an engine or motor to the wheels or to a driven part of a machine. In a car it carries the engine's torque to the wheels that propel the vehicle.

glosses: area studies; interdisciplinary study of a region
explanations: The interdisciplinary academic study of a particular region of the world—its language, history, politics, economy, and culture—combining several fields to understand that region as a whole. Examples include Asian studies and Middle Eastern studies.

glosses: heat transfer; transmission of thermal energy
explanations: In physics and engineering, the transfer of thermal energy—especially between a solid surface and a moving fluid, and more broadly the movement of heat from a hotter to a cooler region by conduction, convection, or radiation.
A respectful term for the daughter of the person one is addressing or referring to, used in formal speech, letters, and ceremonial occasions. The male counterpart is {御令息|ごれいそく}.

The working fluid in an air conditioner, refrigerator, or heat pump that absorbs and releases heat as it circulates, cooling or heating the surroundings. A technical term in refrigeration and HVAC engineering.

glosses: dark ink; thick, deep-black sumi ink
explanations: Sumi ink ground to a deep, dark black, as opposed to {薄墨|うすずみ} (pale, watered-down ink). Used in calligraphy and traditional writing, and standard for congratulatory or formal correspondence.
The final stage or ultimate end of something, especially of the world, of life, or of a long process. Carries a weightier, often apocalyptic or terminal nuance than a simple ending.
A formal document in which a party states in writing that they agree to or accept a proposal, request, or set of terms. Common in business, legal, and administrative contexts.

glosses: putting into practical use; practical application
explanations: The process of taking a technology, invention, or research result out of the experimental stage and making it usable in everyday life or on the market. Often used with する as a verb.

glosses: means of transportation; way of getting around
means of transportation; mode of getting around
explanations: The method or vehicle a person uses to travel from one place to another — a car, train, bicycle, walking, and so on. A practical everyday term for how one moves about.
A device that detects light, heat, motion, sound, or another physical signal and converts it into an electrical output. A loanword from English "sensor," common in everyday and technical contexts.

A traditional Japanese umbrella made of oiled washi paper stretched over a bamboo frame. Now mostly seen at temples, tea ceremonies, and in traditional or theatrical settings rather than in daily use.
The act of taking photographs, whether casually or as an organized session. Often used with する as a verb and in signs stating whether photography is permitted.
The branch of physics that studies electricity, magnetism, and the interactions between them. A standard subject in university science and engineering curricula.
The property of an organism or process that requires oxygen to live or function, as with aerobic bacteria. A biology and microbiology term, the opposite of {嫌気性|けんきせい} (anaerobic).
The hollow beneath the shoulder where the arm joins the body. A medical and anatomical term; the everyday word is {脇|わき} or {脇|わき}の{下|した}.
An organ or group of cells in the body that produces and releases a substance such as hormones, sweat, or saliva. A biology and physiology term.
The state of not falling under a given category, condition, or rule. Common on forms, checklists, and official documents to mark an item that does not apply.
A large formal meeting of a political party's members, held to decide policy, elect leaders, or set direction. A common term in political news.
The act of turning something qualitative or vague into measurable numbers so it can be compared or analyzed. Often used with する as a verb, especially in research and business.
A person who designs the physical appearance of a book — its cover, binding, paper, and overall layout. A specialized creative profession in publishing.

glosses: team member; member of a team
explanations: A person who belongs to a team, whether in sports, business, or a project group. A compound loanword from English "team" and "member".

glosses: firefighter; member of a firefighting unit
explanations: A professional member of a fire brigade whose job is to put out fires and carry out rescues. Formed from {消防|しょうぼう} (firefighting) and {隊員|たいいん} (unit member).
