A water outlet installed on a street or inside a building that firefighters connect hoses to in order to fight fires. Formed from {消火|しょうか} (extinguishing fire) and {栓|せん} (plug, valve).

glosses: volunteer fire corps; community fire brigade
explanations: A locally organized body of resident volunteers who assist with firefighting, disaster response, and prevention alongside the professional fire service. Formed from {消防|しょうぼう} (firefighting) and {団|だん} (group, corps).

glosses: certified copy; transcript (of an official register)
certified copy; full transcript of an official register
explanations: An officially issued copy that reproduces the entire contents of a public register, most often a family register ({戸籍|こせき}) or real-estate register. Contrasts with {抄本|しょうほん}, which copies only part of the register.

glosses: to start dating; to begin associating with
to start going out with someone; to begin a relationship or association
explanations: To begin a romantic relationship, or more generally to start keeping company with a person or group. A compound of {付|つ}き{合|あ}う (to associate with, to date) and {始|はじ}める (to begin).

glosses: to send to each other; to exchange (messages, gifts)
to send to one another; to exchange back and forth
explanations: For two or more parties to send something to each other mutually, such as messages, photos, or gifts. A compound of {送|おく}る (to send) and {合|あ}う (to do mutually).

The process by which a society, company, or activity becomes more open to and connected with other countries. Formed from {国際|こくさい} (international) and the suffix {化|か} (-ization). Takes する to form a verb.

glosses: in the dark; in darkness; in secret
explanations: The state of being in darkness, used both literally and figuratively for situations where one cannot see the way ahead. Formed from {暗|あん} (dark) and {中|ちゅう} (within). Largely confined to set expressions and written style.

glosses: name and reality; reputation and substance
name and reality; both in name and in fact
explanations: The relationship between what something is called or reputed to be and what it actually is. Formed from {名|めい} (name) and {実|じつ} (reality, substance). Almost always used in the set phrase {名実|めいじつ}ともに.

glosses: to turn into; to change into; to become
to turn into; to be transformed into
explanations: For something to change into a different state or thing, often a dramatic or unwelcome one. A literary variant of {化|か}する; the new state is marked with と or に.

glosses: person without a fulfilling real life (slang)
person whose offline life is not fulfilling (internet slang)
explanations: Internet slang for someone who lacks a satisfying real-world (offline) life, especially romantically or socially. The opposite of リア{充|じゅう}. Formed from the prefix {非|ひ} (non-) and リア, short for "real (life)."

glosses: abstract copy; extract (of an official register)
abstract copy; extract of an official register
explanations: An official document that reproduces only the portion of a register relating to one person, as opposed to a copy of the whole register. Almost always used in compounds such as {戸籍|こせき}{抄本|しょうほん}.
Describes flowers whose blossoms have many overlapping petals, or things arranged in many layers. Contrasted with {一重|ひとえ} (single-petaled, single-layered). Here {八|はち} ("eight") stands for "many."
A cherry variety whose blossoms have many overlapping petals, blooming a little later than ordinary single-petaled cherries. Fuller and heavier-looking than {染井吉野|そめいよしの}.

An eyelid whose double fold is partly hidden by the skin above it, so the crease is faint or concealed near the inner edge — falling between a clear {二重|ふたえ} (double eyelid) and a {一重|ひとえ} (single eyelid).
Stronger and more emotive than {汚|きたな}い — describes something so dirty or unkempt that it looks repellent. The らしい suffix adds a "gives off a ... impression" nuance.

glosses: to chill; to relax; to unwind (slang)
to chill; to relax; to unwind
explanations: Youth slang meaning to relax and take it easy, from English "chill" plus する. Overlaps with the slang adjective チルい (chill, laid-back).

glosses: casual player; those who play for fun (slang)
casual player; those who play for fun
explanations: In gaming and hobby communities, people who take part casually for enjoyment rather than competing seriously — the counterpart of ガチ{勢|ぜい} (hardcore players).

glosses: heavy spender; big spender; whale (gaming slang)
explanations: In free-to-play mobile games, players who spend large amounts of money on in-game purchases. From {重|じゅう} (heavy) + {課金|かきん} (in-app charges) + {勢|ぜい} (faction).
A number in the hundreds — one that has three places (100–999). {桁|けた} counts digits or decimal places, so {三桁|さんけた} means three places.
The melting of accumulated snow, especially as managed on roads and roofs in snowy regions; also seen in the names of equipment and agents for melting snow.

glosses: how something comes out (in a photo); photographic result
how something comes out in a photo; photographic result
explanations: The way a subject appears when photographed — whether it looks good, clear, and well-lit. Combines {写|うつ}り (how something is captured) with {具合|ぐあい} (condition, state).

glosses: several vehicles or machines; a few units
explanations: An unspecified small number — usually a few to several — of things counted with the counter {台|だい} (cars, machines, appliances). The prefix {数|すう} attaches to a counter to mean "several."

glosses: shuttered shopping street; street of closed-up shops
explanations: A shopping street where many shops have closed and rolled their shutters down for good, leaving the arcade half-empty — a symbol of decline in local retail districts.
A chemical product for cleaning — removing dirt, grease, or grime from surfaces, machinery, tableware, or the body. Made of {洗浄|せんじょう} (washing, cleansing) + {剤|ざい} (agent, preparation).

glosses: reference room; archive room; document room
explanations: A room in a library, office, museum, or company where documents, records, and reference materials are stored and consulted. Made of {資料|しりょう} (materials, reference data) + {室|しつ} (room).

glosses: light spending; small in-app payments (gaming slang)
explanations: Spending only small amounts of real money on in-game or in-app purchases. Contrasts with {無|む}{課金|かきん} (spending nothing) and {重|じゅう}{課金|かきん} (heavy spending).
An unspecified small number of occasions, typically two to five or so. The prefix {数|すう} (several) attaches to the counter {回|かい} (times, occurrences).

glosses: squalid; stuffy and shabby; cramped and dingy
explanations: Describes a place, or a person's appearance, that is dirty, cramped, and unpleasantly stuffy — shabby and uninviting. Often used self-deprecatingly of one's own home.
Organic kitchen and garden waste broken down into fertilizer, or the container or system used to make it. A loanword from English "compost".

glosses: grass clippings; cut grass; mowed grass
explanations: Grass that has been cut or mown, such as clippings left over from mowing a lawn or field. From {刈|か}る (to cut, to mow) + {草|くさ} (grass).

glosses: dead branch; withered branch; dry twig
explanations: A branch that has dried up and died on a tree, or one that has fallen from it. From {枯|か}れる (to wither) + {枝|えだ} (branch).
The process of decomposing organic waste into {堆肥|たいひ} (compost, organic manure). {堆肥|たいひ} (compost) + {化|か} (-ization). Takes する to mean "to compost".
Visiting an orchard or farm to pick and eat fruit, a popular seasonal outing in Japan. {果物|くだもの} (fruit) + {狩|か}り (picking, gathering).

glosses: profile; bio (casual abbreviation of プロフィール)
explanations: A clipped, colloquial form of プロフィール (profile), referring to a self-introduction page or bio on a social-media or messaging app.
A person who gives live running commentary — especially someone who streams video games while narrating. {実況|じっきょう} (live commentary) + {者|しゃ} (person).
An online entertainer who streams or posts videos using an animated avatar instead of appearing in person. A blend of "virtual" + "YouTuber".
A push — pressing a button, or figuratively promoting or backing something or someone. Also seen in プッシュ{通知|つうち} (push notification). Takes する to mean "to push" or "to promote".
A note or automated alert that reminds you to do something, especially a smartphone or calendar reminder, or a follow-up message. Loanword from English "reminder".
The sound a phone or app plays to signal an incoming notification. {通知|つうち} (notification) + {音|おん} (sound).
A fee charged to register or enroll — for a membership, service, course, or the like. {登録|とうろく} (registration) + {料|りょう} (fee).
A commercial gym with exercise machines and facilities for working out. A wasei compound of "sports" + "gym".
Indicates that something is not used or not contained — especially on product labels, e.g. "additive-free". {不|ふ} (non-) + {使用|しよう} (use).
A substance that helps oil and water mix and stay blended, used as a food additive and in cosmetics. {乳化|にゅうか} (emulsification) + {剤|ざい} (agent).
A food additive that prevents oxidation, keeping food from spoiling or discoloring. {酸化|さんか} (oxidation) + {防止|ぼうし} (prevention) + {剤|ざい} (agent).

glosses: list of ingredients (on a food label)
explanations: The "ingredients" heading on a packaged-food label, listing what the product is made from in order of quantity. {原材料|げんざいりょう} (raw materials, ingredients) + {名|めい} (names).
Socks, especially ankle- or calf-length ones. From English 'socks'. Often used for sportier or shorter socks, while {靴下|くつした} is the more general everyday word.

glosses: to reread; to read over again
explanations: To read something again, often to check for mistakes, refresh one's memory, or understand it better. Compound of {読|よ}む (to read) + {直|なお}す (to redo).
The length of a garment measured from top to bottom, such as the length of a skirt, sleeve, or trousers. By extension, a person's height or the full extent of something.
A container or device for turning kitchen and garden waste into compost. From English 'composter'. Used in gardening and household waste-reduction contexts.
The 'on' state of a switch, device, or setting, as opposed to オフ ('off'). From English 'on'. Frequently used as オンにする ('to turn on') and in the pair オン/オフ.

glosses: pagan; heathen; follower of a different religion
explanations: A person who follows a religion different from one's own, or who does not belong to the speaker's faith. Often carries a historical or religious-conflict connotation, as in accounts of crusades or missionary work.
A stretch of time during which progress, growth, or momentum stalls and nothing much advances. Used of economies, careers, relationships, dieting, and personal growth.

Love or affection directed unfairly toward one particular person or thing, at the expense of others. Implies a lack of balance, as when a parent favors one child or a person is obsessively fond of one thing.
A soldier or armed guard stationed to protect a place such as a palace, gate, or important building. Often refers to the ceremonial guards at royal or government sites.

glosses: fire brigade; firefighting unit; fire crew
explanations: An organized team of firefighters that responds to fires and other emergencies. Refers to the unit or crew as a whole rather than an individual firefighter.
A state of being completely worn out in body and mind. A formal, written-style word that almost always appears in the set phrase {疲労困憊|ひろうこんぱい} ('worn out with fatigue').

glosses: leader; commander; one who leads a group
explanations: A person who leads and unites a group, army, or organization, directing its members toward a common goal. Emphasizes the authority and ability to keep a group under control and moving together.

glosses: view of nature; outlook on nature
view of nature; way of seeing the natural world
explanations: A person's or culture's fundamental way of understanding nature and humanity's relationship to it. Used in discussions of philosophy, religion, art, and cultural comparison.

glosses: view of the universe; cosmology; conception of the cosmos
explanations: A person's or culture's conception of what the universe is and how it is structured. Used in discussions of religion, philosophy, mythology, and the history of science.

glosses: foreign land; place away from home
a place away from home; unfamiliar land
explanations: A place other than one's hometown, where one lives or travels as an outsider. A somewhat literary word that carries connotations of loneliness or longing for home.
Having no value, worth, or usefulness. Used of objects, ideas, efforts, or a person's self-image when they are judged to be of no worth at all.

glosses: paganism; a religion different from one's own
explanations: A religion or faith other than the one regarded as standard by the speaker. From the standpoint of a given religion, it labels other belief systems, often with a historical or judgmental connotation.

glosses: evil cult; heretical religion; false teaching
explanations: A religion or cult regarded as wicked, false, or harmful. Used to condemn beliefs seen as dangerous, immoral, or deceptive, often in contrast to an orthodox faith.
A soldier or guard stationed to keep watch over a place, standing guard at an entrance, gate, or post to detect intruders.
A prolonged period during which activity, performance, or the economy stays sluggish and fails to improve. Applied to businesses, sports teams, industries, and personal careers.
The practice of hanging washed laundry to dry inside the house rather than outdoors, common during the rainy season, in winter, or when pollen and privacy are concerns.

glosses: child with a disability; disabled child
explanations: A child who has a physical, intellectual, or developmental disability. Used in education, welfare, and medical contexts.
A test administered to job applicants as part of a hiring process, assessing knowledge, aptitude, or suitability. Common for companies, government offices, and schools.
A satellite that orbits the Earth at the same rate as the planet's rotation, so it appears to stay fixed above one point on the equator. Used for weather observation and communications.
A person who uses a product, tool, service, or substance. The everyday, general meaning.
In labor law and industrial relations, the party that employs workers—the counterpart of {労働者|ろうどうしゃ} (worker). Refers to the company or individual bearing an employer's legal duties.
The head of a university or college, responsible for its overall administration and academic leadership.
A facility with designated lanes and targets where people practice firing guns safely, for sport, training, or military purposes.

glosses: new address; where one has moved to
explanations: The place or address to which a person has moved or is moving; the destination of a relocation. Often used for mail forwarding and change-of-address notices.

glosses: reminder letter; demand notice; dunning letter
explanations: A written notice urging someone to fulfill an overdue obligation, such as paying a bill or returning a borrowed item. Firmer in tone than a simple reminder.
An unfavorable assessment or rating given to something, indicating dissatisfaction or a judgment of poor quality. Common on review sites and video-sharing platforms.
The sale of a product in restricted quantities, for a limited time, or only at certain locations, creating a sense of exclusivity. Often used with する.
The company or place from which a business obtains the materials, goods, or funds needed for its operations.

glosses: entrance; entryway (esp. a school's, where shoes are changed)
explanations: The entrance area of a building—typically a school—where people go in and out and often change between outdoor shoes and indoor shoes. Also a boarding hatch on a ship or aircraft.
Historically, a person who worked in service to a master's household or shop, often living in and receiving room and board. Especially associated with the Edo period.
The act of putting something together again in a new arrangement, or reorganizing a system, structure, or set of information. Often used with する.

glosses: award history; record of awards won
award history; record of prizes won
explanations: A record or list of the prizes and awards a person or work has received over time.
A person who is wounded or ill, especially one needing medical attention in an emergency, disaster, or first-aid situation.
A pharmacy licensed to fill doctors' prescriptions and prepare prescription medicine, as opposed to a drugstore that mainly sells over-the-counter products and daily goods.
The practice of a hospital or clinic preparing and handing prescribed medicine to the patient on its own premises, rather than issuing a prescription to be filled at an outside pharmacy.

The system in which a hospital issues a prescription and the patient has it filled at an independent pharmacy outside the facility. This is now the standard practice in Japan under the separation of prescribing and dispensing.
A common red ladybird beetle with seven black spots (Coccinella septempunctata), widespread in Japan. It feeds on aphids and is regarded as a beneficial insect.
Describes an effort or situation so earnest, or so pitiable, that it moves one nearly to tears. Most often used of someone's painstaking, self-sacrificing efforts.
A flat stone set in a garden path or across water at intervals, so that one can cross by stepping from one stone to the next. A characteristic feature of Japanese gardens.
A lantern carved from stone, traditionally placed in Japanese gardens, temples, and shrine grounds. Originally used to hold a light, it now serves mainly as a decorative ornament.
A flexible, heat-resistant synthetic material made from silicon compounds, used for kitchenware, molds, sealants, and medical and cosmetic products.
The flexible stems of the rattan palm, and the material woven from them for furniture, baskets, and other goods.
A small mat or pad placed under a glass or cup to protect the table surface from moisture, heat, or scratches.
Describes a relaxed, unpretentious look or style — in fashion, makeup, or interior design — that appears effortless and stays close to natural materials, colors, and forms.

A very casual, emphatic sentence-ending expression used to assert something the speaker treats as obvious, often with a note of insistence or mild reproach. It is a stronger form of じゃん, itself a contraction of じゃないか.

glosses: separation of prescribing and dispensing of medicine
explanations: The system in which a doctor writes a prescription but the medicine is dispensed separately by a pharmacy, rather than being handed out at the clinic. It is the standard arrangement in modern Japanese healthcare.
The nonmetallic chemical element silicon, abundant in sand and rock and central to semiconductors and glass. Also written {ケイ素|けいそ}.

glosses: run of holidays broken up by workdays
series of holidays with workdays in between
explanations: A stretch of the calendar in which public holidays fall close together but are separated by one or two ordinary workdays, so the days off do not form one continuous break. Literally 'stepping-stone consecutive holidays'.
A frozen dessert made from fruit juice or purée, sugar, and water, without the milkfat of ice cream. Lighter and icier than アイスクリーム.
Fine sand and dust blown from the deserts of mainland Asia, especially China and Mongolia, that drifts over Japan mainly in spring, clouding the sky and settling on surfaces.
A belch — gas released from the stomach through the mouth. A somewhat literary or formal word, most often met in the set phrase おくびにも{出|だ}さない.
Describing behavior, a reaction, or a manner that looks intentionally staged rather than genuine, so that it comes across as forced or insincere.
A large, reddish-brown, tree-dwelling great ape native to the rainforests of Borneo and Sumatra, with long arms and high intelligence.
An adult male gorilla whose back has turned silvery-gray with age. The silverback is the dominant leader of a gorilla group.
The single reproductive female of a bee colony, which lays the eggs and around which the hive is organized. Also used figuratively for a dominant woman at the center of a group.
A non-reproductive female bee that gathers nectar, builds and cleans the hive, and cares for the young. Also used figuratively for a person who works hard without much reward or recognition.
A large, black, hairy bee that bores nest tunnels into wood. Despite its loud buzz and bulky body, it is docile and rarely stings. Also written {熊蜂|くまばち}.

glosses: clump of tall grass; grassy thicket
explanations: A patch of ground densely overgrown with tall grass and weeds, the kind of place where insects and small animals hide. Also written {草叢|くさむら}.
A green, long-legged grass-dwelling insect of the katydid family, known for the shrill chirping the male makes with its wings on summer days.
A small, dark, jumping insect whose males chirp by rubbing their wings together, especially on autumn evenings. Also written {蟋蟀|こおろぎ}.
A large green or brown grasshopper (the migratory locust) common in Japanese fields, known for its strong jumping and long flights. Also written {殿様飛蝗|とのさまばった}.
Either of the front legs or paws of a four-legged animal or insect, as opposed to the hind legs. Also written {前脚|まえあし}.

The way an animal resembles its surroundings or another creature — in color, shape, or pattern — to hide from predators or prey. Used as a suru-verb ({擬態|ぎたい}する) meaning to disguise oneself in this way.
Body coloring that lets an animal blend into its surroundings so that predators or prey cannot easily see it. A biology term, also used figuratively for anything that helps someone go unnoticed.

glosses: palate cleanser; something to remove an aftertaste
palate cleanser; something to take away an aftertaste
explanations: Eating or drinking something to clear a lingering taste from the mouth, or the food or drink used for that purpose. Often used after a strong or unpleasant flavor, or between courses.

glosses: median strip; central reservation (of a road)
explanations: The strip in the middle of a road that separates traffic moving in opposite directions. May be a raised curb, a planted area, or a barrier.
A roadside safety barrier made of horizontal metal pipes supported by posts. Common along sidewalks and at intersections to separate pedestrians from vehicles.
A roadside safety barrier made of tensioned steel cables strung between posts. Absorbs the impact of a vehicle by flexing, common on highway medians and mountain roads.

glosses: single steel pipe used for scaffolding and barriers
explanations: A standardized steel pipe, typically about 48 mm in diameter, used with clamps to build scaffolding, temporary fences, and simple structures at construction sites.
Emergency first aid for someone whose heart or breathing has stopped, combining chest compressions and rescue breathing to keep blood and oxygen circulating until professional help arrives.
A short training course, often run by the fire department, that teaches emergency first aid such as CPR and the use of an AED. Open to the general public.
Immediate, temporary care given to an injured or sick person on the spot, before a doctor or ambulance takes over. Includes stopping bleeding, bandaging, and cooling burns.
The closed-fist hand shape in the game janken, which beats scissors (チョキ) and loses to paper (パー). Also refers to a clenched fist more generally.
The two-fingers-extended hand shape in the game janken, which beats paper (パー) and loses to rock (グー). The shape resembles a pair of scissors.
The open-hand shape in the game janken, which beats rock (グー) and loses to scissors (チョキ). Also used for an open, spread hand generally.

glosses: showing one's hand late; acting after seeing others' moves
showing one's hand late (esp. cheating at janken); acting only after others
explanations: Deliberately making one's move after seeing what an opponent has done, so as to gain an unfair advantage. Originally the cheating move in janken; widely used figuratively for opinions or decisions made only once the outcome is clear.

glosses: webbing (between the toes or fingers of an animal)
explanations: The membrane of skin stretched between the toes or fingers of water animals such as frogs, ducks, and otters, used to push against the water when swimming.
A practitioner of {修験道|しゅげんどう} (Shugendo) who undergoes ascetic training in the mountains to gain spiritual power. Recognizable by a distinctive robe, a small black cap, and a conch-shell horn.
A Japanese religious tradition that seeks spiritual power through ascetic training in sacred mountains. It blends esoteric Buddhism, Shinto, and folk beliefs; its practitioners are the {山伏|やまぶし}.

glosses: round-the-world trip; trip around the world
explanations: A journey that goes all the way around the world, returning to the starting point. Used of travel by ship, plane, or any means.

A craftsperson whose trade is sharpening and polishing blades such as kitchen knives, scissors, or Japanese swords, using whetstones. The sword-polishing specialist is a highly skilled traditional craftsman.

glosses: medley; a sequence combining different parts
explanations: A combination performed in one continuous stretch: in swimming, a race or relay that mixes the four strokes; in music, a piece stringing several tunes together without pause.

glosses: frog kick; the breaststroke leg motion
explanations: The characteristic leg movement of the breaststroke, in which the knees bend and the feet sweep outward and then together, resembling the kick of a frog.

glosses: the pull; the propulsive arm action in swimming
explanations: In swimming, the phase in which the arms pull the body forward through the water, as opposed to the kick. Also refers to drills that isolate the arms.

glosses: tugboat; a boat that tows or pushes larger vessels
explanations: A small, powerful boat used to tow or push ships that are too large or disabled to maneuver on their own, especially in and out of harbors.
In baseball, the outfielder who covers center field, positioned between the left fielder and the right fielder.
In baseball, the outfielder who covers right field. A strong throwing arm is valued because of the long throw to third base.
In baseball, the outfielder who covers left field, positioned to the left of center field as seen from home plate.
A baseball statistic measuring how often a batter reaches base — via a hit, a walk, or being hit by a pitch — expressed as a rate.
The closing part of a chapter in a book, especially the summaries or practice problems placed there in textbooks and study guides.

glosses: the tiles held in one's hand; one's hand
explanations: In mahjong, the set of tiles a player holds and manages during play, kept hidden from opponents until they are used or discarded.

glosses: a drawn game of go; a tie
explanations: In the board game go, a result in which the two players' territory is equal, so that neither side wins.

glosses: the season leader in runs batted in
explanations: In baseball, the title given to the player who records the most runs batted in (RBIs) over a season.
A chemical substance produced by the body that regulates functions such as growth, metabolism, and mood.
Internal organs of cattle or pork grilled at a barbecue, a popular casual food especially associated with the Kansai region.

glosses: eating until about 80 percent full; eating in moderation
explanations: The practice of stopping eating before feeling completely full, regarded as good for health. Also said as {腹八分目|はらはちぶんめ}.
A person's former boyfriend. A casual, colloquial term common in conversation and on social media.
A person's former girlfriend. A casual, colloquial term common in conversation and on social media.
Describes movements or relationships that are not smooth — stiff, jerky, or strained. Most often used as ぎくしゃくする.
A worker hired on a day-to-day basis rather than under a long-term contract, typically paid at the end of each day's work.
A security method that requires two separate forms of verification, such as a password plus a one-time code sent to a phone.

glosses: hours of sunshine; hours of daylight
explanations: The length of time during which direct sunlight reaches the ground in a given day or period. A meteorological term also used in farming and real estate.
A small cup for drinking sake, larger than a {猪口|ちょこ}. Often prized as a piece of pottery.

glosses: drive mechanism; drive unit; driving gear
explanations: The mechanism that produces or transmits the power to move a machine or vehicle, such as a drivetrain or motor assembly.
A train car, or a rental car, in which smoking is permitted, as opposed to a non-smoking one.
The degree to which something is compressed, expressed as a ratio. Used for data files, engine cylinders, and materials.

glosses: the samurai class; the shizoku class
the samurai class; the former-warrior (shizoku) class
explanations: The social class made up of former samurai families, an official category designated in the Meiji era after feudal warrior status was abolished.
Microorganisms such as bacteria and yeast that cause fermentation, used in making foods like miso, natto, and yogurt.
A substance used to prevent or eliminate pests, insects, or plant diseases, especially in agriculture and gardening.

glosses: customer-drawing effect; ability to attract customers
explanations: The effect of drawing in customers or visitors; how well something pulls in a crowd. A marketing and retail term.

glosses: to fret; to be anxious; to worry impatiently
to fret; to worry impatiently; to be anxious and restless
explanations: To feel restless anxiety while waiting for or worrying about something one cannot control. Built on the mimetic やきもき, which conveys nervous, fidgety impatience.

glosses: prosperous business; thriving trade; flourishing commerce
explanations: A business doing well, with plenty of customers and sales. A set phrase strongly associated with good-luck charms and prayers for commercial success.

glosses: doing a roaring trade; a constant stream of customers
a constant stream of customers; doing a roaring trade
explanations: A four-character idiom describing a shop or business visited by an endless flow of customers. Literally 'a thousand guests, ten thousand comings.'
The eye on the left side of the face.
The eye on the right side of the face.

glosses: daruma otoshi; traditional block-knocking toy game
explanations: A traditional Japanese toy consisting of a stack of colored wooden blocks topped by a daruma figure. Players knock out the blocks one at a time with a small hammer without letting the daruma fall.

glosses: to drag on into; to carry over into (overtime, etc.)
to drag on into; to end up extending into (overtime, a later stage)
explanations: For a contest, negotiation, or dispute to fail to be settled and spill over into an additional stage such as extra time, a playoff, or a further round. Combines もつれる (to become tangled/deadlocked) with {込|こ}む (to move into).

glosses: walk-off win; game-ending win by the home team
walk-off win; a win scored by the home team in the last at-bat
explanations: In baseball, a victory in which the home team scores the winning run in the bottom of the final (or extra) inning, ending the game instantly. サヨナラ ('goodbye') marks the abrupt end of play.
An overtime format in which the first side to score wins immediately and play ends at once. From English 'sudden death.' Used in soccer, golf playoffs, and various tournaments.
In soccer or rugby, a kick awarded to a team after a foul by the opponent, taken from the spot of the infringement with the defenders held back a set distance.
In soccer and similar sports, the red card shown by the referee to send a player off for a serious offense. The player is ejected and cannot be replaced.
A punishment or disadvantage imposed for breaking a rule or failing to meet an obligation. Used in sports for a penalty awarded against a team, and more generally for fines or forfeits.

glosses: prohibited move; forbidden tactic; banned technique
explanations: A move or technique that the rules forbid, originally in sumo and board games. By extension, any tactic that is off-limits because it is unfair or against the spirit of a contest.

glosses: practice swing; swinging drill (bat, racket, sword)
explanations: Swinging a bat, racket, golf club, or sword through the air without hitting a ball or target, done to warm up or to drill proper form. Read すぶり.
In baseball, the number of official times a batter comes to the plate, excluding walks, sacrifices, and hit-by-pitches. The denominator used to calculate batting average.

glosses: relay pitching; use of relief pitchers
relay pitching; using relief pitchers in succession
explanations: In baseball, the strategy of bringing in one pitcher after another over the course of a game rather than letting a single starter finish. Also used with する.
In baseball, a complete game in which the pitcher allows no batter to reach base at all — no hits, no walks, no errors — retiring every opposing hitter in order.
In swimming, a kick in which both legs move together in an up-and-down undulating motion, like a dolphin's tail. Used in the butterfly stroke and off the walls after a turn.

glosses: stroke; a single stroke of the arms or a racket
explanations: One complete pulling or hitting motion in a sport: an arm stroke in swimming or rowing, or a groundstroke off the ground in tennis. From English 'stroke.'

glosses: entry into the water; the moment of entering the water
explanations: In diving and swimming, the act or moment of entering the water. In diving, a clean, near-splashless entry is a mark of good technique. Read にゅうすい; also used with する.
The alternating up-and-down kicking of the legs used in the front crawl and backstroke. バタ mimics the flapping sound; {足|あし} means legs or feet.
A baseball game in which a pitcher allows the opposing team no hits and no runs through the entire game. From English "no hit, no run"; a {和製英語|わせいえいご} coinage.
In soccer and other sports, a yellow card shown by the referee to formally caution a player for a foul or misconduct. Two yellow cards in one match result in a red card and ejection.
In soccer, a kick taken from the corner of the field, awarded to the attacking team when a defender last touches the ball before it crosses their own goal line.
In soccer, a direct kick from the penalty spot with only the goalkeeper defending, awarded for a serious foul committed inside the penalty area. Also used in rugby. Often abbreviated PK.
The reopening of a shop or restaurant after it has been remodeled or refurbished. Composed of {新装|しんそう} (new fittings, refurbishment) and {開店|かいてん} (opening for business).

glosses: mallet; hammer (with a wooden or metal head)
explanations: A striking tool with a heavy head fixed at right angles to a handle, used to drive chisels, stakes, and pegs or to pound materials. The head may be wood or metal.
A mallet with a wooden head, used where a metal hammer would damage the surface—driving chisels, tapping joints together, or striking soft materials. Composed of {木|き} (wood) and {槌|つち} (mallet).
A power tool with a spinning abrasive disc or wheel, used to cut, grind, or polish metal and stone. In everyday Japanese it usually refers to a handheld angle grinder ({ディスクグラインダー}).
The formal term for a vehicle's turn signal—the flashing lamp that shows the driver's intention to turn or change lanes. Composed of {方向|ほうこう} (direction) and {指示器|しじき} (indicator).
A toothed wheel in a machine, or—most commonly in everyday use—one of the selectable gear settings of a car or bicycle transmission. Also spelled ギヤ.

glosses: engine stall; stalling of the engine
explanations: An unintended stopping of a car's engine while driving or maneuvering, typically from mishandling the clutch. A {和製英語|わせいえいご} clipping of "engine stop" (エンジンストップ). Takes する.
An automatic transmission, or a car equipped with one, which shifts gears by itself without a clutch pedal. A clipping of オートマチック (automatic); the opposite is マニュアル (manual).

glosses: starting off; moving off (of a vehicle)
explanations: The act of a stationary vehicle, ship, or aircraft beginning to move. Composed of {発|はつ} (to set out) and {進|しん} (to advance). Takes する; used chiefly of vehicles, not people.

glosses: to let go of; to release; to set free
explanations: To stop holding something, or to let a captive creature go. The emphasis is on releasing one's grip or restraint, rather than on moving two things apart.
The rearranging of who sits where, especially the periodic reassignment of pupils' desks in a school classroom. Composed of {席|せき} (seat) and {替|か}え (changing). Takes する.

glosses: second class; second grade; second prize
explanations: The second rank in a graded series—second class of travel or accommodation, second grade of quality, or second prize in a lottery or contest. Composed of {二|に} (two) and {等|とう} (rank, grade).

glosses: participation prize; consolation gift for taking part
explanations: A small prize or gift given to everyone who takes part in an event, contest, or lottery, regardless of whether they win. Composed of {参加|さんか} (participation) and {賞|しょう} (prize).
A lottery ticket with a coated area that is scratched off to reveal whether it has won. Short for スクラッチくじ. From English "scratch".

A tall grass ({イネ科|イネか}) that grows near water, and especially its hard, glossy, teardrop-shaped seeds. The seeds are naturally holed and have long been strung as beads. Composed of {数珠|じゅず} (prayer beads) and {玉|だま} (bead).

glosses: straw bag; bale (for rice, charcoal, etc.)
explanations: A cylindrical sack woven from rice straw, traditionally used to hold and transport rice, charcoal, or potatoes. Also serves as a counter for such bagged goods ({一|いち}{俵|ぴょう}, {二|に}{俵|ひょう}).
A shimmering illusion of water on a hot road or field that recedes as you approach it, caused by heated air bending light near the surface.
A species of great ape closely related to the chimpanzee, native to the rainforests of the Congo Basin and known for its peaceable social behavior.
A marine mammal of the eared seal family, with visible ear flaps and the ability to walk on land by rotating its hind flippers forward.
An eared seal with a thick two-layered coat of fur, smaller than the sea lion and historically hunted for its valuable pelt.
The thin, blade-like or paddle-like appendage of a fish or aquatic animal, used for swimming, steering, and keeping balance.
A true seal with a pale grey coat marked by scattered dark spots, common in the cold waters of the northern Pacific and a popular aquarium animal in Japan.
The pair of hoe-shaped metal horns projecting from the front of a samurai helmet, often gilded and used as a mark of rank.
The largest stag beetle native to Japan, with a glossy black body and thick mandibles, highly prized by hobbyist collectors.
A common Japanese stag beetle with long, curved mandibles lined with small teeth like a saw, a frequent summer catch for children.
A stag beetle of cooler, higher-elevation forests, recognizable by the ear-like flanges at the back of the male's head.
The act of connecting or passing something along in the middle of a chain, or a person or place that mediates between two sides, as in trade or negotiation.
A pitcher who takes over the middle innings after the starter leaves and before the closer, holding the game steady.

glosses: closer; relief pitcher who finishes the game (baseball)
explanations: The act or means of keeping something under control — an emotion, a rise in prices, or one's authority over others.
The relief pitcher brought in to protect a lead and record the final outs, typically in the last inning.

glosses: closer; relief pitcher who finishes the game (baseball)
explanations: A relief pitcher brought in to protect a narrow lead and record the final outs, usually in the ninth inning; an English loanword.
A pitching statistic counting the number of batters a pitcher strikes out. Viewed from the pitcher's side, in contrast to {三振|さんしん}, which is the batter striking out.
A batter skilled at making contact and getting on base consistently, valued for a high average and bat control rather than raw power.

glosses: to retire a batter; to get (a batter) out
to retire a batter; to get (a batter) out (baseball)
explanations: (of a pitcher or the fielding side) to put a batter out without allowing a hit, often by inducing a weak grounder or fly ball.

glosses: cleanup hitter; fourth batter in the order (baseball)
explanations: The fourth item in a numbered sequence or order, such as a seat, counter window, or bus route.
The fourth spot in the batting order, traditionally filled by the team's most powerful hitter.

glosses: to listen attentively; to appreciate (music, a lecture)
explanations: To listen with focused attention and appreciation, especially to music, a concert, or a lecture — deliberate listening rather than merely hearing.
The person who leads an orchestra or choir, setting the tempo and shaping the interpretation of the music; an English loanword.
An honorific for a distinguished conductor or a master of a musical art, borrowed through Italian and used as a term of respect.
Holding a post, seat, or membership on an ongoing, permanent basis rather than temporarily. Used attributively before the name of a position or organization.

A performance given as an invited guest with a group or company one does not normally belong to, as when a conductor, actor, or musician appears with another ensemble or theater. Takes する to mean to make such an appearance.
A musician who plays accompaniment — typically on piano — supporting a soloist, singer, choir, or instrumentalist. Formed from {伴奏|ばんそう} (accompaniment) plus the suffix {者|しゃ} (person).
Performed with no instrumental accompaniment — a voice or solo instrument on its own. Formed from {無|む} (without) plus {伴奏|ばんそう} (accompaniment). Used attributively with の or before a noun.
Singing with no instrumental accompaniment, whether solo or in a group where the voices supply all the parts. From Italian "a cappella." Often used adverbially with で.
Adding on to an existing building to enlarge it — an extra room, floor, or wing. The everyday counterpart of the more technical {増築|ぞうちく}. Takes する to mean to build such an addition.

The ratio of a building's footprint (the area it covers on the ground) to the total area of the plot, expressed as a percentage. A legal limit set by zoning that determines how much of a lot may be built on.
The ratio of a building's total floor area (summed over all stories) to the area of the plot, expressed as a percentage. A zoning limit that effectively controls how tall or dense a building may be.

glosses: batting lineup; the batters as a unit (baseball)
explanations: A team's batters considered collectively as an offensive unit, especially with regard to their combined hitting power. Literally the "hitting line."

A pitcher taking the mound to pitch in a game. Literally "climbing the plate/mound." Takes する to mean to pitch in a game. By extension, also used figuratively for someone stepping up to take on a task.

glosses: to bring down; to finish off; to nail (a target)
to bring down; to kill (game or prey)
to finish off; to secure decisively (a win, a chance)
explanations: To kill an animal or target with a weapon, especially in hunting — to hit the mark and bring it down. Transitive, taking を.
By extension, to finish off an opponent or seize a decisive opportunity — landing the crucial blow, hit, or goal that settles the outcome. Common in sports and competitive contexts.

glosses: easy out; weak batted ball that results in an out (baseball)
explanations: A batted ball that produces a routine out — a weak grounder or easy fly with no result — as opposed to a hit. Literally an "ordinary hit." Takes する to mean to make such an out.

glosses: tax affairs; tax administration; tax matters
explanations: Matters and work relating to taxes — filing, assessment, payment, and the administration of tax law. Used attributively in the names of offices, jobs, and procedures.

glosses: real estate transaction specialist qualification (and its exam)
explanations: A common abbreviation of {宅地建物取引士|たくちたてものとりひきし}, the national qualification (and the exam for it) required to handle certain steps in real estate transactions in Japan. Also used for the license and the profession.

glosses: winning a title; taking the championship
explanations: Gaining control over a region, field, or rivals so as to stand above all others. Takes する to mean to dominate or conquer.
In sports and competition, winning a tournament or title outright — beating all comers to the top. {全国|ぜんこく}{制覇|せいは} is a set phrase for winning a national championship.
The opening instrumental section of a song, before the singing begins. A clipping of English "introduction," used almost exclusively of music.
The money paid periodically for the use of rented property, especially land or buildings. A more formal, contractual term than {家賃|やちん}.
Failure to carry out a duty or obligation, especially one set out in a contract. Most often seen in the legal phrase {債務不履行|さいむふりこう} (default on an obligation).
A privately owned automobile, as opposed to public transportation or a company or rental car. A Japanese coinage from English "my car."

glosses: every month; monthly; month by month
explanations: Each successive month, on a month-by-month basis. Used both as a noun and adverbially, most often for recurring payments or amounts.
The sum of money to be paid back on a loan or debt, often figured per period (monthly, yearly) or as a total.
A form a patient fills in before seeing a doctor or receiving a vaccination, giving symptoms, medical history, and current condition.
The board used to play the game of go ({囲碁|いご}), marked with a grid of lines on which stones are placed at the intersections.

glosses: bifocal; progressive (lenses); for both near and far vision
bifocal; progressive; for both near and far vision
explanations: Describing eyeglasses or lenses designed for both near and distant vision. Literally "combined use of far and near."
An animal that has no backbone, such as an insect, mollusk, or worm. Contrasts with {脊椎動物|せきついどうぶつ} (vertebrate).
The state of a bill, fee, or debt having already been paid in full. Often marked on invoices and receipts.
A device used to measure a physical quantity such as length, temperature, voltage, or weight.
The part of a bag, basket, or container that you grip or hang it by to carry it.
The act of producing spoken words. Often used in contexts of language development and speech ability.
A gathering where people study or learn about a topic together, such as a class, seminar, or reading circle.
A table that lists two or more sets of items side by side so they can be compared or matched, such as a conversion or correspondence chart.
Things people do in their free time for enjoyment or relaxation, such as hobbies, sports, or travel.

glosses: water pipe; water main; water conduit
explanations: A pipe that carries water from one place to another, especially a large pipe in a water-supply system.
A report describing the current condition or situation of a project, system, or task.
A period during which farmland is left unplanted, either to rest the soil or because it is not the growing season.
Allowing electric current to pass through a material. Usually appears in compounds such as {導電性|どうでんせい} (conductivity).
A status marking that a payment has already been received or a deposit made. Common in online shopping, invoicing, and accounting to flag an order or account as settled.

glosses: energizing; passing an electric current through something
explanations: Applying electric current to a device or circuit so that it becomes live, typically to power equipment on for operation or testing. Takes する to form a verb.
A table that lays out the features, prices, or specifications of two or more items side by side so they can be compared at a glance.
The sum of money that has been borrowed, for example under a loan or mortgage. Distinct from the interest or the amount already repaid.
A car owned or leased by a company and used by employees for business purposes, as opposed to a privately owned car.
Resentment or ill will that remains long after the event that caused it, often between people or groups with a history of conflict.

glosses: earthbound spirit; ghost bound to a place
explanations: In Japanese folklore and horror, the spirit of a dead person that cannot move on and remains tied to a specific location, typically where they died.
A chemical compound made up only of carbon and hydrogen atoms. Hydrocarbons are the main components of petroleum and natural gas.
A clipping of English 'substitute' or 'sub-'. Refers to a backup or secondary person or thing as opposed to the main one — a substitute player, a spare device, or a secondary account.
In soccer, a defender who plays in the middle of the defensive line, in front of the goalkeeper, and is responsible for marking opposing forwards.
In soccer, a defender who plays on the left or right side of the defensive line. Fullbacks often join attacks down the flank in addition to defending.
In soccer, a midfielder who plays just in front of the defense, breaking up opposing attacks and distributing the ball. From Portuguese 'volante'.
In soccer, a midfielder who plays on the left or right side of the midfield line, providing width in both attack and defense.
In physics and chemistry, a change of a substance from one phase to another — for example from solid to liquid or liquid to gas. Takes する to describe undergoing such a change.
A word chosen to represent the content of a document so that it can be found in an index or search. Used in publishing, libraries, and information retrieval.
In Japanese folklore and popular spiritualism, the spirit of a dead person that drifts from place to place rather than being tied to one location.
A transition of a substance between physical states — solid, liquid, and gas. A standard term in school science, close in meaning to {相変化|そうへんか} (phase change).

glosses: beat; the basic unit of musical time; counter for beats
explanations: The regular pulse that underlies a piece of music, and the counter used to count those pulses. In Japanese music theory it is the traditional term for the English 'beat.'

glosses: groove; the rhythmic feel or swing of music
explanations: The infectious rhythmic feel of a piece of music — the sense of momentum and swing that makes listeners want to move. Borrowed from English 'groove.'
A rechargeable battery that stores energy by moving lithium ions between electrodes. Widely used in smartphones, laptops, and electric vehicles for its high energy density.

glosses: distribution of electric power; supplying electricity
explanations: The delivery of electricity from local substations through distribution lines to homes and businesses — the final stage of the power grid, as opposed to long-distance transmission ({送電|そうでん}).
An electricity network that uses digital sensing and communication to balance supply and demand in real time, integrating renewable sources and reducing waste. Borrowed from English 'smart grid.'
The field of computer science and AI concerned with getting computers to understand, interpret, and generate human language. Covers tasks such as translation, summarization, and sentiment analysis.
A mathematical operation that combines two functions by sliding one over the other, widely used in signal processing and in the convolutional layers of neural networks for image recognition.

headword: ニューラルネットワーク
explanations: A computational model loosely inspired by the brain, made of layers of interconnected 'neurons' that learn patterns from data. The foundation of modern deep learning.

glosses: to be replaced; to be swapped out
explanations: For one thing to take the place of another. The intransitive counterpart of {置|お}き{換|か}える (to replace); the new item that takes over is marked with に.

glosses: built-in; internal; having a component incorporated inside
explanations: Having a part or function built into a device rather than attached externally. As a する verb it means to incorporate something inside; as a modifier ({内蔵|ないぞう}〜) it means 'built-in.'
A service that keeps your files on remote servers accessed over the internet, so they can be reached from any device and shared easily. Borrowed from English 'cloud storage.'
The country of Canada, occupying most of northern North America. Its official languages are English and French.
The island country of New Zealand, in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, southeast of Australia.

glosses: working holiday; working holiday visa program
explanations: A program based on bilateral agreements that lets young people stay in a partner country long-term and take short-term work to fund their travel. The full form of the abbreviation ワーホリ.
A plastic card used in place of a metal key to unlock doors, common at hotels, offices, and apartment buildings. It is read by inserting or holding it over a card reader.
A large agricultural machine that reaps a crop, threshes it, and separates the grain from the straw in a single continuous operation. In Japan most commonly used for the rice harvest.
The compass direction midway between north and west.
The compass direction midway between south and east.
The organized, interrelated whole formed by a country's laws — the way its statutes, codes, and regulations fit together as a structured system.

glosses: compendium of laws; complete book of the Six Codes
explanations: A comprehensive reference volume that collects the texts of the major Japanese statutes, centered on the Six Codes ({六法|ろっぽう}). A standard tool for law students and legal professionals.
The body of law governing commercial transactions and businesses; in Japan, one of the Six Codes. Also used loosely to mean a particular way of doing business.

The body of law that sets out how lawsuits are conducted — the rules of court procedure — as opposed to substantive law, which defines rights and duties. Divided mainly into civil and criminal procedure.
A past court decision, especially of a higher court, that serves as an example or authority for deciding later cases with similar facts. Collectively, the body of such decisions.

glosses: to wipe out (a disgrace); to avenge; to clear (one's name)
explanations: To remove or make up for a disgrace, dishonor, or humiliating defeat, typically by achieving a later success or victory. A formal, somewhat literary word, most often used with objects such as {恥|はじ} (shame) or {汚名|おめい} (a bad name).

glosses: handover; delivery; transfer (of goods, property, or a building)
explanations: The act of handing something over to another party — delivering purchased goods, or turning over a completed building or piece of property to its owner.
The handing over of a person, especially a suspect or criminal, to the authorities or to another country.

glosses: to be far apart; to differ greatly; to be worlds apart
to be far apart; to differ greatly
explanations: To be greatly separated — usually figurative, describing a wide gap between two things in degree, quality, or nature rather than physical distance. Intransitive.
Describes something intended for medicinal use — cosmetics, plants, or household products that contain an active ingredient. Attaches directly to a noun ({薬用|やくよう}{石|せっ}けん) or with の.
The raising of pigs as livestock, and by extension the industry built around it.
The deliberate ending of a pregnancy. A formal term with a legal and clinical tone; in everyday speech {中絶|ちゅうぜつ} is far more common.
A type of persimmon that loses its astringency on the tree and can be eaten raw when ripe, as opposed to the astringent {渋柿|しぶがき}.
A traditional Japanese color — the warm, reddish orange of a ripe persimmon fruit.
The pressure of a sound wave in the air. In everyday audio talk, the perceived force or punch of a sound, especially of loud bass.
A wide version of the traditional wooden veranda ({縁側|えんがわ}), broad enough to set out a table and chairs. Common in ryokan and Japanese-style guest rooms.
The portion of a Japanese phone number that identifies the local exchange. Most often heard in {市外|しがい}{局番|きょくばん} (area code) and {市内|しない}{局番|きょくばん}.
The edge or side portion of a road. A somewhat technical, traffic-related term, most familiar in {路側帯|ろそくたい} (the marked strip along the road edge for pedestrians).
Sand, gravel, or crushed stone mixed with cement and water to make concrete or mortar. It forms the bulk and structural body of the hardened material.

glosses: receiving a gift; accepting a donation
explanations: The act of receiving a present or donation. A formal term seen mostly with museums, libraries, and institutions; it is the receiving counterpart of {寄贈|きぞう} (donating).
An angle that is not a right angle — a slanted angle. Used in geometry, and in machining or carpentry for a cut or join made on the slant.
Strong physical or sexual desire; sensual craving. A formal, somewhat literary word, common in novels and moral or religious discussion.

glosses: the three poisons; greed, anger, and delusion
explanations: In Buddhism, the three root afflictions said to poison the mind and keep beings trapped in suffering: craving, hatred, and ignorance. In general writing it appears as a learned metaphor for the same three failings.

glosses: sum of money; fee; charge; allowance (suffix)
sum of money; fee; charge; benefit payment
explanations: Attached to a noun to name a specific sum of money set aside, owed, or paid out for the purpose named by the base word. Extremely productive in contracts, invoices, and administrative Japanese.
The national agency responsible for weather forecasts, and for earthquake, tsunami, and volcano information in Japan. Its announcements are the standard source quoted in news reports.
A regional membership body of local businesses that lobbies on their behalf, offers management advice to small firms, and administers well-known certification tests such as the bookkeeping exam.

glosses: prime minister's official office; the Kantei
explanations: The building in Tokyo that houses the prime minister's working offices and crisis-management centre. Like "the White House" in English, it is regularly used as shorthand for the prime minister and his immediate staff.

glosses: place of refuge; last resort; safe haven
place of refuge; last resort for people in trouble
explanations: An organization or person that people in difficulty turn to when they have nowhere else to go. Originally a temple that took in women fleeing their husbands in the Edo period; the modern use is almost always figurative.

glosses: hiring through personal connections; nepotistic hiring
hiring through personal connections; recruitment by referral
explanations: Employing someone on the strength of a family tie or personal introduction rather than an open selection process. The word is broadly neutral in business usage but often carries a critical edge.

glosses: kanji approved for use in personal names
explanations: A government-designated list of about 860 kanji that may be used in a child's given name in addition to the general-use {常用漢字|じょうようかんじ}. Characters outside both lists cannot be registered at the city office.
The 1,026 kanji that Japanese children learn during the six years of elementary school, assigned grade by grade. Materials for beginners and children are often written using only these characters.
The condition that results when the body loses more water and salts than it takes in, producing dizziness, headache, and weakness. The standard term in health warnings during hot weather and illness.

glosses: due date; expected date of delivery
explanations: The date on which a baby is expected to be born, as calculated by a doctor. The standard term on maternity forms and in conversation about a pregnancy.

glosses: contamination by a foreign object; foreign matter in a product
explanations: The presence of something that does not belong — a hair, a piece of plastic, a fragment of metal — in food, drink, or medicine. The fixed term used in product recalls and news reports.

glosses: lending rate; interest rate on loans
explanations: The rate of interest a bank charges when it lends money. Contrasted with the deposit rate a bank pays to savers; the gap between them is the bank's margin.
A login method that requires two or more independent kinds of proof — a password, a code sent to a phone, a fingerprint — before granting access. Now standard on banking and workplace systems.

The way computers represent real numbers, with the position of the decimal point stored separately so that very large and very small values fit in the same format. Used almost exclusively in computing contexts.
A prime number that divides a given whole number exactly. Learned in Japanese middle school, chiefly in the phrase {素因数分解|そいんすうぶんかい} (prime factorization).
The number which, multiplied by itself three times, gives the number in question. A standard term in Japanese school mathematics.
A pattern of vertical and horizontal stripes crossing to form squares, and by extension cloth woven in that pattern. The traditional Japanese name for what is now usually called チェック.
The part of speech covering words such as ああ, おい, and はい, which stand alone and express feeling, call to someone, or answer. One of the categories used in Japanese school grammar.
The hospital department that takes X-rays, CT and MRI images, and delivers radiation therapy. One of the department names on a Japanese hospital's floor guide.

glosses: society of commerce and industry; local business association
explanations: A statutory local organization of small businesses in a town or village. It offers management advice, bookkeeping help, and loan support to member shops and workshops, and often runs local events.
A house provided at public expense to a high-ranking official — a prime minister, governor, mayor, or ambassador — for the duration of the post. The occupant lives there but does not own it.

glosses: kanji taught in elementary school; educational kanji
explanations: The set of kanji that Japanese children are taught during the six years of elementary school, assigned grade by grade under the national curriculum. The list currently contains 1,026 characters.
Verifying someone's identity from a physical feature such as a fingerprint, face, iris, or vein pattern, instead of from a password or card.
A pattern of squares of two alternating colors, like a chessboard. Used on kimono cloth, floor tiles, wrapping paper, and design work generally.

glosses: to remember fondly; to reminisce about; to think of with affection
to remember fondly; to reminisce about
explanations: To call to mind a person who is absent or dead, or a time now past, with warmth and a touch of longing. Most often used of the deceased and of one's own younger days.

glosses: to show signs; to begin to appear; to sprout
to show signs; to begin to appear
explanations: For something not yet visible — a season, a feeling, a social change — to give its first faint indication. The subject is the thing coming into being, not the person noticing it.
A flat piece of unused land covered in grass and weeds, especially one in or near a town where children play. Informal and everyday in tone.
The place on a riverbank or shore where a ferry boat takes on and lets off passengers. Common in descriptions of pre-modern travel, before bridges were built.

glosses: way one uses one's hands; hand movements
explanations: The visible manner in which someone moves their hands while doing something. Almost always used with a modifier that judges the movement as skilled, clumsy, gentle, and so on.

glosses: commercialization; turning something into a product
explanations: Developing an idea, technology, or design into something that can actually be sold. Used with する as a verb: {商品化|しょうひんか}する.
Describes a person or attitude that hides the truth or misrepresents it. Also used as a noun for dishonesty itself.
The blank space on a form, contract, or delivery slip where the person signs their name. Also used of the signature box in an email or on a web form.
Postal service that delivers faster than ordinary mail for an extra fee. Items are marked with a red line and handled ahead of regular post.
A ticket or coupon that lets the holder receive something without paying — a meal, a drink, admission, or a service.
A hall where groups gather for meetings, lectures, or community events. Often a shared facility belonging to a neighborhood association, apartment complex, or temple.
Material used to protect goods during shipping — bubble wrap, foam, crumpled paper, cardboard fillers, and the like.
The assorted smaller costs that come with a purchase or transaction on top of the main price — fees, taxes, insurance, and handling charges. Standard wording in real estate, car sales, and travel.

glosses: rate of increase; rate of rise
explanations: How much a figure has gone up, expressed as a percentage of its earlier value. Used of prices, wages, temperatures, and stock indexes.
The proportion of a population that becomes infected with a disease, usually given as a percentage. Also used of computer viruses spreading through a network.

glosses: private residence; personal home of a public figure
explanations: The home a politician, executive, or other public figure owns personally, as opposed to the official residence provided with the post. Used mainly in news reporting.
The way someone moves their hands when working with an object — a knife, cards, a tool, an instrument. Usually said admiringly of speed and precision.

glosses: rate of decline; rate of fall
explanations: How far a figure has fallen, expressed as a percentage of its earlier value. Used of prices, share values, and land values.
How much something has grown, expressed as a percentage of its earlier size. Used of sales, users, wages, and populations, and generally positive in tone.

glosses: fatality rate; death rate among those affected
explanations: The proportion of people who die among those who catch a disease or suffer a particular injury. A medical and public-health term, common in news about epidemics.

glosses: seal box; space for a stamp on a form
seal column; box for affixing a personal seal
explanations: The small marked space on a form or contract where a personal seal is to be stamped. Found on applications, delivery slips, and official paperwork.

glosses: productization; developing into a marketable product
explanations: Taking a technology, prototype, or idea and turning it into something that can actually be manufactured and sold. Used with する as a verb.

glosses: number of infected people; case count
number of infected people; number of cases
explanations: How many people have been confirmed to have caught a particular infectious disease, usually reported for a given day or region.

glosses: grassy field; patch of untended grass
explanations: An open piece of ground left to grow over with grass and weeds. Casual in tone and often used of vacant lots and riverbanks where children play.

glosses: to be in a rush; to feel impatient
to be hurried; to feel rushed; to be impatient
explanations: For a person's mind or breathing to be driven forward by impatience. Intransitive, and most often used of {気|き} (one's feelings) or {息|いき} (one's breath).

glosses: to give everything one has; to use up completely
to give one's all; to put out everything one has
explanations: To hold nothing back — to expend all of one's strength, skill, or ideas. Transitive, and most often used of {力|ちから} or {実力|じつりょく} in sports and work.
The long cranial nerve that runs from the brain down through the neck and chest to the abdomen, controlling heart rate, digestion, and other automatic functions.
A suffix attached to a Sino-Japanese noun to mean "after that event": {退職後|たいしょくご} (after retirement), {卒業後|そつぎょうご} (after graduation). Written-style and very productive.
The largest figure in a set of measurements or the highest value a function or quantity takes. A technical term used in mathematics, statistics, and engineering.
The money a company spends on advertising, treated as a cost item in accounting and business planning.
Someone employed by a state or military organization to gather secret information. A formal term, used in news reporting and spy fiction.

glosses: legal personality; status as a legal entity
explanations: The legal standing that lets an organization hold property, sign contracts, and sue in its own name, separately from the people who run it.
The latitude line at about 66.5 degrees south, and by extension the region south of it where the sun stays up or down for a full day at the solstices.
A customer using a shop or service for the first time, as opposed to a repeat customer. Business vocabulary used in marketing and sales talk.
The paper, film, or containers used to wrap a product for display and sale. Discussed often in connection with waste reduction and recycling.
The percentage by which something — most often an economy, a market, or a company's sales — increases over a given period. Standard vocabulary in business reporting and economic statistics.
The smallest number in a set of data or the lowest value a function or measurement takes. Used in mathematics, statistics, and any context involving recorded figures.
The figure obtained by adding up a set of values and dividing by how many there are. Used wherever data is summarized: test scores, measurements, survey results, and economic statistics.

glosses: advertising expenses; publicity costs; promotion budget
explanations: Money a company spends on advertising and promoting its products. Appears as a line item in budgets and financial statements.

glosses: covert operative; secret agent; undercover agent
explanations: A person sent by a state or organization to carry out clandestine activity — espionage, sabotage, or influence operations — in another country or group. Almost always used of the other side, never as a neutral job title.
A customer a business already has, as opposed to one it is trying to win. Standard marketing and sales vocabulary, usually contrasted with {新規|しんき}{客|きゃく} (new customers).

glosses: death toll; number of deaths; fatalities
explanations: The count of people killed by a disaster, accident, epidemic, or conflict. Standard news vocabulary, usually paired with {負傷者数|ふしょうしゃすう} (number of injured).
The nerve that carries visual signals from the retina to the brain. Used in medical contexts and in explanations of how the eye works.
The continent surrounding the South Pole. Used when the landmass itself is meant, as distinct from {南極|なんきょく}, which can refer more loosely to the South Pole or the Antarctic region.

glosses: to see through to the end; to finish completely
to see through to the end; to carry out fully; to finish completely
explanations: To do something all the way to completion without giving up partway, often with the sense of having put everything into it. Common in talk about work, training, and personal goals.

glosses: extent of a decline; size of a drop
extent of a decline; size of a drop; margin of decrease
explanations: How far a price, index, or value has fallen, expressed as an amount or percentage. Standard vocabulary in market and economic reporting.

glosses: self-important; stuck-up; acting like a big shot
explanations: Describes someone who behaves as if they were more important or knowledgeable than they are. Always critical — it describes the impression the person gives, not their actual standing.

glosses: to go for tea; to hang out at a café
to go for tea; to have a coffee; to hang out at a café
explanations: To spend time at a café or tea shop, chatting over a drink. Casual spoken Japanese; the point is the socializing rather than the tea itself, so it covers coffee and cake just as well.

glosses: that far; to that extent; that much
to that extent; that much; that seriously
explanations: As far as a place already mentioned or visible. Literally そこ (there) plus まで (as far as).

Extended to degree rather than distance: as far as the level the other person has described. Very often used with a negative to play something down — そこまでではない, "it's not that bad / not that big a deal."

glosses: unpaid amount; outstanding balance; accounts payable
explanations: Money that is owed but has not yet been paid. In everyday use it is an overdue bill or arrears; in accounting it is a balance-sheet liability for goods or services already received.
The image produced by an X-ray examination. Everyday Japanese for what a doctor or dentist shows you on the screen or lightbox.

glosses: output terminal; output jack; output port
explanations: The socket or connector on a device from which a signal or current is sent out. Standard wording in manuals and specification sheets for audio, video, and electrical equipment.

glosses: to make a profit; to gain a benefit
to make a profit; to earn a return
to gain a benefit; to profit from something
explanations: To come out financially ahead from a business, sale, or investment.
To obtain an advantage that need not be monetary — a favorable position, useful information, or an improved situation. Often used when pointing out who stands to gain from an arrangement.

glosses: uncollected receivable; outstanding amount owed to one
uncollected receivable; money still owed to one; accounts receivable
explanations: Money that has been earned or billed but not yet received. In everyday use it is an amount a customer still owes; in accounting it is an asset recorded for revenue already recognized.

What a company spends to push sales of a product: campaigns, samples, in-store displays, coupons, and similar activity. A shortening of {販売促進費|はんばいそくしんひ}, and treated as a distinct line item in a budget.

glosses: extent of a rise; margin of increase
extent of a rise; size of an increase; margin of gain
explanations: How far something has gone up — a price, a stock index, a temperature — stated as the size of the movement rather than the final figure. Common in news reporting on markets and weather.

glosses: input terminal; input jack; input port
explanations: The socket on a device through which a signal comes in — the audio, video, or data connector you plug an incoming cable into. The counterpart of {出力端子|しゅつりょくたんし}.
The nerve that carries sound information from the inner ear to the brain. Damage to it causes hearing loss that a hearing aid cannot fully correct.

glosses: number of deaths; death toll; fatality count
explanations: How many people died from a given cause or in a given period, as reported in official statistics. Formal register: used in government releases, news reports, and research.

glosses: to take a short break; to have a smoke or a cup of tea
to take a short break; to pause for a breather
explanations: To stop work briefly and relax. {一服|いっぷく} literally means one dose or one serving, so the break is typically accompanied by a cigarette or a cup of tea — often implied even when not stated.

glosses: to come out ahead; to gain; to benefit
to come out ahead; to gain an advantage; to benefit
explanations: To end up better off than one otherwise would — paying less, getting extra value, or gaining some advantage. The direct opposite of {損|そん}をする.

glosses: move one can make; recourse; available countermeasure
explanations: A course of action still open in a difficult situation. Taken from board games, where {手|て} is a move and {打|う}つ is to play a stone or piece, so the word frames a problem as a game position with moves left or none.
The number dialed before a phone number to reach another country — 81 for Japan, 1 for the United States. Also used for the country code entered in online forms.
An event at which visitors sample drinks — wine, sake, beer, or coffee — usually hosted by a maker, brewery, or shop to introduce products. The food equivalent is {試食会|ししょくかい}.

glosses: customer visiting a store; store visitor
customer visiting a store; store visitor; walk-in customer
explanations: A customer who comes to a shop or restaurant in person, as distinct from one who orders online or by phone. Retail and marketing vocabulary, common in sales reports.

glosses: kaki-no-tane; small crescent-shaped soy-sauce rice cracker
explanations: A snack of small curved orange rice crackers flavored with soy sauce and a touch of chili, named for their resemblance to persimmon seeds. Usually sold mixed with peanuts and eaten with beer.

glosses: celebratory meal; festive tray of dishes
explanations: A special set of dishes served to mark an occasion such as a birth, a wedding, a milestone birthday, or New Year. {膳|ぜん} is the individual tray on which a formal Japanese meal is laid out, so the word names both the food and its presentation.

glosses: medical record; patient chart; clinical record
explanations: The record a doctor is required to keep of a patient's examinations, diagnoses, and treatment. This is the legal and administrative term; in day-to-day hospital speech the same thing is called カルテ.
Goods produced from farm animals — meat, milk, eggs, and hides. A category term used in trade statistics and agricultural policy alongside {農産物|のうさんぶつ} and {水産物|すいさんぶつ}.
A brown so deep that it approaches black. Belongs to written description — field guides, product specifications, scientific and medical writing — rather than everyday conversation.
A holder of the national electrical work qualification, which is legally required in Japan to install or alter household and commercial wiring. The suffix {士|し} marks a licensed professional.
A power tool that cuts with a spinning toothed disc, used mainly for making straight cuts in wood and building materials. Also written {丸鋸|まるのこ} or, in tool catalogs, {丸|まる}ノコ.

glosses: safety fence; protective barrier; guard rail
explanations: A fence or railing put up to keep people away from something dangerous — machinery, a construction site, a platform edge, or a drop. Common on signage and in workplace safety rules.

glosses: accounts receivable; money owed by customers
explanations: Money a business is owed for goods or services it has already delivered on credit. A standard balance-sheet asset account, and the counterpart of {買掛金|かいかけきん}.

glosses: accounts payable; money owed to suppliers
explanations: Money a business owes for goods or services it has already received on credit. A standard balance-sheet liability, and the counterpart of {売掛金|うりかけきん}.

glosses: accrued payable; amount not yet paid
explanations: Money owed for something already received but outside the company's ordinary trade purchases — equipment, advertising, professional fees. Distinguished in bookkeeping from {買掛金|かいかけきん}.

glosses: advance payment received; deposit taken in advance
explanations: Money collected from a customer before the goods are delivered or the service is performed. It counts as a liability until the work is done, because the business still owes something in return.

glosses: depreciation; writing off an asset over time
explanations: Spreading the cost of a long-lived asset such as a building, machine, or vehicle across the years it is used, instead of treating the whole purchase as an expense at once.
The office procedure of submitting receipts for money spent on company business and being paid back for it. A routine monthly task in Japanese workplaces.
