Money spent on activities meant to boost sales — samples, in-store displays, campaigns, and giveaways. The full form of the everyday abbreviation {販促費|はんそくひ}.
An organized occasion at which people try food — a maker testing a new product on consumers, a caterer showing a wedding menu, or a store promoting an item.
A power saw whose teeth are set on a loop of chain running around a guide bar, used for felling trees, cutting logs, and pruning thick branches.
A motor-driven tool that spins a bit to bore holes in wood, metal, or concrete. Sold in both corded and rechargeable versions at any home center.
A motor-driven tool that turns screws in and out. Most household models are rechargeable and are used for assembling furniture and small repairs.

glosses: to lose out; to be worse off; to take a loss
explanations: To end up worse off than one otherwise would — paying more, wasting effort, or missing an advantage. The direct opposite of {得|とく}をする.
The point on a device where a wire or plug connects — a battery post, a screw terminal, or a socket such as an HDMI or USB port.

glosses: fourteen days; the fourteenth (of the month)
the fourteenth day of the month
explanations: A duration of fourteen days. Often written {十四日間|じゅうよっかかん} when the length of time needs to be explicit.
The 14th as a calendar date.

glosses: twenty-four days; the twenty-fourth (of the month)
the twenty-fourth day of the month
explanations: A duration of twenty-four days. Written {二十四日間|にじゅうよっかかん} when the length of time needs to be explicit.
The 24th as a calendar date.

glosses: to skip; to leave out; to overtake
to skip; to leave out; to omit
to overtake; to pass ahead of
explanations: To pass over something that should have been included — a line while reading, a step in a procedure, or a meal.
To get in front of someone who was ahead. Very often used in the passive when someone cuts in line or passes you unfairly.

glosses: to start talking; to begin to speak
explanations: To begin speaking, often after a silence or unexpectedly. The focus is on the moment speech starts, not on what is said.

glosses: to start walking; to set off on foot
explanations: To begin walking after standing still, or to set out toward somewhere. Also used of a baby taking its first steps.

glosses: indoor shoes; shoes worn inside a building
explanations: Shoes kept for wearing inside a school, hospital, or workplace, changed into at the entrance so that outdoor dirt is not tracked in.

glosses: advance payment; prepaid expense; money paid up front
explanations: Money handed over before goods are delivered or services are performed. In accounting it is carried as an asset until the goods or services are actually received.
A portion of the total price paid before the goods or services are delivered, with the balance settled later. Unlike a deposit securing a contract, it counts directly against the amount owed.

glosses: amortization; writing off; paying off (a debt)
explanations: In accounting, spreading the cost of an asset over the years it is used, or removing its remaining value from the books. Most often met in the compound {減価償却|げんかしょうきゃく}.
Clearing a debt or obligation by paying it back in full. More formal than {返済|へんさい} and largely limited to financial writing.
The portion of a fixed asset's cost charged as an expense in a given accounting period. It appears on the income statement even though no cash changes hands that year.

glosses: cash advance; provisional payment; temporary disbursement
explanations: Money paid out before the final amount is known, to be settled up later. Typically an advance given to an employee for travel or entertainment costs, reconciled against receipts on return.

headword: インパクトドライバー
explanations: A power tool that drives screws by combining rotation with rapid hammering blows, giving it far more torque than an ordinary electric screwdriver. Standard equipment on construction sites and popular with home DIY users.

glosses: brush cutter; grass trimmer; weed cutter
explanations: A machine for cutting down grass and weeds, typically the shoulder-carried type with a long shaft and a spinning blade or nylon cord at the end. Used on farmland, roadsides, and around houses.
The opening into which a plug, card, or connector is inserted. Used for electrical outlets, headphone jacks, USB ports, card slots, and similar receptacles.

glosses: contingency fund; reserve funds; contingency allowance
explanations: Money set aside in a budget for unforeseen expenses. Used of national and local government budgets, company budgets, and the buffer built into a project's costs.

glosses: setting sail; departure (of a ship or aircraft)
explanations: A ship or aircraft leaving on a voyage. The focus is on the start of the journey rather than on the act of leaving a particular harbor.

glosses: here and there; sparsely; now and then; in small numbers
explanations: Describes things appearing in small, scattered numbers rather than all at once — a few flowers open, a few people visible, a rumor heard occasionally. Often marks the very beginning of something that will later become general.

glosses: in scattered drops; one by one; haltingly
in scattered drops; one by one; here and there
explanations: Describes things falling or appearing singly at intervals — the first drops of rain, people arriving a few at a time, lights dotted across a dark landscape.
Describes speech that comes out slowly in short bursts with pauses between, typically because the speaker is reluctant, tired, or choosing words with care.

glosses: number of scheduled services; number of flights
explanations: How many scheduled runs a transport service operates over a given period — flights, ferry sailings, long-distance buses, or delivery rounds. Usually counted per day or per week.
A situation that demands immediate action. Almost always used in set expressions about getting through or coping with the crisis rather than on its own.
The work that came immediately before the current one by the same creator or in the same series — the earlier film, novel, game, or album. Used constantly in reviews and promotional writing.

glosses: wind and rain; the elements; rough weather
explanations: Rain accompanied by wind, treated as a single force. Most often used for what a building, plant, or person is exposed to and must be sheltered from.

glosses: in its own way; reasonably; to a certain extent
explanations: Says that something is adequate or worthwhile when judged by what it is, without claiming it is outstanding. It grants modest approval while quietly setting expectations low.

glosses: ability to memorize; powers of rote memory
explanations: The capacity to commit material to memory by heart, especially vocabulary, formulas, or facts for an examination. Discussed mainly in the context of studying.
The process by which economies, companies, and societies become linked across national borders. Used of markets, supply chains, education, and culture alike.

glosses: emergency; time of crisis; state of emergency
explanations: A period when normal conditions break down and extraordinary measures are needed, such as a disaster, war, or serious accident. Used of the situation as a whole rather than of a single incident.
Describes a device that runs on a built-in battery which is recharged rather than replaced. Almost always used before a noun with の, or as a product-description label.

glosses: advance payment; suspense payment; cash advance
explanations: Money a company pays out before the final amount or purpose is settled, typically an advance to an employee for travel or other expenses. In bookkeeping it is held in a temporary account until receipts are submitted and the account is cleared.

glosses: acquisition cost; purchase cost; cost basis
explanations: The total amount originally paid to acquire an asset such as land, a building, or shares, including related fees. When the asset is later sold, this figure is subtracted from the sale price to calculate the taxable gain.

glosses: brush cutter; string trimmer; weed whacker
explanations: A handheld powered tool with a rotating blade or nylon cord on a long shaft, used to cut grass and undergrowth. It is the technical name found in manuals, safety rules, and rental listings.

The general conditional ending, attached to the verb or adjective stem. It presents the first clause as the condition under which the second holds, and is the most neutral and abstract of the Japanese conditionals.

glosses: welcome and farewell party; combined send-off and welcome party
explanations: A single gathering that both sends off members who are leaving and welcomes those who are arriving. Common in Japanese workplaces and schools in spring, when transfers and new appointments take effect at once.

glosses: you know; I tell you (feminine emphasis)
you know; I tell you (feminine sentence-final emphasis)
explanations: A sentence-final combination of わ and よ used in feminine speech to assert something to the listener. It is softer and warmer than plain よ, and often carries a note of reassurance or mild insistence.

glosses: you see; the thing is (feminine explanatory)
you see; the thing is; that's why (feminine explanatory emphasis)
explanations: A sentence-final combination of the explanatory の and the emphatic よ, used in feminine speech. It presents the statement as an explanation or background the listener did not know, rather than as bare new information.
The last of the three terms in the Japanese school year, running roughly from early January to late March. It is the shortest term and ends with graduation and the close of the school year.

glosses: the actual exam; the main examination
the actual exam; the main examination; the real test
explanations: The official examination itself, as opposed to a practice test, a mock exam, or a makeup sitting. The {本|ほん} marks it as the genuine occasion on which the result counts.

Someone who is staying in a place for a period of time without living there permanently, such as a foreign resident, a hotel guest, or a long-term visitor. Mainly used in administrative and statistical contexts.

glosses: running out of time; time-up; expiry of the time limit
explanations: The state of having used up the allotted time before finishing. Used of games, exams, negotiations, and meetings, often with the implication that the matter was left unresolved.

glosses: one's youth; adolescent years; the springtime of life
explanations: The years of late adolescence and early adulthood, roughly the school and university period, seen as a time of energy, friendship, and first love. The word is warm and nostalgic, and is almost always used looking back.

glosses: home country; country of origin; one's own country
explanations: The country a person is a national of, or the country where an organization is based, spoken of from outside it. Used of citizens abroad, foreign residents, and the headquarters of a company or government.

glosses: to create; to originate; to bring into being
to create; to originate; to found
explanations: To bring into existence something that did not exist before — a work of art, a company, a culture, a new future. A kanji variant of {作|つく}る chosen when the writer wants to stress originality rather than manufacture.

glosses: playing in water; water play; splashing about
explanations: Children's play in shallow water — a pool, a stream, a fountain, or a garden hose. It is casual play rather than swimming, and the word is used mainly of small children.
A narrow flow of water, smaller than a river. A literary word found in written descriptions of landscape and in geographical writing rather than in conversation.

The ordinary, non-emergency state of affairs, used above all in contrast with {非常時|ひじょうじ} (emergencies, disasters, wartime). Common in administrative, disaster-preparedness, and corporate planning language.

glosses: transfer expenses; costs of selling an asset
explanations: The costs incurred in transferring ownership of property or another asset — brokerage commissions, stamp duty, demolition or surveying fees. In Japanese tax practice these are subtracted, along with the acquisition cost, when calculating taxable capital gains.

A gathering held to see off someone who is departing — a transferring colleague, a graduating student, a person going abroad. Slightly more formal and celebratory in tone than {送別会|そうべつかい}, emphasizing well-wishing rather than parting.
A person staying overnight at a hotel, ryokan, or other lodging. The standard word in the hospitality and tourism industries, and the usual term in news reports about accommodation.

The period of a person's life from later childhood into the early teens, looked back on as a stage. Strictly it refers to a boy's youth, but it is also used loosely for childhood in general, especially in reminiscence and biography.
Food served quickly and cheaply over a counter — hamburgers, gyudon, fried chicken and the like — and by extension the restaurants that serve it. From English "fast food".

A shop where customers pay by the hour for a seat or booth with free access to a large manga library, drinks, and usually internet terminals. Many stay open all night and are used as cheap overnight lodging.

A shop charging by the hour for a booth with an internet-connected computer, drinks, and usually manga and video content. In Japan these overlap almost completely with manga cafes, and many are open around the clock.

glosses: to pounce on; to spring at; to lunge at
explanations: To leap suddenly at a person or animal in order to attack or seize them. The target takes に. Used of predators, of people attacking in anger, and figuratively of eager rushing at an opportunity.
Unpleasantly loud, whether the source is machinery, traffic, or people talking. Stronger and more negative than {うるさい} is in its mildest uses, and often has a note of complaint.
Demanding and hard to satisfy about a particular matter, marked with に. Applied to people who insist on high standards, and to rules or inspections that are strictly enforced.
Quiet, composed, and gentle in speech and movement. Traditionally used to praise women, so in modern usage it can sound old-fashioned or, said of someone acting out of character, faintly teasing.
Describing a person who stands their ground, says what they think, and does not back down when opposed. Usually admiring or neutral, though it can imply someone is hard to argue with.

glosses: far from; on the contrary; let alone
far from ~; on the contrary; not only not ~
let alone ~; to say nothing of ~
explanations: Denies the preceding statement and replaces it with something at the opposite extreme: not merely "not X" but in fact the reverse. Attaches to plain-form verbs and adjectives and to bare nouns.
Used with a negative predicate to say that even a modest case does not hold, so a greater one certainly does not. The item after どころか is the smaller or easier case.

glosses: to open; to establish; to set up
to open; to establish; to set up (a facility, service, or account)
explanations: To bring something newly into operation so that it is available for use — an office, a shelter, a bank account, a website, a phone line. The emphasis is on starting the service, not on constructing the building.

glosses: secondly; second (in rank or order of importance)
explanations: Marks the following item in a sequence of actions, steps, or speakers. Neutral in register and very common in instructions, presentations, and written explanation.
Introduces the second item in an enumeration, typically after {まず} (first). Also used with に in the pattern 〜の{次|つぎ}に to mean "after ~" or "second to ~".

glosses: Chinese steamed bun; steamed filled bun
explanations: A soft steamed wheat bun with a savoury or sweet filling, sold hot at convenience stores from autumn through winter. The two standard kinds are {肉|にく}まん (pork) and あんまん (sweet red bean).
Medicine taken to stop diarrhea. The everyday word used in pharmacies and at home, in contrast with the technical {止|し}{瀉|しゃ}{薬|やく}.
An organ of the executive branch that carries out public administration — a ministry, an agency, or a local government office. Contrasted with the legislature and the courts.

glosses: such; that kind of; like that
such; that kind of; of that sort
explanations: Modifies a following noun to point back at something just mentioned or known to the listener. The formal written counterpart of そんな, standard in business letters, official notices, and careful speech.
The direction directly contrary to the one in question. Everyday vocabulary for giving directions, describing traffic and train travel, and talking about movement in general.

glosses: anman; steamed bun with sweet red bean filling
steamed bun filled with sweet red bean paste
explanations: A soft white steamed bun with a sweet {餡|あん} (red bean paste) filling. Sold hot at convenience stores in winter alongside the savory {肉|にく}まん.

glosses: nagging; fault-finding; forever telling people off
explanations: Describes a person who comments critically on every little thing, or an atmosphere full of such complaints. Almost always negative, suggesting the criticism is more frequent than the situation deserves.

glosses: timid; faint-hearted; unable to assert oneself
explanations: Describes someone who cannot say no, backs down under pressure, or is easily rattled. The judgment is usually mildly critical or self-deprecating rather than harsh.
An unfinished version of a document, design, or piece of software, circulated for comment before the final version. Common in business and IT.
The system by which professional teams select new players, best known in Japan from the annual {野球|やきゅう} draft, ドラフト{会議|かいぎ}.

glosses: to buy more of; to top up a supply
to buy more of something one already has; to top up
explanations: To make an additional purchase because the amount on hand is not enough. Implies the item is already owned or already bought once, and the new purchase supplements it.

glosses: trotting along; toddling; walking with quick little steps
walking along with quick, light steps
explanations: A mimetic word for the way a small child, small animal, or short-legged person moves: short, rapid, steady steps that cover ground without hurrying. The impression is light and often endearing.

glosses: one's personal opinion; one's own view
explanations: One's own view, offered as distinct from an official position or established fact. Used to signal modestly that what follows is only the speaker's take.

glosses: endlessly; as far as the eye can see; thoroughly; to the very end
endlessly; on and on; as far as one can see
thoroughly; to the very end; utterly
explanations: Of space or a continuing scene: extending without any visible limit. Typically used of roads, skies, fields, and the sea.
Of attitude or degree: refusing to stop or compromise, or being something completely. Often carries admiration or exasperation, depending on context.

glosses: absolutely; by no means; without exception
absolutely not; by no means (with a negative)
absolutely; without fail; come what may (with an affirmative)
explanations: Used with a negative predicate to deny something flatly and with conviction. This is by far the more common pattern.
Used with an affirmative predicate to declare firm resolve. Formal and emphatic, common in speeches and written declarations.

glosses: by itself; automatically; of its own accord
by itself; on its own; without anyone doing anything
explanations: Describes something that happens with no one causing it. Typically used of doors, machines, and physical conditions that change without human intervention — often with a hint of surprise or unease.

glosses: naturally; of itself; in the nature of things
naturally; of its own accord; as a matter of course
explanations: Describes an outcome that follows naturally from the way things are, without anyone forcing it. Literary and somewhat elevated; common in essays, aphorisms, and formal speech.

glosses: naturally; without trying; before one knows it
naturally; of its own accord; without conscious effort
explanations: Describes something that comes about on its own, especially a feeling, habit, or ability that develops without anyone working at it. The everyday, conversational member of this group.

glosses: like; just as; in the same way as
like; as; in the manner of
explanations: Attaches to a noun to compare an action or state to it. The adverbial counterpart of のような, which modifies nouns instead of verbs and adjectives.

glosses: like; such as; the kind of
explanations: Modifies a following noun by comparing it to something else, or by giving an example of the type meant. The noun-modifying counterpart of ように.

glosses: that's right; yes, indeed; well, let me see
well, let me see; hmm (before answering)
explanations: Agreeing with what the other person has just said. The ね invites shared feeling, so it sounds warmer than a bare はい.
A filler that buys a moment before replying to a question. Said with a drawn-out そう〜ですね, it signals that the speaker is thinking, not agreeing.

glosses: like that; in that way; that's how
like that; in that way; doing it that way
explanations: Refers to a method the listener has just described or demonstrated. Often carries a mild criticism when it comments on a habit the speaker disapproves of.
Refers to a way of doing things that both speaker and listener can observe or already know about, but that neither is doing at the moment. Often used when commenting on a third party.

glosses: what kind of; what ~; (with negative) no ~ at all
no ~ at all; not the slightest (with a negative)
explanations: Placed before a noun to ask what sort of thing it is or what it is for.
In the pattern {何|なん}の…も + negative, it denies the existence of the thing completely: not a single one, none whatsoever.

glosses: stocking up; keeping a supply on hand
stocking up in advance; a stock kept on hand
explanations: Buying everyday items before they are needed so that a supply is always available, or the supply itself. Used of household staples such as rice, detergent, and toilet paper.
The clipped form of {月曜日|げつようび}, used where the day is already understood as a day of the week — schedules, timetables, calendars, and casual speech.
Cured, usually smoked pork belly, sold in thin slices or thick blocks. In Japan it is most often eaten in breakfast dishes, pasta, and stir-fries rather than as a standalone side.
A mimetic word ({擬態語|ぎたいご}) for something long that curves repeatedly from side to side or rises and falls in gentle waves — a mountain road, a river, a line of hills, a cable.
A mimetic word ({擬態語|ぎたいご}) for the smooth, twisting movement of a long thin creature such as a snake, eel, or worm — and by extension for anything long that moves the same way.
A mimetic word ({擬態語|ぎたいご}) for something so soft that it has no stiffness of its own and bends or collapses under the slightest force — melted plastic, an overcooked noodle, a sleeping child's arm.

glosses: fighting on alone; a lone struggle
fighting on alone; struggling without support
explanations: A four-character compound ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}) for carrying on a hard fight by oneself, with no reinforcements and no help from those around you. Used of work, sport, and campaigns far more often than of actual battle.
The clipped form of {水曜日|すいようび}, used in schedules, timetables, and casual speech where the word is already understood to name a day of the week.
A traditional candy drawn out into a long rod with a face worked through its whole length, so that every slice shows the same picture of the folk hero {金太郎|きんたろう}.
Used figuratively of people, products, or plans that are interchangeable because they were all turned out to one pattern. Usually critical.
The weekend of the current week — normally the Saturday and Sunday just ahead, and sometimes Friday evening as well. Used adverbially without a particle as often as it is used as a plain noun.

glosses: family-friendly boss; manager who supports staff work-life balance
explanations: A manager who actively backs subordinates' childcare and family life — approving leave, cutting overtime, adjusting workloads — while still delivering results. A coined term promoted in workplace-reform campaigns since the mid-2010s.
Property other than land and buildings — cash, vehicles, machinery, inventory, furniture. A legal and accounting term defined by contrast with {不動産|ふどうさん} (real property).

glosses: equity capital; shareholders' equity; own capital
explanations: The portion of a company's funding that does not have to be repaid — paid-in capital plus retained earnings — as opposed to {他人資本|たにんしほん}, money raised by borrowing.

In mathematics and statistics, the relation of one quantity to another, written {二|に}{対|たい}{三|さん} (2:3). Also used as a suffix meaning "compared with", as in {前年比|ぜんねんひ} (compared with the previous year).

glosses: not at all; nothing much; no problem
explanations: With an affirmative predicate, marks a feeling the speaker cannot quite put into words. Very common in なんとも{言|い}えない (indescribable) and before an adjective of impression.
With a negative predicate, denies the whole of something — that anything is wrong, that anything can be said, or that anything is felt.

glosses: the pathos of things; mono no aware
the pathos of things; sensitivity to transience
explanations: A classical aesthetic ideal: the quiet, moving sadness felt on sensing that beautiful things pass. Associated above all with Heian literature and with the reading of {源氏物語|げんじものがたり}.
A wistful longing for a past time or a place one has left. A literary-flavored loanword, used where the plain adjective {懐|なつ}かしい would sound too everyday.
A single minute of clock time or duration. Often used loosely for "a moment", as in {一分|いっぷん}{待|ま}って (hang on a second).
Treating something sacred or deeply respected with contempt. Used of religious offence and, by extension, of any act that cheapens something people hold inviolable.

glosses: department head; head of a program
head of an academic department; program chair
explanations: The faculty member in charge of a {学科|がっか} — a degree program or department within a university faculty. Handles curriculum, staffing, and admissions for that program.

A performer who wins through refined technique and control rather than raw power or force. Standard in baseball commentary for a pitcher who relies on placement and breaking balls, and used of musicians and writers in the same spirit.
In baseball, a pitcher who relies mainly on raw velocity rather than breaking balls or placement. Also used figuratively of a person who takes a direct, forceful approach.

glosses: the real thing; orthodox type; authentic practitioner
the genuine article; orthodox school; authentic type
explanations: A person or thing that follows the proper, full-fledged form of its field rather than a simplified or gimmicky version. Common in describing musicians, actors, chefs, and (in baseball) pitchers with complete technique.

glosses: genuinely talented performer; person of real ability
person of genuine ability; talent-driven performer
explanations: Someone whose reputation rests on real skill rather than looks, popularity, or promotion. Used especially of singers, actors, and other performers.

In accounting, the portion of a company's funds raised from outside parties and eventually repayable — loans, bonds, and accounts payable. Contrasts with {自己資本|じこしほん}, capital belonging to the company itself.

glosses: net assets; net worth; shareholders' equity
explanations: Total assets minus total liabilities. Used both for companies (the equity section of the balance sheet) and for individuals or funds (net worth).

glosses: soft and limp; floppy; without firmness
explanations: Describes something that has lost its stiffness and gives way when touched — soggy food, overcooked noodles, a deflated cushion. Also used of a body that has gone weak, and of a person with no backbone.

glosses: to jump onto; to hop on; to leap aboard
to jump onto; to hop aboard (a train, bus, horse)
explanations: To get onto something in one quick leap, typically a vehicle that is about to leave or already moving. The nuance is haste, not athletic skill.
Describes a situation or a person's movements as rushed and without pause. Unlike {忙|いそが}しい, which simply reports having a lot to do, {忙|せわ}しい conveys the unsettled, hurried feel of it.
Describes behavior that violates standards of decorum — eating noisily, sprawling in public, speaking coarsely. The judgment is about manners and dignity, not morality.

glosses: how many minutes; what minute (past the hour)
what minute (clock reading past the hour)
explanations: Asks the length of a span of time in minutes. Usually appears with かかる, かかりますか, or 〜くらい.
Asks the minute portion of a clock time, normally in the pattern {何時|なんじ}{何分|なんぷん}.
The hour four on the clock. Note the irregular reading よ, not し or よん, before the counter {時|じ}.

glosses: one's last moments; dying hour; end of life
one's last moments; death; dying hour
explanations: The moment of a person's death, and the circumstances surrounding it. Used only of living beings and, by extension, of organizations or eras being spoken of as if they died.
Rated as clearly above standard. Applied to goods, companies, properties, borrowers, and school records — typically in official or commercial assessments rather than casual praise.
A grammatical form expressing that an action is complete and its result holds — English "have done," or in Japanese the 〜た and 〜ている forms depending on analysis.
A door or opening designated for escaping a building during a fire, earthquake, or other emergency. Standard wording on safety signage and in fire-code documents.

glosses: national emblem; national coat of arms
explanations: The official symbol representing a country, used on passports, government documents, and official buildings. Distinct from the national flag.

glosses: promoter; person driving a project forward; advocate
explanations: The person who pushes a policy, reform, or project ahead and takes responsibility for its progress. Used in business and government contexts rather than casual speech.

glosses: recipient; receiving party; place of receipt
explanations: The person, company, or location that receives goods, money, or a delivery. A form-filling and business term rather than conversational vocabulary.

glosses: denial of permission; refusal of an application
explanations: An official decision not to grant permission for something applied for — a visa, a building permit, a licence. The formal counterpart of {許可|きょか}.
Someone who secretly passes information to the opposing side while remaining part of their own group. Strongly negative — the word implies betrayal, not whistleblowing.

A person, style, or thing that follows the established tradition of its field rather than an experimental or unconventional line. Often used attributively with の to praise something as properly traditional.

glosses: actor known for acting skill; character actor
explanations: An actor whose reputation rests on the quality of the performance rather than on looks or star appeal. Standard praise in Japanese entertainment coverage.

glosses: distinctive type; performer with a strong personality
person or thing with a distinctive character
explanations: Someone (often an actor or musician) whose appeal comes from an unusual, unmistakable presence rather than from conventional good looks or mainstream style. Also applied to shops, cars, and designs.
The sum of everything a company, fund, or individual owns, before liabilities are subtracted. It is the left-hand total of a balance sheet.

glosses: proposer; advocate; originator of an idea
explanations: The person who first put forward a theory, method, or movement and argues for it publicly. Used mainly of academic, technical, and social ideas rather than of everyday suggestions.

glosses: which time (in a series); what number time
explanations: Asks for the ordinal position of an occasion — whether something is the second, third, fifth time, and so on. English has no single word for it, so it is usually translated with a full question.

glosses: here and there; all over the place
here and there; all over; in every direction
explanations: Refers to many scattered places at once, or to moving between them. Casual in tone; it works both as an adverb of place and as a noun taking particles.

glosses: oneself (emphatic, following a noun or pronoun)
explanations: Attaches directly to a person word or pronoun to stress that this very person, and no one else, is meant: {私|わたし}{自身|じしん} (I myself), {社長|しゃちょう}{自身|じしん} (the president himself). It does not stand alone as a subject.
Asks which of the seven weekdays something falls on. It asks only for the weekday name, not the calendar date, which is {何日|なんにち}.
The counter reading for two of something flat: sheets of paper, tickets, plates, photos, or garments.

glosses: mekabu; the frilly root part of wakame seaweed
explanations: The thick, ruffled part at the base of a wakame frond, sold chopped and eaten for its slippery texture. Usually written in hiragana or katakana.
A flowering plant that grows rooted in the sea floor, such as eelgrass. Botanically distinct from {海藻|かいそう} (algae), though the two words sound identical and are often confused.
A count of seven people, using the Sino-Japanese number with the counter {人|にん}. Also read ななにん, which is now more common in speech.

glosses: the second one; the second (in a sequence)
explanations: The second item in a series of countable things, or the second point in a list of reasons or steps. Built from the native counter {二|ふた}つ plus the ordinal suffix 〜{目|め}.

glosses: the 11th of the month; eleven days
the eleventh day of the month
explanations: The calendar date. From the eleventh onward the dates are read regularly with にち, unlike the irregular readings for the first ten days.
A span of eleven days. Which sense is meant is clear from context, and 〜{間|かん} can be added to force the duration reading.
A hollow ceramic pig with an opening in its side, used to hold a burning mosquito coil. A familiar emblem of Japanese summer, often seen on verandas and in seasonal advertising.

glosses: precariousness; the quality of being on the edge of failure
explanations: The nominalized form of {危|あや}うい. It names a fragile, unstable quality that could tip into disaster at any moment — often used admiringly of art, performance, or beauty as well as critically of situations.
A high level of danger or of possible loss. From English "high risk," and used mainly in finance, insurance, and medicine, usually attributively with の or before another noun.

glosses: to shatter; to smash; to dash (hopes)
to shatter; to smash to pieces
to dash; to crush (hopes, dreams, illusions)
explanations: To break something hard into fragments with force. The prefix {打|う}ち〜 adds vigor to {砕|くだ}く, so the breaking is decisive and complete.
To destroy something abstract that someone was holding on to, such as a dream, an expectation, or a belief. This figurative use is the more common one in writing.

glosses: another world; a place utterly unlike this one
explanations: A place or social sphere so different from one's own that it feels like a separate world. Usually figurative — a quiet mountain village, a luxury hotel, or the life of the very rich — rather than a literal other planet.

A musical work in free form, not bound by the standard structures of sonata or dance movements. The Japanese name for the genre Western music calls a fantasia or fantasy; the loanword ファンタジー is used for the literary genre instead.
Literature built on the supernatural, the dreamlike, or worlds that could not exist. Covers both the Western fantasy genre and the older tradition of the fantastic in literary criticism.

glosses: another world; paradise; a place apart
another world; a place apart; paradise
explanations: A place so different from ordinary surroundings that it feels like a separate world. Almost always positive: quiet, beautiful, or refreshingly free of everyday pressures.
Carrying little danger of loss or harm. Used as a noun and, with の, as a modifier — most often in finance, insurance, and health contexts.

glosses: the second; second in order; second one
explanations: The item that comes second in a sequence or ranking. Used with の before a noun, and often with に to say where something ranks.

glosses: seagrass bed; seaweed bed; underwater meadow
explanations: A shallow coastal area densely covered with seagrass or seaweed. Valued as a spawning and nursery ground for fish, and treated in environmental policy as a habitat to be protected and restored.
Placed directly after a noun to isolate the thing itself from its circumstances, results, or associated details. Often used to concede that the thing itself is fine while something around it is not.

glosses: from the standpoint of; in terms of; on
from the standpoint of; in terms of; as far as ... is concerned
explanations: Attached to a Sino-Japanese noun to name the perspective from which a statement holds: {法律上|ほうりつじょう} (legally speaking), {仕事上|しごとじょう} (in the course of work). Common in formal writing and business speech.
Attached to a Sino-Japanese noun to name a stretch of land, a climatic region, or a range on a scale: {温帯|おんたい} (temperate zone), {火山帯|かざんたい} (volcanic belt), {時間帯|じかんたい} (time slot).

glosses: to be able to wait (usu. negative: can't wait)
to be able to wait; (in the negative) to not be able to wait
explanations: To be capable of waiting until something finally arrives. Used almost exclusively in the negative {待|ま}ちきれない, which expresses impatient excitement — "I can't wait."
A set of symptoms that regularly occur together and are treated as one named condition. Also used loosely of recurring social or behavioral patterns, as English does with "syndrome."
The degree to which a tool, device, or service is easy to use. A standard criterion in product reviews and design discussions, alongside price and performance.

headword: グラフィックデザイン
explanations: The design of visual material such as posters, logos, packaging, and web pages, combining type, image, and layout. Used both for the field of work and for individual pieces of design work.

A structured contest in which two sides argue for and against a set proposition under fixed rules, and judges decide the winner. Associated with classrooms and competitions rather than everyday argument.
The question word for a length of time in hours: {何時間|なんじかん}かかりますか (how many hours does it take?). Note that it asks about duration, not clock time — that is {何時|なんじ}.
With も, the same word states that something went on for many hours: {何時間|なんじかん}も{待|ま}った (I waited for hours). The number is not asked but presented as large.
Seven of something counted with {個|こ}, the broadest of the object counters. Typically used for compact, self-contained things such as fruit, eggs, or boxes.
A particular land or locality, especially one with significance for the speaker: {日本|にほん}の{地|ち}, {異国|いこく}の{地|ち}. Somewhat literary; everyday speech prefers {場所|ばしょ} or {土地|とち}.
The ground underfoot, as opposed to the sky. Appears mainly in set phrases and elevated writing, such as {地|ち}に{足|あし}がつく (to have one's feet on the ground).
Attached to a verb stem to express the speaker's own desire to perform the action: {食|た}べる → {食|た}べたい (want to eat). The result inflects like an i-adjective ({食|た}べたくない, {食|た}べたかった).

glosses: be ...ing; be in the state of having ...ed
be in the state resulting from ...
explanations: With verbs that describe an activity lasting over time ({読|よ}む, {走|はし}る, {待|ま}つ), 〜ている says the action is going on now: {本|ほん}を{読|よ}んでいる (I am reading a book).

With verbs describing an instantaneous change ({死|し}ぬ, {結婚|けっこん}する, {開|あ}く), 〜ている says the change has happened and the resulting state continues: {窓|まど}が{開|あ}いている (the window is open), not "is opening."
With a time expression or a plural object, 〜ている describes a repeated or habitual action: {毎朝|まいあさ}{走|はし}っている (I run every morning).

glosses: has been done (and left that way)
has been done and left in that state
explanations: Te-form of a transitive verb plus ある. Describes a state that continues because someone deliberately produced it. The doer is not named, but their intention is felt: {窓|まど}が{開|あ}けてある means someone opened the window on purpose and left it open.

glosses: do in advance; leave (something) as it is
do (something) in advance; do in preparation
explanations: Te-form of a verb plus {置|お}く. Says that an action is done ahead of time so that things will be ready later: {切符|きっぷ}を{買|か}っておく (buy the tickets in advance).
The same form also means to let a state continue rather than change it: {窓|まど}を{開|あ}けておく (leave the window open), そのままにしておく (leave it as it is).

glosses: show signs of wanting to (of someone else)
to appear to want to; to be eager to
explanations: Verb stem plus たがる. Reports a desire that is visible from the outside, so it is used about a third person rather than about oneself: {弟|おとうと}は{行|い}きたがっている (my brother wants to go).
Said of a tool, device, service, or interface that works smoothly and takes little effort or learning. Formed from {使|つか}う plus the suffix 〜やすい (easy to ...).
Dirt made of cooking oil or machine oil that clings to a surface. Most often used of kitchen grime on stoves, range hoods, and dishes, and of oil marks on clothing.
Long, thin round pasta, and by extension a dish made with it. From Italian spaghetti; also written スパゲティ, and older sources use スパゲッティー.

glosses: penne; short tube pasta cut at an angle
explanations: Short cylindrical pasta with the ends cut diagonally, so that sauce catches inside the tube. From Italian penne (quills).
Short, usually curved tube pasta. In Japan it is associated above all with マカロニサラダ and with gratin rather than with Italian-style sauced dishes.

glosses: to get done in time; to make do with
to get (something) ready in time; to make it in time
to make do with; to get by using (something) temporarily
explanations: To arrange things so that a deadline or departure time is met. The transitive counterpart of {間|ま}に{合|あ}う: the subject actively makes the timing work.
To use whatever is at hand as a stopgap because the proper thing is unavailable. Usually marked with で: ありもので{間|ま}に{合|あ}わせる (make do with what we have).

glosses: one song; one piece of music
explanations: {一|いち} plus the counter {曲|きょく} (pieces of music). Used for a single song or instrumental piece in a performance, on a program, or on a recording.
Describes a person who is eager to know about and try new things. Compound of {好奇心|こうきしん} (curiosity) and {旺盛|おうせい} (vigorous, abundant), and almost always a compliment.

glosses: rising star; great hope; promising newcomer
rising star; the one everyone is counting on
explanations: A young or new person whom a team, company, or field expects great things from. Literally "star of expectation," and used most often in sports and entertainment reporting.
Driving faster than the posted {制限速度|せいげんそくど}. A traffic offense punished with demerit points and a fine, and with criminal penalties for large excesses.
Points awarded for match results in a league table — typically three for a win and one for a draw in soccer. The team with the most {勝|か}ち{点|てん}, not the most wins, tops the table.
The evening or night of the day before yesterday. A formal, largely written word; in speech people usually say おとといの{晩|ばん} or おとといの{夜|よる}.

glosses: desertion in the face of the enemy; running away at the crucial moment
desertion in the face of the enemy
backing out just when one is needed most
explanations: Fleeing from a position when the enemy is at hand — historically one of the gravest military offenses.
Used figuratively, and half-jokingly, of someone who abandons a task, a match, or a group right at the decisive moment.

glosses: kanji not included in the {常用漢字|じょうようかんじ} list
explanations: Any character outside the 2,136 {常用漢字|じょうようかんじ} designated for general use. Newspapers and textbooks avoid them or add furigana, though many appear in names, place names, and literary writing.

Operating a vehicle in a state of exhaustion, illness, or medication that makes safe driving impossible. Prohibited by the Road Traffic Act, and the offense employers are charged with when they force such schedules on drivers.
The seven vertebrae of the neck, at the top of the spinal column. Familiar to most people from injuries such as whiplash and from disc problems.
Joint work between companies and universities on research, technology development, and training. {産|さん} is industry and {学|がく} is academia.

glosses: hard to use; awkward to handle; user-unfriendly
hard to use; awkward to handle; inconvenient
explanations: Describes a tool, device, software, or space that works but is troublesome or unintuitive in practice. Formed from {使|つか}う plus the suffix 〜にくい (difficult to do).

glosses: lumbar vertebrae; the lower back bones
explanations: The five vertebrae of the lower back, between the chest vertebrae and the pelvis. Familiar to most people from back pain, disc problems, and compression fractures.
The whitish, chalky film left behind when tap water evaporates, made up of minerals in the water. Builds up on sinks, bathroom mirrors, kettles, and faucets.
A Japanese pasta dish of spaghetti stir-fried with ketchup, onion, green pepper, and sausage or ham. Despite the name, it was invented in Yokohama after the war and is not Italian.
A small round French confection made of two almond-meringue shells sandwiching a cream or jam filling. Sold in bright pastel colors and treated in Japan as a stylish gift sweet.

Pizza, transcribed closer to the Italian pronunciation than the usual ピザ. Chosen by authentic Italian restaurants and wood-fired-oven shops to signal that the pizza is Neapolitan rather than American-style.
The classic Neapolitan pizza topped with tomato sauce, mozzarella, and fresh basil. Treated in Japan as the benchmark by which a pizzeria is judged.

Fish and shellfish considered as food, especially in Western-style dishes. Used mainly on menus and product names; for Japanese cuisine and fish shops the native words {魚介|ぎょかい} and {魚|さかな} are usual.
Tea, from English. Used almost entirely inside compounds on café and convenience-store menus; on its own, tea is {紅茶|こうちゃ} (black tea) or お{茶|ちゃ} (Japanese tea).
Italian-style frozen dessert, denser and less fatty than ordinary ice cream. In Japan it is strongly associated with tourist areas and with shops selling flavors made from local produce.
A team game in which players throw a ball to hit opponents, who are out when struck. A fixture of Japanese elementary-school PE classes and recess.
A person who rides a snowboard. Often used in contrast with スキーヤー when talking about how a ski resort's slopes are shared.
The chairlift that carries skiers and snowboarders up a slope. This is the default meaning at a ski resort.
A machine that raises loads or people, such as a cargo hoist, a car lift in a garage, or a wheelchair lift on a bus.

glosses: waitlist; waiting for a cancellation; standby
waitlist; standby; waiting for a cancellation
explanations: Putting your name down for a fully booked flight, restaurant, class, or hotel in the hope that someone else cancels. Also refers to the waiting list itself.
Short for セルフサービス. Marks a service the customer performs themselves — pumping gas, pouring water, carrying a tray, scanning purchases. Used almost entirely in compounds and on signs.

glosses: visually impaired person; blind or partially sighted person
visually impaired person; person with a visual disability
explanations: A person who is blind or has low vision. The standard neutral term in public signage, laws, and news reporting, covering both total blindness and partial sight.
A killing treated as a criminal incident — the standard term in news reports, police statements, and crime fiction. Refers to the case or incident, not to the act in the abstract.
Negotiating with the other party in person, without going through an agent, intermediary, or higher authority. Common in labor disputes, business deals, diplomacy, and real-estate dealings.

glosses: meat sauce; Bolognese-style tomato and ground meat sauce
explanations: A tomato-based sauce made with ground meat and onions, served mainly over spaghetti. In Japan it is one of the standard pasta sauces, sold ready-made in cans and retort pouches.
The whitish mineral deposit left by hot water inside kettles, pots, bathtubs, and water heaters. Also used for the film that builds up on the inside of a bath.
A room that no one is using or renting. Used of hotel rooms available for booking, unrented apartments, and unused rooms in a house.

glosses: month (suffix forming the names of calendar months)
explanations: Attached to the numbers one through twelve to name the months of the year: {一月|いちがつ} (January), {二月|にがつ} (February), and so on. It names a month of the calendar, not a length of time.

glosses: counter for chairs and legged furniture
counter for chairs, desks, and other legged furniture
explanations: Used to count furniture that stands on legs, above all chairs, and also desks, benches, and stepladders. In everyday speech many people use {個|こ} or {台|だい} instead, but {脚|きゃく} is the correct counter in shops, catalogs, and inventories.

glosses: to be thorough; to be attentive; to reach everywhere
to be thorough; to be attentive; to be well looked after
explanations: Said of care, attention, or management that extends to every corner of something. Most often used in the ている form to describe a place, service, or piece of work as impeccably tended.

glosses: sadness; sorrow; how sad something is
explanations: The noun form of {悲|かな}しい. It names sadness as a quality or a degree — how sad a thing or an experience is — rather than the emotion in the abstract.

glosses: happiness; gladness; how glad one feels
explanations: The noun form of {嬉|うれ}しい. It names the gladness felt at a particular good thing, and often its intensity, rather than happiness as a state of life.

glosses: febrile; caused by or accompanied by fever
explanations: A medical term used before another noun to mean that a condition arises from or comes with a fever. It appears almost only in compounds, most commonly {熱性|ねっせい}けいれん (febrile convulsion).

glosses: increased revenue; higher income; increased yield
increased revenue; increase in income or takings
explanations: A rise in the money coming in — a company's sales, a government's tax receipts, or a household's income. Standard vocabulary in business reporting.
A rise in the amount produced, especially of a crop. Used in farming and industry contexts.

glosses: thousand folded paper cranes (strung together as a wish or prayer)
explanations: A thousand origami cranes folded and strung on threads, given as a wish for recovery from illness, for victory, or for peace. Often made collectively by a class, a team, or a group of friends.
The meat of sheep, as a category of food. A slightly technical or written word: menus and shops usually use ラム or マトン instead.

glosses: trouble; bother; the effort something takes
explanations: The work and inconvenience involved in doing something, especially work imposed on someone else. Most often met in the polite apology お{手数|てすう}をおかけします.

glosses: top floor; highest floor of a building
explanations: The highest floor of a building. Common in property listings, hotel descriptions, and directions inside department stores.
A bad injury, typically one needing hospital treatment. Used of accidents, falls, and sports injuries; also written {大怪我|おおけが}.
The meat of horses, eaten in Japan mainly raw as {馬刺|ばさ}し. Kumamoto and Nagano are the best-known producing areas.

glosses: -year student; student in the nth year
student in the nth year (of a school)
explanations: Attached to a number to say what year of school someone is in: {一年生|いちねんせい} (first-year student), {三年生|さんねんせい} (third-year student). The school itself is understood from context or named separately.
The portion of a passage marked with an underline. Standard wording in exam questions and textbook exercises, which routinely ask about {下線部|かせんぶ}.

glosses: to be raised; to come up; to be cited
to be brought up; to be cited; to be named
to be produced; to be obtained (of results or evidence)
explanations: Said of names, examples, opinions, or candidates that come up in a discussion. This kanji is the one used when something is put forward for consideration rather than physically rising.
Said of results, profits, or evidence that come to hand as the product of effort or investigation.
A rise in profit compared with the previous period. Standard vocabulary in earnings reports and business news, where it is contrasted with {増収|ぞうしゅう} (higher revenue).

glosses: decreased revenue; drop in income; reduced yield
explanations: A fall in the money coming in — a company's sales, a government's tax receipts, or a household's income. Common in business reporting.
A fall in the amount produced, especially of a crop. Used in farming contexts, often after bad weather.

glosses: raw sliced horse meat; horse sashimi
explanations: Thinly sliced raw horse meat, eaten with soy sauce, grated ginger, and garlic. A regional specialty of Kumamoto and parts of Nagano, and a common izakaya dish elsewhere.

glosses: the marked passage; the underlined part
the marked passage; the underlined part (of a text)
explanations: The stretch of text singled out by a line drawn beside or under it. Standard wording in Japanese exam questions, which refer to a passage as {傍線部|ぼうせんぶ}A or {傍線部|ぼうせんぶ}(1) and then ask about it.

glosses: fun; enjoyment; how enjoyable something is
fun; enjoyment; the pleasure of doing something
explanations: The quality of being enjoyable, treated as a thing that can be known, conveyed, or tasted. Formed from {楽|たの}しい plus the noun-making suffix さ, so it names the degree of enjoyment rather than a particular occasion of it.

glosses: grilled mutton dish of Hokkaido; Genghis Khan barbecue
explanations: Slices of mutton or lamb grilled with vegetables on a dome-shaped iron skillet and dipped in a soy-based sauce. The best-known local dish of Hokkaido, eaten at restaurants, at beer gardens, and outdoors.
A photograph one takes of oneself, usually with a smartphone. Borrowed from English and used mainly in fashion, beauty, and social-media writing; in everyday Japanese {自撮|じど}り is far more common.
Half of a circle, or a shape resembling one. Used both as a geometric term and in everyday description of curved shapes and arrangements.
A staircase that turns around a central axis as it rises. Found in towers, lighthouses, and narrow buildings where a straight flight would not fit.
The opening in a lock into which a key is inserted. Also used of the small hole one can peer through in an old-fashioned door lock.

The holding facility inside a police station where a suspect is kept after arrest while the investigation proceeds. Distinct from a detention house for defendants awaiting trial and from a prison for convicted offenders.
A proposal that someone put money into a venture, fund, or scheme. Usually said of an offer brought to you by another person, and very often in warnings about fraud.

glosses: to hold out; to withstand; to endure
explanations: To keep standing under pressure, attack, or hardship without giving way. Somewhat literary on its own; most learners meet it inside the compound verb {持|も}ち{堪|こた}える.
The way a school refers to itself in formal writing and announcements. Used by the institution about itself, never by an outsider talking about someone else's school.
{三|さん} plus the counter {回|かい}, used for repeated actions and occurrences. No sound change occurs: さん + かい stays さんかい.
The number 400. {四|よん} + {百|ひゃく}, with no sound change.
The number 600. {六|ろく} + {百|ひゃく} with a double sound change: ろく becomes ろっ and ひゃく becomes ぴゃく.
The number 700. {七|なな} + {百|ひゃく}, with no sound change.
The number 800. {八|はち} + {百|ひゃく} with a double sound change: はち becomes はっ and ひゃく becomes ぴゃく.
The number 900. {九|きゅう} + {百|ひゃく}, with no sound change.
Horse meat eaten as food. The name comes from the pink, cherry-blossom-like color of the raw flesh, and it is used in place of the plainer {馬肉|ばにく} on menus and in polite conversation.
A facility that holds people awaiting or undergoing trial, and those sentenced to death. Distinct from a prison, which holds people already serving sentences.
The school that is speaking or writing — used by a school about itself in official documents, websites, and announcements.
The principal campus of a school that also operates one or more branch campuses ({分校|ぶんこう}).

A small satellite campus operated by a main school ({本校|ほんこう}), typically set up in a remote area so that local children do not have to travel far. Many are tiny, with a handful of pupils and combined-grade classes.
A proposal or tip presented as an easy way to make money. Usually carries a note of suspicion — the word most often appears in warnings about scams.

glosses: emphasis line drawn beside text; (in horizontal writing) underline
explanations: A line drawn next to a passage to mark it out. In vertical Japanese writing it runs down the right side of the characters; in horizontal writing it appears as an underline.
An extendable rod that holds a smartphone or camera at arm's length so the user can photograph themselves with more of the surroundings in frame.
The person in charge of a single shop or restaurant — responsible for staff, stock, and daily operations. Used both as a job title and as a term of address.
The machine that records sales and holds the cash at a shop counter. In everyday speech it is almost always shortened to レジ.

headword: ウィンドウショッピング
explanations: Looking at goods in shops for pleasure without intending to buy. Takes する to form a verb.

headword: オンラインショッピング
explanations: Buying goods over the internet. Takes する to form a verb.

glosses: portrait rights; right to one's own image
explanations: The right not to have one's face or figure photographed, published, or used commercially without consent. In Japan it is recognized by case law rather than by a single statute.

headword: プライバシーポリシー
explanations: A published statement setting out how an organization collects, uses, and protects personal information. Standard on Japanese company websites and apps.
The number 30,000, formed as {三|さん} (three) × {万|まん} (10,000). No sound change occurs — both parts keep their usual readings.
The number 50,000, formed as {五|ご} (five) × {万|まん} (10,000).
The number 100,000, formed as {十|じゅう} (ten) × {万|まん} (10,000). English switches unit here — "hundred thousand" — while Japanese simply counts ten {万|まん}.
The number 5,000, formed as {五|ご} (five) × {千|せん} (1,000). No sound change occurs.
The number 8,000. {八|はち} shortens to {はっ} before {千|せん}, so the reading is はっせん, never はちせん.
The number 1,000 with {一|いち} stated. Where plain {千|せん} suffices in ordinary counting, {一千|いっせん} is used in formal writing and, above all, inside larger figures such as {一千万|いっせんまん} (10,000,000).
Thirty persons, formed with the counter {人|にん}. From {四人|よにん} upward the counter is regularly {にん}, so no sound change occurs here.
The number 4,000, formed as {四|よん} (four) × {千|せん} (1,000). No sound change occurs, and {よん} is used rather than {し}.
The number 6,000, formed as {六|ろく} (six) × {千|せん} (1,000). No sound change occurs, unlike {六百|ろっぴゃく} (600).
The number 7,000, formed as {七|なな} (seven) × {千|せん} (1,000). No sound change occurs, and {なな} is used rather than {しち}.
The number 9,000, formed as {九|きゅう} (nine) × {千|せん} (1,000). No sound change occurs, and {きゅう} is used rather than {く}.
A duration of three hours. Formed with {時間|じかん} (hour, duration) used as a counter after {三|さん}.

glosses: school closure; closing of a school
school closure; closing down a school
explanations: The permanent closing of a school, usually because enrolment has fallen too low to keep it running. Also used with する as a verb.

glosses: browsing without intending to buy; window-shopping
explanations: Looking over goods in a shop or stall with no intention of buying. Often used by shopkeepers of customers who take up their time.
Making fun of someone in a light or mocking way, especially calling out remarks from the sidelines.

glosses: wild boar meat; boar served as food
explanations: Meat from wild boar, especially as served in restaurants. {牡丹|ぼたん} (peony) refers to the flower-like way the slices are arranged on the plate.

glosses: assistant store manager; deputy shop manager
explanations: The second-in-command at a shop or restaurant, who supports the {店長|てんちょう} and takes charge in their absence.

glosses: to lose (someone to death); to be bereaved of
to lose (a family member or close person) to death
explanations: To have someone close die. The subject is the bereaved person, and the object marked by を is the person who died.

glosses: to go along together; to be partners in life
to go along together; to accompany each other
explanations: For two or more people to travel through something together — literally along a road, or figuratively through life as a married couple. Now a dated, literary word; the derived noun {連|つ}れ{合|あ}い (spouse) is far more common.

glosses: together with; along with (a person or thing)
as; at the same time as (something changes)
explanations: Attaches to a noun to mean 'in the company of' or 'in addition to.' Somewhat formal; と{一緒|いっしょ}に is the everyday equivalent.
Marks two changes that proceed in step: as the first thing progresses, the second happens too. Common with nouns like {時代|じだい}, {年齢|ねんれい}, and {成長|せいちょう}.
Cancer arising in the stomach. Historically one of the most common cancers in Japan, which is why gastric screening is a standard part of adult health check-ups.

glosses: the last one; the final part; the ending
explanations: From English 'last.' Used for the closing part of a film, song, game, or series, and attributively for the final item in a sequence.

glosses: to inflate; to puff out; to build up (hopes)
to inflate; to swell; to puff out
to build up (hopes, dreams, imagination); to expand (a plan)
explanations: To make something expand by filling it with air or otherwise enlarging it. Used of balloons, cheeks, dough, and sails.
To let expectations, imagination, or an idea grow larger. Very common with {夢|ゆめ}, {期待|きたい}, and {想像|そうぞう}.

glosses: intention; will; feeling one wishes to convey
meaning; sense (of a word or text)
explanations: A formal noun for what a person means or intends. Appears mainly in set phrases of the written language, such as {遺憾|いかん}の{意|い} (a sense of regret) and {感謝|かんしゃ}の{意|い} (an expression of gratitude).
The meaning behind words, used in formal or literary phrasing such as ~の{意|い}で ('in the sense of ~').

glosses: the ~ crowd; the ~ contingent; group of people
the ~ crowd; the ~ group; the ~ contingent
explanations: Attaches to a noun to name the set of people who share an attribute, position, or attitude — for example {若手|わかて}{勢|ぜい} (the younger contingent) or ガチ{勢|ぜい} (the serious players).

glosses: bracken; bracken fern (eaten as a wild vegetable)
explanations: A fern whose young curled shoots are gathered in spring and eaten as a {山菜|さんさい} (wild mountain vegetable). It must be treated to remove its harshness before eating.
The powdery outer layer removed when brown rice is milled into white rice. Used in Japanese kitchens for pickling, for removing bitterness from wild vegetables, and for cleaning.

glosses: 110; the police emergency number in Japan
110; Japan's police emergency number; a call to the police
explanations: The three-digit number dialled to reach the police in an emergency. Also used with する to mean 'to call the police.' Normally written 110{番|ばん} in figures.

glosses: to be married to; to live together as husband and wife
to be married to; to share one's life with as a spouse
explanations: To live together as a married couple over a long period. The partner is marked with と. Slightly literary in tone and most often used of long marriages, as in {長年|ながねん}{連|つ}れ{添|そ}った{妻|つま} (the wife he had been married to for many years).

glosses: royal fern; fiddlehead of the royal fern (edible wild plant)
royal fern; its coiled young shoots eaten as a wild vegetable
explanations: A fern whose tightly curled spring shoots are gathered as {山菜|さんさい} (wild mountain vegetables). The shoots must be boiled and soaked before eating, and are often sold dried.

glosses: butterbur bud; butterbur flower stalk (early-spring wild vegetable)
butterbur bud; the young flower stalk of the butterbur
explanations: The pale green bud that pushes up from the ground before the butterbur's leaves appear. Prized as one of the first wild vegetables of the year and known for its strong bitterness.

glosses: final push; last spurt; sprint to the finish
final push; last spurt; burst of effort at the end
explanations: The concentrated effort made in the closing stage of a race, a project, or a period of study. Used both literally in sport and figuratively for any final stretch, usually with かける or に{入|はい}る.

glosses: wild boar hot pot; boar meat simmered in a pot
explanations: A winter {鍋|なべ} dish of thinly sliced wild boar meat simmered with vegetables in a miso or soy-based broth. A regional speciality of mountain areas, especially {丹波|たんば} in Hyogo Prefecture.

glosses: to ripen; to become ripe (of fruit or grain)
explanations: For fruit, grain, or seeds to reach full maturity, becoming sweet, soft, and ready to eat. Intransitive: the fruit is the subject, and there is no object.

glosses: idealistic argument; an argument that ignores practical constraints
explanations: A position that is admirable in principle but takes no account of what is actually possible. Almost always used critically, to dismiss a proposal as unworkable.

glosses: calyx; stem end (of a tomato, persimmon, or eggplant)
calyx; the green cap and stem end of a fruit
explanations: The small leafy cap where the stem joins a fruit such as a tomato, persimmon, eggplant, or strawberry. In cooking it is the part you cut or pull off before eating.

glosses: station name; the name of a railway station
explanations: The official name of a train or subway station, as shown on platform signs, route maps, and in announcements.

glosses: half the number; half of the total
half the number; half of a group or total
explanations: Half of a countable set of people or things. Used in statistics, voting, and survey reports, where the related thresholds {過半数|かはんすう} (a majority) and {半数以上|はんすういじょう} (half or more) matter.

glosses: division into two; splitting in half
division into two; splitting into two parts
one half (in the fraction {二分|にぶん}の{一|いち})
explanations: Dividing something into two parts, or two sides splitting something evenly between them. Often used of opinion, votes, or territory: {世論|よろん}を{二分|にぶん}する (to split public opinion in two).
In arithmetic, {二分|にぶん}の{一|いち} is the fraction one half. The pattern is 'denominator + {分|ぶん}の + numerator', so {三分|さんぶん}の{二|に} is two thirds.

glosses: history of science; the academic study of how science developed
explanations: The field that studies how scientific knowledge, methods, and institutions developed over time. Also used loosely for the historical record itself, as in a turning point in the history of science.
Describes an outcome that is no longer in real doubt, even if it has not been formally confirmed. Common in news writing about election results, promotions, and negotiations.

glosses: come-from-behind victory; a win after trailing
explanations: A victory achieved after being behind, in sport or in any contest. Standard sports-news vocabulary, usually with {飾|かざ}る (to cap off) or {収|おさ}める (to secure).

glosses: dramatic; like something out of a story
explanations: Describes an event, scene, or turn of events so striking that it feels staged. Used approvingly of exciting sports finishes and emotional moments, not of serious problems, where {深刻|しんこく} is used instead.

glosses: gross pay; total amount paid before deductions
gross pay; total payment before deductions
explanations: The full amount of a salary or bonus before tax and insurance are taken out. It appears at the top of a Japanese pay slip, with {手取|てど}り (take-home pay) shown at the bottom.

glosses: to try doing; to do and see how it goes
to try doing (something); to do it and see what happens
explanations: Te-form of a verb plus {見|み}る, written in kana. It says the action is done as an attempt, to find out the result: {食|た}べてみる (try eating it and see how it tastes). The trying is tentative, not effortful.

glosses: Narita (city in Chiba Prefecture); Narita Airport
Narita; the city in Chiba Prefecture, and by extension its airport
explanations: A city east of Tokyo, best known as the site of Narita International Airport. In everyday speech {成田|なりた} on its own usually means the airport rather than the city.

glosses: to stay married for life; to spend one's whole life together
explanations: To remain with a spouse or partner until one of them dies, without separating. Used of a couple, and often carries a note of admiration for the constancy involved.

The practice of letting fruit finish ripening after it has been picked, by leaving it at room temperature for a few days. Used of kiwis, avocados, melons, bananas and similar fruit that are shipped unripe.

glosses: armchair theory; impractical plan; pipe dream
explanations: An argument or plan that sounds coherent on paper but cannot work in practice because it ignores real conditions. Almost always used dismissively, of someone else's proposal.
A wild plant with large round leaves whose long stalks are eaten as a spring vegetable. The stalks are boiled and peeled before cooking to remove their bitterness.

An argument or outlook holding that a situation will turn out badly. Used of a stated position in debate — on the economy, the environment, a company's prospects — rather than of a person's temperament.

An argument or outlook holding that a situation will turn out well. Like {悲観論|ひかんろん}, it names a stated position in a debate rather than a personality trait, and is often used with a hint that the position may be too easy.

glosses: final push; last spurt; home stretch
explanations: The concentrated effort made in the closing stage of a task, a race, or a period of study, when the deadline or finish line is close.

The ring of small green leaf-like parts at the base of a flower, which encloses the bud before it opens and supports the petals afterwards. On a strawberry or persimmon it is the green cap at the top.

The small computer built into an appliance or a piece of equipment to control it. In consumer advertising it is a selling point meaning the device adjusts itself automatically rather than running a fixed timer.
A rice cooker mode that shortens the cycle by skipping most of the soaking time. The rice is ready in roughly half the usual time, at some cost to texture.
A box, especially a purpose-made one that is part of a system or a product name — a storage box, a tool box, a mailbox. Everyday cardboard or gift boxes are usually {箱|はこ} instead.
A small enclosed space for a group or an activity, as in a karaoke room or the facing-seat compartment in a restaurant or train.
A word treated as a unit of search, data, or discussion — a search term, a trending term, a password. It does not replace {言葉|ことば} for "word" in the ordinary sense of vocabulary or speech.
The broken concrete, tiles, timber and other material left when a building collapses. Strongly associated with earthquakes, fires, and war damage.
The price the seller names, before any haggling. Usually used when the buyer either accepts it without negotiating or complains that it is too high.
